in writing. the eu solidarity fund is our main tool to stay united and stronger in the face of natural disasters. between 2002 and 2012, it helped respond to 49 crisis situations, releasing almost €3.2 billion for 23 countries. it is one of those major projects which actually benefit citizens, especially those in difficulty, and thus give meaning to the union. this reform would improve the functioning of the eusf and the quality and speed of its responses without placing additional burdens on the member states' budgets. i particularly support the objective of speeding up payments so that the state in difficulty can receive the funds it needs as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the solidarity fund, set up in 2002 following the devastating floods in central europe, is a very useful support instrument for countries hit by a major natural disaster. the latter may, where necessary, benefit from the financial solidarity of all the member states in addition to the funds they have themselves mobilised. between its creation and september 2012, the fund has been mobilised for 49 disasters (mainly floods and fires), amounting to eur 3.2 billion. the current aim is to make adjustments to make the fund more flexible and operational, in particular by simplifying the eligibility criteria and shortening the administrative procedures for granting. the text clarifies the definitions and categories of natural disasters, possibly incorporating new dimensions such as drought, mediterranean disasters or even disasters of non-natural origin.
in writing. the european union solidarity fund is a key fund to give substance to the principle of solidarity enshrined in the treaties in the event of natural disasters affecting one or other of the member states. i therefore believe that it is essential to do everything possible to reduce the bureaucratic obstacles to its implementation, which have been identified since its inception in 2002. in particular, it should be better able to function in the event of disasters identified as 'minor' and its implementation time should be shortened in order to provide assistance to the victims of such disasters as quickly as possible. with clarified definitions, this revised instrument will thus be able to continue to translate into action the european solidarity that our citizens want to see more expressed in their daily lives in these difficult times of crisis.
in writing. i welcome the position adopted by the european parliament in strasbourg on tuesday 15 january calling for the european union solidarity fund to be maintained. few citizens are properly informed about the solidarity actions carried out by the european union in support of regions that have suffered a major natural disaster. the eu solidarity fund, which has been in existence since 2002, is a very concrete instrument of this solidarity, since it supports the actions of the member states in a region or regions affected by a large-scale natural disaster. to date, the facility has been used in 49 cases in 23 countries, for a total of eur 3.2 billion. france has benefited from this funding on several occasions, notably following the 2010 xynthia storm, which raised eur 35,7 million, and following the 2002 gard floods, which raised eur 21 million. it is not a question of increasing the budget or creating the conditions for an increase in the budget, which is generously provided by the member states, but of rationalizing its use, speeding up the granting of aid and ensuring better publicity.

in writing. in this time of crisis, hundreds of thousands of citizens are suffering the consequences of restructuring across europe. while some of them can be explained, others are the result of arbitrariness and greed. in a globalised economy, the rules governing companies have become international, while workers remain governed by national rules that do not sufficiently protect them. we call on the european commission to take decisive action to support the restructuring of large companies (over 500 employees). the recommendations we make in the cercas report should be the pillars of a european directive. they can be summed up in the following words: anticipation, information for workers, social dialogue, minimisation of the social cost and support by the public authorities. restructuring operations must be explained and, moreover, justified to the workers. dismissals should be a last resort only after consideration of alternative options. the aim is to minimise social costs, maximise the possibilities for reintegration of workers, and develop collaboration with public authorities in the affected regions to finance vocational transition. in short, to give substance to this 'social' market economy.

in writing. the cercas report on information and consultation of workers was intended to change the commission's attitude to the violence of restructuring in europe. these operations, which are carried out at the expense of the workers and without listening to them, demonstrate the urgency of adopting a european framework for restructuring and guaranteeing the workers and their representatives a right to information, consultation and a role in these processes. the cercas report makes these demands and reminds companies of their obligations towards their employees. it also stresses the importance of preserving human capital and, above all, the value of investing in the training of workers planned in multiannual plans anticipating the needs of the company and guaranteeing the employability of its employees. however, the liberal and conservative amendments have reduced the scope of this report by diluting good ideas into vague suggestions, while guaranteeing companies provisions to limit the publication of information concerning the future of their employees. more seriously, the report merely asks the commission to examine the need for a legal act, where a strong directive is needed and its application would be monitored. because of these shortcomings, i decided to abstain.
in writing. we do not need european legislation, as mr cercas' report calls for, to think that social dialogue is a necessary element in anticipating and managing company restructuring. although this report makes some interesting proposals on how companies should behave towards their employees in the event of restructuring, national regulations, whether legislative or conventional, are the most relevant because they are the most adapted to the diversity of the economic situations of the member states. what is certain is that the ultra-liberal ideology of the european commission is largely responsible for the deindustrialisation of europe, and that the schizophrenic attitude of the european institutions to always want to cure the effects without tackling the causes, in particular social and fiscal dumping between member states or the rejection of any intelligent protectionism at the borders, will only increase the number of the 26 million unemployed in the european union. the discussions are about palliative care, not about how to cure the disease. i therefore abstained on this report.
in writing. this report is completely inconsistent. he acknowledges that austerity is aggravating the crisis and increasing unemployment, but he still supports it. it claims to develop 'information' for employees in advance of restructuring decisions in an attempt to avoid them, but gives no way for workers to weigh in on the decision. worse, it promotes the superiority of company-to-company negotiation of working conditions over the law, not only in exceptional circumstances (which is already unacceptable), but in general. this is the logic of sarkozy's "competitiveness-employment agreements", which were re-written into "employment retention agreements" by the agreement signed by three unions with medef on 11 january 2013, which is endorsed here. i am voting against this text and i am fighting the measures it proposes at european level as well as in france.
in writing. on 14 november 2011, the european union adopted a strategic framework for the horn of africa, focusing on several areas such as the promotion of human rights, peace, security and regional cooperation. i voted in favour of this report as i validate the implementation of this strategy, as i did with the appointment on 1 january 2012 of mr alexander rondos as the european union special representative for the horn of africa.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the eu strategy for the horn of africa because strengthening regional security and the fight against terrorism and piracy, as essential as they are, must not overshadow the absolute need to support poverty eradication in the horn of africa in the first place. sudan, somalia, ethiopia are in the hands of terrorist networks that threaten the security of other regions such as europe, the arabian peninsula or south asia. the european union's commitment to the region is guided by its geostrategic importance, but also by the desire to help the people of the horn of africa and lift them out of poverty. if the people can feed themselves, through agriculture, fishing, etc., they will no longer have to resort to acts of piracy and will not succumb to the easy money of a terrorist commitment.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the tannock report on the european union strategy for the horn of africa. i particularly welcome the comprehensive approach to addressing the security and stability problems and to upholding the rule of law in this region, which is experiencing serious difficulties. i also support the concrete measures proposed, which include stepping up efforts to combat piracy.
in writing. the horn of africa is a region facing immense challenges: food, poverty, development, conflict... the lives of its inhabitants are particularly difficult. i welcome the vision of this report: to work for the stability of the horn of africa is to work for the stability of the whole region. i therefore voted in favour of this text, not only because it supports our ambitions in the field of security and humanitarian aid, but also because it urges the european authorities concerned to take account of the economic opportunities in the region for increased and shared prosperity. the commission should also be able to provide the necessary information to the member states and the commission, in order to ensure that the information is available to all member states.
in writing. the political and security situation in the horn of africa is of concern. the insurgency of the al-shabab movement, the lack of governance in somalia, the scale of piracy in the indian ocean, the tensions between sudan and south sudan as well as between eritrea and ethiopia are all elements that contribute to the destabilization of the region. the result is dramatic food insecurity and thousands of refugees and internally displaced persons. the european union (eu) has adopted a comprehensive approach to the horn of africa based on security and development. the future presence of a special representative for the horn of africa and the creation of a delegation to the african union are signs of the european will to play a greater role in the region, as it already does through the atalante and eucap nestor operations, which have helped to strengthen its maritime, judicial and police capacities. the eu must not allow this strategic region in terms of trade and geopolitics to be destabilised. the affirmation of the eu's role in international development and the maintenance of global security depends on regional successes, which will confirm the validity of the european approach.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which is part of the continuity of the strategic framework for the horn of africa, adopted by the european union on 14 november 2011. in a region facing serious conflicts and insecurity, this strategic framework defined a european strategy focused on promoting human rights, peace and security, combating piracy and crime, reducing poverty and regional cooperation. the resolution proposes concrete measures to improve the implementation of this framework and stresses the need to combat piracy more effectively and to continue eu support for the intergovernmental authority on development (igad). it also called for the political transition periods in somalia, ethiopia, eritrea and south sudan to be used to provide better support to the countries in the region.
in writing. the report supports the rehabilitation of pirates in the horn of africa, sanctions for illegal dumping of waste by eu companies on the coast and condemns any support for irregular armed groups. it called for the release of political prisoners and stressed the importance of neutral and impartial eu humanitarian aid. i support her in that. but i cannot accept that this text also contains an implicit support for the logic of the economic partnership agreements which is harmful to these countries, an explicit encouragement to collaborate with nato on the ground and a request for the g20, this illegitimate body, to take the situation under control. i also denounce the support that this report shows for somaliland, an internationally unrecognised state in the hands of invicta capital. i also denounce the blind support for the grand renaissance dam project on the blue nile, on which no valid environmental expertise has been carried out. i vote against it.
in writing. we cannot tolerate the horn of africa becoming a playground for pirates, who are eager to hijack food aid, racketeer and board ships. i therefore welcome this report which sets out a strategy to stabilise this part of the world and ensure the safety of the local population and our citizens. i share the desire to step up the fight against piracy, by supporting operation atalanta, ensuring that pirates intercepted are brought to justice and recovering the ransom paid to them with the help of interpol and europol. i also support the call for the local populations to re-establish the rule of law in the region by developing their maritime intervention forces and judicial institutions. their ability to regain control of the region is crucial to restoring long-term security. until they achieve this degree of autonomy, we must continue our humanitarian, military and judicial efforts, because this is the only way to break the vicious circle of insecurity, instability and poverty in the region.
in writing. the european parliament supports the right of developing countries to benefit from their genetic resources and traditional knowledge. he advocates the fight against 'biopiracy'. this is the lucrative use by multinational companies of medicinal substances and traditional remedies from developing countries without the permission of the latter and without the benefit of the populations who discovered these active ingredients.
in writing. as rapporteur for this text for the legal affairs committee of the european parliament, i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls on the member states to combat the use by the pharmaceutical, cosmetic and agri-food industries of natural resources collected in developing countries. the nagoya protocol, which aims to redistribute the benefits of this commercial exploitation between developed and developing countries by providing for the payment of compensation to the latter, is essential for this. i would remind you that in order to enter into force, this protocol adopted at the united nations conference on biodiversity in october 2010 must be ratified by at least 50 countries. to date, only nine have done so, but none in europe. 90% of the world's biological heritage is in developing countries. the vast majority of patents are held by the industrialized countries. this can't go on!
in writing. biopiracy, which involves patenting traditional knowledge and seeds of indigenous peoples in developing countries and then marketing their use without authorisation, has been practised with impunity by many multinational companies for too long. today, 90% of the world's biological heritage is in developing countries, but the majority of patents are held in developed countries. companies wishing to obtain patents for inventions involving genetic resources and traditional knowledge will now have to disclose the origin of the resources in question and provide proof of the consent of the authorities of the country of origin. such an obligation is an effective means of combating counterfeiting and of establishing fair competition in the commercial field. it also helps to preserve the diversity of genetic resources for food, agriculture and even medicine. but this patent system goes far beyond ensuring the protection of the rights of indigenous peoples and local communities and helping to protect a biodiversity that promotes the eradication of extreme poverty and hunger.
in writing. despite the will of an increasingly conservative european right and the lobbies of the pharmaceutical, cosmetics and agri-food sectors attacking the heart of my report in an attempt to weaken its content, this positive vote in plenary represents a political victory! the three key demands of developing countries were heard: the requirement for patent applicants to disclose their origin (§28 adopted by 38 votes to none), the proof of prior consent and the proof of fair and equitable sharing. meps also want to see the eu's role in the fight against terrorism strengthened, and to ensure that the eu's role in the fight against terrorism is strengthened. the ep reiterates the urgency of placing the nagoya protocol at the centre of a more coherent global governance system and of not bowing to the wto (vote on paragraph 5.2 adopted by 44 votes to none). the ep thus affirms its determination to move towards greater policy coherence for development and its firm will to put an end to bio-piracy, this new colonialism, this rush towards green gold.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to examine the consequences of intellectual property rights on genetic resources for human rights and global food security. genetic resources are the animals, plants and micro-organisms that surround us. this genetic heritage is a real "resource" for man, since it is used for agriculture, food, medicine, industry and many other activities. in recent years, the use of medicinal plants to create new medicines has become widespread. however, the patent law must not be called into question, which would weaken research. we must do everything possible to combat 'biopiracy' while ensuring a successful patent system to encourage companies to invest in expensive research programmes. the report also recommends a number of recommendations, including strengthening traceability controls in the collection of genetic resources, ensuring that the union does not create legal monopolies on biological species, and measures to be taken to better enforce the intellectual property rights of indigenous communities.
in writing. this report warns of the major ecological and social problem of bio-piracy. the commission is proposing that the eu take up the matter and work in international negotiations to combat this phenomenon. it called for the establishment of effective international justice mechanisms. it advocates "cooperation" and "sharing of benefits" rather than free competition. he is concerned about the commercialisation of traditional knowledge. it stresses the need to ensure that everyone has access to affordable medicines, which i support. i regret, however, that the text is silent on the sanctions to be applied to biopirates. i also regret, and above all, that it does not close the door on the patentability of living things. in these circumstances, i cannot possibly vote for it. i'm not going to.
in writing. the protection and conservation of genetic diversity is a key element in the achievement of the millennium development goals. genetic resources, i.e. the natural resources of the various species, are crucial for sustainable agriculture and food security. their diversity is essential for the survival of species and the resilience of the ecosystem. as a result, the depletion of genetic diversity is a fundamental challenge for humanity and poses new challenges for both holders and users of genetic resources. in this context, biopiracy, whereby biological resources are taken from local communities or indigenous populations and patented without the resulting benefits benefiting those communities, has become a major concern in developing countries. the report on aspects of the development of intellectual property rights on genetic resources reflects this problem of biopiracy and defends the rights of indigenous and local communities to their traditional resources and knowledge, and urges member states to implement a globally consistent management system. for that reason i have decided to vote in favour of the report.

i'm the reporter. - madam president, welcome to the irish presidency, hi the irish presidency, thank you. i would like to point out to you, commissioner, that we are now considering - and i hope we will vote on it tomorrow - a report, which is an own-initiative report, on which we have tried to find a balance and to send backwards those who tend to take a somewhat extreme position. there are those who think that because we are going to create eurobonds or stability bonds we will be able to save ourselves a certain amount of effort - that is not at all the opinion of your rapporteur or, moreover, of the team of fictitious rapporteurs who have worked on this subject - but also not to accept certain extreme positions of refusal, in principle, without seeing three elements. firstly, there are difficulties in some member states which may be linked to disturbances in the markets and the more instruments we have that can stabilise the markets and provide liquid assets - which are also sought after, for example, by our own insurers - the better it will be for the stability of the whole. this was also recognised by the european council in june. secondly, there are aspects which are linked to the existence of a single currency. we created a currency. it is also why there is a global securities market backed by this currency. finally, there are also elements in the report which are almost intended to reinforce the measures which we have adopted in this parliament with the council and the commission since the beginning of the crisis. i am thinking, for example, of the idea of a fund which would help the states to meet the very strict commitments to reduce their debt that have been set. again, i think there are good reasons. there may be concerns, but there are also good reasons that need to be stressed and that need to be kept in mind. that is exactly what we are asking. i welcome the presence of commissioner rehn, who, in the six-pack, made commitments with us on a green paper which has since come into being. we would like to continue to study the various hypotheses without rushing, considering many different steps which, moreover, do not follow one another automatically, but which can nevertheless be conceived one after the other, to examine very seriously the obstacles - i would like to say this to the reluctant colleagues - of a constitutional nature in certain member states, or linked to the obligation to ratify the treaties. it is not at all a question of ignoring important legal obligations. nor is it a question of doing nothing under the pretext that some legal instruments should be changed. i would like to end by making a point. i think that this discussion has already brought us some progress, since some time ago the dominant idea in some of the papers of the bruegel think tank, for example, was to pool the debt that would be issued by the various member states. when you look closely at this idea, you realize that this requires an extremely strong conditionality, which is not excluded, but which would end up being extraordinarily intrusive. when you compare, for example, with what has been done - this is not the absolute model, but it is a reference point - in the united states, you realize that this allows each of the american states to issue debt and that what has gained importance and helped strengthen the dollar is the t-bill, which was issued at the level of all the states that make up the federation of the united states. it is also one of the steps - and i personally want to emphasize it - which i am glad is in this report, not to be crossed tomorrow morning, but i see that it is quite broadly in line with the concerns expressed by mr van rompuy, which are reflected in the document at the end of last year, that in front of a currency there may one day need to be a budget, and that therefore, if there are own resources in the budget, there may one day be instruments that are supervised, controlled, but which allow for joint indebtedness. i am naturally asking you to support this report, given that it is a step on a long road.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this report makes three important proposals. first, it draws attention to the urgency of the introduction of eurobills to facilitate the circulation of debt and to provide room for manoeuvre. secondly, the report considers the proposals made in the commission's green paper on the guarantee to be given by the states to eurobonds. the report suggests in the annex that this guarantee should be joint and several, like that which the member states grant to the community budget. these two proposals represent an important step forward. a third proposal is under discussion. the report envisages the creation of a debt amortisation fund. i would have liked the duration of this amortisation to be more realistic, i.e. longer, because the proposed duration condemns the member states to 25 years of austerity. another criticism is that the fund is designed to pay off debt accumulated beyond a volume considered optimal. the 60% of gdp reference figure must be the subject of a rigorous and dispassionate debate, because in economics, the debt of some is the savings of others. the debate is therefore continuing, and this report, which i hope will be adopted by a large majority, is a milestone. unfortunately, some people continue to deny the urgency of eurobonds, while others continue to fear the laxity of the governments which are implementing the biggest austerity package the world has ever seen. it therefore remains to convince these sceptics that eurobonds can be a formidable instrument for mobilising savings and for financing solidarity and growth.

i'm the reporter. - madam president, i would like to thank all those who took the time to read the report. they'll know we're not touching the rule of law. we simply consider it as potentially modifiable. we can also consider changing the treaties one day, for example. that is what we are saying in the report, quite simply. those who have read it will also have noticed that we do not present eurobonds as a panacea, but as one tool among others. they will also have seen that we are not opposed to structural reforms. as for colleagues who are personalising or exaggerating, i have no desire to answer them at all. i will therefore conclude by telling the commissioner that i have received the message about the two-pack, that we have always worked very well, but that there are simply two of us. and even in this case, there are three of us to tango, and maybe that's why we're having a little trouble. however, if the council hears the demands made by parliament, i believe we can close the two-pack fairly quickly. but for us, codecision cannot be 'the council sets the rules and parliament follows'.
madam president, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and the various fictitious rapporteurs on their work, which has been particularly constructive. so it was not as tense as you imagine, commissioner. the important efforts made by both sides have borne fruit and parliament is now in a position to adopt this report by a large majority. this compromise represents a significant step forward in the debate on budgetary policies. the report proposes balanced solutions, which are different from the dogma of austerity, which has done so much damage in europe since the crisis began. it is pragmatically looking at solutions to reconcile growth and debt reduction, a pragmatism that europe has been so lacking since 2009. three main ideas are presented in this report. firstly, recovery also requires productive public investment and requires the use of automatic stabilisers, such as national pension systems. this is a crucial point, because without growth there can be no fiscal consolidation. secondly, the report asks the commission to publish the assumptions used in the estimates of the multiplier and the structural deficit of the member states. if the recent imf revaluations of the multiplier are correct, a consolidation strategy centred on budget cuts could plunge europe into a lasting recession. the report therefore argues that tax reform, aimed at increasing revenue, can also be an important part of consolidation policies. the commission's proposals are not only a means of ensuring that the community's financial resources are used effectively, but also a means of ensuring that the community's financial resources are used effectively. we therefore hope that this report will serve as an inspiration for the commission's work and the council's deliberations.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i would like just to repeat, we have had this discussion numerous times so there is not such great confusion. the commission has no intention of authorising, the european modular system – there are various names for this – or gigaliners to be used all over europe. i strongly support the opinion that this must be left in the hands of the member states. if a member state allows these bigger trucks to be used, as happens in northern countries, then it is in the hands of the member states, and if there are countries where the population does not like them then it is up to their governments to decide that these cannot be used. i think this is the only possible way to deal with this issue. we do not have any intention of authorising the use of bigger trucks in all member states. i want to say that this amendment to this directive includes a great many positive changes in weights and dimensions in order to make trucks more environmentally friendly and more efficient as well. this is why i listed these at the beginning. some member states, as you know very well, have allowed bigger trucks, including several ‘lands’ in germany. there are various reports. some reports say we have had impact assessments, and we have different assessments of the situation, and the various reports do, as mr bach said, give various answers to these questions. that was the issue on which our opinions conflicted and where the problem was created. i admit too that giving a legal answer to a letter which asked what was the legal interpretation was a mistake. we consulted parliament’s legal service with, as you know, all the members of the committee on transport present when we discussed these issues and we thought that it would be enough if we gave legal explanations, and if countries allow the use of bigger trucks they can also cross borders under certain conditions and these conditions are listed. i agree that this could of course have been handled differently. i admit that this was a mistake. i can clearly say that this was our mistake and it could of course be handled with this directive, linked to this directive, and within this directive in parliament and now it is a possibility. so we consider that parliament has full powers during this discussion about amendments to this directive to make whatever amendments – to vote for this amendment, to vote against that amendment – and so this issue must now be settled in this way. it is now for the members of the european parliament, for the committee on transport, to form an opinion about the possibilities of crossing borders between the member states. so far the legal explanation exists. our legal opinion is that these are bigger trucks; if member states allow them to be used then they can also cross borders. about weight sensors: weight sensors are very expensive and we were reluctant to include them in this directive, so they have not been included. they are very expensive and we promote the voluntary use of these sensors. of course, from what i just said i can clearly answer that no infringement procedure has been launched against member states which have allowed their bigger european modular system trucks to cross the borders.

mr president, i am pleased that today the european parliament has voted on a new timetable, taking account of the decision of the court of justice of the european union. it has said the right thing, it has stated very clearly and very explicitly that it is in strasbourg that the 12 plenary sessions of our parliament should be held, 12 plenary sessions a year. it was important that the law be reaffirmed, that the spirit and the letter of the treaties be made clear once again, and that we, the european parliamentarians, be the first to take care to respect the spirit and the letter of the treaties. we do not need to look back at the history of our continent, at the symbol that strasbourg represents for reconciliation between the peoples of europe, to understand that it is in strasbourg that the heart of european parliamentary democracy vibrates and lives.

in writing. everyone remembers the controversy over rating agencies and the french triple a and the "power" of the 3 leading rating agencies in this market. these agencies have thought themselves free to make a difference in the financial situation of the states through their ratings, and they have thought themselves unassailable. the reply has finally come, not from the member states, but from europe. after proposing the creation of a european rating agency to compete with the us agencies, parliament adopted stricter rules on the rating of government debt or credit. similarly, to avoid any speculation about a state's poor performance, the ratings will be made on request to limit conflicts. and the publication of ratings will have to be after the closure of established markets in the eu and at least one hour before they reopen. finally, credit rating agencies can be sued if any of these rules are not respected. these measures taken at european level should help us to avoid financial crises of the magnitude of those we have just experienced.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which aims to regulate the infallibility dogma of the current credit rating agencies by introducing clearer and fairer ratings, and which also supports the idea of creating a european rating agency. while the rating agencies are doing their bit in the financial markets, the european union must propose regulatory rules that increase the civil liability of these agencies, in order to make them liable in the event of badly designed ratings or ratings that have harmed investors or member states. the text will require agencies to explain the main factors on which their ratings are based and to refrain from commenting on the political life of sovereign states. citizens, not rating agencies, decide what policies or reforms to implement.
in writing. the rating agencies do not simply give opinions, as is amply demonstrated by the statements published by standard and poor's and moody's after the us budget agreement: they judge policies and want to dictate their conduct to governments and parliaments, under threat of sanctions. your regulation, however much better it may be than inaction, does not fundamentally change this fact. as long as the entire financing system of the states and many leading companies is based on disintermediation and markets, a risk assessment will remain indispensable to "inform" the choice of investors. and this is all the more so since your attempts to regulate financial activity more effectively have the effect of encouraging banks to withdraw from the market. they keep formalizing the ratings, just trying to limit their automatic impact. including this text. for a very long time, this assessment will therefore depend on three agencies whose credibility has been tarnished, among other things, by the enron affair and the current crisis. i do not believe in the creation of a european public agency, subject to conflicts of interest with the commission and/or the states, or in the proliferation of small private agencies which will suffer from a lack of reputation, experience and space. i believe in a radical change of system.
in writing. i supported the outcome of long negotiations which will put an end to the conflicts of interest and the irresponsibility of the rating agencies, which have plunged many european states into a socially unsustainable debt crisis. the new rules i am supporting today will allow injured parties to claim damages for ratings which have been shown to be ill-conceived and have harmed their interests. in addition, the rating of public debts will be controlled to avoid any manipulation. finally, i welcome the adoption of a roadmap for the creation of a european public credit rating agency for sovereign debt, which is in line with president hollande's commitment to create such an instrument.
in writing. the purpose of this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council was to amend regulation no 1060/2009 on credit rating agencies in order to reduce excessive reliance on them, so that the ratings they issue are considered to be mere pieces of information, but do not have automatic consequences on the activity of economic or financial actors, as may have been the case during the crisis, with the serious consequences we are experiencing. the new regulation, which i voted in favour of, includes the requirement for credit rating agencies to communicate their rating outlooks in advance, the obligation for certain financial institutions to set up an internal rating system and the reduction of the potential for conflicts of interest.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of new measures to regulate credit rating agencies. these stricter rules are designed to protect governments and citizens against speculative attacks by the markets when the agencies downgrade ratings. these rules therefore serve four main objectives: to reduce the reliance on rating agencies, to improve the transparency and regularity of ratings, to eliminate any conflict of interest and to hold agencies accountable by offering damages procedures for investors and stock issuers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which imposes new rules on the agencies which record the debts of governments and whose influence has become very important on economic markets, economic policies and companies. in order to frame their operating procedures and improve transparency, agencies will need to explain and document their rating and should not advocate policy changes. in addition, the internal organisation of the agencies should comply with new rules on conflicts of interest. a shareholder may not hold more than 10% of the voting rights in an agency that publishes ratings on an entity in which it has invested.

in writing. i supported the proposal to regulate the activity of rating agencies in their assessment of sovereign debt. the lack of any control is part of the reason for the crisis we are experiencing. to avoid abuses or excessive reliance on banks by agencies, their assessment methods should be monitored. it is also vital that the union has its own public rating instrument. all rights lead to duties. i therefore felt it necessary to strengthen the obligations of the agencies. they have to follow some simple rules, like not rating any government they have as a client. they must also undertake to provide all information necessary for the evaluation of the ratings they issue. the agencies are an economic thermometer, not elected decision makers. they also do not have to dictate the european political agenda: the european parliament has thus ensured that agencies can no longer, as has already happened in the past, announce a downgrade on the eve of a european council, or important political decisions. if they pass judgments on government economic policies, temporary or permanent bans or fines will be issued.

mr president, it is obvious to all that young people are the future, and yet too many of our children no longer have confidence in that future, because they are faced, in particular, with the complexity of the world of work, while economic crises are increasingly hitting the most vulnerable. almost 24% of young people, or 5.7 million, are now unemployed in the european union. these figures are staggering, yet these young people are making a real effort to be responsible and to be independent. the resolution is therefore entirely legitimate, because it aims to offer young people who have been unemployed for more than four months the opportunity of being offered a job, training or apprenticeship. it is essential to consider european strategies in this area. i therefore welcome the work done by the rapporteur and i shall vote in favour of this report. there is a "but" though. it seems to me that he does not present the whole problem. unemployment and precariousness are only partly linked to problems of matching supply and demand in terms of the supply of jobs, and a better policy of youth guidance and a more vocational training offer will only partly solve the problems posed. the european union must therefore respond to the problem of youth employment in two ways. on the one hand, clear rules should be laid down to regulate the use of precarious contracts and to prevent them from replacing stable jobs where there is a real need for labour. on the other hand, there is an urgent need to act in favour of our industries and the recovery of growth, which alone will make it possible to combat unemployment in general and youth unemployment in particular in the long term.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the 'european youth guarantee'. the aim of this scheme is to enable young people under 25 who have been unemployed for more than four months to be offered a job, training or apprenticeship. the text asks eu employment ministers to adopt a council recommendation by february 2013 to implement the system in all eu member states.
in writing. already introduced in several member states, the youth guarantee is based on a simple idea: 'every young person should be offered a good quality job, further training, apprenticeship or traineeship within four months of leaving school or losing their job'. while we welcome the commission's communication, we want to know more, hence the questions to the commissioner: what means, including financial means, will the eu mobilise to support the introduction of this guarantee in all member states? such a tool has a significant budgetary cost. how does the commission intend to encourage member states to allocate part of their european social fund allocation to developing the youth guarantee? beyond the budgetary issue, it appears that the key to success is close cooperation between the different levels of governance, the social partners, the employment services and the training institutes. we ask the commission to define its strategy for stimulating this cooperation. such a tool can become a pillar of european solidarity and a sign of hope for a whole generation now sacrificed. we therefore urgently need concrete and ambitious progress on this issue.
in writing. i voted in favour of the establishment of a youth guarantee to help young people who are unemployed. the aim is to enable these young people to receive training, an apprenticeship or a job within four months of losing their job or leaving school. this youth guarantee will have to be partly financed by the esf.
in writing. it is important to support this initiative given the employment situation, especially for those under 30, we cannot afford to make beautiful promises and statements. the youth guarantee is not a guarantee of employment, but it should give young people a boost, a start in life, so that they can then gain work experience and enter the working world. all the member states are faced with this situation of unemployment among their young people, some more than others, so it is yet another example of europe as we conceive it, a 'europe of solidarity', and that is why this instrument deserves that we provide it with all the necessary means and that we monitor its proper application. it is also an additional instrument to encourage more europe and more social governance.
in writing. by voting in favour of this resolution, i support the creation of a youth guarantee facility, which will enable young people, the first to be affected by the crisis, to be offered quality education and employment opportunities, appropriate to their needs. what we are asking for is that this mechanism should be directed to those who need it most. and this includes not only those under 25 but also young people in the labour force who still have too many difficulties entering or remaining in the labour market. i therefore voted in favour of this text and i hope that the ministers of the member states will hear our appeal.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because, in this time of crisis, young people are the most affected. their unemployment rate is 25%, and in some countries it is as high as one third: a whole generation is excluded from the labour market, with tragic effects on their career development and on our economy. education is no longer a guarantee of employment, and young graduates often go on to work in apprenticeships with little or no pay, with no prospects. the cost to the european union of inaction on this issue is estimated at around €53 billion, or 1.2% of our gdp. we must therefore implement youth guarantee mechanisms. the member states and the european union must cooperate to establish and finance such a mechanism as soon as possible. all actors (educational and training establishments, enterprises, authorities) must be involved in helping young people to enter the labour market as soon as possible.
in writing. i welcome the proposal to create a youth guarantee to combat youth unemployment, a scourge affecting more than 5.5 million young people in the union, not to mention the approximately 1.5 million young people affected by precarious employment. this was a longstanding demand on the part of parliament, and in particular the s&d group, which had campaigned for such an initiative. now we need funding to match the ambitions. at a time when talk of budget cuts is all the rage, on the eve of the conclusion of the negotiations on the next multiannual financial framework, firm guarantees must be provided to finance this indispensable policy to combat youth unemployment. it is also a matter of promoting the model of a europe which protects its citizens, and in particular the most vulnerable, such as young people, who are particularly exposed to precarious employment. this is the face of a europe that is not just a machine for deregulation, which we want to show.
in writing. the youth guarantee, which is designed to recommend that member states provide employment, training and traineeship for every young person under 25 after a period of four months of unemployment, seems to me to be a major communication operation designed to reconcile young people with the european union. to pretend that the european union is concerned about youth unemployment, when all the policies decided in this house have contributed and still contribute to putting young people out of work, seems to me to be the last stage of hypocrisy. only the abandonment of the economic, financial and monetary policy of the european union, which has led our continent to disaster, will allow our economies to recover and, consequently, reduce youth unemployment. the rest of it will be just plaster on a wooden leg. that is why i abstained on this motion for a resolution by mrs berès.
in writing. i voted in favour of the 'youth guarantee' resolution which would allow young eu citizens and legal residents to be offered a job, continuing training or a good quality apprenticeship within four months of leaving school or losing their job. while the youth unemployment rate has jumped to 23.4%, meaning that 5,680,000 young people are unemployed, partly due to a mismatch between skills supply and demand in the labour market, this system would give an additional chance for young people to enter the labour market and thus avoid the increased risks of future unemployment and social exclusion. the cost of inaction on the problem of young people not in employment, education or training is estimated at around €53 billion, or 1.2% of gdp.
in writing. the berès report makes two relevant proposals concerning the 'youth guarantee' project. it proposes a personalised assessment of the needs of each young person, leading to appropriate measures. it also proposes to define a 'quality framework' and in particular a decent salary for each young person. i support it for these two reasons. i regret, however, that he merely comments on it. these proposals must be demands or at least 'strong recommendations', since this is a recommendation which parliament intends to make here. i also object to the fact that there is not a word in the text to denounce the breach of labour law which the commission is calling on the member states to undertake. i abstain in order to encourage the two key proposals which this report does not defend well.
in writing. according to the european commission, youth unemployment reached 23.7% in the eu in 2012. although the situation varies from one member state to another, the rate is nowhere below 15% - it is 27% in france, over 30% in portugal and over 50% in spain. it is therefore absolutely urgent to find effective solutions to the problem of youth employment. in this connection, the establishment of a 'youth guarantee' system seems particularly relevant. it aims to enable all young eu citizens up to the age of 25 and young graduates under 30 to be offered a job, training or apprenticeship within four months of losing their job or leaving school. in voting for this resolution i support the commission's proposal for a council recommendation to introduce this system in all member states. the text stresses that the fund should be eligible for eu funding, in particular from the european social fund, and calls on the commission to support member states with budgetary constraints in setting up such an instrument.
in writing. i defended the resolution of my comrade p.bérès in favour of a youth guarantee project. as a result of the crisis, more than 23% of young europeans are unemployed. worse, 7.5 million of them are under 25 years old and unable to work or train. youth is the future. it must be at the heart of all our projects. it is urgent to define a strategy accompanied by concrete measures, such as guaranteeing that young people under 25 or recent graduates under 30 are offered a job or training within 4 months of entering the labour market. that is why the council and the commission must agree and launch an ambitious plan for young people. the european social fund must be increased accordingly to finance this guarantee, without reducing the funds for other programmes. i believe that close cooperation between the commission, the member states and the social partners is necessary to ensure that the needs of young people are assessed precisely and specifically. that is the point of this proposal. that is why i support it with determination and conviction.
in writing. this text makes recommendations on how cohesion policy could better support the implementation of the eu's and its regions' new energy priorities. in the forthcoming multiannual financial framework, the european commission has for the first time allocated substantial resources to the energy sector under the european regional development fund. i voted in favour of this text allowing 'at least 50% of the funds to be used for investments in the low carbon economy'.
in writing. i voted for the kolarska-bobinska report. it seems important to me to make clear recommendations on how cohesion policy can support the implementation of the eu's new energy priorities. i am convinced that european energy projects will help to create more jobs. finally, i welcome the emphasis on the need to take account of the specific needs of the various regions of europe.
in writing. cohesion funds can be an important lever in the realisation of the single energy market. cooperation between our territories must also be possible in this area, to enable the development of crossborder energy infrastructure and networks, to finance energy efficiency and renewable energy. i particularly welcome the efficiency approach adopted in this report: where energy policy and cohesion policy complement and even reinforce each other, we must know how to make use of these synergies for the success of the common market, our energy security and the well-being of europeans. if the cohesion fund is used to finance energy projects, we must ensure that they contribute to the cohesion objectives we have set ourselves. the transition to a low-carbon economy is an important objective, which must allow the development of our regions, which have different characteristics and therefore different needs.
in writing. the aim of this report is to highlight the role that cohesion policy can play in the new european energy strategy (energy 2020 and the roadmap to 2050). unfortunately, the rapporteur's initial intention was mainly to represent the special interests of her country of origin. the rapporteur therefore wished cohesion policy to support not only renewable energy but also other sources such as shale gas. the report also calls for funding for energy efficiency projects at the expense of renewable energy projects. this is like "stripping paul to dress peter". for all these reasons, i voted against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which, while recalling that the eu's cohesion programme should not replace energy policy, makes sensible recommendations to support the new energy priorities of the eu and its regions through cohesion policy. the european commission has allocated significant financial resources to the energy sector under the european regional development fund, 50% of which will be used to invest in the low-carbon economy. this resolution highlights the potential of energy projects to promote regional development and create many jobs, particularly through investments in decentralised energy sources and the expansion of energy infrastructure. energy projects supported under the european regional development fund will, however, first have to respect the objectives of cohesion policy, namely to contribute to regional development and to reduce differences between regions.
in writing. i voted against the report on the role of eu cohesion policy in implementing the new european energy policy. this report, which was almost rejected in committee, provides for liberalisation of the energy sector, which means that the member states are relieved of their responsibility for implementing a sustainable and sound energy policy.
in writing. i exceptionally chose to abstain in the vote on this text. the introduction of euro bonds should be a medium-term objective in order to strengthen the budgetary, political and economic integration of the european union. nevertheless, it is essential that european countries first regain control of their public spending. this is not yet the case for all, for example in france. by abstaining, i chose not to block this progress but to emphasise the extreme caution i feel is necessary before putting these stability obligations in place.
in writing. the high and rising levels of public debt are a real sword of damocles for europe. in the medium term, we are talking about the survival of the euro. but to strengthen the euro and stabilise our currency in the long term, the idea of euro bonds, stability bonds, are structural tools. the pooling of debts would be as important a leap forward as the creation of the euro was. it is, of course, accompanied by a clearly defined framework of collective rules. in this sense, my colleague sylvie goulard's report sets out a precise and welcome road map to overcome the various reservations. the report details all the options on the table to move forward. so i naturally voted in favour of this one.
in writing. i voted against the own-initiative report by sylvie goulard. europe will not be able to introduce eurobonds until the member states have completely cleaned up their public finances and provided long-term guarantees. the creation of such a system would lead to a mutualisation of european sovereign debts and thus to a common borrowing and repayment. the risk is that the best students will borrow at higher rates than they do now.
in writing. eurobonds are an opportunity to help us get our economies back on track, and they deserve consideration. in any case, they require a much higher level of economic and fiscal integration than we have today and can therefore only be a solution in the medium or long term. it is good to present a roadmap, which can serve as a basis for further reflection. however, i fear that this text sends the wrong signal. we all know that what is important is to stabilize our economies first. we must not be hasty. we have taken good measures to stabilise and strengthen our economies and our finances, for example with the european semester or the treaty on stability, coordination and governance. but we are still waiting for them to take full effect. we cannot risk destabilizing the situation. for these reasons i have chosen to abstain.
in writing. parliament adopted a resolution urging member states and the european commission to explore all possibilities for sovereign debt pooling and to present them in reports, which could be accompanied by a roadmap for the implementation of the proposals in this area. i am aware of the benefits of debt pooling as a way out of the economic crisis, but i have nevertheless voted against this resolution because there are still concerns. it seems to me that it is still risky to start a process of debt pooling without the european union simultaneously gaining greater control over the expenditure of the member states. such a solution would encourage irresponsible or opportunistic behaviour by the least rigorous states in controlling public expenditure, since the latter would automatically be rescued by others in case of difficulties. the resolution also suggests that the joint issuance of national debt securities or the creation of european debt securities could be contrary to the treaty, which should therefore be revised.
in writing. the report proposes the creation of 'stability bonds' (eurobonds). it considers that the submission to the financial markets and the full repayment of sovereign debts is an insurmountable horizon for the member states of the european union. this leads him to propose partial, temporary or progressive debt-sharing mechanisms in which only those states which implement drastic austerity plans could participate. in this context, any budgetary 'deviation' would be sanctioned once again. when the postulate is arbitrary, the proposed solutions can only be so. the submission to the markets can and must be broken. the european governments have decisive instruments at their disposal: the capacity for direct lending to the states by the ecb, which must be made possible, and their sovereign right to organise a debt audit and not to pay back undue interest. i am voting against this text and denouncing the inability of the parliamentary majority to break out of its ideological blindness and propose valid solutions.

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, i should like to thank mr salafranca sánchez-neyra for his speech and allow me also to congratulate in his absence the rapporteur, mr mauro, and the european parliament for this excellent and comprehensive report on the eu-iraq partnership and cooperation agreement, which highlights the main issues and challenges in the eu’s relations with iraq. while focusing on the agreement, the report also looks into the wider context of the best ways to promote eu interests and the european values in iraq. the eu has a long-standing commitment to support iraq in its reconstruction and transition to democracy, with the objective of helping to build a stable, prosperous and democratic iraq, reintegrated in regional and global structures. the eu has been a major donor to iraq, providing support in many areas, such as basic services, assistance to refugees and displaced persons, as well as the strengthening of the political system, the rule of law and the protection of human rights, for example, through the csdp rule-of-law eujust lex mission. eu overall support to iraq since 2003 has amounted to over eur 1 billion, and this, of course, without counting the bilateral contributions of member states. with the partnership and cooperation agreement, we have opened a new chapter in our bilateral relationship. this is the first such agreement to frame the relations between the eu and iraq – providing a clear legal basis and a comprehensive institutional structure. the vice-president/high representative was very pleased to sign in may last year, with iraqi foreign minister zebari, this historic agreement which is good for iraq, good for the eu, and good for our long-term relationship. we are now looking forward to working with iraq on its implementation. that is what the agreement is about: the start of a new partnership, sealing our common wish to work together on a whole range of issues where we both have a lot to gain. but, it also provides a platform to talk about difficult issues, including the promotion of security, the cooperation in countering terrorism and arms proliferation and the promotion of human rights and fundamental freedoms. the agreement also provides for cooperation in support of iraq’s accession to the international criminal court. we are committed to boosting trade and investment between the eu and iraq. ‘economics meets politics’ is a formula which is dear to the vice-president/high representative: increased trade and investment will be crucial to back the work on the political front to support iraq’s transformation into a stable and prosperous democratic nation. the agreement will support iraq’s reform and development efforts and facilitate its integration into the wider international economy. it should also be a stepping stone to iraq’s wto accession, supporting its adaptation to wto rules and practice. the partnership and cooperation agreement with iraq is a non-preferential agreement based on most-favoured-nation principles. it offers very substantial market access to the eu and some preferential elements in public procurement, services and investments. the agreement also provides ample opportunities for enhanced cooperation on sectoral policies across the board, from energy and environment to education and innovation. let me stress the example of energy, where the eu can help iraq to harness its enormous energy potential, while iraq can contribute to the diversification of the eu’s energy supply and to its energy security as it is a potential source country for the southern corridor. there was a commitment with minister hoshyar zebari during the signature event in may for the rapid implementation of the main parts of the agreement that are provisionally applicable pending ratification. the eeas is discussing with iraqi counterparts the way forward so that progress is made as soon as possible. in this respect, i would also like to emphasise the important role of the european parliament. the parliamentary cooperation committee should be an important forum for the european and iraqi parliaments, providing excellent opportunities to exchange on democratic practice and provide further support to iraq’s transition. this partnership is not of course without challenges. iraq is a young democracy, and the road ahead will not always be smooth. iraq has made considerable progress in its transition towards democracy, but continues to face serious political, security, and socio-economic challenges. the level of violence in iraq is still unacceptably high and recently tensions between the major political forces (shia, sunni and kurdish) are on the rise. this carries a risk of re-igniting sectarian tensions in iraq, and it threatens the fragile balance that the ‘national partnership government’ is based on. it also slows down the necessary reforms as well as socio-economic progress. the human rights situation continues to be of serious concern, with the increased use of the death penalty – an unsatisfactory situation for women and vulnerable groups, including minorities. camp ashraf remains an important and sensitive issue. there has been some progress, but there are still a number of challenges in the critical process facilitated by the united nations with our full support. the eu is also committed to supporting the un process with a contribution of eur 12 million to support the operations of the un monitors and the unhcr refugee status determination process. the vice-president/high representative and the member states all follow the recent developments in iraq with great concern. it is in everybody’s interest to see a stable, democratic and prosperous iraq, where the political system is underpinned by a strengthened rule of law and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. the partnership and cooperation agreement therefore arrives at a very timely moment, since it creates a platform and increases the eu leverage to address these concerns with iraqi counterparts. we must see iraq’s transition also in the regional context – in particular with respect to the dramatic and violent developments unfolding across the border in syria, which we have just discussed, but also iran’s increasing influence. this adds to the difficulty of iraq’s democratic endeavours – but makes its success even more important. let me conclude by stressing that this agreement is above all, a symbol of the eu’s wish to be a constructive partner for iraq in its democratic endeavours. it brings together the eu and its member states and it is the main instrument to show the eu’s unified determination to build a long-term partnership with a stable and democratic iraq, not just for today or tomorrow, but for many years to come.
opinion of the committee on international trade and development - mr president, commissioner, madam minister, the first thing i would like to do is to stress the importance of this agreement, because it is the first one that the european union is going to sign with iraq. this agreement will accompany the democratic transition of that country, its reconstruction and political normalisation within the international community. as rapporteur for the committee on international trade, i would like to highlight the trade provisions it contains and the incorporation of basic world trade organisation rules, but above all i think it is important to highlight the technical and logistical assistance which the commission, which is the european union, can provide to the country at this time of transition. and also, to emphasize that this agreement will facilitate the european union's access to the public procurement and services markets and will thus also balance relations between the european union and iraq. in short, it is about what trade represents as an essential resource for increasing stability and prosperity in iraq, and the agreement we are voting on tomorrow represents a great opportunity for iraq and for the european union.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, madam minister, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to welcome the work of my colleague, mario mauro, on this matter and the presentation made by mr salafranca. like him, i believe that this partnership and cooperation agreement is a decisive step in relations between the european union and iraq. it will enable the union to support the democratic process in iraq more effectively. its 'trade and significant investment' component lays the foundations for a sustainable and mutually beneficial economic relationship within the wto framework, as iraq requested in 2004. above all, it encourages the country to make new efforts and to undertake new reforms, because, despite all the obstacles, iraq is well on the way to democracy. for example, local elections are being held this year and parliamentary elections next year. but i still have a few concerns. firstly, the daily problems of iraqis: physical insecurity - mr president, the tragic fire at the tazreen fashion factory has caused a stir in bangladesh and has brought to light the deplorable working and safety conditions. bangladesh is the second largest clothing exporter in the world, behind china, due to low wages and abundant labour, especially child labour. the conditions of over-exploitation of the garment sector in bangladesh are notoriously extreme, but this does not prevent the major western ready-to-wear and distribution chains from supplying them. due to the involvement of these bangladeshi clothing multinationals, the fire on november 24 also caused a wave of outrage in the world. the whole of south asia, a major exporter of textiles, is affected. the over-exploiting employers and the corrupt asian governments are obviously to blame. but the laws of the global capitalist market are also directly involved. the transnational corporations are competing with the various countries in the region, driving down wages, working conditions and safety standards. the bangladeshi government must immediately impose safety regulations on factories. victims of such breaches of social or environmental legislation, victims of the non-compliance by multinationals, to the detriment of their immediate subsidiaries, with the principles of corporate social responsibility, should be able to bring cases before the courts of the country where the breach has occurred. the establishment of international judicial procedures should make it possible, where appropriate, to sanction companies that break the law. and so to respond to european companies, we must know that these same multinationals are killing european small and mediumsized enterprises.
mr president, madam minister, commissioner barnier, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to express my condolences to the families of the victims, as other members have done. in the six years between the spectrum factory accident in 2005 and the tazreen fashions factory accident last november, more than 600 people died in textile factory fires in bangladesh. these terrible figures show that conditions are deteriorating in the country's 5,000 textile factories. the bangladesh authorities must work with engineers, architects and emergency services to improve safety. and they must punish factory managers who are negligent. we do not deny that the government and some companies have become aware of the problem and are trying to provide solutions. the european union can and must help them to do so! but i would now like to speak, commissioner, about the behaviour of certain multinationals, which other colleagues have already mentioned, without being populist - i am speaking to my colleague mr caspary - and i quote them: wal-mart, c&a, gap. all are reluctant to participate in agreements on the safety of their staff. yet, they are responsible! that's a position i take on a regular basis. because of their weight in international trade, european companies play a fundamental role in promoting and disseminating social and labour standards worldwide. we cannot simply condemn. we must also, and above all, promote the solutions that exist and that work.
