president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i am again very grateful to the house for drawing attention to this very important issue and for organising this debate, in which i am pleased to be participating. corruption is a significant threat to the foundations of our democratic system. it undermines the rule of law on which all of our national systems, as well as the european union, are based. it saps public confidence in the institutions and organisations which are supposed to be at the service of every citizen. it also comes with an economic cost. it is estimated that a sum equivalent to 1% of eu gdp is lost every single year as a result of corruption. corruption thrives on a culture of secrecy and concealment, and we can only begin to tackle it if we are open and transparent. today’s debate is therefore particularly welcome. it is encouraging that corruption is acknowledged and discussed much more openly than it was a few decades ago. that goes not just for europe but also beyond. the eu has had considerable success in getting corruption on to the global agenda. we seek to use our influence through trade and other instruments at our disposal to encourage a more robust approach to corruption. clearly, much remains to be done, but we are starting to get some of our partners to take the issue seriously where once it was simply accepted as a part of normal life. within the eu there has been a strong political commitment at the highest political level to tackle corruption. in the stockholm programme, the multiannual strategic framework covering the area of freedom, security and justice for the period 2012 to 2014, the european council called for concrete measures to strengthen the eu’s anti-corruption policy. furthermore, in its 2010 internal security strategy the justice and home affairs council referred to corruption as one of the main challenges to internal security and called for further action at eu level. these statements reflect a strong political will to tackle corruption within the eu, and they are gradually being turned into concrete measures which constitute an effective and comprehensive eu anti-corruption strategy. the commission adopted an anti-corruption package in 2011. the package includes the decision to establish a new evaluation mechanism to assess anti-corruption efforts within the eu. it is a further step towards increased transparency and provides an incentive for member states to ratify and implement existing international anti-corruption instruments. this is important. there are still several key conventions in this area which have not yet been ratified by all eu member states. the evaluation mechanism announced by the commission in 2011 provides for reports every two years which will assess member states’ overall efforts in the fight against corruption. the first of these reports is due later this year and the council looks forward to the opportunity that this will present to review and strengthen european anti-corruption measures. but, in addition to the measures undertaken by member states, the eu institutions also need to be seen to be taking the issue of corruption seriously. we require a clear commitment from each of the eu institutions to take responsibility for ensuring that effective anti-corruption policies are in place within their own structures. this is essential for the credibility of action at eu level and for the maintenance of confidence in the political decision-making process. the council considers that the integrity of the eu’s institutions can be best demonstrated through the continuing development of measures which translate the principles of good governance into best working practices. this includes areas such as effective codes of ethic, clear rules on addressing possible conflicts of interest, unambiguous regulations on lobbying and increased transparency in policymaking. the council is also of the view that full eu membership of the council of europe’s group of states against corruption, greco, would support and strengthen the eu’s anti-corruption policy, and should therefore be a matter of priority. the council will work constructively in order to take forward its negotiations with greco so that we can find an appropriate solution to eu participation. the commission’s proposals for participation in greco were published in october 2012; following preliminary discussions, we understand that the commission is reviewing its proposal. we will engage constructively with the commission on this and we look forward to receiving a revised proposal from the commission in due course. a key actor in the protection of eu financial interests is of course the european anti-fraud office, olaf. in december, following lengthy and complex negotiations, the council was able to confirm that it had reached political agreement on amending regulation no 1073/1999, which is the basic legal act establishing olaf’s powers. the new regulation, once adopted, will strengthen olaf’s independence and clarify the tasks, duties and scope of action of olaf’s directorate-general and of the supervisory committee. it will also provide for clear reporting obligations, as well as for more timely and effective exchange of information between the various institutions and authorities involved during the different phases of investigations. the council is convinced that these reforms will make a significant contribution to increased protection of the union’s financial interests and very much hopes that agreement in the council will open the way for an early second reading agreement. the council and the eu as a whole take the fight against corruption very seriously indeed. that involves support for anti-corruption measures in the member states but also includes ensuring that our own institutions are an example to europe as a whole. much has been — and is being — done to combat corruption, but we can never afford to be complacent. so i can assure this house that, in the drive to root out corruption both in our societies and in our institutions, you will have the full support of the council of this presidency.
member of the commission. - mr president, on this extremely serious and important subject i would like to present to you a number of replies or observations by my colleague algirdas šemeta, who is currently held back by other obligations and who apologises to you. i also thank the presidency and the minister, lucinda creighton, for what she has just said, which of course goes in the same direction - she has repeatedly said this - as the efforts and actions of the commission, since this fight against fraud - this is the first point i would like to mention - concerning the union's funds, is a fundamental requirement and also a matter of respect for european taxpayers and citizens. it is linked to the fight against corruption, which remains one of the commission's strategic priorities. i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the situation in the middle east, but i would like to say that we should be concerned about the situation in the middle east. i shall begin by talking about the fight against fraud. since 2011, the commission has taken a number of initiatives to revise the institutional framework for the fight against fraud. first of all, the reform of olaf, which lucinda creighton has just mentioned. our proposal for reform of the european anti-fraud office was endorsed at political level before christmas, and i hope that this agreement, to which you have contributed, can be formalised quickly. we needed this new legal basis which will clarify the procedural rights of the persons concerned and strengthen cooperation between olaf, national judicial authorities and the eu institutions in order to make olaf work even better, and in an independent way. the second project is the directive on the criminal protection of the union's financial interests. the commission adopted this proposal for a directive on the protection of the union's financial interests against criminal offences in july 2012. this directive should specify, harmonise and strengthen the criminal law of the member states punishing offences relating to the union budget. why is this directive necessary? because not all member states protect european public money in the same way and these disparities have important consequences. so, ladies and gentlemen, at the end of 2011, national judicial authorities had decided only on 471 of the 1 030 cases that olaf had referred to them between 2006 and 2011. of these 471 decisions, only 199 resulted in a criminal conviction, which corresponds to a conviction rate of 42%. in these cases, the conviction rate varies from 19% to 92% depending on the member state. this is the hallmark of this disparity in the action of the member states. to remedy these differences, which are too great, the proposal for a directive establishes, if you will, a common definition of fraud and fraud-related offences, provides for minimum penalties for these offences and aims to extend the limitation periods. cross-border investigations are complex and time-consuming, and investigators need time to bring these cases to court. the negotiations have begun in the council and, as we had a feeling, ladies and gentlemen, they are not easy, the subject being purely royal. that is why we also need the clear and determined support of the european parliament on this very issue. the third topic is the european public prosecutor's office. we have to go further. it's an old subject. the commission will propose the creation of a european public prosecutor's office in june. experience has shown that crime affecting the financial interests of the union, being by its nature of a european dimension, calls for action at union level. the european public prosecutor's office will be able to collect evidence and prosecute fraudsters in all the member states concerned. it will effectively help - we believe - to ensure that public money does not feed the parallel or underground economy. fourthly, the anti-fraud strategy which we have put in place. of course, the commission is not relying on the member states alone. in june 2011, it presented an anti-fraud strategy to, inter alia, increase risk awareness among its own staff and improve internal tools. i would now like to turn to the activities of the european commission in the fight against corruption. olaf is working closely with the other commission services to set up the eu anti-corruption monitoring mechanism, which was announced in june 2011 in our communication on the fight against corruption throughout the european union. the directorate-general for home affairs, which is leading this initiative, is working under the supervision of my colleague, cecilia malmström. the commission has set up an expert group to provide advice on the general parameters of the monitoring mechanism. in addition, a network of national correspondents has been established, which complements and updates information from a wide variety of sources, including existing evaluation mechanisms, public authorities, experts, independent researchers, non-governmental organisations and civil society. each report on the fight against corruption will focus on a number of cross-cutting issues of particular interest to the european union, as well as on some aspects specific to each member state, which will be highlighted in country-by-country analyses. the report will therefore contain cross-cutting recommendations as well as recommendations for each country. if these recommendations are not legally binding on the member states of the union, the follow-up to them will be followed up in subsequent reports. the first report will be published next summer and will probably deal with we are working on it corruption in public procurement. in this respect, we are working on a pilot project, at the request of the european parliament. the main objective is to develop a method to measure the costs of corruption in public procurement. the indicators of corruption, the best practices in the application of public procurement legislation, for which i am also responsible as commissioner for the internal market, must be highlighted. in addition, reference criteria should be defined and useful operational recommendations should be made to the member states. we are now in the very last stage of preparing this project. the method has been developed and is currently being tested in eight member states, in five selected economic sectors, on which we spend most of the union's structural funds. the results of the study should contribute to better protecting the financial interests of the union and to developing effective anti-corruption policies at both national and union level in the future. these are the remarks i wanted to make on this important subject on behalf of the european commission. in writing. i voted for this resolution because it is important to support iraq in its democratic progress. since 2005, the country has held elections, adopted a constitution by referendum, and established the foundations of a federal state. elections are scheduled again in the coming months, and an iraqi high commission for human rights has just been established. however, challenges remain, including the security situation in the country, the fight against corruption, the consolidation of the rule of law and respect for human rights. despite repeated requests by the union, the death penalty is still applied and cases of torture are regularly revealed.
in writing. this is the first partnership and cooperation agreement (pca) between the european union and iraq. i voted in favour of this agreement, which provides a general basis for strengthening links and cooperation in many areas such as political issues, the fight against terrorism and the promotion of human rights, trade and investment in key areas such as energy and services.
in writing. the signing of a partnership and cooperation agreement with iraq marks a new chapter in the eu's deepening of relations with the country, which began in 2006. through this agreement, the eu is affirming its willingness to play an important role in iraq's political transition and development, and in its integration into the world economy. this historic agreement will strengthen our relations in several key areas, starting with the political area, which establishes an annual dialogue on human rights, democracy and the rule of law, including the fight against terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. in this context, it is important that the union contributes to respect for religious and ethnic minorities. we also welcome the cooperation which will enable iraq to ratify the rome statute, that is to say to recognise the authority of the icc. the agreement will strengthen cooperation in the social, medical and educational fields, helping to rebuild a country ravaged by war, terrorism and poverty, and consolidating its democratic transition. it is a sign of the eu's willingness to contribute to the establishment of lasting peace in this severely wounded part of the world.
in writing. the conclusion of this partnership and cooperation agreement will mark a fundamental milestone in relations between the european union and iraq. it is thanks to him that we will become a privileged partner at a historic moment in the history of this great country, that of its reconstruction and democratic consolidation. i welcome the broad emphasis on human rights and the fight against poverty. we will thus play an active part in the recovery of the country and the strengthening of its institutions, to the benefit of the strengthening of stability in the whole region. i support this commitment of europe to the iraqi people.
in writing. the report proposes to approve an agreement for the gradual establishment of free trade between the union and iraq. reconstruction aid and political dialogue are minor issues in this agreement, as are human rights and the rule of law. the aim is to accelerate the exchange of goods and services, particularly energy resources. the iraqi people have already suffered a long dictatorship and two wars of aggression. he continues to suffer the consequences of all this daily. i refuse to support the fact that it is now being forced to adopt a market economy and fiscal austerity for the benefit of the financial markets, as this agreement requires. i vote against it.
in writing. by voting in favour of this report, i am giving the go-ahead for the cooperation and partnership agreement with iraq. this agreement is historic, first because it is the first agreement between the eu and this country, and second because it will complete its transition to democracy, rebuild and normalise its relations with the international community. it should stimulate ties between the two sides in several areas, from trade to investment and development. the agreement also promotes human rights and fundamental freedoms and aims to combat terrorism and the proliferation of weapons. i would stress that it is crucial to align our political ambitions with the means at hand: to enable the eu to play a meaningful role in the transition in iraq, the eu delegation in baghdad must be fully operational, equipped with the necessary human resources, and have its own premises. in addition, the head of delegation should be able to travel safely to verify the correct implementation of eu-funded programmes and to observe the human rights situation and the reform process.
in writing. i voted in favour of the partnership and cooperation agreement with iraq because it is a question of the union establishing a dialogue with iraq on the long term, and in different areas. this partnership and cooperation agreement is a milestone in relations between the european union and iraq. it will provide a solid foundation for democracy, human rights, economic development and trade relations (the latter developing in the context of iraq's 2004 application for wto membership). the iraqi people are currently living in difficult conditions: insecurity, corruption, unemployment and lack of respect for human rights. iraq's 2012 oil revenue was over $80 billion, while 88% of the iraqi population lives below the poverty line. the union must be present and bring added value to the democratic construction of the country. the first is to support iraq's democratic transition by accompanying the country in its reforms. the trade and investment part of the agreement will develop lasting and mutually beneficial economic relations.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which recalls the political situation in zimbabwe, in the context of the implementation of the interim economic partnership agreement (epa). the economy is an important lever and can help to pacify conflicts, especially political ones, given the upcoming elections in this country.
in writing. the resolution, which enshrines an interim economic partnership agreement (epa) between the european union and the eastern and southern africa region, will give four african countries (madagascar, zimbabwe, the seychelles and mauritius) free access to the eu market. in exchange for the abolition of customs duties and quotas, which will make it easier for them to sell their goods within the european union (mainly coffee, sugar and tobacco), these countries will have to gradually open their markets to european union exports over a period of 15 years. i voted in favour of this resolution because it is the first agreement of its kind with an african region and will enable the countries concerned to promote their economies, their sustainable development and to reduce poverty. however, we also adopted a resolution expressing our concern about zimbabwe's respect for human rights and our doubts, therefore, about the validity of its participation in the agreement.
in writing. the aim of this text is to establish a legal situation compatible with the rules of the world trade organisation, replacing the unilateral trade preferences granted by the european union to imports from the acp countries. i voted in favour of this text, which is a step towards a future global agreement and includes a meeting clause for continuing negotiations.
in writing. this agreement will strengthen the institutions and economies of the countries of eastern and southern africa. our economic relations are bound to develop, strengthening the links between our two regions. i am particularly pleased that these states will be able to protect some of their products which they consider sensitive: the differences in development between our economies are significant, and we must ensure that both parties to the agreement benefit from this, without taking undue advantage of the opening up of our markets. to allow a balanced development of our partners, this agreement will make our relations clearer and stronger, to the benefit of a strengthened and calmer business and investment climate.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which improves the transparency of trade relations between the european union and the states of eastern and southern africa. as the text adopted today makes clear, these agreements must of course be conditional on respect for human rights and the rule of law, which are fundamental values for europeans. this text will also make it possible to promote our local products better by facilitating their export to the markets of eastern and southern africa. the european union is thus showing its support for the products of our lands and is respecting its commitments to defend diversity.
in writing. zimbabwe is one of the few signatories to the agreement. it is true that some violations of human rights are mentioned, both in the explanatory statement and in the resolution which is being discussed alongside this report. i am surprised, however, at the deafening silence of these texts on the corruption and violence of the mugabe regime, especially those suffered by certain ethnic minorities. but it is true that here we have not been moved by the armed expropriation and murder of white farmers who are just as much zimbabweans as their tormentors and persecutors. double standards, as usual when it comes to anti-white racism. i have also seen this house more reactive to measures which violate the principles you hold sacrosanct, such as competition, freedom of investment, wto rules... i am therefore surprised at your silence on the compulsory indigenisation of foreign companies in zimbabwe, requiring the sale of majority shares of their capital to zimbabweans, exclusively black zimbabweans. coming from any european or american country, this measure of national preference and reappropriation of enterprises by national economic actors would have raised an outcry. you are at best naive, at worst hypocritical, at best inconsistent.
in writing. the greens generally take a very critical stance on epas. i voted against the approval of this interim economic partnership agreement (epa) between the eu and the four acp countries in the eastern and southern africa (esa) region. the reasons are simple. this agreement leaves much to be desired. according to the cotonou agreement, sustainable development must be at the heart of epas. however, this epo does not meet that requirement. it does not contain any chapter on sustainable development, respect for labour standards and environmental protection. in addition, it contains many provisions which the acp countries consider to be contrary to their development needs and which they have expressly requested to be amended. it would also destroy efforts to move towards greater regional integration. finally, the fact that madagascar, the only ldc among the signatories, and zimbabwe are parties to this agreement also raises questions of the coherence of development policies, particularly in view of the human rights situation in their territory.
in writing. this report endorses the interim agreement establishing a framework for an economic partnership agreement between the eu and certain states in eastern and southern africa. it therefore endorses the blackmail on the east and south african states which have not accepted the agreement. it also endorses the 'date-set clause' obliging signatory states to sign a full free trade agreement with the eu in the coming years. i denounce the organized plunder of the countries of east and southern africa that this agreement organizes. i refuse to endorse the misery and dependency to which he condemns the people of this part of the world. the collapse of the malian state and its consequences should be a sufficient warning. but the blind free-market ideologues don't care. i vote against it.
in writing. the conclusion of a framework for economic partnership agreements between the european union and the states of eastern and southern africa has been postponed for several years, due to the opposition of many of the countries concerned. the commission has therefore opted for the conclusion of interim agreements with regional sub-groups of these countries. while réunion is in the geographical area covered by these agreements, the european commission has not worked with the elected representatives of réunion to ensure that this agreement really takes into account the expectations and interests of réunion. thus, while the economic partnership agreements are supposed to reduce poverty and bring about greater regional integration of the acp countries, their effectiveness is strongly contested by ngos and the countries concerned themselves. moreover, the agreement contains no mention of sustainable development, respect for workers' rights and trade union rights, nor does it contain any provision on human rights. i have therefore decided to vote against the motion for a resolution on the implementation of the interim epa between the european union and the states of east and southern africa.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it stresses the need to reduce state aid and to target it better. this will relieve pressure on public spending and avoid distortions of competition. the aim is to promote the transition to a knowledge-based economy as defined at european level in the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. state aid is a crucial instrument for our economies: it enables projects that are essential to our citizens to be brought to life. i'm talking about our transportation, our culture, and many other riches. i am therefore surprised that the european commission has opted for a simple consultation of parliament. the subject of state aid is crucial for our companies and our citizens. they must be modernised, as our competitiveness and quality of life depend on it. i therefore supported this resolution, so as not to risk widening europe's democratic deficit on such an important subject.
in writing. in may 2012, the european commission adopted a communication on the modernisation of state aid, presenting a rather ambitious reform agenda, in particular in the area of rescue and restructuring aid. this resolution, which i voted in favour of, was therefore very much expected. in a context of particular attention to reducing the public debts of the member states, it stressed the need to reduce and better target state aid, which should be better allocated to the development of services, knowledge and infrastructure rather than to one-off support for certain enterprises. the resolution also recalls that the primary task of state aid control is to guarantee a level playing field in the european single market.
in writing. this text supports the drastic limitation of state aid to avoid distortion of free competition in the eu internal market. it is not concerned for a single moment with the plight of citizens who are left to their own devices because of the lack of public support for their enterprises. he is concerned about the democratic control which parliament must exercise over the european commission only to check that it does not allow too much state aid. i am voting against this text and denouncing it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which recalls the tragedy of the recent fires in bangladesh. i also supported the amendments recalling and condemning the unacceptable working conditions to which many bangladeshis are subject, particularly in the case of the jeans factories.
in writing. the increasing number of tragic and repeated accidents in recent weeks and months is a testimony to the increasingly difficult working conditions of workers in the textile industry. the number of victims in bangladesh is particularly chilling. europe cannot shirk its own responsibilities. social dumping and practices which are tantamount to slavery are well known. the european union, the world's largest economy with 500 million consumers, can act. we need strong, legally binding decisions to change practices. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. in the face of such tragedies, the eu cannot remain silent, which is why i support the call for the establishment of a system of transnational legal cooperation between the european union and third countries that are signatories to bilateral trade agreements, so that victims of breaches of social or environmental legislation or of non-compliance by multinationals and their immediate subsidiaries with the principles of corporate social responsibility (csr) or fair trade practices can effectively bring cases before the courts of the country where the breach has occurred, and i support the establishment of international judicial procedures that allow, where appropriate, to sanction companies that break the law. even if corporate social responsibility is voluntary, we should be able to punish companies that, outside the eu, forget all the basic principles of human rights. it would also be good if the eu banned the import of products made by manual and mechanical sandblasting. sandblasting, a widespread practice in bangladesh, is very dangerous and even deadly for workers.
in writing. in bangladesh, negligence in terms of safety, overcrowding and (deplorable) working conditions have caused fires in textile factories, which have claimed the lives of more than 700 people since 2006. the extreme danger of these factories, many of which are working for international companies, is regularly denounced, unfortunately without any real consideration on the part of the public authorities or the contractors directly concerned. this situation, which is contrary to the most basic rights and obligations, must be constantly denounced, so that the operators in the supply chain and the state of bangladesh can ensure that the standards of the international labour organization (ilo) and the principles of corporate social responsibility (csr) are finally systematically applied by manufacturers. european companies have a duty to set an example in this respect. some, however, do not live up to the standards of good conduct that they themselves have adopted. the european union and the member states must firmly and resolutely remind them that they must take the necessary measures to ensure the protection of workers and not commit human rights violations.
in writing. the situation of textile workers in bangladesh is alarming today. in the last six years, more than 500 people have died in factory fires. on november 24th, 112 people were reported missing in the tazreen factory fire. the european union is directly concerned, as it remains the main recipient of bangladesh's textile exports. european companies must therefore play an important role in promoting and disseminating social and labour law standards, not only in bangladesh but throughout the world. i voted for this resolution because it is important that the bangladeshi authorities work with engineers, architects and emergency services to improve safety at work. it is also imperative that laws be respected by multinational companies and that sanctions be enforced. the european union has a role to play, particularly at the local level through the eu delegation and the eeas, which are already the contact points for bangladeshi workers.

in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons in the middle east. i welcome the emphasis on security issues in the region, in particular the situation in syria and iran. i also welcome the inclusion of all the actors involved in the process of achieving a middle east free of weapons of mass destruction.
in writing. non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction in the middle east must be a priority for the international community. it is therefore particularly regrettable that the conference on the establishment of a zone free of weapons of mass destruction in the middle east, originally scheduled for 2012, has been postponed indefinitely, jeopardising regional security and the highly desirable prospect of seeing this territorial space so fragile from successive wars finally denuclearized. we cannot continue in this dangerous status quo. the european union's mission is to put pressure on the countries of the region to return to the negotiating table. it is a vital issue for peace but also for the economic development of a region which urgently needs stability.
in writing. this resolution supports the establishment of a zone free of nuclear weapons and all other forms of weapons of mass destruction in the middle east. i strongly endorse this support. i regret, however, the partiality of the text, which expresses concern about the iranian nuclear programme but does not say a word about israel's military nuclear arsenal. this partiality makes the will expressed in this purely declarative text to work towards the establishment of a nuclear-weapon-free zone uncredible. i am voting for it, however, in support of the will expressed.
in writing. i voted in favour of this joint resolution which calls on the commission to undertake urgently a comparative study of the legislation on origin marking in force and applied in each wto member country. this will allow us to analyse the principles underlying them and assess their compatibility with wto rules in order to better protect our businesses too.
in writing. the european parliament voted in 2010 to make it clear how crucial it is for european consumers to have access to reliable and transparent information on the origin of the products they buy. in view of the reluctance of some member states to oppose such a measure, the legislative procedure was blocked, leading the european commission to decide unilaterally to withdraw the draft. we should be able to ensure that consumers are fully informed and traceable, in accordance with the wto rules. the eu's main partners and competitors, such as china, the united states and brazil, require it for goods imported from the eu. we must ensure that products entering the european market are traceable. it was the commission's duty, in the interests of good interinstitutional cooperation and respect for european citizens, to consult the european parliament before withdrawing its proposal.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on origin labelling. since the commission is considering withdrawing its proposal, the european parliament should reiterate its determination and call on the council and the commission to account for this. i believe that legislation on the marking of origin would be of considerable benefit to european consumers.
in writing. "made in" is a useful signature for consumers. this mark enables them to better guide their choices and can be a true sign of trust and quality. do all products have to bear such a marking? this is a matter for reflection, and all avenues must be explored. that is why i voted in favour of this text: it is unacceptable that the commission should withdraw its draft regulation, thus muzzling any constructive discussion. this is a useful reflection for our economy and for the confidence of citizens in the single market. the debate must be reopened, and quickly.
in writing. in 2005, the european commission proposed a european instrument to provide european consumers with full information on the origin of certain products from third countries. as early as 2010, the european parliament called for the swift implementation of such an instrument. but the proposal for a regulation has now been blocked in the council for two years for no apparent reason and the commission is now considering withdrawing its proposal, thus stopping the legislative procedure. the commission cannot withdraw its draft regulation on the indication of the country of origin of certain products imported from third countries without a valid justification without putting forward an alternative proposal in accordance with wto rules. the commission and the council must understand that the european union cannot be left behind in the field of origin labelling, even though other trading powers such as the united states, canada, brazil and china already have this effective instrument at their disposal. this is a step forward that europe needs to make in order to improve the competitiveness of its businesses, to ensure fair competition and to guarantee the protection of its consumers.
in writing. in october 2010, we felt, by a large majority in the european parliament, that it was crucial to enable european consumers to have access to reliable and transparent information on the origin of the products they buy. unfortunately, a number of member states opposed such a measure, thus blocking the legislative procedure. it was in this context that the european commission unilaterally decided to withdraw the project. while some of the new rules laid down by the world trade organisation may indeed require amendments, it seems to me that it is more necessary than ever to ensure full traceability and information for consumers. the european union's main partners, such as china, the united states and brazil, do not hesitate to demand these from goods imported from the union! in addition to the merits of such a system, by adopting this resolution we wish to denounce the method followed by the commission. in the spirit of good interinstitutional cooperation and in the interest of respecting european citizens, the commission should have consulted the european parliament before withdrawing its proposal. we therefore expect clear and reasoned answers from the commission on both the substance and the form.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution calling on the member states to agree on mandatory origin labelling and to adopt european legislation on the indication of the country of origin of products imported from third countries. the european union should have harmonised rules on the indication of the origin of imported products. compulsory origin marking systems have been introduced for certain products by wto third countries such as brazil, canada, china and the united states. common provisions are essential to improve competitiveness among wto member countries and to ensure a level playing field with partner countries that have adopted the marking of origin.
in writing. many countries, such as china, the united states and brazil, have mandatory origin marking systems for the import of goods such as textiles, shoes, jewellery and glassware from third countries. i find it quite extraordinary that the same obligation does not exist in europe for imported goods. european consumers should also be informed of the origin of the products they consume when they come from third countries in order to make informed choices. the commission had put a proposal to that effect on the table, but while the text has been under discussion in the council for several years, the commission announced its decision to withdraw it, considering that it was no longer compatible with wto rules. in this resolution, of which i am one of the co-signatories, we ask the commission to reconsider this decision or, failing that, to propose new legislation compatible with wto rules, and the council to take a decision on the text quickly so that the interinstitutional debate can continue. i hope we'll be heard.
in writing. i voted in favour of this joint resolution, recalling that mercosur is an important trading partner. however, any trade negotiations must give priority to sustainable development, job creation, social justice, the environment and cultural diversity in both the mercosur region and the union. we have asked the commission not to stick to its traditional model of free trade agreement but to design new forms of trade agreements adapted to the needs of its relations with specific partners.
in writing. in 2010, after several years of stagnation, the european union and mercosur officially relaunched trade negotiations with the aim of reaching a comprehensive and ambitious agreement that would consolidate and develop their respective economies. mercosur and the european union are two of the world's largest trading powers and must become privileged trading partners. the two regions must show good will to finally overcome their blockages and make real progress in the negotiations. we hope that the next mercosur-eu ministerial meeting, to be held at the end of january, will be an opportunity for both sides to relaunch the dialogue and to commit themselves to balanced trade objectives.
in writing. we expressed our views in a resolution on the progress of trade negotiations between the eu and its south american counterpart, mercosur. at this stage, negotiations are at a standstill, as there is a certain degree of mistrust on both sides. we have reiterated that trust is essential as the basis of any agreement. we must, for our part, verify that the mercosur area is still in the same frame of mind with regard to the conclusion of a trade agreement, which the protectionist practices of a number of countries on the latin american continent may make relativistic. it is also possible that the negotiating mandate given to the european commissioner for external trade in 1999 should be re-validated.
in writing. this resolution denounces the protectionism put in place by the progressive governments of the mercosur member states in the interests of their populations. it implicitly threatens the mercosur states with trade reprisals. it says nothing about the coup d'état in paraguay (which this parliament has not yet denounced, nor the coup in honduras). i vote against it.
in writing. this resolution, which i supported by voting in favour of, shows our hopes and our doubts about a possible regional agreement between the eu and mercosur. firstly, we hope that these negotiations will one day be concluded with a region which is experiencing tremendous economic growth and which has a population of over 800 million. and then there are the doubts: can the mercosur countries continue to negotiate this agreement with the eu while introducing protectionist measures? the negotiations, which, i remind you, have already been resumed after a long break, can they continue in this context of eroding trust between the two sides? the next eu-mercosur meeting will take place at the end of january, in parallel with the eu-celac summit in santiago, chile. i hope very much that it will help to answer these questions.

the fictitious rapporteurs and the services, on behalf of the commission, for their hard work in producing this excellent report. the adoption of these rules is important, since they are proposals to align legislative texts with the new rules of the lisbon treaty on delegated and implementing powers. these are the first to be adopted in the field of agriculture and rural development. there has been very good cooperation between parliament, the council and the commission and this has created the conditions for adopting these proposals at first reading. the adoption of the texts is important because it makes it possible to apply improved and simplified provisions to farmers in the outermost regions and the smaller aegean islands. the texts also provide for greater budgetary flexibility between the two parts of the programmes, namely the specific supply arrangements and measures to support local production, for those member states which need it. moreover, as regards the posei scheme, the entry into force of the new regulation will allow member states to grant additional aid to banana producers in the outermost regions in 2013 to help them strengthen the sector, making it more competitive and sustainable in the face of changing market conditions. this is important, given the fragile socioeconomic fabric of these regions, which are often very heavily dependent on the banana sector, which is also suffering from a lack of competitiveness. the new regulation also provides that in any analysis, study or evaluation carried out by the commission in the context of trade itself has made commitments. she'll hold them. at the same time, we must, collectively and constantly, adjust our objectives to the realities of the economic situation. the next step we must take is the coordination of national economic policies. it is necessary to redress imbalances. there are countries with surpluses and high competitiveness, others with deficits and work to be done. the countries in the first situation must boost their domestic demand so that the others can at some point experience a return to activity. in the same way, we must reflect on the place of our currency, the euro, in the world. it cannot fluctuate with market sentiment. a currency area must have an exchange rate policy, otherwise it is forced to use a parity which does not correspond to the real state of its economy. the aim here is not to assign an objective to the european central bank, which is independent, from outside, but to initiate the necessary reform of the international monetary system, otherwise it would be tantamount to asking countries to make efforts to improve their competitiveness, which would be annihilated by the appreciation of the euro. the time has come to launch the great project of deepening economic and monetary union. france is ready. it has two principles: integration and solidarity. integration is the definition of shared objectives, it is the harmonization of fiscal policies. integration is structural reforms to make our economies stronger, but also common policies on infrastructure and research. integration is our new financial instrument for launching innovative projects in the fields of new technologies, renewable energy, energy transition and ecology. since we are for integration, we are for solidarity because one cannot exist without the other. solidarity is not just a transfer between european nations, solidarity is a social ambition. it is to guarantee every young european a job or training at the end of his studies, by strengthening exchanges between member states. solidarity means fighting unemployment, particularly in the areas where it is most acute. this is the challenge of the globalisation adjustment fund. solidarity is about career transitions, it is about accompanying employees throughout their career, enabling them to retain their rights to retirement, unemployment insurance, social security when they change jobs and sometimes even countries. solidarity is about opening the minimum wage. solidarity is also a financial instrument, through new resources, through the financial transaction tax, through everything that can make it possible to imagine the future together. the european parliament has led the way in this respect. you have, beyond political sensitivities, launched the idea of joint borrowing. i do not dare to speak of eurobonds, but you have imagined what the very term integration and solidarity could be. the debate on the european financial framework must be seen in this light. i want to open it right in front of you. we are all aware of the difficulties involved in this negotiation. some want cuts, others - sometimes the same people - want guarantees on their checks or discounts. most countries are interested in one part of the european budget but not the other... my position is simply this: save money, yes, but not weaken the economy! (applause) i would like to thank the position of france is therefore based on four principles. the first principle is a level of spending that preserves the common policies. first, cohesion policy, which finances the necessary investments, not only for the beneficiary countries, but for the whole of europe, which benefits from it in terms of growth. the common policy is the agricultural policy, which makes it possible to strengthen an agro-food industry which is valuable to the european union, but which must also respect the environment. direct aid and rural development are therefore complementary. i do not oppose the two policies, as is convenient to do: cohesion policy versus agricultural policy. we must keep the foundation of european policies, otherwise how can we build? my second principle is that the budget, the financial framework to be proposed, must extend the growth pact adopted last june, which means increasing the funds earmarked for innovation, infrastructure and new energy sources. because where would be the coherence of having defined a growth pact in june and then making a deflation pact throughout the european financial framework? my third principle is that the budget must support the most fragile and vulnerable europeans, hence the challenge of the programme of aid to the poorest, which must not only be preserved but properly funded. in writing. i voted in favour of this text which reforms the advantages granted to several greek islands in the aegean sea. given their remoteness, the geographical location of these islands increases costs and complicates the supply of foodstuffs. the aim here is therefore to help compensate for these disadvantages and to strengthen the cohesion of the territory.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr papastamkos. it stressed the need for a systematic approach, a thorough analysis of existing needs and a clear strategy to address the structural weaknesses of agriculture in the aegean islands. the rapporteur calls for a review of these, incorporating measures to protect the environment, increase the agricultural dimension of tourism and strengthen agricultural infrastructure in the region.
in writing. the emphasis in this report on the transport of agricultural products from the smaller aegean islands seems to me particularly important: their insularity is a strength but can also be a handicap. the eu must continue to demonstrate its commitment to supporting these regions, to ensure genuine cohesion between our territories while safeguarding their diversity.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal from the european commission on specific measures in the field of agriculture for the aegean islands, as i considered that it would make it possible to bring the existing legal provisions on this subject into line with the new provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union in a harmonious and streamlined manner. in addition to the traditional constraints on these islands (territorial dispersion, remoteness and isolation), the commission and parliament have recognized that the increase in herd and population pressure has led to greater basic needs. this resolution will therefore increase by 20% the share of budget appropriations allocated to greece under the special supply arrangements, without any upward revision of the overall budget allocated to this scheme.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on specific measures in the field of agriculture for the smaller aegean islands. this report provides for adjustments to the measures allocated under the common agricultural policy, which compensate for the remoteness and fragmentation of the aegean islands, as regards the production, processing and marketing of certain products and their supply of raw materials.
in writing. in the early 1990s, the european union adopted specific measures to support agriculture in the eu's outermost regions (the french overseas departments, the canary islands, the azores and madeira) to address the special situation of these regions. i voted in favour of this text, which modernises the two main instruments: the specific supply arrangements (ssa), which are a system of compensation for the additional costs caused by the insularity and remoteness of the regions concerned, and the measures in favour of local agricultural products (mfpl), which are designed to develop local agricultural production and the supply of agricultural products.
in writing. the programme of specific options for the remote and insularity of the outermost regions (posei) was created in 1991 to provide support to the french overseas departments and was extended the following year to cover the portuguese and spanish outermost regions. the proposal also aims to simplify and clarify the regulation. the report by my colleague mr adrover, which i supported, calls on the member states to improve the programming of support measures for local products wherever possible. the rapporteur also believes that it would be desirable for the european union to strengthen border controls on imports from third countries in order to avoid unfair competition with local products.
in writing. the many economic partnership agreements concluded between the acp countries and the european union reduce or even abolish customs duties on products originating in the signatory countries entering the union, creating a de facto loss of competitiveness for the eu's outermost regions. i therefore voted in favour of maintaining the specific agricultural measures for these regions and for a new allocation of 40 million to support banana producers in the french overseas departments, madeira, the azores and the canary islands. the diversity of crops in the ors is difficult, if not impossible, and therefore only financial support will enable them to remain competitive with latin american producers.
in writing. i support the adoption of this regulation, which will simplify and improve the system of aid for agriculture and production in the outermost regions, which benefits 6 (soon 7 with mayotte) french overseas departments. these territories are the basis of our wealth, our diversity and our radiance: we have a duty to protect them, taking into account the difficulties associated with their insularity or remoteness. the aid scheme allows the maintenance of activity in sectors whose viability would otherwise be threatened. the report stresses the need to ensure that our outermost territories do not suffer from unfair competition due to lower phytosanitary and veterinary standards on products imported from third countries. i support that ambition.
in writing. the outermost regions are hard hit by the economic crisis and the labour market situation is particularly alarming, with a very high unemployment rate: 23.8% in guadeloupe, 28.7% in the canary islands, 28.9% in réunion (eurostat 2009-2010), and an even more worrying youth unemployment rate of up to 60%. it is therefore crucial that the eu provides increased support to local producers. all too often, the latter are dependent on a small number of products, mainly sugar cane, rum, bananas, tomatoes, potatoes and horticulture. in addition, they are weakened by close competition from regions with less stringent social, environmental and health standards than in the european union. with posei, the european union can thus defend the diversity of its agricultural production while maintaining the economic dynamism of the regions most affected by the crisis.
in writing. this report is about the specific programme for agricultural aid to the overseas regions (posei programme). the european parliament has significantly improved the text originally proposed by the european commission. references are made to climate resilience, sustainable production methods (land rotation versus monoculture), reducing the excessive use of fertilisers, local production and short-circuits. the report also calls on the european commission to carry out impact studies in advance of any trade agreement negotiations that would have consequences for farming offshore. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. more than simply amending regulation (ec) no 247/2006 on aid to the outermost regions to clarify its interpretation, this commission proposal introduced the necessary legislative changes in the light of the problems recently identified in the implementation of the scheme. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which will make it possible, in particular, to increase by 20% the ceilings for rsa in france and portugal, to make rsa conditional on the absence of any obstacle to the development of local production or, for the french overseas departments, to re-ship products processed from raw materials from rsa without having to reimburse the advantage.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on specific measures in the field of agriculture for the outermost regions of the union. this report provides for adjustments to the posei measures of the common agricultural policy, which compensate for the additional cost of transporting certain agricultural products to remote areas of small size, difficult terrain or climate. the measures also include aid for the development of local production.
in writing. this report proposes to compensate for the losses that banana producers in our so-called 'outermost' regions suffer as a result of the free trade agreements in favour of chiquita and other large mercenary producers in latin america. it also allows the french overseas departments to re-ship products processed using raw materials which have benefited from the specific supply arrangements without reimbursement of the advantage granted. it proposes a significant increase in the annual funding granted to the doms. that is why i support this text. i would like to point out that the 'rupeization' of new territories, such as mayotte, is not accompanied by additional allocations, as the rapporteurs have advocated. the fact that the french government has given in on this point is unacceptable. i also regret that no conditions relating to employment, farm size and environmental considerations are mentioned in the text. i abstain in order to encourage the support that this report can provide for workers in the overseas regions, but i denounce the fact that they are so little taken into account, both in the free trade agreements and in this text.
in writing. i voted for this report, as negotiated between the european parliament and endorsed by the council, because it shows progress for the ors. i welcome the fact that article 349 has been redefined, thanks to the european parliament and the work of the members of the opr, as the legal basis for posei. this was symbolic, since posei was the first programme created by the eu to respond to the specific nature of the outermost regions and the endogenous constraints on their farmers. i am glad that we have succeeded in increasing the objectives of posei from two to three. from now on, one objective will be to compensate for the additional costs of agricultural production, a second will be to maintain the competitiveness of the traditional agricultural sectors (cane, banana), and a third will be to develop and maintain in the long term the diversification sectors (all other agricultural sectors). however, while we can be pleased with the progress made in the new posei, agriculture in the ors also depends on the cap and the trade agreements signed by the european union, and what is consolidated on the one hand must not be withdrawn on the other.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the agricultural sector in the outermost regions (ors) needs to be strengthened. administrative simplification of the programme of specific options for remote and insularity (posei) is also needed to achieve greater coherence. the geographical remoteness of the outermost regions remains a handicap and makes them vulnerable to commercial competition from third countries. specific measures are essential to encourage local production in the outermost regions and to diversify production while maintaining quality. this development must be accompanied by respect for the environment and the preservation of the biodiversity of these regions. measures concerning the banana sector are also essential to strengthen their competitiveness in the face of the gradual reduction of customs duties for latin american countries. finally, there is an urgent need to consolidate veterinary and phytosanitary standards in the face of the introduction of pests into the octs during imports from third countries. the union should ensure the monitoring of the implementation of these specific measures.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to mobilise new european funding to overcome market failures that are hampering the growth of smes. the text proposes an action plan including a series of policies to facilitate access to finance for europe's 23 million smes and thus make a significant contribution to growth.
in writing. i voted in favour of the philippe de backer report, which agrees that the economic success, excellence and cohesion of the european union will depend to a large extent on sustainable growth and job creation which rely on smes. it is therefore essential to facilitate access to finance for smes. to this end, several measures have been established, including the demand for professionalisation of the sector in the face of a lack of knowledge and the improvement of cooperation and exchange of information between smes and creditors, allowing a more regular monitoring of the financial situation of the sme.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the european commission's action plan to facilitate access to finance for smes. i believe that the success of the european economy depends on the ability of small and mediumsized enterprises to realize their full growth potential. i welcome the proposed measures to increase the visibility of smes to investors and to encourage the exchange of good practice. i also support the rapporteur's recommendations, particularly with regard to reducing the administrative burden on smes.
in writing. smes account for more than 98% of our businesses and almost 7 out of 10 jobs. they alone account for almost 85% of our job creation. so it is obvious for our jobs and competitiveness: entrepreneurs must be encouraged and supported, and the question of funding them must become a priority. i welcome the fact that this text encourages the spirit of enterprise and calls for a second chance for entrepreneurs. these are the positions i have defended in the drafting of this text and i will continue to advocate them.
in writing. there are now 23 million small and medium-sized enterprises in the european union, accounting for 75% of private sector employment. as sources of innovation and growth, smes are the backbone of the union's economic activity. but paradoxically, they have more difficulty than large companies in accessing finance, especially bank loans, to develop new projects or internationalise their activities. it is essential that smes can benefit from easier borrowing and more flexible banking rules, adapted to their needs, for example through the strengthening of local banking networks. banks and other financial institutions need to improve their communication with entrepreneurs so that they are better able to know their repayment possibilities. finally, it is up to the commission to act decisively to ensure that all new regulations limit the administrative burden imposed on smes.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which aims to facilitate access to finance for smes. this text is therefore a good way of supporting smes, which remain the main drivers of jobs and growth. it is only natural that banks, which benefited from public aid or the support of the european central bank during the financial crisis, should be obliged to facilitate the obtaining of loans to smes. supporting this network of smes is to support the attractiveness and economic development of our territories. by adopting this text, parliament is showing that its role is to represent the interests of our citizens and economic operators by making their voices heard in the institutions.
in writing. smes account for 98% of enterprises and 67% of employment in the european union. that is to say, the central role they play in the economic and social fabric of our countries. but what we take away from this report is that the banks are not doing, or are doing poorly, their job of financing the economy, despite the hundreds of billions invested in public funds in their perpetual bailouts. this attitude is probably not without consequences for the survival of smes. the problem with smes is that they are praised for their importance, but they die in the most complete indifference. the press is only interested in the plans for mass layoffs: petroplus, goodyear, psa, arcelor, whose workers will be here tomorrow to protest mr. mittal's amoral attitude. they are wrong to come from elsewhere: all you have to offer them is a false compassion and your blind belief in economic principles which are the very cause of their dismissal. a very recent study shows that the vast majority of factory closures in france since 2009 have been small businesses, with an average of 70 jobs lost per closed unit. the "small" waves of redundancies, which are not often mentioned, are a great social and human tragedy for those who suffer them.
in writing. smes are essential to the health of the european economy, and are a major pillar of it. they are the ones who create jobs, drive growth, support innovation and enable the development of our territories. we saw in the crisis that states with a strong network of smes were better able to withstand the crisis. i therefore voted in favour of this report because it provides tools to support european smes and facilitate their access to finance. supporting our european smes is essential if we are to achieve a lasting return to growth, a lasting reduction in unemployment and a continued focus on creativity and innovation in the eu.
in writing. i welcome the position taken by the european parliament on access to finance for smes, which must be facilitated and encouraged. the instruments and the ideas are there. there are now 23 million smes in europe, representing 99% of the total entrepreneurial fabric in the eu, and two thirds of private sector jobs. in times of crisis, entrepreneurship must be fostered, as smes are the engine of growth in europe. this is something we need to look at actively, and the european parliament's proposals seem to me to be going in the right direction: promoting access to venture capital, removing regulatory and tax barriers, allowing for a more flexible state aid policy, supporting entrepreneurs in setting up their projects... the heterogeneous practices in the member states to enable smes to access finance impose costs which are not in the collective interest of the union's member states. we are facing tough international competition, and that is why we must be able to better protect our companies and help them to expand in foreign markets.
