president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i would like to thank mr groote for his question. the council is working on the european union position for this conference of the parties, cop 16, and will adopt a decision ahead of the conference. parliament will, of course, be informed of that decision. the presidency will make sure that at cop 16 in march in bangkok, as at previous conferences of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), the eu member states act jointly to defend the agreed position of the union and that they therefore speak with one voice. this year, cites celebrates 40 years of existence. during these years, the convention has proved itself to be an important instrument against over-exploitation of our natural resources. constant discussion and improvement of its implementation have shown many times that it is possible to have sustainable trade and also to attain the objectives of the convention if all parties apply the rules and accept necessary restrictions. as usual, the agenda for this conference covers many issues, from strategic questions to enforcement, compliance and conservation. each issue involves a different degree of complexity and, at times, may lead to controversy. the future effectiveness of cites and its role in a global, complex and regulated world will be influenced by decisions on many specific items. the decisions taken, whether on plant or animal species, will show whether cites parties are prepared to find acceptable solutions between different countries and views, between conservation needs and economic justification. we have always maintained that any amendments to the cites appendices should be based on the conservation status of the species concerned and the listing criteria developed by cites. they should, furthermore, take account of the contribution that cites controls can make to improving conservation status, minimise unnecessary administrative burdens and ensure that the parties’ resources are directed towards issues of real conservation concern. it is not by chance that several proposals touch the question of livelihoods. the eu and its member states have always tried to find a way forward in cooperation with other parties, especially those who are not in the position of having sufficient resources for the satisfactory implementation of cites. i am hopeful that other parties will share this view. however, we also go to bangkok having put a number of important proposals on the table. as at previous cops, we will again try to ensure the enhanced protection status of sharks. we have also tabled proposals on the transparency of voting and on conflicts of interest, both of which are essentially about increasing transparency. transparency should be at the heart of the development of conservation policies and practices within the convention, for a number of reasons. firstly, the use of secret ballots can cast doubts on the basis on which decisions are made within cites. indeed, it becomes impossible to demonstrate that such decisions are based on the use of the agreed scientific criteria. secondly, the proposals seek to translate within cites some of the outcomes of the rio+20 summit last year with regard to the kind of institutions we want in order to achieve sustainable development. finally, we remain convinced that undertaking specific steps to move such governance reforms forward will not only result in tangible benefits in terms of increased protection and better management practices, but will also sustain and reinforce the spirit of partnership amongst parties, in the realisation of a common objective. we are, of course, particularly encouraged by the strong and consistent support of the european parliament in this respect. the presidency, together with the commission and the member states, is determined to play an active role in ensuring that cites continues to be an effective tool, in order to attain its two main objectives: conservation and sustainable management of our natural resources. it is our intention to engage with other parties not only in promoting our proposals but also in looking for acceptable solutions that encompass the need for species conservation and, at the same time, respect for the means of subsistence of populations with fewer or insufficient resources. we are therefore prepared to conduct the upcoming deliberations in a spirit of cooperation, mutual understanding and shared interest in the protection of species threatened by trade, in order to maintain a diverse environment for our future generations.
member of the commission. − mr president, as matthias groote said, this is prime time. to begin with i would like add something which is basically connected with the debate on the european semester which you have just held. it is my dream that the environment commissioner will some day be part of the debate on the european semester, because you will certainly recall that in the treaty – i think it is chapter 3 – it says that sustainable development consists of three pillars. these are the economic, social and environmental pillars, and the european semester is definitely the story of sustainable development for europe in the future. but focusing now on cites (convention on international trade in endangered species), i would first like to thank parliament and mr groote in particular for their interest and involvement with a view to the next cites cop (conference of the parties). when the parties to the convention meet in bangkok in march, significant issues will be at stake. cites is a key international treaty for the regulation of trade in endangered species. it is widely seen as a very effective tool for the protection of biodiversity and promotion of sustainable trade. it has a direct impact on trade, due to the legally binding nature of its decisions and its robust compliance tools. the rio+20 conference also recognised its importance. the european union has been a leading force within cites in terms of tabling proposals to extend its scope and strengthening its implementation. the european union has been at the forefront of promoting a fully science-based approach within cites and is the main donor to the secretariat for the implementation of the convention. as you know, we have tabled a draft council decision containing detailed positions on all of the proposals put forward for this cop. as you have heard, discussions in the council have started, and it appears that on the vast majority of issues we will easily find common ground. we have also started outreach to third countries and will intensify these efforts in the remaining weeks leading up to the cop. i am pleased to say that this time round the european union will team up with other countries when tabling proposals for listing, in particular with latin american countries on some marine species. let me now set out what priorities the european union should pursue at this meeting. first, making sure that the convention is fully used for the protection of marine species which are threatened by international trade. marine species deserve the same level of protection as terrestrial species, and we think that cites can have a very important role to play when this is justified. this is why the european union has proposed listing one shark species (porbeagle) in appendix 2 of cites and it is co-sponsoring the proposal by brazil and latin and central american countries to list three hammerhead shark species also in appendix 2. those sharks are particularly vulnerable to overfishing. they are caught in very large numbers for international trade, notably for their fins but in some cases also for their meat. today no clear regime exists to ensure that such trade is sustainable. a cites listing is more justified than ever. the upcoming meeting is also the occasion to finally make progress on the definition of ‘introduction from the sea’, which is about the responsibility of flag states when chartering is involved. the commission has proposed a solution to this issue, taking full account of the need to fight against illegal fishing, and we are working hard with member states to find common ground for cop 16. second, making the convention more transparent. at the last cop, most decisions on controversial issues – marine listing or ivory trade, for example – were taken through secret ballots. today if temporary parties so decide, the decision is voted upon secretly. we propose to change that. in our view, requests to have a secret ballot vote need to be supported by a majority. this would put cites more in line with what one expects of an international convention on the environment in the 21st century. furthermore, we want to introduce a clear policy on conflict of interest in the scientific committees set up under the cites convention. there are currently no provisions at all on this point so we need to ensure that these committees base their deliberations on sound scientific reasoning only. finally, our third priority is implementation and enforcement. we should not look for new listings or delisting proposals unless this is justified on the basis of scientific criteria. what we do need is that the provisions of the cites convention are properly implemented. failure to comply with cites requirements does not only result in biodiversity loss but also represents a loss of income for legally operating actors and for government authorities. wildlife trafficking is more and more associated with transnational organised crime. this is especially the case of illegal trade in ivory and rhinoceros horns which is at its highest level in a decade. we believe that the cop should focus on the most effective ways and means to address these problems. enforcement needs to be made a priority in range states, transit countries and countries of final destination. if necessary we should use all measures foreseen within the cites framework to address persistent failures to take priority measures against poaching or illegal trade. to strengthen international cooperation and capacity building the commission supports interpol with almost eur 2 million to strengthen its efforts to combat wildlife crime. a further eur 2 million will be used to prolong our support to the monitoring of the illegal killing of elephants, the so-called mike programme, which is a unique mechanism which monitors and addresses elephant poaching across the african continent. there are many other important items on the agenda of the next cop. we will define our position on these on the basis of the criteria agreed by the cites parties, which rely on science and the need to convince local populations to participate in the protection of wildlife so that it can actually be successful. let me assure you that the commission will do its utmost for the european union to arrive in bangkok with a well-coordinated position also in cooperation, of course, with the presidency, in order for us to pull our full weight at this important conference. some of the issues, such as polar bears, which were also addressed in the opening remarks by mr groote, i will touch upon in my conclusions.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora plays a central role in the conservation of biodiversity. cites shows that environmental requirements can be combined without compromising economic needs. in the face of the collapse of biodiversity on all continents, it is urgent to ensure that the 16th conference of the parties, to be held in bangkok in march, is up to the challenge. it is essential that the decision-making process be more transparent. we can no longer afford to let cites be held hostage to vested interests when the survival of iconic species is at stake. any change in the classification of a species between appendices must be based on several independent scientific studies. these changes cannot, under any circumstances, be the result of approximations or the result of economic or popular pressures. in times of economic crisis, the temptation to relax the rules can be strong, commissioner. we will not tolerate it! the european union must maintain its leading role in the conservation of biodiversity and, above all, train its partners in this direction. our commitment to cites is absolute and our vigilance will be unwavering.

socialist party and the epp group. this is proof that corporate social responsibility has become a matter of course for everyone. the implementation of csr must therefore be promoted at several levels, both european and national. at european level, parliament will support all initiatives of the european commission to promote csr in companies of all sizes. multinational companies must lead by example and act in a socially responsible manner, even in third countries where they have subsidiaries and subcontractors. smes, as job creators, need to be effectively supported in communicating their csr efforts, so that csr is no longer seen as an additional administrative burden. the european union also has a role to play in gathering and analysing measurable social criteria which will allow a framework of good practice in social standards to be drawn up. unlike environmental standards, social standards are not measurable scientifically. a social standard applied in a small or large company, in the construction or textile sector, will not have the same impact at all. secondly, at national level, member states must also promote csr through legal taxation and the creation of numerous corporate rating agencies. for several years now i have been campaigning for csr to have a social dimension equal to or greater than its environmental component. today it is certainly investors, but above all our fellow citizens, who want to be able to identify companies which are working to improve their working conditions and their environment. these virtuous enterprises deserve recognition, identification by means of a label, a label, a distinctive sign. csr is not a matter of the will or the obligation of business leaders, it is above all a matter of political will.
for the greens/efa group mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would simply like to return to two points which were not supported by the committee on foreign affairs in its opinion and which have only been partially introduced in the reports under discussion today, although i believe they are absolutely fundamental. first, csr can become an effective tool for monitoring the activities of enterprises and this monitoring is essential to the achievement of the commission's objectives of building a more inclusive society and initiating a transition towards a sustainable economy. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information it receives from the public, and it is hoped that the commission will be able to take this into account in its future work. secondly, it is essential that when companies or subsidiaries they control commit violations in third countries, they can be held responsible for these violations in their home countries and not only, as the current wording suggests, for the worst violations of fundamental rights.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, our report to the committee on employment and social affairs calls for the principle of corporate social responsibility to be applied at every stage of the production chain, both for subsidiaries and for suppliers. it also recommends that firms should provide more systematic information on their social and environmental activities. but he avoids mentioning the most important point for us, namely the urgency of making csr legally binding without a binding legislative framework. companies are not exposed to any sanctions and are randomly tracking their social and environmental responsibility. my amendments, which refer, more or less, to the progressive introduction of binding standards, mandatory measures or effective control mechanisms in the field of csr, have not been taken into account. we, the environmentalists, therefore consider this report to be too weak, as does the commission's method of communicating the 2011-2014 csr strategy. since its 2002 communication, the european commission has made fewer and fewer commitments in this area. we cannot ignore this backsliding of the commission. that is why our group will abstain on this report from the committee on employment and social affairs. finally, it is not appropriate to have two reports from two different parliamentary committees on the same subject. this creates confusion and sometimes leads to conflicting positions. in future, let us ensure that we have a consistent distribution of our reports in the european parliament.

in writing. the european parliament voted in favour of the revision of the 1989 directive on the transparency of pricing procedures for medicinal products. this text introduces new elements to facilitate effective and practical implementation of deadlines. the aim is to ensure that a realistic common framework can be respected within the union as regards the time limits for fixing the price and reimbursement of medicines, while enhancing transparency. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i support the report by mrs parvanova, who shares the view that the overall objective of the proposal is to update the existing legislative framework in order to clarify the procedural obligations of the member states and to ensure the proper functioning of the single market.
in writing. the european parliament has today delivered its opinion on the revision of the 1989 directive on the pricing of medicinal products. the text lays down the procedures to be followed for fixing the selling price and the conditions for reimbursement of medicinal products. the most controversial point was the introduction of new processing times for applications which were considerably shortened, unrealistic and accompanied by a clause of tacit acceptance of the price requested by the laboratory in case of non-compliance with the deadlines. such a measure is neither proportionate nor in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity! we were able to extend the time limits, which makes the text acceptable, but the tacit acceptance clause was only removed for requests for price increases, which is regrettable, even if the main thing is that the authorities have the necessary time.
in writing. while the european union has a uniform market in terms of the free movement of workers, goods and capital, there are still huge differences between member states in terms of the functioning of health and reimbursement systems, policies that are the responsibility of the member states. for example, some drugs are now reimbursed after 700 days in some states. without encroaching on the exclusive competence of the member states to set prices and reimburse medicines, it is necessary to provide for minimum rules to encourage the production of medicines, the entry of generic medicines onto the market and the research and development of new medicines in order to make medical treatment affordable for all european citizens.
in writing. a perfect example of social europe! while it is absolutely not within its competence, the european union will be able to limit and control the ability of states to decide on the prices of medicines and all the social and health policy that goes with it. with a big beneficiary: the pharmaceutical industry. and the big losers are the patients and the social security systems! several member states expressed concern about this abuse of power and the clear violation of the principle of subsidiarity by this text. it is a pity that not all national parliaments have played their role as guardians of this principle. it is also a pity that the majority of this parliament has decided to reject the legal basis which recognises the responsibility of the states for the management of health services and the resources allocated to them, in favour of the one which favours the free movement of goods. it's a symbol of something.
in writing. i am very interested in public health, which is generally one of the major concerns of european citizens. the mediator and the third generation pill scandals, more recently, have increased public distrust of government authorities and regulatory agencies, which are seen as ineffective in risk prevention and unresponsive in decision-making. the member states and the european commission must be more vigilant in ensuring a high level of public health, but they must also encourage all measures and initiatives which enable pharmaceutical research to produce innovative medicines. transparency in the measures governing the pricing of medicines is also a necessary measure, as it avoids unfair practices and facilitates rapid access for patients to these innovative medicines. all efforts by the member states to shorten the time limit for admission to reimbursement and for fixing prices should therefore be encouraged.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which i thought was a good compromise between the commission's original proposal and the member states' competence to set prices and reimburse medicines. the commission's intention was to introduce minimum procedural requirements in this area, in particular to facilitate access to affordable treatments for all patients in the european union. the commission proposed, for example, that time limits be introduced for fixing the price and reimbursement of medicines. the amendments adopted by parliament have extended and simplified these new deadlines, which will now be 30 days for generic medicines and 90 days for other medicines.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft directive to increase the transparency of measures governing the pricing of medicinal products for human use. the time limit for a member state to decide on the price and reimbursement of generic medicines has been reduced to 60 days in order to improve the availability of these products. the proposal for a directive should guarantee minimum conditions of transparency throughout the european union.
in writing. according to the european commission, generic medicines are on average 40% cheaper than original brand products. companies are using various means to extend the period during which they can market their products exclusively, without competition from generics, to the detriment of patients and national social security systems. action is needed to remedy this situation and i support this legislative resolution which sets a 60-day deadline for the pricing and reimbursement of generic medicines, with a view to speeding up the availability of these products. in addition, the competent authorities in the member states will have to make public the names and declarations of interest of all their experts and members, in order to ensure the transparency and integrity of their decision-making process, and will have to publish, at least once a year, a list of medicines covered by their public health insurance system together with their price. these provisions seem to me to be real progress and i hope that the negotiations which are about to begin with the council will be concluded as soon as possible in order to allow a rapid adoption of the text.
in writing. this report deals with the marketing authorisation of a medicinal product before it is marketed. the rules in place are intended to ensure that the quality, safety and efficacy of medicines are properly assessed before they are given to patients. the evaluation is mainly the responsibility of the member states, but certain basic conditions of transparency must be met at european level, in particular the measures concerning the fixing of prices and reimbursement of medicines, the time limit for which is shortened here. but under the guise of transparency, the report gives even more power to the pharmaceutical industry, leaving them free to market their products at whatever price they want when the authorities do not take any decisions within the considerably shortened time limits. the objective of rapidly making new treatments available cannot be achieved at the expense of the sick or the already fragile budgetary balance of public health insurance systems. i therefore opposed this text, as did all the members of my group.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union has once again proved to us, through the commission's proposals for reform of the common fisheries policy, that it is aware of the importance of restoring the fish stocks on which the future of our fishermen depends. what's important is that this consciousness is shared. i think it would be absurd to oppose those who would have been for the reconstitution and others who would have been against it. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left behind. it is important to remember that the pillar of sustainable development has three pillars. the environmental pillar, of course, but also the economic pillar and the social pillar. the latter two are the forgotten ones of history. that is why i voted in favour of amendment no 15, which would have allowed a margin of tolerance to be set in the area of the ban on dumping. the total ban on discards is an unrealistic measure and, above all, it seems to me to be unworkable, which shows a lack of awareness of the realities of the fishing sector. it will put a considerable number of fishing businesses and jobs at risk at a time when unemployment in the european union is already at historically high levels. the objectives are the same for everyone, from the legislator to the fisherman, which is why the legislator cannot offer a sustainable future to the fisherman if it is opposed to his present.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which reforms one of the major policies of the european union. the text, which was supported by a large majority in parliament, updates the european fisheries framework for the coming years. for the first time, environmental issues are fully taken into account, and i am pleased about that. particular attention has been paid to the sustainability of the resource by ensuring that stocks can be renewed. however, i would have liked to see some adjustments to this report to facilitate the implementation of these rules.
in writing. both for the preservation of stocks and for the safeguarding of jobs in the medium and long term, the reform of the cfp was highly anticipated. the good philosophy that is now emerging from this common policy clearly shows a path towards a more sustainable fisheries in europe. that's great news. the criteria for the annual renewal of stocks are designed to ensure the survival of the fisheries. traditional fishing techniques are recognised and will be preserved. conserving fish stocks and ending discards - more than a quarter of catches are wasted each year - are crucial for the future of small-scale, artisanal and coastal fishing. for france, which is, as we will recall, europe's leading maritime interface, these are considerable steps forward, and should be welcomed as such. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common fisheries policy' to cover the whole of the eu.
in writing. the report by ulrike rodust sets out a total ban on discards. i have refused to vote on this report because after consulting the fisheries sector it is clear that it is difficult to put such a rule in place. it would be more sensible to provide for a more flexible timetable for different species. even if a total ban is a long-term goal, it is not achievable in the short term for the professionals.
in writing. i voted against the report on the reform of the cfp to express my support for french fishermen. the epp wanted to play an active part in the reform, in particular by voting in favour of amendment no 297, which respects the principle of the landing obligation by arranging it in such a way as to enable the fisheries sector to adapt to this measure. unfortunately, this amendment was not adopted. the reform of the cfp has important social consequences for fishermen. it therefore deserves special attention to support this already highly fragile sector.
in writing. i voted against the rodust report on the common fisheries policy. after three years of work in the parliamentary committee, there is one essential point which i cannot accept in this reform. this is the strict obligation to land all catches with a time limit that is too tight and not applicable today. this is a dogmatic measure, which is why i tabled a compromise amendment which proposed that the landing obligation be made more flexible and realistic. unfortunately, it was rejected, which motivated my opposition. i am, however, pleased that the european commission has proposed the abolition of transferable fishing concessions. as the author of the amendment to abolish these monetised fishing rights, i am pleased that my colleagues in parliament followed my proposal, which was the only reasonable one. the abandonment of transferable fishing concessions remains a significant victory, as it avoids the disappearance of our european fishing model.
in writing. while 65% of european seafood consumption is imported, the eu has a responsibility to do everything possible to prevent the offshoring of our food production capacity. the compulsory landing of all discards risks destroying our fishing enterprises and the most fragile jobs, particularly in the multispecies fisheries. this text should have respected the balance between the necessary renewal of the resource and the sustainability of european fisheries activities which contribute to our food self-sufficiency.
in writing. today, europe's fish stocks, particularly in the atlantic and the mediterranean, are threatened by overfishing. with over 350 000 europeans living off the fisheries and processing industries, a lasting reform of the common policy is needed if we are to preserve this important sector of the european union's economy in the medium and long term. under the new common fisheries policy, the annual renewal criteria will help maintain fish stocks. traditional fishing techniques will also be recognised and preserved. conservation of fish stocks and an end to discards - more than a quarter of catches are wasted each year - are also key elements in the continuation of small-scale, artisanal and coastal fishing. this new common fisheries policy is a major step forward for france, which is europe's leading maritime interface.
in writing. with this report on the reform of the common fisheries policy, parliament is attempting, by means of amendments, to counteract a commission in brussels which is deaf to demands and which is holding to very restrictive positions which are endangering the future of our fishermen. the commission is trying to impose on a profession already weakened by foreign imports the fisheries policies dictated by an ideological and technocratic vision that opens the door to social, environmental and health dumping. the principle of maximum sustainable yield will further reduce the number of fishermen in the fishing industry, which will further destabilise coastal regions. the infantilization of a noble profession which contributes to european food security by offering quality products is outrageous. if some of the amendments are in the right direction, we cannot put french fishermen and their work at risk.
in writing. as we know, overfishing destroys the marine environment and poses a serious threat to the populations that depend on fishing. financing increasingly efficient boats with incentives to fish more and more, short-term interest, centralised management, waste of almost a quarter of the total european catch. after 30 years of failed implementation of a european fisheries policy, the situation is grim. today, for the first time, the european parliament has had the opportunity to express its views and to play its role as a co-legislator in this fisheries area. to prevent our oceans from becoming deserts by 2050, a positive vote by the european parliament was essential. the aim is to exploit fisheries resources in the spirit of 'maximum sustainable yield', to avoid bycatch, to give aid to sustainable practices and to bring fisheries management closer to the ground. today's vote is a step towards a virtuous cfp, in its economic, social and environmental dimensions, which benefits everyone.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it sets out the main principles of a new common fisheries policy which succeeds in reconciling the preservation of stocks and the safeguarding of jobs in the medium and long term. this text paves the way towards a more sustainable fisheries in europe focusing on traditional, small-scale, artisanal and coastal fishing techniques. the conservation of fisheries resources and the end of discards - over a quarter of catches are wasted every year - are key elements of this report and should be welcomed.
in writing. i voted against this report because it endangers the survival of european fisheries. we must support sustainable fishing to preserve our fisheries resources. however, the reform of fisheries must be done in a fair way, without prejudicing fishermen who are already in a difficult situation. the immediate requirement to land all fish caught, even those unfit for human consumption, is a dangerous measure. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's fishing fleet is not displaced. the rejection of this amendment, which respected the principle of the principle of the fishermen's right to adapt, threatens the survival of european fisheries. this amendment was a realistic compromise which would have allowed this obligation to be implemented within a reasonable time. this regulation needs to be revised in order to strike the right balance between preserving fisheries resources and taking account of european fishermen, in particular small-scale fisheries. the latter would not survive an unrealistic policy. the actions undertaken by the profession over the years to promote sustainable fishing are a remarkable step forward and demonstrate its commitment to exploiting resources in a sustainable way.
in writing. i voted against the report by ulrike rodust on the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). while the cfp needs to be reformed to make it more sustainable, the final position of the text seems to me problematic. i considered that we must succeed in reconciling the restoration of fisheries resources by 2020 with the maintenance of good conditions for fishing activities. the need to respect fishing quotas in the context of maximum sustainable yield (msy) is undeniable. however, the timing of implementation is problematic. moreover, as regards the practice of discarding at sea, the obligation to land all catches will not make it possible to combat this waste. we prefer other alternative solutions such as selectivity and management plans. with my french socialist colleagues, we hope that the further negotiations will lead to a more balanced legislation.
in writing. the reform of the common fisheries policy was urgent and the european commission's proposal was highly anticipated. while it is essential to combat overfishing and to restore the fish stocks on which the future of our fisheries depends, the report presented contained, in my view, a dangerous imbalance between environmental and socio-economic considerations. the total ban on discards is an unrealistic and, above all, unenforceable measure which will endanger a considerable number of fisheries and the jobs they create, at a time when unemployment in the european union is already at historically high levels. the amendment tabled by alain cadec, which would have allowed a margin of tolerance to be set in the area of the ban on discharges, was not adopted, so i voted against it.
in writing. by significantly increasing the environmental constraints on fisheries and implementing them within such tight deadlines, the rodust report simply proposes the death knell for the sector. under the guise of good intentions, such as zero waste, and under pressure from the environmental lobbies, the european parliament has given in to demagogy and shown its total ignorance of the realities of this profession and the constraints it already faces. fisheries professionals presented alternative solutions that were environmentally friendly and ensured the future of their sector, but they were not heard. the small-scale fisheries will of course be the first to suffer. it is our food security, the maintenance of jobs and the economies of our coastal areas that are at stake. this report, which purports to advocate a balance between the sustainability of fisheries resources and the economic and social sustainability of the fisheries sector, is in fact a radical and ideological reform. this is proof, if there is any, that europe does not like fishermen. i voted against mrs rodust's report.
in writing. this report removes the obligation to privatise fishing rights, the worst is avoided. it confirms the implementation of the maximum sustainable yield and its postponement to 2020. it establishes a multiannual fisheries management system which is coordinated by all the players in the sector and which is in line with the best scientific advice, a provision which will make it easier for fisheries undertakings to read the text. it takes account of the social and economic viability of fisheries activities and endorses the introduction of sustainable aquaculture and shellfish farming in the cfp. that is why i support this report. i would point out, however, that while the so-called zero-emission measure is intended to increase the selectivity of fishing gear, it should not condemn the sector. its application will have to be conducted by fisheries, on a case-by-case basis, after feasibility and socioeconomic impact studies. fleet modernisation planning is needed to enable selective, sustainable and safer fishing for seafarers. this report does not provide for any such provision. i am voting for the many advances in this text, but i am denouncing this serious shortcoming.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the common fisheries policy. this report takes similar directions to those which emerged from my report for an opinion on the cfp in the committee on regional development. i am also pleased that my proposal for the creation of an advisory committee on the outermost regions was adopted by a large majority in the european parliament's plenary. as regards the overall challenges of the cfp reform, we must bear in mind that the disappearance of fish will bring with it the disappearance of fishermen. if we continue at the current rate of predation, there will be no fish available for commercial fishing by 2050. there is an urgent need to limit overfishing and ensure the recovery of fish stocks. this is a major issue for the protection of biodiversity and the sustainability of the fisheries sector, which parliament has taken fully into account. i regret, however, that no compensatory measures have been provided for fishermen, especially the most vulnerable. the report is a real breakthrough in environmental matters.
in writing. i voted against the proposal for a regulation on the common fisheries policy, because despite the progress made in committee, this text did not strike the right balance between the need to renew resources and the sustainability of european fisheries, which is part of our food self-sufficiency. i particularly regret that the maximum sustainable yield (msy), a tool that allows scientifically to measure what can be fished without jeopardising the renewal of the resource, has been over-emphasised, leading to the aim of 'beyond' msy by 2020, a vague and arbitrary notion. i also regret that no concrete proposals have been made to improve the scientific knowledge of stocks. finally, i regret that parliament has approved the compulsory landing of all waste, a job-destroying measure which will legalise the marketing of waste processed into animal flour. there were better ways of eliminating waste and keeping it alive, through increased selectivity of gear, modernisation of ships and their technologies, management plans. i will remain committed to ensuring that the discussions in the trilogue continue to make positive progress on this reform.
in writing. the vote on the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) improves the commission's proposal by linking the allocation of fishing rights to environmentally and socially responsible management. the proposal for transferable fishing quotas was rejected and discards of fish not corresponding to the species sought are strictly controlled. the amendments adopted take account of small-scale fishing and call for it to be distinguished from industrial fishing. but i would have liked parliament to go further and adopt the gue/ngl amendments on taking better account of the socioeconomic aspects of the conservation of fisheries resources, in particular through compensation for fisheries and local economies. i also regret that french rups are not treated like other european rups. this vote by the european parliament is a clear signal that the current cfp is a disaster and that the reform proposed by the european commission is not enough to put an end to overfishing, which at the current rate is a real threat to fisheries resources. the ball is in the council's court, whose delays raise fears that a real reform of the cfp will be postponed until 2020.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i am of course in favour of measures which will help to protect public health and the environment by reducing the noise level of motor vehicles. we all know that noise pollution is a source of stress, anxiety and even illness, and that it is a matter of concern to many of our citizens. but do we really have a sense of priorities? we are struggling to recover from an economic and financial crisis which has left our industries either completely exhausted or severely weakened. growth in the european union is almost zero, unemployment is stagnating at a historically high level. is it really the priority, in such a context, to add new constraints, new standards to our car industries? the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. there is now a consensus on the priorities for the coming years, namely growth and employment. we must therefore work in line with these objectives and not, it seems to me, adopt contradictory legislation. let us try not to shoot a bullet in the foot of a european union which, at the moment, is already having so many difficulties in moving forward, so many difficulties in being legible to our fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to limit the noise of motor vehicles while allowing manufacturers time to adapt. the european parliament also recommended the introduction of a labelling system to inform consumers of the noise levels of new cars. noise is a public health issue that needs to be addressed.
in writing. millions of europeans suffer daily from noise pollution from motor vehicles. but technology now exists to reduce these inconveniences considerably. the time limits mentioned in this report seem to me to be reasonable and easily digestible by the automobile industry. on the contrary, a major amendment adopted today by the european parliament will make it possible to install minimum thresholds on electric vehicles to prevent accidents with people with sensitive hearing. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which has produced a good compromise.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr ouzký, which supports the commission's proposal on the fight against noise emissions from motor vehicles, particularly for the population in urban areas. i would also like to stress the importance of reducing the noise emitted from the road surface via the tyres and not just from the car itself.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because improvements can be made in terms of noise generated by vehicles. however, we must be careful that any new legislation does not worsen the economic situation of our european companies, as the automobile industry is already weakened by the crisis. i voted in favour of amendment no 66, which focuses on hybrid and electric vehicles. they are too silent and therefore a source of accidents for the visually impaired and for young children, so we want an ad hoc sound system to prevent this kind of risk.
in writing. noise is a public health issue for me. it can cause exhaustion, health problems and the development of diseases. more than half the population of the european union is exposed to noise levels above 55 db. 1.8% of heart attacks in europe are attributed to excessive noise levels, and noise from rail and road transport is responsible for 50,000 fatal heart attacks and 200,000 cases of cardiovascular disease each year in europe. it was therefore urgent to revise these standards, which were almost 20 years old: technology allows advances and progress to reduce these human tragedies. of course, we must not ignore technology and productivity: in the period of crisis in the european automobile industry, it seemed crucial to us socialists to give manufacturers sufficient time to adapt to the many environmental laws. so reducing noise levels by 4 decibels in 8 years seems to me to be the responsible balance for the health of europeans and the future of our car industry.
in writing. the position adopted by the european parliament in this vote is courageous and ambitious. by voting in favour of this text, we make a clear choice not to sell out the health of our citizens or our competitiveness. we refuse to set unrealistic environmental targets: we do not want to sacrifice our jobs when there is a middle way that does not endanger our health. the european parliament wants a realistic reduction in noise emissions, for a europe that protects its citizens, their health and their jobs.
in writing. there is now evidence that persistent exposure to high levels of traffic noise is harmful to human health, leading to both physical and mental illnesses. half of the union's urban population is exposed to road traffic noise exceeding 55 decibels, and the limit value for noise in a car set by european legislation is 74 decibels. legislation was therefore needed to further limit the noise pollution caused by motor vehicles. by also looking at the quality of road surfaces, aerodynamics and tyres, the european union is promoting a balanced approach to reduce noise production, noise pollution and to preserve the quality of life of people living in urban areas, but also in favour of the automobile market players. noise emission limits will be scaled according to vehicle types and vehicle noise labelling will provide adequate information to car buyers. finally, it should be noted that hybrid and electric vehicles will be equipped with acoustic warning systems, in order to maintain a sound level sufficient to ensure the safety of visually impaired pedestrians.
in writing. the last time the noise limits for vehicles were lowered was in 1995. so while the result may not be what everyone expects, i believe that the final result strikes an acceptable balance between public health requirements and the interests of the car manufacturers who are facing profound difficulties in europe at the moment.
in writing. on wednesday 6 february, the european parliament adopted the report on the noise level of motor vehicles. i understand the interest in lowering the maximum decibel thresholds for different categories of vehicles, because noise pollution can poison the lives of city dwellers in particular. however, the french automobile industry is in a serious crisis. its sales are continuing to fall, forcing some of its historical companies to restructure and close down sites. this alarming situation must not be aggravated by unrealistic proposals which would merely deliver the final blow to an already weakened industry. that is why i rejected the amendments calling for a lowering of the maximum decibel thresholds to a level which seems to me to be excessive in the present context. i also rejected the amendment on the test conditions for measuring the noise level of vehicles which was based on new tyres, which did not correspond to real traffic conditions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the noise level of motor vehicles. as constant exposure to high levels of traffic noise has a negative impact on health, it is important to lower the noise limits of cars. a first phase would apply to new vehicle models, and a second phase to all new vehicles entering service. vehicle noise emissions also depend on road surfaces, tyre noise and aerodynamics. the new cars should also be labelled with their sound characteristics in order to inform the consumer. finally, electric and hybrid vehicles pose a threat to pedestrians and should in future be audible with a vehicle acoustic warning system.
in writing. half of the european population living in urban areas is exposed to noise emissions from traffic above 55 decibels. constant exposure to high levels of noise can cause physical fatigue, organ dysfunction and cardiovascular disease. i supported the report by my colleague ouzký, who proposes new noise limits for vehicles (reduction from 74 to 68 decibels for standard cars). these new standards would be introduced gradually to allow industry to adapt (with a delay of 6 to 8 years). the text also provides for new cars to be labelled with their sound characteristics in order to inform consumers. electric and hybrid vehicles are too quiet, endangering pedestrians and the visually impaired. the introduction of a 'vehicle warning system' is provided for in the text, which i believe is beneficial to ensure the safety of all. although these elements seem to me to be positive, it also seems to me important to pay some attention to the road surface, the noise of the tyres and the aerodynamics of the vehicles, which have an impact on their noise emissions.
in writing. noise pollution is a public health issue. nearly 70 million europeans suffer from excessive noise exposure, severe sleep problems, anxiety and heart problems. one of the main sources of noise pollution is urban traffic, which exposes half of the european urban population to noise levels above 55 db. i therefore supported the commission's proposal for a directive to limit noise emissions from motor vehicles. i have, however, been keen, together with my political family, to correct and improve this proposal, taking account of the latest technical innovations and the overall feasibility of the objectives. it was also appropriate to create a specific category for cars produced in limited series. i believe that we have succeeded in proposing realistic objectives which will ensure both the improvement and innovation of vehicles, without imposing excessive constraints on our manufacturers, and better protection for european citizens.

in writing. i supported this text which maintains technical conservation measures. these are rules that fishermen must observe every day when they go out to sea to ensure that the way and place of fishing is sustainable. these measures concern minimum landing sizes, minimum mesh sizes of nets and fishing areas. the aim is to encourage the use of more selective fishing gear in order to protect the marine environment.
in writing. technical conservation measures are rules to be observed daily by fishermen throughout the european union to ensure that the manner and location of fishing activity meet the criteria of sustainable development. i therefore give my vote to the rapporteur, pat the cope gallagher, who recognises the need for these measures, but also points out that they must be formulated and designed in harmony with the evolving nature of fisheries management and in accordance with scientific advice. the rapporteur points out that poorly designed or inappropriate technical measures can result in unsustainable fishing practices.
in writing. i voted for the gallagher report on technical measures for the conservation of fishery resources. i believe that it was necessary to update the existing measures in line with the latest scientific advice. this report will ensure that fish stocks are fished sustainably and that ecosystems are maintained and protected. i therefore welcome the adoption of this text, especially since inappropriate technical measures can result not only in unsustainable fishing practices but also, in certain circumstances, in endangering the lives and safety of fishermen.
in writing. according to the european commission, 80% of fish stocks in the mediterranean and 47% in the atlantic are affected by overfishing. a major reform of the common fisheries policy is therefore urgently needed, and i supported this text, while at the same time being concerned to protect small-scale and recreational fisheries from excessive restrictions. the main points are as follows: - maximum sustainable yield: from 2015 onwards, no more should be fished than a given stock can produce in a given year - stocks should thus be restored by 2020. - end discards based on species or size - one quarter of the eu's total catch: mandatory landing of all catches in accordance with a timetable setting specific dates for the different fisheries, starting in 2014. - long-term planning: multiannual fish stock management plans to improve market predictability and help the sector to invest and plan for the future. negotiations with the member states will begin, and i hope that we will reach an agreement as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of the regulation on technical measures on which i was rapporteur for my group. while the vote on this text was only intended to extend transitional measures until january 2014, pending the adoption of the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp), our discussions anticipated the complexity of the technical overhaul to come. while the cfp basic regulation is intended to define the broad guidelines of fisheries for the next ten years, the technical regulation defines the rules applicable by geographical area, trade, target stock, period of the year, etc. a genuine work of art, which makes it possible to put into practice, as closely as possible to the territorial realities, a policy conceived in a global way. the work on this transitional text has thus made it possible to put the cfp debates in perspective with reality and to ask the question of the implementation of many of the measures proposed in the reform, which are beautiful on paper but whose feasibility in everyday life is questionable, such as the compulsory landing of waste, for example. the follow-up in 2014...

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it seems to me essential today, commissioner, that the commission should ensure that this request is fully in line with the provisions of the european regulations for the protection of designations of origin, geographical indications and traditional terms applicable to third countries. the use of these indications is authorized provided that they meet the same or equivalent conditions as those required of our member states. if this is not the case, this unlawful authorization would create unfair competition between american and european wines bearing the traditional terms 'château' and 'clos'. firstly, because american wines, unlike european wines, are not made exclusively from grapes harvested from a single holding and whose winemaking is entirely carried out on that same holding. secondly, because it would be misleading consumers about branded products unrelated to a farm. finally, because such authorization would constitute a misappropriation of the reputation acquired through decades of work and identification efforts. we would thus be exposing ourselves to the risk that these traditional terms would no longer be protected against competition from other parts of the world. this would set a dangerous precedent which, in the future, could affect many other traditional european names such as abbazzia, casa, torre and burg. in view of the economic situation and the cultural challenges facing our european viticulture, commissioner, can you honestly assure us that the american application is admissible and above all fully complies with the conditions of validity concerning the traditional term and, in particular, its definition as provided for in community legislation?

in writing. while european citizens are still suffering the effects of the crisis, the reports by richard howitt and raffaele baldassarre are a reminder that europe's recovery must be sustainable. while the hallmark of csr is its voluntary nature, a policy combining the regulatory and voluntary approaches is necessary to ensure that csr is taken into account on a widespread basis. the un smart mix is not the enemy of business as some, fiercely opposed to any regulatory approach, would have us believe. companies have taken the lead and are innovating in csr: the vast majority of the largest european companies are already communicating on this subject. the regulatory power is lagging behind the market. the two reports adopted on csr are a first step towards recognising its added value in the social market economy. the commission must now put its idea into practice with a legislative proposal on the transparency of non-financial information published by companies. france has led the way in this respect. since the new economic regulations act 2001 large companies have been required to publish social and environmental information in their annual reports. this obligation is about to be strengthened and extended.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague raffaele baldassarre which abolishes the dichotomy between voluntary and compulsory approaches. the commission has so far focused its discussions on csr. in addition, the report aims to improve transparency and self- and co-regulation processes and to make csr more attractive to businesses. a central element in these sectors is progress, which increases citizens' confidence in business and reduces the gap between citizens' expectations and what they actually perceive from business.
in writing. we have just sent a strong signal to the commission to effectively implement its 2014-2020 csr strategy, to governments to promote csr through legal or tax incentives, and to business leaders to dare to set ambitious social and environmental standards regardless of the size of their structure. the application of csr in europe is now a matter of political will. but it is also a legal issue, because if csr is to remain on a voluntary basis, it needs to be promoted through public procurement, trade agreements, reporting of non-financial activities. without these legal tools to encourage csr, the political will may not be sufficient to spread it as a 'normal' practice across european companies of all sizes.
in writing. businesses, especially smaller ones, would benefit greatly from having better access to existing information and good practice. because they have a direct impact on their communities, because they are the main job creators in europe, i welcome the angle taken in this report, which gives a central place to smes.
in writing. corporate social responsibility, which means the voluntary integration by companies of social and environmental concerns into their business activities, should guide european companies in their activities, especially abroad, and especially when investing in countries where social and environmental standards are less stringent than in europe. while many european companies have subscribed to the principles of csr as set out in the un global compact for business, progress remains slow, with some european companies even being prosecuted for human rights and labour rights violations. europe must give substance to the social dimension of private sector activity and set an example in moralizing business practices. csr must be applied by all european enterprises, especially smes. to achieve this, a flexible and cooperative approach is needed, allowing for the flow of information and the dissemination of good practice. csr must become a shared issue and be thought of as a worthwhile and positive investment. the union must also integrate a strong social dimension into its trade policy and always mention csr in trade agreements with third countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to strengthen corporate social responsibility while preserving its voluntary nature. companies must be accountable and transparent to citizens about their activities. however, this approach must remain voluntary if companies are to go beyond compliance with the minimum standards in force. it is not by imposing new rules that companies will become more responsible. nevertheless, the european institutions can help and support the changes in mindsets in the business community so that they comply with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. voluntary 'good practices' are not enough and transparency should not be an option. it is essential to break with this purely voluntarist approach to corporate social responsibility and move towards legal obligations. in a context of intensive exploitation of natural resources in the south, there are many examples of abusive behaviour by european companies in the extractive industry, with the dramatic health, social and environmental consequences we know. a system of controls and binding instruments must be put in place, and the extractive industries transparency initiative must be included in all trade agreements. as it stands, in this report, the account is not there. so i refrained.
in writing. i welcome the positive signal given by the european parliament on corporate social responsibility. csr is defined as the responsibility of enterprises for the effects they have on society. in other words, concerns and values in the social, environmental and ethical fields are no longer the preserve of large companies but extend to the business world as a whole, as the actions and activities of companies have a direct and indirect impact on society. businesses contribute to the development of our economies and the flourishing of our societies when they are realistically and respectfully anchored in them. csr is an ambitious but achievable objective which must be borne by the companies themselves, because they know better than anyone else their possibilities and limitations. the csr approach must be implemented in a timely manner without the additional regulations and administrative burdens that would hinder its appropriation. we must encourage our companies to respect social, environmental and ethical principles and values, and we must support them in this process, not impose on them an additional burden which would ultimately lead to a lack of confidence in europe and harm their competitiveness.
in writing. in its new strategy, the european commission proposed to redefine corporate social responsibility (csr) as 'the responsibility of companies for their effects on society'. parliament welcomed this new definition, which abolishes the dichotomy between voluntary and compulsory approaches that has so far polarised discussions on the subject, and which clearly shows that csr development is based on several processes. however, it amended the commission's proposal, rejecting any approach to csr which would involve the taking over by enterprises of the functions of public authorities, and in favour of an approach to csr which is guided mainly by enterprises themselves, on the basis of their own possibilities and needs. i therefore voted in favour of this amended version.

extreme poverty. more than 2.6 billion people lack access to sanitation and about 1 billion lack access to safe drinking water. and chronic hunger affects more than 800 million people, most of them in sub-saharan africa. that is why, like the icd, our parliament wants at least 20% of the funds of the next acp edf to be used to meet basic social needs such as health, education, access to water and sanitation. in view of this, we cannot but deplore the amount of the edf budget as decided by the council a month ago. we therefore hope that the need for flexibility and mid-term review, which our assembly calls for in the next multiannual financial framework, will also allow the edf to be upgraded by 2017. budgeting has become a necessity, not only for obvious reasons of democratic control, but also to enhance the visibility and coherence of the union's external actions. the commission must therefore stop procrastinating and present a clear roadmap detailing a timetable for the budgetisation of the edf after 2020. this context of severe budgetary constraints should encourage us to move as quickly as possible towards the introduction of innovative financing. the financial transaction tax recently adopted by the eleven member states is to become a source of revenue for development aid. fortunately, there are other ways to strengthen our commitment to developing countries. the agenda for change has provided some ideas, including support for the private sector and the mix of loans and grants. as regards the private sector, we want the resources of the 11th edf allocated to it to be used as a priority to support local enterprises in order to bring know-how to the fore in the acp countries. otherwise, there is a great risk of promoting development and growth that would be neither sustainable, nor inclusive, nor balanced. for the loan/donation mix, the 11th edf will have the investment facility mechanism, the ceiling of which has been increased substantially compared to the 10th edf. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. and regardless of their level of development. i think that's very important. while these countries have an interesting way of presiding over their own development, they are also home to the majority of the world's poor. that is middle-income countries in specific areas, such as tax reforms or the establishment of social security systems. these countries are of vital diplomatic importance to our international objectives, for example in the fight against climate change.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the current overseas association decision (oda) of 2001 linking the overseas countries and territories to the european union expires at the end of this year. the renewal of this association framework became indispensable, as the regional and international context in which the overseas countries and territories operate has changed considerably. the globalisation of trade, new environmental challenges and the risks of climate change are all new issues that they are facing directly. long before overseas countries and territories are made relays of eu development policy, it is important to ask the question of the challenges linked to the development of these territories themselves. due to their physical characteristics, the octs face a number of challenges linked to the fragility of their environment and the need to firmly anchor the environmental pillar of sustainable development. this is why the revision of the dao for the period 2014-2020 was undertaken with a view to realism and put the notion of partnership at the heart of the text. i would also like to stress that this new dao has been the subject of intensive preparatory work, since the reflection was launched in 2008 with a wide public consultation, via a green paper which led to a commission communication in 2009 and the signing of a common position document between member states and the octs two years ago. finally, as you know, the committee on development also contributed to this reflection by organising a hearing on the octs last september. overall, i am particularly pleased that the future eu-oct partnership marks a significant change of direction, moving from an approach based mainly on poverty reduction to a development framework that is truly adapted to the specific needs of the octs. nevertheless, certain points need to be examined in depth if this association is to be firmly oriented towards the future. the first point concerns the four priority objectives of the dao proposal. the commission proposes, in sum, few lines of action to implement the first objective of increasing the octs' competitiveness. as octs' competitiveness can only be based on low costs, innovation and entrepreneurship are essential to meet the challenges they face. in addition, areas of cooperation for sustainable development could include competitiveness and refer to community programmes on innovation, research and enterprise. the second part of the dao proposal could include provisions to improve oct participation in these programmes, develop operational local information relays and facilitate oct membership of networks such as the europe-enterprise network. we also know how important trade issues are for those regions which are highly dependent on community markets. the union's trade policy has also led to a gradual erosion of the octs' tariff preferences, which puts them in direct competition with third countries with lower production costs. finally, the commission does not go far enough on the question of rules of origin, although it intends to make it easier for oct companies to access eu markets and continues to treat better certain acp island countries such as mauritius or the seychelles, whose exemptions from the rules of origin are automatically renewed, which is not always the case for the oct. another point which seems to me to be essential is the simplification of procedures to ensure the best possible implementation of the 11th edf. beyond the legitimate challenge to the financing of the octs through the edf, the provisions of the implementing regulation of the dao will have to take account of the institutional links between the octs and their member state of attachment, as well as the existence of strict public management rules guaranteeing the safe use of the edf by the octs.
mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur for his work and collaboration on the report on the overseas association decision. this is the first time that the european parliament has spoken on the relations between the european union and the overseas countries and territories, and i am pleased as an oct mep. in addition to the question of the creation of oct-specific financial instruments which would respond more effectively to the challenges facing the octs, i would also like to stress the new paradigm which the commission proposes to develop in the context of the new overseas association decision. this is a major step forward and it should be emphasized. the aim of the partnership with the oct is no longer the fight against poverty, as is the case in the acp countries, but the development of competitiveness or the regional integration of the oct. one of the important points of this report is the establishment within the various dgs of a oct reference point which should enable the oct to be better taken into account in the community programmes in which they can participate. this is a major breakthrough.
