president-in-office of the council. − madam president, last october it was announced that the european union had been awarded the nobel prize for bringing peace to our continent. we can be proud of the achievements of the european union. it has brought peace, stability and prosperity – all on the basis of freedom, democracy and rule of law. but we should never be complacent about our achievements. the fact that we need to organise a europe-wide week against racism is a clear indication that europeans still live under the shadow of discrimination, prejudice and aggression. the council stands firmly alongside this parliament in rejecting all forms of racism, xenophobia and homophobia. these are violations of the principles of liberty, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. the eu’s charter of fundamental rights prohibits all discrimination on the grounds of race, colour, ethnic origin and religion or belief. furthermore, the treaties provide the union with the competence to take appropriate action to combat such discrimination. all the institutions of the eu must stand shoulder to shoulder in defending fundamental freedoms and fighting all forms of discrimination. we can never rest until the scourge of discrimination has been completely banished from our societies. let me first address the situation in which we find ourselves today. sadly, as fresh research published by the fundamental rights agency has shown, discrimination in europe is far from being a thing of the past. lgbt persons, ethnic minorities, including jews and roma, and other groups continue to face prejudice, discrimination, harassment and worse. it is unacceptable that europe in the 21st century should still be a witness to homophobia and to racist attacks against jews, roma and others. i commend this parliament for keeping this issue high on the agenda. in your resolution of may last year you called for more determined action and referred to specific concerns in some third countries. i also recall your recent report on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union (2010-2011), which paints a disturbing picture and which also rightly calls for further action. this leads to my second point – what is the eu doing? the treaties provide the union with a number of powers, and these have been used successfully to introduce a range of legislation. the council has in particular taken steps to protect european citizens from all forms of racism and xenophobia. the council’s framework decision of 2008 ensures that such behaviour constitutes an offence across all member states. amongst other provisions, it requires member states to criminalise public incitement to violence or hatred directed against persons belonging to a group defined by reference to race, colour, religion, descent or national or ethnic origin. it also demands that such conduct be punishable by effective, proportionate and dissuasive criminal penalties of at least between one and three years imprisonment. more generally, the eu has taken a number of measures for tackling discrimination. the legal protection which the eu offers to racial and ethnic minorities is already fairly broad, covering employment, social protection, healthcare, education and access to goods and services. we have also taken steps to combat discrimination in the workplace on the grounds of religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. president, honourable members, allow me to conclude by addressing the issue of what more might be done. we already have extensive legislation in place, and more legislation is under discussion on protection against discrimination in areas outside of employment. in addition, member states have their own domestic laws covering these areas. but the reports from the fundamental rights agency clearly show that the adoption of legislation is not in itself sufficient. it also has to be implemented and properly enforced and we also have to raise awareness. events such as the action week against racism play a vital part in keeping these issues in the public eye and so bringing abuses to light. all of us have a role to play in this regard – and i know that this parliament in particular takes these responsibilities very, very seriously. the european union should be encouraging the development of a society based on equality, tolerance and respect for human rights. those are the values on which it is founded. bigotry and discrimination have no place in the europe of the twenty-first century. the nobel prize was a way of honouring the european union. let us live up to the ideals which it represents. it is in that spirit that the irish presidency put the question of hate crimes on the agenda of the informal meeting of justice and home affairs ministers in dublin in january. this subject is at once very focused – concern about the growth in xenophobia, anti-semitism, homophobia and other extreme forms of intolerance and how to take effective action at national and at eu level to combat these evils – and very broad, in that it touches on fundamental questions about the rule of law and the effective functioning of political and public institutions in the protection of the fundamental rights of citizens. a specific theme of the discussion by ministers was that the solution is not just about legislation, but about getting into the minds of people and encouraging positive attitudes. the irish presidency suggested that a mechanism to better support protection of fundamental rights and the rule of law in member states, by sharing best practice, benchmarking practice and outcomes in an objective way and formulating appropriate recommendations and guidelines for action, would provide such a holistic framework for effective responses to these issues. jha ministers agreed to invite the commission to give further consideration to this matter and to initiate a broad public debate taking account of the commission’s annual report on the eu charter of fundamental rights with governments and public institutions in member states, to include national human rights and equality bodies, civil society etc. so as to raise awareness and understanding of the importance of the rule of law, common values and protection of the fundamental rights of all in europe. the commission will then come back during the course of 2014 with the results of this process. the fundamental rights agency has a very important role to play in providing expert and independent analysis in this process.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, it is important that parliament raises these matters because we all know that recent reports by the fundamental rights agency show that racism, xenophobia and hate crimes remain a matter of concern all over europe – and it is not just the fundamental rights agency which tells us this, as we read about it constantly in the media. many of the hate crimes, we know too, remain unreported, meaning they are not prosecuted and that those who commit them are not punished. so the problem is even greater than we can see. that is why i am very grateful to my colleague alan shatter who, to start the irish presidency, held a gathering of the justice ministers in dublin in january this year in order to discuss the problems of racism, xenophobia and hate crimes, anti-semitism, islamophobia, anti-gypsyism and homophobia – all those manifestations which are completely incompatible with european rules and with the basis on which europe is founded. we have had for many years now a solid framework to address these hate crimes at eu level. the commission monitors the transposition and implementation of this eu legislation, which prohibits discrimination and hate speech and hate crime. i will report on the application of the race equality directive and the employment equality directive, as well as on the transposition of the framework decision on combating racism and xenophobia. you know too that the commission, together with parliament, always insists that the equal treatment directive – the so-called article 19 directive – should be taken in hand by the council but progress is slow, if not to say non-existent. as you know, the council has to adopt this text by unanimity; nothing is moving on this. in addition to legislation, of course, the commission lends its support to a number of activities to prevent acts of intolerance and also to remember our common past, because only if you know the roots on which you are growing can you prevent things from happening again. the commission supports activities aimed at preserving the memory of the mass violations of human rights during the period of nazism and stalinism. under the new citizenship programme of 2014-2020, i have proposed an increasing amount of financial assistance to be provided for remembrance projects. i hope it will remain in place, so i appeal to parliament to have a look at this because i believe it is important for our next generation to know the horrors on which europe has been built, in order for these horrors not to happen again. you know also that the fundamental rights agency is crucial for the collection of data on hate crimes and that our roma integration work is crucial in order to prevent more and more strategies will be given to this house in the spring. jointly with this report, i am working together with the experts to come up with – and i have not told you this yet but think it is necessary to take this step – a council recommendation in order to open new avenues to improve the effectiveness of measures by member states to achieve roma integration in real terms and not just on paper. concerning hate crime: you know that we have the 2008 council framework decision on racism and xenophobia. this is our central tool in fighting hate crimes. it requires all member states to penalise hate speech and to ensure that a biased motivation for any other offence is taken into account in the severity of the penalties. this is european union law. but laws are only as good as the extent to which they are enforced and implemented in practice. the treaties prevent the commission from launching infringement procedures in respect of this type of eu law, because it is a framework decision and it will be a framework decision until 1 december 2014. nevertheless, the commission will put a report on compliance by member states with this eu law on the table at the end of this year. this house also knows that we have completed the victims’ rights directive, which gives victims of crime a broad set of procedural rights, including access to justice, compensation and restoration. particular attention is paid to the special categories of victims of hate crime. so these instruments – that is the european protection order which was decided by the council last week and which will become law very soon – provide for the mutual recognition of protection measures when victims move to another country. this will also be of utmost importance in fighting those kinds of crimes. racism, xenophobia and hate crime are a common concern to the whole of the eu. no member state can boast a clean record when it comes to these crimes. fighting these crimes requires both preventive and corrective action and i thank parliament for helping us to ensure that this happens in real terms.

president of the state of israel. − mr president, my dear friend martin schulz, distinguished members of the european parliament – of this great house of freedom and peace, that has changed the history of europe and affects the future of the entire world – i want to thank you for the privilege of addressing you. it is, for me, an important opportunity and it is a meaningful occasion for the people of israel. i stand here before you with burning memories in my heart and great hope in my soul. i carry profound pain concerning the past, and i look with great confidence to the future. i immigrated to israel in 1934, at the age of 11. in 1942, most of the inhabitants of my town were burned alive. had my family delayed their emigration by eight years, we would have been exterminated. a year before the creation of israel, in 1947, i was recruited to the haganah headquarters. since then, israel has been attacked seven times in 65 years of existence. we were outnumbered and outgunned. we had just one choice before us: to win or to die. i also participated in the confrontation of another enemy – the desert. we won. we made the desert bloom. i have many memories, but i carry many dreams as well, and i did not come to reminisce. i have come to continue my dreams. people age. dreams are ageless. we changed. europe changed. i come to express our admiration for the changed europe. europe picked itself up in the wake of the worst war in history. it divorced the past, it created a new europe. you converted the divided europe of the last thousand years into the united, modern europe of today. you replaced military camps with scientific campuses. europe which knew racism now considers it a crime. i know that you are facing an economic crisis, but your skies are without the clouds of war. a european country introduced the nobel prize. now, a united europe has rightly won it. europe corrected its mistakes and is building a better world. for us, the europe of shoah is now becoming the europe of support for our renaissance. friends, the idea of the rebirth of israel was born on european soil. in the past thousand years, more jews lived in europe than in any other continent in the world. alas, more jews were murdered in europe in the last hundred years than in the preceding 2000 years. we experienced here the worst tragedy of our history. here, at the same time, we dreamed an impossible rebirth. six million – a third of our people – were murdered here by starvation, gas, rifles and fire. what remains from them is ashes. we shall not forget that the righteous among the nations – your people – carried candles of light in the darkness. they were small in number, but great in heroism. israel was born from those ashes at the end of the second world war. if somebody had stood up then and said that within three years a jewish state would be created, he would have been considered a delirious visionary. but this dream became a reality, and i have to add that if somebody had stood up on the same day, and said that in six short years a new united europe would be born, with borders erased and barriers lowered, he would have been considered an author of fiction. six countries signed the treaty of paris and became a community of 27 nations across europe. our relations here and now are a dialogue between two miracles: your miracle and our miracle. israel enjoys an association agreement with europe and close ties with the european union in nearly all fields. i have come to thank you for your friendship, based on common values, geographic proximity and a long history. politically, israel is a western democracy with a mediterranean experience. religiously, israel is the cradle of the three monotheistic religions. scientifically, israel is advanced, even by european standards. israel is small: just one thousandth of the area of the middle east. its soil, typically for the middle east, is barren rather than fertile. water is scarce. we have just two lakes, one dead, the other dying. we have a single river – the jordan – rich in history, poor in water. the land is rich in archaeology and poor in natural resources. the only natural resource we have discovered is human potential. israel is an example of a country where the people have enriched the land more than the land enriched the people; where the devotion of the people and the merits of hi-tech forced deserts to surrender and to bloom. we went through seven wars, and we won them. but when peace became possible, we returned all the land and all the assets which we had won during the war to the countries that we made peace with: egypt and jordan. we started a peace process with the palestinian people, which enabled both of us to build a palestinian authority. then – and people forget this – we evacuated the gaza strip. we dismantled 22 settlements and we brought back all the settlers from there. it was an opportunity for the palestinians to build a strip of independence and of peace. unfortunately, they turned it into a terrorist base. we do not know why, but we know it became a setback to the peace process. israel is an island in a stormy ocean. we have to defend our island, and we have an interest in the tranquilisation of the sea. some people claim it will take generations, but europe has proved that great events can be achieved in six years. we live in a new era in which events are moving at the speed of a plane, and no longer at the speed of a carriage. for that reason, i believe peace can be achieved in a relatively short while. the peace process with the palestinians has already produced agreement on the beginning and on the solution. the solution is based on two nations and states: an arab state, palestine, and a jewish state, israel, living in peace and economic cooperation. the remaining disputed issues can and should be negotiated and concluded. peace for israel is not just a strategic choice. it is a moral call which stems from the depth of our heritage. since the exodus, our heritage has condemned slavery and rejected mastery, and all persons are considered to be born equal. our legacy calls upon us to pursue peace. together with my partner, yitzhak rabin, who was assassinated, i laid down the foundations for peace with the palestinians. now it is time to continue and to renew the peace process. we must continue to work with the palestinian authority. we have to support the palestinian economy. together we have to make and complete peace. a palestinian security force has been formed. you and the americans trained it, and now we are working together with it to prevent terror and crime. ladies and gentlemen, our hand remains stretched out to peace with all the countries in the middle east. in a short while, a new israeli government will be formed. it is an opportunity to resume the peace negotiations and to realise the two-state solution. there is no other solution, either for the palestinians or for us. this is not only our preference, it is what the present reality calls for. jordan, israel and palestine find themselves in a similar situation. terror endangers each of them separately and all three of them collectively. collective dangers call for collective security. i have the highest regard for the king of jordan. like his father, he has proved to be a king courageously committed to peace. i have known the president of the palestinian authority, mahmud abbas, for many years. he condemns terror and he is a real partner for peace. europe has been and continues to be a major partner for peace and a major enemy of terror. next week, we will be hosting president obama in israel as a welcome and esteemed guest. his support for our security is extraordinary and his devotion to peace is unshakeable. we are glad that the united states and europe are now working together to support peace and to stop terror. the greatest danger to peace in the world today is the current iranian regime. it became a dictatorship cloaked in a religious mantle, and it developed an impossible imperial appetite. nobody threatens iran: iran threatens others. it endangers the independence of the arab countries. it menaces the existence of the israeli state. it smuggles arms to many countries in order to undermine their stability. the iranian regime denies the holocaust and calls for another holocaust. they are aiming to build a nuclear weapon and they deny they are doing it. a nuclear bomb in the hands of an irresponsible regime is an imminent danger to the entire world. the european union and the united states together drew the conclusions necessary to create a policy to stop that from happening. to this end, you rightly decided to impose economic sanctions. you made it clear that if the iranians will not respond, other options are on the table. in addition to the nuclear bomb, iran is constructing long-range missiles equipped with nuclear warheads. it can reach the far corners of the world, including europe. i believe that, in addition to controlling the production of highly enriched uranium, there is a need to control the means of delivery: to control the production of missiles capable of carrying nuclear warheads. khamenei has declared that religion prohibits the production and the use of nuclear arms. why then does he build missile capabilities capable of carrying nuclear warheads? during the helsinki conference which took place in 1975, the united states placed the issue of human rights in the soviet union at the top of the world’s strategic agenda. it was a surprising move and it was effective. it shows that the moral voice is no less important than a diplomatic approach. today, such a call should be addressed to iran. a clear voice must be raised against the violation of human rights by the iranian regime. a clear voice must be raised against a regime that hangs people without bringing them to court; that throws journalists into prison without trial; and that fires live bullets at civilian demonstrators, with no respect for their lives. a clear voice must be raised against a regime that discriminates against women. instead of sharing the oil-generated profits with their own people, they spend them on terror and arms, and endanger people all over the world. enriched uranium impoverishes hungry children. a moral voice will encourage the iranian people in their fight for freedom and their struggle against misery. very soon, elections will take place in iran. the ayatollahs should not be allowed to falsify the results and to frustrate the right of the people to make their own free choice. your voice, ladies and gentlemen, will show the iranian people that the world has not turned its back on them. the present leaders of iran are violating the charter of the united nations, which condemns the violation of human rights and aggression against other nations. yet they are being given the opportunity in the united nations to abuse its platforms. iran supports terrorism throughout the world. its main proxy, hezbollah, carries out terror attacks and threatens the stability of the entire region. the historic sykes–picot agreement between france and england gave birth to modern lebanon – to become a multicultural country where muslims, christians and druze together lived in peace. today, hezbollah, supported by iran, is destroying lebanon. hezbollah is a terror organisation, not a political movement. its members collect missiles. they are trigger-happy. they hide missiles in peaceful towns and villages, and by doing so, they turn them into a war target. hezbollah divides lebanon politically, religiously and ethnically. it has turned the land of the cedar tree into a land of scorched cedars. hezbollah is a state within a state. it is a private army, apart from the national army. it sends soldiers to support the massacre of the bloody dictator in syria, without the authorisation of the government of which it is a member. recently there have been no fewer than 20 terror attempts by hezbollah throughout the world – in india, thailand, georgia, south africa, the united states, egypt and greece, among others. last month, the government of bulgaria, a member state of the european union, identified hezbollah as the author of the terror attack in burgas in which five israeli tourists and one bulgarian citizen lost their lives. cyprus recently arrested a hezbollah terrorist planning a terror attack. distinguished members of parliament, we appeal to you: call terror, terror. save lebanon from terrorist madness. save the syrian people from iran’s proxies. save your citizens and ours from hezbollah. the international community has to designate hezbollah a terrorist organisation, because it is a terrorist organisation. today, terror reaches far beyond its previous limits. recently, terrorists attempted to take over mali. had they succeeded, it would have halted the impressive endeavour of the african continent to recover from its past. one of the highest hopes of all of us is to see the success of the brave attempt by the african people to build a new science-based economy like that in europe. the free world cannot stand by as terror imposes its grip on any part of the world, far or near. it cannot stand by when a massacre is carried out by the syrian president against his own people, his own children. assad recently built a nuclear installation and an arsenal of chemical warheads. the nuclear installation was destroyed in time; the chemical arsenal remains in his hands to this day. it is a terrible danger for the syrian people, for the entire region and indeed for europe. a way must be found to prevent the chemical weapons from falling into the wrong hands. the best option for putting an end to the syrian tragedy might be to empower the arab league, of which syria is a member, to intervene. an intervention by western forces would be perceived as a foreign intervention. the arab league can and should form a provisional government in syria to stop the massacre and prevent syria from falling to pieces. the united nations should support the arab league to build an arab force in blue helmets. dear friends, 18 years ago i came to brussels to sign the association agreement between the european union and israel. i am happy that reality has surpassed our expectations. indeed, an association agreement became a partnership and, before long, the partnership became a friendship. it is on this steady ground that i propose that the european union and israel should cooperate for the benefit of stability and prosperity in the middle east and in other places in the world. israel is described as a ‘start-up nation’. i believe that the whole middle east can become a start-up region. hi-tech incubators can be created all over the region to help people escape poverty. israel is small, so we try to take advantage of our smallness. we have discovered that small countries can become great pilot projects. today, we are trying to build a social model that will bridge the gap between the ‘haves’ and the ‘have nots’. the social gap is a major problem for all, rich and poor. we are looking for a new way to overcome the gap through the democratisation of health, the democratisation of education and the democratisation of communication, and by reducing the cost of food and housing. for the younger generation, this is a burning need. it is nice to be young, but today it is extremely expensive! we intend to improve the human condition, to enable each person to possess the capacity freely to choose their way of life, by entering the secrets of our brains. the brain is the most illustrious instrument in the world. it has enabled us to build artificial brains, yet we are still far from understanding the way the brain functions – our brain. as a matter of fact, we are strangers to ourselves. discovering the mechanism of our brain will enable us to become friends with ourselves and with our fellow men. i am glad that this effort has been accorded new priority and has become a major focus of cooperation between our governments and non-governmental organisations, and between us as individuals. our global world has no global government. it has become almost ungovernable, and we have to look for an alternative. i believe that the future way of governing will rely on three pillars: national governments will continue to be in charge of the husbandry of the national state; global companies will invest in research and development; and individuals will enjoy the capacity to govern themselves by knowing how their brain functions. science today is more telling than politics. it is universal: it is borderless. armies cannot conquer wisdom. police cannot arrest science. i believe that scientific aid to developing countries can enable them to escape poverty. science-based global companies can help change the world. globalisation will end racism, for you cannot be global and racist. it empowers the individual. global companies do not impose their will upon people; on the contrary, they respect the will of their clients. they can provide scientific know-how for growth. they can assist young people to acquire high education and they can create jobs befitting their skills. this may be the best help we can offer to our young people and to the younger generation in the arab world and, this is our hope to answer the challenge of the new age. i have proposed a plan for a joint venture between the european union, national governments and global corporations, to cope in a new way with these challenges, and i know that it requires your support as the european parliament. allow me to count on your understanding and help. by combining europe’s wisdom and israel’s experience, we can overcome tomorrow’s challenges. facing the lack of a global government, we can foster close cooperation between governments and global companies. facing the dangers which threaten the values for which we stand, we shall fight terror – wherever it is – relentlessly. president schulz, jean monnet, the father of the european union, once said: ‘everybody is ambitious. the question is whether he is ambitious to be, or ambitious to do.’ the time has come to do. let us remember that we are as great as the purpose we serve. yes, the challenges ahead of us are daunting, but who better to defy the seemingly impossible than the two miracles i have mentioned? let us join forces, the european union and israel, to fulfil the teachings of our heritage. in the words of my forefathers, let us ‘fix the world’ or, as we say in hebrew ‘tikkun olam’. in the words of jean monnet, i say ‘let us do it!’ let us work together for a better middle east, by a daring europe. let us fulfil the values of our people: peace, democracy, human rights. yielding to no obstacle, and daring the new, we shall be servants of the future rather than rulers of the past. my friends, as i look upon the future of the friendship which ties israel to the european union, i am filled with hope and determination. hand in hand, we shall build a brighter tomorrow for tomorrow’s generation. thank you, and shalom. i'm the reporter. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this is a report on the control of radioactive substances in drinking water. in order to ensure consistency in the text and after consulting the european parliament's services and the political groups, i would like to make a technical amendment to amendment no 2 in order to delete the following words: 'after transmission of the draft legislative act to the national parliaments and having regard to the opinion of the committee of the regions'. following the vote, i would thank you, madam president, if you would allow me to speak briefly again to address a message on behalf of the european parliament to the european commission.
i'm the reporter. - madam president, thank you for your conscience and this crucial vote. i would ask the commission, on behalf of the european parliament, to forward this report as amended by the european parliament to the national parliaments and the committee of the regions and to resume the legislative process in codecision. this report proposed by the european commission is a democratic nonsense. all the members of the european parliament in the committee shared my view during the vote in committee and i thank them very much for that. this report concerns the monitoring of radioactive substances in water. this is therefore a public health issue in which the european parliament must be involved. in doing so, the commission is depriving the european citizens of their legitimate right to democratic debate and vote. the question here is not whether we are for or against nuclear power, but whether we are protecting the quality of the water we use every day. and the euratom treaty is by no means a legal basis. the legal basis for co-decision is therefore article 192 of the lisbon treaty.
madam president, allow me to echo what our colleague said because, indeed, the commissioner who is still present here was quite long in his speech, so unfortunately he has diluted the message he was supposed to deliver to this house. but the declaration was a full part of the agreement, so it was very important that this declaration be made in public in this house, during voting time.
in writing. european energy policy must ensure that european citizens have sustainable, secure and affordable energy. in the face of insufficient integration of the internal energy market, the commission has proposed bold lines for the future of this policy, with particular emphasis on competitiveness, security of supply, sustainability and decarbonisation. i voted in favour of this report, which stresses the importance of interdependence between states and promotes more concerted, rapid and integrated action by the european union. the eu's energy and climate policy is a great way to boost economic growth through job creation and the investments it underpins. the new regulation thus encourages the modernisation and interconnection of energy networks. in this it defines a moderate number of transeuropean priority corridors and areas covering electricity, gas, oil and carbon dioxide transport networks. the report also calls for the administrative procedures for projects of common interest to be streamlined in order to simplify and shorten them.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal to ensure the completion of strategic energy networks by 2020, through energy corridors and priority areas for electricity, gas and other transmission networks. projects which represent this 'common interest' in implementing these priorities will then be eligible for special funding. at present, energy infrastructure works are very slow and expensive. in germany, for example, 100 km of power lines have been built, whereas the target for 2015 was 850 km. however, there are european budgets if the project is labelled a 'project of european interest'. the new rules will thus provide clarity and better access to finance for these major infrastructure projects.
in writing. in voting in favour of the correia de campos report, i want to stress the importance of developing energy interconnections in europe. by strengthening the single market, reducing costs and ensuring energy independence for the european union, this report will have very positive practical implications for european citizens.
in writing. this report will help to accelerate the development of transeuropean energy infrastructures. for our energy security, and for a reliable and affordable energy supply for all europeans, we must now create the infrastructure needed to complete the single energy market. these infrastructures are still too often slowed down by lengthy and costly procedures. the aim of this text is to put an end to these barriers, which are slowing down the establishment of a genuine european energy market. we are promoting transparency and speed in the process through a renewed permit granting procedure. the benefits are clear: for the operators, it is a saving of time, money and efficiency, which will affect their competitiveness in the world market. and the positive effects, in terms of both cost and security of supply, will be felt by consumers and businesses. the text rightly emphasises the costs to the end user. this is a question on which i am particularly concerned.
in writing. i voted against the adoption of this agreement between the council and parliament. the purpose of this text is to define 12 priority corridors for energy supplies between member states. if i can support energy supply infrastructure projects aimed at ensuring greater solidarity between member states and more efficient energy management, i am opposed to the way in which these corridors are adopted, even though they are presented by the commission as 'projects of common interest'. these projects are aimed at speeding up the completion of the internal energy market and are therefore fully in line with the liberalisation of the sector. in addition, the selected projects will benefit from special regulatory treatment by the commission, in particular through so-called rapid authorisations, which will be nothing more or less than to circumvent national procedures considered too long and delaying the implementation of projects. there is therefore also a risk of circumvention of public consultation procedures; the text can therefore also be seen as part of the authoritarian and anti-democratic drift. this text is therefore for me a symbol of what not to do and of the processes that are fuelling the growing distrust of citizens towards the european institutions.
in writing. our union is a union of projects, of which trans-european energy infrastructures are prominent. i am therefore pleased that our parliament has seized the opportunity to create the conditions for modernising our existing network, whose efficiency is hampered by fragmentation, environmental footprint and physical deficiencies. i supported this regulation, which in particular adapts the trans-european energy network to the challenges of the europe 2020 strategy: interconnection, interoperability, energy security, sustainability, economic, social and territorial cohesion. the aim is to achieve a single european energy area based on sustainable, high-quality transnational infrastructures, sources of growth, jobs and competitiveness. there are many needs, especially if you want to deploy infrastructure to support the development of renewable energy, but you have to focus on the most strategic projects, setting priorities that will avoid the waste of public and private funds. this is therefore a major step forward for europe, to the benefit of citizens and businesses. the ball is now in the court of the states, which must cooperate, and of the companies in the sector, which must work with the public authorities. this is essential if we want to have a future energy network and make europe a world leader in energy.
in writing. objectivity and impartiality are two fundamental guarantees of democratic and effective public governance in order to avoid any potential conflict of interest. that is why i voted in favour of this report which calls for the adoption of a general regulation for more efficient administrative procedures in the union. this report calls for lessons to be learned from the european ombudsman's inquiry into the complaint by 27 organisations asking the commission to take account of the negative consequences of the expansion of vienna airport. i strongly support the ombudsman's recommendations that the commission reconsider its approach to the complaint and take appropriate action to redress the errors highlighted by the ombudsman's inquiry. the report therefore calls on the commission to take into account in future 'the obligation on national authorities to ensure that (i) complainants can bring an action and (ii) that action is taken in respect of a manifest conflict of interest in the application of directive 85/337/eec'.
in writing. as a full member of the committee on petitions, i had already voted in favour of this report, which highlights the limitations of the 'environmental impact assessment' during the 1999 extension of vienna airport. the most important point discussed in this case is not the failure to carry out the environmental impact assessment, but the way in which it was carried out ex post facto by the authorities. i agree with the ombudsman when he points out the need for more transparency and dialogue between the authorities and local people in the context of such major construction works with such an impact on the environment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to clarify the situation at the request of our citizens. the analysis proposed here sheds light on the limitations of existing legislation such as the eia directive. without going into the specific case of vienna airport, this example shows the relevance of a citizen mobilization with the european authorities.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which stresses the need for rigorous, harmonised and detailed accounting rules for the utcatf (land use, land use change and forestry) sector. the aim is to eventually bring the sector within the european target of a 20% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, in particular to meet international requirements such as those of the kyoto protocol. we have ensured that the integration of this sector into the eu's wider climate policy does not lead to administrative burdens for member states and the private sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of the compromise on accounting rules and action plans for greenhouse gas emissions and removals from land use, land use change and forestry activities. it was imperative for the eu to establish a harmonised legislative framework of accounting rules in line with the decisions recently adopted under the united nations framework convention on climate change. this is a strong signal that parliament has sent in the fight against climate change, alongside the horizon 2020 programme.
in writing. we are committed to accounting for our greenhouse gas emissions in the most comprehensive and appropriate way possible. this text specifically addresses activities related to land use and forestry. if we are to meet our obligations to reduce emissions without penalising our farmers and operators, we must ensure that the accounting rules we use are fair and effective. that is the aim of this text, and that is why i support it.
in writing. thanks to this report, the forest is finally recognised as an actor in the fight against climate change; that is why i voted in favour of this text. parliament has abolished an exception to the kyoto protocol on the accounting for carbon stored in wood products. the kyoto protocol considered that cutting down a tree was equivalent to releasing carbon dioxide into the atmosphere in the form of a greenhouse gas. wood products are now counted as storing co2. let's not forget that every cubic meter of wood stores 0.9 tons of co2, not counting the co2 saved compared to other more energy-intensive materials. this text is an example of good european legislation. it complements previous legislation (this sector was excluded when the energy-climate package was adopted in 2009 and was not part of the eu's 20% greenhouse gas emission reduction target for 2030), it is the subject of an interinstitutional consensus and it does not create additional obligations for professionals (for farmers or for foresters).
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, whose main objective is to progressively integrate land use, land use change and forestry (lulucf) into the union's overall climate policy, as it will ensure an appropriate accounting framework while avoiding additional administrative burdens for member states and the private sector. as the accounting of the kyoto protocol commitment varies considerably between member states, improvements were needed to create a level playing field for these sectors.
in writing. i welcome the european commission's proposal to introduce binding accounting rules on greenhouse gas emissions and removals in the forestry and agriculture sectors, which is not customary. i denounce the fact that the parliamentary committee on the environment proposes to exempt companies from any accounting or reporting obligations. i also object to the fact that it tends to exclude forestry from the scope of the directive, whereas this sector represents no less than 70% of the scope. i abstain in respect of the advances but condemn these setbacks.
in writing. i voted in favour of this agreement between the council and parliament which was reached after very long negotiations. this decision will allow for the partial accounting of greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions from agricultural activities, land use change and forestry. this will not help unless this is accompanied by the development and implementation by member states of action plans to reduce and better absorb ghg emissions. this is all the more so as the european parliament has asked that the new provisions do not create any new administrative burdens for the sectors concerned, leaving them a fair degree of flexibility. on the other hand, it is welcome that the european parliament has called for transparency and public participation to be ensured. this text is a step in the right direction, also because it gives the eu a mandate to include these ghg emissions in international negotiations on global warming. i voted for it because it is an instrument to put pressure on the member states and to enable concrete action to be taken in the fight against climate change.
in writing. the fight against climate change is an unquestionable imperative of the 21st century: the european parliament has understood this and is working on it, including in this report, which i fully support. up-to-date, reliable and accurate greenhouse gas emissions data are essential to measure the progress of the eu and states towards achieving international targets. this data is fundamental to the development of new, robust and sustainable climate policies. it was therefore time to look at improving the transposition into european law of the commitments made by the european union and the member states in terms of monitoring greenhouse gas emissions. this report proposes progress in this area, by helping member states to implement the necessary climate and energy package. we did not want to extend the scope of application in order to avoid any unnecessary constraints arising from european legislation.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of this report, which extends the scope of the commission's proposal and strengthens the various aspects of monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gases.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new mechanism for monitoring greenhouse gases and for reporting climate change information at national and european level. these new provisions are in line with recent un standards. while it has been proposed to extend the scope of the new mechanism considerably, i believe it is better to simplify and harmonise the declarations rather than being too ambitious and rendering the mechanism inapplicable.
in writing. i support this balanced text, which maintains a high level of ambition for our greenhouse gas emission reduction targets. it provides a solid basis for the continuation of our policy to combat climate change and for the european union to continue to play its leading role in this field. i particularly welcome the attention paid to a concrete objective for the daily life of european businesses: to reduce the administrative burden on them. our emission reduction targets must not be a hindrance to our growth. in addition, the inclusion of our space tools in the text is also a good thing: our satellite data are essential tools to improve the monitoring of our emissions, and i support the idea in the text that the data provided by gmes/copernicus should be used to the best possible advantage.
in writing. mitigating climate change is a priority. the european union must take active action on the issue of climate change and thus follow up on the international commitments it has made in this area, particularly in the framework of the kyoto protocol. that is why i supported this text, which allows for a revision and improvement of the mechanism for monitoring greenhouse gas emissions. the union is here to support the member states in implementing measures to achieve the objectives set together.
in writing. the new rules adopted today will strengthen the method of accounting for greenhouse gas emissions and the way they are reported by member states. this is a fundamental step forward in ensuring the environmental integrity of the european union's (eu) climate policies. i therefore voted in favour of this report. member states will now have to report annually on their overall climate contributions, which is crucial for the eu's credibility in international climate negotiations. governments will be required to report on policies adopted to meet the eu's long-term climate goals and commitments to reduce emissions by 2050. for the accuracy and integrity of emissions reduction efforts, the omission of the mention of wetlands is regrettable, but the inclusion of cultivated land management in the accounting is a real step forward.
in writing. this text will review the monitoring mechanism and thus improve the existing system in order to better comply with the commitments and obligations entered into by the european union and the member states under current and future international agreements on climate change, to meet the legal requirements arising from the climate and energy package, and to facilitate the development of instruments at union level to mitigate and adapt to climate change. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. i welcome the fact that my colleagues on the environment committee have reaffirmed the eu's commitment to comply with the greenhouse gas emission reductions recommended by the intergovernmental panel on climate change. i welcome the desire to streamline the monitoring system for this necessary reduction and to develop an eu-wide strategy for adaptation to climate change. i regret, however, that this system remains anchored in the dangerous logic of the carbon market.
in writing. i voted in favour of the agreement between the european parliament and the council strengthening the mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions in the context of the union's and member states' internal and international commitments to combat climate change, in particular in relation to the kyoto protocol framework and their support to developing countries. the aim of this legislation is to ensure that the union and the member states meet their commitments to reduce ghg emissions and combat climate change. the union and the member states should therefore, in theory, clearly implement the energy and climate package adopted in 2009. however, it is regrettable that many of the european parliament's requests have not been accepted by the council, such as the reduction of the deadlines for member states to present their low-carbon economy strategies by 18 months or the requirement for additional data from industry and smes. the margin of manoeuvre left to member states which do not fulfil their commitments therefore leaves room for scepticism.
in writing. online dispute resolution is a priority in consumer protection at european level. in order to ensure its effectiveness and ease of use, such online dispute resolution should be fast and inexpensive. the report, which has broad support from political groups, envisages the creation of a platform for settling consumer and trader complaints online. these consumer disputes will be dealt with via a standardised complaint form, combined with a translation service, and will ultimately be assessed by the dispute resolution bodies. i support this report which provides for the implementation of this relevant and useful platform for consumers and businesses.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, roza grafin von thun und hohenstein, which provides for the implementation of an online platform where complaints from consumers and traders can be lodged. they will then be dealt with by the dispute settlement bodies.
in writing. i supported the project to create an online platform for consumer complaints. this platform will allow for a cheaper and faster procedure for all disputes concerning online sales. more and more shoppers are using the internet. the commission will also be able to use the existing legal framework to provide for the possibility of a new legal basis for the application of the rules on the protection of personal data.
in writing. the proposal to create a single online platform will be a major step forward for consumers and traders alike, as they will now be able to turn to a standard form, which will facilitate their procedures and guide them throughout the dispute settlement procedure. the advantage is that it is easy to access and understand. a european platform that will link all national out-of-court dispute resolution bodies will provide simplified procedures for consumers and traders alike. we are putting an end to a system that is too burdensome for consumers, made up of various dispute settlement mechanisms that were supposed to help them in difficulty.
in writing. the growth of e-commerce and the increase in cross-border purchases do not always allow buyers to properly assess the quality of the goods they are purchasing. the creation of a european platform for online dispute resolution is a first step in the necessary securing of this form of trade, which is expected to expand considerably in the coming years. the single web-based point of sale, which is intended to centralise the settlement of consumer disputes, will provide consumers with security by providing an easy and fast means of redress. it will also benefit smes and small traders who do not automatically have the means or administrative capacity to deal with such disputes. available in all 27 eu languages, free of charge and subject to the requirements of online data protection, this tool adequately replaces the old, widespread and incomplete oer mechanisms and accompanies the development of the european digital market.
in writing. i voted in favour of this decision, which is an essential element in the establishment of the european single market. the regulation is above all a more convenient and much cheaper way for european citizens to make a claim via this internet platform. it therefore seemed logical to me to support this decision, which allows for better protection of the european consumer and is in line with my commitment to support the creation of a single market that meets the idea of our fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted for this regulation because it will guarantee the possibility for consumers, everywhere in the european union, to lodge a complaint through cheaper, faster and simplified procedures. the european parliament has succeeded in ensuring that this regulation will apply to all disputes concerning online sales, regardless of where the seller is established, which will effectively protect consumers. the latter will be able to lodge a complaint on an online platform, set up and managed by the european commission, accessible via the your europe portal. in order to save time, all stages of the complaint can be handled online. the online dispute resolution platform will provide a standardised complaint form and will include an online translation functionality.
in writing. i voted in favour of the online dispute resolution for consumer disputes to set up a european platform to serve european citizens. these important texts are a concrete realization of the european project through the single market. online shopping is growing and offers new opportunities for european consumers who increasingly buy products outside their national borders. 30% of consumers have made an online purchase in the last three months. the new eu regulation will create an online platform where a standard form will be available in all eu languages and a guide for buyers to help them find the most suitable solution. the form, accessible via the 'europe is yours' portal, will be processed by the platform and will direct buyers to the most appropriate dispute resolution system. the establishment of a single point of contact is an important tool for citizens to facilitate the out-of-court resolution of consumer disputes.
in writing. today, many consumers and businesses are reluctant to buy or sell on the internet because they fear they will not know where to turn if they have a problem. however, the bodies competent to settle such disputes amicably are scattered and incomplete throughout the eu. moreover, while half of them offer consumers the possibility to submit their complaint online, very few allow them to complete the entire procedure there. that is why i voted in favour of this regulation: it provides for the creation of a platform which will offer consumers and traders a single point of contact for the out-of-court settlement of their online disputes, and will enable them to easily find the out-of-court dispute settlement body which is most appropriate to their case. the possibility of completing the entire procedure online via the platform, for those who wish to do so, will also save time for the parties and simplify communication between them. finally, we have provided for the platform to provide an electronic complaint model and digital translation, and for the information exchanged to be protected in accordance with european data protection and privacy rules.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which guarantees all consumers in the union the possibility of lodging complaints against traders using simple, fast and inexpensive procedures. the extrajudicial settlement of disputes advocated in this report seems to me to be an appropriate instrument for avoiding the traditional judicial procedure, which is often burdensome and bureaucratic for the citizen. the draft directive on out-of-court dispute settlement builds on existing mechanisms in some member states, while aiming to develop this type of recourse more widely in the eu.
in writing. this regulation sets out a set of measures that will enable european consumers to lodge complaints through simplified, faster and cheaper procedures. traders will be required to inform consumers of the odr bodies they depend on and how to contact them. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this regulation.
in writing. i am pleased that the european parliament has adopted legislation making it compulsory to set up dispute resolution mechanisms to resolve disputes between consumers and traders without a court ruling. this is a real breakthrough. one in five consumers had problems with a purchase in 2010, and most of them do not enforce their rights, due to the complexity and cost of legal action and their lack of knowledge of the out-of-court bodies. there are over 750 in europe, not always independent of companies, and not in all regions.
in writing. − j'ai voté en faveur de cette décision, car cette procédure de règlement extrajudiciaire des litiges de consommation est une alternative peu coûteuse, rapide et simple à la procédure judiciaire traditionnelle. il sera en effet beaucoup plus facile pour les citoyens européens de faire appel à cette procédure plutôt qu'à la procédure judiciaire classique, à laquelle il n'est pas toujours facile de s'adapter, du fait de sa complexité, de la longueur des procédures et, parfois, des coûts financiers élevés qu'elle peut engendrer pour les citoyens. partout dans l'union, la justice est confrontée à d'importantes restrictions budgétaires. il est important d'offrir aux citoyens, lorsqu'ils le souhaitent, une alternative leur permettant de trouver une issue plus rapide de leur dossier.
in writing. this text, which complements the draft online consumer dispute settlement, will also make it possible to better protect consumers in the event of a dispute with a trader. they will have quick and inexpensive access to alternative mediation systems to the often lengthy and very expensive trials. while most member states already have systems for out-of-court settlement of consumer disputes, their use by consumers remains complex and therefore uncommon. the text therefore obliges the member states to ensure that there are impartial mechanisms for the out-of-court settlement of consumer disputes in all economic sectors.
in writing. i supported this text, which will guarantee that any european consumer who has a problem with a consumer contract will have the opportunity to submit his complaint to an impartial, independent and high-quality out-of-court dispute settlement body. the prospect of a trial is often frightening. our idea here is to enable european consumers to settle their disputes with traders quickly, efficiently and inexpensively outside the traditional judicial channels, whether these disputes are related to goods or services, online or in-store, in the consumer's member state or across its borders. it should be stressed that access to justice is maintained by the directive: the handling of a complaint by an adr body will not deprive the parties of their right to be heard. in parallel, we plan to improve consumer and professional awareness of the existence and operation of these procedures, otherwise the exercise would be almost useless. we have for example made provision for the systematic obligation for traders to inform consumers of the odr bodies to which they belong and to indicate to them how to effectively contact them.

in writing. since the beginning of my mandate, i have worked tirelessly to defend the interests of the overseas countries and territories (octs). it is with this same logic of defending these territories that i have decided to vote in favour of the proposal for a decision on the association of the octs with the european union. convinced that these territories represent real assets for the union as a whole, and that the union should promote their economic and social development, i support the idea of a strengthened association agreement between the eu and the octs. i therefore believe that the identity and specific features of each oct should be better taken into account in this agreement, and that particular emphasis should be placed on the creation of sustainable jobs and regional cooperation between these territories, particularly with their neighbouring outermost regions. i also advocate that the interests of the octs be better taken into account in the trade agreements that the eu enters into with the neighbouring octs.
in writing. as promoters of its standards and values, the overseas countries and territories (octs) are europe's outposts and assets. and they are directly linked to the new challenges facing europe, such as the globalisation of trade, new environmental challenges or the risks of climate change. the current association decision (aoa) of 2001 between the octs and the eu sets out the legal framework for promoting the social and economic development of the octs and their economic relations with the eu. this decision shall expire on 31 december 2013. the renewal of this association framework is essential for the octs. the revision arrangements proposed by the commission last july were already a very good basis. the rapporteur has usefully supplemented them, making them a realistic and ambitious roadmap for the coming years. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i abstained from voting on the report introducing new requirements for monitoring radioactivity levels, not because i rejected the content of the proposal, but because i rejected the chosen legal basis. nuclear safety issues have so far been dealt with under the euratom treaty (intergovernmental approach), while the legal basis adopted for this text is the lisbon treaty (co-decision procedure). by abstaining i have indicated my refusal to see the legal bases being changed in this way.
in writing. although this resolution contains very important elements which i fully support, such as the public health imperative, i nevertheless wished to abstain from voting on it for a very different reason. this proposal should have continued to be legally based on the euratom treaty and not on the treaty of lisbon. the purely technical aspects and the substance contain interesting elements, since the aim is to protect public health by better regulating radioactive substances in drinking water, but the basic change proposed by the green group rapporteur sets a dangerous precedent. it would then risk extending to other aspects of our nuclear independence and subsidiarity. it would be unwise to adopt it without discussing the problems which would arise from such a change in the legal basis.
in writing. in the event of a nuclear accident, some food may be contaminated by radioactive particles in the air. the commission has proposed a text and maximum levels for this, but we think that these thresholds are too high, in accordance with the precautionary principle, and especially for sensitive people such as children or pregnant women. we want to have a say in this important matter and we demand codecision on this matter. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we will fight for the democratic determination of activities which may lead to radioactive contamination and the permissible levels of radioactivity. with this resolution, which i supported, we not only tried to improve public information - which must have sufficient information about the risks of nuclear activities in the vicinity - but also reviewed and changed the radioactivity standards, taking into account natural and artificial radioactivity and the type of population likely to be affected, especially sensitive and critical people.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because, in accordance with the precautionary principle, it is essential to use the scientific knowledge available to protect the health of the consumer, always taking into account the most vulnerable. i believe that it is necessary to strengthen the protection of the european consumer in the matter of drinking water and the radioactive substances that may be present in it. greater transparency on the quality of water consumed is required and as such, information on water quality, risks, and corrective measures must be easily accessible. in parallel, if certain parameters that serve as indicators of water quality are not respected, the state will have to take rapid measures to determine the cause, assess the level of risk, and initiate action to ensure the distribution of water. finally, member states should put in place monitoring programmes to check the quality of water on a regular basis.
in writing. a proposal for a directive on radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption was needed to complement the 1998 drinking water directive. the latter did not take into account a number of substances which are hazardous to health, such as tritium. the report by mrs rivasi corrects some essential points in the commission's proposal. the directive took as acceptable dosage limits not those for the most vulnerable, such as children, but those for adults. moreover, there is indeed a need to distinguish better between natural and artificial sources of radioactivity in order to ensure better control and better possibilities for long-term solutions. the report also criticises the fact that the directive is based on articles of the euratom treaty which do not allow the european parliament to be involved in co-decision with the council (the so-called ordinary legislative procedure). this is only an opinion. so this report is going in the right direction, which is why i voted in favour.
madam president, i voted against this report because the two-pack is locking the people of europe into a winter of austerity which will lead to ever greater unemployment and misery. so lower wages and pensions, higher taxes for the middle classes, and reduced social spending should lead to an improvement in our living conditions. what a foolishness! austerity benefits only the rentiers of finance, austerity, as in the 1930s, can lead to fascism. the american paul krugman, nobel prize winner in economics in 2008, who is not a communist, calls on european leaders to break with austerity and not to repay a public debt that is illegitimate and artificial. let's do as the icelanders did: refuse to pay back the tens of billions of illegitimate debts, nationalize the banks and jail the bankers responsible for the crisis for financial crime. while the rest of europe is in recession, iceland, which is being blamed by european leaders, is growing by 2.7%, driven by a rise in job creation. yes, we need an icelandic spring!
in writing. after more than a year of interinstitutional negotiations, the two-pack finally complements the stability and growth pact for the euro area countries adopted in 1997. this report promotes the deepening of economic and monetary union in order to deal with the economic and financial crisis affecting the european union today. in this context, the union has adopted procedures for budgetary and economic surveillance of the member states. the coordination of economic and social policies between states must respect a number of principles, such as responding to the democratic principles of the union and taking account of all the objectives and basic texts of the eu. the european parliament has therefore called for more democratic control over the interventions of the commission and the 'troika' (commission, ecb and imf). i voted in favour of this report, which was prepared by my colleague, mr jean-paul gauzès.
in writing. i voted in favour of the two-pack on economic governance. at a time when the member states are being asked to reduce their deficits, we have given the commission new powers to monitor the budgets of the euro area countries, under the control of the council and parliament. monitoring will be carried out in particular through the introduction of a 'european semester', a six-month period during which the commission will assess the budgetary objectives of the member states and help them to put in place sound budgetary policies. however, care must be taken that the budgetary efforts required of member states in difficulty are not at the expense of growth and employment.
in writing. i welcome the progress we have made in the two-pack. finally, proposals dating back to the report of the 'crisis' committee are back: the setting up of an expert group on the partial mutualisation of debt - in the form of a depreciation fund - and on 'eurobills'; proposals to provide the euro area with budgetary capacity to help countries in difficulty overcome their structural problems; proposals on the deduction of productive investment from the calculation of government deficits; the commission's commitment to combating tax fraud and tax evasion is stated in the declaration. as with the financial transaction tax, we were right too soon. the right, with its record, must be humble.
in writing. we now have new common preventive tools to dissuade member states from accumulating debts, to better monitor those benefiting from an aid programme and to better guard against the risk of contagion of financial difficulties from one member state to the whole euro area. beyond this accountability, the 'two-pack', which would have benefited from a more readable name, will make possible the solidarity that is indispensable today between the eurozone states when it comes to preventing the risks of financial and budgetary instability that can have serious repercussions on the whole union. another important step forward was the commission's commitment to set up a group of experts to analyse the feasibility of a partial pooling of part of the national debts of the eurozone via a european sovereign redemption fund and the creation of short-term bonds (eurobills). we've been calling them for a long time. finally, the union's budgetary surveillance activities will be subject to democratic control: the european parliament will now have a say in the activities of the troika and in the renewal of the commission's surveillance powers. this gives democratic legitimacy to decisions which have been taken for too long in the back of an intergovernmental chamber.
in writing. after a long and difficult negotiation, an agreement was reached on the two-pack of economic governance for the euro area. because we judge the consequences of austerity policies to be catastrophic for the peoples and economies, we have fought to change these two texts. the budget cuts will have to save investment for growth, the timetables for reducing deficits will be relaxed in the event of a severe recession, the commission will be subject to better scrutiny by the european parliament and national parliaments, and work will be carried out on debt mutualisation. these are steps in the right direction and i have therefore supported both texts.
in writing. parliament also adopted the two-pack of texts definitively during this part-session. these are regulations that strengthen budgetary surveillance within the euro area and the european union. by introducing increased surveillance for countries with excessive deficits and financial instability, these arrangements contribute to strengthened economic and fiscal governance, which is essential to prevent the implosion of our common currency. presented as the 'right of brussels to see' the preparation of national budgets, these texts in effect raise the question of greater interparliamentary cooperation at european level, between national parliaments and the european parliament, and of greater involvement of national parliamentarians in european affairs, both vis-à-vis their respective executives and vis-à-vis their fellow meps.
in writing. the two 'two-pack' proposals for regulations will increase the commission's powers of surveillance over member states' budgets. the commission will now have a right of review and intervention and will be able to decide on budget cuts and structural reforms to be implemented if the 3% deficit is not respected. it is our budgetary sovereignty which is now in the hands of the brussels technocracy. the consequences will be severe for the people of europe, who will be forced by brussels to undergo unprecedented austerity measures: lower wages and pensions, higher taxes and lower social spending. all measures that will worsen the economic crisis and poverty in europe. that is not what i want for my people and that is why i opposed the adoption of these two regulations.
in writing. the result of the trilogue is as one might expect: the height of austerity. the commission proposal is made even more serious by proposing to subject to increased surveillance all 'member states facing serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability' and not just those who request financial assistance. it is only to be welcomed that countries which do not comply with the austerity plans are no longer being cut off from eu payments. the only other austerity measures removed are those contained in the tscg, which is now in force in almost all the euro area. the troika's enhanced surveillance until 75% of the financial assistance granted has been repaid and beyond if necessary is also maintained. even the possibility of taking safeguard measures in respect of 'movements of capital to and from third countries which cause, or are likely to cause, serious difficulties for the functioning of economic and monetary union' was not considered. this text is a declaration of war on the democracy in force in our countries. i vote against and denounce the countless abuses of power which he institutes.
in writing. i voted against the proposal for a regulation on the strengthening of economic and budgetary surveillance of the member states of the european union. this regulation would allow a member state whose currency is the euro to be subject to enhanced surveillance when it is experiencing or is likely to experience financial disturbances; the commission's proposal is to establish a european system for the monitoring of the economic performance of the member states. in other words, this regulation only institutionalises the austerity measures at european level a little more, in line with the two-pack already adopted by the eu. i strongly reject the logic of these policies of austerity which are leading europe right into the wall. as the european countries are suffering the full brunt of the crisis, it is more necessary than ever to break with austerity. europe needs a lasting recovery based on the general interest and bringing about more solidarity in the euro area and the european union as a whole.
in writing. this report, like the report by the socialist elisa ferreira of the two packs, is part of the commission's twin legislative proposal on strengthening budgetary surveillance of the eurozone countries. it specifically concerns the enhanced budgetary and economic surveillance of euro-area member states in or threatened with financial difficulties. the final adoption by parliament, in agreement with the council, will make the budgetary surveillance of the countries receiving financial assistance more automatic and oblige them to submit to the commission so-called macroeconomic adjustment programmes. these states will have to adopt measures to combat sources of instability and to seek technical assistance from the commission. we all know what that means. this is nothing but the translation into european texts of the so-called budgetary treaty and therefore the callous pursuit of austerity measures. at a time when the french national assembly is about to vote on the nap, it is cynical to claim to involve trade union organisations and civil society in the process of adjustment programmes. i therefore voted against this report, which can only plunge the union and its peoples further into the recession they have been experiencing for years.
