in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which is part of the two-pack, because it makes it possible to ensure a more sound management of our euro area. these governance rules, initiated by nicolas sarkozy and angela merkel, are the final touch on fiscal convergence within the european union and the euro area. the european commission may ask a parliament to revise its copy if the planned national budget is in flagrant contradiction with the deficit reduction objective. however, national parliamentarians will continue to have the final say, and the two-pack does not entail any further transfer of sovereignty. parliament also called for the creation of an expert group on the introduction of euro bonds. the euro crisis has shown that without common rules and sound management of national public finances, the single currency cannot be viable. this text is a further step towards better european economic governance and a bulwark against further budgetary crises.
in writing. this legislative report, like the report by jean paul gauzès, is part of the 'two packs', the commission's double legislative proposal on strengthening budgetary surveillance in the euro area countries. the report covers the monitoring and evaluation of budgetary plans and the correction of excessive deficits in the euro area member states. the agreement reached between the council, the european parliament and the commission last february covers the monitoring of budgetary rules at national level by independent institutions, the submission of draft national budgets to the commission for evaluation and reorientation, if necessary, in accordance with the stability and growth pact, the introduction of graduated monitoring, including an 'early' detection of member states in excessive deficit including quasi-automatic sanctions for states that do not fit in, etc. this is nothing more than the translation into european texts of the so-called budgetary treaty and the callous pursuit of austerity measures which are daily plunging the european union deeper into recession. i therefore voted against this agreement and therefore cannot but regret that it was adopted by a very large majority in the european parliament (including the socialists and the greens).
in writing. we could not continue to have a common currency without coordinating the management of our national budgets! this worked for a while: the nordic countries, with their tradition of austerity, allowed the latin countries to go into debt at a low cost, taking advantage of the credibility and good health of the euro zone. but this asymmetry in the management of budgets has come under suspicion and some countries in crisis have almost taken the euro family with them in their fall. the euro area must now ensure better management of public money. this work began with the european stability treaty, initiated by nicolas sarkozy and angela merkel, and it ends with the two-pack. with these new rules we are now in a position to avoid the problems faced by some countries and which have threatened the whole euro area, with the commission now able to challenge national budgets which do not comply with deficit reduction obligations. far from losing its sovereignty, the commission will play its role as guardian of the euro's interests, which are closely linked to the interests of the member states, economic actors and citizens.

the rapporteur. - madam president, madam representative of the commissioner, i would first of all like to join in all the thanks that have just been addressed by the first rapporteur. i want to say a friendly word to the elected and administrative team that has accompanied me in this work. the commission's proposals for the common organization of the market mark a new stage. they mean that public resources for managing markets will now be more limited and they open up new possibilities for producers to organise themselves in order to have a greater say in trade negotiations. the committee on agriculture and rural development, however, considered it necessary to supplement them as they should take better account of a number of recent developments such as, for example, the increased volatility of raw material prices. the agricultural markets and production cannot therefore be left without any form of management. the safety net logic must therefore be fully developed: it is necessary, in particular, to ensure that the definition of reference prices and the arrangements for activating private storage aid are not totally disconnected from the evolution of prices on the markets, production costs and producers' margins. if we accept the general philosophy of disengagement, operated by the public authorities in the day-to-day management of the markets, leaving public intervention and private storage at a safety net level, this also presupposes that farmers have a clear vision of the market and that they can make their choice of manager in a transparent and fully informed manner. the role of the private sector is therefore much greater than in the past. this requires producers to gain real market power within the supply chain in order to rebalance the functioning of the supply chain. strengthening the market power of the agricultural production sector must thus enable the cap to achieve one of its fundamental objectives: to ensure a fair standard of living for the agricultural population, while guaranteeing consumers security of supply and health security at an acceptable cost, another essential objective of the cap. the tasks entrusted to producer organisations and interbranch organisations must therefore be secured and strengthened. they cannot, however, lead to the formation of cartels which divert producers from the necessary efforts to improve their competitiveness, innovation and production, which they must continue to make, but they must enable them to escape from the economic dependence in which they are still often locked up. it is still necessary that these tasks can be properly and effectively fulfilled in practice. this therefore requires a reflection on the application of competition law, which often thwarts joint initiatives by agricultural producers or sectors, even though their organisation and strengthening are at the heart of the reform of the cmu. the european union is also bound by international agreements. it must of course implement them, but it must do so only at the same rate as its partners are implementing them. i am thinking here of export refunds, which could only be used in the event of a serious crisis but which should be definitively eliminated only on the basis of full reciprocity with the main exporters of agricultural products. in the field of international trade, consumer protection also leads us to impose the same requirements on imported products as on intra-community products. finally, a word on some sectoral policies. the rights of plantation in viticulture are a fundamental guarantee of the economic, social and cultural balance of our territories. let's keep them safe. the sugar quotas should enable european production to become fully competitive on world markets for a few more years. let's protect them. milk quotas no longer seem to be the most appropriate solution for the development of a dynamic sector, but their abolition will create serious problems for many regions. let's go with them. by firmly defending these priorities, the european parliament will also be affirming its willingness to reach a renewed cap in a trilogue. i am sure the commissioner has the same wish.
the committee on regional development has tabled a number of amendments to the proposal. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, that is not the case. the new cap will not change the directions of our agriculture which are so harmful to the balance of our territories and to our future generations. as a member of the south-west, i can tell you that we are facing acute problems of water pollution, to the extent that france has been called to order by the commission for the level of nitrates in its watercourses in the lot and garonne and in the pyrénées-atlantiques. this pollution is mainly due to the monoculture of maize, which consumes a lot of water, inputs and pesticides, and which has been encouraged by successive cap reforms since 1992. without crop rotation, without compliance with the water and pesticides directive, without stopping gmos, without a ceiling on aid, the same logic of monoculture will prevail, with its harmful consequences. so, since this is the first time parliament has to take a decision, i ask the question: how long are we going to continue to subsidize modern epidemics which are linked to agriculture which is more concerned with its balance sheet than with the health of our children?
the committee on regional development has tabled a number of amendments to the proposal. - madam president, since 1968 the sugar sector has been governed by a common organization of markets based on the principles of quotas and prices. the new reform, after the one in 2006, completes, in my view, the weakening of all these principles. the common thread running through all this is clear: it is to bring it into line with the framework desired by the wto for ever greater liberalization of agricultural markets and products, with the ultimate aim that the reference price should be only the price set by the world market. i reject this logic because it condemns the sugarcane growers to the merciless rule of a large world market, which allows blind productivism and social dumping to triumph. if this reform is accepted as proposed by the commission, then the only thing that will ultimately remain for the sugarcane growers is the customs duties which could protect them from global competition, and we all know that this will not be enough. if we are to rely on the fate of banana production or milk production, we can only be skeptical. that is why our committee calls on all colleagues to adopt the proposal of the agri committee calling for a postponement until 2020. it is a postponement that is necessary, particularly for sugarcane growers in the outermost regions.

president of the commission. − mr president, madam president of the council, honourable members, i will today focus on the economic agenda of this week’s meeting of the european council and the key role it plays in the next phase of our reform path. it is crucially important to be aware of the debate taking place across europe about the state of our economy. in each and every member state, political opinion is passionate, public expectations are high, and rightly so. over the last months and years, through consistent and courageous efforts at both european and national levels, we have come a long way to fight the root causes of this crisis and to pave the way for a sustainable future. but we have yet to tackle the most immediate fears and concerns of many of our citizens. we must do everything possible, at all levels, to help them out of the crisis. there is justified disappointment about the slow recovery of the real economy. growth as an eu average was lower than expected at the end of last year and will be close to zero this year. unemployment figures are unprecedented and simply unacceptable. this means we must strengthen our focus and our resolve to respond to this crisis; a response that also addresses the short term needs and does not lose sight of the structural reforms we have signed up to; reforms that we know are necessary and that will form the basis of future sustainable growth. we can see that the reform efforts for competitiveness are starting to bear fruit, correcting very important imbalances in the european economy – most importantly in the programme countries. indeed, the example of ireland, the country holding the rotating presidency of the council, is a good demonstration of this point. let us not forget that less than one year ago analysts were speaking of the implosion of the euro. but now we see an improvement in terms of financial stability: since their high point in 2009, budget deficits have come down by half and they are expected to get down to the 3 % limit by the end of the year, while the interest rates paid by a number of member states have gone down significantly. current account imbalances are being corrected, and exports in some of the least well-performing member states are reviving. we can also note the progress in terms of overall economic confidence, with consumer confidence for the euro area improving by 30 basis points over the last months, and business confidence by 20. however, good news in some key areas should not hide the fact that there has not been enough progress to address the issue of growth, notably in the real economy, and that there was a deterioration of the employment situation. let me say that, when i see the situation in some of our member states, it is clear to me that some of the costs paid by the most vulnerable in our societies are becoming simply unbearable. fair burden-sharing must be a core element of our policies. let us also not forget why we are in this situation: we are still feeling the effects of a sorry state of affairs that was fuelled by unsustainable public debt and private debt and by irresponsible behaviour by many in the financial sector. we all knew that the process of adjustment would always have a negative effect in the short term. however, we cannot repeat the mistakes of the past, accumulating new debt and leaving structural reforms for competitiveness for later. in fact, we are correcting those mistakes, and we have reason to show more self-confidence over the progress europe has made so far. in the past year alone we have agreed on the compact for growth and jobs, we have agreed the fiscal pact, we have inaugurated the european stability mechanism, the ecb’s outright monetary transactions was announced, we reached a unanimous agreement on the single supervisory mechanism and we brokered a deal on the so-called ‘two pack’. let me congratulate the european parliament on the approval, yesterday, of this very important package of legislation. we have put flesh on the bones of the european semester and we are continuing to go forward in terms of financial sector regulation. all these decisions have given a clear signal on the irreversibility and integrity of the euro, and have sent the right message about europe’s capacity to act. on top of that, the commission has presented its blueprint for a deep and genuine economic and monetary union, offering a vision of future developments and integration. we will not allow the momentum for the european union’s reform to slow down. the proper functioning of the emu requires that its governance structures are completed, in particular in the area of economic policy coordination and support to structural reforms. that will be the focus of the june european council, and we are already working on specific measures and a time-bound road map on the ex-ante coordination of major economic reforms; on the social dimension of the emu, including the social dialogue; and on a framework for mutually agreed contracts for competitiveness and growth, combined with the respective solidarity mechanisms. at the same time, we are pursuing the social agenda as an integral part of our strategy to exit the crisis. the position we took in the mff discussions consistently made the same point: that the european investment agenda needs also to focus on solidarity and growth, aiming funds at those who need our support the most. the youth employment initiative, the youth employment package which includes the youth guarantee scheme and the social investment package are just a few examples. let us be honest, we need short term measures to reinforce the perspectives for growth. implementation of the compact for growth and jobs is too low and too slow. mr president, today's syria is a country of 70,000 dead, two and a half million internally displaced persons and a million refugees in neighbouring countries. the humanitarian situation in syria is catastrophic and dramatic and the aid provided is paltry in relation to the needs. the worst thing is the children. two million syrian children are suffering from malnutrition, disease and multiple traumas. what action do you envisage for them? the list of dead grows longer, while europe is hesitating between the us and swiss agendas. the union must quickly and firmly mobilise all the actors for an effective and lasting solution to the crisis. a strong political will from the eu would save lives and bring about a political solution to the syrian crisis. i call on the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy to conclude an agreement on humanitarian aid as a matter of urgency, allowing people to access convoys across borders and front lines and guaranteeing the safety of humanitarian workers, medical facilities and patients.
member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, the last time we discussed the situation in mali, on 15 january, the situation was in full crisis. i want to explain the progress made since then, the european union’s role in it, the challenges that remain, and what we are doing to support mali – and the region – in overcoming them, so that the people of mali can live in peace and security and return to the path of development. i must pay tribute first of all to the efforts and sacrifices of one member state, france, in driving the terrorists out of the cities and regions of the north, taking the battle to their retreats in the northern mountains. i pay tribute also to all those who have provided support to that effort, whether european, african or american, in particular the armed forces of chad, who have made a significant sacrifice. thanks to these efforts, the people of northern mali have been liberated from control by the terrorists, but we must not underestimate the threat that remains. this requires security forces to remain present and active, to head off potential terrorist attacks in the future. but the situation is now very different. we are today acting on all fronts in a coordinated manner. this is an illustration of what a comprehensive approach is all about and how we turned it into concrete actions. since the extraordinary foreign affairs council in january, we have convened two crisis platforms, with all eu services involved, in order to produce a comprehensive overview of our activities – covering the european union training mission, our support to the african-led international support mission to mali (afisma) and a quick identification of a stabilisation and development package. we have also immediately deployed in the field an inter-service mission to support our delegation in bamako. this has made it possible to identify european union activities in the field of stabilisation and development, but also to start implementing them. our work involves liaising diplomatic activity with security and policy development in a mutually reinforcing way. on the security side, our long-term objective is to enable the malian security services and armed forces to protect their own citizens. this is why we accelerated the planned launch of the eu training mission to 18 february. the force commander is there and the first counselling actions have already taken place. if things go according to plan, training of forces should begin in april. this has required great effort on the part of the member states, but there has been a real collective will to act. with this training mission, we aim to help the re-structuring of the armed forces to ensure their effectiveness and we plan to make sure that human rights is part of the training of the malian troops. united nations human rights experts are already in the field and we are also working with the african union to provide monitors to afisma forces. it is encouraging that mali has withdrawn five of its troops from timbuktu following accusations of human rights abuses. this must be taken seriously. there are still challenges in re-equipping the malian forces, but we are working on it. it will take time for the malian forces to be ready. the european union is therefore supporting afisma with eur 50 million, committed at the fund-raising meeting hosted by the african union on 29 january 2013. a number of member states are helping train and equip afisma troop-contributing countries. as you know, converting afisma into a un-hatted force would assure future funding. the discussions on such an option are presently going on in new york, where the united nations secretary general should report to the security council before the end of this month. on the political track, the high representative hosted a meeting in brussels of the international follow-up and support group on 5 february. the malian government presented its roadmap for the transition back to democratic and constitutional rule. the european union has pledged to support its implementation. on behalf of the high representative, i would like to stress two key elements. firstly, the establishment of the national commission for dialogue and reconciliation on 6 march, which should bring together all the different political forces in the country, including from the north, to discuss how to rebuild the country’s political structures on an inclusive basis. it is essential that the political structure is free of military influence and inspires the trust of all communities. secondly, the holding of presidential elections by end of july 2013, to re-establish a legitimate national government following the coup d’état a year ago, which interrupted the elections planned for april last year. legislative elections will follow later. we will provide assistance to the electoral process and, as you know, we are examining the possibility of an electoral observation mission. finally, on the development and stabilisation track: european union development ministers have agreed to gradually resume european union aid to mali. eur 250 million is available under the edf for state-building contract budget support and specific projects in the field of small irrigation and key infrastructure. an additional eur 20 million of fast-disbursing assistance is available from the instrument for stability to support the restoration of public authorities and services in post-conflict areas, for reconciliation activities and for the first phase of the electoral process. we will host two important meetings in the near future to support mali. in early april the high representative will co-chair, with ms bachelet, the un women’s envoy, and with romano prodi, the un special envoy for the sahel, a meeting on women in the sahel. their role will be vital in re-establishing a stable and viable future for the region. women’s rights and gender balance must be an integral part of everything we do. talent is wasted, wisdom is lost and economic opportunities are missed when a society refuses to break with inequality, whether in north africa, europe or indeed the sahel. secondly, in mid-may, the european union and france will convene in brussels a high level international conference on development in mali, to bring together the key donors to coordinate our support for the reconstruction of the country. the government of mali will present its 2013-14 national action plan as a basis for our collective action to help restore the economy and government services. the high representative is conscious that solving mali’s problems, in development and food resilience as much as in the struggle against terrorism and political exclusion, requires an approach that encompasses the whole sahel region. that is the principle underlying the eu’s strategy for security and development in the sahel, which remains as relevant as ever. in the same spirit, a european union special representative for the sahel is to be nominated in the coming days. the european union will remain heavily engaged and fully committed to mali and the region. it is in our interests to do so, as instability in the sahel can threaten our own citizens. so we will continue to help the people of mali in their efforts to re-establish their sovereignty, democracy and prosperity.

in writing. the european parliament (ep) is not involved in the negotiation of the european development fund (edf) because this instrument is not part of the european budget. the budgetisation of the edf is a recurring request from the green group, which proposes that the edf be financed by own resources such as the financial transaction tax. the commission plans to budget this by 2020. even if our influence is limited at present, the debate on the future edf budget is nevertheless fundamental in the ep. this 11th edf will finance eu cooperation with african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries and the overseas countries and territories (octs) for the period 2014-2020. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report because it shows the will of the members to work towards a better relationship between the eu and the acp countries and the octs. we need a budget that is up to the objectives we have set, which are, in the long run, the eradication of poverty and the independence of the beneficiaries from the donors.
in writing. the eu is currently the world's largest provider of development aid and is an undisputed world leader in this field. it is essential that the union and its member states maintain their commitments to the poorest, and in particular that they do not abandon their objective of allocating 0.7% of their income to development aid. however, it is clear that the budget decided by the council for the 11th edf - the main instrument for the provision of eu development assistance to the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries and the overseas countries and territories (octs) - which is €3 billion lower than the european commission's proposal, is far from living up to the union's commitments. it is essential to send a clear message in defence of international solidarity, and i have therefore voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the financing of cooperation with the acp states and the octs for the period 2014-2020. in addition to a budget that is adequate, i would like to see the principle of policy coherence for development applied more effectively. i also support better coordination of programmes between the acp countries, the octs and their neighbouring outermost regions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution rejecting the political agreement reached by the eu heads of state and government on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. the european parliament has opposed a very large majority to a draft budget which is being reduced, without a vision, without a strategy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services. the union needs a budget that is better adapted to its present and future needs, so as to give priority to economies of scale and more efficient management in the long term. we fought on four fronts: the consolidation of budgets for the 2013 amending budget, budget flexibility, the introduction of a revision clause and finally the need to provide the eu with own resources. this resolution does not yet represent the final vote of the european parliament, but it defines the mandate of the parliament for the forthcoming negotiations with the council.
in writing. with this vote, the european parliament says no to the agreement of 8 february. as it stands, copying is not acceptable. reaffirming our role as legislators, we set out our conditions for opening negotiations with the supporters of a europe without ambition, coherence and vision. to date, this budget of austerity, this budget of the past and of shopkeepers, has been hammering away at a multiannual financial framework that is in no way capable of restoring confidence in european construction to european citizens who are still hard hit by the crises. because let us be serious: who can believe today that the union will fulfil its missions, defend growth and employment with a budget representing 1% of european gdp and more than fifty derogations - in the form of various gifts - made to each other? in the long term, the european budget should be in the order of 4 or 5% of european gdp. it is only on this basis that we can really achieve a sustainable development policy, a social pact for europe, an ambitious research policy, a european energy policy capable of achieving the objectives of a low-carbon economy, a policy of major works and infrastructure (maritime, rail, river).
in writing. i voted against the proposed agreement in its current form because it does not reflect the priorities and concerns related to the general european interest. under the lisbon treaty, the european parliament must now approve the budget, which was not the case for previous multiannual financial years. we have just been vigorously asserting the rights of the only european institution democratically elected by the citizens of europe. the multiannual framework has been designed to ensure the sustainable financing of major european policies. but here, this multiannual framework now prevents any funding for genuine common policies. we need more flexibility between budget lines and from one year to the next. we must be able to demand the possibility of revising the budget for the current year and we need to set up own resources for the eu, which are currently financed by almost 80% of the member states' contributions. nor is it possible to accept a budget with an estimated deficit of between 16 and 17 billion euros for 2013 alone. this would be to guarantee a financial framework which could lead the eu budget into a structural deficit.
in writing. by voting in favour of this resolution, we wanted to send a clear warning to the heads of state and government: we will not accept this multiannual financial framework as long as our demands, those of the europeans, are not taken into account. our demands are clear: growth, competitiveness, solidarity. for a europe that protects europeans, for a europe of solidarity, for a europe of dynamism, which does not mortgage its future. we do not want our ambitions for the next seven years to be reduced by gloomy forecasts linked to the crisis we are currently experiencing. we therefore ask for the possibility of revising this financial framework which is currently being implemented. the negotiations with the council will therefore be able to rely on a strong parliament position, in the forefront of defending the interests of all europeans.
in writing. our parliament has rejected the draft budget 2014-2020. it has rightly asked for the council's commitment on four points. debt settlement: the council must commit itself without delay to settling its past debts without deferring them to future years: the union cannot suffer from growing deficits, already estimated at some eur 17 billion, if it fails to meet its commitments. flexibility between headings and over time: the long-term budget must be flexible enough to meet new challenges. budgetary review: in the context of global economic and political changes, it is no longer possible to decide once and for all on guidelines for seven years. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budget is properly implemented. own resources: these would gradually replace the current system based on national contributions and put an end to small-scale bargaining by the states. our parliament has a duty more than ever to lift europe up. it starts with a healthy, fair budget.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which rejects the compromise adopted by the member states on the 2014-2020 budget. as proposed by the council on 7 and 8 february, the budget for the next seven years will be, for the first time in the history of europe, lower than the previous period. it is this regression in the construction of europe that the european parliament has rejected. the european parliament must be united in its strong defence of an increased and future-oriented eu budget. only at european level will it be possible to cope with the crisis through investments in the energy transition, aid to the most deprived and training for young people. the european parliament will have a say for the first time in approving or rejecting the budget. i voted for this resolution because it recalls the need for an open, transparent vote, allowing the citizen to see what each member has voted.
in writing. i supported this resolution on the negotiation of the european union's multiannual financial framework. because we need an ambitious budget, serving the general european interest, especially in times of crisis, we reject the agreement reached at the european council on 7 and 8 february in its present form. several conditions will have to be met for parliament to validate the 2014-2020 european budget: the budget will have to be flexible in time and according to the programmes, a mid-term review will allow other budgetary guidelines to be defined for the following years, and a system of own resources will finally be established to feed the european budget.
in writing. on 13 march, the european parliament adopted its position on the european budget for the period 2014-2020. this vote marks the start of negotiations with the european commission and the member states. in this period of severe budgetary constraints, everyone must tighten their belts, including brussels. nevertheless, the agreement reached by the heads of state or government on 8 february is not the right solution. the agreement reduces the cap budget by 11%, the regional cohesion policy budget by 8%, the budget for the solidarity fund by half and the globalisation aid fund by one third, which is intended to help workers affected by factory closures and restructuring to make a new career. the aid for the poorest, which i have been fighting for for two years, is down by a third, and it's only 5 cents a day in aid to the beneficiaries. what parliament is proposing is simple: to revise the budget so that it is more responsive and adapted to the needs of citizens and businesses. the european budget is 94% investments in competitiveness, research, regional aid and the cap.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution to show my determination to ensure that the voice of the european parliament is heard and that its power of co-decision on budgetary matters is respected, and i am glad that it has finally been adopted. i think the budget agreement reached by the member states is very disappointing, both in its overall amount, which has fallen for the first time, and in its lack of flexibility. we therefore call for the possibility of revising the current budget, for the reimbursement of the deficit incurred for 2013, but also for the establishment of own resources for the european union, which is currently financed by the member states to the tune of about 80%, which places it in a situation of too great dependence.
in writing. on wednesday, we voted on the agreement negotiated by the heads of state and government of the 27 eu countries on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, which is, in a sense, the eu's multiannual financial law. we voted a resolution which clearly expresses our rejection of this agreement as it stood at the european council on 7 and 8 february. we believe that the european union needs a budget that favours growth and competitiveness in europe through genuine solidarity. the sums contained in this agreement give priority to national achievements and do not make it possible to prepare for the future by financing genuine common policies. this is why the european parliament has proposed that the main lines of this budget be reoriented towards more investment in sectors of the future. we also want more flexibility in the way the budget works and, above all, we want real progress to be made in the area of the union's own resources.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the multiannual financial framework, as it does not reflect the priorities of parliament and neglects its role as provided for in the lisbon treaty. in order to respect the treaty, it is not acceptable that the figures proposed by the council do not respect the principle of budgetary balance with an amount of expenditure greater than the ceilings for commitment appropriations. the problem of unpaid invoices in 2012 should also be resolved before the conclusion of the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework (mff). indeed, european programmes such as erasmus were short of funds at the beginning of the year because the bills were not paid by the member states. we also want a part of the european budget to come from own resources and thus reduce the share of contributions based on gross national income in the union budget to a maximum of 40%. finally, more transparency is needed in the way member state representatives negotiate and agree on national allocations under the cohesion policy and the common agricultural policy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution rejecting the conclusions of the european council of 7 and 8 february on the multiannual financial framework. the draft agreement of the european council on the future multiannual financial framework of the european union for the next seven years is unacceptable, because it paves the way for seven years of austerity and economic slowdown in europe and denies the notion of european solidarity. the proposed agreement provides for cuts in areas which mainly affect the lives of european citizens in times of crisis, including the poorest citizens, youth, farmers and fishermen, researchers, local authorities and environmental projects, thus fuelling the growing rejection of the european union by its peoples. i cannot accept the abandonment of the redistributive policies of the european union and the abandonment of the project of a union based on solidarity.
in writing. with a decline of 3.5% in current euros compared to the period 2007-2013, the financial framework proposed by the heads of state or government is inadequate for an enlarged europe with new powers. at a time when everyone is recognising the need for greater european integration, i do not think we will be able to do much more with much less. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution on the conclusions of the european council of 7 and 8 february which calls for this proposal to be rejected as it stands. it is now to be hoped that the negotiations now under way will make it possible to bring about significant improvements to this multiannual financial framework. to meet the challenges of the crisis, europe needs to become more involved in growth and competitiveness policies such as research, development, infrastructure, training and support for smes, and to do more to tackle the distressing problem of youth unemployment. while the budgetary resources of the member states are very limited, it should also be remembered that the pooling of expenditure at european level would allow for serious savings in the public expenditure of the member states for a more efficient result.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it is essential that the european parliament can take part in the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework (mff). the lisbon treaty allows it to do so and parliament must ensure that its legislative prerogatives are respected. the european union must find solutions quickly for its future and its citizens, and the mff negotiations must be refocused on the objectives of growth, employment, competitiveness and solidarity between member states. in order to ensure sustainable financing of community policies, we must focus on a flexible mff, allowing for the transfer of amounts from one sector to another, in order to achieve a fairer and more balanced budget. the commission is also proposing to introduce a review clause so that in future parliament can express its views on the mff and adapt it to changes in the economic situation. finally, the eu needs to have its own resources to pursue its objectives and values. finally, the commission must resolve the issue of the 2013 amending budget to cover payment appropriations not used in 2012.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because the proposal for a multiannual financial framework finalised by the european council of 7 and 8 february 2013 is not acceptable as it stands. we must send a strong political message: we reject this agreement unless the council and our assembly start genuine, open and transparent negotiations. our red lines include investments for growth, for jobs, the european fund for the poorest, which has been cut by more than 30%, erasmus, crossborder cooperation and investments in research and innovation. we also ask for respect for our legislative prerogatives, a revision clause once the budgetary crisis has passed and a change in the nature of the union's resources, which are too dependent on contributions from the member states. after the bargaining of the states, the democratic debate must take over.
in writing. - the resolution on the agreement of the european council of 7 and 8 february on the multiannual budget expresses parliament's position on a number of important points. i agree that more flexible funding allocation conditions should be introduced, as well as the possibility of revising the budget at mid-term to meet specific economic challenges. the eu must also be strictly own resource-based, for example, part of the revenue from the new financial transaction tax should be channelled to the eu's own resources. the successful implementation of the europe 2020 strategy is needed in the face of major economic, political and social challenges. this requires increased investment in innovation, research and development, infrastructure and other growth-enhancing areas. unfortunately, the european council agreement provides for an 8% or €29.6 billion cut in funding for economic, social and territorial cohesion. at the same time, eu administrative expenditure is expected to remain at 6%, with an increase of eur 4.5 billion in absolute terms. the increase is also foreseen in budget headings not related to the recovery of economic growth. for example, the security and citizenship section is expected to grow by €3.3 billion, or 27%, and the eu's foreign policy-related global europe section by almost €1.9 billion, or 3%. in these areas, it would be possible to reduce expenditure, for example by optimising the functioning of diplomatic missions in third countries and by implementing more effective defence cooperation.
in writing. i have of course voted against the european council's draft agreement on the multiannual financial framework. the european budget represents only a small part of eu policies: more or less 1 000 billion for 7 years. in favour of national self-interest (more than 500 discounts on a case-by-case basis), the few solidarity programmes were the most affected by the reductions made by the member states. the drastic cut in food aid is symptomatic of this agreement: €1 billion less than the €3.5 billion of the eafrd, and this at a time when it is being extended to all member states, and when the number of poor people in the eu is reaching a sad record. i welcome the fact that this resolution was voted by a large majority (including, it should be noted, members who are usually supportive of austerity policies). the european parliament thus affirms its determination to exercise fully its legislative prerogatives over the european budget. it is to be hoped that this determination will be lasting... i regret that all the gue/ngl amendments calling for a fairer system of contributions for the member states have been rejected.
in writing. i welcome today's vote which demonstrated that parliament has fully assumed its role as co-decider of the budget provided for by the lisbon treaty. the council has announced the adoption of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, which is the fruit of bargaining and lacks any vision for the future despite the efforts of the socialist minority and in particular françois hollande. the overwhelming majority of meps are speaking for the people, demanding today another ambition for the europe of tomorrow, namely a policy of collective growth based on innovation and with the necessary resources to finally overcome the crisis. to do this, europe needs real own resources so as not to be dependent on the contributions of the member states, which account for 80% of its budget. moreover, it is unacceptable that the planned budget should be structurally in deficit. at the end of 2012, 16 billion was missing, which prevented the funding of erasmus! we therefore demand a revision clause so that we can change this budgetary framework from 2014 onwards, after the elections in germany and the european parliament, which i hope will open up new prospects and put an end to this absurd and suicidal austerity cure, the bible of the european conservatives.
in writing. the council has proposed a multiannual financial framework 2014-2020: i would give it the "can do better" label. the present situation requires that we control our expenditure and national contributions. but be careful not to make the union a giant with feet of clay, with a budget that would render it impotent. our demands are clear: we support a lower budget, subject to the triple condition of a mid-term review, flexibility between budget lines and budget years and alignment of payment and commitment appropriations. why would you do that? because we can expect a recovery in growth that will allow for greater investment by 2015-2016. because it is essential that we can break down this multiannual budget into annual budgets which can be adapted to the needs. and because it is inconceivable that the appropriations committed at the beginning of the year are no longer guaranteed at the end of the year. ladies and gentlemen, our budget is not a spending budget but an investment budget. our fellow citizens are asking us to make exemplary efforts, but not to turn the union into an empty shell, without resources and therefore without results. i ask the council to revise its copy, proposing a budget which is indeed in crisis but which is fair, effective and negotiable in the process.
in writing. the european union needs independent, reliable, comparable and timely statistics and economic accounts to analyse the economic situation of a member state or region. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which aims to update and improve the rules for the collection and publication of this key macro-economic data in the union. this report aims at a thorough revision of the european system of accounts, building on the latest revision of the united nations system of national accounts in 2008. this should produce the highest quality statistics based on a viable methodology, gradually moving towards automated real-time data collection by member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new system for collecting and publishing key macroeconomic data in the eu member states. in times of crisis, it is important for policy-makers, economic voters and citizens to have reliable, independent and timely data. i could not but welcome this new accounting system which integrates environmental and social accounts
in writing. this report concerns the revision of the european system of national and regional accounts (esna), which brings together macroeconomic statistical data from the member states in order to analyse the coordination and convergence of economic policies. this is already a programme in the present context and one shudders when it is stated that we must move towards automated methods of real-time data collection to ensure "maximum transparency". numbers, especially those relating to public accounts, can be used to tell a lot. we see this every day now when we try to understand european politics. this purely quantitative view of economic and especially budgetary policies leads nowhere. a hospital, for example, is not an investment, a cost to be justified from an economic point of view, but a matter of public health and general interest. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. the european union must comply with the requirements of the international conventions to which it is a party. the maritime sector is not exempt from this: the maritime labour convention adopted by the international labour organisation calls for the definition of common minimum standards for all flags and seafarers. directive 2009/13/ec is in line with this international body of legislation to ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships. i supported this report, which fills a gap in the directive as regards the responsibility of the flag state: the proposal aims to harmonise the conditions of competition in this sector by applying the maritime labour convention in all european ports. the amendments submitted should provide flag states with a sound reference framework for verifying the compliance of vessels with directive 2009/13/ec.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the provisions of the maritime labour convention 2006 on flag state control should be incorporated into eu law in a more detailed and specific way. the incorporation of the maritime labour convention into european union law has the major advantage of ensuring a much stricter enforcement regime within the union, for example through european union infringement procedures. in order to avoid differences of interpretation between member states, which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping, the provisions of the european union concerning flag state control should take much better account of the specific and express requirements of the maritime labour convention.
in writing. the year 2014 will be the first year of implementation of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. i voted in favour of this report, which states that the priorities for 2014 are sustainable and competitive economic growth, the recovery of employment and the fight against youth unemployment. i welcome the fact that this report calls for the union to be endowed with its own resources in order to ensure its independence from the member states and that it provides for an improvement in the accuracy of budget forecasts, which must be realistic and sufficient. the report also rightly recalls the increase in the level of outstanding commitments to be paid and highlights the role played by the european supervisory authorities in financial regulation and supervision. the regulation on this financing framework therefore calls for a sufficient and realistic level of payments in order to avoid unnecessary complications in the implementation of the budget. finally, it affirms the key role of the union budget in implementing the europe 2020 strategy and in economic growth and job creation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the budgetary guidelines for 2014, which will be the first year of application of the multiannual financial framework. the european budget suffers from delays in payment of the 2012 budget, which is insufficient for 2013. the 2014 guidance is focused on a realistic level of payment, with a focus on supporting economic growth and employment. as part of the horizon 2020 perspective, i could only support guidelines that focus on spending on smes, research and vocational training.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the jensen report on the guidelines for the 2014 budget - section iii. it shows a great deal of foresight in spending priorities, and this in a context of crisis and with limited resources. the parliament thus places growth, competitiveness and employment, especially for young people, at the top of its priorities. i am also very keen to see the proposal for reform of the own resources system, since the current system has shown its limitations, by not allowing the european union to meet its obligations in terms of payments.
in writing. at a time when the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework is the focus of all attention, we are now looking at the 2014 budget. in view of the difficulties encountered in the implementation of the 2012 budget, we are sending a clear message here: the 2014 budget will be a budget for growth, but a budget for balance. the european budget is an indispensable tool for investment in europe, it is our best lever for recovery. but it must not be based on falsehoods, and the question of the amounts still to be paid for the previous year must therefore be settled as soon as possible.
