in writing. this report, which i voted in favour of, contains provisions for the event that the various parties to the current budget negotiations fail to reach agreement in time, which seems increasingly likely. the text suggests in particular that the european commission may draw up a draft budget for 2014 on the basis of its own proposals and that it may extend the ceilings for the last year of the current multiannual financial framework, adjusted with a fixed deflator of 2% per year, until the adoption of the new multiannual financial regulation. this would allow the european commission to set a realistic level of payments for 2014 and to settle the european union's debts quickly to avoid further bottlenecks in negotiations and budgetary situations similar to last year.
in writing. the european budget, which is largely devoted to investment in the member states, remains a privileged tool for overcoming the crisis that has been affecting us for years. i therefore voted in favour of mrs jensen's report, which reaffirms the role of this budget in promoting growth, employment and competitiveness. in particular, we reiterate our willingness to invest in training, research, innovation, infrastructure and support for smes, with a specific focus on youth unemployment, which is reaching alarming proportions in many countries. that is why i am very concerned about the fact that the member states are not honouring the payments they owe to the european budget, even though most of them have increased their own budgets in recent months. the european budget, however, makes it possible to achieve significant savings in public expenditure by pooling resources and thus to support the essential return to balance in the national accounts.
in writing. the distribution of seats in the european parliament was to be revised as a result of the treaty of lisbon establishing a maximum number of 751 meps (compared with 754 today) and in anticipation of the forthcoming arrival of croatian meps in the chamber. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report on the distribution of seats in the european elections due to take place from 22 to 25 may 2014, even though i do not find it entirely satisfactory. it shall determine the distribution of seats in accordance with the principle of degressive proportionality. to this was added an additional rule: no loss of more than one seat per state (except germany). while some ten countries will lose seats in the parliamentary chamber, france will retain its current seats. i do not consider this choice to be fully satisfactory because it creates a gap in representation (number of members per citizen) between the member states. however, we needed a quick solution and i supported it because we demand that it be only temporary. a new proposal for a more sustainable and transparent distribution of seats will be tabled by parliament in 2015.
in writing. in a democracy, the composition of the members responsible for representing the voice of the citizens is a crucial issue. at european level, this issue is of a particular nature. the european parliament, let us repeat, the only european body elected by direct suffrage, has therefore the duty, if not the obligation, to reflect as closely as possible the demographic weight of the various member states. this report takes completely unfounded liberties with this elementary principle. the common thread of this report, refusing to change the existing distribution more than marginally, is to lock the european parliament into a status quo which is clearly unacceptable. the entry of croatia into the european union should have allowed for a redistribution of cards. it's not like that. so it is a very unfortunate missed opportunity.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of this report, which aims to achieve a more balanced distribution of seats between the member states in the european parliament following the accession of croatia in july next year. a concrete measure is the two-stage approach: this proposal would apply only to the 2014-2019 parliamentary term, and it is planned to present by the end of 2015 a new proposal for a decision establishing a sustainable and transparent system that would allow for the allocation of seats in an objective manner, based on the principle of degressive proportionality.
in writing. the accession of croatia on 1 july requires an adjustment in the number of seats allocated to each country, in accordance with the treaty of lisbon, which sets a maximum of 751 meps. it currently takes less than 70 000 citizens to elect a maltese mep, but it takes almost 900 000 to elect a french mep. i therefore voted in favour of this report, although it is not perfect. as it is politically impossible to reduce the number of german members by more than three, france, the united kingdom and spain are abnormally under-represented. this could only be avoided by increasing the number of members from these countries. but the arrival of croatian members cannot be used as a pretext for increasing the number of french members. i would like to see a system in place in future, before each election to the european parliament, which will make it possible to allocate seats between the member states in an objective manner, on the basis of the principle of degressive proportionality, taking account of any increase in their number and demographic developments, without excluding the possibility of reserving a certain number of seats for members elected on transnational lists.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the composition of the european parliament for the 2014 european elections, tabled by mr trzaskowski and mr gualtieri. the solution proposed by the two co-rapporteurs is pragmatic and politically realistic, as it deals with the complex and extremely important question of the democratic legitimacy of elected members of the european parliament and the european parliament. in view of the enlargement of the eu to include croatia, and the fact that the number of meps is capped at 751 by the treaty of lisbon, the number of meps per member state will logically be modified while minimising seat losses. i will continue to be vigilant, together with the french delegation of the epp, to ensure that a member state such as france does not see its representation in the european parliament reduced.
in writing. meps from the democratic movement contest the political approach of the rapporteurs regarding the composition of the european parliament in 2014 and voted against it. the treaty of lisbon provides that the european parliament is to be composed of representatives of the citizens of the union, whose representation is to be ensured on a degressively proportional basis. but this democratic principle has now been denied. whatever the mathematical formula used, the degressive proportionality should have given france additional seats, but also spain, italy and the united kingdom. instead of following this legally established path, the report, which aims to integrate future croatian elected representatives, is content to maintain the current balance, de facto leading to the principle of representation of the peoples, the foundation and raison d'être of the european parliament, being called into question. the ball is now in the council's court. it will be up to france, with the help of other member states, to find a solution which respects the letter and the spirit of the treaty.
in writing. the european parliament was to decide on the future composition of its assembly from 2014. the logic would have been that some member states would gain more seats and that medium-sized powers would lose more. the solution was a kind of status quo, with no state winning or losing more than one seat, with a meeting clause in the run-up to the 2019 elections to find the most relevant and least chaotic solution. this delicate choice avoids pitting national delegations against each other in the context of the electoral campaign and crystallizing debates on this secondary issue. in approving this report, the european parliament has chosen to act with wisdom and caution. france will not lose a seat in 2014, and i believe that the immediate interest of voters is not the number of meps they are struggling to identify, but the programmes, actions and solutions that the european parliament, a real legislative power too little known, can propose in order to respond to the real concerns of citizens, such as employment and purchasing power.
in writing. i voted in favour of this pragmatic, albeit not ideal, resolution proposed by the two rapporteurs of the text. it is true that the solution adopted only partially respects the principle of degressive proportionality which derives from the european treaties and that it will deprive certain states, including france, of several seats to which they could have claimed by virtue of the same principle. but when it comes to budget negotiations, it is necessary to avoid the division between the most populous member states and the others, and in the face of the lengthy negotiations that this debate on the composition of the parliament for the 2014 elections has raised, the word 'compromise' makes perfect sense. i believe that it is essential for an elected official to keep in mind the reason for his work and his political struggles, which is the general interest, and this was indeed the most realistic solution, the one that went in the direction of the maximum general interest for the citizens of europe. i am therefore pleased that it was adopted today and that the reservations of some have not overridden the general interest.
in writing. we took a position on the report on the composition of the european parliament for the 2014 elections, which will allow our eleven future croatian colleagues to enter the parliament, if the ratification process for croatia's accession is confirmed. we propose that twelve states, in addition to germany, which will lose three seats under the lisbon treaty, lose one seat each. the 're-allocation of seats' due to the accession of croatia nevertheless gave rise to the question of the representation of the member states, which must be in line with demographic developments. it will be up to the next parliament, the one elected in 2014, to work on a system of seat allocation that meets the expectations of our citizens: balanced, modern, transparent and democratic. as vice-chairman of the afco committee, i spoke about the current under-representation of france. but it did not seem to me sensible or politically expedient, when other hot topics confront the eu, to advocate, unlike the french government and some of my colleagues, an increase in the number of french meps.
in writing. absinthe is the fruit of a traditional recipe combining artemisia l., absinthe and anise, appreciated by its consumers for its characteristics and its long tradition of production. in order to harmonize legislation to protect the european absinthe-producing sector, the commission had rightly proposed a balanced and qualitative definition of absinthe in european legislation. this commission proposal was the result of a fair compromise between all the players in the sector. this definition was relevant in many respects, notably to protect consumers with quality products. i therefore deeply regret the european parliament's veto of this compromise, which puts quality absinthe at risk, since there is still no definition recognised at european and international level. this is to take the risk that switzerland will appropriate the term 'absinthe' by registering it as a geographical indication and prohibiting its marketing to european producers.
in writing. i voted against the resolution calling into question the european definition of absinthe. the name 'absinthe' is a guarantee of quality, and selling it in this way opens the door to a lower quality absinthe, misleads the consumer and opens the way for the swiss who wish to appropriate the name. while france last year lifted the 96-year ban on absinthe, we must support the 15 french absinthe producers who represent the wealth of our know-how.
in writing. absinthe is a traditional european alcohol produced in a few member states, including france. although the recipe for this drink is precise, the category 'absinthe' does not yet exist in the union. many imitations are now sold as such. in order to finally allow european producers to use the name absinthe and to guarantee the authenticity and quality of the alcohols marketed in europe, the union must clearly define the composition of this beverage. a strict definition of absinthe should make it possible to combat counterfeit absinthe alcohol from europe or third countries much more effectively.
in writing. i wanted to vote against this text. the definition of absinthe proposed by the european commission was a definition that favoured product quality. the proposal included a threshold for anethole (which allows the water to be disturbed and therefore for detecting counterfeits) and thuyone (a characteristic of the plant). it will now be possible, without a european definition, to buy products under the name of absinthe without even using the plant 'absinthe'. moreover, as regards the timing, this rejection is dangerous since switzerland has applied for a geographical indication for absinthe at the same time. now that there is no community definition, the swiss can ask for the term to be banned for products manufactured outside their territory, and we cannot go back. it is therefore a vote which is against the safety of the consumer and of our community producers.
in writing. i voted against this resolution because i find it scandalous. admitting that a drink is marketed under the sales name 'absinthe' without providing proof that the plant of the same name has been used is clearly deceitful. baudelaire would turn in his grave! it is not just about preserving our traditions but also about protecting consumers. the name 'absinthe' cannot be sold and must remain a guarantee of quality. in reality, this is only a matter of defending the interests of certain companies in the region of the rhine which wish to produce wormwood of inferior quality in order to gain market shares. this is a scandal! i regret that the members of the european parliament are now threatening the traditional absinthe recipe which is the richness of our know-how. by delaying the introduction of a european definition of absinthe, the european parliament is shooting itself in the foot! the european union is in danger of being duped by switzerland, which wants to appropriate the name 'absinthe' by registering it as a geographical indication.
in writing. i regret the adoption of the resolution on spirits, which seems to me to be a complete nonsense! the european parliament has taken an absurd position by calling into question the european definition of absinthe, at the risk of confiscating the name 'absinthe' by switzerland, which intends to register it as a geographical indication. such an aberration puts the future of small businesses and distilleries at risk, since the adoption of this resolution amounts to a ban on the marketing of european products, and in particular french absinthe, which is known for its historically high quality.
in writing. i regret that our assembly has rejected the definition of absinthe proposed by the commission. i am convinced that the commission was on the right track in setting a minimum level of anethole and thujone in alcohol as the legal definition of alcohol, and the level of levels set by the commission seemed to me to guarantee both the specificity of absinthe and the health of consumers. to go back to these two criteria would, in my view, remove all substance from the legal definition of absinthe, and thus allow alcohols that are far removed from it to use its name. the present situation is detrimental to the producers of traditional absinthe and, of course, to consumers who are thus misled about the product they are buying. in addition, the race with switzerland should not be lost, since that country has accepted an application from its operators for recognition of the geographical indication 'absinthe'. with the rejection of the definition proposed by the commission, our producers could end up being deprived of our name 'absinthe', which must be avoided.
in writing. i voted against this resolution. the text, drawn up by the parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety, is opposed to the european commission's proposal to define precisely the drinks that can be called 'absinthe', and for the wrong reasons. under the guise of protecting the health of european citizens, the supporters of this text are in fact signalling the death of traditional absinthe production in europe. by defining this liqueur strictly, the european commission was protecting both consumers who had the guarantee of a quality product and european producers, because switzerland is currently trying to appropriate this name. i hope that the commission will propose a new text similar to this and that my colleagues in the house will hear our arguments.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which stresses the need for a greener, more profitable and fairer common agricultural policy. as a member of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i welcome this cap along greener lines, with a significant part of direct aid now conditional on compliance with environmental standards, such as the increase in areas of ecological interest. the revised cap offers greater support and a simplified scheme for small farmers with an increased one-off annual payment. i also support this report which calls for the states to commit themselves more to young farmers, by allocating 2% of the direct aids budget to them. finally, the european parliament has campaigned for a fairer and more sustainable cap by ensuring greater external convergence in the distribution of aid within the union and greater internal convergence within each member state. a progressive cap on direct aid is provided for in order to target the holdings which are most in need of european aid.
in writing. following the vote on the cap, it is clear that the original ambitions have been seriously undermined: the plenary assembly has remained stuck on the agricultural policy of the past. the greening is reduced, whereas it was one of the biggest advances in the original proposal. another key measure that would have changed the face of the cap considerably was not adopted: the cap on aid of €200,000 was rejected by two votes to one. the lack of fairness in support for farmers is now glaring. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. balancing also with developing countries (decs). i am a supporter of food sovereignty and self-sufficiency, from local to continental, and regret that the monitoring and evaluation of the impact of the cap in the developing countries has not been adopted. for all these reasons, this vote is a missed opportunity. the cap has not yet been reformed, and negotiations are still ongoing. for a healthy farming system, which allows farmers to live off their labour, which provides quality products and which is part of sustainable development, the mobilisation of both parliamentary and citizen representatives remains more necessary than ever.
in writing. by introducing the green payment, we want to give the cap's direct payments greater legitimacy. the report proposes to link 30% of the national ceiling for direct payments to three environmental practices: crop diversification, permanent grassland and pasturage and ecological focus areas. i have therefore decided, in the light of these elements, to vote in favour of the report by mr luis manuel capoulas santos.
in writing. i voted in favour of capping aid to farmers for a more environmentally friendly and fair agricultural subsidy system. direct aid was capped at 30% and subject to compulsory greening measures. we have, however, taken care that these environmental measures are gradual and flexible, so as not to place too much pressure on farmers.
in writing. i voted in favour of the capoulas santos report, supporting the vote in the european parliament's agri committee. the report calls for better targeting and a fairer distribution of direct aids, and emphasises support for young farmers, a crucial aspect as the profession is becoming increasingly disadvantaged. environmental measures are also made compulsory, but with sufficient flexibility to avoid burdening the competitiveness of farms. i therefore consider these positions to be balanced and realistic in view of the trilogue negotiations with the council.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of this resolution, which will open negotiations on the future of direct payments to farmers under our common agricultural policy. i particularly welcome the measures for young farmers: we see that agriculture is a key sector for our economies, our culture, our environment and our health. it is not right that so few young people are attracted to agriculture, even though the sector is recruiting. it is to reduce the difficulties faced by farmers and to make this sector attractive again that i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. the general objectives of a new common agricultural policy need to be re-examined. europeans have new expectations of food. they want an agriculture that respects the environment, the quality, traceability and food safety of products and the carbon footprint. this new policy will also have to be part of a global vision. the challenge is to meet the doubling of food requirements by 2050 in a context of water scarcity, a decline in arable land and a new energy situation dictated by the fight against climate change. the global organisation of agricultural markets will have to be redesigned taking into account the two main inspirations underlying the common agricultural policy: ensuring food security and preserving the living fabric of farmers everywhere.
in writing. while i regret the substantial reduction in appropriations that the cap is about to undergo in the future financial framework (2014-2020), we must not lose sight of the objective of a fairer cap. i supported this text which caps aid to farmers at eur 300 000. this is a positive first step which should allow for a more parsimonious distribution of public money and a rebalancing of aid in favour of small and medium-sized farms (particularly in the south-west). i would have liked a more ambitious vote with a limit of eur 200 000 but unfortunately parliament did not see it that way.
in writing. in this important period of cap reform, agriculture is once again at the centre of the debate. the french want quality agriculture, efficient agriculture, meeting high environmental standards and sustainable agriculture for our farmers, but without ideology or excessive bureaucracy. the initial proposals of the european commission do not meet these expectations. the farmers must be able to work in good conditions and receive a decent income as a result of their work. on the other hand, our regional products (sometimes of a cultural nature), such as wines and many cheeses, deserve special attention so that they are not reduced to the status of ordinary commodities. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster is a welcome one.
in writing. i did not vote for any of the negotiating mandates on the common agricultural policy. even if they are amended, these texts are not a good basis for discussion with the council. what parliament is going to negotiate does not fundamentally change the cap designed by the eurocrats since 1992: it is still a question of deregulating european agriculture and leaving it to the sole forces of a totally liberalized world market. by supporting financially the euthanasia of our farmers, who have no chance of being competitive with the strong euro, the production costs and the draconian standards they must obey, but which must never be imposed on imports that compete with them. nothing in these texts is conducive to achieving the broad objectives of what a genuine agricultural policy should be: food security and food independence; decent incomes for farmers; quality products at reasonable prices for consumers. all this can only be achieved by regulating markets and implementing national and european preference. you're doing the exact opposite.
in writing. i voted against this regulation because, as it stands, it will not allow the common agricultural policy to change direction. the environmentalists have suffered a serious and bitter defeat, as the overwhelming majority of our demands have not been voted on. the european parliament has made its choice between quality agriculture and productivist agriculture. and it's not mine. parliament voted against crop rotation, the only way out of monoculture. he voted against compliance with the water framework directive, a key european text for environmental protection. he voted against the disqualification of farmers from receiving subsidies for growing gmos. and against the reduction of the subsidy ceiling to eur 100 000. finally, the texts make almost no mention of the coherence of public policies for development.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my socialist colleague, mr luis manuel capoulas santos, for the establishment of a common agricultural policy (cap) which is more environmentally friendly, fairer and more equitable. in order to tackle the challenge of greening, i support the conditioning of 30% of direct aid to farmers to environmental standards, such as crop diversification or the maintenance of permanent grasslands. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the cap. in this respect, i welcome the introduction of the french proposal for a bonus for the first hectares, which will help to promote small farms, since they are the ones that provide the most jobs. similarly, the young farmer payments encourage new entrants to the sector and contribute to generational renewal in agriculture. i regret, however, that the amendment on the ceiling of eur 200 000 has not been adopted. he was only two votes short of the cap reform to become even more redistributive.
in writing. i welcome the balanced approach that the european parliament has chosen to take to the common agricultural policy, ensuring the future of our farmers while meeting the legitimate social and environmental expectations of society. as regards direct payments, the european parliament has approved the introduction of the greening principle to ensure that agriculture is more respectful of the environment and our landscapes. i am particularly pleased with the measures taken to help young farmers, who, as i see every day in my region, are becoming fewer and fewer in number to take up a difficult but essential occupation for the food self-sufficiency of our country. i also wanted the new cap that is being drawn up to take account of the concerns of our farmers about the distribution of aid. that is why i supported the capping of aid at eur 200 000 so that redistribution would benefit small and mediumsized farms more, but unfortunately this option was not taken.
in writing. another key issue is the reform of the common agricultural policy, which remains the union's first common policy, accounting for almost 40% of the european budget. we have also made known our political messages to the council and the commission and voted on the mandate we give to our parliamentary negotiators. in this mandate, we express our desire for the cap to be more balanced, to continue to reduce disparities between farmers in the union, and to be more environmentally friendly through the so-called 'greening' of the cap. we want 30% of direct aid to farmers to be conditional on compliance with certain environmental practices, but with flexibility for small farms. we also want aid to be distributed first to 'active farmers', i.e. those who derive all or a very large part of their income from their agricultural activity. it is also a strong support for young farmers and small farms that the european parliament wishes to affirm through the ambitious mandate given to its representatives in the negotiations that are now opening.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on direct payments to farmers because the environment is more taken into account by farmers implementing environmentally friendly measures in order to receive 30% of the aid to which they are entitled under the basic payment scheme. it is also important to set a maximum amount that a holding can receive in order to redistribute aid between holdings in the member states in a balanced way. small farms should also benefit from a simplified scheme and young farmers should be granted a supplementary payment to keep the young generation in the agricultural sector. in order to address the shortcomings of the last programming period, member states should draw up a list limiting the allocation of european aid to active farmers.
in writing. the weight of agricultural producers in the food supply chain and the maintenance of a form of management of agricultural markets are, in the context of the current reform of the cap, two elements that i supported in my vote. the abolition of export refunds remains problematic and its immediate effect is likely to cause very serious difficulties for certain sectors. it is in this sense that it is important to work on an emergency system which would maintain a financial reserve in the event of a one-off agricultural crisis.
in writing. our food security is our most precious asset. we owe much of it to the common agricultural policy (cap), which has made it possible for us to provide for our most basic need - food. it was a historic eu policy, it had to be modernised and i can say that we have done so successfully. we voted for a fairer, more flexible and greener cap. by placing a ceiling on aid to large farms, introducing a system favouring small farmers and organising convergence of aid between the states and the regions of each state, our assembly is responding to the demand for a fairer and more efficient distribution of aid. we have also managed to ensure some flexibility for the cap 2014-2020, allowing member states to transfer part of agricultural income support to rural development, and vice versa. finally, i am pleased that we have found a compromise for sustainable agriculture, with environmental objectives to be achieved according to the capabilities of each farmer. the cap benefits 500 million europeans, but it must also take account of the specificities and needs of farmers.

in writing. i voted in favour of a new approach to the functioning of agricultural markets, which have hitherto been closely supervised by the public authorities. in the era of globalisation, the weight of producers in the management of markets and risks must be increased, which requires a strengthening of the powers of collective structures and an adaptation of competition law to agriculture. some sectors (such as sugar and milk) continue to be protected to give them more time to adapt, but quotas are not a permanent solution. by designing farms as enterprises, farmers can finally break out of the economic dependence in which they are locked.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, the result of a long and intense negotiating effort within the european parliament's agri committee. the compromise reached takes account of the specific features of the agricultural activity and the food chain. the report also takes a reasoned approach by allowing for exceptions to the normal competition rules within a well-defined framework. this will give producer organisations the much-needed role to play in order to gain a greater competitive edge over other players in the agri-food sector. in contrast to the increased liberalisation of agricultural markets, this report is in line with the reality experienced by the vast majority of our farmers who benefit from the cap, namely globalisation and the changes in their sector of activity which they feel are constraints and have to face.

in writing. the european parliament met in strasbourg on wednesday 13 march to set out its position on the cap for the forthcoming negotiations with the european commission and the member states. one of the texts in the package concerns the reform of the common organisation of the markets in agricultural products, which strengthens the regulatory powers of farmers and the sectors which will now be able to take over from the public authorities. i welcome the desire to give farmers and producer organizations more power, so that they can finally take control of their destiny and production and ensure the economic viability of their farms. i am also pleased with the european parliament's decision to extend sugar quotas until 2020, which will allow the beet sector to prepare for the transition in a calm manner. i am not forgetting the disastrous effect of the 2006 reform, which led to the closure of 83 sugar factories, the loss of more than 22 000 direct jobs and the cessation of beet cultivation by more than 150 000 farmers, particularly in the auvergne.

in writing. the reform of the cap gave the european commission the opportunity to propose an amendment to the cmo regulation, which since 1968 has provided for a common organisation of markets based on the principles of quotas, guaranteed prices and management of the supply chains. the reform proposed by the commission was aimed at the almost immediate abolition of sugar quotas and of any protection for community sugar production. i reject this logic absolutely, because it condemns sugarcane growers and other agricultural sectors to global competition, social dumping and total deregulation of the market. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of maintaining the common market organisations until 2020, its quota, price guarantee and supply chain management systems, thus safeguarding the interests of sugarcane growers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a decision because the common agricultural policy (cap) must continue to meet its objectives while modernising and adapting to the varied profiles of european agriculture. greening and convergence of aid are at the heart of this modernisation of the cap. the first must be implemented in a flexible manner so as not to lead to a fall in production and endanger european agriculture. the convergence of aid also remains a sensitive issue. it must be applied gradually to avoid causing the collapse of the aid of certain farmers. finally, it is essential to support and accompany young farmers in their establishment and in their daily lives.
in writing. agricultural markets are not like other markets. they are subject to the vagaries of weather and disease and therefore require intelligent management and regulation. that is why, when i voted for the reform of the cap, i insisted on the extension of the mechanisms of public intervention, aid for storage and the maintenance of certain quotas, which guarantee a balance between supply and demand and a fair income for farmers. i am particularly pleased that the unanimous vote in favour of the extension of planting rights was in response to a request from the wine growers in my region. this will enable us to obtain from the council a system of production control capable of guaranteeing the quality and traditions of wine growing in france. i also supported the provisions which strengthen the status of producers, particularly in the fruit and vegetables sector, so that they can act on the market and thus ensure a fair distribution of added value among all the actors in the food sector. the food industry and its producers are like two sides of the same coin, they can't be opposed if they want to thrive.

in writing. rural development pursues three objectives for the common agricultural policy (cap): the competitiveness of agriculture, the sustainable management of natural resources, and the balanced development of rural areas. it is complementary to the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and is part of the common strategic framework which better links funds and maximises the impact of eu investments. i voted in favour of this proposal for a decision because rural development will lead to better competitiveness and sustainability of farms, in particular through the transfer of knowledge and innovation. it will also continue efforts to protect the environment and biodiversity by promoting the efficient use of resources. finally, rural development includes an economic and social dimension by including measures that promote the objectives of poverty reduction and economic development of the agricultural sector.
in writing. i welcome this vote which will give rural areas new means to develop over the period 2014-2020. following on from the previous eafrd, this new fund will finance a multitude of projects by local economic actors aimed at strengthening the agricultural sector, preserving the environment in rural areas and diversifying their activities. i have, however, wished to make some changes to this fund, which, in my view, should provide additional aid to regions with specific natural constraints, such as terrain, aridity or soil quality. i have asked the eafrd to recognise the mediterranean climate as a natural constraint, in order to help farmers in paca to cope better with drought and other constraints linked to this particular climate. the european commission must now come back to us with a legislative proposal on the designation of areas likely to be subject to natural or specific constraints. i'll make sure the mediterranean climate is in the picture.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets out the plan for the financing, management and monitoring of the common agricultural policy for the multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020. this report builds on the europe 2020 strategy by promoting resource efficiency for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth for eu agriculture and rural areas. the cap system proposed here maintains a two-pillar structure but stresses the need to deliver on the key priorities of the european union. as a member of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i am pleased that the priority of direct payments is to sustainable production in a more respectful environment.
in writing. following the vote on the cap, it is clear that the original ambitions have been seriously undermined: the plenary assembly has remained stuck on the agricultural policy of the past. the greening is reduced, whereas it was one of the biggest advances in the original proposal. another key measure that would have changed the face of the cap considerably was not adopted: the cap on aid of €200,000 was rejected by two votes to one. the lack of fairness in support for farmers is now glaring. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. balancing also with developing countries (decs). i am a supporter of food sovereignty and self-sufficiency, from local to continental, and regret that the monitoring and evaluation of the impact of the cap in the developing countries has not been adopted. for all these reasons, this vote is a missed opportunity. the cap has not yet been reformed, and negotiations are still ongoing. for a healthy farming system, which allows farmers to live off their labour, which provides quality products and which is part of sustainable development, the mobilisation of both parliamentary and citizen representatives remains more necessary than ever.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of the report by my colleague giovanni la via which aims to simplify the cap and the rules governing the procedure for submitting applications for funding. it contains various simplification elements, in particular by bringing together all the rules on cross-compliance in a single legislative act, thus improving their legibility.
in writing. we have approved new and more transparent rules for the management of the cap. the penalties system has been redesigned, penalties for non-compliance with greening requirements have been reduced, in order to give farmers time to adapt to these new environmental requirements. greener agriculture, yes, but not at the expense of jobs and growth in an already particularly fragile sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report and fully support its desire to simplify an administrative apparatus which farmers consider too complex and to lighten the burden on farmers. i welcome the new developments in the agricultural advisory system, which make it possible for public and private actors to coexist, which will make it more effective. the priority given to small farming enterprises is also a key point for me in the development of this sector. finally, i welcome the development of the sanctions system towards greater anticipation (warning system) and proportionality, which will demonstrate to european citizens that the european union is not only a punitive attitude without discrimination.
in writing. the general objectives of a new common agricultural policy need to be re-examined. europeans have new expectations of food. they want an agriculture that respects the environment, the quality, traceability and food safety of products and the carbon footprint. this new policy will also have to be part of a global vision. the challenge is to meet the doubling of food requirements by 2050 in a context of water scarcity, a decline in arable land and a new energy situation dictated by the fight against climate change. the global organisation of agricultural markets will have to be redesigned taking into account the two main inspirations underlying the common agricultural policy: ensuring food security and preserving the living fabric of farmers everywhere.
in writing. i voted against this regulation because, as it stands, it will not allow the common agricultural policy to change direction. the environmentalists have suffered a serious and bitter defeat, as the overwhelming majority of our demands have not been adopted. the european parliament has made its choice between quality agriculture and productivist agriculture. and it's not mine. parliament voted against crop rotation, the only way out of monoculture. he voted against compliance with the water framework directive, a key european text for environmental protection. he voted against the disqualification of farmers from receiving subsidies for growing gmos. and against the reduction of the subsidy ceiling to eur 100 000. finally, the texts make almost no mention of the coherence of public policies for development.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text on the financing, control and monitoring of the cap. it provides greater transparency and aims to strengthen the commitment of citizens and farmers to the common agricultural policy (cap). the european parliament wants to make public the names of the beneficiaries of the cap and the amount of agricultural aid, in order to increase the confidence of european taxpayers. the report also ensures that aid is still conditional on compliance with basic environmental, health and animal welfare requirements. finally, the report makes the cap easier to read and less bureaucratic for farmers by simplifying administrative procedures.

in writing. we have today voted in favour of an ambitious new cap which will finally take into account environmental requirements, food security and fair redistribution. on this last point, we were unable to obtain a reduction in the ceiling of aid to eur 200 000, but the principle is nevertheless well established, as is that of the surplus on the first hectares, which is being supported by france. the requirement of transparency vis-à-vis taxpayers will also become a reality with the identification of the beneficiaries of the cap. on the environmental side, the cap must finally be reoriented towards an ecological transition taking into account the need to feed the continent, but with quality products and respecting our environment while accompanying our farmers in this change. finally, we have rejected the liberalization of this vital and fragile sector: we must regulate agricultural production and markets, in view of the risks of speculation for producers, our food independence and the quality of the products. the negotiations with the council are now beginning, and i trust our representatives and the progressive ministers, including stéphane le foll, to bring to a conclusion this major reform of a policy which is essential to the common destiny of europe.
in writing. carbon emissions must be reduced by 85% by 2050, including through energy efficiency, renewable energy or nuclear energy. it is essential to secure energy supplies and to maintain competitiveness without affecting the environment in a lasting way. this is why the eu has set up the eu emissions trading scheme (ets): a mechanism of co2 emission rights to reduce overall co2 emissions and meet the requirements of the kyoto protocol. the report aims to strengthen the mechanism for monitoring greenhouse gas emissions and to provide guidance for the deferral of co2 allowances in the european union. in favour of decarbonising the european union, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the transition to a low-carbon economy is a key eu objective. to achieve this, it is interesting that the union presents a roadmap, the idea being to draw up the energy mix by 2050, translating into concrete actions the path to a decarbonised economy. there was good in this own-initiative report, whether it was on renewable energy or energy efficiency. but i voted against the report in the end because of the very positive paragraphs on nuclear energy and the rejection of binding targets for greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and energy efficiency for 2030. while it is normal that, under the scenarios envisaged by the eu and in all likelihood, the energy mix should include all energy sources, without a priori, nuclear energy should not be considered as essential. the aim, in france as in other member states, is to reduce the share of nuclear energy in energy production. this will be achieved through voluntary energy diversification and the integration of the transition into a framework of energy efficiency and sobriety.
in writing. in the context of the 2050 objectives, ms tzavela recalled that it was up to the member states to set their own rules in this area, while recognising the merits of developing a coordinated european approach. it is with this in mind that the rapporteur calls for the establishment of a policy framework for 2030. it also highlights the importance of renewable energy sources, the global challenges we face, research and new technologies. as these issues are central to european citizens, i decided to give my vote to this report.
in writing. the european union has set out a roadmap for a low-carbon economy by 2050. non-binding targets have been adopted for greenhouse gas reduction, renewable energy and energy efficiency, to allow member states time to adapt their economies to these environmental constraints. i did not, however, vote for the ets. a report on this subject is due in april, so i have decided to abstain until the expert's conclusions are known.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is essential to have a sound energy policy for the future of the european union. this report highlights the eu's responsibility in this vital area: its main task is to coordinate national energy policies. we must have a role in stimulating and regulating member states' energy policies and help to find incentive and innovative funding sources, particularly through public-private partnerships. research and innovation must be encouraged. we need a european energy market that is fluid and without barriers. member states must be able to work together to achieve a coherent and relevant european energy policy that responds well to the challenges of the future. there are many difficulties which require us to devote particular attention to this issue, notably the question of energy independence due to certain complex geopolitical balances or the need for a transition to a more varied energy package, for an economy with a smaller impact on the environment.

in writing. on the occasion of the sad anniversary of the fukushima nuclear accident, the european parliament adopted a resolution to ensure the safety of nuclear power stations in the union. i am in favour of the idea that these stress tests are useful and that closer international cooperation is needed to ensure nuclear safety, now and in the future. i abstained on this report, however, because i considered that the debate had been diverted by the european greens who had launched an alarmist accusation against nuclear energy. tackling nuclear energy in this way directly challenges the achievement of the energy mix targets of a 20% reduction in co2 emissions by 2020 and could prove dangerous for the economy and research in the european union.
in writing. the european level stress tests conducted after fukushima have highlighted the shortcomings and the need to strengthen the safety of the european nuclear fleet (according to the european commission report published after these tests). in france in particular, the work to be done is very large - in the order of tens of billions of euros. the fact that a plant has passed the stress tests does not guarantee its safety: the idea is shared in parliament, as is the need for binding safety standards. i voted against this resolution in the final vote. i regret that the closure of the oldest plants was not called for, and that the idea that the risk is still present, regardless of the results of the stress tests, was not supported. finally, it is regrettable that parliament does not support a european supervisory mechanism.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which aims to guarantee and improve safety at nuclear power stations in europe. the text adopted is ambitious and binding. once the stress test is completed, member states will have to implement the recommended improvements. i voted against the idea that nuclear power operators should bear the full cost of any measure. this obligation is too undifferentiated and exclusive.
in writing. the second anniversary of the fukushima disaster reminds us of the importance of nuclear safety in europe. nuclear power plants now produce almost one third of the electricity and 15% of the energy consumed in the european union. the majority of nuclear reactors in operation today are located in europe, although not all member states have built them. there are currently 144 operational reactors in 16 member states and 6 under construction. the member state with the most reactors in operation is france, with 59. following the japanese disaster, the european union conducted stress tests on all eu nuclear power stations. these tests have shown that the safety standards recommended by the international atomic energy agency (iaea) and international best practices are not fully applied by all member states. we cannot accept this risky situation for long. all recommended safety improvements should therefore be implemented as a matter of urgency. with the nuclear safety directive about to be revised, it is essential that the european union has a real and strong nuclear risk management policy.
in writing. i welcome the fact that this resolution focuses on the prospects for improving nuclear safety in europe following the stress tests carried out in the wake of fukushima and does not call into question the place of nuclear in the energy mix of some member states. no serious risks requiring the closure of a power plant were identified. however, areas for improvement in safety have been identified for extreme events (seismic hazards, floods) and will require an adequate response. the independence of national nuclear safety authorities will also need to be strengthened and the eu will need to continue to promote the highest safety standards globally. in the interests of transparency, greater involvement of the european parliament - representing the european people - should be guaranteed in future debates on nuclear energy and nuclear safety in europe, but in compliance with the euratom treaty and the defined competences. i therefore abstained on the final vote on the resolution for legal reasons in order not to challenge the framework of the euratom treaty.
in writing. the report recalls that in europe more than 100 000 people live within a 30 km radius of 47 nuclear power stations. he said he was aware of the need to draw lessons from the fukushima daiichi accident. but he doesn't get any consequences. it does not call for the closure of nuclear power stations where several serious problems have been detected. it reiterated the need to improve the safety rules in nuclear power, but did not at any time call for an end to the subcontracting of nuclear safety checks to private bodies. the reality is alarming. the logic of profit means that these works are carried out by too small a number of workers and with too little time to ensure maximum safety. the text does not mention that there is no such thing as zero risk in nuclear energy. so he has no plans to release this dangerous energy. i abstain in support of the few improvements to the safety rules proposed. i would like to point out, however, the blindness of the authors of this text.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report which calls for the european union to take action to protect the health of citizens from endocrine disruptors, chemicals that interfere with the hormonal system. we are in contact almost daily with these endocrine disruptors which can be found in plastics, cosmetics, paints and food packaging. caution should be exercised in relation to the health damage that endocrine disruptors can cause, such as breast cancer or reduced male fertility. that is why we want to include these potentially dangerous substances under the cover of the reach (registration, evaluation and restricted authorisation of chemicals) regulation to ensure appropriate information and assessment methods.
in writing. compared to well-identified chemicals, endocrine disruptors remain unknown to both the general public and national and european legislation. endocrine disruptors are chemical molecules that are found everywhere - in our environment and in many of the objects we use every day - and that are thought to have an impact on our endocrine system and our health. the own-initiative report adopted today by the european parliament warns of the dangers and the need to take these chemical molecules more seriously. given their widespread presence, the causal link between a suspected disruptive substance and its health effects remains very difficult to establish. however, in this report we call on the european commission to revise its strategy on this subject and in particular to come forward with proposals for general criteria based on the definition developed by the world health organisation and to introduce a clear definition of 'disruptive' substances in the eu. finally, we call on the commission to concentrate its efforts on informing and raising public awareness of the existence of these substances and their potential effects.

in writing. the text has two main aims: first, to better protect europeans, especially the most vulnerable, from the risks these substances could pose. the second is to increase information on these substances, so that their potential effects can be better assessed. these endocrine disruptors raise major uncertainties: they must be addressed urgently and that is why i supported this report.
in writing. endocrine disruptors, exogenous chemicals that cause harmful effects on the body, can be found in all types of everyday products, such as medicines, cosmetics or food additives. as the commission is currently reviewing its strategy on endocrine disruptors, it is important, above all, to ensure a high level of protection of the health of europeans. respect for the precautionary principle, which guides eu public health action, means refusing to set a minimum exposure threshold below which endocrine disruptors would be harmless, when the current state of research is still insufficient to judge this, and uncertain in relation to the potential 'cocktail effects' of endocrine disruptors mixed with other substances. further research into these products will help to better understand their effects on human health and to better manage the risks. in this sense, chemicals for which data are lacking and which have endocrine disrupting properties should be covered by the reach regulation.
in writing. given the incomplete knowledge we have about the effects of these chemicals on our hormones, it is essential to apply the precautionary principle and to put in place the measures necessary for their identification and study, but above all for their regulation at european level. i have therefore supported the adoption of this text, which helps to protect the health of our fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution. endocrine disruptors are natural or artificial substances outside the body that can disrupt the functioning of the hormonal system and cause harmful effects in both the short and long term on an individual and his offspring. they are everywhere: in plastic bottles, pesticides, electronic devices, cosmetics and even in the nipples of baby bottles in some member states. a pregnant woman may unknowingly expose her unborn child to the risk of hormonal imbalance. in some countries, up to 40 percent of young men have poor sperm quality. nearly 800 chemicals are known or suspected to interfere with hormone receptors. this will be the subject of a proposal for european regulation in the coming months.
in writing. this own-initiative report, which i voted in favour of, responds to the steady and sharp increase in reproductive disorders (such as impaired sperm quality, testicular cancer, precocious puberty, sexual organ malformations, congenital malformations, cancer and diabetes in general) and neurological disorders, which are now known to be caused by endocrine disruptors. the report therefore proposes very ambitious measures which will make it possible to limit the use of endocrine disruptors in products targeted at certain consumers (skin care products, textiles, toys, etc.) without, however, penalising the major industrial sectors too heavily.
in writing. in the last twenty years, there has been an increase in the incidence of diseases and hormonal disorders in humans, leading to numerous reproductive problems, an increased incidence of certain cancers and an increase in metabolic disorders. an increasing number of scientific studies suggest that chemical endocrine disruptors (pesticides, plastic additives, steroids, etc.) play a role, although it is still difficult to establish a definite causal link between exposure to various chemicals and hormonal imbalances that may have adverse health effects. in this context, it seems to me essential to speed up research in order to resolve the remaining questions, while taking measures to protect human health. the precautionary principle must guide policy action in this area and it seems to me crucial that the current rules be thoroughly reviewed with a view to a rapid update. in addition, consumers need to have clear and reliable information on the potential dangers of endocrine disruptors, their effects and the possibility of protecting themselves against them, and the commission as well as the member states should act in this regard. that is the spirit of this resolution, which i support.
in writing. the major demographic changes ahead call for a rethink of our approach to legal immigration in europe. the working-age population is expected to decline by 14 million over the next decade, and the reception and integration of new immigrants must be encouraged and improved to ensure the long-term economic growth and social balance of the european union. coordination of our social security systems, and even of our migration and asylum policies, is possible, provided that national specificities, particularly those relating to the labour market, are taken into account. i do not think that there is any need for harmonization of these policies at the moment, which is why i voted against this report, which goes too far in its proposals. each state must remain in control of its immigration policy, but this must be done within the framework of effective european cooperation. as such, i oppose the right to vote of non-eu foreigners and refuse to recognise illegal immigration.
in writing. managing migration flows, the quintessential european subject, is a central challenge in the european union today. the initiative report by nadja hirsch on the integration of migrants is to be welcomed for its progressive approach. given that the working age population will start to decline from 2012 onwards (despite record unemployment) in the union, the integration of migrants is a public policy necessity. integration is a mutual commitment; if employment is the key to successful integration, the fight against discrimination, particularly at work, is paramount. the principle of equal pay and working conditions must apply to all. the principle of round trips, as is possible with circular migration, would be a significant step forward. in this report i voted for the principle of the right of migrants to vote in local elections; i regret that paragraphs concerning more specifically the undocumented and refugees were not adopted. finally, i support the rapporteur's proposal to create a mechanism for the recognition of qualifications and diplomas of third country nationals.
in writing. the demographic situation in the european union is such that the working age population will decline by 14 million over the next decade. this requires us to take social and economic measures to allow the integration of new immigrants that europe will need when growth and employment levels are restored. however, while coordination of our social security systems may be necessary, our migration and asylum policies remain subject to imperatives linked to each national situation, in particular the labour market situation. european coordination in the field of immigration is to be considered, but in no case harmonization. the report does not make that distinction, so i have decided not to support it.
in writing. the demographic situation in the european union is such that the working age population will decline by 14 million over the next decade. this requires us to take social and economic measures to enable the integration of new immigrants that europe will need when growth and employment levels are restored. international labour mobility can be an opportunity for europe if immigration and employment legislation fosters the integration of immigrant workers, and if the portability of pension rights and the coordination of social security systems are improved. however, i did not vote in favour of this report because, under the guise of the necessary european coordination of our policies, it introduces measures to facilitate access to employment for asylum seekers and foreign students, and to introduce the right to vote for migrants. i think that at the moment it is not responsible to our fellow citizens to consider such harmonised legislation at european level on immigration and asylum without a boost to growth and employment.

in writing. asbestos has now virtually disappeared from the european union, with many substitutes being introduced and developed to compensate for its use and its disastrous health consequences (cancer risks). this own-initiative report emphasises the possibility of establishing action plans for the safe elimination of asbestos in public buildings and in buildings required to provide services requiring public access as early as 2028. i welcome this report which calls on the european commission to prepare a specific directive establishing minimum requirements for the vocational training of workers in the construction and maintenance of buildings.
in writing. the causal relationship between exposure to asbestos - even in small doses - and the development of specific diseases, including cancers, is no longer debated: the number of victims in europe is estimated at between 20 000 and 30 000. asbestos in public and private buildings is a serious public health hazard. the european parliament was not spared, as asbestos dust was released recently when a pillar was pierced, causing part of the institution to be contaminated - albeit temporarily. the report by stephen hughes aims to highlight the risks and calls on the commission to introduce minimum training standards applicable throughout the eu. in order to give real scope to the recognition of asbestos-related diseases, but above all to empower decision-makers, this own-initiative report advocates compensation for victims as a matter of course, without the burden of proof of their damage being on them. legislation providing for exemptions from criminal liability for decision-makers is condemned: everyone must bear the consequences of the acts. finally, in the wake of the clemenceau case, we call on the commission to ban exports for the purpose of asbestos removal where workers are not protected.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the elimination of asbestos which still exists. i supported the idea of giving member states time to conduct impact studies and cost-benefit analyses, so that they can develop plans to eliminate traces of asbestos in public buildings by 2028. it should be recalled that france has banned the use of asbestos in new building construction since 1997 and requires an "asbestos test" for the purchase of any building or house dating from before 1997.
in writing. asbestos remains a serious public health problem. too many europeans are still exposed to this dangerous substance because of lack of knowledge and information. i support the approach taken in this report, which is to focus on training the actors involved at all levels of the hierarchy and on recognising victims to ensure that they are properly supported. prevention and repair, two keywords that should guide our approach to asbestos.
in writing. as the health of european workers is at stake, i felt obliged to vote in favour of this text, which paves the way for stricter regulations on asbestos. in view of the many health risks associated with the presence of asbestos in buildings, it seems necessary that the european union should take all possible measures to manage and eliminate asbestos. that is why i fully support the specific request in this text for the union to remove asbestos from the buildings of the european institutions. the union must set a good example.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because, although a great deal has been done to solve the public health problems related to asbestos, we still have a lot of work to do. in france, for example, new cases continue to be detected, even though asbestos has been banned there since 1997. asbestos is still present in many buildings and equipment. its exact location is often unknown (thus posing a threat to the general public). asbestos-related diseases are now the second leading cause of occupational diseases and the first cause of workrelated deaths (excluding accidents). this slow poison can affect many years after exposure. in some factories, real asbestos removal is needed, not just partial dust removal. the cleaning should not be entrusted to an in-house team but to professionals in the asbestos field. we need to know better the european statistics and figures on this problem. it is necessary to list the cases identified, the quality of the treatment offered to the patients, and to create a european map of the problems still existing.
in writing. i voted for this text because of the obvious public health imperatives. although the use of asbestos is now virtually banned in the eu, the number of asbestos-related cancers in western europe continues to rise and various occupational groups are still at risk of exposure to asbestos, whether they are aware of it or not. the major health hazards of asbestos are no longer to be demonstrated and it was therefore important to make the monitoring system for the prohibition of the use of asbestos more effective, which this text will make possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the risks of asbestos to health at work and the prospects for the complete elimination of asbestos still in existence, so that the commission takes further action to protect european workers from the risks of exposure to asbestos, which is known to be toxic, even in small quantities. despite the ban on the use of asbestos, it is still found in many public and private buildings, as well as in ships, machinery, tunnels, water pipes, and so forth. for example, the european strategy for renovating buildings to improve their energy performance should be accompanied by a strategy for asbestos removal. models developed by the european commission should allow the monitoring of asbestos in buildings, including housing, and other infrastructure and workplaces. progress is also possible on the part of the member states in informing workers and employers about the risks of asbestos before work begins. this would be in addition to the existing health and safety protections imposed by eu law.
in writing. "every week 20 workers die of asbestos-related diseases" has long been the rallying cry of a campaign by european trade unions. despite the eu ban on the production and import of asbestos or products containing it, asbestos remains present in many public and private buildings, and in some transport and materials. under pressure from the alde and ppe groups, the original report was somewhat watered down. the references to "mandatory" community action have been removed. but it is still moving in the right direction. it called for the detailed detection and registration of products containing asbestos to improve working conditions and promote the recognition and compensation of asbestos victims, with the aim of a complete ban by 2023. it also calls for increased monitoring and awareness-raising programmes and activities and for systematic medical follow-up of victims. i therefore voted in favour of this report, especially as the main demands of my colleague sabine wils, the fictitious rapporteur for the gue/ngl, have been incorporated into the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which contains several proposals to allow mutual societies to operate at european and cross-border level. this status of european mutual society would be an opportunity to place mutual societies on an equal footing by giving all of them the same opportunities to give a european dimension to their organisation and activities. this status should provide them with the legal instruments necessary to facilitate their cross-border and transnational activities and a means of grouping together and developing their organisation and activities within the single market. this report makes relevant proposals to the commission on the status, scope and governance of this european mutual fund.
in writing. based on values of solidarity, mutual societies are important actors in the 'social' market economy which the european union must strive to promote. by defending the general interest, promoting sustainable practices and demonstrating a high degree of social responsibility, mutual societies are working to preserve the european social model and are playing a positive role in these times of crisis. they have indeed withstood the financial crisis well, particularly in the field of insurance and social protection. for all these reasons, they should be given greater recognition in the european union. their diversity and specificity are not negligible assets for europe today. that is the meaning of the european parliament's vote: to vote - once again - in favour of a european statute for mutual societies. the idea is to give mutual societies the same tools as any other company: mutual societies must be able to work at european level, to group together, to develop on an equal footing with other companies in europe. we therefore call on the european commission to make a new proposal creating a european mutual insurance statute.

in writing. facilitating the establishment and operation of mutual societies at european level means streamlining the insurance market on the continent, for the daily benefit of europeans. this report is intended to stimulate reflection on the subject, and i support the ambitions it sets out.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, luigi berlinguer, because it is important that the commission finally commits itself to proposing an instrument to create a european mutual status, which has many advantages. mutual societies play a major role in the european union's economy, providing healthcare to over 160 million european citizens and employing over 350 000 people. this common statute could provide a legal basis for mutual societies to operate across borders, as opposed to the current system whereby mutual societies are subject to competition from conventional for-profit undertakings. it will also allow for better account to be taken of the specific features of mutual societies in european legislation. finally, it could promote and spread the mutualist model in europe. in the context of the crisis we are experiencing, it is important to promote mutual societies in their role as a social buffer. this is all the more urgent as the crisis threatens the union's social cohesion, growth and, more broadly, political stability itself.
in writing. this report asks the european commission, which alone has the legislative initiative, to propose a statute for european mutual funds. in its recommendations, the european parliament refers to the basic provisions of european mutual societies and to the principles and values which should always govern the organisation, operation and objectives of mutual societies in the eu member states: democratic governance, solidarity, reinvestment of profits in activities, absence of shareholders, organisation and provision of services and services in the interests of their members, etc. the adoption of such legislation would finally make it possible to make progress towards the recognition of the different families of the social economy in the european union and to bring it into line with the principle of freedom of enterprise, whatever its status, and not to want for all purposes that all enterprises are gradually obliged to imitate capital companies, in particular in the name of the so-called prudential rules. it is high time the commission acknowledged that it made a mistake in withdrawing a legislative proposal in this direction in 2006. i therefore naturally voted in favour of this report.
