mr president, the spanish socialist delegation, aware that the wto rules do not allow the tariff exemptions that the union offers to the asia-caribbean-pacific countries - the acp countries - to be maintained indefinitely, has argued that the deadline for their abolition should not jeopardize the development of these countries or the activities of economic operators on both sides. the commission has therefore concluded that the measures in question constitute state aid within the meaning of article 107 (1) of the treaty. this is the only realistic and reasonable timeframe which would allow the acp countries a certain amount of time to sign and ratify their association agreements and allow economic operators sufficient time to adapt to this new situation. unfortunately, today our support was not enough to approve this date. in this context, we have supported the october 2014 date as the lesser evil, although we consider it too short a timeframe, and we deeply regret the responsibility in this matter of the council and of some political groups, such as the epp, which will cause more than one difficulty to some of the developing countries.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to comment on the european parliament's approval of the exclusion of 18 countries from trade preferences under future epa agreements. as members of the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly, we have had a lot of discussion on this subject with our colleagues from the acp countries, who have expressed their deep concern about this change and have asked for a sufficient extension of the deadline. since this approach has not been adopted, i would like to express my disappointment today and stress the need for the union to put its policy of development cohesion into practice by establishing strong links between development aid and the other sectoral policies of the european union, in particular agricultural, trade and fiscal policies. i would also like to point out that the acp countries and regions are ready to conclude fair and mutually beneficial epas in the spirit of the cotonou agreements. i am therefore criticising this logic of punishment, whereas these agreements must be built on successes and fair trade relations.
in writing. relations between the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries and the european union are governed by the acp-eu partnership agreement concluded in cotonou on 23 june 2000 for a period of 20 years. in this agreement, the two sides agreed to replace existing trade provisions with economic partnership agreements (epas) in order to gradually remove barriers to trade and improve cooperation in all trade-related areas. i voted in favour of this report which seeks to put an end to the incompatibility of special tariff concessions granted to countries which have not accompanied the process of ratification of the epas. the proposed regulation was an exception to the normal system of tariff concessions under the rules of the world trade organization as it was a special derogation for acp countries. i therefore support the european commission in sanctioning countries which do not comply with the provisions of this regulation, the non-signatories of the epa. the amending regulation also divides the 18 acp countries which have not signed the epa into three categories according to their income level.
in writing. i voted in favour of amending the number of acp countries benefiting from preferential tariff regimes for their trade with the eu. at present, 36 countries imported into the eu without paying any taxes. some former acp countries have taken advantage of this wto derogation to disregard the rules and not ratify the economic partnership agreement, when they are now able to assume the normal wto rules. in accordance with the principle of fairness, we have therefore chosen to exclude from the list certain countries which will no longer benefit from the preferential regime as of october 2014.
in writing. to help the poorest countries in the world develop, the european union has committed itself to concluding economic partnership agreements with the acp (africa, caribbean and pacific) countries in order to boost trade. pending the formal conclusion of these agreements, the european union has granted preferential access to its markets to products from acp countries since 2008. while some economic partnership agreements are already in force, negotiations for these agreements between the eu and 17 acp countries are still ongoing. the eu's trade preferences for products originating from these countries were originally due to end on 1 january 2014, to make way for the new trade regime provided for in the economic partnership agreements. in view of the longer negotiating period, it became necessary for the union to grant an additional 10 months of trade preferences to these 17 countries, in order not to create instability detrimental to the states parties concerned, the time to conclude and ratify balanced agreements respecting the interests of both parties.
in writing. the trade preferences currently enjoyed by acp countries are contrary to wto rules. the union then put in place new economic partnership agreements in line with wto rules. however, some countries have not signed these new agreements, which poses a real problem of fairness towards those who have signed them. i supported this report which seeks to exclude from trade preferences those countries which have not yet signed these new agreements. in this text, the european union puts a point of honour on respecting the rules of the wto and the principle of fairness.
in writing. the european union has entered into negotiations with 36 countries in the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) region to conclude asymmetric free trade agreements known as economic partnership agreements (epas). however, while some regions have already ratified interim agreements since 2007, other negotiations have not yet been concluded. there is a diversity of situations within the acp area. while 18 countries have ratified the agreement, the other 18 countries that have not can be classified into three categories: least developed countries benefiting from the "everything but arms" initiative; countries benefiting from the generalised system of preferences; and countries benefiting from the "everything but arms" initiative. and middle-income countries. the eu is obliged to comply with wto rules and to honour its commitments to countries that have ratified epas. i therefore welcome the position adopted by the european parliament and widely supported on tuesday, 16 april, to exclude those countries which have not taken the necessary steps to ratify these agreements as of october 2014.
in writing. certain acp countries (africa, caribbean and pacific) continued to benefit from tariff preferences for their exports to the european union, even though they no longer met the criteria justifying this preferential treatment. as this is illegal under the world trade organisation system, there was an urgent need to regularize the situation and consider signing economic partnership agreements (epas) with these countries. by voting in favour of this text, which sets 1 october 2014 as the date by which the states concerned must have ratified the epas, i believe i have supported a fair compromise, which will give the countries concerned enough time to prepare for this change.
in writing. this report at second reading is a step back from the already despicable report which was put to our vote last september. it continued to support the institutionalisation of blackmail excluding the benefit of trade preferences on acp governments which refuse to ratify economic partnership agreements. the only 'advance' proposed in the text is to delay the implementation of the threat by a few months. pillage or punishment. this is the only alternative that the majority here present has left to the peoples of botswana, burundi, cameroon, the comoros, côte d'ivoire, the republic of fiji, ghana, haiti, kenya, lesotho, mozambique, namibia, rwanda, swaziland, tanzania, uganda, zambia and zimbabwe. i denounce this odious text. the time for colonies is over! i vote against it.
in writing. the report proposed for second reading aims to exclude a number of african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries from the list of countries benefiting from trade preferences, on the grounds that they are not ratifying the economic partnership agreements (epas), free trade agreements with the eu, quickly enough. such a measure is designed to put pressure on the acp countries to sign these epas. however, some of the provisions of these agreements are controversial and could seriously harm the development of the acp countries, in particular by putting their local products in direct competition with eu products and reducing their customs duty revenue. for all these reasons, i have decided to vote against this proposal.
in writing. in the interests of the acp countries, i believe that the deadline for the latter to have preferential access to the eu market should have been postponed to 1 january 2016, two years longer than the european commission's initial proposal. such a decision would have sent a positive signal to our acp partners, for whom ratification of the economic partnership agreements with the eu will have major consequences. the european right does not seem to regard the acp countries as respectable partners, but would rather impose trade liberalisation on them. the date of 1 october 2014 was therefore finally decided today by the european parliament's vote. this date, which is the result of the compromise reached last month with the council, has the merit of giving the acp countries nine more months to prepare for this profound change in our trade relations. this compromise is the lesser of two evils, and i have therefore supported it today. but i would like to reiterate that it does not represent my initial position or that of our acp partners.
in writing. around 20 countries (cameroon, mozambique, haiti, etc.) have refused to take the necessary steps to ratify the economic partnership agreements (epas) with the eu. the commission and the council want to encourage these countries to sign these agreements as soon as possible. the commission's regulation threatens to exclude them from the list of countries which grant them preferential customs duties, which would put them in great budgetary difficulty. worse still, the arrival of low-priced european agricultural products risks destabilising food agriculture in these countries. and converting to export monocultures would inevitably lead to the destruction of local production at the expense of the food of the population and major ecological imbalances and make them even more dependent on fluctuations in world markets. the only room for manoeuvre we had in parliament was, at best, to postpone this measure from january 2014 to october 2014, leaving a tiny bit more time for countries to prepare. i voted for all the amendments setting the earliest possible dates and i would like to denounce here this institutional blackmail which leaves us with no choice but to set the cut-off date for these countries.
in writing. the european carbon emission trading scheme (ects) is the cornerstone of the eu's climate policy. this market system aims at the progressive reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in the union in order to meet the international commitments under the kyoto protocol. however, an over-allocation of emission allowances for the third phase of the ets (2013-2020), combined with the economic crisis and the impact of other energy objectives, led to an over-allocation of allowances in relation to industrial needs. the market is suffering from a severe imbalance, and the price of a ton of carbon has fallen by 30% in one year. i am very sorry that the members have rejected the commission's proposal to freeze quotas, although i am convinced that the ems must be saved by reforming it both in the short term and structurally in the long term. i believe that if a market is not functioning properly, we must have the courage to regulate it by correcting the rules. that is why we must continue to work on the reform of the etuc.
in writing. twenty votes were missing to adopt the backloading bill and give fresh life to our greenhouse gas emissions trading system. what a failure! the european parliament's rejection of the postponement of the auctioning of 900 million tonnes of carbon allowances is a serious setback for the eu, and de facto reduces our ambition to exercise leadership in the fight against climate change. even as non-eu countries adopt the system, we will bury ours! immediately after the vote, the price per tonne fell to 3 euros, which means that this is not the way to encourage the development of cleaner energy sources. i welcome the determination of commissioner hedegaard, who has already announced that she still intends to raise the price of the tonne. so of course, the barter system is not the panacea, far from it. but this backloading was an emergency measure, nothing more, because the need for structural reform is recognized by all and proposals are already on the table.
in writing. i voted against the commission's proposal to freeze 900 million 'rights to pollute' on the carbon market in order to limit the number of securities available on the market and thus better manage the carbon price. the proposal would have had the direct consequence of increasing the cost of energy, and in these times of crisis it is important to think first of our industries and our jobs. i remain convinced that a policy to reduce greenhouse gases such as the ets is necessary, as is support for investment in renewable energy. but in this difficult period for our companies, we had to make a rational choice and think about our jobs.
in writing. the emissions trading scheme is a symbol of the european union's leading edge in the fight against climate change. i think we urgently need structural reforms to get it back to working properly. is this the right time to artificially raise the price of carbon? in these times of crisis, we must not do anything which might even cause fear of a loss of competitiveness in our companies. it is the jobs of europeans that are at stake. that is why i spoke against the commission's proposal. this matter has been referred to the committee on the environment, so we shall have the opportunity to continue our reflection on the subject.
in writing. at the global level, tackling the effects of climate change is probably one of the greatest challenges of all time. since the 1990s, the european union has taken bold steps in this regard, including the establishment of a carbon market to limit emissions from the most polluting industries. but the european system of trading quotas is now facing a crisis that threatens its existence and credibility. in addition to the deteriorating economic environment, the lack of visibility into the 2030 and 2040 constraint and the weak perception by market participants of the political will to support the market today and in the longer term have a strong impact on carbon prices. a first emergency measure could have been backloading, i.e. postponing the auctioning of 900 million tonnes of carbon allowances. but beyond this measure, which was referred back for consideration by a small majority in the european parliament, what we need above all is an ambitious and lasting reform of the system for combating climate change.
in writing. the ets was introduced in 2005 with the aim of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. the market is now in serious difficulty, with the price of a tonne of carbon being less than 5 euros. it therefore seemed essential to react and vote in favour of this text which will help to save this system, which is the very heart of european policy to combat climate change. contrary to many of the arguments put forward, this measure should encourage the development of an industry that is more environmentally friendly.
in writing. i voted in favour of rejecting this proposal and, at the very least, in favour of referring it back to committee. because it seems to me that the european commission is a little contradictory. for years its entire policy has been based on the belief in the efficiency of markets, and now on this particular issue it is proposing to manipulate the market on the grounds that the price per tonne of co2 is too low. it is true that the real issue is ideological: economic realism versus global warming religion. the opposite majorities in the committees on industry and the environment are symptomatic in this respect. the problem is that these prices are perfectly justified in the light of the current economic crisis. and if the system is bad, then it's the whole system that needs to be changed, not trying to fix it up one by one.
in writing. the carbon market is the only operational instrument of eu climate policy to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions. due to the crisis and the "generosity" of the states in allocating quotas to industrial sectors, this market has completely collapsed since 2008. to remedy this, the european commission is proposing to intervene in the european market for co2 allowances by freezing 900 million surplus allowances. this proposal, which was not sufficient, would have allowed the european carbon market to survive and opened up the prospect of a thoroughgoing overhaul of the european emissions trading system. by rejecting this proposal, the european parliament is undermining the efforts of many companies to reduce their emissions and contribute to the decarbonised economy we need to achieve by 2050 to avoid climate catastrophe. that is why i voted against this report. the proposal is currently being referred back to committee and will return to the plenary in a few weeks' time. i hope that this time the members of the european parliament will be up to the challenge.
in writing. the european parliament's rejection of the european commission's proposal to intervene in the co2 emission allowance market and artificially raise the price per tonne is a common sense decision. we cannot afford to add crisis to crisis while our industries are suffering the full effects of the economic downturn in europe and the pressure of global competition. in 2008, nicolas sarkozy's government committed the eu to reducing its emissions by 20% by 2020. this is a goal we are keeping in mind and we must acknowledge the efforts already made by industry in this direction. the rejection of the commission's proposal does not mean the death of the european carbon trading system but the will not to disrupt the activities of industries and their long-term investment plans which will serve, when growth reappears in europe, the objective of combating climate change. today, however, the priority must be to maintain industrial activity and our jobs in europe.
in writing. i have chosen, like the majority of my epp colleagues, to reject the european commission's proposal to freeze the auctioning of excess co2 allowances under the european carbon trading system, the cornerstone of the european union's climate policy. while it is certain that the eu will achieve its 2020 emission reduction targets (a 20% reduction), i do not want to aggravate an already very painful situation for our european businesses in these times of economic crisis.
in writing. the european parliament chose to refer this proposal, which aimed to increase the price of the 'polluting permit' within the european union, to the environment committee. this will give members more time to debate the subject, which i thought was necessary. the question is far too complex and transversal, and the proposal did not contain any measures to provide a comprehensive answer. on the other hand, the economic situation is such that a rise in the price of carbon would risk reducing the competitiveness of our companies and industry, especially small and mediumsized ones, which would be hit the hardest.
in writing. i personally voted against the freezing of the auctioning of 900 million tonnes of surplus co2 emission allowances. far from separating the 'good' and the 'bad', those who would be in favour of the environment and the fight against global warming and those who would be hostile to it and would have 'sold out' to the industrial lobbies, i think that the freezing of the auction of the auction proposed by commissioner hedegaard would lead to an extra cost of the price of energy for both individuals and companies. and this really doesn't seem like the right time! moreover, the european union is an example, it is perfectly capable of meeting its co2 emission reduction targets by 2020 without going through this freeze. i therefore voted, with the majority of my colleagues, to refer the text to the relevant parliamentary committees so that they can work on a solution to adapt the market management system to the economic realities of the moment without hindering the continuation of the fight against global warming.
in writing. the text does not call into question the carbon market, whose inefficiency and even harmfulness have now been proven. it does not at any time refer to the competition of auction platforms for polluting rights and their derivatives. it merely allows the commission to make a change to the timetable for auctioning the polluting rights without ever asking what the commission's intentions are in this respect. it also stressed the need to take precautions to avoid encouraging companies to relocate. another report that benefits the markets and harms the environment. i vote against it.
in writing. the current european system for combating greenhouse gas emissions, based on a european carbon market where 'polluting rights' are sold, is far from effective. for example, it has not achieved the emission reduction targets. this is partly because carbon prices tend to be too low to provide an incentive for a transition to cleaner production methods, which is not acceptable. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the commission's proposal to clarify the provisions on the timing of the auctioning of emission allowances to increase carbon prices, and thus to encourage companies to further reduce their emissions. however, beyond this provision, i would like to see a much more profound reform of this system. in order to meet the challenge of climate change, the european union needs to develop new, more ambitious and truly effective policies to support the transition to a low-carbon economy.
in writing. it was inconceivable that i would support this proposal. and i am very glad that parliament has rejected it. i am sorry to see that parliament has left the door open to further negotiations. the price of co2 emission allowances, which was the aim of the manoeuvre, would have been artificially increased, and all our efforts to restart industrial activity would have been foiled! this would have further weakened the competitiveness of our industries vis-à-vis our competitors. on the one hand, because of the almost instantaneous increase in the cost of energy and, consequently, in production. and secondly, the legal instability of our standards would have pushed our entrepreneurs and investors even further to leave europe. let's not add crisis to crisis! the fight against climate change must of course be and always remain at the centre of our priorities. but europe is a good student, and we will achieve all our greenhouse gas emission reduction targets without any problems. this is confirmed by many experts. so let us get rid of these blinders that prevent us from identifying the real emergencies and let us try, once and for all, to save our economic model!
in writing. parliament voted this week on the temporary freezing of 900 million tonnes of co2. this was a measure to save the co2 market by raising the price of a tonne of co2. i voted for this freezing of quotas and i deeply regret that it was rejected by a majority of members. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. in reality, this was an important pro-environmental measure that effectively combats co2 emissions. moreover, voting against this text not only does not encourage virtuous behaviour but, on the contrary, penalizes companies that have made investment efforts to make their activity less emissive.
in writing. the european emissions trading scheme is a unique carbon marketplace created to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from european industries. companies have carbon credits, which they can auction off if they reduce their emissions. the crisis has weakened energy-consuming companies, reducing their production and thus their emissions. the commission wanted to raise the price of a tonne of co2 to encourage renewable energy. however, this proposal risks raising the cost of energy, destabilising the market and increasing the advantage of industries outside the european union. i therefore voted against this proposal in order to consider how to improve the system on a permanent basis without calling into question the principles of the system.
in writing. the european parliament has given its opinion on the timetable for greenhouse gas emission allowance auctions. the european union has set up a quota trading system to reduce co2 emissions from european industries, which are responsible for global warming. however, as a result of the crisis, the tonne of co2 has fallen dramatically (from eur 30 at the end of 2011 to less than eur 7 at present). i regret that parliament has decided to leave the system as it is with a ton of very cheap co2. i have personally voted for a reform of the system so that the price of a tonne of co2 is raised. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the products it produces. and, beyond these environmental considerations, it should be stressed that green technologies are a particularly important source of jobs for the european union. i also want to encourage the many smes in europe to invest more in less polluting technologies.
in writing. parliament's rejection of the possibility of freezing the auctioning of 900 million tonnes of co2 emission allowances seriously calls into question the relevance of the very existence of the emission allowance market, and shows the limits of the commodification of pollution. the price of a ton of carbon, which is supposed to limit emissions by imposing a dissuasive price, has only fallen since its creation: from 30 euros per ton when it was launched, it was 10 euros last year, and fell to 2.63 euros at 2 pm, after the rejection of the parliament. 89% of europeans consider global warming to be a serious issue and believe that it can also help boost the economy and employment (eurobarometer 2011). if a reassessment of the system seemed necessary, it will now undoubtedly be necessary to focus on the union providing a credible response to the problem posed by the lack of deterrence of the existing system. the question of environmental dumping is indeed a problem, exacerbated by the economic and social crisis we are going through.
in writing. given the unprecedented circumstances facing the eu in relation to the ets, i believe that the commission should be able to adapt the auction timetable exceptionally, in the interests of stability of the regulation and in advance of the implementation of long-term structural measures. it is also important to send a signal of political commitment to market players. that is why i supported the groote report. europe needs concrete and rapid action, particularly when projects are launched under ner300. the proposals to reject the ets, on the contrary, presuppose a long and cumbersome implementation of an alternative system, which would destabilize the market. moreover, the arguments that the increase in the price of the carbon tonne is harmful to undertakings are not valid, since the objective is to restore the price of the tonne as it was at the launch of the ets. in addition, sectors subject to international competition are already protected in the basic system. the groote report responds well to current concerns by ensuring the stability of the ets while paving the way for the establishment of long-term measures.
in writing. − the european commission's proposed suspension of allowance trading is not to be supported as it creates uncertainty about the future of the eu emissions trading system (ets) and threatens the future of local manufacturing companies. i believe that the commission should be more cautious with such measures, by carefully assessing how the suspension of quotas will affect european producers, including latvian companies that export their products to third countries. the commission's aim in encouraging the suspension of the trading of allowances and thus artificially driving up the price of co2 allowances on the market is an ill-conceived proposal to reduce harmful emissions into the air. the commission's initiative would bring transparency to climate change legislation by affecting the current trading period provided for in existing legislation. this would introduce a certain degree of uncertainty and create a situation in which european producers, including latvian producers, would find it difficult to plan production for the coming years. at a time when we need to think about how to get out of economic stagnation, postponing quota trading would further limit the recovery of production and put jobs at risk. that is why i am voting against the commission's proposal.
in writing. under pressure from the industrial and employers' lobby, the right wing of parliament rejected the commission's proposal to freeze a large part of the excess co2 emission allowances of the european emissions trading system (ets). this is a real scandal because a large number of european industries have benefited from the over-allocation of quotas since the creation of the ets. the freeze was intended to help raise the price of co2 and to encourage manufacturers to invest in cleaner production processes. it's a bummer because the current system has been ineffective for years. the gue/ngl group remains hostile to the carbon market system, but it is the only mechanism at the moment to try to reduce co2 emissions. the commission has therefore at least to be better placed to compel manufacturers to reduce their emissions. the only long-term solution is a thorough reform of the ets and the establishment of a genuine european policy to combat climate change, which is more necessary than ever. the vote by a majority of parliament is therefore totally irresponsible because by maintaining the status quo of the ets system, it leaves open the right to pollute for industrialists.
in writing. the greenhouse gas emissions trading scheme (ges) for intercontinental flights departing from and landing at european airports is an ambitious environmental policy programme of the european union. i voted in favour of the interinstitutional agreement freezing the entry into force of this programme for the year 2012. the aim is to 'stop the ets pendulum' for one year for intercontinental flights (operated by eu and third country airlines) at departure and at landing at eu airports. this freeze on the entry into force of the directive will help to ease tensions with our partners in third countries and to negotiate with them an international agreement on carbon emissions from the aviation sector. if successful, european aviation will no longer face competition from airlines not bound by the same climate obligations. it is now up to the council to decide on the freezing of directive 2003/87/ec. he has to do it by april 30th.
in writing. on 16 april, the european parliament put forward directive 2008/101/ec which incorporates airlines into the greenhouse gas emission allowance system. ceding to pressure from its major trading partners (china and the united states in the lead), a small majority of elected officials has just contributed, as is no longer customary in these times of crisis, to the eu's leadership in the fight against global warming. the majority voted to postpone the application of the scheme to intercontinental flights to and from the eu until the international civil aviation organisation ag scheduled for november 2013. the reasons given are more than wrong: how could this measure, which continues to apply to flights within the eu, distort competition or hinder competitiveness, when its application only increases the price of the air ticket by about one euro per passenger? even less clear is how this would strengthen the eu's negotiating capacity within icao, as it is weakening its positions even before the start of negotiations that are supposed to lead to a global agreement on the issue. that is why i opposed the postponement of the directive.
in writing. i voted in favour of the derogation from the ets regime in the field of continental flights. the ets system set up by the commission aims to introduce 'polluting permits', but this system is suspended for intercontinental flights to and from airports outside the european economic area, in order to facilitate progress towards a comprehensive agreement within the international civil aviation organisation (icao). this derogation is only temporary (one year), and the eu is trying to put some pressure on the icao negotiations to move forward.
in writing. how can aviation, whose greenhouse gas emissions have increased substantially, be encouraged to take better account of its impact and responsibility in climate change? this vote is a strong signal to all our partners, a signal of our goodwill: we are ready to negotiate an agreement that will suit everyone. but this vote also shows our determination: if no concrete and effective solution is found, we will apply the emissions trading system (ets) to all international flights. we are now awaiting the results of the icao's work. this derogation is not a renunciation: it is intended to enable us to conduct the negotiations on a sound and calm basis with our partners, and i therefore fully support it.
in writing. the next summit of the international civil aviation organisation (icao) in september 2013 has a good chance of reaching a multilateral agreement establishing a global market mechanism to regulate co2 emissions in the aviation sector. in order to send a positive signal to its international partners, the european union has decided to temporarily suspend its system of carbon emission quotas for intercontinental flights by european and non-european carriers for a period of one year. the hand extended by europe on the eve of the international negotiations in the icao must now be translated into rapid and effective results in reducing the quantities of greenhouse gases produced by aviation, which have almost doubled in the last 20 years and represent 3% of the total.
in writing. i supported the postponement of the application of the emissions trading scheme to the aviation sector for flights to and from third countries in order to allow for the continuation of internal negotiations. the european union must strengthen its dialogue with its partners by the end of the year so that this issue can be addressed constructively when new negotiations are opened in the icao next autumn. the european union must be firm in maintaining this objective, but it cannot ignore the opposition of many of our key partners who regret the use of the dialogue method on this issue. it is urgent to strengthen contacts so that these tensions are reflected in the implementation of retaliatory measures against aviation actors who cannot be supported by this major political blockade.
in writing. the european parliament's rejection of the european commission's proposal to intervene in the co2 emission allowance market and artificially raise the price per tonne is a common sense decision. we cannot afford to add crisis to crisis while our industries are suffering the full effects of the economic downturn in europe and the pressure of global competition. in 2008, nicolas sarkozy's government committed the eu to reducing its emissions by 20% by 2020. this is a goal we are keeping in mind and we must acknowledge the efforts already made by industry in this direction. the rejection of the commission's proposal does not mean the death of the european carbon trading system but the will not to disrupt the activities of industries and their long-term investment plans which will serve, when growth reappears in europe, the objective of combating climate change. today, however, the priority must be to maintain industrial activity and our jobs in europe.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague peter liese in plenary. the report was adopted by 577 votes in favour, 114 against and 21 abstentions. i welcome the adoption of this report which will allow for a temporary derogation from the conditions of directive 2003/87/ec establishing the ets (greenhouse gas emission allowance trading scheme) in order to allow for global regulation of emissions in the aviation sector.
in writing. the report proposes to remove any obligation to meet greenhouse gas emission quotas for flights to or from airports outside the eu. the commission has therefore submitted to pressure from the us airlines, which has been rejected by the court of justice of the european union. the pretext for this backsliding was the development of a global market mechanism for the exchange of emission allowances between airlines. therefore, no consequences are drawn from the inefficiency of the carbon market. i am voting against this inept text.
in writing. created in 2005 to combat climate change, the european carbon market operates on the basis of emission quotas, real 'polluting rights', which are supposed to encourage industry to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. but today we see that this system has failed. it has failed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions or encourage investment in cleaner production methods. in some cases, it has even helped finance the biggest polluters. moreover, the carbon prices defined by this market are volatile and tend to be too low and fraud is widespread. that is why i opposed the proposal to safeguard this inefficient system by freezing some of the excess co2 allowances on the market. what we need is an end to this carbon market, a change of direction to adopt ambitious measures to effectively combat climate change, and a deeper transformation of our energy, financial and transport systems, as well as our modes of production, distribution and waste management.
in writing. in the plenary vote, i supported the european commission's proposal because i believe that the 'concentration at the end of the period' it envisages is a necessary option, at the risk of endangering the emissions trading system (ets) itself. we have seen this: the day after the vote, the price per tonne fell to 2 euros. the eecsc is at the heart of european policy to combat climate change and is beginning to take off in other major powers (australia, korea, china). if we europeans no longer support our own system, how will we be armed in future world markets? i hope very much that this matter will be brought back to our agenda as soon as possible so that we can find a positive solution together.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to strengthen regulation of the banking sector, whose deregulation was one of the main causes of the financial crisis. the crd iv package proposed by the european commission thus amends the eu rules on capital requirements for banks and investment firms. i fully support this proposal for a directive, because these new rules are designed to regulate banking activities in order to protect individual savers from taking excessive risks. for example, imposing capital requirements on banks. it was also necessary to limit the bonuses of bankers and traders, so that their remuneration could no longer exceed the total amount of their fixed salary. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions. this proposal is the new cornerstone of a stable and more transparent european financial system.
in writing. i voted in favour of a package of measures to make banks more resilient, including capping bankers' bonuses, strengthening capital, and increasing supervision of speculative activities. this package of measures will also boost growth by facilitating access to loans for smes. the texts adopted constitute the foundation of a future banking union, providing a single supervisory mechanism, a deposit guarantee scheme and a new banking culture. it was a matter of being ambitious and showing that the european parliament was ready to move towards this banking union.
in writing. the aim of this vote is to put banks back at the service of the real economy. i hope that this agreement will be an important step in that direction. with this text we will not only make the banks more resilient to the risks of crisis, but we will also make a great step forward: that of limiting the bonuses for bankers.
in writing. the economic and financial crisis in which the european union has been embroiled for several years has highlighted the urgent need to regulate banks more strictly so that they are more resilient to uncertainties and more focused on their primary mission, the financing of the real economy. the european union has therefore drawn up a fundamental reform that should make it easier for banks to lend to businesses, to invest more securely in the markets and to be better equipped to deal with possible crises. european banks will now have to devote more of their capital to lending to smes. they will be required to have a larger share of 'own capital', reserves of non-virtual money, which can be mobilised quickly in case of emergency and which are intended to avoid the risk of bankruptcy. bankers' bonuses will be capped to reduce unreasonable speculative risk-taking. finally, banks will have to be more transparent, reporting to the commission their profits, turnover, taxes paid and the number of people they employ. this should eventually consolidate our business network and encourage production and thus the creation of sustainable jobs.
in writing. i voted in favour of these texts, which represent a significant step forward in the establishment of a banking union. as the financial crisis has unfortunately shown, the economic and monetary union today lacks a banking and financial component in order to be fully effective and coherent. these two texts are already a first step, pending the actual establishment of this banking union.
in writing. i could not vote in favour of the two karas reports, which were supposed to adapt european and national banking law to the requirements of basel iii, and which were watered down by the basel committee itself a few months ago. the cap on wages is a good thing. but this does not offset other problems created by this regulation. i am thinking in particular of the increasingly disintermediated financing of the economy, the rush to deposit, and the very slow and very elaborate transposition of these same requirements in the united states. and last but not least, we know the objections raised by the banking sector against basel iii. and if he is satisfied with the compromise reached today, it is because it is not that good.
in writing. since 2008 a lot has been said about banks and their responsibilities in the crisis we are going through in europe. many also stressed the need to support smes and the real economy. but so far all these statements have been well-intentioned. with this text, which i supported, we have just made a real breakthrough. firstly, in the transparency of the financial sector and the soundness of the banks. secondly, in support of smes and the real economy. this is a key point for a lasting solution to the crisis which has been besetting europe for too long. because without investment and support for those who create and innovate, we will not be able to reverse this trend in a sustainable way.
in writing. i supported this report which finally confirms the launch of a genuine european banking reform to better control and prevent speculative financial deviations. this package of reforms provides for several significant and pioneering developments in the world. first, the bonuses of bankers and traders will now be capped and will no longer be allowed to exceed the amount of their fixed salary without consulting the shareholders. secondly, the text requires banks to be more transparent. they will have to publish the precise details of their activities in each country. third, banks will need to have a higher level of liquidity in the future to better contain the risks of bankruptcy and costly bailouts for taxpayers. finally, i welcome the fact that this banking reform provides for concrete measures for the real economy, for example by making it easier for european smes to obtain loans.
in writing. at the plenary session on 16 april, i supported the report by my colleague othmar karas on credit institutions and prudential supervision. the report was adopted by a large majority, with 608 votes in favour, 33 against and 68 abstentions. i welcome the adoption of this report which will ensure the proper functioning of banking markets and restore confidence in the sector. the new legislation will deal with credit institutions and investment firms in a single body and will allow for a consistent application of all the provisions.
in writing. i voted in favour of these reports, which are part of the reform package setting new rules for credit institutions and investment firms, because this is a fundamental issue and a key step in the reform of the european banking system. the measures adopted will prevent the abuses that led to the crisis, which completely paralysed the banking market, from happening again and will also help to stimulate growth. for example, capping bonuses for bankers (up to twice their normal salary) will discourage dangerous speculation, which has been allowed too often in the past, and will encourage banks to lend more to the real economy, especially to small and medium-sized enterprises. the increase in the quantity and quality of capital requirements will make banks more independent of each other and thus more resilient in the event of a crisis.
in writing. the april part-session was marked by progress in the banking sector, with the adoption of two texts, which, under the impetus of commissioner michel barnier, respond to the challenges of european banking regulation required by all european citizens. the supervision of european banks continues to progress, step by step, despite some resistance, and the project of a genuine european banking union, which should enable us to cope with new financial and banking crises in the future, is within reach. i voted in favour of the capping of the bonus for bankers and in favour of the strengthening of the capital of banking institutions.
in writing. the report proposes to limit the exorbitant bonuses of bankers. that's a good thing. it is regrettable, however, that it does not propose to limit the remuneration on which these are based. the text also proposes to raise the capital requirements of banks beyond the basel iii ceiling and to leave some room for manoeuvre to governments in this respect. i regret that the margin of manoeuvre is so small and the ceiling so low. i shall vote for the few advances in this text.
in writing. i voted for this report which lays the cornerstone of the moralization of financial capitalism. the package of measures adopted by meps is the most ambitious banking reform ever proposed in europe. these new rules will apply uniformly to all the eu's 8300 banks. bankers' bonuses will be capped against their salaries at a ratio of 1 to 1 to reduce reckless risk-taking. banks will also be required to set up a reserve of 8% of equity capital easily convertible into cash in order to pay depositors in case of emergency, reassure customers and avoid bankruptcies. five years after lehman brothers, and thanks to the decisive action of nicolas sarkozy at the height of the crisis, europe has a responsible banking system that can finance the real economy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the othmar karas report to provide the european union with a set of rules to strengthen the european banking system. the recent financial crisis has shown that international finance has lost all control and that banking institutions are no longer fulfilling their primary function: banks must finance the real economy by offering loans to individuals and businesses. this uncontrolled financial system has plunged europe into an unprecedented economic crisis. so we have learned from this crisis by adopting an ambitious reform package to boost growth, by facilitating lending to smes, the engines of the real economy. among the measures designed to strengthen our banking system, i also voted in favour of capping the bonuses for bankers.
in writing. i chose to abstain on the proposal for a directive on access to the activity of credit institutions and the prudential supervision of credit institutions and investment firms. this text contains several elements which go in the right direction, unlike its predecessor, which was adopted in the form of a regulation. it stressed the importance of combating tax evasion and increasing the transparency of financial activities. this is more than necessary, in order not to repeat the financial disaster of 2008 it also encourages sustainable banking activities, such as mutual credit unions and cooperative banks, which primarily serve the interests of individuals, in particular through their members. it also denounces the excessive influence of external credit ratings on these institutions. however, the text was largely emptied of its content during the negotiations with the council. and many of these proposals are simply invitations, not binding ones, to the member states to increase supervision of banking activities. most likely they will continue to let the banks operate as they do today.
in writing. the reform of the crd iv proposed by the european commission brings the international banking prudential rules of basel iii into line with the european level in order to strengthen the quantity and quality of bank capital. i voted in favour of this report setting out the prudential requirements applicable to credit institutions and investment firms. the lessons of the financial and economic crisis must be learned if sustainable growth is to be restored and the battle for competitiveness won. the new regulation thus introduces capital requirements with a directly applicable regulation, in order to avoid divergent transposition between member states. this regulation is accompanied by a liquidity requirement by requiring institutions to hold liquid assets. in addition, in order to ensure long-term funding, a stable net funding ratio will be implemented to ensure that institutions have access to stable sources of funding. finally, member states will be able to impose stricter macroprudential requirements on nationally authorised financial institutions for a period of up to two years in order to address increased risks to financial stability.

in writing. i welcome the fact that parliament today confirmed in strasbourg the agreement reached with the council on the most important banking reform since the subprime bubble and the start of the crisis in 2008. the french and european socialists have acted to win, after the introduction of the financial transaction tax, this new major battle in the long political battle against finance: the capping of bank bonuses, to put an end to the greed of bling-bling traders, is a socialist victory; the transparency imposed on banks to obtain details of their activities country by country is another socialist victory; the requirement of higher and better capital in banks to prevent the casino economy is always a socialist victory.
in writing. with this text, we will be able to create the conditions to guarantee greater stability for our banks and financial institutions, for the benefit of all europeans and our competitiveness, and therefore our jobs. i hope that these new rules will help to trigger a real change in mindset. i particularly support the emphasis on the protection of smes and start-ups in the application of this new regime.
