in writing. i have chosen to vote against the proposal for a regulation on prudential requirements for credit institutions and investment firms. regulating the way financial institutions operate is urgently needed to avoid a repeat of the 2008 crisis. this financial catastrophe has turned into an economic and social disaster for the people of europe and the world. the original aim of this proposal was to strengthen transparency, accountability and regulation. the council has stripped this text of its substance in the negotiations with the european parliament. in this text, there are no guarantees that economically and socially useful banking activities can be effectively favoured over sterile speculative practices. for example, there is no assurance that the rules will be different according to the 'risk profiles' of institutions. thus, a public bank financing projects of general interest could be subject to the same rules as high-risk credit companies. for these reasons i have opposed this deceptive text which purports to regulate financial activities. it does not in any way prevent the banks from continuing to act as they do today.
in writing. the rules on the organisation of groundhandling services at community airports (handling of baggage, cargo, cleaning and refuelling of aircraft) needed to be revised in order to improve the efficiency of these services in europe. i voted in favour of this report, which proposes a cautious but necessary liberalisation of stopover services. on the other hand, this compromise establishes a system of quality standards that airports with more than 5 million passengers will be able to require from their service providers. these standards would cover the performance of providers (maximum waiting time for passenger check-in or baggage collection for example), training requirements, equipment (minimum stock of aircraft defrosting liquid, maximum time to defrost aircraft). the proposal also provides greater protection for workers. the text was finally adopted by a comfortable majority in the european parliament, after a first rejection for reconsideration in committee last december. the negotiations on the airport package will therefore be able to continue with the council.
in writing. the efficiency and safety of travellers depend on the quality of services and working conditions in ground handling services at airports. i voted in favour of this resolution because it aims to encourage competition in the sector, to provide adequate training for applicants and to provide information and assistance to the millions of passengers who pass through our european airports every year. the text of course requires compliance with social provisions, including the obligation to apply the respective collective agreements of the member states, and the limitation of the use of subcontracting. the european parliament gave its green light to the negotiations on the text in the trilogue, where it will defend the social issues linked to the development of inland waterway assistance services.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which is intended to continue the still too limited opening up of the market for groundhandling services in the european union. it is in the interest of the traveller to have a choice between a large number of service providers, stopover assistance providers. otherwise, the presence of a duopoly leads to higher prices and a lower quality of service. the compromise proposals put forward by the rapporteur prevent any massive and uncontrolled deregulation, which i am extremely sensitive to.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of the european commission regulation on the liberalisation of airport ground handling services. these services are already liberalised in france. the crucial point was the protection of workers' rights against social dumping by service companies, including subcontractors. handling companies and subcontractors are now obliged to apply collective agreements and to respect national laws.
in writing. ground handling services used by airlines, transport commissioners and passengers at major eu airports require a high level of efficiency in order to meet high standards of reliability, safety and environmental protection. the commission's legislative proposal on this subject, which was referred back to the committee in the december plenary session, has fortunately been improved and now allows progress to be made in finalising the 'legislative package' on airports. harmonised european rules including a time limit for baggage check-in and better information on flight delays and cancellations will now be mandatory for ground handling services. in addition, opening up competition to a third operator at seven of the largest eu airports will increase the supply of services and prepare the sector for increased international competition. this market opening must necessarily be accompanied by fair working conditions and adequate social standards for the staff of these service providers.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this third part of the airport package. this regulation allows users to benefit from better airport services. lost or damaged baggage, delayed flights, airports closed due to frost, excessive transfer times between terminals are all areas that will be improved. the text also meets the requirements of transparency in these markets by clarifying, in particular, the procedures for calling for competition. the measured openness to a third party in some airports opens up the currently regulated markets while increasing the attention paid to staff training, for example. the social clauses send a signal to the employees in this sector: let us put an end to monopolies but let us ensure that working conditions are preserved. however, i regret that the demagogy of certain groups has won the day by allowing the adoption of a promise to employees which cannot be kept: the ban on dismissals. while companies are calling for flexibility and increased dialogue, the rhetoric of such a measure will only cause disillusionment and a sense of betrayal of the policies when employees in the sector find that these measures remain contrary to national legislation and therefore inapplicable.
in writing. last december i voted to refer this text back to committee so that it could be reworked to achieve a better balance. the new proposal, which i supported, offers positive advances for this sector, and i think that should be welcomed. while providing important guarantees for workers, this text makes it possible to modernise a sector which sometimes has difficulty functioning. the reform will affect only the very large european airports, the smaller ones being preserved.
in writing. the air transport sector has developed considerably in recent years. the number of passenger flights, the quantities of cargo, are increasing sharply and it seems essential to regulate the activity more for obvious safety reasons. whether for the safety of passengers, the rights of workers or the sovereignty of the member states, this sector must be protected and regulated. unfortunately, the opposite has been done. the new directive even increases competition between service providers. this is an unbridled competition which always ends up hurting the safety and social conditions of the employees. it's a change of direction that the industry needs. yes, the public service must be given the means to take over these activities, to ensure better social protection for employees and the necessary and imperative safety conditions for both users and goods. for us it is obvious that the competitive process will lead to at least-so-called social for employees, and in its race to reduce costs, will endanger passengers. that is why i voted against the directive.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague artur zasada on groundhandling services at eu airports. this report is an integral part of the airport package. it was rejected by the european parliament last december and referred back to the committee on transport. the report was finally adopted at the april plenary session by 455 votes to 239 with 18 abstentions. the report has three objectives: 1. to reduce delays due to failure in the service delivery chain; 2. to improve the quality of services; 3. to end the monopoly situation in regulated airports.
in writing. with this regulation, the commission aims to continue the limited opening of the market for groundhandling services in the european union, which is hampered by the persistence of monopoly or duopoly situations at certain airports. the final version of this text, which had previously been rejected in plenary and referred back to committee, seems to me to be much more balanced. airlines will have a wider choice of providers at major airports, airports will have better tools to coordinate in-flight assistance operations, workers will benefit from social standards unknown in other sectors, third party service providers will have a single, common authorisation system with mutual recognition throughout the eu and passengers will benefit from minimum quality standards. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. i voted in favour of these new rules which improve the quality of services at airports. these include waiting times for baggage check-in, delays for baggage receipt on arrival, transport at the airport and defrosting services for aircraft. the aim of the text is also to introduce a little more competition between service providers to avoid monopolies, while imposing minimum standards that protect workers' rights. airports with more than 15 million passengers and/or 200,000 tonnes of cargo per year will therefore need to have a minimum of three ground handling operators. the text is part of an 'airport package' which also includes a revision of the rules on the allocation of flight slots and the limitation of noise nuisance.
in writing. the report aimed to endorse the liberalisation of ground handling services (gas), i.e. the outsourcing of services to air carriers at airports. allowing at least one third independent ground handling company to enter the market will result in further liberalisation and an increase in the number of ground handling service providers, with catastrophic social consequences for airport workers. this highly controversial text was referred to a parliamentary committee for the first time. unfortunately, this time it was approved, despite the opposition of the gue and thanks to the votes of a majority of social democrats, including french ones.
in writing. i supported this report which stresses the need for changes to the technical measures in place in the fisheries in the skagerrak, the strait between norway and denmark that connects the north sea to the kattegat and leads to the baltic sea. these measures need to be improved in order to ensure the sustainable exploitation of marine biological resources. the rules of the member states and norway concerning technical and control measures in the area more than four nautical miles from the baselines should be harmonised in order to reduce the level of by-catches and to limit discards. among the proposed changes, the rules on the landing obligation should enter into force on 1 january 2014: the sale of juvenile fish for charitable purposes would then be prohibited and a remote electronic monitoring system would then be implemented.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of the report by my colleague werner kuhn, which aims to improve control and enforcement measures in the fisheries in the skagerrak, the strait between norway, sweden and denmark. the aim is to reduce the level of bycatch and discards in this area in order to ensure sustainable fishing and thus the renewal of marine biological resources. the proposed measures concern the landing obligation, the treatment of juvenile fish, the nets used and the introduction of a remote electronic system.
in writing. i voted in favour of amending the fishing conditions in the skagerrak, the common fishing area between the eu and norway. in the absence of specific rules, discards and bycatches were very high, so the technical measures and regulations of the eu and norway had to be harmonised. the report is part of the eu's broader commitment to tackling marine litter, as part of the new common fisheries policy adopted by the european parliament in february.
in writing. i voted against the kuhn report introducing new technical and control measures in the skagerrak. although i think the rules in this area should be harmonised, this is not only because norway has been practising the landing obligation for 30 years. i would argue that the objective to be pursued is the significant reduction of discards as i advocate in the context of the reform of the common fisheries policy. the amendment to make the electronic remote control system optional was not adopted. i am in favour of voluntary rather than compulsory video surveillance, which is why i voted against this report.
in writing. continuous filming of people poses ethical problems, especially in the workplace. furthermore, while the skagerrak fishermen go out during the day, it is not difficult to imagine that this measure, applied to other fisheries in which the fishermen go out for several weeks in a row, would be all the less sustainable. the report adopted by the european parliament raises another major problem: it does not ask for reciprocity from norway, as norwegian fishermen refuse video surveillance as a means of control. this means that fishermen concentrated in a very small area will not be subject to the same constraints, which will inevitably generate tensions. i have therefore decided not to support this text: europe cannot be a house of correction.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text as it will avoid the negative effects of the current fishing practice on the marine environment in this region. by making it compulsory to land fish caught in the skagerrak, the european union is ensuring a more environmentally friendly fishing and, more particularly, a sustainable exploitation of marine biological resources.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on technical and control measures in the skagerrak which implements the ban on the discharge of unwanted fish species between the north sea and the baltic sea. the ban on discards was decided by parliament during the reform of the common fisheries policy last february. the technical provisions, which are based on a remote electronic monitoring system and are supported by european funds, will apply the measure to the territory.
in writing. i support sustainable fisheries management and therefore the development of selective gear to limit by-catch. the landing obligation is intended to encourage research and use of such craft. however, the objective pursued must not lead to the development of privacy-invading surveillance devices. the use of cameras in the city is insufferable enough not to import them at sea. i'll hold off.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which deals unequivocally with the issue of dumping at sea in the skagerrak. it is high time to put an end to 'disposal', the irresponsible practice of dumping fish into the sea on a massive scale because of their size or species, which exacerbates overfishing and is an unacceptable waste (we all know that most fish thrown into the sea die). we propose a gradual implementation (2014-2016) of a ban on the discarding of 35 unwanted fish species: fishing vessels will have to land the fish caught and minimise catches of unwanted and juvenile fish. automatic monitoring will be carried out remotely from electronic equipment, the implementation of which could be financially supported by the european maritime fund. another point of interest in the proposal is the harmonisation of our rules with those of norway. since the end of the international fisheries agreement in the region, european vessels will be required to respect the rules of the countries where they fish. the text could greatly facilitate compliance with these provisions, given that the country requires all fish caught to be landed.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which proposes a ban on the discarding of 35 species of fish with the obligation to land all fish caught in the skagerrak. the problem of discards is a recurring issue for european fisheries: the majority of unwanted fish - too small or out of quota - discarded at sea die, exacerbating resource waste and overfishing. however, the obligation to land all fish poses logistical problems for fishermen and may encourage a 'shadow market' of non-compliant fish. the text serves as a pilot project to prepare the fisheries reform after 2014 which is under discussion in parliament and the council.
in writing. i voted against the kuhn report on technical and control measures in the skagerrak. the proposal to introduce video surveillance to monitor the activity of fishermen is particularly shocking. i believe that it creates an absurd situation of unfair monitoring to ensure the control of a measure, the landing of waste, which is in any case uncontrollable and unenforceable as it stands. these measures are thus a profound restriction on individual freedoms and thus a precedent that must not be tolerated. i remain in favour of more selective and sustainable provisions in the common fisheries policy. in the skagerrak sea as in the whole of the european union.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we celebrated international women's day on 8 march and the european parliament took advantage of the march plenary session to adopt a number of reports and resolutions on women's rights. this new report, which asks the commission to assess the degree of transposition of the 2004 directive on equal treatment for men and women in the provision of goods and services, is therefore far from the first on the subject of gender equality. in the face of these numerous texts on the subject, i sometimes hear voices arising to assert that we have already achieved parity within the european union and that in times of crisis this is not the priority anyway. so i invite those who think this to do a very simple but very informative search on the internet. it is simply a matter of typing the phrase "women should not" in the search bar. it is then noted that the first word that appears in the suggestion is "work" followed closely by the word "vote". this, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, is proof that the fight for equality between men and women is far from being won and remains a priority, including, and probably especially, in times of crisis. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. as a strong advocate of equality between women and men, i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which aims to assess the transposition and application of directive 2004/113/ec implementing the principle of equal treatment between women and men in the access to goods and services. this was the first directive on gender equality outside the workplace. in this context, the european commission is requested to provide a synthesis report in 2014 on the use of gender in the member states as a factor in the calculation of premiums and benefits for insurance and related financial services. meanwhile, the european court of justice, in its test-achats judgment of 1 march 2011, created controversy by requiring all states to prevent the use of sex as a factor of discrimination in the calculation of premiums and benefits. i welcome this report which calls on the european commission to take account of cases of discrimination linked to pregnancy and maternity, which can lead to gross injustices in obtaining loans for women entrepreneurs.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the gurmai report, which is a step forward in taking gender equality into account outside the workplace. the test-achat judgment on the reference to gender in insurance services and the subsequent legislative adjustments at the end of 2011 led the commission to postpone the submission of its report on the implementation by member states of directive 2004/113/ec on equal treatment between women and men in the supply of and access to goods and services to 2014. we remind the commission that it must respect its commitments, since the directive is not limited to the insurance sector and had to be transposed as early as 2007. moreover, this resolution reflects our concern about the inadequacy of the commission's guidelines on equal treatment in insurance pricing policies. we therefore ask the commission to propose new legislation in line with the guidelines resulting from the test-achat judgment, paying greater attention to cases of discrimination linked to maternity, whether in the area of access to housing, access to loans or medical services.
in writing. this report provides an update on the implementation by member states of the directive implementing the principle of equal treatment between women and men in the access to and supply of goods and services. the report regrets that the commission has not presented its report on the application of the directive, nor has it shown in concrete terms the recent progress in the field of equal treatment between men and women. in addition, the report provides an update on access to loans and credit for women entrepreneurs, who face barriers based on gender stereotypes. i have voted against this report because of the discrimination based on sex. it is hard to imagine that such differences in treatment between men and women could still exist today.
in writing. the 2004 directive on equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services was a major step forward in our efforts to achieve genuine gender equality. it is essential to ensure that it is properly implemented. however, the commission has decided to postpone the preparation of its summary report assessing its implementation, which will not be available until 2014. i think that is a mistake and we should at least have had a progress report, to keep us informed of progress and the obstacles encountered, so that we can respond to them effectively and quickly. this report underscores this point. it also stressed that one of the key elements for the effective implementation of the directive was the proper training of lawyers. i think this is particularly relevant, and i am regularly campaigning for the training of gender lawyers, because they are the guardians of the effectiveness of this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague zita gurmai because the fight against gender inequalities in the workplace and outside it must be strengthened. the differences in treatment between men and women in access to certain goods or services must end, and member states must comply with european law as soon as possible. i also support the proposal to extend the scope of the current directive to fill a number of gaps and to better prevent discrimination in relation to pregnancy and maternity, in particular in relation to housing, loans and access to medical services.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague zita gurmai on the principle of equal treatment between women and men in the access to and supply of goods and services. the report was adopted by 488 votes in favour, 152 against and 35 abstentions. the objective of this report was to assess the impact and the degree of implementation of directive 2004/113/ec, to identify existing shortcomings and to propose solutions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs gurmai on the implementation of the directive on equal treatment for men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services. the report stresses the need for the commission to put an end as quickly as possible, by proposing new legislation, to the legal uncertainty created by the ecj's test-achats judgment on insurance services, which has the effect in particular of increasing insurance premiums for women. i also voted in favour of amendment no 1 because as a member of the lgbt group i want to see better consideration in eu legislation of gender identity discrimination as a ground for discrimination. i also voted in favour of paragraph 19 to include advertising and media which convey many gender stereotypes in the scope of the directive. finally, the fight against these stereotypes, which are ingrained from an early age, requires a great deal of awareness-raising in the educational world, which i think it is essential to support.
in writing. as early as 2004, the european union had promoted the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the provision of goods and services. yet, almost a decade later, no evaluation has been made to measure its effects. if we do not act quickly, the credibility of european legislation will be undermined, especially on a fundamental issue of human rights. in adopting this report, which i voted in favour of, my colleagues in the european parliament and i have therefore called for the rapid completion of this evaluation and for the strengthening of the rules on gender equality, particularly with regard to pregnant women.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the application of directive 2004/113/ec on equal treatment between men and women in the access to goods and services, following the controversy over the use of sex as a risk factor by insurance companies. discrimination on grounds of sex is contrary to the principle of equality as well as to european values and is incompatible with the eu charter of fundamental rights. it is essential that the european union provides legal protection against discrimination on grounds of sex, as against all forms of discrimination.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the state of play of gender equality in europe. the 2004 directive was a major step forward for equal treatment of men and women in access to goods and services. states had until 2007 to transpose it, and the commission was to report on its application by the end of 2012. however, there is still no report, due to a legal loophole in this directive allowing insurers to set differentiated rates for men and women, particularly for cars or health care. the court of justice has declared these provisions to be contrary to the principle of equality between men and women, requiring states to change their legislation before the end of 2012. these incidents show how long the struggle for women's rights is still going on, and the resolution adopted by parliament serves as a reminder.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the transposition and application of council directive 2004/113/ec implementing the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services. this report addresses gender equality and gender discrimination outside the world of work. when voting on this report, i supported paragraph 19 of the report which calls on the committee to include media and advertising content within the scope of the directive. it is necessary to combat the stereotype of the "woman-object" which is increasingly conveyed by many media and advertising.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report and welcome the decision of the committee on women's rights to ask the commission to prepare its evaluation report on the implementation of directive 2004/113/ec on gender equality in the access to and supply of goods and services without delay. despite some progress on gender equality, the march 2011 decision of the cjeu, the test-achats judgment, finding article 5 (2) of directive 2004/113/ec invalid, which allows for a gender differentiation in rates for certain insurance premiums and benefits, is evidence that inequalities in treatment persist. it is to be hoped that the fight against discrimination will take precedence over the rules of the market, which are focused on ever-increasing profits. the ecj decision will have consequences for the adaptation of both national legislation and insurance practices to eliminate discrimination on grounds of sex. i particularly welcome the rapporteur's recommendation to include media content and advertising within the scope of the directive, given that inequalities are firstly fuelled by the gender stereotypes very often carried by the media.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i opposed the adoption of the svensson report on promoting the development of countries through trade. of course, the trade we have with the developing countries can and should be a driving force for them. but i think that as fair a trade as possible is one of the major levers of development under certain conditions. the svensson report contains statements which are simply false and which have prevented me from supporting it. i cannot accept that support for european farmers is guaranteed and that at the same time it is thought that this support is jeopardizing the development of these countries. it's not in line with reality. this casts a dangerous suspicion on our farmers. the food security of the european union depends on the support it gives to its farmers. the food sovereignty that everyone wants for the developing countries must not come into conflict with our own food sovereignty. i regret that this was the case with the svensson report and i regret that we have seen a perfectly binary view of development.
in writing. i am convinced of the potential of the european union's trade policy in promoting and cohering policies for development. the instruments available must be focused on generating positive spill-over effects at local, regional and national levels; on accelerating the diversification of economies and on more modern and more profitable production. negotiations on future trade agreements should therefore take place in a clear and transparent development framework, with an emphasis on achievable targets, monitored and validated by key indicators. in the light of future cooperation, i support this report which stresses that the private sector must be included in this cooperation as an additional guarantee of the sustainable development of these companies.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of the report by my colleague alf svensson, which stresses the role played by the european union's trade policy in developing countries. the development of smes in these countries must be a priority. the eu must also ensure that good governance, which is essential for the development of a country, is ensured.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the eu's trade policy towards developing countries must serve to reinforce the results achieved by our policy. the eu's core values, as well as its treaty obligations, must guide its trade policy towards developing countries. to better serve development objectives, eu trade policy must focus on positive impacts on local, regional and national economies, as well as on promoting the diversification of developing countries' economies; it must also encourage more advanced and more profitable production. however, particular attention should be paid to possible imbalances in food sovereignty in both the eu and developing countries. that is the meaning of the amendments i tabled to this report.
in writing. i support the view expressed in this report that trade is an essential tool for development and that it should be used more directly for this purpose. i regret, however, that some of the passages in it may be harmful to our agriculture. i tabled amendments to restore the balance which i believe is necessary: the development of third countries is certainly an essential objective, which has positive consequences for our economies; but it is precisely in this spirit of complementarity of our interests, and not of sacrifice, that our ambitions must be achieved. i would like to stress that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens.
in writing. this parliament, which for decades, to make it more effective, has made the mordicus claim that globalisation and the liberalisation of international trade would bring peace and prosperity to the world, discovers some of its negative effects on developing countries: increased poverty, danger to local production, increased dependence on imports or exports of raw materials... to conclude what everyone except it already knew: the countries that have done so have developed by protecting their fragile nascent industries. it also expressed concern at the return of spectre from the mia, the multilateral investment agreement, through appeals to wto panels. if the agreement had been successful, it would have enabled investors to escape national legislation which might have been harmful to their private interests. today, multinational companies are trying to achieve this goal through case law. it's because the worm is in the wto's spoiled fruit. unfortunately, the report does not go so far as to call into question the very principle of globalisation as orchestrated by the marrakesh agreements. i couldn't vote for it.
in writing. this report contains good statements on investment policy and on the absence of automatic links between the effects of trade liberalisation and poverty eradication. however, it was considerably weakened in the plenary, almost emptied of its substance, by the conservatives with the support of the socialists and liberals. i abstained on this because the vote in plenary deleted several essential paragraphs. these included the export tax on raw materials (an important tool for developing countries to develop and diversify their economies) and the legally binding value of corporate social and environmental responsibility, which are essential to moving towards greater policy coherence for development.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague alf svensson, which was adopted in plenary. trade policy is one of the most important areas of action for the development of the countries of the south. in order to better serve development objectives, the report recommended a number of essential measures, such as promoting the diversification of the economies of developing countries and the need to provide targeted aid to promote and encourage the development of small and medium-sized enterprises in developing countries.
in writing. i opposed the adoption of this report. the trade we have with the developing countries can and must of course be a driving force for them, but it must be done under certain conditions. the svensson report contained false statements which prevented me from supporting it. i cannot accept the argument that support for european farmers is detrimental to the development of those countries. it is not in line with reality and it casts a dangerous suspicion on our farmers. the food sovereignty that everyone wants for these developing countries must not be in conflict with our own food sovereignty, which is heavily dependent on the aid that the european union provides to its farmers.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the question of promoting development through trade, as it highlights a number of elements which i consider particularly important. i am thinking, for example, of the efforts still needed to achieve the millennium development goals (mdgs). i am also thinking of the principle of policy coherence for development (pcd); the eu's external relations policy should be based on the principles of the european union's external relations policy, including its trade policies and its economic partnership agreements (epas) with the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries. it is also important to remember that economic trade with developing countries must not be at the expense of their development, local production and regional integration.
in writing. developed countries have a responsibility towards those which did not experience an industrial revolution in the late 18th - early 19th centuries and are thus experiencing less development. the union is clearly aware of this. it is therefore using its commercial policy to promote their development. no one will doubt that this instrument is a driver of growth and a means of reducing poverty. that is why i welcome this report. i think that we must, however, remain pragmatic on certain issues. the principle of reciprocity in access to public procurement, the taxation of raw materials and the limitation of exports of raw materials to our territories must not be subject to too many concessions. the european union must also defend its own interests.
in writing. trade and investment, while they can be relevant means of development, are only relevant if they are adapted to the partner country's level of development. the eu has understood this well, and since 1971 it has been proposing a system of generalised preferences for developing and least-developed countries. this tool, based on general rules of the world trade organisation and recently revised, is also used by the united states, but too few other trading powers, especially emerging ones, use it. the report, to which i have contributed in an opinion and which i supported in plenary, contains simple but effective trade measures to promote growth in low-income countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on 'promoting development through trade'. the instruments offered by trade policy can have a considerable impact on the development of poor countries. trade policy is one of the most important areas of action for policy coherence in the development of the european union. the agricultural or industrial actions of the northern countries must not be allowed to penalise the southern countries, while we are helping them through the policy of development and cooperation. it would be counterproductive. we must therefore formulate trade agreements that allow developing countries to participate properly in the international economy and to reap the benefits of globalisation. the millennium development goals can only be achieved if the european union provides itself with the means to do so. this requires a courageous trade policy and support for the development efforts of the countries of the south, so that they can do without our aid and provide for their own people.
in writing. i voted in favour of the parliament's report on promoting development through trade. this report is better than the title, because it is about fighting against anything that can distort international trade to the benefit of the richer countries and to the detriment of small producers in developing countries. the eu's policies in this area are a vast programme, since economic partnership agreements with developing countries are far from synonymous with development for them. on the contrary, they are often the main cause of the destruction of local production in developing countries and of their growing dependence on exports. the eu cannot continue to lock the countries and peoples of the south in a role of suppliers of raw materials, but must instead allow them to limit and regain control over their exports. that is the meaning of this report. one can be sceptical (the word is weak as to the reality of its implementation by the other authorities). but if we stick to the content, we can see it as a sign that the european parliament is moving in the right direction.
in writing. trade between the european union and developing countries must be a sustainable and functional engine for development and growth for the next decade. this own-initiative report has received wide support in the committee on international trade. several key variables seem to me to be essential in the negotiation and sustainability of these trade agreements, such as fostering greater regional integration and cooperation and improving local governance within the developing countries concerned. the conclusion of these agreements will thus send a positive signal to third countries involved in these exchanges, inviting them to continue their efforts with the european commission in defining a comprehensive and mutually beneficial agreement. more generally, i voted in favour of this report, which contains asymmetric clauses which leave the developing countries the necessary margin of freedom to gradually adapt their economic systems with a view to integrating them more fully into world trade.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague tokia saïfi on how the effectiveness of trade policy as a tool for development can be enhanced. to achieve this, it is necessary to take account of the particularities of developing countries, especially the least developed, to continue investments while ensuring good governance, to better coordinate the various european initiatives and to take account of the progress made in the various sectors (agriculture, industry and services).
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because we need to improve the synergies between trade and development policies. we must take into account the needs and capacities of recipient countries, and promote sustainable and inclusive development; create jobs and strengthen skills and human capital development while reducing social inequalities; it is also important to support the development of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, in order to encourage their participation in trade and investment at local, regional and cross-border levels. finally, we must step up our efforts to help improve budgetary governance, fight corruption, tax fraud and evasion, money laundering and tax havens.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this own-initiative report, which aims to put trade at the heart of growth. the desire to make trade policy more effective should also be emphasized. to achieve this, measures such as greater differentiation between developing countries, better complementarity between trade and development instruments, or, for example, increased public and private investment to stimulate growth in developing countries, are all ways which i support and which are highlighted in this text.
in writing. trade can be a real springboard for development, and europe can therefore provide valuable assistance to its partners by supporting them in developing their capacities. i therefore support the view expressed in this report that we should better coordinate our trade and development policies to achieve ambitious results. i support the measures proposed in this report because they strike a balance between supporting our partners and protecting european interests, particularly in the agricultural and industrial fields.
in writing. despite the budgetary crisis we are experiencing, it is necessary to continue contributing to the development of the world's poor countries. however, it is no longer appropriate to contribute to their development by simply providing direct financial aid. trade can now be a real instrument for development. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which incorporates the development dimension when concluding a trade agreement with a developing country.
in writing. i congratulate my colleague, mr tokia saifi, on the adoption of his report on trade and investment for development. it is clear that official development assistance cannot be the sole factor in the development of the least developed and developing countries. first of all, we must recognize that not all countries face the same constraints and obstacles to development. the differentiated approach needs to be strengthened. our trade policy can support the development of these countries, but they must also undertake the necessary reforms to improve investment conditions. this requires good governance and the implementation of social, environmental and labour standards and the respect of fundamental principles such as human rights. i believe above all that the trade and development link should not be a concept applicable only to trade relations between developing countries and the eu, but that it should also be promoted by other developed and emerging economies.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague, mr tokia saïfi, in the plenary session of 16 april. this very high quality own-initiative report was adopted by a large majority, with 521 votes in favour, 34 against and 71 abstentions. in this own-initiative report, tokia saïfi reviews the european commission's proposals to make trade-based growth a driver of sustainable development. the european commission recommends, in particular, that the differentiation between developing countries be strengthened, that efforts be concentrated on the poorest among them, that the complementarity between trade and development instruments be strengthened and, finally, that support for national reforms to strengthen good governance and the trading capacities of developing countries be increased.
in writing. i support this report because i believe it is essential to use trade as an instrument for development. trade measures are very useful tools to encourage the improvement of social, environmental and labour standards in emerging countries, not to mention respect for human rights. but the use of these measures must be adapted to the countries envisaged. we must therefore take account of the particularities and capabilities of each individual, for example by introducing asymmetric clauses in future agreements. at the same time, developing partner countries have a responsibility to provide the most favourable environment for the exploitation of the investments from which they will benefit. it should be borne in mind that the aim of these countries is to become sufficiently strong economically to eventually integrate into world trade.
in writing. we are preparing our position on the post-2015 millennium development goals. more than ever, we need to inspire solutions that have proven themselves on the ground! this is the direction i wanted to give my report, asking that the needs and solutions determined by the beneficiary countries themselves be taken into account. the ivory coast, for example, is a country which, in the eyes of all observers, has been able to catch up with its development lagging behind thanks to an innovative and systematic trade and investment policy. this is also the case for the financing of trade in development aid: in the context of the current economic and financial crisis, we must be pragmatic not only in the management of available funds, but also in the search for innovative financing solutions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague tokia saifi on 'trade and investment, growth drivers for developing countries'. trade policy is one of the most important areas of action for policy coherence in the development of the european union. the agricultural or industrial actions of the northern countries must not be allowed to penalise the southern countries, while we are helping them through the policy of development and cooperation. it would be counterproductive. we must therefore formulate trade agreements that allow developing countries to participate properly in the international economy and to reap the benefits of globalisation. the millennium development goals can only be achieved if the european union provides the means. this requires a courageous trade policy and support for the development efforts of the countries of the south, so that they can do without our aid and provide for their own people.
in writing. i abstained in the vote on this report on trade and investment as growth engines for developing countries adopted by the european parliament. this report contains some positive proposals. it stresses the need for decent wage levels in global production chains and the importance of preventing speculation on agricultural products. but, beyond this expressed desire to encourage development in the countries of the south, certain essential conditions are not met. unlike the svensson report, which was voted on the same day on the same subject, this report does not address the need for social responsibility clauses in trade agreements. some of the provisions, such as the gradual removal of restrictions on agricultural exports, are even worrying in view of the current situation. today, trade liberalization is not synonymous with development, but is instead an instrument of domination for the benefit of the richer countries. the two accounts can be said to be somewhat contradictory. once is not customary.

before the beginning of next year. a number of issues will determine whether it will be possible for these guidelines to enter into force on 1 january next year. if not, that will trigger a prolongation of the present guidelines during the first months of 2014. one of the issues involved – which you have mentioned – is the need to ensure consistency between the regional aid guidelines, regional policy and the new framework for the structural funds and cohesion funds. this does not mean that the map of the assisted regions and the criteria should be exactly the same, because the purpose of these guidelines – to create a framework to provide compatible aid to some investors in some regions – is not exactly the same as the objectives, the priorities and the instruments of the do so. you raised two or three points that i want to address in particular. first of all, population coverage. in the original draft we reduced this coverage. in the present guidelines the total population covered by these possibilities of compatible aid is 45%. in our initial proposal it was 42%. now in the present version of our draft it is again 45%. because of the need to take into account the particular situation of countries in very deep crisis – and here i am thinking in terms of greece or cyprus – it may be that the final coverage of population will be higher in the new guidelines than in the present ones. but i do not think this is a reason to be worried, mrs hübner. second, aid intensities. it is true that, with the exception of the poorest regions, in the case of other assisted regions we are proposing lower intensity. why? for two reasons. firstly because, taking into account the whole of the eu, their regional disparities have decreased. and this is a good result of previous policies and strategies on territorial cohesion, regional aid for investors and many other elements. so regional disparities overall are decreasing, and we need to take this into account. the second reason is, however, more important in my opinion. we have increased divergences in the budgetary and fiscal capacity of the member states and regions that need to give subsidies to investors. if we do not reduce aid intensities – if we maintain the same aid intensities that were decided before the crisis, when the fiscal capacity was more evenly distributed among member states – it is possible that, instead of helping to reduce regional diversities, we will create an instrument that can increase regional diversity, because only those who have a very strong budgetary situation will use in full the possibilities of giving compatible aid to regions. this has been analysed and discussed, and i think that the argument is quite a sound one. and i can add another. in our experience, part of the aid that was given under compatibility with the framework in the past did not have a real incentive effect. that aid did not trigger additionality in the investment efforts in regions that are below the eu average in per capita gdp but was money that was given to investors who in any case would have invested in the same place, with the same resources. so we need to take into account this point in particular, given the extremely difficult situation of quite a number of our member states in terms of budgetary capacity, not only today but in the coming years in which these guidelines will be in force. you mentioned – and this is my last comment – the mid-term review, and i fully agree with you. i cannot remember right now how this possibility of a mid-term review is worded in the present draft of the guidelines, but of course a mid-term review, in particular during the period 2014-2020, is absolutely warranted, given the consequences of the crisis in terms of the different evolution of gdp per capita between and within member states. thank you very much.

president-in-office of the council. − madam president, honourable members, the agreement of a cypriot macroeconomic adjustment programme has been the focus of much energy and attention over recent weeks. i feel it is important at the outset again to recall that i am here as a representative of the council, and i am happy to be here in that capacity to discuss this matter. however, the discussions surrounding cyprus were not conducted under the stewardship of the irish presidency but rather under the stewardship of the president of the eurogroup. so, as i do not speak for the eurogroup, i am clearly somewhat constrained in the contribution that i can make to this important debate. i think there is very little – if any – disagreement that the situation in cyprus is extremely regrettable, and the human consequences of it for the cypriot people are the most regrettable elements of all. it is important to emphasise – and for us to note, i think – that the situation in cyprus was, and is, exceptional. a combination of a number of factors, including the size of the financial sector, the nature of the risks assumed and other issues, including supervision issues, left the country particularly vulnerable to financial market turbulence. when two of cyprus’s largest banks ran into trouble, the cost of recapitalising them was such that cyprus was left with little alternative but to seek assistance from other euro area member states. to resolve an exceptional situation, country-specific measures for a macroeconomic adjustment programme were agreed by the troika and the cypriot authorities, and subsequently by the eurogroup. i do not intend to comment in depth on those measures, but elements of the programme include a restructuring of the banking sector, an audit of the anti-money-laundering framework, fiscal consolidation and economic restructuring. on the basis of the programme, the euro area agreed – in principle – to provide up to eur 10 billion in financial assistance to cyprus, subject to the imf’s contribution. the eurogroup has since been able to welcome a staff-level agreement between cyprus and the representatives of troika institutions on the policy conditionality underlying the macroeconomic adjustment programme. national procedures required for the approval of the european stability mechanism (esm) financial assistance can now be launched. i understand that what is now envisaged is that a final agreement by the esm board of governors should be reached by the end of april, and that the first esm disbursement is scheduled for mid-may. clearly, the road ahead for cyprus will be very challenging. but this should not prevent us from recognising that these measures, however difficult, grant real assistance to cyprus – assistance which is absolutely necessary, both to allow cyprus the chance to get its public finances and economy back on a sustainable path and to safeguard stability inside the monetary union. this is both in the cypriot and in the european interest. while the news in recent weeks may have been about cyprus, it is true to say that the wider difficulties we have faced in a number of euro area countries have taken place against a backdrop in which financial turmoil has exposed significant weaknesses in our monetary union. as the presidency, as you know, our focus has been in advancing the measures which are designed to redress those shortcomings. this effort goes to the heart of the union’s efforts to restore stability. above all, this has meant working on banking union, work in which we would want again to acknowledge the central role and constructive engagement of the european parliament. in adopting that focus, our presidency has followed the lines of the priorities outlined by the european council. banking union is important because it will reinforce confidence in europe’s banking system and its supervision. it will also help to break the link between sovereigns and banks and to foster the reintegration of financial markets. during the irish presidency, good progress has been made on the banking union dossiers. to date, the capital requirements directive (crd iv) proposal has been finalised and the agreement on the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) is currently being finalised. political agreement on the ssm was reached at the informal ecofin council in dublin last week, where ministers also reaffirmed their commitment to the urgent completion of all the agreed elements of banking union, and this will continue to be a major priority for us in the weeks and months ahead. the setting up of the supervisor will also pave the way for the european stability mechanism to take on the direct recapitalisation of banks. the remaining elements of the banking union package include the bank recovery and resolution (brr) proposal, consideration of which has been accelerated by the irish presidency to meet the june deadline which was set by the european council for its agreement with the european parliament. bank recovery and resolution will lay the foundation for a single resolution mechanism, a detailed proposal which we expect to see published by the commission very shortly.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, as president barroso is attending the funeral of baroness thatcher today, i am presenting the commission’s views in this important debate together with my colleagues joaquín almunia and michel barnier, with whom we have worked very closely as a team over the past years. we are about to finalise a support programme for cyprus. it will enable cyprus to avoid a disorderly default, with all its dramatic ramifications for the cypriot people. this marks the beginning of a joint effort to bring cyprus onto the path of sustainable growth and job creation. the process that led us to this agreement has been very difficult, and not without mistakes. the cypriot authorities, the member states and the european institutions had to find unique solutions to exceptional problems. they had to do so without previously tested instruments and, in the final stages of negotiations, under enormous time pressure. thus, there are at least two key lessons to be learned from this difficult process. first, there must be absolute clarity about secured deposits. in this respect, the eurogroup and cyprus took rapid corrective action and underlined that secured deposits are indeed secured in europe. second, the developments in cyprus demonstrate the reasons why a banking union is a necessary element of a true economic and monetary union. we need a well-functioning single supervisory mechanism with a single rulebook to prevent the emergence of an unsustainable banking sector, as happened in cyprus. and we must ensure that, even if reinforced supervision fails, we have a single resolution mechanism to provide the instruments for a timely and effective restructuring and resolution of problem banks. but those instruments are not yet in place, and in this process we had to work with the less adequate ones that we have at present. the problems of cyprus had built up over many years. at their heart was an oversized banking sector that thrived on attracting foreign deposits with very favourable conditions. these capital inflows also contributed to a property boom and the accumulation of external imbalances. in fact the depth of the banking problems stemmed from poor risk management practices. lacking adequate oversight, the two largest cypriot banks were allowed to build far too concentrated risk exposures. it was the problems in these banks which caused the troubles for sovereign debt and the economic decline of cyprus – not the other way round. in november 2011, the commission notified the cypriot authorities that a financial assistance programme would be unavoidable unless the persistent economic problems were immediately addressed. eventually, cyprus asked for financial assistance, but only in june 2012. after half a year of talks, a staff-level agreement on the necessary structural reforms and fiscal measures was reached. many of them, including anti-money laundering measures, were adopted by the cyprus parliament before the end of 2012. the commission’s aim during the whole process of agreeing a support programme for cyprus has been threefold: to help cyprus onto the path of sustainable growth, to preserve financial stability in cyprus and in the eurozone and to protect the integrity of the euro and the single market. the commission’s preferred scenario was a more gradual adjustment of the cypriot banking system and real economy, while ensuring debt sustainability. however, there was a very firm financial constraint. the euro area member states were ready to commit official support up to eur 10 billion, whereas the total financing needs had been estimated at eur 17 billion. this constraint severely limited the options available. as time was running out, the scenario of the more gradual economic adjustment was not on the cards any more, unfortunately. the state of the banks deteriorated rapidly. soon it became clear that the second biggest bank, laiki, had to be resolved immediately. the risk of a complete collapse of the entire banking system – and thus a sweeping loss of deposits and savings and a disorderly sovereign default – was indeed very real. that would have been a disaster for cyprus and for the cypriots. without a bank resolution law and without a programme in place, the cypriot banks remained closed and the bank holiday was extended. the cypriot authorities imposed capital controls to avoid the flight of deposits. the commission, as the guardian of the treaties, is closely monitoring the impact of capital controls in cyprus. the temporary restrictions were justified in the circumstances, but they are a very serious limitation on the free movement of capital. therefore, the commission will ensure that these measures last no longer than strictly necessary. the support programme will enable cyprus to restore the health of the economy and to create a more sustainable economic model. i agree with the minister of finance of cyprus, haris georgiades, who said yesterday that he wants to shun the blame game and focus on the future. he said as follows: ‘we are determined to adopt and implement all those reform measures which we should have adopted a long time ago, but we failed to do so’. we now have to concentrate all our efforts to facilitate the emergence of new sources of economic activity and to alleviate the social consequences of the economic shock. the commission decided in march to set up a support group for cyprus to assist with the implementation of the adjustment programme. we are now mobilising our resources to provide technical assistance. the support group will rely on expertise from across the commission services. the immediate priority is to identify the relevant resources available from the current structural funds. the commission stands by the cypriot people in these challenging times; we are committed to help cyprus to get through the tough times and overcome the current difficulties. i trust that we can count on the support of the european parliament in together mobilising the available resources for cyprus, as quickly and as effectively as possible. mr president, i am looking forward to a forward-looking and constructive dialogue on the subject.
on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, madam president-in-office of the council, mr president of the commission, mr commissioner, the situation in cyprus is catastrophic. cyprus is now on the verge of bankruptcy and the cypriot people are suffering. the european parliament has been able to reach agreement on the broad lines of an economic adjustment programme, as you have just said. it is not easy to implement. everyone must be aware that the consequences for the cypriot people will be significant. without going into all the causes of the situation in cyprus, i would like to emphasize two of them. firstly, the manifest lack of vigilance on the part of the european institutions. there has been no effective intervention to prevent or limit the foreseeable risks of an unbalanced economy through the growth of financial activity. this sector is clearly oversized €120 billion in assets in relation to the island's economy, since it represents seven times its gdp. nor was there any effective intervention to counteract the decisions of the then cypriot government, which ended up concealing reality and evading all control by seeking financial support in russia. however, the effect of these subsidies was to increase the risks beyond what was reasonable. secondly, the particularly risky behaviour of the cypriot banks, which have made serious mistakes. for example, they bought up hundreds of millions of dollars of greek debt at a time when all the holders were rushing to sell it. at this point, we must, without complacency, learn from this crisis. in the absence of more solidarity and institutionalised transfer, the european union cannot tolerate economic specialisation which seriously jeopardises the situation of the country concerned. secondly, the european union must act in a transparent manner, but also with the will to explain and make these decisions understood by all citizens. the collective behaviour of the finance ministers has been a catastrophic fiasco. i'm not questioning the content, but the method of communication. the citizens perceived the foreground as a hold-up that could strike them all across europe. so how do you get credibility? the announcement by the eurogroup of the cypriot rescue plan was made under very bad conditions, which the emergency does not excuse. this has contributed to discrediting europe, european economic policy and the system of banking crisis resolution advocated by commissioner barnier. the european union can no longer tolerate a clear disproportion between the weight of one country and the predominance of a quasi-unique economic sector. that's a considerable risk factor. the cyprus crisis, after others, shows us that an economy with a hypertrophied banking sector is not sustainable in the long term. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the member states do not specialise in a single sector of activity, unless there is a transfer, as happens in a national state. the european union's assistance plan requires cyprus to reduce its over-stretched banking sector. that's a good thing. structural reforms are also needed to build a strong foundation for the economy and return to sustainable growth in the long term. the banking union and the single supervisory mechanism must also be set up as soon as possible. the situation in cyprus shows that direct supervision of euro area banks by the european union is a key element in avoiding crises similar to the one in cyprus. the union must also deal with the difficult question of tax regulations which deviate from a reasonable average and create tax havens. tax harmonization is necessary. this crisis also shows us that we need to move faster towards more europe. more europe means a more profound europe, more united, but also better controlled. the necessary tools have been developed with great effort, as you mentioned, commissioner rehn, and they must now be used quickly and in a spirit of good cooperation between the states. our duty today is first of all to restore the confidence of the cypriot people through a europe of solidarity. we must support the cypriot people and in this respect we trust the new government of nikos anastasiades to put in place the necessary measures for recovery, with sound public finances and financial stability. to this end, the rules for the use of european funds must be relaxed so that these funds are quickly effective. and of course, mr vice-president, we share the commission's desire to use all possible means to find, within the current legal framework, the measures and resources that can be granted to cyprus, particularly in the budget under consideration.

in writing. since the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament's budgetary powers have been strengthened. in procedural terms, discharge represents parliament's final check on the proper implementation of the budget. this right of scrutiny enables parliament to ensure that public money is being managed properly. in this case, the european court of auditors publishes an annual report examining the eu's finances. on the basis of this report, the european parliament shall decide whether or not to grant discharge for a given year. the geier report, which i have approved, concerns the commission's discharge for 2011.

in writing. the budget of the european parliament is prepared in accordance with the rules of the bureau of the european parliament and of the committee on budgets. it will be integrated into the commission's 2014 budget proposal. an agreement was reached at a conciliation meeting between the european parliament's bureau and the committee on budgets. the commission is proposing to set up a two-stage budgetary procedure: first an estimate in the spring and then a vote on structural reforms and budget cuts in the autumn. the preliminary draft estimates for the 2014 financial year of the parliament amount to eur 1 808 144 206. this budget is up by 3.29% compared to 2013, with a special budget allocated in the run-up to the 2014 european elections. the budget estimate has already been reduced by €5 million. i voted in favour of this report, whose agreement in the conciliation procedure was supported by all the political groups in the european parliament.
in writing. i voted in favour of the estimates of the 2014 budget of the parliament. the parliament, like the other institutions, is seeing its real budget fall, partly because of cuts and partly because 2014 will be an election year, which will inevitably lead to a number of unusual expenditures. we have also succeeded in keeping the amendment on the single seat out of this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the hohlmeier report, which sets out the figures for parliament's budget for 2014. this draft budget is very realistic, and i welcome this: it includes a number of cuts, despite the accession of croatia, and therefore the welcome of croatian meps, and the imminence of the european elections, which will entail unusual expenditure.
