in writing. this report welcomes the 56% reduction in translation costs in the european parliament. it therefore ignores the need for members to work in proper conditions. i vote against it.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation establishing a financial assistance mechanism for member states whose currency is not the euro follows the adoption of the '6 pack' and '2 pack' of economic regulation in the european union. the scope of the regulation, however, focuses only on member states outside the euro area. the legislation on this subject dates from 2002, so it was necessary to update it to bring it into line with the applicable legislation of the euro area countries. the final aim is to provide financial assistance to banks in countries with balance of payments difficulties. i voted in favour of the interim report which asks the commission to take a position, in particular on the question of the circumstances in which banks in non-euro area countries could be directly recapitalised by european funding such as the european financial stability facility. the report advocates indirect recapitalisation in the form of a bank recapitalisation loan, as this would avoid exposing the european budget directly to the risks facing banks.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report updating the financial assistance measures for countries not using the euro. to deal with the financial crisis, the european union has created several mechanisms (such as the european stability mechanism) as well as strict budgetary control policies, which consequently impact countries outside the euro area. it was therefore necessary to adopt a new version of the financial assistance mechanism for non-euro area countries, to ensure a certain degree of coherence between countries using the euro and those not using it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by danuta hübner on the financial assistance mechanism for member states whose currency is not the euro. it was absolutely necessary to revise the legislation on this matter, which dates back to 2002, in order to take account of developments within the euro area, in particular since the beginning of the crisis, the creation of the european stability mechanism, and the two-pack and six-pack legislation. a financial assistance facility has been set up to provide loans or credit lines to non-euro area countries in difficulty. for the sake of consistency, a number of points from the two-pack have logically been added. this is a remarkable step towards greater solidarity within the european union, which i very much welcome.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which establishes financial assistance for the eu member states outside the euro area. it is a means of strengthening economic cooperation between the member states of the european union. solidarity between the peoples of europe is essential for economic and financial stability within the union, but above all it seems to be the only solution for all european countries to emerge from the crisis.
in writing. i have agreed with the european parliament as a whole to amend the existing legislation dating from 2002 on the financial assistance mechanism for non-euro area member states. this amendment is consistent with the logic of coherence and cohesion, since it is mainly a matter of adapting legislation to the new realities, taking into account the tools put in place in recent years, the european stability mechanism (esm) but also the two-pack and six-pack regulations that apply to the euro area countries.
in writing. i voted against the financial assistance mechanism for member states whose currency is not the euro. this bank recapitalisation instrument is similar to the european stability mechanism (esm). as in its predecessor, it provides for the introduction of 'enhanced surveillance' of national budgets under the control of the commission, if necessary, but also of the ecb and the imf. after the social catastrophes caused by these blind austerity measures, particularly in greece and more recently in cyprus, we have seen how budgetary sovereignty and democracy have been confiscated by the troika, to impose ultra-liberal policies on the people in the name of budgetary austerity. the text proposes to bring the same "solutions" to countries outside the euro area. under the guise of solidarity, the golden rule is once again being imposed. repeating and reaffirming these old recipes, which are dangerous for the population and especially the poorest, will not allow the member states of the european union to get out of the crisis, but on the contrary will contribute to deepening it. i therefore opposed this new financial assistance mechanism.
in writing. i strongly support this report which supports the policy decisions taken by the ecb, in particular with regard to its monetary policy and its own initiatives. the ecb's annual report was prepared in a difficult economic environment, with a deepening sovereign debt crisis in most member states threatening to relaunch the banking crisis. to counter the effects of the crisis, the ecb used new instruments to break the link between the two types of crisis and set historically low interest rates. the ecb should avoid giving the impression that it is directly financing the public debt. the report, however, calls on the ecb to remain cautious in order to face the future with confidence.
in writing. i voted in favour of the ecb's 2011 annual report, which was originally very critical of the institution, but we have managed to amend it sufficiently to make it acceptable. we have called on the ecb to do more to ensure that its low-interest loans reach the real economy. we also want it to become more transparent and accountable, in line with its growing role in the eurozone crisis. with such expanded responsibilities and powers, the ecb will be better able to promote growth and employment.
in writing. the explanatory memorandum to ms matias' report is more informative than the body of the report itself and significantly more negative about mr draghi's action. i regret that in the text we adopted (but which i did not vote for, for this reason in particular) there is no mention of the role of the ecb, no criticism of the way in which it intervenes or goes beyond its mandate, no denunciation of the fact that its interventions have more often been part of the problem than part of the solution in crisis situations, and no expression of doubt as to the need for the bank's independence. this leads mrs matias to a clear conclusion, even if it is unthinkable for her to call into question the now sacrosanct 'euro': at a minimum, the bank's statutes must be amended, its objectives redefined, its decisions subject to political imperatives and closely controlled. it's a beginning of awareness. it is not in the text that was voted, which is ultimately just a compliment to the former goldman sachs executive. how many more countries must he ruin, how many more unemployed must he make before this parliament, which boasts of democratic control, really taps him on the fingers?
in writing. in the crisis the european union is going through, if there is one institution that has particularly widened its scope of action, it is the european central bank. but if it has done much in the storm we are facing, it must do more for growth and jobs in europe. we have repeated this in our positions. there will be no lasting improvement in europe unless we provide clear and massive support for the real economy. that is the message i wanted to convey by voting for this resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which clearly calls for more transparency from the european central bank (ecb) and points to the lack of democratic accountability of this institution which plays a significant role in the wake of the eurozone crisis. as the driver of monetary policy, the ecb must move away from austerity to get out of the crisis and move more towards boosting growth and jobs. in this respect, it is essential that the ecb ensures that low-interest loan guarantees to banks genuinely feed the real economy and support european smes more directly.
in writing. in this report, which assesses the activities of the european central bank, parliament expressed the wish that the ecb should do more to promote growth and employment rather than just price stability. to this end, my colleagues and i call in particular on the ecb to take measures to guarantee low-interest loans to the real economy and to take an active part in the drafting of a future banking union. although the ecb cannot of course solve the crisis on its own and it is essential that the member states clean up their public finances, this text is good on the whole. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. this parliament motion for a resolution concerns the 2011 annual report of the european central bank (ecb), a report which describes the changes in policies and strategies made by the ecb in response to the crisis. i voted against this report because i think it is grossly inadequate. it does not question the draconian and counterproductive measures and the bad bailout plans decided by the ecb. i believe that the european parliament, as the only european institution elected by the citizens of europe, must send a clear message on this matter. the lack of transparency with which the troika and the ecb are acting is simply intolerable. by imposing austerity policies on the member states, the ecb not only offers no viable prospect of a way out of the crisis for the european people, but it also goes far beyond its mandate. i am therefore advocating an ecb which serves the real economy and the citizens, not speculative and financial interests, an ecb which is transparent and democratic.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report assessing the activities of the european central bank for 2011. some of the observations made in this report deserve to be heard. the current crisis only confirms that it is high time to review the economic governance of the euro area: the question of a budget specific to the states sharing the same currency has merit to be asked, as well as the question of the control of the troika (eu, imf, ecb) and the drastic requirements imposed for the granting of aid to states in difficulty. the absence of conditions attached to loans to banks and the exceptional profits made by the ecb seem to me completely unacceptable. finance is an instrument for the economy and not the other way around: the ecb must not be able to make a profit, and guarantees on the use of funds by banks must be required. the report rightly stresses the need for transparency in the ecb. the effects of its decisions are disastrous for employment, purchasing power and public service. europeans deserve a democratic debate; they deserve to be heard. it's inconceivable that we're not more informed.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report which stresses the need to amend the vat directive to clearly define the different types of 'vat vouchers', with a view to harmonising their vat treatment. vat vouchers are instruments which entitle the holder to receive goods or services, or a rebate or discount in respect of the supply of goods or services. the common rules on vat are outdated, adopted in 1977, and in particular the use of vouchers which pose additional difficulties for businesses, which were not envisaged at the time. the absence of common rules has led member states to adopt uncoordinated solutions, leading to inconsistencies in the taxation of transactions: problems of double taxation or non-taxation, tax evasion, distortions of competition, obstacles to business innovation. the proposal is designed to cover the tax consequences of the various types of vouchers at the time of their issue, distribution or exchange.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to define clearly the different types of vouchers and to harmonise their vat treatment. the 'vouchers' entitle the holder to a rebate in respect of the supply of goods or services. at present, the absence of common rules has led to uncoordinated action within the eu and inconsistencies in the taxation of transactions. while parliament adopted several texts during this plenary session which go in the direction of a 'european banking union', supporting this text ensures the consistency of our political line.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, and i fully share its premise: as vouchers are increasingly being used by community enterprises, which was not the case at the time of the first vat directives, it was necessary to establish common rules for the vat treatment of vouchers. otherwise, the door would remain open to distortions of competition, non-taxation or double taxation and the risk of tax evasion. i therefore consider that the broad consensus which has surrounded the adoption of this technical report constitutes a real step forward in the completion of the single market.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which is a further step towards the completion of the european single market. in view of the massive use of vouchers by businesses, each member state of the union currently has its own measures. the european union is thus faced with a mosaic of legislation. it seems essential to harmonize the vat rules on vouchers in order to establish a coherent economic and monetary policy for all the member states. the new measure will also make it possible to combat tax evasion and tax fraud more actively and effectively within the european union.
in writing. the increase in the use of vouchers has introduced difficulties not foreseen by the common vat rules. this legal vacuum has therefore led member states to develop their own solutions, resulting in inconsistencies and problems of taxation, tax evasion and obstacles to business innovation. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal, which amends the vat directive to define clearly the different types of vouchers and to harmonise their treatment when they are issued, distributed or exchanged, whether in a single member state or in a transaction involving several.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the common system of value added tax as regards the treatment of vouchers because the common rules on vat date from 1977 and need to be updated. this is the case with "bonds", which are instruments that give the holder the right to receive goods or services. the absence of common rules has led member states to adopt uncoordinated solutions. we are seeing inconsistencies that need to be addressed and double taxation, tax evasion and distortion of competition avoided.

in writing. the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance, adopted on 23 november 2007, aims to ensure the effectiveness of the international recovery of child support for these key family members. the convention has given priority to the protection of children, since the vast majority of maintenance claims directly concern them. this convention is a tool for all citizens, as it provides a mechanism by which child support obligations can be claimed and guaranteed when the person liable is resident in a third country. the european parliament has already signed that convention on behalf of the european union since 6 april 2011. however, for the convention to be applicable in the union, the deposit of the instrument of approval is necessary and must be accompanied by information on the national central authorities and any reservations that may apply to certain articles of the convention. i strongly support this report which stresses the need for swift approval of the amendments in order to ensure rapid and effective implementation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the ratification by the european union of the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance. the issue of transnational divorces is a subject on which i am strongly involved, and any initiative to facilitate legal and administrative procedures must be taken. the aim of the new legislation is to end the impossibility of claiming maintenance outside the eu in the event of non-payment and to introduce better coordination between central authorities on maintenance and the recognition of maintenance decisions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which provides real legal certainty for the parties concerned by maintenance obligations by harmonising the conditions for international maintenance recovery. until now, maintenance obligations have been governed by the law of the state of the creditor's habitual residence. now a person in need will be able to receive financial assistance from a close family member even if the latter is resident in a third country. it is a real protection that is being provided here to the beneficiaries of these food aid and more particularly to the children.
in writing. the ratification of the hague convention of 23 november 2007 on the international recovery of alimony for children and other family members is particularly important. it obliges parents who are able to do so to pay child support payments due to their children whether they reside in the same state as them or not. this convention recognizes the right of children to a dignified life and places it above parental evasions. i vote for it.
in writing. parental divorce is always a heartbreaking experience for children. the hague convention, which deals with the international recovery of maintenance for children and other family members, avoids adding to this separation, often experienced as a trauma, the material inconvenience caused by the absence of payment of maintenance. i believe that no parent should be able to evade his obligations simply because he resides in a third country. as a father of two children myself, i am particularly concerned about these issues. i therefore welcome the proposal for a council decision which will allow the deposit of the instrument of approval of the convention and its entry into force as soon as possible.
for the greens/efa group madam president, it is true that we do not often have the opportunity in this parliament to report at such an exceptional political moment as that which turkey and the region are going through, on the one hand, and relations between the european union and turkey, on the other. i think we should really congratulate ria oomen-ruijten, who has succeeded in making this report a report of a political partner, without paternalistic overtones, while being able to address situations and issues which are of great political sensitivity, such as the question of minority rights, freedom of expression - we have just spoken about this - the situation of women or environmental issues. i therefore believe that this report is very useful in what i would call an exceptional situation. in what way? because in diplomatic relations as well as in political changes, important things happen. the political change in france has already had its first effects: the lifting of a veto on chapter 22, which will itself have effects in the context of the peace talks, which have been bravely and even admirably launched by the turkish government with its kurdish political partners. i think that's very important. i regret that there are still more than 40 of us who would delete our message at the opening of chapters 23 and 24. the european parliament has already expressed its support for the democratic reforms in turkey, but it must also support the powerful levers of negotiation around these two chapters, which concern precisely the question of fundamental rights, justice, freedoms and the judiciary. so this amendment is really quite deplorable in our institution. as i said, something is happening in turkey today, something we have not yet seen in its full extent, namely this direct negotiation between someone who is in prison - mr öcalan - and mr erdovan, a negotiation which is very widely supported by the population, by civil society. this is a very important point, and it is also closely linked to the debate on the new constitution, since the question of defining a new citizenship, the question of the possibility of being educated in one's mother tongue, the question of decentralisation and democratisation in turkey are all linked to the political solution of the kurdish question and to the progress of this peace process. i think that the call, the strength and the support of all the european institutions for this process is absolutely essential today. the european union has much to offer in this area, both its experience in reconciliation and peace and its capacity to create political compromise, political dialogue and respect in political debate, which is still sorely lacking in the turkish political space. (the speaker agrees to answer a question on the 'blue card' (rule 149 (8) of the rules of procedure))

in writing. today, each member state has its own method of calculating and collecting demographic data, which it communicates to the european commission. the stakes are high: these statistics are used in defining european policies, in accessing certain european funding, or in calculating the number of votes in the council. it therefore seems crucial to increase european harmonisation in this area. that is the meaning of this report, and i support it. the new rules that member states should comply with (negotiations with the council will now begin) include the obligation for member states to provide the european commission with data on the 'usually resident population' - that is, people who have been living in a member state of residence for at least one year or who arrive in a member state with the intention of staying for at least one year. the aim is to ensure that each resident is considered only once.
in writing. the measures put in place by the european commission are aimed at strengthening the conditions for the dismantling of decommissioned ships by using eu-listed facilities. the proposal for a regulation applies to ships flying the european flag but also to ships flying other flags that regularly call in the eu. the main objective, and i believe it is paramount, is to reduce the harmful effects of shipwrecks which are not environmentally friendly. on the other hand, the financial means employed place too heavy a burden on the companies. i therefore voted in favour of the text, but i rejected the article on the financial charge. the project created a recycling fund on the basis of the polluter-pays principle, in which a fee would be paid by shipowners whose ships call at european ports. it should be noted that a system of penalties is also in place: landlords who resort to negligent demolitions will thus be obliged to pay penalties. a new financial incentive proposal is therefore expected from the european commission, with a view to resolving the issue of the recycling fund.
in writing. almost all (90% in 2009) eu shipowners circumvent the general ban on the transfer of hazardous waste to non-oecd countries and dismantle their ships in, for example, india or bangladesh. through the ship recycling regulation, which i voted for, the eu intends to establish a global list of recycling facilities meeting minimum health and environmental standards in order to avoid dismantling having dramatic consequences for the environment and workers in the major recycling countries (india, pakistan, bangladesh). this regulation is a step forward, but i regret that parliament has refused (by 7 votes to one) to create a financial mechanism which would have enabled the polluter-pays principle to be applied by creating a recycling fund fund funded by the shipowners themselves and used to support the installations on the list (thus fighting social and environmental dumping). without this mechanism, there is a risk that ship owners will continue to evade their obligations simply by changing flags and selling their wrecks to the highest bidder. the revision clause adopted on this text will hopefully enable us to move this legislation forward, which, while commendable, is still insufficient to achieve its objective.

in writing. the negotiation process with turkey, which began in 2005, is a long-term venture. it is undeniable that turkey has carried out reforms necessary for its modernisation and the improvement of its democratic system. in this context, a programme for the development of relations was launched in 2012, but it does not constitute enhanced cooperation. turkey is a major economic player in the european union with bilateral trade amounting to almost €120 billion in 2011. however, accession to the european union remains conditional on compliance with the copenhagen criteria, which are still to be met by turkey. i noted the lack of real progress in the ratification of the ankara protocol and the recurring difficulties in its relations with cyprus. i therefore voted against the opening of negotiations on new chapters, such as fundamental rights, justice and home affairs.

in writing. i voted against this report because i question the progress made by turkey towards the rule of law. the final resolution does not mention the serious concerns about the independence of the turkish judiciary. it is worrying to note the length of time that activists, lawyers, journalists and members of the opposition parties elected to the grand national assembly of turkey have been held in pre-trial detention. a truly democratic society requires real freedom of expression, including the right to dissent. finally, i would like to reiterate my opposition to turkey's accession to the european union. that is why i voted against the final report and against the opening of the negotiating chapter between the european union and turkey on the judiciary and fundamental rights.
in writing. i wish to dissociate myself from the position taken by the european parliament on the accession negotiations with turkey. the decision to allow the opening of five new chapters of negotiations seems to me premature at this stage. the political conditions are not now in place for a new stage in the accession procedure. much remains to be done in terms of political freedoms, the recognition of minority rights, respect for freedom of expression and the media, and the independence of the judiciary. the dispute between turkey and greece is still unresolved, and i regret the attitude of turkey during the cypriot eu presidency in 2012. by taking this position we are sending a political signal to public opinion which will not be received with kindness. we know that the question of turkish integration and enlargement is a problem for our citizens who are facing a serious crisis that affects their immediate reality. by allowing new chapters to be opened, we are telling our citizens that their concerns are not being heard. i'm sorry about that.
in writing. i refused to comment on the follow-up report on the negotiations for turkey's accession to the european union in order to express, like most of my french colleagues in the epp, my opposition to the opening of new negotiating chapters at a time when the political situation in turkey calls for the utmost vigilance in the defence of human rights, women's rights and freedom of expression.
in writing. parliament, by calling for the opening of accession negotiations on new chapters, is moving slowly but surely towards turkey's future membership of the european union. all this angelicism and political correctness is dismaying me. i say it today and i will say it again as often as necessary: turkey has no vocation to be part of the union! apart from the common sense observation that turkey is not geographically located in europe, we must be pragmatic. the union of 27, and soon 28, is already facing enormous difficulties at the moment. is it reasonable, then, to keep on widening the gap? who else is with a country whose demographic weight would completely undermine france's influence in the decision-making process? with a country in open conflict with two of our member states? with a country that a few months ago, jailed a french student, whose only fault was her political views? let's open our eyes! there is still time to backtrack and stop this accession process, as nicolas sarkozy courageously did during his five-year term.
in writing. as every year, parliament takes a position on what is commonly called turkey's progress in its application for eu membership. parliament expresses its unequivocal condemnation of the repressive practices which are common in turkey: preventive detention of activists, lawyers, journalists and political opponents, particularly kurds. however, and to top it off, this report is below the one that the commission also published at the end of 2012. the report also ignores the question of the occupation of part of cyprus and even proposes to grant observer status to the inhabitants of the occupied part of the island, in a way anticipating the recognition of the partition. in addition, visa facilitation between the european union and turkey is conditional on the signing of an agreement on the readmission of migrants, the catastrophic human consequences of which are well known. the report also calls on the eu member states to strengthen cooperation with turkey in the fight against terrorism. and we know what that means for political opponents, especially kurds. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on montenegro. i welcome the remarkable progress made by this official candidate country to the eu, which is firmly on the path to membership. i believe that the accession process should remain the driving force behind the continuation of the reforms launched in the country. in this context, civil society has a fundamental role to play. i regret, however, the difficulties the government is facing in fighting organised crime and corruption.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the situation in montenegro. while we welcomed the solid progress made towards montenegro's eu accession, there is still a long way to go to guarantee press freedom, women's rights and gender equality. this report is a signal of encouragement to montenegro, which i have chosen to support.
in writing. the report provides lessons for montenegro on its unemployment rate and on the fight against corruption. i would point out to the authors that montenegro could legitimately object to them that the eu member states are far from being blameless in this matter. it also welcomed the liberalization measures implemented in the country. worse, it encourages the trampling of workers' rights and the implementation of austerity plans to curb the rise of public debt. i am voting against this text.
in writing. the european union opened accession negotiations with montenegro on 29 june 2012. since then, the country has made significant progress in satisfying some of the political criteria: electoral reform has been carried out, elections have been held successfully and, in parallel, regional cooperation has been established. it is necessary for montenegro to continue these efforts and to place greater emphasis on the rule of law by implementing irreversible reforms to combat organised crime and corruption. progress is also expected in other areas such as gender equality, dialogue with civil society and the fight against the informal economy. i voted in favour of this resolution in view of the progress made by montenegro and its desire to deepen its rapprochement with the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft resolution on serbia. with its status as a candidate country for the european union granted in 2012, serbia confirmed its commitments to the union. serbia is a crucial player for the union as it lies at the heart of the balkans and plays a significant regional role. the new status also confirms serbia's efforts to normalize relations with kosovo, which are necessary for the stabilisation of the region.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the situation in serbia. accession negotiations with serbia are expected to begin by june 2013, subject to the government's reforms in the areas of justice, the fight against corruption, freedom of the press and the protection of all minorities. moreover, i supported the new name of macedonia as arym, since france did not recognize the name "macedonia".
in writing. the report argues that accession negotiations with serbia can only be opened once the country has become a fully market economy. he denounces the desire of serbia to "partition kosovo" even though kosovo remains in the eyes of many states, including several eu member states, a serbian province and does not have the status of a state! the text goes so far as to state that "the idea of partitioning kosovo or any other country in the western balkans is contrary to the spirit of european integration". the declaration of independence of kosovo is in fact an idea of partition from serbia. the eu does not recognise kosovo as a state, with five member states opposing it! i am voting against this text and denouncing the blackmail of the european commission against serbia in the negotiations for its accession to the eu in order to obtain recognition of the state of kosovo.
in writing. since serbia was granted candidate status, it has made significant efforts to meet european criteria. on the political front, the last elections were well-run and an effective anti-corruption policy was implemented. the commission has also taken note of the fact that the council of ministers has adopted a decision on the establishment of a european central bank. as regards relations between serbia and its neighbours, it should be noted that considerable work has been done in the area of reconciliation. the country has worked to develop a stable dialogue with bosnia and herzegovina, montenegro, macedonia and croatia. in parallel, and with the support of the european union, serbia is continuing its dialogue with kosovo in order to maintain good, lasting and visible relations. i voted in favour of this resolution in order to support serbia in its political, economic and social progress and to enable it to meet the criteria for membership of the european union as best it can.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft resolution on kosovo. kosovo's independence is widely recognised in the european union and internationally. the draft resolution stresses that all eu member states are in favour of kosovo's prospect of membership of the european union. in this medium-term perspective, the normalisation of relations and the resumption of dialogue between serbia and kosovo seem to me to be crucial. this is essential for the stabilization of the region.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the situation in kosovo. relations between serbia and kosovo are developing in a positive way and we in the european parliament have decided to encourage this new trend. i am in favour of kosovo being recognised as a country in its own right, which could then start negotiations for membership of international organisations and, in the near future, of the european union.
in writing. the european union already has economic and cultural relations with kosovo and is interested in upgrading its status as a potential candidate country. despite the complex situation, progress in the negotiations on the association agreement with the union requires that kosovo resolves its problems of corruption and organised crime, improves the situation of refugees and internally displaced persons and strengthens the protection of witnesses. at international level, the union encourages the deepening of the belgrade-pristina dialogue and supports the normalisation of relations with serbia in the long term. i voted in favour of this resolution in order to support the european union and kosovo in their negotiations and to encourage further political, economic and social progress.
in writing. as a member of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, which is a key instrument for the future governance of the euro area. the scoreboard for the macroeconomic imbalance procedure is a policy tool that was introduced with the 'six-pack' as part of the reform of banking regulation at european level. this instrument is an essential basis for economic governance in the euro area, as it directly addresses macroeconomic imbalances that may have an impact on other member states.

weaknesses, for example the 10% target in the transport sector with the weaknesses of sustainability, the commission's supplementary proposal which is currently before parliament to curb the eyelook factor and to stimulate research is a correction of our otherwise pioneering european energy policy. if you want to achieve only 10% in the transport sector, but you want to achieve 20% overall, there is actually a third factor, a third figure, that comes into play. in addition to transport, we are also concerned with heat and electricity. if you want to achieve 10% in transport but 20% in everything, you need 30% or more in heat and electricity. heat is first and foremost a regional issue. it is our job to advise and control. heating in buildings and in industry is a regional problem, but electricity is increasingly becoming a national, continental, pan-european dimension. i therefore believe that the subject of renewable energy sources converted into electricity is rightly given special importance in this report. we believe that the findings of the last few years should be seen above all as a weak point: retrospective intervention. we believe that some member states have provided support partly from public budgets. there has been over-subsidization, there have been budgetary problems, and then there have been retrospective cuts or retrospective cancellations of commitments. it is true that trust is destroyed when the investor has no certainty of planning for the promised number of years of an investment. we therefore propose a general approach to the future development: any change can be discussed, but retroactive deterioration, the retroactive withdrawal of commitments by reason or by amount, destroys confidence far beyond the member state concerned. we believe that the european commission's green paper has asked the important questions. we are currently in consultation. and the commission will be consulting before the end of the year and deciding whether we make a new proposal for the period after 2020. the 20-20-20 criteria will be in force for another seven years. but for investors, whether in renewables or infrastructure and storage, 2020 was yesterday and 2030 is tomorrow. we must therefore decide at once - parliament, council, commission - on the objectives we wish to set for the next decade: reduction of co2 emissions, efficiency and renewable energy. we as the commission have not yet reached a final opinion. we respect the consultation, but it is clear that a further co2 reduction target seems essential, together with a wise further development of our ets system. secondly, if you want to be completely technology neutral, you don't need another goal. i believe, however, that the success story of european renewable energy provides good arguments for formulating another renewable target - perhaps not in the transport sector, as long as we are only able to produce the first generation of biofuels, perhaps only in the electricity and heat sectors. the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. clearly, the further development of renewable energy sources for electricity now that renewables are maturing, with a 20, 25, 30% share of the annual electricity conversion mix, requires firstly a stronger link to transport infrastructure, the development of new pan-european networks, secondly an intelligent infrastructure smart quits and smart metering , thirdly a stronger involvement of the consumer, so that he can adapt his consumption behaviour to electricity more closely to supply and demand and thus contribute to the stabilisation of the network and to increased storage capacities. this means that it is now, in fact, a much more delicate event, but one which must be held in a more european manner. i believe that this is why the right way forward beyond 2020 must be to move from purely national support to european coordinated or even harmonised support in the support systems. and then it's about doing it cost-effectively, which means, by smart development, helping to keep electricity affordable and therefore not causing social disruption and keeping electricity affordable for industrial jobs and not having to relocate to other parts of the world. in sum, your report and decision tomorrow or the day after tomorrow, our green paper and our communications will all be mr president, in 2010 the european union adopted an ambitious text to regulate audiovisual media activity. apparently, it was a success. it called for better accessibility of european works, greater protection for minors, the promotion of cultural diversity and a limit on inappropriate advertising. i would draw your attention to paragraph 13 of mr borys' report, in which he explicitly calls for media and audiovisual services to be excluded from any trade agreement. on thursday we will vote on the mandate for the free trade agreement with the united states. parliament must be consistent and also ask for the explicit exclusion of audiovisual services from the mandate of this negotiation. an agreement which would include these services would jeopardise the future improvement of the directive under discussion today. if we accept the liberalization of this sector, we are threatening cultural diversity, one of the founding principles of the european construction. let us vote on the question of the united states, keeping in mind the defence of european culture and audiovisual, as stated in the borys report.
in writing. the latest audiovisual media services directive aimed to better reconcile technological developments with the democratic principles of equal access, fair remuneration of authors and protection of freedom of expression, cultural diversity and privacy. the report on the implementation of the directive shows that it has helped to strengthen culture in the audiovisual sector, to protect vulnerable audiences and to improve accessibility for the greatest number of people. other findings, however, call for corrections. firstly, it is necessary to harmonise the application of the rules in the member states, in particular for 'hidden' advertising (in films, programmes, etc.), for mechanisms of media concentration and for accessibility. secondly, self-regulation must give way to coercion, particularly in the area of the protection of minors and alcohol and tobacco advertising. beyond its economic weight, european audiovisual is a strategic sector for our culture but also for the world's cultural diversity. its defence is based on support for european programme quotas and the exclusion of audiovisual media services from trade agreements to guarantee cultural exceptionalism.

president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i am very pleased to have this opportunity to discuss with you the preparations for tomorrow’s meeting of the european council. as you will be aware, president van rompuy has taken the initiative to organise regular thematic discussions in the european council with the aim of ensuring that all eu policies contribute to promoting the objectives of improved competitiveness, job creation and strong and sustainable economic growth. these debates are important in themselves in ensuring that key horizontal challenges that the union faces are worked through, and that direction is given at the highest level, and beyond the council formation in which they are normally treated, but also in as much as they can feed into a more wide-ranging discussion on the economic and social challenges europe faces and, indeed, into the europe 2020 strategy discussions. tomorrow’s european council will discuss and establish the direction for further work on two policy areas which are of crucial importance to europe’s economy: energy and elements of taxation. on energy, the council will build on the discussion under the irish presidency, including at the informal meeting of energy ministers in dublin recently. ensuring the uninterrupted supply of affordable and sustainable energy is of critical interest to individual citizens who are affected directly by any interruption, or threatened interruption, in supply as well as the impact of high energy prices. they are equally essential for ensuring that industry and the jobs that go with it remain in europe and are an important factor in attracting new industrial investment, and they can therefore be considered as a key condition for a return to growth. in order to secure the objective of affordable and sustainable energy, and to ensure the reliability of supply, we have to meet our objective of completing the internal energy market by 2014 and of developing greater interconnection. tomorrow’s european council will set out the additional work that is required in order to meet these objectives within the agreed time frame. interconnections and the modernisation of energy infrastructure generally require very significant investment. this is largely expected to come from the private sector, which means we must be able to offer a predictable and reliable climate and energy policy framework in which investment can be encouraged. the european council will set priorities for action needed to facilitate investment including the ten-e or structural funds as well as through the eib, and it will also address the regulatory environment and highlight priorities for improvement. particular stress will be placed on the need to improve energy efficiency: the cheapest energy is that which we do not use. innovative financing methods, more systematic supply diversification and improved liquidity in the internal energy market can all contribute to reducing energy costs. the commission has agreed to prepare an analysis of the composition and drivers of energy prices and costs by the end of the year. tomorrow’s european council will also discuss tax issues and in particular the problem of tax evasion. it is crucial, in the current difficult economic climate, to tackle tax evasion and fraud. at a time of fiscal consolidation we must take action to protect revenues if we are to ensure the confidence of citizens in the fairness and effectiveness of our tax systems. this is an issue which has rightly become the focus of public attention and is one to which the presidency attaches particular importance. that is why we support the initiative of president van rompuy to put this issue on the agenda of tomorrow’s european council meeting. it is why minister noonan, as chair of ecofin, together with commissioner šemeta, took the initiative of spelling out key areas where concrete action can be delivered in the short term. we welcome the close interest of parliament on this issue, and i would like to take this opportunity to acknowledge the work which mojca kleve kekuš and ildikó gáll-pelcz have put into their respective reports on this subject. tomorrow’s discussion will, in part, build on the very positive outcome on these issues of last week’s ecofin council. for example, the announcement of a pilot facility for the automatic exchange of information between administrations is a useful contribution to further work in this area both within the eu and internationally. at eu level, the commission intends in june to propose amendments to the directive on administrative cooperation in order for the automatic exchange of information to cover the full income range. at international level, the eu will play a key role in supporting and promoting the automatic exchange of information as the new international standard, taking account of existing eu arrangements. following the agreement at ecofin last week on a mandate to update the eu’s agreements with switzerland, liechtenstein, monaco, andorra and san marino, we hope that negotiations will begin very soon to ensure that these countries continue to apply measures equivalent to those in the eu. there is also consensus on the scope of the revised directive on the taxation of savings income, which should enable it to be adopted by the council by the end of this year. further work includes measures to counter vat fraud, where the council is due to adopt directives on the quick reaction mechanism and on the reverse charge mechanism by the end of june, and cooperation in the area of tackling aggressive tax planning and profit shifting, both within the eu and more widely. tomorrow’s european council is a relatively short meeting, but the two main issues to be addressed are critical for the future competitiveness of europe. we look forward to constructive discussions and concrete results which we will be taking forward in the months to come.
president of the commission. − mr president, at moments like these, when growth forecasts for the near future are low, our job is to make europe work, to the benefit of european citizens – of all our citizens. on the agenda of this week’s european council meeting are two issues that, technical as they may seem at first, are crucial in that respect. first, energy, where there is so much more benefit to be reaped – both for citizens and for the competitiveness of our businesses – from european integration and investment. second, tax fraud and tax evasion, where by sharpening our common european tools against the tax avoiders we can start to restore the sense of fairness that citizens and small businesses have lost as a result of the financial crisis. at a time when debate about europe is all too often a futile shouting match between believers and non-believers, this is a discussion that separates those who like to talk from those who are willing to act, and those who prefer to attract attention to themselves from those who are determined to achieve results for citizens. i trust that most of us are on the side of the citizens and working for concrete results. we are all very much aware of, and concerned by, the immediate growth prospects for europe. this very challenging outlook should galvanise the efforts of all of us, both at european level and in the member states, to mobilise every growth lever we have at hand and give any impetus we possibly can to help citizens and businesses through these very difficult times. a stronger european energy policy is a particularly important tool to help achieve this. we know that europe is not endowed with abundant natural riches. the global energy equation is changing fast, and if we want to avoid losing in this race for resources, we will have to step up our joint european efforts. while the united states is on its way to becoming a net exporter of gas instead of an importer, as a result of the shale gas boom, europe’s import dependence is further increasing and, for oil and gas, is set to grow to over 80% by 2035. already in 2012, industry gas prices were four times lower in the us than in europe. for electricity prices, the eu is almost twice as expensive as the us. so this is above all a debate about our energy security and our competitiveness. the situation for citizens is also increasingly problematic. energy bills are rising, adding up to a share of between 7% and 17% of average household expenditure in different member states. the weakest income groups are even harder hit. so this is also a debate about social equity. in short: we are in a difficult strategic environment. but we must not be resigned to it. we cannot single-handedly change long-term global trends, but we can clearly influence them by stepping up our european efforts and making our energy policy more secure, competitive and sustainable. of course, different member states have different energy mixes. yet the added value of stronger european integration in this field is evident. let me outline a few urgent steps which i will push for at tomorrow’s summit. first and foremost, it is crucial that we complete our internal energy market by the end of next year, as agreed by heads of state or government. market opening has brought prices down for consumers wherever real opening was achieved. but there is still plenty of room for improvement, including in cross-border trade, integration and fair competition. we urgently need to implement the third energy package to keep prices for our consumers and businesses in check. at the same time, we should also be clear that it is not just commodity prices but policy choices of member states – like taxes, levies, support mechanisms, etc., which have a great impact on price variations – on which we must reflect to avoid fragmentation. in preparation for this european council – since the president of the european council has asked me to make a presentation of these policies – i have distributed to all member states a comparison of the price structure in our member states (it is available to you as well, and i have also sent a copy to the president of the european parliament). it is amazing to see how big the differences are across europe, precisely because of different national policies that in fact make having a completely fragmented internal market in this area almost unavoidable. secondly, we have to push for more public and private investment in energy infrastructure – the backbone of the internal market. the financial crisis has limited the means available for such indispensable investments, but the needs are huge: by 2020, we estimate that eur 1 trillion will be needed in the energy sector. these investments will have to come from the private sector mostly, but the european union can play a key role. remember, we are expecting to devote some eur 5 billion of the next mff to energy interconnections, through the connecting europe facility, which must become operational rapidly. member states can also devote a bigger share of their structural funds to investing in energy and energy efficiency. thirdly, we must continue to strengthen the internal and external diversification of our supplies. this includes tapping new international sources, for instance through the southern gas corridor, which i have been pushing hard and on which we expect decisive decisions soon. it also means speaking with one european voice on global energy matters. internally, it requires a more coordinated approach between member states on the positive rise of renewables. last but not least, we need a balanced, union-wide approach on using the potential of unconventional hydrocarbons, such as shale gas, on which the commission is preparing an initiative. to conclude on energy: the right policies are in place. we know the way forward, but implementation is too slow. there is a clear ‘cost of non-europe’ here. we must do more together to ensure economic competitiveness and energy equity. we are not heading towards an age of cheap energy, but we have the choice between investing scarce resources in our own sustainable and smart energy and paying for imports. for that, we must complete our internal energy market, become more energy-efficient, invest in infrastructure and innovation, exploit renewables more cost-effectively and further diversify our external supplies. these are the policy priorities that i will argue for tomorrow in the european council. the european council will also debate our common engagement against tax fraud and tax evasion. now, as the two reports debated later today make clear, i do not have to convince this house of the urgency of this issue. commissioner šemeta will, later this morning, present the commission’s views on these two very important reports. i would like to thank now their respective rapporteurs, ms mojca kleva kekuš for her report on the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens, and ms ildikó gall-pelcz for her tax report focusing on how to free the european potential for economic growth. as mr šemeta will explain in more detail, the commission is very grateful to parliament for the strong support given in these reports to our joint efforts in this crucially important area. let us not forget that the commission has been putting these issues on the table in very concrete terms for several years now; with our proposal in 2008 to close the gaps in the savings directive; with our proposal in 2011 for a negotiating mandate with neighbouring countries; with our june 2012 communication and the action plan we presented last december; and with our two recommendations on tax havens and on aggressive tax planning, also from last year. we can now see a growing interest in these issues amongst the member states which, frankly, was not there before. therefore let us not miss but seize the favourable momentum to make progress. there are burning questions to which we need to give convincing responses. how can we explain to honest households and businesses feeling the squeeze yet still paying their fair share of taxes that there are other parts of society and enterprise which are deliberately avoiding paying up? how can we justify the fact that fiscal consolidation is requiring member states to make difficult choices to reduce expenditure yet at the same time there are whole piles of cash that should be in the public purse but are never collected? the total loss of revenue due to illegal fraud and unacceptable evasion is estimated to be around eur 1 trillion a year. let us put that into some perspective. eur 1 trillion is nearly double the 2012 combined annual budget deficit of all member states. it is more than the total spent on health across the european union in 2008. it is more than six times the size of the annual budget of the european union. in other words, this money is roughly one multiannual financial framework. and, yes, it is the same amount that i mentioned earlier: the investments necessary to cover the needs in the european energy sector by 2020. that is a huge amount of money to simply let fall through the net. we have already identified most of the actions that are needed to tighten the net – your reports make that clear – yet we face a delivery gap. so our actions at national, european and international levels have to be accelerated and better coordinated. first, at national level, the reform of tax governance and tax administrations will feature prominently in the country specific recommendations the commission will present a few days from now. member states also need to get on and implement the commission’s action plan on tax evasion and avoidance of last december, and our recommendations on tax havens and aggressive tax planning. at european level, we have already built up an impressive toolbox to support member states’ ability to fight tax fraud and evasion. now we need to use it as much as possible and reach agreement without delay on the proposals the commission has already made to go further. that means concluding the negotiations on the revision of the savings taxation directive, further closing loopholes by extending it to investment funds, pensions, innovative financial instruments and payments made through trusts and foundations. tomorrow at the european council, i will push for a political commitment on one very simple principle: that on 1 january 2015 the european union should have automatic exchange of information for all forms of income. the commission will shortly table a proposal to amend the directive on administrative cooperation. this already applies an automatic exchange of information for a range of income, such as employment, pensions and insurance, from 2015. the new proposal will further extend the scope of automatic exchange of information between all member states to cover all relevant types of income, such as dividends and capital gains. with the savings proposal on the table, the existing provisions on administrative cooperation and the forthcoming commission proposal, this is indeed a feasible target – provided the political will is there. the proposals pending on tackling vat fraud, the common consolidated corporate tax base, which will deal with the problems of transfer pricing, and the revision of our anti-money laundering framework also have the potential to make a real difference. i am happy to note the adoption, last week, of a mandate to start negotiations on our savings agreements with switzerland, liechtenstein, andorra, monaco and san marino, and i assure you the commission will take forward these negotiations as a priority. but that is no substitute for doing our own homework, namely through the adoption of the savings directive, where we need all the member states to signal their agreement. at global level, the upcoming g8 and g20 summits are an excellent opportunity to make progress, and the eu is taking the lead in this, based on our experience and expertise. let us remember that automatic information exchange has been the underlying principle of our approach since the 2005 savings taxation directive. i want to see this principle of automatic exchange become the standard at international level as well, and we will continue to work together with international partners to keep up the momentum on this. we can only do this if we speak with one voice, if we have done our concrete homework internally, if we speak and act as a union. some member states have signalled their readiness to go further, faster. i really welcome their political engagement. but if we are to be really effective, internally and globally, there is no alternative but to go all the way, together, and build on our common eu framework. to conclude, these two debates are crucial at this time. they matter for our public finances, for our competitiveness, and also for the cost of living of our citizens. even more, they are essential for the credibility of our efforts to fight the crisis, for the political capital we are willing to invest in it and the legitimacy of the demands the crisis makes on those who struggle to pay their energy bills or their taxes. they need any relief they can get – and by confronting the specific challenges of our energy markets, we can make a real difference. they need to know that the burden of the crisis is shouldered by everyone in a fair and equitable manner and that we will act jointly and decisively against those who refuse to carry their fair share of the burden. they need assurance that we can show political leadership and take on the political responsibility to do anything and everything possible to support them. we have debated these issues in the past, and progress has already been made. now is the time to go further: not with more words and further analysis but by approving and implementing concrete proposals and actions. in writing. i voted in favour of the introduction of legislation on offshore oil and gas activities. this is the first time the eu has legislated on this subject, through a directive. we have insisted on the need for a separation between the body responsible for the security of operations and the one responsible for its economic development in order to avoid any conflict of interest. many incidents with massive environmental consequences, such as the bp oil rig explosion in the gulf of mexico in 2010, have shown the need for strict regulation of offshore activities. parliament today committed itself to securing offshore activities by requiring operators to provide proof of their financial capacity to cover any damage caused and to submit an internal emergency response plan and a major hazard report.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report on the security of offshore oil and gas activities. it was imperative that parliament should address this issue to avoid major accidents on drilling rigs with serious environmental and economic consequences. the good practices that this report calls for to be shared seem to me to be full of good sense: an increased eu capacity to intervene in emergencies, clarification of legal provisions on liability/compensation, sharing of good practices by the oil and gas industry in terms of risk management, and sharing of good regulatory practices between european jurisdictions. i also welcome the increased role of the european maritime safety authority. the very short transposition period will also require member states to take responsibility.
in writing. the european parliament voted in favour of new rules governing offshore oil and gas platforms. the initial objective was to ensure, according to commissioner oettinger, that a disaster like the deepwater horizon in the gulf of mexico in 2010 could not take place in european waters. the text voted on is unfortunately not very comprehensive. offshore mining is a dangerous activity that requires a strong regulatory framework. environmental amendments were voted on in the envi committee, including a moratorium on drilling in the arctic and the introduction of financial and civil liability for industrialists. these positive achievements were rejected in three trialogue meetings with the council - under the cypriot and then irish presidencies. i regret that these concessions were made under the influence of industry and the member states directly concerned by these drilling (denmark, the netherlands, the united kingdom). the independence of safety assessments can no longer be guaranteed. the european maritime safety agency (emsa) should have been given more powers for supervision and certification. although the world is on the verge of an oil boom, oil rigs continue to be used and threaten the seabed and coastlines.
in writing. offshore oil and gas activities can be the cause of real disasters: an accident can destroy an entire coastal or marine environment, and the economies that depend on it. it has become necessary to secure these operations. the aim of this text is twofold: not only to reduce the number of accidents by working on prevention, but also to reduce their scale by responding quickly and better to their consequences. by emphasizing the special attention that must be paid to the arctic, this text makes the choice that europeans expect from us for the protection of this unique, but so vulnerable and threatened, ecosystem. i think that these provisions were sufficient to take account of this issue, and that is why i opposed the amendments proposed by the green group, which attempted to introduce into the text issues which would have to be settled at the level of the states concerned and of international bodies, in particular the arctic council.
in writing. in the face of the scale of the damage caused by the 2010 bp deepwater horizon oil rig fire in the gulf of mexico, it was vital that the eu put in place measures to ensure the safety of offshore oil and gas platforms with very high environmental risks. companies must be held directly liable for any damage caused by their operations and will now have to prove that they have the financial capacity to cover such damage. they will also be required to submit hazard reports and contingency plans before operations begin. these new standards will also help to overcome the fragmentation of the regulatory framework governing the safety of offshore oil and gas operations in europe.
in writing. following the explosion on the deepwater horizon platform in 2010 in the gulf of mexico, which caused a black tide of 4.9 million barrels of crude oil, the commission presented a text aimed at reducing the risks of major accidents linked to oil and gas activities and, above all, limiting their consequences. it is in the name of preserving the environment and the precautionary principle that i voted in favour of this text, which will make it possible to increase the safety of these platforms and also to take greater account of the victims of disasters.
in writing. on 21 may, the european parliament delivered its opinion on offshore oil exploration and production. the first amendment adopted by the commission is more than harmful to the protection of the environment and the safety of workers on the platforms, by turning the draft regulation into a directive. this change is not a trivial one, since it will allow the text to be applied in a variable geometry, depending on how the different member states apply it. a regulation would have allowed for the same application to all, for issues which are in fact transnational in nature. secondly, although i had asked for it, the application of the seveso standards on industrial accidents was rejected, whereas it would have allowed for better supervision and much stricter protection of nature and man. finally, and this is the most important point, the protection of employees is only dealt with very briefly in this text, in a few sentences... the health and safety of workers on the platforms is far too important to be dealt with by a quick spray, without concrete and strong measures. for these reasons i have decided to vote against this text.
in writing. offshore drilling activities are essential for the exploitation of deepwater oil and gas reserves. but in such a sensitive field of activity, any accident would have irreversible consequences for our environment, leading to a new ecological catastrophe. it is therefore necessary to draw up rules to prevent any risk of accidents. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which sets minimum european standards for oil and gas safety. such legislation will make it possible to clarify the liability of the operators concerned and to better assess the risks of accidents.
in writing. i supported the report on offshore oil and gas exploration, development and production. indeed, the risks associated with these activities are of major importance as evidenced by the dramatic environmental and economic consequences of the deepwater horizon case in the gulf of mexico in 2010. regulation at eu level is therefore needed to regulate oil and gas extraction activities in european seas. we propose to establish a set of minimum european standards for oil and gas safety. the directive also aims to deepen cooperation between national supervisory authorities and provides for a crisis management mechanism, in partnership with the european maritime safety agency.
