in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the recommendations contained in it make it possible to improve the security of our oil and gas installations. it was also very important to me that the employees were involved in this process of securing safety, and that is exactly what this report advocates. that's why i voted for it.
in writing. i voted against the report on offshore oil and gas exploration and production activities, because it is far from sufficient. apart from a few suggestions for repairing the damage caused by oil accidents, this report does not address the real issues and risks of offshore oil and gas exploitation. on the contrary, instead of protecting the environment, the safety of workers and the rights of citizens, the report protects the big oil companies and their interests. it seems that the gulf of mexico oil spill and its devastating effects on the environment and on the surrounding populations were not a lesson learned. in guyana, if the oil companies, in addition to not creating jobs to the extent that they could by training young guyanese, are not bound by strict and strong rules, we are heading for disaster.
in writing. the european union has learned from the environmental disaster caused by the bp oil rig fire in the gulf of mexico in 2010. i therefore voted in favour of this report which sets out stricter safety rules for offshore platforms. this directive lays down in particular minimum standards for the safety of offshore oil and gas drilling, licensing procedures, emergency plans and information-sharing obligations. these standards also provide for the obligation to study the financial solvency of applicants in the event of economic and ecological damage. european companies will be obliged to report on all incidents on their platforms, even if they are not located in a maritime zone of the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the directive on offshore oil and gas drilling. it is designed to protect the environment and ensure the safety of the personnel working there. the 2010 disaster in the united states, which saw some 780 million litres of oil spilled into the gulf of mexico, is a reminder of the need to ensure the sustainable operation of this industry. the directive provides that before a drilling permit is obtained, companies will have to submit, in consultation with the staff, an assessment report of the 'major hazards' and contingency plans to deal with any eventuality. in addition, companies will have to be able to prove, before operation, their ability to repair the damage their operations might cause. at national level, member states will also have responsibilities, such as preparing response plans, which will be reviewed by the european maritime safety agency (emsa). such measures seem to me appropriate and just, and i would be of the opinion that we should take comparable measures concerning the safety of ships at sea by recognising in european law the concepts of 'ecological damage' and 'chain of responsibility', as recognised by the court of cassation.
in writing. this report seemed to be well-intentioned in proposing to set out the conditions for offshore oil and gas exploration, development and production activities, but was emptied of its contents during negotiations with the council. the moratorium on drilling in the arctic zone, which threatens the biodiversity of the region, was abandoned following lobbying by the oil giants. the role of the european maritime safety agency in monitoring the exploitation of these resources has been reduced. once again, the interests of the big companies take precedence over the protection of the environment and the interests of the people. the sea is part of the world heritage, it is a common good that must be protected as such. it cannot be left to the law of profit and the interests of a few multinational corporations. this text is therefore a missed opportunity to defend biodiversity and to avoid major disasters, such as the one that occurred in the gulf of mexico in 2010 on the basis of british petroleum's drilling. i therefore voted against this proposal for a regulation.
in writing. we all remember the image of the 2010 oil spill in the gulf of mexico and the environmental disaster it caused. by our vote, we have given the eu a range of measures to safeguard european waters and to ensure maximum safety in oil and gas activities. i naturally voted in favour of this report because the measures proposed guarantee the protection of european waters and coastlines. they also serve as an example at international level and encourage other countries to align themselves with the eu's leading environmental standards. the legislative framework is overseen by the european maritime safety agency, which will make it possible to benefit from its expertise and resources, in consultation with the member states. it is also a great satisfaction that the precautionary principle has been enshrined as a prerequisite for any deployment of offshore activities. industry and activities at sea are a response to the challenge of eu energy independence; so let us be careful that they do not endanger marine, marine and coastal ecosystems.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the eu's renewable energy perspectives in the internal energy market. this was in response to the commission communication 'renewable energies: a major player in the european energy market'. according to the report, the share of renewable energy will be at least 30% of the eu's energy mix by 2030. the text also stresses the need to strengthen our infrastructure by modernising the various networks. i am in favour of quantified targets for 2030 for renewable energy but considering that it is too early to set this target now, i have decided to abstain on an amendment calling on the european commission to propose such a quantified target now. for the same reason, i have chosen to reject an amendment proposing a binding target of 45% renewable energy by 2030.
in writing. the debate on the energy transition is in full swing in france and in our neighbours: germany, the united kingdom, poland - to name just a few. while the stated ambition of the european council is to build a european energy policy, the european parliament is leading the way. following up on the european commission's 2050 roadmap, we have today adopted an own-initiative report on 'today's challenges and prospects for renewable energy in the internal energy market'. i co-signed an important amendment, which was the focus of the debate, which was in favour of a binding target for renewable energy (r) by 2030 and to set this target between 40% and 45% of the union's energy mix. i welcome the adoption of the principle of a binding target - so that we can continue our progress towards the energy transition. but i regret that the idea of a 'fork' between 40 and 45% has been rejected. any reference to quantified targets for 2030 is thus removed, resulting in a less ambitious text than the one recommended by the commission. the parliament is here showing its distrust of the need to invest in the r & d.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new strategy to ensure that renewable energy is an integral part of the european energy market by 2020. the current support mechanisms will need to be improved and made more transparent in order to strengthen coherence within the internal market. i voted in favour of a binding target of 30% of europe's energy supply from renewable sources by 2050. this objective seems to me to be quite proportionate and achievable, given the current financial and economic difficulties.
in writing. i supported the reul report on the current challenges and prospects for renewable energy in the european energy market. it proposes to draw up a precise roadmap to achieve an increased share of renewable energy in our energy mix by 2050. pragmatic and realistic, i agree with the objective of convergence of national models. i also believe that it is very important to set up european infrastructures to ensure the proper functioning of the single electricity market. it is a crucial issue for the competitiveness of the european union and the quality of life of future generations.
in writing. to meet the renewable energy challenge and achieve a real european energy market, clear guidelines must be set today to enable all actors to anticipate and participate in these crucial developments. this ambitious text sets out our essential requirements, including the need to strengthen cooperation between the member states in order to achieve greater consistency in our energy choices. companies certainly need visibility for their investments. and europe must continue to be at the forefront of the world's ecological transition. but in the current crisis setting new binding targets risks hurting our businesses, our competitiveness and our jobs. there is still time to consider the next steps, and this must be done in consultation with all the parties concerned.
in writing. renewable energy is the future of the european union's energy supply and equipment. thanks to the policy pursued by the union since 2007 under its '20-20-20' commitment, which provides for 20% of the energy consumed in europe to come from renewable sources by 2020, the dependence of the european territory on conventional energy sources has already been reduced. the dynamism of the renewable energy sector has also helped to create 500,000 jobs in europe. the union should be able to set itself an even more ambitious target for 2030 to increase the share of renewable energy. in addition to the creation of sustainable jobs, this ambition should have positive effects for european industry in terms of prices, the improvement of existing technologies and the development of new technologies. it is therefore vital that support for the development of renewable energies be provided within the framework of an ambitious common industrial policy. the union must also protect its businesses from unfair practices by certain emerging economies that could undermine the technological development of this leading sector, for example by restricting the export of rare earths.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this own-initiative report which calls for greater convergence between the 170 renewable energy support schemes in the different member states and for the development of an appropriate and better integrated european support scheme for the period after 2020. the european union must make a firm commitment to decarbonising its economy, but all renewables are not the panacea. before deciding to commit to a quantified renewable energy target for 2030, let us first make sure that we unlock the funding for the infrastructure, networks and storage technologies that are essential for the integration of renewables into the european energy market. in addition, technological neutrality must continue to be guaranteed and safe nuclear energy retains its strategic importance for european energy policy in the years to come. in order to prepare for the major choices of 2030 and 2050, the european union's energy and environmental policy must be linked to our industrial policy with the objectives of reducing the cost of energy and defending competitiveness and employment.

in writing. no one can now question the legitimacy of renewable energy. it is true that their development helps to offset the negative externalities of fossil fuels. this is not to be a matter of showing complacency and refusing to be critical of them. the question of the costs of developing these sources of energy, their profitability and the time needed to pay off the investment required to implement them must be considered. there is a lot of uncertainty about this today. therefore, setting binding targets and figures in a timetable for the share of renewable energy in the european energy mix seems to me to be useless, even absurd. this would be to forget that the definition of the energy mix remains the responsibility of the member states! what's the point of setting goals if we don't all have the same reference? on the other hand, price deregulation would be absurd if it had the effect of restricting the access of disadvantaged households to energy.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report on media freedom across the eu. i agree with the stated objectives: ensuring editorial independence, pluralism and protecting the fundamental right to freedom of expression and information, which is indeed essential for democracy and the rule of law. it is also urgent to avoid media concentration in the hands of large monopolies, as in france, where the main press groups are owned by industrialists whose activities are concentrated in other areas, including the arms trade. a little transparency on media ownership wouldn't hurt. similarly, regular monitoring of the amendment of the legislation of the relevant member states could perhaps help to prevent the development of freedom-threatening laws for the press as in hungary. i have no illusions about the reality of eu practices, but i systematically support anything that can help to introduce respect for the charter of fundamental rights into the eu legal reality and establish sanctions in this area that are more in line with so-called european values than austerity policies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted for this motion for a resolution because i believe that the subject of pensions is far too important not to be discussed at the right level, that is, at european level. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. deep reforms and convergence of european pension systems must be implemented to ensure a decent pension for everyone. of course, it is extremely sensitive to reform systems that were the subject of long and difficult negotiations several decades ago. but perhaps it is precisely because this consensus is old that it needs to be debated again. the economic context has changed, the world has changed, and we are endangering our social security models if we do not have the courage, today, to face reality. our birth rates are falling, our young people are going to school longer and longer, life expectancy is getting longer and longer. these reforms have already waited far too long. we must therefore urgently review the financing of pensions, show courage and show concerted action so that the solutions found are supported by the greatest number of people.
in writing. the vote of this european parliament resolution followed the publication in february 2012 of a european commission white paper on a strategy for adequate, safe and sustainable pensions. i voted in favour of this text, which draws the consequences both of the ageing of europe's populations and of the pressures exerted by the financial crisis on national pension systems.
in writing. how will the future of our pensions be secured? most member states are now engaged in reflection on the subject. the european commission is also considering this and is not shy about making recommendations to the member states. the report by mrs oomen-ruijten is contradictory from the outset: pensions remain a national competence, but the union decides on the strategy to be adopted and makes recommendations to the states. in the empl committee we had achieved good things, including a stronger focus on the first pillar of pension systems, namely the universal public pension system, which must retain its central role in ensuring decent incomes for pensioners. i have, however, abstained on many paragraphs and on the final vote because i remain sceptical of the approach taken by the commission and endorsed by parliament. the multi-pillar system cannot be achieved without recalling the priorities and specific features of our welfare state. it is obvious that life expectancy should be taken into account in the reform of pensions, but we must also take account of the burdens involved. i am very sorry that there is nothing in the report on this subject.
in writing. with this vote we ask the member states to introduce or maintain diversified pension systems. one third of the eu population is over 55 years old, so the very sustainability of pension systems is at stake as public finances are constrained. we must maintain publicly funded pensions to ensure decent living conditions, as these remain the main source of income for pensioners, particularly in the countries most affected by the economic crisis. if this is the responsibility of the member states, eu coordination is more than necessary. in this respect it is regrettable that the commission's white paper does not address the importance of this pillar in the fight against poverty.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which calls for the creation of a macro-regional strategy for the alpine regions. the community's action in this field is based on the principle of subsidiarity. since these problems are not confined to a single 'national side' of the mountain range, it seems appropriate to deepen existing crossborder cooperation to find solutions. it is not a question of creating a new level between the state and the region, or of reducing the prerogatives of the former. based on a shared will of the actors on the ground, the aim of such a strategy is really to bring all the stakeholders together to build concrete projects that improve the alpine economy and the daily lives of the inhabitants of this area.

in writing. i voted against this resolution on pensions, which is a real trap. it automatically links increasing life expectancy with the legal retirement age. it's not fair to long and arduous careers. it is also not financially viable in the long term: we will not finance social protection with such rust on the backs of the employees. the text also calls for the development of pension systems based on capitalisation. we are in favour of pension systems based on a system of distribution and we do not want public money to be used to make life insurance more attractive, because that would seriously undermine the solidarity of our social protection.
in writing. the economic crisis has reminded us of the vulnerability of public and private pension systems in europe. in voting for this resolution i wanted to say that even though pensions are a matter for the member states, a minimum of european coordination is necessary. we therefore recommend that the member states ensure a sustainable and secure approach to pensions, combining pensions financed by the state and those provided for by collective agreements. i voted against the emphasis on 'retirement savings', which i consider to be an inadequate solution because it is more costly and less transparent.
in writing. i voted in favour of the ria oomen-ruijten report in response to the european commission's white paper on pensions, as it is important that in the context of the economic crisis and ageing of the population, member states introduce and maintain diversified pension schemes. this is done through a 'multi-pillar' approach, combining public pension schemes (pillar one), supplementary pension schemes resulting from collective agreements, company agreements or national law (pillar two) and private savings (pillar three). this approach should allow for better consideration of national specificities and decent living conditions. finally, the resolution also proposes to balance working time with retirement time, develop a code of good practice for occupational pension schemes and ensure better protection of occupational pension rights in the event of the insolvency of the employer.
in writing. the european parliament has spoken on pension systems in europe, which nevertheless remain a competence of the member states. while employment, the return to growth and the competitiveness of enterprises are major immediate concerns, the reform of our pension systems is another key issue which has already been undertaken in many countries since the end of the 1980s but which is slow to be implemented in france. thanks to the determination of president sarkozy, we have laid the foundations for this necessary reform and the efforts must be continued. unfortunately, we are witnessing the current government's hesitation to put the debate off until next autumn.
in writing. a thorough reform of the private and public pension systems is needed today to be able to meet the challenges of tomorrow. with nearly a third of the population over 50, action is needed now. that is why i have voted in favour of this text, which proposes a harmonised overhaul of pension systems to ensure that everyone has a decent pension. diversification is clearly the condition for an effective pension system. while the distribution of pensions must remain the main source of income, despite the current economic difficulties, it must not be the only system available to citizens. they must also be able to benefit from other schemes such as supplementary pensions or retirement savings.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on adequate, secure and sustainable pensions for our fellow europeans. while pensioners represent a significant proportion of the population in the european union, the crisis has magnified the problem of ageing in europe and the need to ensure sustainable pension systems. although this is a matter for national competence, we recommend that governments coordinate their policies. the state must, however, remain the main guarantor of its pension system.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on adequate, safe and sustainable pensions. this challenge will become more pressing as the population ages. with one third of the eu population over the age of 55, the sustainability of pension systems is under threat. in addition to promoting an increase in the employment rate by allowing those who wish to work longer, member states should develop a 'multi-pillar' approach. pensions could be financed by the state but also by pension savings and the establishment of collective agreements.
in writing. the report calls for the development of collective funded pension schemes and private individual savings. he has announced new attacks on the public solidarity regimes. this is all the more intolerable since pensions are the responsibility of the member states and not of the european union. the attention paid to women and a few generous phrases cannot mask this provocation, at a time when a new battle is being fought to defend the right to retire in france. i vote against it.
in writing. this report advocates a new approach to pension funding through a combination of different funding systems. this combination would result in the weakening of the pension distribution system in favour of the capitalisation system and individual private saving. the system of shared pensions, which is rooted in our french tradition, is based on the principle of solidarity between generations. however, to remove this solidarity and to destroy the public solidarity schemes would have considerable negative impacts on the situation of workers. the report is therefore a decoy and does nothing to ensure 'adequate, secure and sustainable' pensions for european citizens. i therefore voted against.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the overall increase in life expectancy, record unemployment rates and the poor financial health of the member states are pushing us to reform our pension systems in depth across europe. it doesn't matter which system you choose, capitalization or distribution. we're going straight into the wall. it is not just a question of simply raising the retirement age. it is also about ensuring that everyone, regardless of age, can find a job. this is made possible by increased access to training and learning. this is particularly so as a person who has been in the labour market for a longer period is more likely to change careers. similarly, it is essential to encourage individuals to subscribe to supplementary retirement savings products. in view of the state of public finances in the member states, it is essential that pensioners are not entirely dependent on them and receive supplementary income.
in writing. the ageing of the population is the major challenge facing pension and retirement systems in the union. one third of the european population is already over 55 years old and our continent continues to age. the ageing population is compounded by the impoverishment of the elderly due to the crisis and the drastic cuts in social assistance from national budgets. it is therefore necessary to adapt our pension systems to one of these two constraints. the european union, which is not meant to intervene directly in the choices of states, can help coordinate reforms and propose solutions. i therefore voted in favour of this report which advocates a 'multi-pillar' approach combining state-funded pensions, supplementary pensions provided for by collective agreements between companies and finally personal savings by employees. one of the options envisaged is to increase the employment rate, by limiting early retirement schemes and allowing older people, if they wish, to work beyond the legal age.
in writing. − the financial and economic crisis across europe has severely affected the pension income of millions of europeans. until now, the pension issue has been resolved only at national level, but the economies are interconnected and it is no longer possible for each country to guarantee the adequacy, security and sustainability of its social protection systems on its own. i therefore supported the european parliament's resolution which recommends that the eu and the member states assess the current and future sustainability and adequacy of pension systems and identify best practices and policy strategies that can ensure the safest and most cost-effective pension provision possible. the resolution draws the attention of the european commission to the importance of first-tier pension schemes. in latvia, as in other poorer eu member states, it is the first level of pension that accounts for the largest number of pensions in the country. this is why member states need to implement first-rate pension reforms to ensure that people, especially those belonging to the most vulnerable groups, have a decent standard of living and economic independence in old age. when we think about a better future for pensioners, we should also think about the people who are working today. one of the obstacles that often prevents latvians working abroad from returning to latvia is the fact that all pension contributions made will remain in the country concerned. it is therefore important for latvia that workers have the possibility to change their place of work within the european union, while maintaining the right to receive and maintain an occupational pension.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, let me first thank the members very much for their very pertinent questions. the commission welcomes parliament’s draft resolution on future legislative proposals on emu. against the backdrop of the current economic outlook, the case for structural reforms and for rebuilding the economic and monetary union is evident. we have already substantially reinforced our economic governance – with the essential support of parliament – but more work is nevertheless required, as the chair of the committee, ms bowles, has just stressed. in the very short term we need to complete the repair of the financial sector in europe. the construction of a banking union will reinforce confidence and help restore the flow of credit to households and enterprises, especially smes, which are crucial for job creation. further important elements for improved economic integration were set out in the two communications that we published in march: one on the ex ante coordination of major economic policy reforms and the other on a convergence and competitiveness instrument. let me stress the consultative nature of these communications. they set out ideas and suggestions and pose questions. on the basis of the input we will receive from parliament, the member states, stakeholders and national parliaments, the commission will consider its proposals on the way forward. parliament will be fully involved in the shaping of any prospective initiatives, in line with the treaties. further on the role of parliament: the commission’s objective is to extend the economic dialogue to cover these initiatives. parliament could invite the commission, the president of the council or the president of the eurogroup to discuss a commission opinion or the conclusions of discussions in the council. i would also find it very useful if parliament could also invite member states to participate in an exchange of views on major economic policy reforms and explain their policies and defend their positions. this would enable public scrutiny and provide peer pressure. on your question regarding the relationship of the communications to the fiscal compact, or rather the treaty on stability, coordination and governance, the concept of ex ante coordination of plans for major economic policy reforms was introduced by article 11 of this treaty. the treaty foresees the incorporation of its substance into the legal framework of the european union within five years, at most, of the date of its entry into force. the consultative communication presents options for the integration of such coordination into the community framework. with regard to your question on the nature of the contractual arrangement under the convergence and competitiveness instrument: the instrument would be based in the treaties but the contractual arrangement would be of a political nature. as the current treaties do not allow for the possibility of legally binding contracts, conditionality would imply that no financial support would be paid or be recovered in case of non-compliance. finally, on your question as to which reforms should be a priority under the convergence and competitiveness instrument: the key aim of this instrument is to contribute to the effective and smooth functioning of the economic and monetary union. it would do so by increasing the commitment of member states to implement specific reforms and by providing financial support to help member states to do so. these reforms would benefit not only the member state itself but the euro area as a whole. as the crisis has underlined, a lack of reform can have significant effects across the euro area. thank you for your attention and i look forward to hearing your views on the future legislative proposals of the emu.

allow us to judge the seriousness of the commitments and the reality of the political will to achieve greater efficiency in the economic action of the european union. recent history shows that while the european union has tried to be reactive, the shortcomings of the organization, particularly of the euro zone, have been detrimental. the crises have accumulated and have been dealt with in a certain improvisation, in the absence of appropriate instruments or means. the consequence of this situation has been that attempts have been made to compensate for the absence of community instruments by a systematic return to intergovernmentalism. this has created a dual legal system which must not continue. it is urgent to return to community instruments and to have the instruments needed to react effectively and, even better, to prevent dangerous situations. nevertheless, much work has been done. i would like to pay tribute to your determination, mr vice-president, which was not easy to implement because of the resistance or reluctance of the member states. the two commission communications set out the next steps in the project of achieving a genuine economic and monetary union. these communications, i would remind you, follow up on the commitments made by the commission in november 2012 in its draft and respond to the call of the european council and parliament. the future of economic and monetary union will be discussed again at the next summits, and we dare hope that concrete measures will be proposed and defined. the objectives are commendable: on the one asked the question. i shall not comment on all the points, of course. the resolution is precise and contains a number of useful contributions from parliament. i would like to stress a few points which i think are important. firstly, the prior coordination of major economic policy reform projects, which is essential. the implementation of national measures in areas which naturally fall within the european dimension is harmful and should be avoided. we have an example today with the proliferation of national banking laws, which anticipate what will be proposed by the commission in july or september as part of the reform of the banking sector. the fact that some member states adopt specific national provisions a few months in advance makes subsequent negotiation and harmonization of regulations more difficult. similarly, it is also necessary to ensure that national policies have an impact on other countries, which is something that must be taken into account. as regards the convergence and competitiveness instrument for the euro area, which provides for contractual arrangements, it certainly deserves to be specified and not rejected in principle, since the objective is to restore macroeconomic balances. in this respect, we want the principle of conditionality to be applied to the disbursement of funds. without the implementation of the planned reforms, there can be already being held are certainly a first step towards harmonizing positions. finally, i would like to say that it is important to strengthen the social dimension of economic and monetary union and to create, for example, a social and employment scoreboard to inform the discussions on the european semester.

on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, commissioner, on 14 december you were given the task of preparing a roadmap for the completion of economic and monetary union, in partnership with president van rompuy. this road map had four dimensions. the college has tabled two proposals for which you are responsible and refuses to table the text we are waiting for on the social front. but when i look at the unemployment situation in the european union, i see that it is a sign of the failure of your policy. and the silence of the college on the social dimension of economic and monetary union is a sign of the failure of mr barroso's presidency of this commission. you will not get out of the imbalance we are in, which is not just a macroeconomic imbalance. stop keeping a close eye on government deficits and debt. the question of social imbalances is equally important. sometimes the best and the worst comes from the united states. look at how the united states rebuilt its economy. it's because of the automatic stabilizers. we ask you to do the same in the social field, at european level, because this crisis has social origins, it has social consequences, and you will not get out of this crisis without introducing this social dimension, without setting up an automatic stabilizer by defining a minimum of unemployment benefits. it is a fair measure, it is an effective measure, and it is one which will enable you to correct precisely those macroeconomic imbalances which you cannot compensate for by your policies. after world war ii, we were also in situations of crisis almost as severe as those we are experiencing today. and it's thanks to the welfare state that we've got it back on track. today you have the chance, the possibility, if president barroso will listen to us, to set up the equivalent and the embryo of this; it's this automatic stabilizer. we ask you to initiate, not you, because we do not trust you to do so, but the european commission, under the responsibility of commissioner andor, the setting up of this automatic stabiliser. work on it! there was an embryo in the blueprint. that's a good idea, but you immediately abandoned it. we need to get her back on track. the commission must prepare the work of the next mandate with a green paper on the automatic stabiliser.

in writing. i voted in favour of this legislative resolution by which parliament calls on the european council not to consider the proposal for treaty amendments requested by former president vaclav klaus to allow the accession of the czech republic to the derogating protocol agreed with the united kingdom on the application of the charter of fundamental rights. i believe that the european union must guarantee its citizens and residents equal rights. it would therefore have been unacceptable for citizens of the czech republic to be excluded - as unfortunately british citizens are - from the rights recognised by the charter and to suffer a weakening of their legal protection. i would remind you that the charter of fundamental rights has been applicable to the czech republic since 1 december 2009, the date on which the treaty of lisbon entered into force. it has significantly increased the level of protection of the fundamental rights granted to czech citizens. a reversal is therefore not admissible.
in writing. during the negotiations on the lisbon treaty, the government of the czech republic expressed the wish that its country should join protocol no 30 on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to poland and the united kingdom. the european council consulted the parliament on the advisability of examining the proposed amendment. it should be noted that protocol no 30 does not exempt the united kingdom and poland from the binding provisions of the charter, nor is it a 'non-participation clause'. furthermore, the czech senate, in its resolution of 6 october 2011, opposed the adoption of protocol no 30 by the czech republic on the grounds that it would lower the level of protection of the fundamental rights and freedoms of czech citizens. we have therefore voted in favour of this report, which shows our concern and our scepticism about the czech republic's request.
in writing. i supported this text which proposes 'the establishment of rules governing a simple and rapid mechanism for the recognition of civil protection measures ordered in a member state'. given the freedom of movement within the eu, it was necessary to harmonise our legislation in this area and to complete the criminal law component adopted in 2011. i believe that everyone should be able to enjoy equal protection against domestic harassment or violence wherever they are in the eu. the text in question makes it possible, in particular, to simplify procedures for rapid protection of victims.
in writing. the proposal on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters is part of a package of measures to strengthen the rights of victims in the european union. the proposal complements a proposal for a directive aimed at ensuring the mutual recognition of protection measures taken in criminal matters. this is to protect victims of violence and to ensure that temporary protection granted in one member state remains valid when a person travels or settles in another member state. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal which aims to protect victims of violence, including domestic violence, stalking and violence against children. the aim was to ensure and simplify the mutual recognition of civil law protection measures taken in a member state. the rules on information, translation and information to the parties have been strengthened. the problem of mutual recognition of measures taken by an authority in a member state is one which i very often face in the committee on petitions, to which i belong, since the same problem concerns measures for the protection of minors in divorce cases. while land borders no longer exist in europe, administrative borders remain and it is important that even temporary protection measures granted in one member state remain valid when a person travels or settles in another member state.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which aims to strengthen the rights of victims in the european union and improves the commission's proposal for a regulation. the amendments to this report, which allow for easier recognition of protection measures, a strengthening of the rights of parties to information, translation and assistance, and a simplification of administrative procedures, will have a positive impact on european citizens.
in writing. given the existence and constantly increasing freedom of movement within the european union, it was necessary for the union to take the necessary measures to recognise and protect victims of crime. with this text, which i supported, people protected by a member state of the union as victims will now be able to move freely and safely within the territory of all the other member states of the european union. this text represents a real step forward in strengthening the rights of european victims.
in writing. this is the second time we have taken a decision on the question of mutual recognition of protection measures, the first time in criminal matters, this time in civil matters. in a european area without frontiers, it is necessary to ensure that the protection granted to a person, a victim in one state, also applies, and in an uninterrupted manner, in any other member state to which that person travels. all this sounds obvious, as a logical continuation of the further construction of a european area of freedom and justice, of the establishment of a genuinely european legal order: the protection granted by a state to a victim must accompany the victim when he or she is on the move. today's vote marks a further step forward in judicial cooperation and a major step forward in prevention, and i am very pleased about that. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the rights of victims are respected and that the rights of victims are protected.
in writing. while more than one in four women in france have reportedly been the victim of repeated domestic violence, i welcome the adoption of this text which will facilitate the freedom of movement of union citizens, women in particular, while ensuring better protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence by relatives, such as physical violence, harassment, sexual assault, stalking, intimidation and other forms of coercion. these victims of violence will thus be able, through a simplified procedure, to live and work outside their country of origin, with the assurance that the obligations imposed on the person posing a threat to their dignity, safety, personal freedoms and sexual integrity will apply wherever they are in europe. so this is a serious step forward for the rights of victims, which i strongly support.
in writing. as a member of the femm committee, i welcome the adoption of this regulation by parliament after the agreement reached with the council which closes the adoption of the victims package and allows mutual recognition between member states of protection orders in civil matters. victims will be able to move freely throughout the union with the certainty that these measures will be applied in the same way in all member states. the victims package will remain a major achievement of this mandate by significantly improving the rights of victims. it should be remembered that the majority of these victims are women, since the council of europe estimates that 20 to 25% of women will experience physical violence at some point in their lives.
in writing. within the european union, there is mutual recognition of protection measures in criminal matters, but no equivalent in civil matters. it was therefore necessary to address this so that victims of stalking, harassment or gender-based violence who are protected in one member state would benefit from equivalent and readily accessible protection if they travel to another country in the european union. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which fills the legal vacuum in this area.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the new measures to protect victims of violence across europe. the aim is to ensure that victims of such violence, in particular women and children, are fully protected in all member states. until now, protection could cease when a person moved from one state to another. a new regulation will thus apply directly at national level to allow for the mutual recognition of civil protection measures. it will also simplify the administrative procedure by means of a single, multilingual certificate. in the past, the cost of translation and the length of the procedure did not provide sufficient protection for victims of violence and threats to physical and moral integrity.
in writing. by joining the stockholm programme and allowing for the mutual recognition of civil decisions for the protection of victims of violence, this report allows for the harmonisation of the different procedures existing within the european union. i therefore vote in favour of this report because it corresponds to the objective of harmonizing the various european rights, which i can only welcome.
in writing. the objective of this report is to ensure mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters, in order to strengthen the rights of victims in the european union. in other words, victims of violence who benefit from a protection measure in one member state should be able to enjoy the same level of protection in other member states, so that they can exercise their right to move freely within the union without hindrance. by providing for a rapid and effective mechanism for a certificate issued by the state of origin to be recognised in the host state and by not providing for any grounds for refusal of this certificate, this text ensures more effective protection for victims within the european union. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. the freedom of movement we enjoy as european citizens is regarded by the vast majority of us as a very positive development. but sometimes it can be double-edged. although protection measures are already recognised in criminal matters, this is not yet the case in civil matters. as a result, victims of violence, especially family members, are likely to find themselves completely deprived when travelling to other eu countries if protection measures in civil matters are not recognised. it seems to me absurd that one of the great achievements of european cooperation should, because of a legal vacuum, make some of our fellow european citizens particularly vulnerable. that is not my idea of the european union. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which is intended to remedy this intolerable situation.

mr president, i would like to draw your attention to the respect for the european cultural exception. for more than twenty years, europe has been engaged in a process of protecting and promoting culture and cultural heritage. in this context, audiovisual services enjoy a privileged status since they are not subject to the services directive for the simple reason that the european union does not consider culture as a commodity like the others. the unesco convention on the protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions has enshrined the specificity of cultural and audiovisual goods in the field of trade. it is because of this specificity that aid for the development of culture finances a significant proportion of the budgets devoted to film production in the union. with such a system, we promote all culture, we encourage all artists. liberalising culture would be tantamount to encouraging production that is not generative of cultural and creative heritage, but ephemeral and focused on the immediate.

member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, the alpine regions have a long-lasting tradition of cooperation with a number of networks and associations that are already in place. good experience has been gained in facilitating coexistence between modern cities and traditional countryside areas, and between innovative activities and traditional ones. any new strategy approaches would need to be complementary to the existing tools, include the relevant stakeholders at the different levels and learn from existing experience in and outside the alps. the european commission therefore wants to have an in-depth analysis and a political discussion about the evaluation report on macro-regional strategies, which will be available in june, before making further decisions. a clear european added value in concrete fields of action needs to be shown, and it should be demonstrated that the strategic approach of a macro-regional strategy is the most appropriate way to reach those goals. even before our evaluation of existing strategies is complete, one thing is very clear: territorial cooperation programmes like the alpine space programme can play a very useful coordination role, but no single programme will have the scope or the funds to make a reality of a whole macro-regional strategy. this means that the authorities will need to align funds other than cooperation funds: all european structural and investment funds (esif) could and should be used in the strategy. so where do we stand today? the last alpine regions meeting took place in milan on 22 february 2013. in that meeting, it was agreed to strive for an alpine macro-regional strategy to be taken up at the european council in december 2013. to this end the regions, together with national governments, will work out a short document d´interpellation in a joint editorial team. this document will build on existing contributions: the initiative paper of the regions, the expert report of the alpine space programme and the contribution of the alpine convention. it should also determine the major cornerstones of a potential macro-regional strategy for the alpine space. the french government, which had offered to coordinate the process, was asked to approach national governments at high political level and invite them to appoint a technical member to join the editorial team for collaboration. the document is due to be decided at a political conference in france in early autumn 2013. further cooperation between the alpine space countries is definitely desirable, in order to tackle the common challenges. to be successful, it needs local commitment as well as national support: a bottom-up approach implies positive ownership, while central government support ensures greater coherence of the initiatives. but stepping up cooperation in this way requires more than political commitment; it requires technical expertise, stable and adequately-qualified staffing and institutional support to deliver results and make a success of this kind of initiative.
