in writing. the customs union plays a fundamental role in the functioning of the single market, which can only function properly through the common and consistent application of common and modern customs rules and procedures. that is why, in view of the evolution of customs and related legislation, it was necessary to propose a revision of the union customs code, in particular to align the regulation with the procedural requirements arising from the treaty of lisbon. in view of these facts, i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text providing for the revision of the customs code, which will be aligned with the provisions of the new lisbon treaty. in order to function properly, the single market needs to be regulated by common and modern customs arrangements. customs activity remains essential in the eu, as nearly 20% of all world imports pass through european customs, or two billion tonnes of goods a year. customs authorities have to process over 200 million customs declarations every year. it was therefore important to simplify the administrative system while maintaining our obligations to protect consumers and to fight fraud.
in writing. in order to give parliament and the council the time needed to consider the revision of the community customs code, i voted in favour of the text postponing the date of application of the regulation establishing the community customs code to 1 november 2013.
in writing. on thursday i voted in favour of amending the date of application of the draft community customs code, which i am responsible for as rapporteur. the entry into force of the modernised customs code, which was due to take effect on 24 june 2013, should be postponed to 1 november 2013. we will thus have the time to propose a satisfactory revision of the customs code which responds to the present challenges. the report aims to address the shortcomings of the first version of the revised customs code, which was published in 2003 and which was never taken into account by the member states. the revision of this text is, however, a major challenge, since the original text was published in 1992 and must be adapted to the new realities of the european union.
in writing. this report proposes to postpone the date of application of the modernised eu customs code by five months. i'm fine with this postponement. i do, however, dispute the limited grounds for which it is envisaged here to postpone that date. this postponement should be an opportunity to reformulate the customs policy of the european union. i propose that we discuss the need for european solidarity protectionism, which the new proposed code is seriously undermining. at a time when a growing proportion of the population is unemployed or precarious, it is criminal to set up a customs code which is intended solely to facilitate free trade and to take away the control powers of the member states. a broad debate on the union's customs policy must be initiated with the citizens. five months is a little short to do this, but if the union really had the means, it would certainly be possible.
in writing. following repeated human rights violations, burma has not been granted preferential rights under the eu's generalised system of preferences since 1997. noting its steady progress, the european commission has proposed to re-allocate these preferences to the country, provided that it continues to make progress. i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation because it is a good political signal and a relevant practical application of the 'more for more' rule which has governed the european union's external action for the past two years. i will, however, remain vigilant about the strict application of this principle: if further violations are found, i will call on the european commission to reopen a procedure for suspending preferences.
in writing. in 1997, the gsp tariff preferences for burma were temporarily withdrawn because of forced labour practices - a situation that was subsequently confirmed by the international labour organisation. in view of the improvements in the conditions of workers, the re-establishment of the generalised tariff preferences should enable burma to accelerate its economic growth and increase its exports. however, the country needs to undergo profound reforms. in view of these facts, i have voted in favour of the martin report.
in writing. the eu had withdrawn the benefit of the tariff preferences granted to myanmar in 1997 because of the systematic and widespread use of forced labour in the country. the country has since made great progress in this area, international restrictions have been lifted, so it was up to the eu to recognise the path taken towards the democratization of the country. i therefore voted in favour of restoring the tariff preferences for myanmar, including the introduction of the 'everything but arms' initiative in the country. i found the report balanced, acknowledging the significant progress the country has made, while pointing out the remaining difficulties in implementing these efforts.
in writing. i fully support the repeal of the 1997 regulation temporarily withdrawing the benefit of the generalised tariff preferences from burma. the regulation was adopted following the finding of the systematic and widespread nature of forced labour practices in that country. the international labour conference (ilo) last year recognised that significant progress had been made in this area. although limited, progress has also been made in democratization, so much so that a review of eu/burma trade relations was fully justified. i remain, however, vigilant about the development of respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law in this country.
in writing. we are witnessing great changes in burma and it is our duty to accompany the country on the path of openness and democratization. it still has a long way to go, but i am hopeful that the european union can help the country to make a just transition that will benefit the burmese people. the re-establishment of the generalised tariff preferences will be an important tool towards achieving this objective, as it will facilitate trade between burma and the european union, in particular by ensuring better access to the union market. it is an unlikely tool for myanmar's growth, and thus for the well-being of its people and the creation of new jobs. but we must remain vigilant about the situation, particularly with regard to the very worrying issue of child labour.
in writing. the introduction of the generalised system of preferences is a relevant initiative to help developing countries. first, it allows them to reduce poverty by generating income through international trade through tariff preferences applied to products they export to the european union. since burma now appears to respect the fundamental rights of workers, it seems essential to support this text with a view to restoring this system of tariff preferences so that the european union can contribute to the economic and social development of this partner.
in writing. as a member of the droi subcommittee, i voted against this text because the democratic transition process underway in burma remains fragmented and fragile. despite the undeniable progress in democratization, it seems to me risky to write a blank check to the burmese leaders who have not yet released all the prisoners and who impose various restrictions on those who have been released (deprivation of passports, etc.). in addition, the burmese authorities still refuse to grant burmese citizenship to the rohingya, the most discriminated minority in the world, stateless, deprived of most of the rights granted to the other 135 ethnic groups (citizenship act, 1982). according to some observers, humanitarian aid is being denied access to rohingya camps in rakhine state. ngos do not hesitate to accuse the authorities of complicity in ethnic cleansing and denounce the practices of the nasaka, the border police, which acts with impunity. for example, dr. tun aung, a respected figure in the rohingya community, has been imprisoned since june 11, 2012, during inter-communal violence in maungdaw. he is now being held in solitary confinement, unable to receive visitors or make a telephone call.
in writing. i supported the report calling for the re-establishment of the benefit of the generalized tariff preferences in myanmar. this policy of the european union aims to contribute to the development of developing and poor countries by offering them preferential access to our internal market. in practice, countries benefiting from this measure pay less customs duty on all or part of the goods they sell to the union. however, as was the case for myanmar in 1997, the union may decide to terminate this preferential treatment in the event of serious and repeated violations of the fundamental principles laid down in international conventions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. however, we remain vigilant about the progress of these reforms and their actual implementation, as the political situation remains fragile.
in writing. this report proposes to re-establish the system of generalised tariff preferences with burma. it is based on the few advances, largely cosmetic, made by the burmese regime in the field of human rights. the double standard imposed on cuba, where no ethnic extermination is taking place, where the shameless exploitation of workers is not a law, and where children are educated and not conscripted into the army, is blatant. free trade and energy resources are not worth more to me than the lives of my fellow men. i therefore vote against this report and denounce it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which follows the european commission's proposal for a regulation to return myanmar to the generalised system of preferences (gsp) after many reforms have been put in place following the opening up of the burmese regime. the granting of the gsp is primarily a measure to encourage the continuation of the transition process so that the burmese people can benefit from the political reforms under way.
in writing. the european union is now considering restoring the benefit of the generalised tariff preferences to burma, which were abolished in 1997 because of forced labour in the country. i think it is unacceptable to lift the sanctions against burma when there is a real massacre of the muslim minorities. instead of reminding burma of its commitment to its core values, the european union is only encouraging, through its silence and therefore its tacit approval, this ethnic cleansing of the muslim minorities. i believe that the union must be uncompromising in respecting human rights and that it is imperative that it shows consistency between the values it defends and the trade agreements it concludes with third countries. i therefore want sanctions to be imposed on burma, and i shall therefore vote against this report.
in writing. suspending economic benefits to encourage a state to follow the path of democracy is a common practice and often successful. burma is a good example of this. the european union had chosen to temporarily suspend the benefit of generalised preferences against it in 1997 because of the widespread practices of forced labour. it is clear that this tactic has borne fruit: democratization is underway in myanmar, although efforts are still needed. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not affected by the crisis. this is especially so as the measure will promote myanmar's exports in the textile sector. we know from experience that economic development is conducive to democratic progress.
in writing. following repeated human rights violations, burma has not been granted preferential rights under the eu's generalised system of preferences since 1997. noting its steady progress, the european commission has proposed to re-allocate these preferences to the country, provided that it continues to make progress. i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation because it is a good political signal and a relevant practical application of the 'more for more' rule which has governed the european union's external action for the past two years. i will, however, remain vigilant about the strict application of this principle: if further violations are found, i will call on the european commission to reopen a procedure for suspending preferences.
in writing. the report supports the reinstatement of trade preferences for developing countries in burma. the country has been ruled by a military junta since 1962 and is one of the most repressive regimes in the world. however, it was not until 1997 that the european union decided to abolish its preferences. the european commission considers that the legal conditions are now in place for these preferences to be reinstated. despite some democratic openings that allowed aung san suu kyi and some of her friends to enter the burmese parliament, this is doubtful. human rights remain largely violated in the country as evidenced by the persecution of minorities, particularly the rohingya, and the persistence of forced labour; the reality is that the eu and its member states want to regain access to the country's resources without neglecting the geopolitical aspect of china's strategic position as a major neighbour. i therefore voted against this report and the parallel resolution on tariff preferences.
in writing. the proposal on investor-state dispute settlement specifies who would bear the financial responsibility when compensation is due: the financial responsibility for the cost of settling the investor-state dispute and the right to defend a case are shared between the eu and the member states according to whose actions led the investor to file a claim. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the eu now has competence to conclude investment agreements. although no agreement has been reached at present, discussions with canada provide for the possibility for an investor to lodge a claim against a state. i voted in favour of this report because it clarifies the responsibilities of the member states and the eu in terms of financial responsibility when compensation is due. a mechanism will be put in place whereby the financial responsibility for the costs of settling the dispute will be borne by the party whose actions prompted the investor to file a claim.
in writing. this text is an essential element in the construction of a genuine common european trade policy, as it provides a clear framework for dealing with the issues of financial responsibility arising from the settlement of disputes between investors and states. the stability and predictability of the legal framework in this area are crucial. that is why i support this text, because it will provide the security needed to make international investments, which are essential drivers of growth in europe and the world.
in writing. in view of the increasing number of foreign direct investments and their importance for economic growth in europe, i felt it was essential to vote in favour of this text, which provides the legal clarification needed for the effective and fair settlement of disputes between investors and member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework on financial liability in relation to investor-state dispute settlement tribunals established by international agreements to which the european union is a party. in the context of foreign direct investment, which has been the union's competence since the lisbon treaty, disputes may arise when a state fails to comply with the agreement and financial sanctions may result. the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to establish a legal framework at european union level to define, in the event of a dispute between two states, when responsibility falls on a member state on the one hand or on the european union on the other, by virtue of the law it imposes.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the non-commercial movement of pet animals, which aims to facilitate the movement of pet owners with their animals and to maintain a high level of public and animal health.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to facilitate the transport of pet animals in europe while ensuring a high level of protection of public and animal health. a key point in this report is the possibility for the commission to take action in the event of a resurgence of rabies, which is currently eradicated in europe, in order to protect the health of european citizens.
in writing. non-commercial movements of pet animals have been hampered by an inadequate transitional regime. after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, it was necessary to amend this system by improving the procedures for identifying animals and making the regulations more readable for veterinarians, owners and authorities. the report also calls for the introduction of a european animal health code, which would make it easier to travel with a pet while still complying with the health requirements.
in writing. the movement of pets was regulated in 1983; it was adopted at a time when the european union was embarking on a campaign against rabies. as the disease was not completely eradicated, a special transitory regime for the movement of pets was necessary. but the rage is no longer a threat. that is why i have voted in favour of this text, which seeks to bring the existing legislation into line with the present situation. it is therefore appropriate to facilitate the movement of pet owners and their animals, while maintaining a high level of public and animal health.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new legislation proposed by the council on the non-commercial movement of pet animals. we are adopting this text in order to simplify travel for users with pets while ensuring the safety of people through reliable health standards. in particular, the new legislation will impose rules on the identification and proof of vaccination of animals. these new rules for simplification and security are essential, given that one in four european households lives with a pet at home.
in writing. the changes introduced by the proposal for a directive amending directive 92/65/eec on animal health conditions governing trade in and imports into the union of dogs, cats and ferrets are mainly technical changes on which consensus has been reached. that is why i voted in favour of the report amending directive 92/65/eec on the health conditions governing trade in such products.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to facilitate the transport of pet animals in europe while ensuring a high level of protection of public and animal health. the main measure of this report is that veterinary checks on the health of the animal will be strengthened.
in writing. this text introduces technical amendments to ensure better protection of cats, dogs and ferrets during transport and details the procedures for clinical examination of these animals before shipment. the text will make it easier to transport your pet on the move, thanks to clearer, more accessible and easier to implement regulations.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on animal health conditions governing trade in dogs, cats and ferrets. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be allowed to apply the same rules to the transport and exchange of such animals. in particular, the draft proposes to extend the time limit for the health examination to 48 hours before the animal is transported, instead of 24 hours as is the case at present.
in writing. i voted in favour of changing the rules governing trade in and imports of domestic animals (dogs, cats, ferrets) into the european union because the new rules applying are more protective of animal welfare, simplify travel procedures for owners and respect the most basic health rules.
in writing. traveling with your pet across the eu is now relatively complicated, with owners facing administrative hassles. in europe, however, one in four households has a pet - including 64 million cats and 66 million dogs. it is therefore important to simplify the existing rules. that is the aim of this text, and i support it. currently, owners can only travel with more than five animals at a time - to prevent abuse for commercial purposes. now, an exemption is possible if the owners prove their participation in a competition, a fair, a sporting event or a festive occasion. another example: at present owners must ensure that their animals have been properly vaccinated against rabies. under the new rules, young animals aged 12 to 16 weeks who have been vaccinated but not yet immunised will be allowed to travel. in addition, the new legislation provides for clearer rules on pet passports and rabies vaccination. these amendments, when they come into force, will make it easier for citizens to travel across europe with their pets, and i welcome their adoption.
in writing. i voted in favour of the pet-related resolutions, even though one might ask once again what the eu is getting into. these two reports make it easier for pet owners to move pets, with the same rules in all member states, so it is rather a good thing for both animal welfare and public health reasons. the european union now has 72 million domestic animals and their movements are increasing. it is therefore necessary to ensure that these are supervised so that they take place in decent conditions and that the medical checks on the animals correspond to the recommendations of the world organisation for animal health. studies on animal welfare in commercial practices will also be carried out, as it is clear that animals cannot be treated as commodities. these two resolutions are therefore rather common sense texts, adopted by a very large majority.
in writing. economic integration brings efficiency and stability to all the economies of the member states making up the european union. given the efforts made by the commission for macroeconomic governance and the need to reform economic policies at the level of the european union and to coordinate the economic reform policies undertaken by national governments, i have spoken in favour of future legislative proposals for economic and monetary union.
in writing. i voted in favour of these proposals, which support the commission's work on the coordination of the economic policies of the member states. an incentive mechanism to strengthen solidarity, cohesion and competitiveness must go hand in hand with the adoption of new economic discipline measures. the commission has done a great deal in the field of competitiveness; the commission has now to include the tax evasion dimension, and social and employment issues.
in writing. in economic governance, priority must be given to implementing what has already been decided: i am talking here about the six pack, the two pack, and the whole framework that has already been set. the most important thing is to ensure that the important and rapid developments we are implementing are given the democratic oversight they deserve. the commission must broaden its view of competitiveness, to take account in particular of tax evasion issues, and recognize the european parliament's rightful place in the legislative process.
in writing. i supported the resolution in response to the commission's communications on economic and monetary union. in this text we reiterate our concerns: in particular, we must strengthen democratic control over the proposed tools. as it stands, decision-making processes are largely outside parliamentary control. secondly, the proposals made focus on competitiveness, minimising the risks of fraud and tax evasion, employment or social issues. since the outbreak of the economic and social crisis, many economic governance instruments have been put in place: we must ensure that they are fully implemented before we want to add new tools.
in writing. this text, which i voted in favour of, calls on the european commission to ensure full implementation of economic governance measures and to involve meps in transfers of sovereignty. the financial crisis has exposed fundamental weaknesses in the economic governance of the european union and the responses to this have been adopted in a hurry, without the involvement of the european parliament. the text is therefore in the right direction, but it is necessary to recall that the european parliament wants the commission's next initiatives in this area not to be limited to mere rigour but to be geared towards a strengthening of solidarity.
in writing. i voted in favour of the parliament's motion for a resolution on the future legislative proposals on economic and monetary union (emu). i support the reform of european economic governance, which aims in particular to improve cohesion and solidarity between the economic policies of the member states. the coordination of member states' reform programmes should make europe more competitive and more coherent. we also want to introduce democratic principles into the management of emu, such as strengthening the role of national parliaments and introducing democratic principles for decision-making.
in writing. this report endorses the fact that member states and/or the european union should bear the costs of arbitration when a foreign investor denounces a state or the eu, whatever the reason for the complaint. it even insists that if a european rule is not respected, the governments must bear the full costs. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the european union (the 'european investment bank') is based on the principle of the protection of the financial interests of the union by the european investment bank (eib) and the european investment bank (eib). it therefore supports the jurisdiction of the international centre for the settlement of investment disputes, the icsid, which it claims to have. this body is the proven tool for legitimizing the interests of multinational corporations against the sovereignty of states. i will never allow the interests of investors to be put before the interests of the people. legal stability for investors is only meaningful if it is not contrary to the public interest. i am voting against this text which advocates the opposite.
in writing. the tragic conflict in syria is already an indelible historical task, and we must grasp all its horrors. in addition to the endless list of mourners that continues to grow week by week, the syrians have no choice but to go into exile in an attempt to preserve their lives. at this level, the international community and the european union must mobilize and unconditionally engage in the great humanitarian struggle. it's the least we can do. the european union has valuable expertise in this area. the action of the european union in this area is welcome and it is therefore appropriate to continue our efforts to alleviate the terrible suffering of the syrian people.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which expresses the european union's deep concern at the crisis currently affecting syria and its repercussions on neighbouring states. beyond the political and humanitarian crisis in the country, the flight of syrians is weakening the entire region. with this vote, we have sent a strong message of support to the oppressed syrian people and called on the international community to redouble its efforts to provide a humanitarian response to the refugee crisis, including food, water and medicine.
in writing. europe must urgently mobilise to support the syrian people in their dramatic ordeal. the conflict poses a very significant risk of destabilising the region, and the flow of refugees to neighbouring countries places a heavy burden on the host countries. it is our moral duty to seek a swift solution to the conflict and to support those countries that are providing assistance to the syrian people. the text calls for major actions to mark the commitment of the entire international community.
in writing. after two years of civil war in syria, the international community faces a very serious humanitarian emergency that it is struggling to respond to. there are now 1.5 million refugees and the number is increasing every day, making it increasingly difficult for neighbouring countries to take them in. the unhcr now says it is unable to meet the needs and the breaking point has been reached, as the commission, the main donor, has just pointed out, having recently agreed to an additional €65 million in aid. without political action, the international community will not be able to contain the flow of refugees into neighbouring countries, which threatens the stability of the region. it is imperative that the eu and its member states act in two directions today. on the humanitarian front, the eu must step up its solidarity efforts and accept more syrian refugees. on the political front, we must support the current attempts to find a political and diplomatic solution to the conflict and affirm our firm support for the syrian opposition in order to shift the balance of power. the opposition forces will have to be legitimate in the eyes of all syrians to gain power.
we will continue to support the syrian people. after more than two years of conflict, tens of thousands of deaths and nearly two million refugees, the international community has still not succeeded in silencing the weapons. in order to ensure that the syrian situation does not fall into oblivion, i voted in favour of this resolution, which i was a co-signer of, calling for respect for human rights and humanitarian law in syria. as is always the case in conflicts around the world, the answer is not one. the european parliament reaffirmed the need for political and humanitarian action, and reminded the member states that these two actions were absolutely inseparable from ending the violence in that country.
in writing. parliament raised a new alarm on thursday over the situation of syrian refugees in neighbouring countries. in the face of a humanitarian situation that is deteriorating day by day, the european union must further strengthen its political, financial and logistical commitment in the region. we have, among other things, urged the european commission to present a comprehensive aid package, including increased humanitarian aid and the capacity and infrastructure of the host countries. the european union and in particular the european external action service must also facilitate a syrian-led political process. beyond action in the region, member states must also fully assume their responsibilities towards syrian refugees arriving on european territory. as parliament prepares to vote on the 'asylum package' soon, the european union could hardly justify the lottery of asylum to which syrian asylum seekers are still too often subjected.
in writing. i voted for the parliament's resolution on the situation of syrian refugees in neighbouring countries. the influx of refugees into the countries bordering syria is a major issue as reception capacities are being significantly reduced and human rights violations threaten the integrity of people. we therefore call for the opening of a humanitarian corridor to help the affected populations and to contain the spread of the conflict beyond the syrian borders. at the same time, parliament advocates a long-term solution by supporting a political process to resolve the conflict with the support of the international community.
in writing. in the last 24 months, the situation of the syrians has become unsustainable. according to some ngos, more than 94,000 people have already been killed in the conflict, while the number of wounded and refugees continues to rise. i voted in favour of this text, which recalls the importance of a political solution to the conflict and the urgency of ending the armed conflict and respecting human rights and humanitarian law in syria. the european union must act to prevent this civil war from spreading to neighbouring countries, in particular by helping these countries to manage the influx of refugees.
in writing. the fall of dictators in the arab spring countries has led to the freezing of their assets by the united nations in foreign countries. i voted in favour of this resolution which seeks to provide for a mechanism to recover stolen assets belonging to these countries. it is difficult to assess and trace these hidden assets, but it is even more difficult to ensure that these assets are returned to the country that is the rightful owner. in france, a large-scale campaign on "badly acquired assets" has been launched in recent years to uncover the hidden assets of foreign leaders. for example, the former tunisian president ben ali recently had nearly 12,000 properties confiscated, scattered throughout his country and across europe, including france. the important thing is to ensure that the money raised by the auction goes back to the coffers of the tunisian state to help with its reconstruction.
in writing. the recovery of assets frozen in the context of the arab spring uprisings must not become a brake on the recovery of these countries, and it should be ensured that it takes place in the most efficient and fairest possible way. the text therefore calls for a set of measures to reduce the complexity and length of recovery procedures, which can vary enormously from one country to another. the eu should encourage initiatives to improve transparency and pooling of efforts, which would allow us to actively show our support for the stabilisation of this region.
in writing. although i welcome the adoption of this resolution on asset repatriation, which calls for greater coordination between the arab spring countries, the european union and key international actors such as the world bank, which is mainly through the exchange of expertise and information on legal matters. i regret, however, that the amendments tabled by the greens/efa group in the negotiations with the other political groups were not included in the final compromise text because they asked the european external action service and the member states to temporarily suspend the repayment of the debt of these countries until an audit has been carried out to determine the illegitimate and odious part of it. in the face of an impatient population, these transitional governments, still very fragile politically and economically, must be able to count on the full support of europe. we must help them to repatriate these funds which have been misappropriated and finally return them to a population which is waiting for us to take concrete action.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for the arab spring countries in transition to recover assets. following the fall of several dictatorial regimes in north africa, including egypt, libya and tunisia, the european union froze the assets of the dictators, their families and those associated with these regimes. as these assets represent a significant economic asset, the return of these assets to the people and new governments of the arab spring should help the economic reconstruction of these still fragile states. this measure also has a strong symbolic aspect.
in writing. this resolution calls for the return of assets stolen by former leaders to countries that have gone through civil revolutions. the european right and the social democrats who have been so close to dictators are finally waking up. that's good. but the text ignores the root causes of the economic, social and political difficulties in the maghreb, mashrek and the middle east. he is silent on the eu's responsibility for these difficulties. it says nothing about the need to combat the debt which maintains the domination of finance over these states. he says not a word about the repression that is going on in some states. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. following the arab revolutions, the eu swiftly froze the assets of former dictators, their families and many people linked to these regimes, notably in egypt, tunisia and libya. it is important to clarify that while the freezing of assets is a matter for the union, the recovery and repatriation of such assets is a matter for the member states. the procedure for the recovery of assets is therefore complex and time-consuming. i supported this resolution for two reasons: firstly, the union must play a leading and coordinating role in the recovery procedure. new efforts are needed to facilitate restitution and member states need to work in close cooperation with the national authorities of the arab spring countries. these efforts will strengthen mutual trust between states and deepen relations with the societies of the region. secondly, because these assets, once recovered, will contribute to the success of the democratic transitions in the countries concerned. the success of these procedures will also determine the success of the establishment of strong and fair democracies.
in writing. i voted for this resolution calling for facilitating the recovery of assets looted by the former dictators of the arab revolutions from their peoples and frozen by eu member states in early 2011. the resolution, which is weak in relation to the issues at stake, does not acknowledge the responsibility of the eu and its member states for supporting these dictators until their fall. i regret that the amendments which i had tabled with my colleague willy meyer on behalf of the gue/ngl, in particular the requirement for an audit of the debt of these countries in order to extract the odious debt which benefited the dictators and their relatives, have all been rejected. however, the rapid return of these assets, which amount to millions or even billions of euros, even if it is a small amount, is absolutely imperative for tunisia, libya and egypt, which desperately need them to meet the social demands of their populations. it is also necessary that the member states provide themselves with the means, including judicial means, to release these assets and that the imf, the ecb and the eu do not impose on these countries structural reforms in parallel similar to those they are implementing in southern europe.

in writing. in consultation with my colleagues from modem, i abstained on this resolution expressing parliament's position on the proposed negotiation of a free trade agreement between the union and the united states. i am skeptical about this agreement, both in substance and in form, to say the least. my abstention is to acknowledge that negotiations are about to be opened on this subject, and we cannot deny that they are taking place. but the agreement is already questionable. let's stop trying to make people happy against their will. this agreement will be at the heart of the debate in the next european elections. in substance, we should be sure that the european commission, which has a mandate to negotiate, will defend our european model. in addition to the question of the cultural exception in parliament's text, the agreement should provide for the preservation of our agricultural model and environmental standards. it should explicitly exclude eu gmo legislation from its scope, just as it should not call into question the application of the precautionary principle. in form, it is a transversal agreement which potentially affects everyone. the ep is therefore entitled to demand the highest level of transparency.
in writing. a free trade agreement with the united states would allow an annual increase of 0.5% in gdp for the eu within 15 years. although an agreement with the united states is beneficial to the european economy, there are still sensitive sectors which deserve our full attention, starting with culture. i have spoken in favour of excluding cultural and audiovisual content services from the negotiating mandate, in order to protect and maintain a film and audiovisual industry in europe. in view of these factors, i have voted in favour of the final vote. it is now up to the council to vote on a balanced negotiating mandate.
in writing. the liberalisation of world trade is one of the keys to growth only if the conditions of competition are equal. it is in this spirit that we have been campaigning for agriculture, defence and culture to be given specific treatment in the new draft eu-us agreement. we therefore demand the complete opening of the american markets to all our products which are currently prohibited by federal or regional legislation, the application to american products of the health rules we impose on our producers and strict respect for our designations of origin. under these conditions, our producers will be able to benefit fully from the opening up of trade, while preserving the food security of europeans. the eu-us agreement can be beneficial for european economies. but for this europe must not hesitate to set its own conditions. meps have taken up their responsibilities to defend french and european interests, and we expect the government to have the courage to do the same in the council. social, health and environmental harmonisation must always come from the top. this is an imperative for europeans, and it is the major contribution europe can make to a balanced globalisation.
in writing. i support this resolution adopted by the european parliament on the mandate of the european commission for the negotiations on the transatlantic agreement with the united states. it is essential that such an agreement be concluded, given the economic challenges it poses, both in terms of exports and in terms of jobs. i welcome the exclusion of cultural and audiovisual services from the agreement, but i deeply regret the inclusion of defence procurement.
in writing. i voted against this resolution. while i welcome the exclusion of the audiovisual sector from the negotiations, i can only express concern at the mandate given today by the european parliament to the european executive to negotiate the eu/us free trade agreements, which are a real american takeover bid on the european union. from health and environmental regulations to the protection of personal data, public services, defence, gmos, etc., it is clear that we do not have the same requirements as the americans. and unlike the french right, which supported this resolution, i am not prepared to sacrifice the european project on the altar of free trade! moreover, with the maintenance of intellectual property rights in the negotiating mandate, netizens may fear a new acta. more generally, i think that commissioner de gucht and president barroso are launching a forced market negotiation one year after the end of the european commission's mandate.
in writing. the european parliament is sending a clear signal to the leaders on both sides of the atlantic today: yes, we want an ambitious and comprehensive agreement with the united states, but we refuse to broaden europeans' expectations in matters such as culture. the european parliament has the power to say no: the heads of state and government and the commission therefore have every interest in taking the result of this vote into account. the broad consensus on the protection of the cultural exception shows that the europeans will not compromise and that their expectations are clear. i will remain involved throughout the negotiations to ensure that all our expectations are taken into account, in particular to preserve the quality of european agriculture and products, to engage in better cooperation in the field of energy and more effective regulatory coordination.
in writing. as the eu prepares to negotiate an ambitious free trade agreement with the us, it is essential that the union is vigilant and firm in defending the interests of europeans vis-à-vis the americans, who will not fail to do so in turn. for it to remain a growth opportunity for both our economies, it is imperative that the future transatlantic partnership does not weaken european standards or call into question the european model of society. in addition to the audiovisual and cultural exceptions, which we are asking to be excluded from the negotiating mandate, the agreement must preserve our agriculture and in particular exclude gmos and cloning from the agreement, as well as our health and environmental rules. finally, as regards the form, the transatlantic negotiations will have to be conducted with the greatest possible transparency if the european commission does not want to repeat the failure of the acta agreement on counterfeiting which our european parliament rejected. obviously, the us congress will play an influential role in these negotiations to defend the interests of its country in a strong and offensive way. the european democracies, the european parliament and national parliaments, must therefore also address this issue and be involved at all stages of the negotiation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which approves the negotiating mandate given to the european commission for the free trade agreement between the union and the united states on trade and investment. this agreement will have extremely positive consequences for the european economy and for political and economic relations with the united states. however, this agreement must not be achieved at any cost! because of their characteristics, certain sectors cannot be the subject of a free trade policy with the united states. that is why i voted to exclude the audiovisual and film services and defence from the scope of this agreement. i actually co-signed an amendment to exclude the defense.
in writing. the transatlantic agreement does not call for urgency or absolute necessity. except perhaps for mr barroso's hopes of a reward that would be in the sights of the secretariat-general of nato or the un. the issue in this agreement is the submission of europe, the maintenance of us global leadership against china and the primacy of trade law over all others. the united states, like the commission, is calling for a comprehensive negotiation, without exclusion a priori. everything will be negotiable, especially on the european side, starting with the precautionary principles and the protection of personal data, our standards, including food and health standards, our power to legislate, whether there is a mechanism for settling investor/state disputes allowing multinationals to challenge our laws, our public procurement and public services and even our cultural exception. on the american side, the government cannot commit itself to the federal states on many points. the deal will be unbalanced, to our detriment. the european citizens must take up the matter and we will help them to do so. if there are negotiations, this agreement must become a "dracula" agreement, which, like him, is dying to be exposed. he will die in the indignation of the people and their revolt against the dictatorship of the so-called elite.
in writing. i voted against this resolution which calls for the opening of negotiations on a free trade agreement with the united states. the transatlantic negotiations are aimed at creating one of the largest free trade areas in the world. customs tariffs between the two blocs are already very low, however. so the issue is not that. given the potentially hegemonic nature of this agreement, the real issue is our development model. these negotiations are a danger to multilateralism. the wto negotiations are deadlocked. transatlantic trade already accounts for one third of world trade. this strategy of bilateral agreement is therefore a response to multilateral blockages. and there is a strong chance that the outcome of the negotiations will affect the entire international community and set a new standard. negotiations are not democratic. the european parliament has nothing to say, it can only approve or reject the agreement. and the states give the european commission a mandate, without interfering afterwards. of course, civil society will not be involved.
in writing. i did not vote for this resolution, preferring to abstain rather than give the commission a blank cheque on a matter of such importance for our continent. if the united states is a historic and leading partner with whom we must have close ties, we must not sell our european model, and in particular our agricultural and cultural model, in the name of hypothetical growth points promised by the european commission. europe is in a deep economic crisis, but it is a mistake to think that the united states alone will help us to get out of the rut. it is up to europeans, together, to find the tools to do so. then it will be time to negotiate with the united states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this trade and investment agreement between the european union and the united states. this free trade agreement is expected to benefit many french and european industrial sectors. i am thinking in particular of the aviation industry or the agri-food industry, with, for example, the export of our wines to the american market. but the european union must, among other things, ensure that it does not compromise its high food standards. these strict criteria which guarantee european quality products to our consumers must not be sacrificed. the vote on this resolution also led to the exclusion of audiovisual services from the agreement. it's a great win. the full scope for national and european public policy in the audiovisual field must be preserved in order to ensure the capacity of the eu and its member states to regulate this sector in the future. it is about protecting and promoting cultural diversity. for this agreement, as for all the others that the european union will have to negotiate, i hope that social, health and environmental harmonization will always be done from the top.
in writing. i abstained on the resolution on the negotiations for a free trade agreement between the eu and the usa. in fact, in the current state of the negotiating mandate, many concerns remain about the protection of the rights of european consumers and citizens, whether in the areas of agri-foodstuffs, health, public services, or the protection of personal data. parliament has made clear the need to exclude the cultural and audiovisual sectors from the negotiating mandate, but i do not think that this is sufficient. vigilance will be required throughout the negotiation process, bearing in mind that parliament may reject the agreement if it considers it to be insufficiently protective.
in writing. the european parliament approved on thursday 23 may the launch of trade negotiations with the united states. this is a strong political signal to citizens, as a free trade agreement could help to revive the european economy and create millions of jobs. it is estimated that this agreement could generate 119.2 billion euros in profits per year and increase exports by 28%. i am particularly pleased with the determination of the french epp delegation, which was able to echo the concerns of the citizens and succeeded in imposing its red lines in the resolution. i am thinking of the exclusion of the cultural and audiovisual sectors but also of the emphasis on agriculture, which we will be particularly vigilant about. the work of our farmers and the quality of our products must not be sacrificed in favour of a less demanding agreement which would threaten our jobs, the quality of our agriculture, the values and principles we hold dear. i now hope that the member states will continue this dynamic and clearly include in the mandate to be given to the european commission the red lines which the european parliament, listening to the citizens, has rightly underlined.
in writing. as the european union is preparing to open negotiations with the united states with a view to adopting a free trade agreement, the european parliament, which cannot take part in the negotiations directly, nevertheless wished to give its position on them. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of consumers. this is the case for audiovisual services which were excluded from the negotiating mandate. but it is also the case with agriculture, and more particularly with regard to gmos, growth promoters, food decontamination treatments and cloning; the european standards in these matters are much more demanding than in the united states. the agricultural sector has not been excluded from the negotiating mandate and although i voted for this resolution, i am not entirely satisfied with it and will be watching closely the development of the forthcoming negotiations.
in writing. i voted in favour of parliament's text on the negotiations for a future free trade agreement between the european union and the united states. the agreement can open up new economic opportunities for a europe in crisis. as regards cultural and audiovisual services, i opposed the inclusion of this sector in the negotiating mandate to be given to the european commission for the coming years, and i welcome the broad support of parliament for the maintenance of the 'cultural exception'. it is a victory for the whole french delegation of the epp group, which has fought to protect european culture. the film and audiovisual industry is not an economic sector like any other, it is the bearer of european identity and should not be sold off to hollywood productions. we are also committed to defending european standards, such as geographical indications, health standards and the exclusion of gmos or cloning.
in writing. i have opposed the transatlantic market project, but not because i was anti-american. i am doing this with determination because voices must be raised, while an anti-democratic, ultra-liberal and anti-freedom project is being prepared (acta). far from being a power, far from being a desire to protect our economies and our citizens, the transatlantic market will expose us to even more savage competition for the sole benefit of ever more gigantic multinationals and ever more rapacious financial markets. the rejection of smart borders and smart safeguards in the european union is already wreaking havoc on our agriculture and industry; imagine what it will be like tomorrow when we extend this crazy principle to this vast expanse that is the united states of america. worse when we think of the strategic sector of defence which risks being absorbed by an american power more vigorous and sovereign than the disarmed europe our leaders have put in place. our nations must stop being left defenseless to the most savage globalization of this black hole of uncontrolled global finance, which will swallow up what is left of our agriculture, industry and services.
in writing. the draft trade and investment agreement with the united states is an economic, social and ecological mistake. it is contrary to the objective of relocating production. it will lead to further relocations to the detriment of the ecological and social quality of production. since us environmental and social standards are in most cases less stringent than those in europe, this will bring down all european regulations. the agreement would also put europe in a geopolitical impasse by prolonging the imperial dominance of the united states in economic and financial matters to the detriment of emerging countries.

in writing. i voted in favour of opening negotiations for a free trade agreement with the united states. according to the european commission, this agreement could increase the eu's gross domestic product by 0.5%. however, we wanted to draw our own red lines: culture, defence and agriculture (including the question of gmos and animal welfare standards) cannot be considered commodities like others. i would like to stress in particular the explicit exclusion of the audiovisual sector from the negotiations. we cannot liberalize this sector, or else we will be crushed by the hollywood compressor roller. the citizens want a europe which protects and safeguards their culture first and foremost.
in writing. i voted against the parliament's resolution on the european commission's negotiating mandate in the discussions for a free trade agreement with the united states. if we french socialists have achieved a significant victory by maintaining the cultural exception, too many elements remain questionable. we have not succeeded in excluding from the negotiations public services, social, environmental, health and food standards (e.g. gmos). these standards, known as collective preferences, cannot be traded because they protect citizens. i would add that with the removal of customs barriers the union would thus be depriving itself of part of its own resources. the european union is also expected to take a more active role in the negotiations on the new rules. an agreement with our american partners, yes. to push for the enlargement of the european union across the atlantic, no.
in writing. the negotiations for an eu-us trade and investment agreement are a great opportunity for our two regions, as it should help to exploit the full potential of economic cooperation. however, the french socialist delegation, in line with its government, agreed on a number of points which must be defended in the negotiations, or which must be excluded from them in the interests of preserving european interests. these include: the non-challengeing of society's choices in health, work, consumption and agriculture; the explicit exclusion of audiovisual services from the field of negotiation, as it is the guarantee of the protection of the cultural and linguistic diversity of the eu countries; the degree of protection of personal data, etc. all these are preconditions for the opening of negotiations. while i am pleased that a majority of members voted in favour of excluding cultural and audiovisual content services from the negotiating mandate, too many points remain unresolved (regulations on health, environmental standards and public procurement, etc.). i cannot therefore support this report.
in writing. it is the return of the great transatlantic market; the mandate is broad, to say the least: 'total abolition of customs duties on industrial and agricultural products' and 'the aim of achieving the highest levels of investment liberalisation'. the tone is set ! the resolution adopted by the european parliament is therefore intended to influence the negotiations which will take place at the next council of ministers, but not to block them. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's external borders are not blocked. we are firmly resolved, together with the gue/ngl members and in particular those from the left front, to oppose this draft agreement by all means. we voted for all the positive amendments, but we rejected the very principle of this agreement by voting against this resolution. there is no question of abandoning the european social and environmental standards, which are already badly broken, or public procurement to north american multinationals.

in writing. i strongly support this resolution, which calls on burma to continue the process of democratization that started with the release of aung san suu kyi in late 2010. the text of the resolution is balanced, balancing the progress already made and the challenges facing the country. i welcome the epp group's amendments, which have placed a strong emphasis on respect for the rule of law and democracy, whereas the original text was mainly focused on corporate social responsibility.

in writing. i supported the report calling for the re-establishment of the benefit of the generalized tariff preferences in myanmar. this policy of the european union aims to contribute to the development of developing and poor countries by offering them preferential access to our internal market. in practice, countries benefiting from this measure pay less customs duty on all or part of the goods they sell to the union. however, as was the case for myanmar in 1997, the union may decide to terminate this preferential treatment in the event of serious and repeated violations of the fundamental principles laid down in international conventions. in view of the significant number of reforms undertaken by the burmese government since 2011, parliament supported the reintroduction of trade preferences to encourage the country to move towards development and respect for human rights. however, we remain vigilant as to the progress of these reforms and their practical implementation, as the political situation remains fragile.
in writing. suspending economic benefits to encourage a state to follow the path of democracy is a common practice and often successful. burma is a good example of this. the european union had chosen to temporarily suspend the benefit of generalised preferences against it in 1997 because of the widespread practices of forced labour. it is clear that this tactic has borne fruit: democratization is underway in myanmar, although efforts are still needed. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not affected by the crisis. this is especially so as the measure will promote myanmar's exports in the textile sector. we know from experience that economic development is conducive to democratic progress.
in writing. the alpine region has its own specific characteristics, in terms of economic activity, agriculture and transport. it has to face particular environmental and energy challenges and overcome natural handicaps. i strongly support the establishment of a macro-regional strategy for the alps. this strategy, which has long been advocated by the rhône-alpes and paca regions and by the conference of the alpine regions, has today received the support of the european parliament in a joint resolution adopted by a very large majority. that's good news. social and territorial cohesion can only develop through the intertwining of territories and cooperation between the state and the regions. we must go beyond the 'alpine space' programme and provide these territories with a real strategy enabling them to act more effectively to ensure socioeconomic development and the preservation of their natural heritage.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the commission to prepare a strategy for the alps, as it has done for the baltic, the danube and soon for the atlantic arc. these strategies aim to coordinate funding and actions to meet the challenges of mobility, energy security and environmental protection, due to the structural complexities of this mountainous area. this strategy is based on the articulation of the region's various priorities, both those of the large cities and those of the remote mountainous areas.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which calls for the creation of a macro-regional strategy for the alpine regions. these countries, regardless of their status, face common environmental, economic, social or demographic problems. since these problems are not confined to a single 'national side' of the mountain range, it is appropriate to deepen existing crossborder cooperation to find solutions. it is not a question of creating a new level between the state and the region, or of reducing the prerogatives of the former. based on a shared will of the actors on the ground, the aim of such a strategy is really to bring all the stakeholders together to build concrete projects that improve the alpine economy and the daily lives of the inhabitants of this area.
in writing. the alpine regions contain unique resources and ecosystems which must not only be protected but also enhanced, taking into account their specificities. the establishment of a macro-regional strategy would make this possible, as has been done for the baltic sea and danube regions, for example. we expect the commission to present an action plan for the region which will make it possible to better coordinate european funding, particularly that of cohesion policy, to implement joint projects in order to better protect this unique environment and take account of its specific challenges.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution in favour of a macro-regional strategy for the alps. the concept of macro-region is well suited to the alpine area as it aims to define a large territorial area, beyond national and administrative borders, facing common realities, and relevant for the coherence of policies and projects according to an overall vision of territorial cooperation, in the service of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. as regards concrete examples of cooperation, i welcome the recent example of the joint initiative of the parco naturale delle alpi marittime (italy) and the mercantour national park (france), of which i was president. in addition, i attach the greatest importance to the alpine-mediterranean euroregion, which brings together five french and italian regions (provence-alpes-côte d'azur, liguria, piedmont, valle d'aosta and rhône-alpes) and which can act as a driving force within the alpine area. this euroregion is to be legally structured by the creation of a european grouping for territorial cooperation in order to strengthen franco-italian cooperation.
in writing. i do not see what more a macro-regional strategy for the alps could bring than the alpine convention. i think it might even hurt him. there is already an 'alpine area' funded by the union, and strangely enough alsace is part of it, which, it seems to me, is not in the heart of the alps! i have already had the opportunity to say in this chamber that the macro-regional fancy in vogue today is aimed at promoting short-circuiting at the national level. it also maintains the blurring not only of internal borders but also of external borders, since regions of non-eu countries are invited to participate. the blurring of the internal administrative boundaries of the member states is also to be added, since only parts of the regions could be selected because of certain specific features and not others. it even calls into question the borders of the continents: i seem to recall a report adopted here which proposed a mediterranean macro-region including north africa and the middle east. the icing on the cake: these macro-regions give the commission a role in cooperation which could very well do without them or which has done very well up to now.

in writing. the textile factory that collapsed earlier this month in bangladesh was mainly producing clothes for european and american brands. over 1,000 people were killed. it's the worst industrial disaster in this country. one official said that four huge generators were installed on the roof of the building in violation of all safety rules. that's the weight that caused the collapse. the mayor of savar was suspended for authorizing the construction. but is he the only one responsible? bangladesh is the third largest supplier of clothing to the european union. the member states which allow goods produced under these conditions to be sold on their territory are at best complicit in having turned a blind eye. an increase in the monthly wage of bangladeshi workers from 30 to 80 euros a month would cost european consumers 28 cents per garment. at the same time, the relocation of companies to countries such as bangladesh is creating unemployment in europe. in the face of this globalisation of exploitation, we propose ecological and social visas which tax goods produced in conditions of labour law violations. it is in the interest of all, europeans and bangladeshis.

in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution following the fires and the collapse of textile factories in bangladesh, which killed over 1000 people. in this resolution we call on the union and the member states to do everything possible to help improve working conditions in that country. the resolution also calls on the commission to draw up a report on the respect of the various conventions on human rights in bangladesh. european companies, for their part, must take responsibility and respect labour law obligations so that clothing produced in bangladesh ceases to be clothing paid for with blood.
in writing. in response to the tragic incidents in bangladesh on 24 april, meps drafted a resolution which received overwhelming support in plenary. i myself support this resolution, which calls on the bangladeshi authorities to act without delay to ensure that the factories in the country comply with international labour rights. it calls on multinationals to adhere fully to internationally recognised corporate social responsibility practices and the conventions of the international labour organisation, and to carry out in-depth investigations into the way their subsidiaries and supply chains operate. the european socialists also stressed the need to create a system of transnational judicial cooperation to facilitate access to justice for victims. we also call on the authorities to bring to justice those responsible for criminal negligence or criminal responsibility at any level for the collapse of the rana plaza building and the fire in the tazreen workshop.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on working conditions in bangladesh. the tragedy of the collapse of rana plaza, a building occupied by many textile workshops working for european and american brands, has brought to mind the deplorable working conditions for workers, especially female workers, in this country. it is urgent to put pressure on the bangladeshi government to prevent such disasters from happening again and to put an end to the irresponsibility of western policy makers. the fact that a number of major brands have refused to sign a legally binding commitment is a testament to the failure of the voluntary corporate social responsibility (csr) regime and the hypocrisy, if not cynicism, that prevails in this area. i therefore regret that the amendment tabled by the gue/ngl to establish a legally binding csr system has been rejected. this resolution, adopted by an overwhelming majority, seems to me to be a very weak declaration of good intentions in view of the issues at stake. it can nevertheless be a signal to the commission and the member states to finally take action with european companies operating abroad.
author. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the execution of mohammed afzal guru on saturday 9 february is a sign of an alarming and regressive trend towards the resumption of the death penalty in india. this is the second execution in three months in india after an eight-year hiatus. india thus finds itself in a counter-trend to the abolitionist trend observed in the rest of the world. in total, 140 countries, or more than two thirds of the world, are abolitionist in law or in practice. in 2011, only 21 countries applied this punishment, which means, ladies and gentlemen, that 90% of the states abstain from it. mohammed afzal guru was sentenced to death in december 2002 by a special court established under the prevention of terrorism act 2002. there are serious doubts about the fairness of his trial. he did not choose his lawyer, nor did he decide to be represented by a lawyer with adequate experience in the trial. it was the practice of the indian authorities to make publicly available information on the rejection of appeals for clemency and the dates of execution before any execution. this new approach of carrying out executions in secret is therefore particularly alarming. this parliamentary resolution recalls that we are opposed to the death penalty in all circumstances, without exception, whatever the nature or circumstances of the crime committed, whether the convicted person is guilty or innocent. we therefore call on the indian government and parliament to adopt a permanent moratorium on executions with a view to abolishing the death penalty as soon as possible.
