in writing. putting the consumer at the heart of our actions means making the citizen the driving force of a new europe. consumer spending represents 56% of the eu's gdp and therefore plays a key role in the eu's overall economy. consumption, under favourable and unhindered conditions, contributes to the growth of the european economy. the european parliament therefore wants to ensure that the conditions are met and the obstacles removed so that the citizen can buy and consume with confidence. the commission will therefore have to take care to inform consumers better of their rights, to eliminate cross-border litigation in the case of online purchases and to guarantee the right to appeal.
in writing. like the vast majority of my colleagues, i supported the garcés ramón report. the report, adopted by 586 votes to 52, with 9 abstentions, dealt with the shaping of a new european consumer policy aimed at stimulating demand and thus increasing growth. it focused in particular on consumer and professional safety and information, as well as on ensuring that consumers have a right to a remedy and that their rights are aligned with economic and social developments.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new agenda for european consumer policy. european consumers' spending in the single market accounts for 56% of eu gdp. the aim of this european policy is to strengthen consumer confidence and participation in the market. meps stressed that the eu should be able to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are protected from unfair competition and that the eu should be able to take action to protect consumers' rights. the new agenda therefore sets out a series of concrete measures to achieve these objectives.
in writing. the european consumer policy should be improved by 2020 to ensure consumer safety, to improve consumer and professional information and to ensure the availability of redress. i think it is particularly important to give consumers the tools they need to enforce their rights.
in writing. despite some common sense measures to promote the rights of european consumers to information and redress, this report is based on the socially devastating principles of european economic liberalism. these same principles (logic of increasing competition, forced productivism, absence of the precautionary principle, etc.) lead its authors to an intolerable contradiction: it asks europe to protect consumers from the harmful effects of competition, while asking the commission to increase competition. i cannot therefore approve this text, i am voting against.
in writing. i believe that there is a need for effective consumer protection within the european union to ensure a certain degree of consumer safety and effective judicial protection. however, this report, under the guise of establishing a set of initiatives in favour of consumers for the period 2014-2020, merely reduces consumers to economic actors in the internal market who can contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, without really caring about their interests. the desire to protect european consumers should be guided by the general interest rather than being a purely economic objective. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. i supported this report because european consumers play an active role in the growth of the union: their spending accounts for more than half of the eu's gdp. in order to continue to stimulate the european economy, it is therefore important to increase consumer confidence and protection, in particular for certain sensitive products and sectors such as nanotechnologies, genetically modified organisms, financial services and the digital sector. the new agenda is more specifically concerned with dangerous products, misleading advertising, unpredictable roaming charges and illegal online practices. it will increase consumer awareness and improve consumer knowledge, safety and rights. but to achieve these objectives, collaboration between consumer associations and public institutions will be needed more than ever.
in writing. i voted against the resolution on european consumer policy. the report was a good initiative in the beginning. it gave priority to the need to protect the rights of citizens who are consumers. these were considered citizens before they were mere consumers. the text was even critical of the commission's european consumer agenda. it is regrettable that the epp and alde groups have rejected the compromise amendments and have completely changed the priorities of this report: in particular, all the references to 'social europe' have been deleted. the text also contains the fallacious argument that the deepening of competition and the internal market will improve the situation of consumers under the guise of a 'social single market'. the balance sheet of liberalization and privatization, particularly in transport and energy, shows us the consequences of the dogma of the law of the market alone. the text does not therefore protect the rights of citizens who are consumers. i have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. the european consumer policy protects us every day by banning misleading advertising and ensuring that prices and information about our food are transparent. beyond the requirements it seems to impose on economic operators, it actually establishes the conditions for confidence between consumers and businesses, which is essential for the development of commercial activities. and it is precisely because it is an essential condition for growth that i have supported this report by making an inventory of the improvements we can make to it. the horse meat crisis has highlighted the need for improved traceability of products in order to identify responsibility immediately and to avoid any further health scandals. the financial crisis has also exposed the glaring lack of transparency on products sold by financial institutions, which have sold off consumer rights to enrich themselves. in both areas, i am sure we will be able to prevent fraud better and to provide consumers with more effective and protective remedies. the eu will be judged on the progress it makes!
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by my epp colleague tadeusz zwiefka which aims to improve access to justice in cross-border cases. it is necessary to approximate our laws, for example, on legal aid, so that everyone can be defended in crossborder disputes, regardless of their income level.
in writing. all member states have a system which allows persons who do not have sufficient resources to afford a lawyer to be represented before the courts (in france this is called the "avocat commis d'office"). however, the application of the system is not the same in all eu countries, which leads to complications in the event of crossborder disputes. the report also calls for the establishment of a european network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment and for the protection of the environment. finally, to remedy the lack of awareness of the directive, the report proposes tools for communicating the existence of legal aid in the event of a crossborder dispute.
in writing. i voted in favour of the evaluation of the directive on access to justice in crossborder cases. all member states have a system of legal aid for persons without sufficient resources. the provisions differ in all member states, which makes it difficult to access justice in crossborder disputes. the report aims to raise awareness of the existence of legal aid so that the directive is no longer widely unknown.
in writing. to enable european citizens to exercise all their rights fully, effective access to justice must be guaranteed, particularly in the case of crossborder disputes. i therefore support the ambition of making legal aid more accessible, as do all the measures aimed at informing citizens better of their rights.
in writing. while european legislation to improve access to justice in crossborder civil and commercial disputes is a step in the right direction, its implementation in the member states still needs to be improved. the harmonization of the criteria for assessing applicants for legal aid is one of the first objectives to be achieved. it will enable the persons liable to obtain a more consistent response from the authorities responsible for assessing their resources. it would therefore be useful if the requesting authority could issue a certificate attesting to the applicant's eligibility for legal aid recognised in all the member states of the union. in order to ensure better access to justice, financial assistance should also be more comprehensive and cover travel costs from the beginning of the proceedings, i.e. also for attending the hearing before the judge responsible for deciding on the possible granting of legal aid. it should of course be remembered that these improvements to help the offenders must be brought to the attention of the public and the legal profession. this is the necessary guarantee of their usefulness.
in writing. free movement within the territories of the member states is a right of every citizen and an essential condition for the functioning of the internal market. in order to guarantee respect for this right, it is essential that european citizens, and in particular the least well-off, have the possibility of accessing justice in another member state. this legislation already exists, but its application remains very uneven between member states. the european union needed to improve the current legislation so that all european citizens, regardless of their member state, could benefit from crossborder legal aid. that is why i supported this text.
in writing. since the explosion of online commerce, cross-border litigation has increased. however, while all member states have systems of legal support and advice for those who cannot afford it, these vary widely from one member state to another. however, with the crisis, citizens tend to look for cheaper consumer products on the internet, which is not necessarily accompanied by sufficient legal guarantees. access to legal aid exists, but too often this possibility is not recognised. this is why the first step in improving access to legal aid is better information and awareness among citizens. that is what this report proposes, and that is what i support.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague, mr tdeusz zwiefka, in the plenary session of 11 june. this report deals with the application of directive 2003/8/ec on access to justice in crossborder cases. this directive was largely unrecognised and the report proposes a range of measures to improve awareness of the existence of legal aid in crossborder litigation. the report also provides a series of improvements to make this aid an effective tool. i am glad that parliament has adopted it.
in writing. i supported the report on improving legal aid in crossborder civil and commercial litigation. the aim of the project is to raise awareness among european citizens of the right of access to foreign courts in cross-border litigation. we also want to improve access to this right by improving the language training of lawyers and by promoting the appointment of practitioners with competence in crossborder cases.
in writing. the zwiefka report makes some interesting points, including better information for european citizens on their rights, easier access to legal forms and the establishment of specific training for legal professionals funded by the eu. it also focuses on the most vulnerable groups and proposes solutions to the problems of random definitions of cases for aid. i vote for it.
in writing. very few citizens and professionals in the european union are aware of the rights conferred on them by directive 2003/8/ec on access to justice in crossborder cases. according to the european commission, only 12% of europeans were aware of legal aid in a cross-border context, which is still very low given the volume of cross-border trade within the eu. there is an urgent need to inform or remind citizens of their right to legal aid in crossborder civil and commercial disputes. an effective information campaign launched throughout the european union is therefore necessary. moreover, it is a question of making this legal aid effective. the creation of a specific database will make it possible to identify legal practitioners competent for cross-border litigation; the commission will also be able to provide legal aid to the victims of the crime. these guidelines, which are set out in the report, are in the right direction and that is why i voted in favour of them.
in writing. as a frontier resident, i voted in favour of this report which proposes improvements to the 2003 directive on legal aid in cross-border disputes. unfortunately, the main problem with this directive is that it is not widely recognised. according to the commission, only 12% of citizens were aware of the existence of legal aid for crossborder disputes. if citizens are not informed, how can they benefit from this right when they are confronted with the situation? the improvements requested are aimed at simplifying judicial procedures and inviting the member states and the commission to launch an effective information campaign to ensure appropriate legal support. the report calls for the creation of databases of crossborder legal practitioners and the establishment of a single authority responsible for crossborder legal aid. finally, the report calls for the possibility for citizens to claim legal aid either in the member state of residence or in the member state where the aid is needed.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which establishes procedures enabling customs authorities to prevent the movement of goods which could infringe intellectual property rights. i believe that it is necessary to take all the measures that can facilitate the work of our customs officers to ensure that intellectual property is respected in europe. the report provides for a simplified procedure for all infringements of intellectual property rights.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which aims to modernise customs procedures to monitor the respect of intellectual property rights. procedures will be simplified, particularly in the case of small consignments of suspected counterfeit goods, which can now be destroyed without the intervention of the right holders. the aim of this report is to modernise and simplify controls on counterfeit and pirated goods, in order to improve trade in the internal market.
in writing. counterfeiting is a threat to our businesses, but also to europeans: using a counterfeit product can be a threat to our health or safety. that is why i support this text, which will improve the rules for intercepting and destroying counterfeit goods that try to enter the eu. a simplified procedure will enable customs authorities to act more quickly and efficiently.

in writing. i voted in favour of parliament's new rules on the control by customs authorities of the respect of intellectual property rights. the counterfeit products that reach european soil are both a threat to the health of european consumers and a significant loss of profit for our companies. customs authorities will now have simplified rules for the destruction of illegal goods in a shorter time. innovation and intellectual property are engines of growth in europe that we must protect.
in writing. counterfeiting costs european businesses more than eur 250 billion a year and poses a serious threat to the health and safety of consumers. in 2009 alone, customs authorities intercepted more than 40,000 suspicious packages representing 118 million items. in order to combat this phenomenon, which now extends beyond luxury goods, fashion, music and films, the commission must ensure that these counterfeits are stopped as they enter the european union. i supported the rapporteur's proposal on the council's position at first reading because it recognises that customs authorities have a privileged role in the fight against counterfeiting and piracy, but also because it aims to cover small packages of counterfeit goods sent by post, the overwhelming majority of which are the result of transactions carried out over the internet.
in writing. i welcome this vote which strengthens the capacity of customs officers to intercept counterfeit goods at the eu's doorstep. cigarettes, household products and toys are all counterfeit consumer goods which are illegally distributed by the millions in the eu every year and which, by exceeding our health standards, threaten the health of european citizens. these illegal copies, which come mainly from third countries, constitute unfair competition which is unfavourable to our companies and destroys thousands of jobs in europe. in a fragile economic environment, efforts must be stepped up to combat this phenomenon and protect honest european workers. one of the most effective ways of doing this is to rely on customs agents, who are ideally placed to seize and destroy counterfeit goods. we must also negotiate an agreement with our trading partners, where counterfeiting is particularly widespread, to combat this scourge more effectively. i regret that passion has outweighed reason when acta was voted on. it is the right instrument to protect us against counterfeiting and its harmful effects.

in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation which aims to provide better controls on food intended for vulnerable populations. it is extremely dangerous for both the consumer and the control authorities to distinguish between food intended for everyday consumption and food intended for target groups. we are talking about infants, people who need low-calorie diets, diabetics and gluten intolerant people, the so-called celiacs, who are increasingly numerous: 1 in 100 people in the union. all these categories of people are not ordinary consumers. the regulation imposes, for example, strict compositional criteria, mandatory labelling or precautions for use for these vulnerable populations. the labelling and presentation of these foods will be more precise, clear and easy to understand for consumers.

in writing. the european union has from the outset sought to establish food safety within the european territory, including rules on product labelling to inform and protect consumers. however, consumers such as infants, young children or seriously ill persons are not normal consumers and must therefore benefit from specific regulation. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which lays down stricter rules on composition and labelling and makes it easier to distinguish between foodstuffs for everyday consumption and those intended for specific groups.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on rules on the labelling and content of infant formulae and other foods for special medical purposes. in order to better protect consumers, and in particular certain vulnerable groups such as infants and the sick, parliament wanted to strengthen the quality of specific food products and their labelling in order to distinguish them better from other products.
in writing. the council text introduces some improvements compared with the commission text: the delegation of power to the commission is limited to five years (unlimited in the original text) and the member states are given the possibility of maintaining national rules on food purity that are stricter than those of the eu (article 15 (5)). however, it does not call into question the general logic of the principle, which is to base food safety and food quality criteria on the 'functioning of the internal market' and the non-distortion of competition. once again, the market is being promoted at the expense of human health and food security. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by my colleague from the french epp delegation, elisabeth morin-chartier. the text now requires employers to protect their employees against the risks of electric, magnetic and electromagnetic fields by setting limits on workers' exposure to these fields and by minimising or eliminating the identified risks. the text also provides for appropriate medical surveillance so that exposed workers can be treated promptly in the event of a problem being identified.
in writing. the report sets maximum exposure values - values which are determined on the basis of the impact on health and biological considerations - for workers to electric, magnetic and electromagnetic fields. it also specifies the obligations of employers, appropriate medical surveillance and specific information and training for workers on risk management. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of a text which balances the protection of the health of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields with the use of electromagnetic fields when they are beneficial, thanks to the hard work of my colleague elisabeth morin chartier. in fact, in a number of cases, their use is necessary for european citizens, particularly in medical matters. this directive protects the health of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields in all sectors of activity. we have also made arrangements for all workers to be informed and trained on the dangers of electromagnetic fields. finally, we have set up medical surveillance of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields. we also helped to define the harmful effects of exposure to electromagnetic fields on workers, in particular by calling for greater consideration of risk groups and, in particular, pregnant women.
in writing. with these new rules, we are giving ourselves the means to protect the health and safety of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields. the exposure values are revised, and we increase the responsibility of the employer, who must better assess these risks and take appropriate measures to reduce them. at the same time, we do not jeopardise the use of certain technologies, such as magnetic resonance imaging (mri) or military applications.
in writing. according to who studies, prolonged exposure to electromagnetic fields can be harmful to health. at the same time, there is no denying the tremendous progress in medicine through the use of these electromagnetic fields to make diagnoses. a balance must therefore be struck between more effective protection of workers' health with a more stringent system of exposure limit values and the possibility of derogations, particularly for the medical and military sectors. the long-term health effects of electromagnetic fields are still poorly understood, even though they are increasingly used in everyday life. the commission will be responsible for monitoring scientific progress on the subject and adapting european legislation accordingly. it's a precautionary principle at its best.
in writing. this text guarantees greater protection for workers who are exposed to electromagnetic fields in the course of their work. the health of people who use, for example, high-frequency welding machines or induction furnaces in their work is threatened every day. that is why the european parliament had to propose a text to prevent the risks associated with exposure to these electromagnetic fields. employers will now have to respect this legislation and take responsibility for the best possible protection of their employees.
in writing. i voted against the report by ump mep elisabeth morin-chartier on the safety of workers exposed to electromagnetic waves. the report leaves the door open to derogations concerning the level of protection of workers. if the report provides for sensory effects exposure limit values, these may be exceeded 'where justified by practice or treatment'. it's hard to find a more extensive exemption. this leaves employers far too much room for manoeuvre to ensure that the directive actually benefits employees. this agreement goes far beyond what the mri alliance wanted to achieve (medical sector waiver), now offering a large number of industry-wide waivers at the national level if a member state wishes to use them. this report is a missed opportunity to improve the protection of workers, once again the interests of large companies have prevailed in a european parliament, for the moment, with a right-wing majority.
in writing. we adopted the report on the protection of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields by a large majority, with 594 votes in favour, 40 against and 28 abstentions. as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on energy, research and technology, i welcome these results. the old 2004 directive needed to be revised urgently. the limit values for exposure to electromagnetic fields would have limited the use of mri. yet, it is a vital tool in the diagnosis and treatment of many diseases. the medical community will now have an exemption from the exposure limit values for the use of mri. through this exemption, the report takes a balanced approach which will ensure a high level of protection for workers and support european research.
in writing. electromagnetic fields can have a negative impact on the health of citizens, which is why it is necessary to protect workers who are particularly exposed to them effectively. nevertheless, their use is becoming indispensable in certain fields, such as medicine and the military. i therefore voted for this text because it strikes a perfect balance between the worker's exposure and the need to use physical agents. it provides for limits on exposure to electromagnetic fields in accordance with international standards, while allowing a certain degree of flexibility for the sectors which use them.
in writing. on tuesday i supported the report on the safety and health requirements for workers' exposure to risks from physical agents. the parliament is thus seeking to improve the protection of workers by establishing strict safety limits and procedures for exposure to electromagnetic fields. in addition, the magnetic resonance imaging (mri) technique used in hospitals for medical purposes was exempted from these common rules. given the importance of mri in the diagnosis and treatment of many diseases on the one hand, and the many safety procedures put in place by hospital members on the other, we considered it legitimate to exclude mri from the scope of this text.
in writing. the text adopted strikes a good balance between improving the protection of workers from electromagnetic fields and their use in the military or health field. employers are required to assess and reduce risks by, for example, choosing equipment.
in writing. workers' exposure to electromagnetic fields is a major occupational and public health issue. however, after 10 years of negotiations, the standardisation was suspended and a new document was discussed without consulting the esc. it is understandable that relaxation of the rules for the use of mri for medical purposes is necessary and the parliament's report specifies the conditions under which a derogation is possible, but not to the extent of lowering the previous standards. on the other hand, there is no reason why nato should benefit from a special regime, which is a derogation from european common law. this privilege granted to north american military imperatives in europe is intolerable. i cannot vote for a text which provides for such a derogation. i vote against it.
in writing. electromagnetic fields can have various effects on the body: skin reactions, discomfort, visual disturbances, etc. some workers are particularly exposed to it, which can put their health at risk. therefore, it is necessary to protect them particularly against excessive exposure to electromagnetic fields. i supported the agreement reached with the council on new rules to protect european workers exposed to electromagnetic fields more effectively. the new provisions, incorporating the new international limits, apply to all sectors of activity but more specifically to workers exposed to high risk, such as those working in the steel industry, or to persons working long hours in the vicinity of television and radio broadcasting installations and radar installations. some flexibility is provided for the military and medical imaging (mri) sectors. employers are obliged to assess and reduce the risks faced by workers. i welcome the adoption of these new rules, which i believe are balanced and ensure a high level of protection for workers at risk. i call on the council of ministers to formally adopt this agreement as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague elisabeth morin-chartier which sets minimum safety and health standards for workers exposed to electromagnetic fields. the proposal introduces a distinction between exposure in the low frequency range (0 hz to 100 khz) and exposure in the high frequency range. these new rules apply to all sectors of activity and in particular to workers exposed to high risks, such as those in the steel industry or radar installations. the directive replaces a 2004 text that could never be implemented because of its rigidity on mri (magnetic resonance imaging) which, despite their high emissions, are essential to modern medicine.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which 'proposes a guide for more effective european and national legislation on the fight against organised crime, corruption and money laundering'. these illegal and criminal activities benefit from the erasure of borders within the european union, and a strong, coherent and coordinated response is absolutely necessary to combat these scourges. the text certainly provides answers to these criminal activities by proposing, for example, a common definition of organised crime.
in writing. the report identifies the priorities that will form the basis for the development of the roadmap to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the fight against crime is all the more difficult now that it is transfrontier, which requires coordinated police and judicial action by the states and the harmonization of their legislation. the report also stresses that more flexible and accountable public administration, faster and more credible criminal justice, and more transparent banking and business systems would help fight corruption and send a positive signal to european citizens. in view of the points made in the report, i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to strengthen crossborder judicial and police cooperation in eu countries, but also with third countries, in order to protect the eu's financial interests against organised crime, corruption and money laundering. we have agreed on a definition of the crime of participation in a mafia-type organisation and the abolition of banking secrecy, with the aim of depriving criminal organisations of their financial resources.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the mid-term report of the crim special committee on organised crime, money laundering and transparency. for the first time, the european parliament is tackling these vital problems, both economically and democratically. in concrete terms, by proposing a common definition of mafia-type criminal activity, we will be able to combat it better. the creation of a 'european public prosecutor's office for the protection of the eu's financial interests' is another relevant means to this end. simplifying the rules on confiscation of criminal assets will also cut the grass under the feet of outlaws. the report also proposes that anyone convicted of corruption, money laundering or any other serious offence against public authorities should be excluded from any tendering procedure in the union. i therefore welcome these strong proposals, which would have a real impact on the lives of european citizens.
in writing. organized crime is changing, and our responses must change just as quickly. this is a huge challenge and i welcome the work of the special committee on this. i support the idea that a more effective fight against crossborder crime requires first and foremost a harmonious, more coherent and clearer legal framework to develop our common action. i particularly support the inclusion in this text of the importance of satellite imagery in the fight against organised crime.
in writing. the income from international criminal activities represents 3.6% of global gdp, while corruption in eu member states amounts to 1% of eu gdp, the equivalent of the european budget. this international organised crime, which covers a wide range of activities, such as drug trafficking, human exploitation, corruption and money laundering, is a complex reality which requires a concerted and comprehensive strategy by the union and the member states. firstly, it is vital to improve transparency, in particular through increased cooperation between the judicial and police authorities of the member states and the community agencies, as well as with the authorities of the third countries involved. secondly, we must put an end to the banking secrecy that enables some organizations to launder money from their criminal activities. finally, deterrent sanctions must be applied to those responsible for these crimes, both in terms of criminal sentences and the amount of fines, and states must be encouraged to develop effective legal instruments to enforce them. the harmonization of sentences at community level and greater cooperation between the prison systems of the member states will make it possible to offer a higher and fairer level of protection to citizens throughout the european territory.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it will allow for better cooperation between member states in the fight against organised crime. it is important to act now to ensure that mafia organizations gain ground in southern europe and create a climate of terror. in practice, the text proposes to strengthen police cooperation and to give greater support to new technologies. the implementation of the report will make our citizens live in greater security.
in writing. not everything in mr iacolino's report is bad, particularly the strengthening of police and judicial cooperation and the proposal to hit criminals in the pocket by systematically seizing their assets. but there are also some surprising things: fighting illegal immigration by relaxing immigration rules, or demanding deterrent sanctions... which would leave the bulk of the alternative sentences to imprisonment. and as always when the european union's policies have had negative consequences or are a clear failure, we need more europe: a harmonization of criminal law and procedure in defiance of national judicial traditions, a unification of prison policy, the creation of a european prosecutor's office, a european fbi, a european intelligence service... finally, it is a pity that mr iacolino has not drawn any conclusions from his lucid observation: organised crime has taken full advantage of the abolition of internal frontiers and globalisation, in particular the free movement of capital which facilitates money laundering. he's not proposing anything against it. i therefore abstained on that text.
in writing. organised crime, corruption and money laundering threaten the eu's economy, democracy and the lives of eu citizens and those in developing countries. i abstained on this report because, although the crim committee's text clearly highlights the links between organised crime and tax havens, and the need to set up registers of lobbies, which is a very useful instrument for transparency, the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. it does not provide a convincing answer to the challenges of organised crime, corruption and money laundering. we cannot oversimplify the various threats and recommend an approach based solely on repression and surveillance.
in writing. organised crime, corruption and money laundering in the european union are plagues that are eating away at europe, along with violence, insecurity, etc. in order to put a stop to these phenomena, parliament has for the first time expressed its opinion on these matters by adopting the interim report of the crim parliamentary special committee, which recommends the drawing up of a european union strategy and the adoption of binding legal instruments at european level and in the member states. there is an urgent need to act because, beyond economic considerations, organised crime is a danger that threatens the freedom and security of all european citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this mid-term report because it offers a useful roadmap for better tackling organised crime, corruption and money laundering in a homogeneous way in the european union. while this phenomenon costs about 770 billion euros a year, of which 120 billion euros are spent in europe alone, we need to have more effective means to stop it. from the preventive freezing of the assets of criminal organisations before the individuals are convicted, to the banning of access to public procurement by mafia organisations, to the five-year ban on access to electoral mandates for persons convicted of corruption, all avenues must be explored to end the impunity enjoyed by these criminals. european coordination in this area will certainly have added value, which should not be overlooked.

in writing. the revenues from international criminal activities amount to 3.6% of global gdp. within the european union, corruption alone costs about 1% of european gdp. action is then necessary to protect the financial interests of the union against such organised crime. the text i voted for is in line with this, by giving a common definition of organised crime in the member states and by combating bank secrecy, which allows criminal organisations to place money without being controlled. the strengthening of crossborder judicial and police cooperation, provided for in the text, between eu countries but also with third countries will make it possible to combat mafia-type crime more effectively at european level and more generally at global level.
in writing. on tuesday i voted in favour of the report on organised crime, corruption and money laundering, which is a major issue in europe. since the era of globalisation, these illicit activities have grown exponentially and represent a serious threat to the stability of the european economy, our society and our institutions. therefore, in the face of this global threat, the union must provide a collective response by coordinating european and national legislation to combat these crimes and illegal practices. parliament therefore decided to strengthen judicial and police cooperation at european level and to ensure greater protection for whistleblowers, witnesses and informers of mafia crimes. finally, we call for the abolition of banking secrecy to cut off the financial resources of criminal organizations and to put an end to this scourge.
in writing. this report identifies quite well the causes of the contemporary development of organised crime in connection with globalisation and the opening of borders induced by the eu. it proposes some effective concrete solutions, such as lifting banking secrecy or imposing sanctions on banks that are complicit in money laundering. but the report is essentially based on the commission's initiative to harmonize definitions and procedures in the fight against organised crime and money laundering. in the present state of the treaties, this harmonization can only lead to a new wave of deregulation, which in fact makes it easier for organised crime to operate. on the contrary, an effective fight against money laundering requires that the free movement of capital be called into question, which is not assumed in this report. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. this report calls for enhanced international cooperation between member states, the european union, the united nations and the oecd to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the measures recommended are guided by the intensification of controls and repression. however, the report seems to forget that such breaches are often difficult to detect because they are embedded in opaque circuits. this opacity is likely to worsen as the financial circuits used by laundered funds become more and more complex. this will make these measures inadequate and difficult to implement. i also regret that this report does not deal with the question of preventive measures, which are useful means, which will make it possible in the long term to curb corruption by bringing about a change in mentality. i therefore call for more prevention and have therefore voted against this report.
in writing. organised crime is a threat to the european economy and society. this phenomenon has changed considerably in recent years: economic globalisation and new technologies have helped to establish organised crime as a player in the world economy. indeed, according to the latest commission estimates, the proceeds of criminal activities represent 3.6% of global gdp, while the cost of corruption in the eu reaches 1% of european gdp. an appropriate policy response coupled with a prevention effort is essential. i therefore voted in favour of this report which calls on the commission to present a coherent legislative framework to combat organised crime. this is illustrated by a clear definition of these crimes, the end of banking secrecy, and a strengthening of police and judicial cooperation, both at european and global level. these strategies should be complemented by action to raise awareness among citizens, while promoting a culture of legality.
in writing. i voted against this report on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. apart from the many common features, it offers little new insight into the phenomenon of organised crime. it pretends to discover its transnational and international dimension, without saying anything at the same time about the root causes of the birth and development of mafias, namely the inability of the states to fulfil their royal functions and to guarantee access to public services for all. overall, this report still supports the same purely security vision without taking into account the need and importance of preventive measures or the actions of civil society, which are nonetheless decisive as shown by the action of the anti-mafia citizen movements in italy. finally, i could not but oppose a text combining trafficking and immigration in its part on the management of maritime borders, and calling for an increase in the funds allocated to europol, eurojust and frontex, whose role in building the fortress europe is well known to be decisive.

refugee agency and non-governmental organisations have noted many failures in the application of the previous directive. in fact, it is enough to compare recognition rates from one member state to another to see how much applying for asylum in europe can be a lottery depending on the country responsible for the application. while the recognition rate in 2012 was less than 1% in greece, it was 90% in malta, 29% in germany and 14.5% in france. in addition, the level of protection varies greatly from one state to another depending on the nationality of the applicants. for example, if an afghan seeks asylum in europe, his chances of being offered protection vary from 8 to 91 percent depending on the state where he files his application. it was therefore necessary and urgent to revise the asylum procedure directive, both in the interests of asylum seekers and of the states. but the process of reform has been far from a long, quiet river. almost four years ago, in october 2009, the commission made a proposal to amend the directive. the council has not done so, and i am not sure that the council will be able to do so. he quickly argued that the amendments would generate financial costs and facilitate abuse and procedural misuse. to break the deadlock, the commission put forward a new proposal which took greater account of the council's reservations. parliament has made an ambitious and, in my view, courageous commitment, and we have been actively working towards a position that places the slide rule very high on the side of upward harmonization of protection standards. with this first step, parliament wanted to overcome a somewhat too manichean view of asylum, namely that it should be exclusively a matter of costs and abuses. and we wanted to counter the cost-effectiveness arguments used to limit reforms by pointing out that it is rather poorly used and poor quality procedures that cost the states dearly. after years of sometimes arduous discussions, we have managed to find common ground and to draw up the new outlines of the asylum procedure within the european union. is the compromise we have reached really exactly what we would have liked? of course not! but we have respected an overall balanced strategy, as parliament wanted, which combines the quality of procedures, respect for rights and the efficiency of the decision-making process for the member states. the result of the discussions is undoubtedly added value for the texts on procedures: the rules are specified and clarified, the procedural guarantees are strengthened and the procedures are fairer and more efficient. here are some brief examples of some of them: for example, among the improvements, the clear and precise rules on the compulsory training of the authorities responsible for examining applications; the introduction of an identification mechanism for vulnerable people, including, of course, the identification of needs, but also the response that is formulated for those who have these needs; detailed provisions on individual maintenance, which must be carried out on a near-regular basis; the right to an effective remedy, which is a fundamental point in our text which follows developments in case law; the introduction of procedures for access to the procedure with now defined time limits; and of course, speaking of deadlines, the introduction of a general six-month period for examining an asylum application subject to some exceptions, but in the interests of both applicants and states. these improvements respond to the deficiencies and dysfunctions which have been identified in recent years by the various observers of asylum procedural systems in the member states. these improvements should also make it possible to deepen the process of harmonisation and to unify the current patchwork of asylum procedures in europe.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text on illegal fishing. the text aligns a 2008 regulation with the provisions of the lisbon treaty, in particular as regards the actions that the european commission can take to limit illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting is a very important one.
in writing. this report sets out the commission's responsibilities in the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. the commission may adopt delegated acts, in particular to establish different notification periods, to amend the list of products not covered by the regulation, to modify the deadlines for submitting fishing authorisations depending on the type of fishery product, the distance to the fishing area, the type of vessel used, etc. the commission may adopt implementing acts concerning the technical provisions of the regulation. i voted in favour of the report because of the division between delegated and implementing acts.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to classify the commission's powers in terms of delegated and implementing acts in the area of illegal fishing. the delegated act procedure allows the commission to adopt binding acts itself without waiting for parliament and the council to give their consent, which allows it to be more reactive and to have more room for manoeuvre. the commission is now the body which classifies third countries as non-cooperating with the eu in fisheries, but this delegation of power is limited in time to avoid distorting parliament's powers in this area.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by raul romeva i rueda, which provides for alignment of the regulation establishing a community system to prevent, deter and eradicate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing with the provisions of the lisbon treaty. the proposed classification of the commission's competences between delegated acts and implementing acts is not problematic and the changes introduced do not give the commission disproportionate competences. like the rapporteur, i am very much in favour of the delegation of powers to the european commission not being unlimited in time, so as to allow parliament to assess its prerogatives regularly.
in writing. this text enables the commission to take the necessary measures to deal with the consequences of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing for biodiversity and food security. this is an important step forward, but the commission will have to remain vigilant to ensure that these measures do not lead to price increases, supply disruptions or loss of profits for operators.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it will make it possible to combat illegal fishing effectively without destabilising the european economy. illegal fishermen sell fish at a lower cost, while fishermen who respect eu rules and quotas are forced to sell their fish at higher prices to cover their costs. this unfair competition cannot be accepted and the european union must protect legal fishermen and thus ensure the quality and monitoring of the product. the text will also help to safeguard certain species threatened by non-compliance with quotas.
in writing. today, the european parliament has approved a new procedure concerning the list of countries that do not cooperate in the fight against illegal, unregulated and unreported (iuu) fishing. this is good news and i voted in favour of this text because this blacklist is an essential tool to tackle illegal fishing. we had to give the green light to a faster procedure to add countries to this list. this will allow the commission to add further countries to the current list of non-cooperating states and to publish the list of vessels involved. with iuu fishing, vulnerable fish stocks are under serious threat. transparency of the states and the vessels involved is a crucial measure to tackle this problem. if the countries on the list do not make rapid progress, the commission must propose sanctions.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague raül romeva i rueda in the plenary on 12 june. this report concerned the classification of the powers currently conferred on the commission by regulation no 1005/2008 as delegated or implementing powers. as the report called for, it was important to limit the delegation of powers proposed to a certain period. it was a single vote and the report was adopted by 668 votes to 7, with 10 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. i voted for the parliament's report on illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. these illegal activities are lucrative because they allow their perpetrators to sell fish cheaper by avoiding quotas and environmental criteria. they have a significant cost for fishermen who comply with european rules and thus find themselves in a situation of unfair competition. parliament therefore adopted new rules to strengthen inspection operations during landings and transhipments of vessels, including those from third countries. the text also provides for a set of sanctions at european level.
in writing. the aim of this report is to make the commission's powers under the regulation compatible with the new rules on the functioning of the european union. the proposals reinforce the provisions to prevent, deter and eradicate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing in a consolidated legal framework. in this sense, no authority is withdrawn from the european parliament. i vote for it.
in writing. antonio masip hidalgo recommended that the council's position at first reading be adopted on this text, which aims to improve the reception conditions for asylum seekers in europe and to bring eu legislation into line with european standards in this field. the commission's initial text proposes in particular to facilitate access to employment for an asylum seeker and to prohibit the detention of a person solely on the grounds that he is seeking international protection. i, like most of my colleagues, approved of this recommendation.
in writing. the objectives of the report are of several kinds. the first step is to ensure that persons applying for international protection are provided with the best possible conditions (access to the labour market, duration of asylum processing, detention and conditions of detention, etc.) for treatment in accordance with international standards. the second step is to harmonise the reception rules in order to limit the movement of persons seeking international protection within the eu in order to obtain better protection. i voted for the report because of the points made in it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the 'asylum package', which, although it does not meet all the expectations of the socialist group, makes it possible to modernise and make the rules on asylum in europe fairer. we now call on the council to abandon its accounting approach to asylum and to adopt minimum rules applicable throughout europe. the current system is unfair to asylum seekers, as the chances of their application being successful vary considerably depending on the country in which it is lodged. in addition, the conditions under which applications are received and processed are sometimes not in keeping with the values which europe stands for. the texts adopted by the european parliament provide an initial improvement by creating common standards. i would like to mention in particular: - the setting of a six-month deadline for examining applications, and the right to an effective remedy; - better access to information for applicants; - the strengthening of the rights of unaccompanied minors and the most vulnerable people.
in writing. i voted in favour of a new structure for european asylum policy. the text introduces common rules for processing applications and ensures minimum rights for asylum seekers entering the union. more readability and simplicity is a given if we really want to help those who need it most and are in a situation of emergency and distress. a more efficient system is also, and above all, a system which is better able to manage the flow of applications properly and to ensure that all the rules and criteria we set are respected.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text as it allows for a clarification and strengthening of the standards for the reception of asylum seekers at european level. the text sets out minimum standards for reception so that applicants can live with dignity and equality in each member state. this measure establishes a clear and reasonable system of solidarity and will allow the eu to assert itself in its role as defender of human rights.
in writing. after more than four years of tough negotiations with the council, this vote on the remaining four items of the asylum package marks a remarkable step forward and finally gives the green light to the establishment of a genuine european asylum system. the new system provides for common time limits for processing asylum applications, stricter rules on staff training, better access to information, better supervision of detention, the widespread use of suspensive remedies, responses tailored to vulnerable persons such as victims of torture or unaccompanied minors, etc. - all improvements that will address the identified shortcomings and take the process of harmonising asylum further. i regret that we have not achieved an even more ambitious and protective reform (since several points were lost in the negotiations with the states), but i welcome these votes which mark a historic step forward! the transposition of these regulations and directives and the effective application of these rights of applicants for international protection will now have to be monitored. we have a duty to welcome these people into the european union, respecting their dignity and fundamental rights.
in writing. i voted in favour of the revision of the directive on reception conditions. the conditions of reception and living conditions for asylum seekers in europe today are extremely disparate, so it was essential to reform the existing legislation. the text adopted at the end of the discussions is not as ambitious as parliament had hoped and defended in the council. but in the face of strong opposition from the states, we have succeeded in shifting the balance towards an upward harmonization of protection standards. the revised directive introduces clear rules on detention and the conditions applicable. the legal vacuum that has persisted until now has allowed some states to have quite scandalous practices in the matter of detention. in addition to this improved framework on detention, the amended directive establishes that it will now be the responsibility of states to identify vulnerable persons, to determine the nature of their needs and to meet them in their reception system. that said, we will have to be particularly vigilant in the transposition of the amended directive at national level in order to check that no misinterpretation or incorrect application of these provisions is made.
in writing. the european parliament adopted the asylum package on wednesday 12 june, five years after the european pact on immigration and asylum which i proposed and championed under the french presidency and which was adopted by the european council in october 2008. we recognised then that international migration could be an opportunity in a comprehensive approach, but that poorly managed immigration could undermine the social cohesion of destination countries, which were not always well equipped to cope with increasing flows of migrants, including asylum seekers. france is the second country to receive asylum applications in europe with over 60,000 applications in 2012. this is no minor phenomenon. i therefore hope that the standards adopted will be balanced and compatible with the evolving capacities of our national asylum systems. the effective operation of our system and the best possible european cooperation will not only serve the interests of our states but also those of asylum seekers for whom the minimum standards for reception have now been clarified.
in writing. i supported the recommendation of my colleague antonio masip hidalgo in the plenary session of 12 june. this recommendation concerned the raising of treatment standards for reception conditions for asylum seekers. it also concerned the harmonisation of national rules on these reception conditions in order to limit the movements of asylum seekers between member states. although the initial report was somewhat unrealistic, the compromises subsequently found were fully satisfactory and i am pleased that parliament has adopted this text.
in writing. on average, the european union deals with around 300 000 asylum applications per year and this number is increasing year by year. it is therefore necessary to establish common and effective legislation on the reception of applicants for international protection. i voted in favour of this text because it aims to set up minimum standards for the reception of asylum seekers throughout the european union in order to guarantee them a decent standard of living while avoiding the phenomenon of asylum-shopping and administrative burdens too heavy for the member states.
in writing. on wednesday, i voted in favour of a european asylum policy. it provides for common standards for all member states for the treatment of asylum seekers entering the european union. these harmonised rules should improve the management of flows at the union's borders, avoiding abuses linked to divergent national systems. in view of the difficulties encountered by several member states in the face of the massive influx of migrants during the so-called 'arab spring', the european parliament, in line with the european pact for asylum and immigration, initiated by brice hortefeux, under the french presidency of the european union, is taking up its responsibilities.
in writing. the adoption of the asylum package allows us to have common rules to ensure decent treatment of asylum seekers while putting in place clear rules to prevent and deter abuse of our asylum system. these common standards guarantee that every asylum seeker in europe is treated with dignity. but this common base also allows us to better combat the practice of 'asylum shopping', which is the practice of choosing the country with the most favourable reception conditions to apply for asylum. by making the reception conditions uniform, we prevent such practices.
in writing. the report proposed by mr hidalgo gives precise conditions for the reception of asylum seekers. the report proposes an increase in eu funding for member states dealing with large arrivals, which place a disproportionate burden of asylum seekers on their reception services. the report also provides for the unification of european rules in this area, which is entirely in line with the wishes of the european parliament. i am therefore very much prepared to see this report continue on its way to implementation, which is why i gave my vote a positive direction.
in writing. while the aim of this text is to establish more harmonised and humane standards for the reception and treatment of asylum seekers by the member states of the european union , it is far from that goal. on the contrary, by legislating on the conditions and grounds for detention, this report accepts and legitimises detention as a way of managing people seeking asylum in the european union. it thus trivializes the confinement of asylum seekers, including minors and particularly vulnerable persons in situations of great distress, in centres and prisons. i, for my part, advocate humanizing the reception conditions for asylum seekers. the right to seek asylum is a right, and it is particularly shocking that an individual should be deprived of his liberty for the sole reason that he is seeking international protection. i therefore oppose this report.
in writing. 330 000 asylum applications were registered in the union in 2012. to meet these demands, i voted in favour of the new rules proposed in this report, which call for more humane treatment but also for more stringent measures in the handling of cases. these rules provide for common time limits for asylum procedures which should not exceed six months, and minimum rights for applicants in respect of housing, subsistence and health benefits. in the event of doubt as to the age of an isolated young person, the latter shall be considered a minor, to enable him to have a representative accompanying him in his activities. however, it will be possible to keep applicants in detention under certain conditions, in particular where there is a risk of absconding. finally, in order to combat organised crime, the police will have access to the eurodac file which stores the fingerprints of asylum seekers over 14 years of age and irregular migrants apprehended on the territory of a member state or when crossing a border. this will enable europe to defend its humanist values while protecting its citizens from uncontrolled immigration.
in writing. i am very pleased with the outcome of the vote on the european asylum system, which creates a genuine common regime for all member states. the previous legislation was often referred to as the 'asylum lottery'. depending on the nationality of the asylum seeker and the state in which the application was lodged, the chances of recognition of the right to asylum varied from 1 to 90%. we have created a maximum period of six months to examine asylum applications where there was none before. the authorities will no longer be able to remain silent and refuse to respond to an asylum application. in addition, vulnerable asylum seekers such as unaccompanied minors, pregnant women and victims of torture will be better protected. finally, the detention of asylum seekers will be more supervised. administrative detention can only be used in certain specialised centres and in special cases. applicants will be able to benefit from a medical and psychological assessment. they will also have faster access to employment. in the end, this new european asylum system is not as ambitious as i wanted it to be. it does, however, make excellent progress in relation to the existing disparities in national legislation.

in writing. the evaluation of dublin ii implementation has shown that there are a number of shortcomings which the report proposes to address in order to ensure the efficiency and effectiveness of the system. improvements have been made: the distribution of procedures between member states, the clarification of the sole reason for detention - the serious risk of absconding - the extension of family reunification opportunities for unaccompanied minors to siblings, uncles and aunts and grandparents (at the same time, a clarification of the definition of 'family member' is made), a new early warning mechanism and free legal assistance in case of a challenge to the transfer decision to another member state. i voted for the report because of the improvements it proposes.
