in writing. i voted in favour of this report which updates a 2000 regulation establishing eurodac (european dactyloscopy), the european database for fingerprints of asylum seekers and illegal immigrants. the main purpose of the text is to incorporate the provisions of the lisbon treaty into this regulation. i voted against an amendment by the gue/ngl and greens/efa groups which sought to remove all the provisions allowing access to eurodac for law enforcement purposes.
in writing. the eurodac system allows fingerprints to be compared of asylum seekers from third countries or stateless persons. the system aims to prevent, detect and investigate potential terrorist threats and serious crime. the revised text will allow immediate access to the eurodac database, without prior and mandatory checks, to data on approved asylum seekers, and access to eurodac for law enforcement authorities. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the macovei report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the creation of the 'eurodac' system, a fingerprint database to allow comparisons between european countries. police forces in the member states and europol will now have access to the fingerprints of asylum seekers in order to combat terrorism and serious crime. we have ensured that personal data is protected, including by ensuring that these safeguards are used only for this purpose of fingerprint comparison and thus prevent any form of misuse.
in writing. eurodac allows the european union to record the fingerprints of asylum seekers: it is an essential tool for us to manage applications, effectively protect applicants and prevent abusive applications. in order to respond to the developments, particularly technological, which have taken place since its entry into force, we are adapting it to improve its functioning, particularly in terms of data protection. this is a necessary step forward for the efficient and fair processing of asylum applications in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which extends the possibility for member states to use eurodac. this database would allow member states to compare the fingerprints of asylum seekers across the european union and to determine whether an asylum seeker or an irregular migrant has already lodged an asylum application in another member state. in order to combat terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences, national police authorities really need an effective european system for comparing fingerprints and this is exactly what this text is now putting in place.
in writing. after more than four years of tough negotiations with the council, this vote on the remaining four items of the asylum package marks a remarkable step forward and finally gives the green light to the establishment of a genuine european asylum system. the new system provides for common time limits for processing asylum applications, stricter rules on staff training, better access to information, better supervision of detention, the widespread use of suspensive remedies, responses tailored to vulnerable persons such as victims of torture or unaccompanied minors, etc. all these improvements will address the shortcomings identified and further the process of harmonising asylum. i regret that we have not achieved an even more ambitious and protective reform (since several points were lost in the negotiations with the states), but i welcome these votes which mark a historic step forward! the transposition of these regulations and directives and the effective application of these rights of applicants for international protection will now have to be monitored. we have a duty to welcome these people into the european union, with respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.
in writing. access to the eurodac database by national police forces and europol has long been requested by the states, which have clearly conditioned their efforts on the other files in the asylum package. the s&d group welcomed the commission's proposal to extend the scope of eurodac to law enforcement agencies, but felt that it was not appropriate to do so. access to the file will only be possible as a last resort, when the law enforcement agencies have failed to find the information they need in their own systems or in those of other member states. eurodac will also be allowed only if an asylum seeker is suspected of serious crime or terrorism. the consultation of eurodac will therefore not be systematic. parliament will now have to ensure that the commission closely monitors eurodac, and in particular to assess the reality of stigmatisation of applicants and the negative impact on the integration of refugees into their host society.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague monica luisa macovei in the plenary on 12 june. this report focused on the redesign of eurodac on fingerprint comparison in order to update it, make it more efficient and more consistent with the eu asylum acquis. it stresses in particular the need for access to eurodac to be strictly regulated. it also stressed the need to delete immediately data which had been transmitted to eurodac, as soon as the results of the comparison of data had been transmitted to the member state of origin. the report was adopted by 502 votes in favour, 126 against and 56 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the eurodac regulation, which has been in force since 2003, stores the fingerprints of asylum seekers over the age of 14 and of irregular migrants apprehended on the territory of a member state or when crossing a border. this database provides valuable information to member states on the quality of asylum seekers already listed, but is not accessible to europol and the police services. however, it is necessary that law enforcement agencies have access to this database in order to be as fit as possible to combat terrorism and serious crime. i voted in favour of this text because it provides for this possibility.
in writing. i supported the report on the creation of the eurodac system for comparing fingerprints. created in 2000, eurodac is now a key database to be used in the fight against organised crime in europe. we have therefore authorised access to eurodac resources by member states' services and europol, to support their actions against criminal activities. in this context, eurodac should facilitate the prevention and detection of terrorist offences, trafficking in human beings, criminal networks or other serious criminal offences.
in writing. the commission proposes to extend the use of the eurodac system for comparing the fingerprints of asylum seekers for law enforcement purposes. this is a misuse of a tool which is intended to enable the right of asylum to be properly applied. this leads to all asylum seekers being suspected of crime and even terrorism. the need for police or judicial authorities to access the system has not been proven. the parliament's report makes some timid corrections. the commission has also proposed to amend the data protection rules to include the right to access data for law enforcement purposes. but these marginal improvements are not enough to remove the text's stigmatizing logic for asylum seekers. i vote against it.
in writing. the creation of the eurodac system for comparing fingerprints will allow for better care of migrants within the european union, in particular by moving towards the harmonisation of asylum law for the different member states on this issue. this text, which was the result of long negotiations between the european council, the european commission and the european parliament, preserves the sustainability of reception systems in each member state and ensures respect for and safety of migrants. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to improve the efficiency of the system for recording the fingerprints of asylum seekers which has been in use since 2003 under the dublin convention. however, it goes far beyond the mere issue of asylum management, by giving national law enforcement authorities and europol the possibility to use these databases, containing the fingerprints of asylum seekers, in order to prevent and combat crime and terrorist acts. this opens the door to many deviations and shows an undeniable distrust of asylum seekers, who are in fact considered potential criminals and terrorists. these same asylum seekers are also receiving poor reception conditions on european soil. i am opposed to this stigmatising process and i am against this text.
in writing. i voted against this agreement between the council and the european parliament revising the eurodac regulation on the fingerprinting of asylum seekers. eurodac was set up in 2000, even before the attacks in new york, which, in the name of the fight against terrorism, have served as a pretext for so many regressions in public freedoms. the revision will, in particular, allow member states' law enforcement agencies and europol to have access to the eurodac database, which will be kept for three years after the applicant's refugee status has been recognised. this legislation therefore creates a total confusion between asylum seekers and irregular immigrants. as all ngos say, this is a challenge to the right of asylum and therefore a violation of the eu's international obligations. the negative opinion of the edps on the grounds that it constitutes a serious intrusion in the rights of these persons did not change the inflexible attitude of the member states. i cannot, in principle, support such a system and i regret that a large majority of the european parliament has adopted this revision. asylum seekers are thus criminalised and the european union increasingly considers asylum seekers as fraudsters.
in writing. in 2011, at the instigation of former president nicolas sarkozy, the european commission presented two texts aimed at improving the functioning of this area. the first text, followed by my colleague renate weber, expands the situations in which member states are allowed to re-establish internal borders. at present, internal borders can be re-established in the event of serious threats to public order or internal security. in addition to these situations, there are serious and persistent shortcomings in external border control. i voted in favour of this text, which will improve the functioning of the schengen area and thereby promote the free movement of european citizens. let us be clear: this is not a question of turning europe into a fortress closed in on itself. however, i believe that the dysfunctions that occurred in 2011 following the popular uprisings in tunisia and libya have demonstrated that a re-design of the schengen system was unavoidable.
in writing. in order to respond to critical situations, such as the massive influx of immigrants following the arab spring, the amendment of the schengen borders code became a necessity. the changes made concern the rules on external border controls, the possibility of reintroducing internal schengen border controls, which should only be reintroduced as a last resort and with a view to adopting measures stabilising the situation at the relevant part of the border. the aim was to strike a balance between respect for the prerogatives of the states and the establishment of common rules between all the states. the result was satisfactory and could ensure solidarity between the states, so i voted in favour of the legislative resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of the reform of the schengen borders code, as part of the overhaul of the schengen governance package. the border code already allows for the reintroduction of border controls in the event of exceptional circumstances that constitute a threat to public order and national security. the reintroduction of controls therefore remains an exception and a measure of last resort. if member states reintroduce controls, justified by a serious threat to public policy or internal security for more than 30 days, the commission, after consulting parliament, will have to decide on the appropriateness of such controls and their possible extension. free movement is one of the eu's most impressive achievements. 62% of the european population believe that this is the most positive result of 50 years of european integration.
in writing. we have demonstrated that it is sometimes necessary to temporarily reintroduce controls at our national borders to deal with a particularly difficult situation for our security or for public order. the aim of this text is not to go back on one of the foundations of the european union, it is not to call into question our freedom of movement, it is above all to guarantee our security and public order in exceptional situations. i therefore support the measures contained in this text and the ambition for a decision-making system that is both flexible and responsible, and which includes the european parliament. the aim is to ensure effective democratic oversight of this mechanism.
in writing. the lack of solidarity shown by some european countries in april 2011, considering that the management of tunisian refugees on the island of lampedusa was the sole responsibility of italy, has seriously challenged the schengen acquis, one of the eu's major achievements. more recently, the syrian tragedy and its consequences in terms of refugees have also once again demonstrated that securing the external borders must be everyone's business. it is high time to renew the spirit of european solidarity. europe must have a common immigration strategy, which is humane and reasonable. a state cannot unilaterally decide to close its borders even exceptionally as denmark did in 2011. this is not legally or politically acceptable. the establishment of a european mechanism for the reintroduction of temporary control based on the analysis of the schengen acquis is therefore a more appropriate solution. this new mechanism will thus help to preserve the schengen area as an area without internal borders. subject to the democratic control of the european parliament, its implementation will have all its democratic legitimacy, an indispensable prerequisite for the proper functioning of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which specifies the conditions for the re-establishment of internal borders. by giving member states the possibility of reintroducing internal border controls on a timely basis, the schengen area now has the means to react quickly to the various threats to public policy or internal security, without calling into question the acquis of the convention which european citizens hold so dear.
in writing. i did not vote for the weber report or the coehlo report on the possibility for states to re-establish controls at all their borders because in fact this possibility is abusive. the compromise reached does not go as far as the commission's aberrant claims that it alone decides on the re-establishment of internal borders. but giving him the right to make an unannounced inspection on the spot to ensure that there was no actual control is inadmissible. nor is there a 'collegial' assessment of the need for safeguard measures, or the strict limitation of such measures in the event of a serious and unforeseeable event. we cannot trust institutions that consider that an influx of migrants at the external borders cannot by definition be considered a threat or that a wave of terrorist attacks can be contained in 10 days. the schengen agreements must be abolished and, as a first step, the absolute right of the member states to enforce safeguard clauses according to their own assessments of the threats and circumstances must be recognised.
in writing. i voted in favour of this regulation. it is necessary to provide a common response to situations having a significant impact on the internal security of the european union or of one or more of its member states by allowing the reintroduction of internal border control in exceptional circumstances. the current schengen system, which is based on an intergovernmental peer review system, is not strong enough to address the weaknesses of some member states. the regulation allows a member state to re-establish border controls for a limited period of time when a serious threat to public policy or internal security requires immediate action. any extension of the period will then be decided in a coordinated manner.
in writing. in september 2011, at the instigation of nicolas sarkozy, the european commission presented two proposals for reform of the schengen area. the current migratory pressures and successive enlargements called for urgent adaptations of the schengen system. it's a done deal now. the european parliament adopted on wednesday 12 june two recommendations on schengen governance and the clarification of the conditions for the reintroduction of borders in the event of a failure to control external borders. we cannot put at risk the principle of free movement of european citizens, which is one of the pillars and cardinal principles of the european union. this reform reaffirms the principle of free movement while strengthening border security and allowing the temporary reintroduction of internal borders when public order and the security of our citizens are threatened. we must, however, remain vigilant about the effectiveness of these reforms, which must be assessed rapidly, and consider, if necessary, complementary measures, particularly as regards the role of the frontex agency, which must be placed at the heart of the system.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague, renate weber, in the plenary on 12 june. the report aimed to amend the schengen borders code established by regulation no 562/2006 in order to extend the possibilities of temporarily introducing border controls. the report was adopted by 506 votes in favour, 121 against and 25 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the creation of the schengen area is undoubtedly one of the greatest achievements of the european union. the schengen code states that the abolition of internal border controls remains the principle, while the temporary reintroduction is the exception. however, at a time when illegal immigration is being debated within the european union, it was necessary to revise the code. i voted in favour of this text because it provides for reintroduction if there are serious threats, foreseeable or not, to public policy or security, or when the member state concerned does not bring its external border management into line in a serious or persistent way.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the reintroduction of internal border controls. within the schengen area, which comprises 22 member states and 4 non-eu countries, the principle of free movement allows citizens of the states parties to cross borders without being subject to permanent border controls. however, in certain exceptional cases where there is a clear threat to public order, governments may decide to re-establish these controls for a maximum period of six months. in order to preserve the integrity of this fundamental right, we recommend that this decision be taken in a collegial manner at european level, with uniform rules for assessing threats to public order.
in writing. we have gained two things with this reform of schengen governance: the fundamental freedom of movement of european citizens is preserved and the security of the schengen area is strengthened. we have given ourselves the means to react and to reinforce border controls if necessary, so that citizens do not have to bear the price of porous borders. if a shortcoming is found at our borders, it will be remedied: the member state concerned will have to act immediately and put in place an action plan to strengthen border control at the borders in question. if such a failure were to persist, and if the borders were to give way to too much migratory pressure, then it would be possible to temporarily reintroduce internal border controls to protect our european citizens from uncontrolled flows. it is not to be naïve to say that there are very specific situations which call for the temporary and careful re-establishment of frontiers. that is why the member states are also rightly free to temporarily re-establish internal borders for reasons of security and public order, because the safety of european citizens must come first.
in writing. the possibility of temporarily reintroducing internal border controls already exists for the states. this report extends the powers of the commission, which has no legal authority to decide, validate and renew such decisions. this text reinforces the cases of restrictions on the freedom of individuals. at the same time, the european union continues to encourage the full free movement of capital and goods and to encourage the posting of workers to enable the exploitation of the poorest. this hypocritical imbalance is unbearable. i vote against it.
in writing. this text takes a responsible approach by giving member states the possibility to temporarily re-establish borders within the european union, in particular in the event of a threat to public policy or internal security, while giving the european commission the power to monitor the impartiality of inspections and thus to strengthen mutual trust between member states. i have always imagined the european union in this light and therefore voted in favour of mrs weber's report.
in writing. freedom of movement for european citizens is a fundamental freedom guaranteed by the treaties. it should therefore not be subject to any restrictions. a limitation of the rights granted to european citizens would in fact be a challenge to the acquis communautaire. the text allows member states to reinstate border controls in the event of 'threats to public policy or internal security', but does not specify what is meant by this term, thus leaving member states a certain latitude in this relatively vague framework. this is tantamount to leaving the reintroduction of controls to the discretion of the member states, which could abuse this possibility to control large migratory flows at the borders. although safeguards have been introduced, i doubt that they will be sufficient in the face of states which never lack imagination when it comes to circumventing the law. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. since 1993, citizens of the schengen area have been able to move freely. it is an inalienable right that we cannot question. but this system was almost obsolete. the de facto solidarity between all the member states was not very real. we had to complete the system, so as not to leave it to the eurosceptics. with this vote, we have won a battle. on the one hand, we are preserving our model of free movement, but on the other hand we are strengthening the security of our borders. that is what the people asked for. effective border control can now be examined at european level. in return, member states will be able to impose the closure of a border with another state which is a little too lax on its own borders. and each member state is in control if an extreme emergency situation forces it to temporarily re-establish border controls. the essential thing we must always keep in mind is to strike a balance between free movement and the safety of our fellow citizens.

in writing. four years after the implementation of the regulation establishing a community code on the rules governing the crossing of frontiers by persons, technical amendments were necessary, as the time allowed. these amendments are intended to respond to the problems encountered in the last four years and to reduce the possibility of divergent interpretations of the current text. in addition, a legal framework has been developed for bilateral agreements on the implementation of joint border checks in road traffic. the definition of 'residence permit' has also been clarified in legal and semantic terms. i voted in favour of the resolution because of the positive effect that these amendments could have.
in writing. i voted in favour of the amendment to the schengen code, which is part of the revision of the schengen governance package. the new schengen code will strengthen the free movement of citizens, reduce intergovernmental procedures for greater european participation and strengthen cooperation between the commission and the member states. free movement is one of the eu's most impressive achievements. 62% of the european population believe that this is the most positive result of 50 years of european integration.
in writing. i welcome these amendments to the community code on the crossing of frontiers, which will make it clearer, more uniform and, in short, more effective. this is therefore a step forward for europeans, who will benefit from greater legal certainty when travelling within this area. the more legible the rules, the better the guarantee of free movement.
in writing. the schengen agreement is extremely positive in that it allows mobility for all citizens across europe. i supported this text because i thought it was essential to adapt the schengen borders code to the present requirements: this proposal will make cooperation between member states more effective. the text proposes to simplify the common border control measures. it will thus provide better protection for our territory and our fellow citizens.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague georgios papanikolaou in the plenary on 12 june. this report dealt with the amendment of the schengen borders code and the convention implementing the schengen agreement. after four years of application, it had become necessary to make a number of technical changes. the commission proposal and the report have made sensible improvements. so i'm glad he was adopted.
in writing. the schengen borders code entered into force following the adoption of the regulation of 13 october 2006 by the council and the parliament. after a few years of practical application, it became necessary to evaluate its effectiveness and activity. i therefore voted in favour of this text because it provides answers to the practical problems of using the code by clarifying it and reducing the possibility of divergent interpretation. it provides for a number of technical amendments, including clarification of the legal framework applicable in the case of joint checks on the roads and a clear definition of the method of calculating stays of no more than three months in a six-month period.
in writing. on wednesday i voted in favour of amending the schengen code and the convention implementing the schengen agreement. on the one hand, we want to strengthen the rules that facilitate and promote free movement within the schengen area. on the other hand, we support the establishment of a rigorous framework for control and security at the external borders of the european territory. by strengthening the capacity of the european agencies for immigration control and control, schengen provides a mechanism for the objective evaluation of the quality of external border controls by the member states.
in writing. this text mainly deals with highly technical issues and aims to harmonise the application of the law in the schengen area. i could vote for it if it did not, by way of an amendment by parliament, include a reference in the schengen borders code to the return directive adopted in 2008 and which i voted against. i'm not going to.
in writing. since 1993, citizens of the schengen area have been able to move freely. it is an inalienable right that we cannot question. but this system was almost obsolete. the de facto solidarity between all the member states was not very real. we had to complete the system, so as not to leave it to the eurosceptics. with this vote, we have won a battle. on the one hand, we are preserving our model of free movement, but on the other hand we are strengthening the security of our borders. that is what the people asked for. effective border control can now be examined at european level. in return, member states will be able to impose the closure of a border with another state which is a little too lax on its own borders. and each member state is in control if an extreme emergency situation forces it to temporarily re-establish border controls. the essential thing we must always keep in mind is to strike a balance between free movement and the safety of our fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted against this report on the temporary reintroduction of internal border control in exceptional circumstances. this report is a reaction to the events of april 2011, when france closed its borders to refugees from the north african revolutions coming from italy. now, in the event of an 'imminent threat', member states can 'invite' the commission to discuss the temporary reintroduction of internal border control. the free movement of persons within the territory of the european union is a fundamental right, recognised by the treaties. once again, the free movement of persons is less real than that of capital, services and goods. this text confirms the european union's security vision and the lack of democracy and transparency in the management of the schengen area. even if the ep and the commission have limited the possibilities of reintroducing these controls to the greatest possible extent, despite the pressure from some member states, i think this is a matter of principles from which we should not depart. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. the reform of the schengen area preserves the freedom of movement of people within european borders. the commission will have to consult parliament before sending an inspection team to control the borders. this control procedure will neutralize any objectionable initiative by member states, such as nicolas sarkozy's unilateral decision to close the border between france and italy on 17 april 2011 following the arab spring. moreover, any reintroduction of border controls by states will have to be justified by exceptional circumstances. in no case may immigration be used as a reason for threatening public order and internal security to justify the reintroduction of controls. moreover, if member states reintroduce internal border controls, they cannot last for more than six months. the free movement of persons within the borders of the member states is a fundamental pillar of the european union, one of those 'concrete achievements which first create a de facto solidarity' that robert schuman wished for. the movement of people must therefore be facilitated, while safety and confidence must be improved through cooperation between member states.
in writing. my colleagues rafal trzaskowski and roberto gualtieri recommended that meps give their approval to the draft european council decision setting the composition of the european parliament. the adjustment was legally necessary to integrate the new croatian meps, while not exceeding the 751 limit. however, i consider that this proposal was not fully satisfactory because it deviates from the strict application of the principle of proportional degressivity. nevertheless, i voted in favour of the report for two reasons. the first was that a compromise solution had to be found quickly, and this proposal provides in particular that no state should lose seats. secondly, the recommendation provides that by the end of the next parliamentary term, in 2019, the european parliament will look more closely at the issue of the distribution of seats by member state. this proposal was the subject of a broad consensus within most political groups. the draft now needs to be approved by the heads of state and government.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new distribution of the european parliament, which will take effect after the next european elections in may 2014. the lisbon treaty has fixed the number of 751 parliamentary seats for 2014, and in order to allow the arrival of croatian members of parliament, we decided that 12 member states would lose one seat and none would gain. germany loses three, austria loses one and france is spared. i found this new distribution fair, it does not lead to heavy losses for the medium and small states and increases for the large ones. the distribution of seats will be revised before the 2019 elections in order to redistribute them according to demographic trends in the member states.
in writing. article 14 (2) of the treaty on european union provides that the number of seats in the european parliament allocated to each member state is to be fixed in accordance with the principle of degressive proportionality. the report on the composition of the european parliament for the 2014 elections adopted by the european parliament at first reading denied this principle of representation of the peoples, which is one of the foundations of the european parliament. while confirming the method of calculation used for the 2014 elections, the council also stressed that for the 2019-2024 and subsequent legislative elections, the distribution of seats should be carried out in an objective, fair, sustainable and transparent manner, reflecting the principle of degressive proportionality. this is the minimum.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this recommendation even though i regret that, for fear of not being able to meet the unanimity requirement for such a decision, the so-called 'pragmatic' approach has been imposed, not allowing strict compliance with the principle of degressive proportionality, and according to which france should have had additional members. however, it is clear that this distribution will only be valid for the 2014-2019 parliamentary term and that the european parliament will have to decide within a limited period (before the end of 2016) in order to avoid the scenario experienced during this parliamentary term, which did not allow us to calmly discuss a new distribution of seats more in line with the principle of degressive proportionality. i therefore support the inclusion of a cut-off clause so that the problem of the strict application of degressive proportionality is resolved by the 2019 european elections. the future distribution can only be done in an objective, fair, sustainable and transparent way, reflecting the principle of degressive proportionality, all of which are elements to prevent any unfair reform in the future. parliament must therefore allow itself sufficient time for discussion to establish this future distribution, in order to avoid any criticism of partiality.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleagues rafal trzaskowski and roberto gualtieri at the plenary session on 12 june. this report dealt with the redistribution of seats in the european parliament for the next parliamentary term. the rapporteurs have applied the principle of degressive proportionality as laid down in the lisbon treaty. the important thing is that france will not lose any elected representatives in this reconstitution. the draft decision now has to be adopted by the heads of state or government at the next european council on 27 and 28 june. the report was adopted by a very large majority, with 574 votes in favour, 71 against and 39 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the composition of the parliament in 2014. the treaty of lisbon sets the number of meps in the european parliament at 751. the european council has already decided that the european union should be able to take part in the next european elections, and that the european parliament should be able to vote on the accession of croatia. 12 eu countries will therefore lose one seat in the next european elections, and no member state will gain one. this new distribution respects the principle of lamassoure-severin degressive proportionality and will only be valid for the next parliamentary term. the population/seat ratio of each member country will need to be reviewed before the end of 2016. france, for its part, retains all 74 seats.
in writing. the new composition of the parliament reduces the gap between france and germany. from 27 mps elected in 2009, the gap has been reduced to 22. this is a significant improvement, but it is still proportionally higher than the population gap between our two countries in favour of germany. to be strictly identical to the demographic gap, and considering that germany has 96 meps, france should have 77 meps instead of 74. the lisbon treaty has therefore not corrected the imbalance. in any event, only a perfect equality between france and germany is tolerable in accordance with the well-understood interests of europe and the lessons of history.
in writing. the council needs to confirm the decision on the fixing of the seats of the european parliament for the 2014-2019 term of office as soon as possible. for this reason i supported the adoption of this recommendation, even though it is unfavourable to french parliamentarians. the method used should have respected the principle of degressive proportionality as provided for in the treaty of lisbon, according to which france should have additional seats. however, we have obtained that this allocation can only be valid for the 2014-2019 parliamentary term, and that the european parliament should take a decision within a limited period - 2016 - for the next parliamentary term in order to discuss a new allocation more calmly.
in writing. unlike some members of my political group, i voted in favour of this motion, which is in response to a commission communication entitled 'investing in social policy for growth and cohesion, including through the european social fund, over the period 2014-2020'. as the text states, i believe it is necessary to stress 'the need to improve the coordination of economic and social policies at union level, so as to avoid disparities, develop synergies between them and enable them to reinforce each other's objectives'.

in writing. i voted in favour of the vlasak report on 'regional policy in the wider context of state aid schemes'. like the rapporteur, i am concerned about some of the commission's proposals for the next community framework for regional state aid (the eafrd), which will come into force in 2014. the reduction in the volume of aid advocated by the commission, the prohibition of aid to large firms in areas c without distinction, do not seem to me to be conducive to a less strict approach to competition policy, which is necessary in times of crisis. moreover, the discrepancy between the zoning of the eafrd and that of cohesion policy prevents greater synergies between the latter and competition policy, whereas they should be encouraged.

in writing. i voted in favour of this annual report on competition policy as it highlights the central role that competition has played in the fight against the economic crisis. competition policy has proved its worth by avoiding, in particular within the union, any form of protectionism and market fragmentation which would have had serious consequences for the economies of the member states. in times of economic crisis, competition allows new players to enter the market and thus create jobs, but also offers european citizens affordable and high-quality consumer goods. the text also recommends that competition, a fundamental principle of the european union, should be further promoted.

in writing. the eurostat statistics for april 2013 on youth unemployment are alarming: 62.5% in greece, 56.4% in spain, 42.5% in portugal, 40.5% in italy and 26.5% in france. it is more urgent than ever that the member states take up this matter and propose concrete and immediate solutions to this scourge. the rapid inflation of the number of young people out of work is sinking our economy and putting more and more young people in an unacceptably precarious situation. the commission has already proposed a number of measures, but the member states will have to take their responsibility at the european council on 27 and 28 june by encouraging the employment of young people through measures which help to reconcile enterprises with young people through education and training, but also through a taxation of enterprises more adapted to current realities.

in writing. in view of the forthcoming european summit of heads of state or government on 27 and 28 june, i supported parliament's resolution on the european plan to combat youth unemployment. since the start of the crisis, the unemployment rate for young people has been growing exponentially in the eu (23.5%), with very alarming rates in some member states such as greece (62.5%), spain (56.4%) and portugal (42%). today's young workers are tomorrow's wealth creators. it is therefore essential that the european council should decide on concrete measures and a comprehensive strategy for youth employment. in particular, we call on the member states to establish an effective strategy for youth in their national employment plans. priority should also be given to vocational training for unemployed young people. the house also welcomed the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu.
in writing. it is important to strengthen voluntary mobility among young people by removing existing barriers to cross-border apprenticeship, training and traineeship contracts. with the establishment of a youth guarantee, all unemployed young eu citizens should be offered a job, continuing training or a good quality apprenticeship within 4 months of losing their job or leaving school.
in writing. this resolution calls for an increase in the financial resources devoted to the fight against youth employment in the next european budget. that's good. that's good. but why not demand a specific amount? perhaps because the epp and the pse have approved the budget in their countries which they hypocritically contest at european level. the resolution also supports the merkel-hollande initiatives and the old liberal approaches to combating unemployment. it does not propose any new solution. and she says nothing about the austerity policy, which is the main cause of the explosion in youth unemployment. i vote against it.
in writing. access to documents and transparency of information in the eu should be a priority, and in voting in favour of this proposal we deplored the resulting deadlock. the institutions of the union must try to work together to find a solution and a compromise that is acceptable to all.
in writing. i gave my full support to this resolution because the impasse in which the revision of the regulation on access to documents of the european institutions has been since 2008 is no longer tolerable. the commission and the council must also commit themselves to greater transparency in the decision-making process. on the eve of an important election for the european union, it is their responsibility to show european citizens who have lost their confidence that europe cannot be reduced to a large bureaucracy that takes decisions away from their concerns and in the greatest opacity. the absence of an ambitious agreement on this text would be a real failure and would greatly undermine the legitimacy of the union's decision-making process. it is regrettable that the conservatives have refused to join in this effort, thus endorsing the obstacles to achieving real transparency at the expense of our fellow citizens.
in writing. the joint resolution dealt with the revision of regulation no 1049/2001 on public access to european parliament, council and commission documents, which is currently in a deadlock. although i am in favour of the principle, i did not support the joint proposal. i preferred the wording of the resolution tabled by the epp.
in writing. i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution stating that the negotiations on the revision of regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 had been closed. this text, which aims to ensure greater transparency of the union's decision-making process for european citizens, has been blocked in the council since 2011, following negotiations and trilogues. transparency has been a new priority for the union since the treaty of lisbon. greater access to union information is a key condition for ensuring european citizens' trust in their institutions and increasing their involvement. we therefore call on the commission and the council to make every effort to find appropriate measures to bring about a political agreement on this text.

in writing. the reuse of public sector information differs from one member state to another. the existence of common rules would facilitate the exchange of public sector information (with exceptions) between member states and the activity of undertakings on this market. even beyond the commercial and non-commercial benefits that european businesses could benefit from, facilitating the re-use of public sector information would also be a positive for citizens and governments. the establishment of common rules in the member states could reduce the marginal costs of producing, reproducing and disseminating documents (with the exception of public sector bodies which must generate sufficient revenue). the rules on the digitisation of documents held by cultural institutions will be reviewed at the end of the 10th year. the documents exchanged should also be available in different formats. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. the public sector has a wide range of information in a wide range of fields, including social, economic, geographical, meteorological and tourist information. in 2003, the european union adopted a directive that provides for the possibility of reusing its public sector information. it has had a positive impact on the european economy, in particular by creating new jobs. however, over the last 10 years, digital content has been continuously improving to such an extent that there is now a real data market in europe. it is therefore necessary to revise the 2003 directive to bring it into line with the current context. in addition, the introduction of a new legal framework will stimulate the economy and create new jobs. i therefore voted in favour of this text because it is perfectly suited to this.
in writing. i have approved the parliament's text on the reuse of public sector information. in the course of their activities, public administrations collect and produce information such as statistical or geographical data. this reliable and up-to-date information is a valuable resource for businesses and economic operators. the economic gain from the reuse of this data is estimated at eur 40 billion. the aim of parliament is therefore to promote transparency in public administrations while stimulating innovation and private sector growth. private information is exempt from these provisions and is protected against any illegal use.

in writing. currently, the reuse of public sector information is subject to a wide range of national interpretation. it was time to harmonise the rules at european level in order to fully achieve the objective of this legislation: to provide maximum transparency on public sector data. more specifically, the widest possible dissemination of this data would benefit everyone: citizens, businesses and even governments. however, a number of exceptions to confidentiality are necessary in certain cases. but some of this information is still not widely disseminated, due to the lack of resources for the administrations, whereas it is a source of transparency and accessibility for citizens. the harmonisation of rules at european level will therefore allow the market to take full advantage of the commercial (for businesses) and non-commercial (for administrations, ngos, citizens) opportunities offered by the re-use of public data.
