in writing. turkey is a large country and a legitimate candidate for accession to the european union and is recognised as such by the european institutions. in recent days, there has been a disproportionate and excessive repression of protests in the country. that is why our european parliament has decided to express its opinion on the situation in turkey by adopting this joint resolution. recep tayyip erdogan is democratically elected, but this should not prevent him from listening attentively to the legitimate aspirations of a part of his population to respect their rights, freedom of expression and media. turkey is playing an increasingly important role on the international scene and is becoming an indispensable player in the crises affecting the region. but its legitimacy will be complete only when it has improved its democratic institutions, strengthened the rule of law and ensured respect for fundamental freedoms.
in writing. the ongoing protest in turkey has prompted the european union to react because turkey has always been a close partner. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled by the european parliament. we have strongly condemned the intolerable violence and the growing authoritarianism of the government in power. by adopting this text, we wanted to send a strong signal to the turkish people in their fight for democracy.
in writing. i supported the joint motion for a resolution b7-0305/2013 on the situation in turkey. this resolution strongly condemns the events currently taking place in turkey. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report by the european parliament.
in writing. i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution condemning the use of excessive force by the police against demonstrators in turkey. the european parliament has voted in favour of the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. in a democratic society, we have recalled, freedom of expression for citizens and the media is a fundamental right. we therefore condemn the turkish government's violations of these principles, as well as the police's severe and disproportionate repression of the demonstrators. we demand that those responsible for police violence be brought to justice and that the government engage in a policy of dialogue and conciliation with civil society. therefore, these violations of eu rights and values prove that turkey is not ready to integrate into the european union and that many long-term reforms are needed.
in writing. the resolution has the merit of condemning the repressive crackdown currently being carried out by prime minister erdogan against the popular and peaceful protests in turkey. the congratulations in this resolution to the other leaders of the conservative religious party in power in turkey (president gühl and deputy prime minister arinç) seem to me to be misplaced. europe does not have to sort out between good and bad "religious conservatives" who have been applying the same policy of imposing religious norms on turkish society for several years at the expense of freedoms. the lessons of democracy and separation of powers addressed to turkey also seem to me to be out of place coming from a european union whose institutions are far from democratic. moreover, the call in this resolution for consensus between the government and the opposition to solve the country's problems does not seem to me to be a democratic solution that respects the will of the turkish people. i cannot therefore support this resolution, even though i share the condemnation of the violence of power which it expresses. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. europe, the cradle of human rights, has decided to condemn the acts committed in turkey in recent weeks. democracy and the fundamental freedoms it provides, such as freedom of expression for citizens and the media, are core values of the eu. turkey has long wanted to join the european union, but these acts remind us of some of the reasons why we are reluctant. it is imperative to remember that fundamental rights and freedoms are unconditional.
in writing. i voted for this resolution condemning the crackdown on protesters in turkey in taskim square. as a reminder, many protesters occupied taksim square on may 31 to protest against the cutting of trees to allow a new real estate project in gezi park in istanbul. this resolution, although imperfect, is nevertheless a resolution of solidarity with the demonstrators and denounces the attitude of the turkish government and in particular of prime minister erdogan. the police brutality is widely condemned, as is the silence of the mainstream turkish media, which i welcome. for me, these events only make erdogan's authoritarian ways visible on the international stage. and that's a good thing because it's been too long. i signed my group's amendments which recalled that this movement was a sign of the deeper problems facing the turkish people, who do not enjoy basic rights and freedoms as citizens and workers and whose living standards are not improving despite the economic growth of their country.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of a resolution on the situation in turkey, expressing our deep concern at the brutal police crackdown on protesters in istanbul's gezi park over the past two weeks. we warn the turkish government against taking harsh measures against peaceful protesters. we also ask prime minister erdogan to choose a position of unity and conciliation so as not to further aggravate the situation. what started as a simple protest against a planned urbanisation of downtown istanbul has become a national revolt against the authoritarian turkish government. police overstepped their law enforcement role, resulting in the deaths of four people and the imprisonment of more than 70 journalists. the denial of freedom of expression and the right to protest shows the authoritarian drift of the regime. those responsible for police violence must be brought to justice, peaceful protesters currently detained must be immediately released and victims compensated. this repression is clearly contrary to the principles and values which the european union is committed to defending, such as pluralistic democracy and the rule of law. the situation in turkey can only have adverse consequences on its eu accession process.
in writing. i fully supported this report by my colleagues elmar brok and roberto gualtieri, which takes stock of the functioning of the european external action service (eeas), three years after its creation. the european union is a global actor and as such, it must make its voice heard beyond its borders. in this respect, the eeas should have more ambitious action. in addition, better coordination between the diplomatic services of the 27 member states and the eeas could bring about significant economies of scale and increase both the effectiveness and the scope of action undertaken at european level. for all these reasons, it is necessary to develop the eeas to make it an indispensable actor in international relations.
in writing. when the eeas was established in 2010, it was expected that its organisation and functioning would be subject to review in mid-2013. the role of the eeas is to conduct the external policy of the european union. the rapidly changing global political and economic situation requires the eeas to adapt its activities, which must be proactive in coordinating its human and financial resources if europe is to have a significant impact on the international scene. in order to enhance the efficiency and visibility of the eeas, it is essential that foreign ministers take part more regularly in european external action. strengthening the coordinating role of the vice-president of the commission/high representative and her leadership should also improve the visibility and the power of action of the eeas. in the future, the eeas will have a key role to play in relations with third countries and external financial instruments. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of simplification and increased synergy between the council and commission services. the eeas, which was set up two years ago, is the eu's chance to see a genuine european foreign policy come into being. it is currently handicapped by structural and political problems, which is why i voted for a revision to improve the functioning with a view to unifying the crisis management units and improving recruitment. the new feature of the eeas was the creation of european delegations abroad, which are still struggling to find their place alongside the embassies of the member states. we have therefore considered the possibility of grouping together certain services provided by the diplomatic and consular services of the member states at european level to provide protection for european citizens not represented in a given country.
in writing. i supported the recommendation proposal by my colleagues elmar brok and roberto gualtieri. this proposal for a recommendation concerned the 2013 review of the organisation and functioning of the european external action service. significant progress has been made in the establishment of the eeas. however, it is clear that improvements are needed in terms of synergies and coordination between institutions, political leadership and visibility. i welcome the adoption of this proposal which highlights these needs.
in writing. the european external action service was launched in 2011. it must be the essential asset in the creation of a genuine foreign policy of the european union. to this end, it is necessary to strengthen the powers of the service, including by enshrining an increased role for the high representative as vice-president of the commission and by adapting the competences of the european delegations to meet the needs of the eu and promote its interests. i voted for this text because it is perfectly in line with this.
in writing. on thursday, i voted in favour of the revision of the organisation and functioning of the european external action service (eeas). the eeas was established in 2011 following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty to ensure the coordination and coherence of the eu's external action. under the leadership of the high representative of the union for foreign affairs, catherine ashton, the eeas promotes the emergence of a european foreign policy that safeguards european interests. with this in mind, we have decided to strengthen the political leadership of this institution and its diplomatic corps. we want to facilitate coordination between the commission and the council and give the high representative more weight. in addition, the structure of the eeas needs to be simplified in order to provide a more efficient command and a more effective crisis response system. the reform comes after the crisis in mali, where the eu failed to provide a rapid and united response.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because we will need to improve the efficiency of the european external action service. duplication with the council secretariat can be avoided and savings made. parliament's control must be strengthened.
in writing. the european external action service (eeas) is essential in the creation of a genuine european foreign policy. yet the eu's diplomatic voice is still struggling to be heard, as illustrated by its slow response to the crisis in mali. the functioning of the eeas needs to be further improved to be more efficient. in this context, this resolution, which i support, calls in particular for: - the eeas decision-making process to be more coherent, clear and cost-effective; - the role of the high representative as vice-president of the commission to be strengthened; - in unstable or fragile countries, eu delegations to be staffed with security and defence officers to have the appropriate skills to be able to effectively defend and promote eu interests in each region; - the eeas' accountability to parliament to be strengthened, with its scrutiny being essential to enhance the legitimacy of eu external action and ensure that it is understood by citizens.
mr president, mrs andrikienė's report on the promotion and protection of freedom of religion or belief contains some excellent things, but it contains many inaccuracies and sets out principles which are so broad and ill-defined that it is difficult to apply them to all the member states. it would undermine the traditional principles of some. for example, the right to observe holidays in accordance with the precepts of one's own religion. in france, by national tradition, the days of rest are fixed according to the calendar inspired by the christian history of that nation, and it would be difficult for the republic to adapt to each religion. similarly, there must be complete freedom of expression, of course, in criticism of religion, of the absence of religion or of atheism. but it cannot be used to ridicule, under the guise of blasphemy, the convictions of everyone, whose violation would undermine the right to respect for the person. i have no sympathy for the charlie hebdo cartoons and i have a lot of criticism of exhibitions such as piss christ.
in writing. i consider freedom of religion or belief to be a fundamental principle of democratic values as promoted by the eu and that is why i voted in favour of this text. the promotion of religious freedom should be one of the pillars of european foreign policy towards third countries.
in writing. in voting in favour of this resolution, i wanted to recall the importance of freedom of religion and belief, as well as pluralism and diversity in the media. recent events have shown once again that freedom of expression and the media are constantly under threat, and it is up to the eu to play a role in promoting the interdependence of cultures and in combating violence in response to free speech protests.
in writing. freedom of belief or religion is a fundamental element of our individual freedom. i support the ambition to adopt european guidelines in this area: this would make it possible to clearly state our ambitions and our action to our international partners. the european union has a responsibility to defend our values throughout the world.
in writing. i supported the own-initiative report by my colleague laima liucija andrikien in the plenary on 13 june. the report recalled the need to create an ambitious set of instruments to advance the right to freedom of religion or belief in the context of the union's external policy. i'm glad you did.
in writing. freedom of religion or belief is a fundamental right of the european union, enshrined in article 10 of the charter of fundamental rights. however, the reconciliation of this with freedom of expression is a frequent source of tension. indeed, modern media tools today contribute to a strong interdependence of cultures and times, which significantly increases the risk of ethnic conflicts. the union must therefore take measures to prevent intercultural violence. i have taken a position in favour of this text because it promotes freedom of religion or belief without threatening other freedoms and rights such as freedom of expression.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the promotion and protection of freedom of religion or belief in the world. as a defender of fundamental rights, the european union has a role to play on the international stage in promoting these principles. parliament has adopted a set of objectives and instruments to significantly improve respect for these human rights. these measures will therefore make it possible to identify more effectively and provide practical support to victims of violations of freedom of religion or belief.
in writing. the european union should promote freedom of religion or belief without threatening other freedoms or rights and should place this freedom at the heart of all the union's external action.
in writing. this report makes some concessions to the principle of secularism. he calls for the "secularisation" of public education and the denial of the existence of blasphemy offences. these are principles which are not guaranteed in many eu countries. however, the report prefers the anglo-saxon concept of "freedom of religion and belief" to the more broadly and equally protected concept of "freedom of conscience" that protects the right to believe or not to believe. however, without the protection of absolute freedom of conscience, religious freedom can lead to a strong grip of religions on public space and public debate to the detriment of secularism and the equality of citizens. i would also point out that the report considers that the right to practice a religion in a collective manner should not be limited to places of worship. despite a commitment in principle to secularism, this report does not therefore assume all the consequences. secularism is not a partial operating mode. it's global or it's nothing. i vote against it.
in writing. being fundamentally convinced of the merits and benefits that the eu could derive from a deep partnership with the united states, i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by my epp colleague francisco josé millan mon. the united states and the eu have a special responsibility on the international stage and the common values we stand for must lead us to cooperate in international forums such as the un.
in writing. according to the figures provided by the commission, the free trade agreement with the united states should allow the eu to increase its gdp by 0.5% per year within 15 years. the aim of this report, along with the figures put forward by the commission, was to assess the current state of transatlantic relations - economic, trade, political, environmental and social - not only with the united states and the european union but also with the entire american continent (north and south), and to identify the elements which could strengthen them. the report thus mentions the areas where enhanced cooperation will be essential during the negotiations: governance, human rights, security, energy, social and economic issues, the closure of guantanamo.
in writing. as negotiations for an eu/us free trade agreement have begun, this report looks at the transatlantic relationship and makes proposals to strengthen this partnership. i agreed on the need to strengthen eu-us cooperation, particularly in the areas of governance, human rights, security and energy, in order to adopt common strategies and to form a 'bloc' to maintain a strong presence on the international stage in the face of new emerging players such as china.
in writing. a broad partnership between the two sides of the atlantic is the guarantee of stronger growth and job creation, and that is why i support the conclusion of a free trade agreement, while ensuring that we do not destroy everything that makes up our identity, our specificity, and the standards that protect europeans today. but this partnership must also be political, and i support the proposals in this report, which calls for a common agenda of international objectives, or for the creation of a transatlantic political council. a genuinely strengthened cooperation will only be achieved through a strong and institutionalised dialogue.
in writing. the transatlantic relationship is based on very strong historical, political, economic and cultural links. it is important for the united states and the european union to strengthen their partnership and continue to work together. in many areas, such as global governance, human rights, international security and climate change, europeans and americans can further deepen their cooperation. however, the privileged relationship between the european union and the united states must be balanced. the recent scandal over the us prism spy programme reminds europe of the importance of being demanding in respect of its rights and independence. europe must above all defend its model of society and the interests of its citizens. the commission will have to be vigilant when it starts discussions with the us administration on a future trade and investment agreement.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is about broadening europe's horizons, which will bring about interesting long-term economic benefits for the eu. the creation of a transatlantic political council will help to maintain the eu's privileged relationship with the united states and even to penetrate the asia-pacific region more deeply. the text will thus help our states to maintain a strong position on the world stage.
in writing. i supported the own-initiative report by my colleague josé millán mon at the plenary session on 13 june. this report focused on the eu's role in promoting a broader transatlantic partnership. a comprehensive trade and investment agreement would provide a major boost to the european and american economies. it would also revive the relationship between the european union and the united states. i therefore welcome the adoption of this own-initiative report.
in writing. on thursday i voted in favour of the enlarged transatlantic partnership. on the one hand, we have stressed the importance of bilateral relations between the european union and the united states. trade between the two partners is a source of growth and employment. moreover, these two actors have a common role to play in the fight against organised crime and terrorism at global level. we also want to extend this partnership to all the countries on the atlantic coast, including latin america, the caribbean and africa. with the development of globalisation, we believe that wider cooperation will open up new growth opportunities, exploiting the potential of these emerging trade networks.
in writing. the report calls on the us and the eu to explore 'the areas and frameworks' through which wider transatlantic cooperation could be conducted. while a trade agreement with the united states could be beneficial to the union, it is nevertheless necessary to protect european interests by excluding the audiovisual sector from the negotiating mandate.
in writing. the report proposes to further strengthen the eu-us transatlantic partnership and to integrate the southern shores of the atlantic in the form of 'triangular cooperation'. he grants blind satisfaction to the us, including less credible ones such as welcoming "president obama's renewed commitment to the fight against climate change". it welcomed the launch of negotiations on an eu-us free trade agreement and called for the eu's partnership with nato to be strengthened. this strategy of aligning itself with the united states and nato has put europe in a deplorable geopolitical impasse. the report, which advocates the creation of a common 'geopolitical model' based on the integration of the two largest market economies, expresses an aggressive western imperialism towards the rest of the world, and in particular towards china and russia. i vote against it.
in writing. france has had close relations with the united states since its independence. cooperation between our two countries is paramount and must remain so. it is therefore important for us today that the european union deepen and strengthen its partnership with the americans. the creation of a transatlantic political council would allow the two great powers to discuss and propose common solutions to important global problems. this partnership must also be extended to other states in order to increase its impact, in particular the countries of asia and the pacific. with this enhanced cooperation, key areas of the world today can be addressed, such as human rights, security and economic issues. the us and the eu have a big role to play in the world of tomorrow. but we must remain pragmatic: our discussions with the united states must be conducted on an equal footing. europe is sometimes too timid and too hesitant, and this is detrimental to the assertion of our principles.
in writing. the democratic future of mali depends on the outcome of the situation in the tuareg town of kidal. the presence of minusma could be a solution to avoid any further reprisals feared by the long-persecuted tuaregs and allow the peaceful conduct of the presidential elections at the end of july . we must also ensure that the corruption in the army, which has cast heavy suspicions on the first battalion of the malian army, supervised by the european union mission in mali, is eradicated, even though we must particularly welcome the training work carried out for several months by the french militia. i would also remind you that mali is the scene of the exploitation and massive recruitment of hundreds of children, mainly boys aged 12 to 15, by the various armed movements. and that in february 2013, 86% of the students still in the north were still denied access to education due to damage to schools. i would like to recall that the restoration of mali's territorial integrity and the political transition will also have to be accompanied by a new effort to promote economic and social development.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the reconstruction and democratization of mali. it extends the debates held regularly since the beginning of 2013, which highlighted a strong demand from parliament for the european union to support france's action in that country. in my speech in plenary the day before, i had said that the elections scheduled for this summer would not be enough to ensure stability in mali. it is important that the european union remains committed to maintaining peace in the region. the fight against terrorism involves a long-term effort which must be supported by the international community, particularly in the fields of education and social cohesion. the french socialist delegation welcomed the results of the donor conference, which raised eur 3.25 billion.
in writing. the security and humanitarian situation in mali remains a matter of concern. the european union must therefore not relax its commitment to all those involved in the reconstruction of the country. the eu should engage in broader thinking to develop a strategy for the security and development of the whole sahel region.
in writing. the malian conflict is a global conflict, affecting africa, europe and the rest of the world. the challenge today is to create the conditions for peace and security: the union must draw up a roadmap to ensure the transition to the restoration of the rule of law throughout the country through the organisation of democratic elections. these elections are not an end in themselves but a first step towards a process of national reconciliation. this first political step must be accompanied by a clear and sustainable development strategy that allows mali to provide the services essential to the well-being of its people - and thus to the stability of the country. we must also make progress on the economic front and ensure that the commitments made at the donors' conference are put into practice, with the malians, and provide effective development aid. the question of the malian army is also raised. the union must help the country to set up an army that respects the institutions and is able to protect all malians throughout the country. finally, europe must not let up its ambition to secure the sahel. this means that the two inseparable aspects of development and security must be better coordinated.
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution on the reconstruction and democratisation of mali. the epp had drafted excellent amendments on this issue, which were mainly aimed at recalling the recent events in mali and to harden the language against the national movement for the liberation of azawad (mnla) which still holds the city of kidal and thus endangers the process of reconciliation between the different ethnic groups in mali. i am glad that this excellent parliamentary work has been adopted.
in writing. i supported the report on the reconstruction and democratization of mali. after the military intervention by france, it is essential that the union should embark on a project of development aid and peacekeeping support. parliament stressed the importance of democratisation, which is a prerequisite for stability in the sahel region. with this in mind, an eu election observation mission will be sent this summer to monitor the smooth running of the elections for the new government. the stakes are high, these elections represent the foundation of the future democratic society in mali. finally, we welcome the commitment of the international community to provide a total of eur 3.5 billion in financial assistance, which should allow for the full implementation of the 'strategies for security and development in the sahel' launched in march 2011.
in writing. the french intervention for the reconstruction and democratization of mali must be welcomed. mali is now in the process of political stabilisation. i welcome the establishment of a national dialogue and reconciliation commission. but the european union and the united nations must do more to support mali in this regard.
in writing. this resolution rightly notes that the resolution of mali's political and security problems is inseparable from its economic and social development. it is, however, unaware of the responsibility of the liberalization policies promoted by the imf and the european union in destabilizing the african economies in general and mali in particular. the reconstruction of a sound and just malian economy requires protection against the plundering of multinational firms and markets. although it favours the democratic way of elections to resolve the political crisis in mali, this resolution does not express itself in favour of a rapid and total withdrawal of french troops who have intervened without any real international legitimacy. i cannot support a resolution which welcomes such foreign military intervention. its extension jeopardises the return of full sovereignty of mali over its territory and affairs. i therefore abstain, noting the good intentions expressed in favour of reconstruction and democratisation but deploring the ineffectiveness of the military and trade liberalisation solutions supported by the eu in mali.
in writing. the occupation of northern mali by terrorist groups has led to numerous human rights violations: torture, extrajudicial executions, the imposition of sharia law, rapes... today, the malian president and his interim government have put in place a roadmap that organizes presidential and parliamentary elections starting in july. in addition, a commission for dialogue and reconciliation has been set up, which will bring the ethnic groups closer together and, in particular, put an end to the feeling of rejection that the tuareg feel. the resolution therefore falls within the european union's policy of providing financial support (donor conference for the revival of mali), humanitarian support (agir-sahel), military support (eutm mali) and political support. it is thanks to the efforts of the entire international community, ngos and civil society that democracy and the rule of law will be restored in mali, that human rights will be promoted and that terrorist groups will be repelled. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. i abstained on this resolution taking a position on the reconstruction and democratization of mali. it is true that the latter is primarily concerned with the future of the country and has many positive aspects, such as the need to respond beyond security problems by a long-term commitment to tackle the problems of governance, development and humanitarian aid. the resolution also welcomes the replacement of french troops by un troops and the strengthening of misma, which is an undeniable step towards a lasting multilateral solution. however, the resolution also multiplies the appreciation not only to france for its intervention but also to the union for its 'major complementary training role which provides decisive assistance for the long-term capacity building of the malian army'. the positive aspects of this are yet to be demonstrated. so there's no way i'm contributing to this operation of self-gratification. so i decided not to.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which suggests a framework for the millennium development goals beyond 2015. the millennium development goals were adopted in 2000 with the aim of meeting certain targets in terms of poverty reduction, access to water and access to education by 2015. the un must define a new framework for action in 2013, a process in which the eu will have to be involved by adopting a coordinated position.
in writing. i have approved this report, which shows both the progress made and the enormous work that remains to be done. the union is now the largest donor of aid and has shown a consistent commitment to the achievement of the millennium development goals. between 2004 and 2009, nine million children were able to access primary school and 32 million men were able to access safe drinking water. the target of halving extreme poverty has been achieved and infant mortality has decreased. however, we must not rest on these results: progress is significant, but the scale of the task to be accomplished remains enormous. the current targets do not sufficiently address the root causes of poverty or environmental damage. millions of people are still hungry or at risk of becoming so. the union has committed itself to allocating 0.7% of gross national income to official development assistance by 2015. this commitment must be respected, and it is the minimum. this is the essential role of this report: to be a call to action in the face of indifference. in this spirit, i have co-signed with charles goerens and many other members of parliament from all political parties an appeal to our governments to respect our development commitments.
in writing. adopted by the united nations in 2000, the millennium declaration sets out goals to be achieved by 2015. what can we take stock of in 2013? the target of halving the number of people without reliable access to improved drinking water sources has been achieved, as has the target of halving extreme poverty. while improvements have been made in reducing infant mortality and access to primary education, this should not be a distraction from the fact that millions of people around the world still suffer from poverty, hunger, exclusion and insecurity. it is because the european union has a decisive role to play in this debate that it was necessary to adopt a coordinated position with that of the other european institutions, in view of the united nations conference on the millennium development goals. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the millennium development goals, which list the new challenges ahead, such as poverty eradication, good governance, environmental sustainability and the eu's position on the future development framework for developing countries. i agreed with the need to provide access to health care in developing countries, especially for women and vulnerable people.
in writing. the millennium development goals are for 2015, and although immense progress has already been made, we are still far from having met all our goals. the european union must continue to affirm its strong commitment to development and better coordinate its action with that of its member states: making our action clearer is necessary if we want it to be understood and supported by all. i support the idea that special attention should be paid to the role of women in development, and i am committed to this issue.
in writing. i supported the own-initiative report by my colleague filip kaczmarek at the plenary session on 13 june. this report focused on the definition of the post-2015 framework in the context of the objectives adopted by the united nations in the millennium declaration in september 2000. many of the goals have been achieved, including halving extreme poverty, or halving the number of people without reliable access to improved drinking water sources. however, much remains to be done. the report wisely targets progress beyond 2015. it will enable the european union to engage in this debate with a coordinated position. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. on thursday, i voted in favour of the parliament's report on the millennium development goals (mdgs). launched by the united nations in 2000, the mdgs are concrete targets to be achieved by 2015, such as halving extreme poverty or halving the number of people without reliable access to safe drinking water. the house also welcomed the fact that the eu had already taken action to combat poverty in the region, and called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's policies are consistent with the eu's commitments. in this context, we have emphasised the principles of human rights, equality, non-discrimination, sustainability, good governance and coherence of development policies. in order to have an impact on the post-2015 negotiations, it is essential that the union adopt a coordinated and coherent position.
in writing. the current rate of child marriage is worrying: if it continues, about 140 million girls will become child wives by 2020. the post-2015 mdg framework should include measures to address all forms of violence against women and girls, such as harassment, rape and sexual abuse, prostitution, slavery, exploitation, murder, female genital mutilation, forced marriage, domestic violence. we also wanted to reiterate our commitment to eradicating poverty, improving access to health and education, and fighting malnutrition.
in writing. the report rightly recalls that poverty eradication is part of the millennium development goals for 2015. strangely enough, he says nothing about the growing poverty in the european union. with 24% of people living in poverty and 9% living in extreme poverty according to the latest eurostat figures for 2011, and knowing that the situation has only gotten worse since then, the european union is backsliding on the goals it says it sets for the world in this text. worse, eu policy is directly responsible for the spread of poverty in europe and where it constrains its partners. i am voting against to support the objective and to denounce the hypocrisy of the text.
in writing. while the millennium development goals (mdgs) expire in 2015, this report underlines that poverty eradication must remain the priority of the post-2015 development agenda. it also stressed the importance of respecting the principle of coherence of the european union's development policies. the report also stresses the need to meet the commitments made by member states to allocate 0.7% of their gni to official development assistance by 2015, a target that is far from being met in the vast majority of european countries. i believe it is essential to remind states of their commitments to global solidarity and to stress the many steps still to be taken in the fight against poverty. i therefore supported the report.
in writing. the united nations has set eight millennium development goals. on a first look, we see that the millennium development goals are a success for developing and middle-income countries. on the other hand, it appears that inequalities continue to grow between the states. in the wake of an unprecedented economic crisis, a redefinition of geopolitical actors, natural disasters (japan), crises in syria and mali, the european union must redefine objectives to adapt them to these changes in order to achieve the objectives set. the millennium development goals are part of the policy of the european union and the european parliament. i voted in favour of a resolution with clear objectives in terms of human rights and the promotion of freedoms. i therefore voted in favour of sexual and reproductive rights, which i regard as fundamental women's rights, in accordance with the guidelines of the french delegation to the epp. i am proud to support this resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on on the the millennium development goals. the drastic budget cuts have made it impossible to achieve the eight goals set for 2015. despite progress, 1.2 billion people worldwide still live in extreme poverty. the text reminds member states that they must honour their commitments and devote 0.7% of their gross national income to official development assistance. we must at some point decide to take account of the realities of the world and ensure that the fight against hunger, poverty and the promotion of human rights and equality do not remain mere speeches for the countries that remain the richest on the planet. i am therefore pleased that the amendments tabled by my colleague, mr mikael gustafsson, on gender equality have been adopted. however, i remain sceptical about the association of the private sector with the mdgs as a "development partner". this text, adopted by a large majority, should not remain a declaration of good intentions but a strong signal to the member states and the commission, which will shortly adopt a communication on the millennium development goals.

mhí anuas. of the european parliament, president of the european commission, distinguished leaders of the political groups and members of the european parliament, as taoiseach, i am very pleased to speak here at the european parliament this morning in this review of the irish presidency and the mff. ireland’s seventh presidency of the council concluded on sunday. it was a hectic final week, ending an extraordinarily busy and productive six months. through the support and partnership of the european parliament, ireland’s presidency did achieve very significant results. i want to thank you, the members of the parliament, for your confidence and your commitment as we discharged our presidential duties. when i last addressed this parliament it was to mark a new presidency in a new year. i spoke of what we intended to do and of the urgent need to get results. today i am proud to say in this parliament that we have achieved those. six months ago, i set out on behalf of our presidency our objectives based on the three pillars of stability, of jobs and of growth. we set out to make good on our commitments, in particular those made at the highest level of the european council. we could do no less since at this difficult juncture it was imperative that our citizens and the markets would see clear evidence that our union could and would follow through on commitments made and entered into. such follow-through has been the hallmark of the irish presidency. i believe that what we have achieved in that regard has bolstered the credibility of the european union, its role and its work in the eyes of our people and of our citizens. since we assumed the presidency after a particularly torrid period, achieving and sustaining stability was an obvious and a key objective and goal. banking union was of critical importance. we needed to repair, to restructure and to renovate our banks to do two vital things. firstly to generate sustainable economic growth and secondly to prove to our citizens they could depend on us to do what we said we would do at the meeting of heads of state and government and that was to sever the link between banks and sovereigns. the follow-through achieved in the irish presidency was seen in three further developments. firstly, the new single supervisor; secondly, stronger capital rules for banks; and, thirdly, just last week, in agreeing new rules for the winding-down of banks. these new bank resolution rules will protect taxpayers from having to bail out banks again in the future. equally in our presidency, we also worked to put in place positive drivers for growth and job creation right across europe and, when it comes to those all-important jobs and sustaining our families and our communities, trade is absolutely crucial and fundamental. therefore we concentrated on securing agreement on the mandate for negotiations for the eu-us trade talks. such agreement is essential to what should be a game-changing transatlantic partnership – one based on an equal and open relationship, and in the current circumstances i hope that that can be proven to apply. this will allow us to turn the enormous potential for jobs and growth into reality. you know that small and medium enterprises are the lifeblood of job creation, so we made europe’s small businesses a priority every step of the way. for example, we managed to achieve the political agreement that will make it easier for our small and medium enterprises to access the two trillion euro public procurement market of the european union through a simpler and cheaper bid process and with this everybody wins: more bids, governments get better value for money; our small businesses can really compete and expand and that means jobs in your countries for your citizens. research and development is something that this parliament holds very dear. the eur 70 billion horizon 2020 programme agreed in principle last week is crucial in terms of research and development. the proportion of such funds taken up by small and medium enterprises should go up by one third. but we could have done little or none of this without the close cooperation of the institutions. securing agreement with the european parliament on the eu’s common agricultural policy for the next seven years has been one of the more important achievements of this presidency. it will greatly enhance our efforts to transform our agriculture and fisheries industries into sustainable, green sectors for growth and jobs in the future. i welcome the parliament’s strong support for the eur 16 billion erasmus+ programme. like many here, i have read and understand the theories of umberto eco. we believe that it is indeed our culture and not war that cements our amazing 70-year peace. i am especially happy with work done on the european globalisation adjustment fund. this will provide real support for an important sector of our society, namely our redundant workers. can any politician here be happy with a situation where 26 million people are unemployed across the european union? i know you are not happy with that; nobody can be and this is a small but important help in that direction. we, as politicians, can never underestimate the layers or the depth of trauma and despair and disappointment of a hard worker being made redundant in any of your countries. throughout our presidency we retained and maintained a strong focus on all those important high-potential sectors, like the digital sector. equally, we made major progress on data protection and on e-identification legislation. both of which i know are central to your own parliamentary agenda here. we made headway too on issues like the european protection order, on access to lawyers in criminal proceedings and on insolvency. we concluded, successfully, the historic negotiations that will allow this union to accede to the european convention on human rights, extending the same standards of protection to our citizens in their dealings with the european union institutions as when dealing with their own governments. we have also shown significant leadership in the area of csdp (capability development, maritime surveillance and cyber security) and in addition we have laid the initial groundwork for the thematic discussion on defence at the december european council. but there has been one signal issue of ireland’s presidency, and that was our absolute commitment to ending, insofar as is possible, the blight of youth unemployment. it is an abomination against our young men and our young women, too many of whom have reached working age and have yet to know what it feels like to get up and have a job to go to every day; who have yet to realise the sense of purpose and pride and dignity of a job well done and being well done. our union has to be 100% sure that we will not allow unemployment to lock our young men and women out of their futures, out of the happy and successful lives that they could and should have with this initiative and that they could now be living. i am heartened then that in just the second month of our presidency we managed to secure the commitment of all the member states to the youth guarantee. when implemented effectively, this will give young people under the age of 25 the opportunity and the chance of training or a new job within four months of their becoming unemployed. it is clear to all of us that to tackle the scourge of unemployment among young people we must press ahead with adapting our education and training systems to 21st century norms, including partnerships with employers. to boost employment and employability we have taken important decisions on cross-border mobility, including a stronger eures job-search facility. presidency agreements on the expanded erasmus+ programme and on professional qualifications recognition will make an important contribution to this area, as indeed will agreement with parliament on the proposal on portability of pension rights. in all of this, and in particular in front-loading for the youth guarantee, we worked with you, mr president, and your parliament. everybody knows there was one other fundamental issue here and that was the mff – the multiannual financial framework – and the budget. our work on the mff has underpinned so much of our presidency endeavours and achievements. it was just last thursday in brussels that president schulz and the presidency, along with president barroso of the commission, reached a long and eagerly-awaited agreement on the multiannual financial framework. as a parliament you vote on this agreement and resolution tomorrow. you cast your vote on a complex series of texts dealing with important technical and financial matters that affect every citizen in our union. you know that the negotiations to this point were long, were difficult, were highly sensitive for both the council and parliament and indeed the commission. the results identified the best way to ensure that the almost eur 1 trillion for the mff is released as soon as possible into the real economy. i might say, mr president, that from the outset you made it clear – you made it very clear – that the priorities for this parliament were the arrangements for flexibility, for review, for revision, for own resources and for the president of the european commission. − mr president, let me first thank the taoiseach, enda kenny, for his excellent cooperation during this council presidency and very sincerely congratulate him on the impressive work and results. let me add a special thanks to the tánaiste eamon gilmore and the europe minister lucinda creighton and to all their political colleagues and civil servants for their dedication and their competence, which made this a focused and very successful council presidency. the core priorities over the last months were clearly set out at the start of the irish presidency and carefully maintained thereafter: stability, growth and jobs. we have made further progress in updating the european union’s architecture to the pressures of the 21st century economy, showing that we are learning lessons from the crisis. some of the main deliverables of the past months were in the field of financial services, where political agreements were found between co-legislators on two cornerstones of the banking union: the single supervisory mechanism and the capital requirements directive and regulation. a general approach was also agreed in council on bank resolution and recovery, on the directive and regulation on markets and financial instruments and on packaged retail investment products. a political agreement at second reading on deposit-guarantee schemes still needs to be found. indeed there has been a standstill for one and a half years. on the economic governance front, the two-pack has entered into force. the european semester method is gaining strength and we have started a debate on ex-ante coordination of major economic reforms and on the convergence and competitiveness instrument, which is the way forward to guaranteeing the responsibility of and solidarity between member states in the future. let me especially thank the irish presidency for the support given to the consolidation of the european semester. as i said in the previous debate and i will not repeat myself, now we have a much more structured and credible exercise of collective economic governance in the european union. we also made clear in the previous debate that we have made progress on measures which can help create more growth and jobs directly. today we can say that youth employment is at the top of the priorities for european union action and of course the irish presidency made certainly a very important contribution towards this. following the commission initiative, the recommendation on the european youth guarantee was adopted earlier this year. this is one of the main elements in breaking the cycle of youth unemployment. with the preparations during the past months and the decisions taken just last week we are ensuring that we will meet that challenge together. now the key is implementation. let us be under no illusions about what european-level action can do. much has to be done at national level but we have now the political momentum to make this a reality: the success of the fight against youth unemployment. during the irish presidency we also launched negotiations on a free-trade agreement with japan, and we now have a mandate to start negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership with the united states. both negotiations will be difficult and sensitive, but the potential benefits of ambitious deals would be unprecedented. ireland clearly understands the importance of the boost these deals can bring, and i thank you for your support and leadership in the council. on taxation – one of the priorities of the may european council, and which is so important for the legitimacy of every other effort we make in terms of public finances – we now have a mandate for negotiating savings and taxation agreements with non-european union third countries, as well as the council decision authorising enhanced cooperation for a directive on the financial transaction tax. in the area of enlargement, the historic decision to open negotiations with serbia was confirmed and the council agreed to open negotiations on a stabilisation and association agreement with kosovo. so it was an eventful six months, but no deal was more important than the political deal reached on the multiannual financial framework last week. last week’s agreement represents a good compromise between the interests of the member states and the objectives of the european parliament. as you know, this is the result of the longest and hardest-fought budget negotiations ever. i believe the final result sends out an important signal that the institutions of the european union are able to work together and agree on a budget that will help the european union emerge from the crisis. the commission has played its role fully, and i am happy that president schulz and the taoiseach were able to meet with me, first to unblock the negotiations and then to build on that to come to an agreement at political level on the mff. we hope this will be formally endorsed by all. the dynamics of the negotiation process, unanimity in the council and consent by absolute majority in parliament, require that all sides move towards a consensus. i want to praise all those that have worked for this objective, namely parliament’s negotiating teams – without their commitment this could not have been possible – and those from the irish presidency and the commission. for the commission, the objective has been to ensure that the future budget is workable and manageable. as you know, our initial proposal was more ambitious, but the final outcome respects those principles, maintains a necessary balance and keeps the basic structure of the initial proposal intact. from the beginning, the commission called for as much flexibility as possible, and we have strongly supported parliament in this demand. i am satisfied that this was finally achieved. the role of the parliament throughout the negotiations has been very significant and successful. in addition to the flexibility of payments and commitments, parliament was able to secure a number of important breakthroughs. let me just mention some of them: on the midterm review of the mff, on support for measures against youth unemployment, education, research and smes, on the consolidation of the programme of aid to the most deprived and the clear commitments regarding the amending budget for 2013, which need to be fully honoured. i would also like to remind you of the decisions concerning the follow-up on the issue of own resources. taken together, they show how parliament was able to use its consent power responsibly and effectively. for this reason, after member states in the council have already given the mff their full backing, i hope this house, in its political resolution, will also support it tomorrow. we need this budget, not for the european union institutions but for our citizens and our regions, particularly those that are in a more difficult situation where investment from the european union makes up by far the lion’s share of public investment. in the context of the mff, i also need to refer to the very important achievements on some of the sectoral mff programmes during the irish presidency. let me name just a few of them as examples. an important agreement was reached on the reform of the common agricultural policy after 2013 – which was another of the irish priorities – strengthening the position of farmers within the food production chain, making direct payments fairer and greener and making the cap more effective and more transparent. an agreement on the reform of the common fisheries policy was also reached. there is now a political deal for other sectoral mff proposals, some of them very innovative and a source of special pride at the commission, such as cosme for smes, the connecting europe facility, creative europe, erasmus+ and horizon 2020. to conclude, the irish presidency had all the elements of a successful one: a clear set of priorities, genuine political commitment, technical knowledge and drive, and a safe pair of hands to manage it all, as well as the capacity – as the taoiseach underlined – to build on and reinforce the relationship of trust and respect between the presidency of the council and the european institutions such as the european parliament and the european commission. thank you for your hard work and close cooperation. we will all benefit from that in the next six months which, under the lithuanian presidency – the first ever lithuanian presidency – promise to be just as important for europe’s economic and political future.

mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr commissioner, i should first like to thank the irish presidency. it has gone beyond a negotiating mandate which was terribly constrained by the requirement of unanimity. i would also like to pay tribute to the whole team of rapporteurs for their outstanding collective work and thank the commission. parliament has shown realism. the european budget is financed by national budgets, and national budgets are ruined. it was not possible to obtain higher figures. with such figures, will the union be able to finance the objective it has set itself? no, you can't! and daniel cohn-bendit was right to say that. so what do you do? first, reopen the whole case very quickly. the new commission, the new parliament and the council will be able to work on it as from 2016. secondly, to lay the foundations for autonomous financing of the union budget. a new procedure will be launched in the autumn. the national parliaments will be associated in a kind of european mini-convention. finally, better and faster use of scarcer resources to promote employment for young people, investment in the future and aid for the poorest. no, this compromise does not save europe, but it does finance the most urgent needs and it sets out a method and a timetable for a lasting solution to the present budgetary impasse. i recommend that parliament accept it. in accordance with this political agreement, we will proceed to the legal vote at the beginning of the year, when the council has adopted the necessary payment appropriations for 2013.
