in writing. i voted in favour of amending the staff regulations of european civil servants, with a view to saving money and modernising the european civil service. at a time when great efforts are required of our fellow citizens, it was important to take this into account and apply the same efforts to union officials. we have therefore approved the freezing of salaries for two years, the raising of the retirement age from 63 to 66 for new civil servants and to 65 for those already in office. these new constraints have been calculated on the basis of the union average, so that the efforts required of national civil servants are also applied to european civil servants.
in writing. we need to ensure that europeans' money is used efficiently, and that is why i support the spending reduction measures in this proposal. the citizens are particularly attentive to these issues and will be able to recognise the improvements contained in this text. this status raises questions, particularly with regard to the provisions on working time. the text is therefore moving in the right direction, towards greater efficiency in the european civil service.
in writing. the status of european civil servants is often the subject of discussion. it is undeniable that this status is advantageous compared to the practice (pay, working conditions, taxation, etc.) of a majority of european states. far from the original few hundred civil servants, it now affects almost 50,000 people and is in dire need of reform. the report does not go far enough, but at least it is moving in the right direction. but the problem is not that the european public service is not responsible for the eu's shipwreck. it executes and implements the increasing number of competences that national governments have transferred to brussels. now, more than ever, is the time to take back power.
in writing. i voted against the reform of the staff regulations of european civil servants, which provides for an increase in the retirement age. not a word about the precarious salaries, which are numerous in the european institutions, nor about the differences in salaries, which are nevertheless considerable: a language teacher, who is of course outsourced, may earn up to 10 times less than his student. the report's main measure is a two-year pay freeze for civil servants. what purpose? to claim that austerity is more just because it is shared by those who implement it. but there is no justification for austerity measures to be imposed by an unelected institution. the report does not call into question the salaries of certain european officials who are paid handsomely to be the enforcers of austerity and to justify, in a supposedly scientific way, the budgetary consolidation that is bleeding the peoples for nothing. first of all, we must change the way they are taxed. for french civil servants, for example, the difference between the community tax and the tax which should have been paid in france should be paid to the french state. this is the differential taxation proposed by the left front for all french nationals during the presidential campaign.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague dagmar roth-behrendt. this report dealt with the amendment of the staff regulations and the conditions of employment of other servants of the european union. it rightly pointed out in particular that, despite the current crisis, the reduction in the number of staff in the union institutions and agencies entailed risks and could lead to the union institutions and agencies being prevented from carrying out their tasks and duties. i welcome this position taken by the european parliament.
in writing. the economic and financial crisis has forced governments to take difficult but necessary decisions to return to the path of fiscal stability. the european union welcomes these efforts and continues to encourage them to continue the reforms undertaken. so, at a time when the question of the status of civil servants is being raised, it seems to me that it is right to reform the european civil service. that is why i have decided to support this text, because it is aimed at saving money and modernising the service. the increase in the retirement age from 63 to 66 and the introduction of a new solidarity levy seem to me to be justified.
in writing. this report rightly criticises the european commission's intention to make drastic savings at the expense of staff, especially the lowest paid. the commission thus uses the pretext of a partial revision of the staff regulations of european officials, necessitated by the expiry of certain transitional provisions, to propose a very broad revision of the staff regulations motivated solely by accounting considerations. while expressing this right criticism and calling for the commission to substantially amend its proposal, the report nevertheless endorses such false and retrograde ideas as the raising of the retirement age which would be made necessary by demographic change. this led the commission to propose raising the minimum retirement age for european civil servants from 63 to 65 and to encourage them to work until they are 67 or even 70. i am voting against this report which, despite the criticisms of the commission's accounting blindness, deals a severe blow to the right to retire.
in writing. − at present, several eu member states are faced with a choice of economic priorities trying to maintain traditional but costly social guarantees or re-engineering the national economy to boost competitiveness in the long term, thus ensuring jobs and economic growth. faced with the financial and economic crisis, the latvian government reacted to the situation by significantly reducing budgetary expenditure, including public administration expenditure. similar action is also needed at eu level, especially in view of the fact that the eu budget for the next programming period is smaller than initially planned. i believe that the salaries and social guarantees of officials in the eu institutions must also be in line with economic trends in europe, which also means that we cannot ask member states to take austerity measures without also introducing them into the eu administration. i did not vote in favour of the amendments proposed by the ep's legal affairs committee, which made the report more accessible, because, although it contains necessary changes such as the extension of the working week to 40 hours a week, it does not include several important reforms from the european commission's original proposal. this applies both to the various types of basic salary allowance and to pensions, which the legal committee report unfortunately proposes to keep within the existing limits. i also consider that the proposal for a reduction in the salaries of civil servants contained in the commission's proposal was adequate, especially when compared with the salaries of civil servants in the poorest eu member states.
in writing. i have chosen to vote against the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the staff regulations of officials and the conditions of employment of other servants of the european union. under pressure from the trade unions, progress has been made on the commission's initial proposals. this explains why the proposal put before the european parliament had the support of these organisations. but i cannot support a text which does not take into account the situation of precarious workers, those who receive the lowest, even the very lowest, salaries, many of whom are employed in the european institutions, contrary to the image usually given to them from outside. moreover, as a matter of consistency, how can we support a text which raises the retirement age from 63 to 65?
in writing. the international nuclear liability regime is governed by the vienna convention - adopted to provide adequate and equitable compensation for victims of damage caused by nuclear accidents - and the paris convention. since the vienna convention was amended by the 1997 protocol and the paris convention by the 2004 protocol, the commission proposed that the council authorise bulgaria, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland, the czech republic, romania and slovakia, which are contracting parties to the vienna convention, to ratify or conclude the 1997 and 2004 protocols. accession to the protocol is optional for these five states.
in writing. i voted in favour of ratifying the protocol of amendments to the vienna convention convention establishing a system of compensation for victims of damage caused by nuclear accidents and a special regime for civil liability in the field of energy. the problem is that some member states are not members of the convention; some are members of the paris convention on the same subject. there is therefore a real heterogeneity among european states in terms of nuclear damage. the aim of this report was therefore to articulate the various schemes. to put an end to these misunderstandings, the commission will soon be proposing a proposal to establish the primacy of european law over international conventional law, which will oblige all european states to respect european rules, which take precedence over the various international conventions.
in writing. with this text, we are ensuring that victims of nuclear damage can obtain compensation in the same way, regardless of their country of origin. this harmonization of our rules will make it easier for victims to read, and most importantly, more justice for all.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which proposes a fundamental reform for greater coordination between member states on the nuclear issue. the text allows some central and eastern european countries to adopt the 1997 protocol amending the vienna convention. the text thus makes it possible to harmonise the european regime of nuclear liability, thereby leading to greater coherence within the european union.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague alajos mészáros. the report concerned the commission's proposal to allow member states which are contracting parties to the vienna convention on civil liability for nuclear damage to ratify or conclude the 1997 protocol amending it. this proposal is a step in the right direction and was particularly concerned with the countries of eastern europe. so i had no reason to object.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft legislation on the vienna convention on civil liability for nuclear damage. this convention, adopted in 1960, establishes an international regime for the rules of compensation for civilian victims of nuclear accidents. in 1997, a new protocol amended the jurisdiction and enforcement of judgments. the european union has therefore acquired competence in this area. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. this is the case for bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia. the european framework will therefore be more widely applicable, providing better protection for victims of nuclear damage.
in writing. the intention to improve compensation for victims in the tragic event of a nuclear incident is commendable. she admits the danger. two points raise a problem: firstly, although the vienna convention and the paris convention are very similar texts, the commission does not solve, by this text, the problem of legislative distortion in civil liability for nuclear damage. the method of inducing a state at european level to ratify an international convention seems to me to be akin to interference. it does not correspond to a procedure provided for in the treaties. i would not accept that this method be used for france; i cannot accept that it is for another state. by abstaining, i support the improvement of victim compensation and i disagree with the method adopted by the commission.
in writing. i voted in favour of reforming the state aid regime so that it contributes more to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and is truly part of a process of consolidating public finances. the main points are to increase controls by the competent authorities and to improve the handling of complaints. state aid is a key instrument of the state, especially in the current crisis, but it must be used in a way that does not represent a disproportionate obstacle to competition.
in writing. if we want public money to be used in the best possible way, to create growth and jobs in the fairest possible way, we need more efficient state aid. that is why i support the reform of this regulation, which, in the more general context of the reform of state aid, will make it possible to improve the efficiency and transparency of procedures.
in writing. the reform of state aid procedures must above all improve the effectiveness of state aid control. the text does this by advocating improved complaint handling and more efficient information gathering from market players. i voted in favour of this text because it represents a necessary reform of state aid.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague sirpa pietikäinen. the report focused on improving the handling of complaints and establishing efficient and reliable information collection from market participants. it is part of a general drive to modernise the european union's state aid policy. i am therefore pleased that it was adopted by a large majority of members: 651 votes in favour, 26 against and 33 abstentions.
in writing. on tuesday i voted in favour of the report on the application of article 93 of the ec treaty to modernise eu state aid policy. in theory, public subsidies granted by a national government to support domestic activities are contrary to eu law and the principle of free competition. however, the union does allow and provide a legal framework for certain exceptions where the action is in the public interest. the objective of this report is to redirect aid towards the europe 2020 strategy and the consolidation of public finances. we also want to reform the complaints procedure for sanctioning states which do not comply with the union's conditions, by means of a faster and more efficient handling of cases which are most damaging to the single market.
in writing. this report supports the reform of state aid control proposed by the european commission. in the name of free and undistorted competition, this hunt for state aid is already responsible for the absurd prohibition of public financing of certain productive activities of general interest or the dismantling of certain public undertakings. the proposed reform would further strengthen the commission's powers of investigation and control over the states, with the aim of concentrating controls on the largest state aids. i am voting against these new weapons given to the european commission against state aid.
in writing. in the european union, aviation represents €365 billion and 5.1 million jobs. in the face of the challenges posed by aviation, the commission published a communication, which is the basis for this own-initiative report, on the challenges facing the european union: some regions of the world are proposing more favourable legislation for the construction of modern airports, which should lead the european union to look at its airport capacity at the risk of european travellers moving towards these new, more competitive infrastructures. the european union must consider the investments needed to change its airport infrastructure. initiatives to improve the service and safety of european passengers and to support european airlines to remain competitive on the world market have already been launched to meet its challenges: the new generation air traffic management system (sesar), the clean sky initiative and the european aviation safety agency (easa). in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the amendment to the european aviation policy, which aims to combat distortions of competition caused by the practices of certain foreign airlines to the detriment of european airlines. in europe, state aid is granted to certain local airlines for the opening of regional routes to the detriment of other airlines, thus creating a de facto distortion of competition. it was therefore proposed to revise the community guidelines on state aid and start-up aid. it is important to regulate aviation effectively, as this is a key sector for the future (forecasts of 5% growth per year until 2030, mostly outside the european union).
in writing. i voted in favour of the marinescu report, which gives a very fair account of the situation at airports and in the aviation sector in the european union. i agree with his view that improving the competitiveness of this sector so that eu airports are of the highest international standard is also an asset for its reputation and attractiveness. like the rapporteur, i believe that the decoupling of the single market in the area of single sky regulation should be accelerated. i also think it is vital to put the principles of reciprocity and fair competition at the heart of the union's external strategy for aviation, otherwise companies in the sector will probably be denied access to new markets. finally, in the framework of bilateral agreements governing cooperation in the field of aviation with third countries, it is also important to set minimum standards to be respected in order to avoid a 'less-than' regulation which is detrimental to passengers' rights.
in writing. europe is the world's leading tourism market: the european aviation sector has everything to gain from this success and must urgently seize the opportunities this situation offers it, in order to become a real springboard for growth and employment. with this text, we are putting in place measures to support this sector and help it to combat certain unfair practices of its competitors. i particularly welcome the emphasis on the role of gnss: the european satellite navigation system will be a key tool to better respond in real time to passenger needs, through the improvement of our monitoring and navigation tools.
in writing. the aviation sector plays a major role in the european economy. it represents 2.4% of european gdp and connects our continent to the rest of the world through a very dense network of airports. although european aviation is efficient, it faces very strong competition, especially from the gulf countries which subsidize their airlines. the european union must therefore develop an aviation policy aimed at guaranteeing fair conditions of competition with the airlines of the partner countries, but also increasing its investments in the sector to become more competitive. airbus, for example, is one of the most successful examples of european economic cooperation. finally, europe must work within the international civil aviation organisation to create a global system for the exchange of co2 emissions.
in writing. with competition raging in the global and european aviation market, it was important to remember that the rules of the game must be fair to operate in an open and undistorted market. the european union must react as quickly as possible and support the aviation sector in its transformation by adopting tools to support and combat any form of market distortion. protecting the aviation industry means protecting the competitiveness and attractiveness of the 5.1 million jobs in our territories, but also protecting our network of regional air services so important for our citizens! our manufacturers are faced with the emergence of new players, especially from asia, taking advantage of permissive legislation. but the battle is also between airports; if the union does not invest rapidly in its airport infrastructure, the global connecting platforms will shift to those same regions where heavy infrastructure investments are now paying off. and not to mention our airlines, which are now fighting against the emergence of asian companies with substantial funding, but also against the incredible growth of low-cost airlines. i welcome this position of the european parliament. a strong europe is an open and competitive europe, but also a europe that protects and acts in the interests of its citizens.
in writing. i supported the own-initiative report by my colleague marian-jean marinescu. this report focused on aviation, a key sector of the european economy. new challenges are being launched from parts of the world where much more permissive legislation exists. this report rightly points out the areas where progress is needed to cope with the crisis. the commission is proposing to increase the capacity of airports in the european union so as not to risk becoming less competitive. the rapporteur also stressed the worrying delay in the implementation of the single european sky and the sesar system. the report was adopted by a very large majority: 650 votes in favour, 54 against and 5 abstentions.
in writing. i supported the parliament's vote in favour of the eu's external aviation policy. in the european economy, aviation is a key sector employing 5.1 million people and contributing over €365 billion to the eu's gdp. however, competition from emerging powers, notably from asia-pacific, the middle east and south america, is threatening the european aviation sector. indeed, giant airports are being built or planned in these geographical areas, and risk diverting some of the airport activity outside the european continent. the union therefore needs a strong external policy and a long-term development strategy to remain competitive in the aviation sector. we must support european industry in this area and anticipate the expansion and modernisation of our airport infrastructure. in addition, cooperation at eu level, such as the single european sky programme, needs to be stepped up.
in writing. the aviation sector is a sector in the midst of change. the global market is important for european aviation and difficult in view of international competition. better cooperation is needed at european level. we should focus on air agreements at eu level rather than at national level as is the case. in order to remain competitive, incumbent airlines and new low-cost carriers should engage in a dialogue to share the market. state aid must not be an obstacle to fair competition.
in writing. i have chosen to vote against the resolution on the european union's external aviation policy. this resolution highlights the importance of the aviation sector to the european economy. the sector employs more than 5.1 million people. this sector has indeed undergone many changes since 2005. but behind the 'progress' highlighted in the report, the sad reality is the creation of an increasingly fierce competition that is developing at the global level but also between european actors. european aviation is indeed facing many new competitors from the asia-pacific, middle east and south america regions, but it is also facing more and more low-cost operators with shameful social and commercial practices that are gaining ground. the results are worrying: worsening working conditions, a lack of concern for the safety of passengers and crew. in short, there is no safeguard against the increasingly unbridled liberalisation of the sector, so it is a vote against without feeling.
in writing. the purpose of export credits is to support trade and investment by european companies in international trade. in 2010, as part of the update of the oecd provisions on export credits in eu legislation, parliament negotiated stricter reporting requirements. these were first implemented in 2011. in this own-initiative report, the inta committee, of which i am a member, welcomes the efforts made to improve and guarantee transparency. it is also worth noting the action of some member states which tend to report in a clear and transparent manner on their compliance with certain objectives of the european union's external action. in the light of the information available, i have voted in favour of this own-initiative report.
in writing. export credits support trade and investment by european companies in international trade. the rules in terms of declarations were strengthened in 2011; the commission therefore provided us with the conclusions of its observations for 2012. i voted in favour of this report to welcome the commission's efforts to increase transparency at eu level and for its cooperation with the other bodies (council working party and eeas) in setting up a sound information methodology in line with the oecd guiding principles.
in writing. export credit is a key tool for our companies to expand internationally. it is important to point out, however, that we do not have all the relevant information on this issue, which is regrettable: such a lever for growth and influence for our companies must not remain in the dark, it must be possible to evaluate it in order to derive full benefits from it.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on export credit agencies in the member states. the task of these national bodies is to assess the conformity of export credits with european rules. each year they publish a report to the institutions of the union on the activities of the states. the parliament noted that these reports did not make it possible to determine whether the actions of the states were in conformity with european law or not. therefore, a common methodology should be established to guide the procedure and content of the annual accounts. in addition, the assessment of the environmental risks associated with the exports of the member states must be given special attention, with a view to establishing a comprehensive strategy to reduce the carbon footprint of our economic activities.
in writing. this report welcomes the assessment by the european commission of the activity of national export credit agencies and their compliance with the objectives of the european union. it stresses the importance of these public export subsidies for the european economy. but it does not address the ecological impasse created by the priority given to exports, which multiply the ecological footprint of production. it is thus silent on the objective of relocating productive activities. to this end, public support for export sectors of general interest should be combined with mechanisms of solidarity protectionism which will enable each state not to see its economy destroyed by free trade. the report also welcomes the eu's efforts to put trade policy at the service of human rights and the fight against climate change. but he is silent on the current negotiation of a free trade agreement with the united states which is jeopardizing these very objectives. i am not going to vote for a report which, despite its good intentions, ignores such important issues as the environment and freedom.
in writing. export credits are an instrument designed to support trade and investment by european companies in international trade. they are very important for the international development of our companies because they provide them with great opportunities for trade and exchange. in 2011, new reporting obligations were introduced for member states to increase transparency in the credit institutions system. it is important that the member states continue their communication efforts to harmonise these appropriations and that new rules can be developed to promote the proper functioning of this system. in addition, the oces have to comply with a number of rules, they have to be in line with eu objectives, and these communications by the member states allow for more effective control and therefore greater effects of the appropriations. only by ensuring european political coherence can the eu become a reliable and influential player at the global level. this report demonstrates the effectiveness of communication, so that export credit agencies are more efficient and more equal between states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the regulation of export credit agencies (eca). these state-guaranteed bodies offer credit, insurance and guarantees to private european companies operating abroad, particularly in developing countries, under financial and political conditions which can be risky. but these funds are mainly used to finance projects which are not transparent and whose dramatic environmental and social consequences are well known. in 2011, the estimated value of member states' ceos actions was €250 billion - almost double the annual budget of the union by comparison. the resolution could have gone further, for example by requiring member states to include representatives of ngos and trade unions in the monitoring of the activities of these bodies. i have nevertheless voted in favour of this report, which is in favour of greater transparency in this area.

in writing. port state control ensures a harmonised inspection system and the detection of ships that do not meet the defined control standards. port state control within the european union is governed by the paris memorandum of understanding on port state control of ships, signed in 1982 by 27 states. the aim of the inspection is to ensure maritime safety by means of inspection. in addition, a list of countries at risk (countries whose ships are not in compliance with the conventions in force in the maritime field) is drawn up. the non-normative memorandum has three objectives: the protection of human life at sea, the prevention of marine pollution by ships (such as the erika disaster), and the respect of standards of living and working on board ships. it should be noted that the control of foreign vessels calling at ports of call applies only in the ports of signatory countries. in order to ensure the effectiveness of controls and the harmonisation of inspection procedures, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of a change in the procedures for inspection of ships by port authorities. ships arriving in ports may be subject to controls by the authorities and may, where appropriate, be denied access if they do not comply with the conditions imposed by the port authorities. port inspection procedures at european level are part of the wider framework of the paris memorandum on port controls, which also includes non-european countries for better convergence of procedures between states.
in writing. port state control of ships, this allows us to ensure that any ship calling at a port in the union must comply with the international standards to which we adhere. this is obvious if we are to protect not only the seafarers, their lives and working conditions, but also our marine environment. the maritime labour convention is a key instrument in this respect and i therefore welcome the fact that this proposal for a directive aims to complete the integration of this convention into european ship inspection mechanisms.

in writing. the directive on state control of ports voted by the european parliament is a step in the right direction. the european parliament recognises that there is insufficient control by masters and flag states of compliance with the relevant rules on board, and calls on the european union to put in place mechanisms to verify that the relevant standards are applied on board all ships calling at european ports, irrespective of the nationality of the seafarers or the flag of the ship. this directive is theoretically the beginning of the fight against flags of convenience. the report is also a milestone in the fight against social dumping at sea, since it sets minimum standards for working and living conditions on board ships. this report does not solve all the problems of flags of convenience or compliance with labour law at sea, but it can bring new rights to employees. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which aims to ensure that the sea is not a zone of no-go, in the hope that it will be implemented.

in writing. this report is part of the technical inspection package, which has three components: periodic technical inspections, road technical inspections of commercial vehicles and vehicle registration. the aim of the current regulation is to introduce additional checks for commercial vehicles. the type of vehicle will be selected according to the risk profile of the farms (the more at risk the enterprises are, the more their vehicles will be checked), a profile established on the basis of previous road and technical checks (number and severity of the failures found). the checks will be extended to light commercial vehicles. the number of road checks per year and per member state will depend on the number of registered commercial vehicles. how will these checks be carried out? step by step: initial verification and further roadworthiness check based on the result of the first inspection. these checks will also cover the stowage of the load (as stowage problems can cause up to 25% of accidents involving trucks). the report also addresses the question of equal treatment by harmonising standards for the assessment of failures, the level of knowledge and competence of inspectors, etc. in view of these factors, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. this report amends the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council aimed at harmonising european roadworthiness testing standards for commercial vehicles. it proposes that member states establish a classification of union undertakings whose vehicles pose a risk to road safety and that targeted road checks on commercial vehicles be used only as a complement to the mandatory periodic technical checks. the report recommends a combination of administrative simplification of controls and harmonisation of european standards from the top. i vote for this report.
in writing. i voted for the exclusion of motorcycles and i regret that a majority preferred to include them in the scope of the technical control package. in my view, the introduction of compulsory controls for two-wheel drive is not appropriate. the studies on which the european commission based its proposal for inclusion are controversial. they do not in any way prove the effectiveness of these controls. i also believe that in this area it is up to the member states, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, to decide on their own rules. the union does not, in this particular case, have any added value. i therefore voted against the kuhn report. let us now wait to see what we can do in the negotiations between the council and parliament to bring this proposal back into balance.
in writing. this report is part of the technical inspection package, which has three components: periodic technical inspections, road technical inspections of commercial vehicles and vehicle registration. the current regulations set minimum standards for the periodic inspection of motor vehicles (except scooters and motorcycles). the report provides that two- and three-wheel vehicles are also covered by these checks. in addition, checks will be carried out on the basis of variables such as age and annual mileage (the older the vehicle and the longer the vehicle is running, the more it will be checked). the controls will respond to and follow defined inspection methods, while inspectors will need to demonstrate a certain level of competence and knowledge in order to carry out quality controls. it should be noted that any controls carried out by approved private bodies will be subject to national supervision. any evaluation will be carried out in a harmonised manner in all the countries of the european union. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of a technical control for large wheels of 2 or 3 cylinders, which should be gradual and more flexible than that imposed on cars, because i believe that road safety is not just about motorists, we have a duty to protect motorcyclists. from 2016, abs or other braking systems will be mandatory on large cylinders, and even though the 2 wheels are the subject of special mechanical attention on the part of the owners of these vehicles, no one can control an abs system without the appropriate electronic machines. the text adopted by parliament will be the subject of negotiations with the council. whatever the outcome of these negotiations, i hope that the objective of ensuring better safety for motorcyclists will be achieved and that a balanced agreement satisfactory to all will be found.
in writing. i am disappointed by the adoption of this report, which enshrines the obligation of technical inspection for two-wheelers, which i do not think is in the consumer's interest, by introducing more bureaucracy and complexity in obtaining and maintaining such vehicles.
in writing. i support the ambition to improve the harmonisation of our technical control rules: allowing motorists to move from one european country to another subject to the same safety requirements is a matter of course if we want to give substance to the freedom of movement so fundamental to our union. however, i could not vote in favour of this text because the exclusion of two-wheelers was not approved by the vote of the members. this measure is unacceptable because it is disproportionate and imposes too great a burden on two-wheelers, without any real evidence of its effectiveness in reducing road accidents.
in writing. the final text proposed the introduction of a technical inspection for two-wheelers. i could not therefore vote for it, because it went against all the efforts made in the committee on transport to exclude this type of vehicle from the negotiations. to date, no reliable and independent studies have been able to demonstrate the effectiveness of this measure in reducing the number of deaths on our roads. it therefore seems inconceivable to impose a requirement representing such a cost to the motorcyclist's wallet without measuring the real impact on their safety.
in writing. i voted in favour of excluding two-wheelers from the draft harmonised technical control in the european union. i regret, however, that this position has not been followed by a majority in the european parliament. i am firmly opposed to the introduction of compulsory technical inspection for these types of vehicles. but the part is not totally lost in that the text adopted today will be submitted to the member states. a majority of them are opposed to the inclusion of two-wheelers. i am also pleased to see that the frequency of these checks is maintained at two years and not reduced to one year for other vehicles. the increase in the frequency of technical inspections for cars seems to be in contradiction with their technological evolution which makes them more reliable for longer. moreover, as older vehicles are usually owned by drivers with modest incomes, the intensification of controls would have resulted in a heavy burden for their owners. finally, it is up to each member state to assess whether this is appropriate.
in writing. the european parliament has accepted the amendments tabled by the socialist, green and liberal groups calling for the reintroduction of compulsory technical inspections for two-wheel vehicles, although these same amendments were rejected in the votes in the committee on transport. it is a regrettable decision, not based on any tangible scientific evidence. the european commission's studies, which establish a correlation between road accidents and the absence of technical inspections for two-wheelers, are questionable, since they were carried out by the company which itself carries out the technical inspections in germany! i would remind you that the member states have themselves spoken out against the technical inspection of two-wheelers. at present we cannot predict the approach that will be taken for two-wheelers. the relevant provisions will be the subject of negotiations between the council and the european parliament. i remain hopeful that an acceptable solution can be found.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague werner kuhn. this report focused on the alignment of the inspection frequency of high mileage vehicles with that of older vehicles. it also dealt with the proposal to introduce new requirements concerning several aspects of the quality of controls. this report is part of the 'technical inspection' package, which aims to promote and enforce the rules on the technical inspection of motor vehicles and their trailers in order to improve road safety and environmental protection. i can only support such proposals. i therefore welcome the adoption of the amended proposal by the european parliament.
in writing. directive 2009/40/ec sets minimum standards for periodic checks and applies to passenger cars, heavy goods vehicles, coaches and buses but not to scooters and motorcycles. however, for several years now, the european union has been trying to generalize technical inspection by making it compulsory for both wheels. i am firmly opposed to this initiative because, firstly, its usefulness has not yet been demonstrated and, secondly, it would again be a penalty for the most modest households, many of whom have only this means of transport to get to work. that is why i opposed this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the periodic technical inspection of motor vehicles and their trailers. in order to reduce the number of road accidents in europe and to ensure better protection of the environment, we have decided to increase the frequency and to impose stricter rules on the technical inspection of passenger cars, buses and coaches, and heavy goods vehicles. the aim is to guarantee a high level of safety on all european roads. the new conditions also apply to trailers of more than two tonnes and caravans of more than 750 kg.
in writing. this report amends the proposal for a parliament and council regulation on the european harmonisation of periodic technical inspection standards for four-wheel vehicles and trailers. despite its desire to give priority to harmonisation of technical inspection standards at the top, to maintain the sovereignty of the member states in the implementation of inspections, to improve prevention rather than repression, and to ensure the independence of inspectors, this report largely gives priority to safety standards over environmental standards. for this reason, i abstain.
in writing. the draft european regulation on the unified technical inspection of motor vehicles provides for the imposition of a technical inspection on two-wheelers at the same frequency as on motor cars. i am opposed to this measure and have argued that motorized two-wheelers and three-wheelers should be excluded from the scope of this regulation. the technical inspection of motorcycles is not currently compulsory in france and this decision would impose significant costs on motorcyclists. furthermore, while very few accidents are due to poor maintenance of two-wheelers, this decision does not take sufficient account of the reality of the situation. i therefore opposed the report.
in writing. i was opposed to the introduction of a technical control for two-wheelers, which was clearly disproportionate: the commission relied on studies of dubious reliability to propose a measure at a significant cost to motorcyclists. we believe that the commission should have carried out a proper comparative impact study beforehand. there are lobbies behind this proposal. control centres and other commercial forces want to create a new market for themselves by standardizing technical controls across the union. the increase in the frequency of vehicle checks seems excessive to us; that is why we also rejected it in the committee vote.
in writing. the commission wanted to amend the legislation on technical inspection. the commission wanted to include new vehicles such as motorcycles in the periodic technical inspection. road safety is very important, but i am not sure that imposing roadworthiness tests on new vehicles like these would reduce road accidents. there is no evidence of any causal link between road accidents and possible technical problems with motorcycles. it would be appropriate for the european commission to carry out a thorough investigation establishing the link between the two before taking such a decision. and in that case, we might decide to take steps to protect road users. it is regrettable that the other members did not follow this, albeit relevant, position. motorcyclists take special care of their motorcycles, so asking them to do a technical check will result in extra, excessive and unnecessary expenses.
in writing. i abstained on this resolution on periodic vehicle inspections. the proposal contains provisions for improving road safety. it thus extends the scope of mandatory checks to the groups of road users most at risk. it also increases the frequency of checks for vehicles over six years old (annual checks rather than biennial checks) or with a high mileage (160 000 km). it also provides for improvements in the quality of controls by establishing common minimum standards for faults and equipment. however, this resolution ignores the root of the problem. those who own old vehicles are the poorest employees who live far from their workplaces and have little access to public transport. we can therefore ask ourselves what motivates the european institutions to legislate in this way, and we can ask ourselves whether the measures chosen are appropriate. that is why i supported the requests of the motorcyclists and i am glad that they have been given a period of time in the hope that it will allow them to ask the right questions. i am also glad that the vote is not final and that the text has been referred back to committee.
in writing. the european parliament voted by a very narrow majority to introduce periodic technical inspections of motorcycles and scooters from 2016. i have personally opposed the introduction of a two-wheeler technical control: as it stands, this measure is grossly disproportionate. the commission relied on studies of dubious reliability to propose a measure at considerable cost to motorcyclists. we believe that the commission should have carried out a proper comparative impact study beforehand. the commission has also proposed to increase the frequency of technical checks on motorists. i also rejected this measure, which was rejected by parliament. after this vote, the directive will now be renegotiated between the institutions. the council has already adopted a position against the extension of technical inspection to two-wheel vehicles: we hope that the negotiations will go in this direction.
in writing. i regret the vote of our assembly which, contrary to the opinion of the committee on transport, wishes to impose a technical inspection for scooters and motorcycles. for these vehicles, as we know, the quality of the infrastructure and the behaviour of the driver are the main factors in accidents, with technical failures appearing as the main cause of accidents in less than 1% of cases. such a measure therefore seems unjustified and disproportionate. it will impose an additional cost on the owners of these vehicles, without any real improvement in road safety. the european commission, which is taking this action, had clear and precise information on this matter: a study it had itself commissioned highlighted the low added value of such an obligation. i asked her about these contradictions, but she gave no convincing answer. that is why i refused to give a mandate for negotiations on the basis of the text adopted, and if the final agreement reached by the council and parliament does not exempt this category of vehicles, i will oppose it again.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by my colleague richard seeber, which aims to update the list of priority substances to be controlled and reduced in european waters. for the first time, this draft directive provides within two years for a strategy to combat water pollution by pharmaceutical products, which, for reasons of public health, is a major step forward.
in writing. i voted for this report on chemicals in water. it adds 15 substances to the list of 33 pollutants already monitored and controlled in surface waters in the union, including three pharmaceutical substances: diclofenac, an anti-inflammatory harmful to fish and certain birds; 17-beta-estradiol, a hormone that acts as an endocrine disruptor in nature; and alpha-ethinyl estradiol, a synthetic hormone. the regulation, which was agreed with the council, provides that these substances will now be measured regularly in order to prevent health risks. at a time when many studies are highlighting the harmfulness of endocrine disruptors of all kinds, it is to be hoped that this regulation will be followed by concrete measures to limit the emission of these substances. as water, which should be considered a public good, becomes an increasingly contested resource, fighting for its quality is a priority that we must not neglect. in this sense, i support updating standards and setting environmental standards for priority substances.
in writing. the report lists the priority substances for european water policy. since chemical pollution of surface waters is a threat to the aquatic environment and to human health, a review of priority substances (including 3 pharmaceuticals) has been carried out. thus new substances have been added. environmental quality standards (eqs) have been established for these new substances, while the eqs for existing substances have been revised. why the change ? this is to take account of scientific progress. new monitoring methods, such as passive sampling, may be introduced to ensure water quality. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. in approving the addition of 12 new substances to the list of substances that may pose a risk to the aquatic environment, i voted in favour of a stricter water policy. these substances, which represent a potential risk to the environment, will have to meet certain concentration levels in water in order to preserve surface waters, which are the first victims of water pollution. we have decided to adopt new and more stringent environmental quality standards to protect the environment in the long term.
in writing. this text is aimed at a clear improvement in the quality of aquatic environments. i particularly welcome the proposal in this report to create a single website to provide information on river basin management plans. good information for europeans is one of the keys to the success of our strategy to combat water pollution, which directly affects their environment and health. i support the general emphasis on good information and enhanced communication to the citizens of the union so that they are able to measure the effects of these preventive measures in practice.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it envisages the establishment of a coherent sustainable water management policy. by increasing the number of substances recognised as harmful to the aquatic environment, the text will lead to greater environmental protection and the conservation of healthy and clean water. this text will thus allow our fellow citizens to live in a cleaner environment by limiting chemical pollution.
in writing. i supported the agreement at first reading on this draft directive. the guidelines of the compromise between the european parliament and the council are aimed at improving the quality of aquatic environments. the inclusion of three pharmaceutical substances (synthetic hormones 17alphaethinylestradiol and 17beta-estradiol and the anti-inflammatory drug diclofenac) in the watch list rather than in the priority list is a satisfactory point. we shall consider whether or not they need to be included in the list of priority substances in the next revision of the list of priority substances. the establishment of this watch list is a step in the right direction to ensure harmonised eu-wide collection of data on the presence of substances in european surface waters. i regret, however, that the inclusion of bisphenol a in the list of priority substances has not been taken into account. a recent us study provided evidence that exposure to bisphenol a increased the risk of prostate cancer. some member states have even banned it, and i hope that the european commission will be able to tackle this problem quickly in order to harmonize this ban.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague richard seeber. this report dealt with the proposal to review the list of priority substances for water policy with a view to achieving good surface water chemical status. in particular, it shall amend the list of priority substances in a timely manner in order to achieve optimum protection. the report was adopted by a large majority, with 646 votes in favour, 51 against and 14 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. water policy is a long-term policy whose main objective is to ensure that everyone has access to safe and clean water. i voted in favour of this text, which provides for improving the existing water policy by amending the water framework directive and the environmental quality standards directive. the text also provides for the addition to the eu list of 12 new priority substances that may pose a risk to the aquatic environment and the addition of three pharmaceutical substances to the watch list of emerging pollutants.
in writing. i voted in favour of parliament's position on the european water policy, as regards priority substances withdrawn from the market, given the harmful environmental impact they represent. water is an indispensable resource for man and his environment. it is therefore a long-term action and strategy which will guarantee clean water for european citizens in the future. in this context, 15 new substances which are or may be water pollutants have been added to the list of pollutants under surveillance. studies will be carried out to determine the risk these substances pose before a decision is taken on whether or not to withdraw them from the market.
in writing. monitoring water quality and cleanliness is of paramount importance to european citizens. new substances added to the list of priority substances, including 3 pharmaceutical substances, will be subject to increased surveillance.
in writing. water, soil and groundwater are constantly and increasingly polluted by chemical and pharmaceutical residues, endangering both the health of citizens and the protection of the environment. in view of the seriousness of this situation, ensuring a quality water supply should be a priority, and all necessary measures should be taken to ensure the proper conservation of this vital resource. therefore, the inclusion in this report of pharmaceutical substances in the watch list rather than in the list of priority substances is not acceptable. i also object to the postponement of the deadlines for compliance with the environmental quality standards for new substances. it is regrettable that the legislation originally proposed has been greatly weakened in the negotiations with the commission and the council. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ensuring clean water is essential for the environment and human health. unfortunately, studies have shown that we are far from having good surface water. a review of the current legislation in this area is therefore essential. a stricter regulation will ultimately improve water quality. with the text adopted today - which i supported - twelve new substances will be added to the european list of substances considered to be a risk to the aquatic environment. these new substances will be subject to a maximum concentration level in water, which will take effect in 2018. member states will therefore have to introduce additional controls by then. in addition, for the first time, a watch list for emerging pollutants will be drawn up. the effects of these substances will be monitored with a view to their inclusion in the list of priority substances if necessary. note: this list includes three pharmaceutical substances (including two synthetic hormones and one anti-inflammatory).
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because water policy is central to the health and living conditions of 500 million europeans. it is in this sense that measures must be taken on priority substances to combat water pollution. the member states and the union must pay more attention to pollutants, including pharmaceutical substances, in water and increase their vigilance, in particular through the establishment of monitoring stations. climate change and the increase in global population are making this resource more vulnerable, and we need to find a solution for its sustainable management. the european union must therefore develop a strategic and sustainable water policy in close cooperation with the international community.
in writing. implementing effective measures to limit chemical pollution of water is an important challenge for the sustainable management of this common good. the council, the european parliament and the commission agreed, in the context of the revision of the water framework directive and the environmental quality standards directive, to add 15 new priority substances presenting a significant risk to the list of 33 pollutants already monitored and controlled in surface waters in the union. three pharmaceutical products have been simultaneously withdrawn under pressure from the lobbies. the european union must take responsibility for the member states: water policy cannot directly influence the health policy of the member states. we are still in a post-market control, without really questioning the polluting production methods. there is even concern that the text will encourage the development of advanced water technologies, which allow water purification, while they consist of increasing chlorination instead of reviewing private water management and the use of pesticides in agriculture. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. i am pleased that the three amendments tabled by my colleague mr belet, which i co-signed, obtained a majority of votes in the european parliament. in this report on state aid, these amendments were intended to recall the specific nature of sport as an economic activity and to emphasise that, in general, amateur sport cannot be considered an economic activity. we also recall, although it may seem obvious, that although, exceptionally, amateur sports involve economic activities with public support measures qualifying as state aid, it must be borne in mind that they have only very limited effects on the internal market. finally, our amendments stress that the court of justice has recognised the legitimacy of the objective of promoting the training of young people in the context of professional clubs. a clear framework is therefore needed to enable states to achieve this objective, in particular by supporting sports organisations.
in writing. in order to modernise public aid policy, categories of aid that would be exempted from the notification requirement have been identified, such as aid to residents of peripheral regions for transport, state aid for certain broadband infrastructures, etc. a balance must be struck between the impact of the exemptions from the notification requirement on the internal market and the fact that too many services are not excluded from state aid control. the report also states that free and fair access to state aid should be guaranteed to all relevant market players. in addition, state aid schemes should be given priority over individual aid. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. in the context of the reform of the state aid notification system initiated by the commission, i voted in favour of the exemption from notification to the commission of aid for research, development and innovation. these areas are the flagship initiatives of the europe 2020 strategy and the horizon 2020 objectives, and therefore the conditions for granting state aid to them had to be simplified. the public passenger transport service is therefore perfectly in line with this requirement for simplification in order not to infringe the rights of public transport users.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this text, which helps to make our state aid more efficient and clearer. by increasing the number of categories of aid which can be exempted from the notification requirement, we aim to reduce the administrative burden on businesses and encourage them to grow and create jobs. the text we voted today will thus support the research, environmental and tourism sectors, which must play a key role in the recovery of a strong and competitive european economy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which strengthens transparency on state aid. by clarifying which state aids need to be notified to the european union, the text focuses the attention of the controllers on certain limited state aids. the text thus avoids unfair competition between member states without depriving each of them of the support it needs to support a fragile and essential economic sector, such as culture and heritage. the report therefore envisages greater cooperation, without weakening the member states on their local specificities.
in writing. i supported this report on the definition of categories exempted from the notification requirement in the case of state aid. these exemptions would cover areas such as culture, heritage conservation, natural disasters, etc. these proposals are part of a drive to modernise and simplify administrative rules. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report by the european parliament.
in writing. i have approved the report on horizontal state aid and public passenger transport services by rail and road. state aid is money granted by the national authorities to support domestic activities. however, in order to ensure that they do not impede the principle of free competition, the union sets out guidelines and limits for the granting of such subsidies. the aim of this report is to modernise the commission's monitoring of practices by focusing on those cases which have the greatest impact on the internal market. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. in addition, a simplified procedure should be established to deal more quickly with cases with a lesser impact. finally, new categories of aid were authorised, in particular for grants with a social purpose and in the public interest, such as the opening up of peripheral regions through transport infrastructure projects. we are thus allowing the states to invest in the construction and coordination of rail and road networks, in order to increase the mobility of citizens throughout the territory.
in writing. this text does not call into question the principle of free and undistorted competition but provides for the relaxation of certain controls in the award of public aid. the commission is taking the right course, as is not customary, by proposing to add areas to the list of those benefiting from these facilities. but parliament's report refuses to relax the conditions for public aid in the name of public transport, even though the liberals in the commission agreed to this. the dogmatism of the right wing of parliament is unbearable. i do not want to impede the relief gained by other sectors such as amateur sport or culture from the control of the commission's anti-subsidy bureaucracy. i'm not going to.
in writing. i abstained on this legislative resolution on state aid. the commission is asked to focus on the largest aid schemes, to simplify the rules and to speed up the authorisation processes. we can only be pleased. i have also proposed with 40 of my colleagues that aid to the sports sector, and in particular to amateur sport, should now be exempted from notification of aid to the commission, which is to include it in the mechanisms for which the gis benefits. however, the fundamentals underlying the text remain unchanged. the liberal provisions of the treaties continue to treat state aid as an exception, in breach of article 14 tfeu, which reaffirms the subsidiarity of the member states in defining what constitutes the general interest. more sectors should have been exempted. finally, the commission has attempted to amend an act adopted under codecision by means of a procedure whereby parliament is merely consulted and has therefore flouted parliament's legislative prerogatives. so much for not having sex.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, europe is the world's leading maritime area, thanks to its outermost regions. it was therefore important that, in this report on blue growth, they should be clearly identified as an essential element of the european strategy, as the union's relays in the world, by their expertise in seaside tourism, thanks to the panoply of renewable energies at their disposal, on the basis of the important discoveries in the field of mineral and energy deposits. but blue growth must be part of an integrated management of maritime and coastal areas. the sustainability criterion should therefore be at the heart of maritime activities, as they are based on extremely fragile environments, with the aim of avoiding that some negative externalities related to maritime activities are harmful to others. it is therefore essential to structure these activities and the coastal area at community level and, as such, the report by mrs isabelle thomas on maritime spatial planning will be decisive for the economic development of our coasts.
in writing. about half of europe's population now lives along 89 000 km of damaged european coastline. the situation requires sustained and careful management, otherwise we are headed for an ecological and human disaster. it is very difficult to assess the consequences of human activity on marine ecosystems and even more difficult to repair them. that is why in this report we are advocating the sustainable and responsible management of our coastlines, combining infrastructure, social considerations and respect for our waters. seasonal tourism, respect for biodiversity, training of seafarers and the need to create a single maritime area are all areas where the union can add value. the european commission has integrated this idea of blue growth around five key areas: blue energy, aquaculture, maritime and coastal tourism, marine mining and blue biotechnology. in this report we encourage the commission to develop a fully integrated strategy for the maritime area around 'blue growth'.
in writing. the commission, in the europe 2020 strategy, has recognised the economic potential that blue growth could represent. the objective of the blue economy is to achieve a healthy maritime economy, a source of innovation, growth and sustainable development. what are the obstacles to this objective? the issue of appropriate qualifications, access to venture capital, fragmentation of marine data, environmental challenges and the complexity of planning mechanisms. the report identified two main objectives: integrated sustainable growth but also growth coupled with a high employment rate. as blue growth is an asset for the economy of tomorrow, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of launching a joint initiative of the commission, member states and regions working together to harness the potential of the maritime dimension of the europe 2020 strategy. sustainable and integrated blue growth, but accompanied by a high employment rate, is needed to increase the attractiveness of employment in this sector. i am in favour of creating strong maritime clusters, while protecting smes in the sector. assainie, blue growth can be a source of innovation, growth and sustainable development.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on blue growth because i share the rapporteur's main objectives, namely sustainable and integrated growth with high employment in sectors linked to the coastal economy. in line with the guidelines of the future integrated maritime policy, it is essential to link the maritime sector to the development of coastal areas, which is why it is important to give priority to tourism, as this report does. similarly, it is crucial to plan a sustainable shipping policy to preserve vulnerable marine ecosystems, while taking a realistic approach to these issues, so as not to burden economic activity. in this respect, i am pleased that this report takes a balanced approach.
in writing. i welcome the approach taken in this report, which puts our ambitions for growth and jobs at the forefront, while linking them to our imperatives for protecting the environment and combating climate change. there is still a great deal of untapped growth potential for coastal regions and the marine sector and, as this text rightly emphasises, this is an opportunity for women and young people to seize: vocational training and the integration of new entrepreneurs is indeed a key issue, to which we must give full importance if we want to create a blue growth that is both sustainable and dynamic.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is essential to ensure greater european cooperation on the sustainable and ecological exploitation of the marine environment. the text proposes in particular the promotion of environmentally friendly marine fuels and the expansion of recycling and waste management industries, which makes it possible to envisage a healthier and more environmentally friendly economy. the text also provides for effective protection of smes, reducing the risk of increasing the burden on these types of enterprises, which is so important for our territories.
in writing. i supported the own-initiative report by my colleague, mr spyros danellis. the report made proposals to improve sustainable growth in the union's marine sector, maritime transport and tourism. improving growth is a major objective of the union and i support any measure to that end. i therefore welcome the adoption of this text by parliament.
in writing. more than 70% of the earth's surface is covered by oceans and seas. the latter will play an increasingly important role in the economic growth of tomorrow and will be able to respond to the new challenges facing the european union. i therefore voted in favour of this text because it maximises the benefits of the implementation of blue growth. it ensures that workers in the maritime sector are provided with the skills needed to ensure growth with a high employment rate and aims to ensure the integrated sustainability of this growth.
in writing. on tuesday i voted in favour of the report on blue growth. indeed, maritime and coastal areas offer very positive opportunities for economic growth and job creation. the aim of this text is to establish a comprehensive plan for innovative and sustainable development in order to mobilise the economic capacities of these geographical areas effectively and fully. improving maritime transport, developing renewable energy sources on the high seas, including wind power, aquaculture, maritime and coastal tourism, marine mining and blue biotechnology, are promising sectors that should boost economic activity and innovation in these regions of europe. through this project, we want to promote the establishment of integrated and sustainable growth that will benefit a large number of europeans.
in writing. humanity, whose population has tripled in a hundred years, is about to enter the sea. the question is not whether man will exploit the oceans, but to ensure that he does so in a sustainable way. it is a matter of survival for our ecosystem and therefore for humanity. therefore, it is not appropriate to recycle past revenue and 'buy' growth, but to make a qualitative leap by creating the conditions for progress. in blue growth, the problem is not the color. the intentions and objectives of this report are commendable, particularly in terms of the centrality of the sea issue in future human development possibilities. however, it is the one that is most responsible for deregulation and competition in the recommended means. i'm not going to do it to raise awareness.
in writing. the european union, the world's leading maritime area, intends to defend an ambitious blue economy which today represents 5.4 million jobs. the report thus presents a comprehensive and coordinated strategy to develop the potential for growth and job creation of the sea and coastline. the socialists have placed a great deal of emphasis on the sustainable management of the marine environment and the pool of highly skilled jobs in the fisheries sector.
in writing. the eu remains the world's leading maritime power and is expected to generate €590 billion in value added and 7 million jobs in the sector by 2020. the maritime and coastal economies are the levers for growth, employment and competitiveness in the european union, and this is particularly true in my euro-region. this report on 'blue growth' is a real roadmap to achieve these objectives. it encourages sustainable practices, makes the professions in the sector more attractive, supports innovation and stresses the protection of the environment and biodiversity. that is why i voted in favour of it, especially as it will strengthen the european competitiveness of our industries and help to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.

in writing. cooperatives make a positive contribution to our so-called social market economy. with 11 million employees in the union, the sse sector has a considerable weight, which is still too often unrecognised and therefore undervalued. the ess should be able to benefit from conditions for development no less favourable than those of other forms of enterprise. cooperatives are sometimes the result of a transfer of ownership from the enterprise to the employees. the possibility of passing on the company to the employees should be encouraged in order to ensure the continuity of the activity in the form of a cooperative. restructuring in the form of a cooperative should be supported by a specific union budget line also covering financial instruments. this would be an important step, both for employees, who become shareholders, to ensure the continuity of economic activity in our territories and to promote corporate governance based on the long term and proximity. this report has been adopted by a large majority in the institution, but i regret that the alde group abstained, whereas this report calls for the support of a whole section of the economy which, and this is no small thing, carries within it the model of society that we should promote in the aftermath of the crisis.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, the contamination of milk with melamine in 2008, the h1n1 influenza pandemic in 2009, the volcanic ash cloud and the aluminium sludge spill in hungary in 2010, or the e. coli bacteria in 2011, are all health catastrophes that have revealed the weaknesses of national and european crisis mechanisms. to deal with h7n9 avian influenza and coronavirus, we need to be better prepared. there are now many national and community mechanisms for preventing and responding to health crises, but these different systems are poorly coordinated and ill-suited to the international dimension of most threats. these mechanisms sometimes even interfere with each other. for example, during the 2009 h1n1 influenza pandemic, several member states competed to buy vaccines in bulk, increasing prices and time frames, and ultimately having far too many vaccines available. this decision on serious crossborder threats to health, which was unanimously requested by the health ministers, will fill a legislative gap. the aim is therefore to extend the current coordination mechanism applicable to communicable diseases to all threats to health of biological, chemical or environmental origin. the decision proposes a number of measures to improve the effectiveness of the fight against serious health threats. among these i can mention the extension of the risk assessment and coordination measures currently applicable to communicable diseases to all threats to health of chemical, biological or environmental origin. secondly, the possibility of declaring a european health emergency to speed up the provision of the medicines needed to combat the crisis, even before the world health organisation. thirdly, the obligation to inform and consult each other between the member states and the european commission on national preparedness and response plans for health crises. fourthly, the role of the health and safety committee should be strengthened with a view to better coordinating crisis management measures. fifthly, the creation of a legal basis for the coordination of the purchase of vaccines and medicines in europe. as rapporteur for the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i have been working, and we have been working, for almost two years on this exciting subject. we then, after the almost unanimous vote in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, began six months of trilogue negotiations and reached an agreement on 6 may. i am obviously very pleased with the agreement reached. we have managed to strike a balance between the intergovernmental and the community dimension, which is rare in a sensitive subject such as public health. the priorities of each were respected through a real spirit of compromise. i would also like to thank the fictitious rapporteurs who supported me and who also showed this willingness to compromise. the greatest success of this decision is undoubtedly the creation of a legal basis for the coordination of the purchase of vaccines or medicines in europe. this decision will make access to vaccines more equitable as they will be available at fairer prices, a welcome development, especially for the smaller member states, which simply could not afford to pay the exorbitant prices charged during the recent pandemics. that is the added value of this decision, mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen.
