in writing. the current european system for combating greenhouse gas emissions, based on a european carbon market where 'polluting rights' are sold, is far from effective. for example, it has not achieved the emission reduction targets. worse, it has even helped finance the biggest polluters in europe. this is not acceptable. for these reasons, i have decided to vote against the commission's proposal to clarify the provisions on the timing of the auctioning of emission allowances, because this proposal is to save the system by trying to make it a little less inefficient. this is not the way to reduce european environmental policy. what we need is not a marginal measure but a fundamental reform of this system and ambitious policies to promote the transition to a low-carbon economy.
in writing. the eu's emissions trading system was faced with serious imbalances. the economic crisis has led to a deep and lasting reduction in industrial production. as an indirect consequence, the supply of carbon allowances far outstrips demand, and the price of carbon has fallen to a level that is no longer a deterrent. because of the first rejection of the text at the april plenary, we were forced to make a number of concessions in order to reach an agreement. but we saved the system, and that's the bottom line. two thirds of the revenue will have to be reallocated to eco-innovation and renewable energy, i.e. the value of 600 million allowances out of the 900 million frozen. this revenue will have to be put into a new fund specifically dedicated to these purposes. the ets is returning to its primary function as a stimulus for the development of low-carbon technologies. the system saved, we can now improve it.

in writing. the european union has set up a quota trading system to reduce co2 emissions from european industries, which are responsible for global warming. the crisis has led to a dramatic fall in the price of a tonne of co2 (from eur 30 at the end of 2011 to less than eur 5 at present). i personally voted for a reform of the system so that the price of a tonne of co2 is raised. indeed, a very low price per tonne of co2 will not encourage european industries to innovate in greener and less polluting technologies, which i believe represent the technologies of the future. i therefore supported the report.

in writing. i voted in favour of introducing a financial transaction tax in 11 voluntary states at 0.1% on stock and bond transactions and 0.01% on derivatives transactions. the european parliament laid the foundations for this tax, and it is now up to the council to organise this enhanced cooperation. the basic idea of this text is to tax more highly speculative financial instruments (shares, bonds, derivatives) and less highly speculative activities (pension funds and smes). this approach seemed to me the most fair, since it protects small investors and smes.
in writing. despite the reluctance of some states, and after 12 years of persistence, the green light has finally been given to the enhanced cooperation of 11 countries to introduce a financial transaction tax (ftt): austria, belgium, estonia, france, germany, greece, italy, portugal, slovakia, slovenia and spain. while it is important to take the time to define the modalities and details of the application of this tax, it is also necessary to send a strong political signal by reaffirming parliament's support for the ftt. the ttf will eventually have to cover a wide range of financial instruments such as shares, bonds or derivatives, but be careful not to affect market operations involving smes. if this tax is to be effective and enable funds to be raised on the financial markets and speculation to be combated, we must take care to preserve the development of the real economy. in the meantime, this tax is a good signal to the world, because the goal is still to reach an international agreement. the moralization of finance must indeed become a shared objective to prevent the crisis we experienced in 2008 and which continues to produce adverse effects on our economies.

in writing. despite deep doubts, i voted in favour of the financial transaction tax. the increase in exemptions, although legitimate, leads to the tax being imposed mainly on companies, to the detriment of growth. in tax matters, a broad base and low rates are better. but taxation of the financial sector in proportion to its place in the economy remains necessary. the ep is only consulted. he's not a co-legislator. the council to reach a solution which is both fair from a tax point of view and positive for the real economy.

in writing. i supported parliament in favour of the implementation of enhanced cooperation in the field of the financial transaction tax. eleven member states (germany, austria, belgium, spain, estonia, france, greece, italy, portugal, slovakia and slovenia) have decided to introduce a tax on shares and bonds of 0.1% and 0.01% for derivatives. while the most risky speculative operations may be taxed more heavily by the states parties, this agreement limits the increase in charges for the activities of small and medium-sized enterprises, the real economic lungs of europe. the european union thus has a new resource of its own and is increasing its budget without depending on the goodwill of national governments.
in writing. the proposal for enhanced cooperation between 11 eu member states is an important first step in the area of the financial transaction tax. this should apply mainly to the riskiest speculative investments.
in writing. the tax had two main objectives: to increase the eu budget and to reduce speculation. the first objective will not be met, not only because of the low amounts involved (eur 30 billion per year) but also because the budget will not increase in proportion to the tax, which will replace the funds already allocated by the member states. the second objective is also limited: the basic level of this tax (0.1% and 0.01%) is too low to discourage speculation: the united kingdom has a tax of 0.5% on all transactions of buying or selling british shares in the world, which does not prevent it from attracting all kinds of speculative capital. the commission is also proposing to reduce the rates for pension funds to 0.05% (0.005% for derivatives) until 2016, as well as for investors in sovereign bonds and certain types of derivatives. i'm sorry about the setbacks. nevertheless, i vote in favour of measuring the progress made since my proposal for a financial transaction tax in the senate in 1999.
in writing. this text concerns the enhanced cooperation in the field of financial transaction tax that eleven member states of the european union, including france, wish to establish. while i regret that some countries have blocked the application of this tax to all eu member states, this decision is nevertheless an important first step in the fight against financial speculation and towards a fairer tax system. it is high time that european countries regulate their financial markets and adopt measures in the interests of european citizens rather than a financial sphere disconnected from reality. i therefore supported the report. i regret, however, that the measures adopted are still far too timid: pension funds, for example, are exempt from this tax. there is still a long way to go before there is any real regulation of international finance.
in writing. because financial speculation is partly responsible for the crisis we are experiencing, finance must pay for the damage it causes. this is the objective of the enhanced cooperation on ftt that eleven member states - including france - want to introduce: to combat speculation while creating a new budgetary resource. i am proud that the socialists have won the battle for a broad base: the pension funds will not be safe! because europe is playing with its credibility, it is now crucial that the council introduce ftt as soon as possible.
in writing. this tax is crucial. nicolas sarkozy was the first to propose it at the g20 level, and since then a lot of pedagogical work has been done. it was time for europe to act. its aim is to prevent financial transactions from undermining the efficiency of financial markets and to secure the financial system. at the same time, it would make it possible to ensure that financial markets contribute to public finances in a fair and substantial way. europe would be at the forefront, as such a tax has never been introduced at regional level.
in writing. finally, a small step towards the introduction of a financial transaction tax (ftt). the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question are imputable to the state. the champions of tax dumping, luxembourg and great britain in the lead, have opposed it with all their might. eleven member states (belgium, germany, france, estonia, spain, greece, italy, austria, portugal, slovenia and slovakia) have therefore decided to establish the ftt by applying the enhanced cooperation procedure for the first time in tax matters. i would have liked to see the proposal include pension funds in its scope or to see the proposed rates (0.1% for equity and bond swaps and 0.01% for financial derivatives) be more ambitious. but while the gue/ngl was the first to defend the tobin tax in the european parliament, we considered that an embryo tax was better than no tax at all. i voted for this resolution.
in writing. because financial speculation is partly responsible for the crisis we are experiencing, finance must take responsibility for the damage it causes. the new proposal for a council directive to implement the financial transaction tax (ftt) on the basis of enhanced cooperation between 11 countries, including france, is based on two main lines: implementation on 1 january 2014 and the extension of the base to all financial products, including pension funds. i welcome this: for us socialists, this is the culmination of a long struggle which began with the drafting of a report last march calling for the creation of a special commission on the financial, economic and social crisis. the fight against speculation and the creation of new budgetary resources would be a great step forward, indispensable for european identity and the necessary solidarity between peoples. it is now crucial that the council introduce ftt as soon as possible.
in writing. the financial sector has been the trigger for the crisis we are experiencing. it is therefore only natural that this economic sector, which is again recording impressive profits, should be put to work to pay for the broken pots. this tax will bring in tens of billions of euros each year, which can be paid directly to the eu budget, which is itself 94% reinjected into the real economy. it is therefore useful and necessary for the member states to commit themselves to making it an eu resource. now, for this system to be effective, as this resolution calls for, it must involve as many member states as possible, and i regret that the united kingdom is trying to protect the city instead of learning from the financial crisis. by increasing the fees on each transaction involving shares, bonds, or derivatives, this tax would allow listed companies to better guard against speculators and stabilize their shareholders in the long run. this initiative would therefore by no means kill finance as some claim, but would, on the contrary, avoid speculative bubbles which always end up bursting and, in the end, burdening european taxpayers.

in writing. i voted against this report which endorsed latvia's entry into the euro area on 1 january 2014. the report says that latvia's efforts to join the eurozone should be welcomed. we all know what that means. with a public deficit of 1.2% and a public debt of 43.2% of gdp, latvia is a good student of austerity, while unemployment is 15%. it is not because we voted against this report that we are against latvia's entry into the euro zone (it is not for us to decide that, by the way), but rather against the consequences of this accession for its people. moreover, the report modestly mentions the "weak to moderate support for the euro" of the latvian population - two thirds are against it! they are understandable when we look at the current situation in the euro area.
in writing. i am naturally in favour of the introduction of measures at european level to protect the lives of europeans on the roads: too many accidents still occur which could be avoided, in particular by improving emergency services. i voted in favour of one article in the text which expressed our concern that several countries had increased speed limits on their motorways and i regret that it was not adopted. the speed limit is a crucial tool for saving lives: we cannot let our guard down.
in writing. i abstained from voting on this text aimed at europeanising the policy to combat road safety. the death toll on our roads is still a scourge that we must combat, but it is the member states that must be held responsible, pointing the finger at inadequate road infrastructure for example. i believe that the road safety tools should be left in the hands of the member states, so that governments can adopt the measures that are most appropriate for their territory and most suited to the behaviour of their population. the balance must be struck between prevention, obligation and repression, and it seems illusory to rely on just one of these instruments to reduce the number of victims. while it is now time to correct habits and adapt infrastructure in our territories, a europeanisation of road safety policy does not seem appropriate. it is essential to stop generalizing and to respond to locally identified needs in order to see a real decline in accidents on our roads.
in writing. i voted in favour of the parliament's motion for a resolution on road safety in europe. the eu needs a comprehensive strategy to combat road accidents, with the aim of significantly reducing the number of serious injuries. we therefore recommend that new european standards be applied to promote the integration of technical progress into vehicle equipment and to promote investment in infrastructure. we also call for better protection for vulnerable road users, such as pedestrians and cyclists, who are the victims of half of all serious accidents in urban areas. finally, national authorities need to improve the efficiency of first aid services, as well as the long-term medical care and rehabilitation of seriously injured people.
in writing. although the number of people killed on european roads fell by 9% in 2012, 73 europeans die on the roads every day. in total, road accidents in 2011 killed more than 30 000 people and injured nearly 1 500 000 in the european union. the commission has therefore launched an eu road safety action programme 2011-2020 with the aim of halving the number of deaths on european roads over the next ten years. i supported this report because it proposes solutions to achieve the objective of reducing the number of serious injuries on european roads and protecting vulnerable road users. for example, pedestrians and cyclists alone account for 50% of all deaths in urban traffic accidents. the european union and the member states must therefore seriously consider enforcing the traffic rules and continue to develop awareness campaigns for drivers. at the same time, there is an urgent need to improve first aid and medical care after accidents.

in writing. in february 2012, a high-level expert group (the liikanen group) was mandated to study potential structural reforms of the european banking sector that could strengthen financial stability and improve system efficiency and consumer protection. the liikanen group argued that structural reforms were needed, including the legal separation of deposit activities from speculative activities. this separation will ensure transparency in banking activities, and better supervision and crisis resolution. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal which profoundly reforms european banks. i have endorsed the principle of the personal involvement of the members of the boards of directors of banks in the event of errors and a better separation between the more risky banking activities and the more prudent operations. this proposal is part of the more general framework for reform of the banking system. the cleanup of the system has become a necessity in the context of the economic crisis.
in writing. this is the refutation of those who say that europe is doing nothing to avoid the situation of 2008. it was difficult, it was complex, but it's a breakthrough.
in writing. structural reform of the european union's banking sector is necessary to avoid a repeat of the financial crisis that hit europe in 2007-2008 and which spared no type of bank. there is a real priority to separate deposit banks from market banks, i.e. to create a separation between the activities of banks which are useful for investment and employment, and the speculative activities that banks carry out on their own account. the banks will now have to set up an ad hoc branch and isolate their speculative activities in that branch. the subsidiary, which will have neither the same name nor the same governance as the parent company, will have to be capitalised and financed autonomously. the savings deposits of the depositors will no longer be able to be used to finance the activities of these branches, even if they encounter difficulties.
in writing. i abstained on this text. the banking sector is in need of a major reform and the text contains some good proposals. but i am surprised that after highlighting the role of the glass-steagall act in solving the 1929 crisis and the disastrous consequences of its repeal in 1999 under the clinton administration, the whole report is actually about avoiding the sensible and necessary solution of the actual separation of banking activities. if the legislation being prepared by the commission is in line with what is outlined in the report, then the french government is reassured: its cosmetic reform of the "casino bank" will be euro-compatible. the financial lobby will have won. risky and speculative activities will simply be confined to subsidiaries, and the implicit public guarantee will have been maintained. so we haven't changed much. the big loser, and the big ultimate payer, of any new banking incident - and there will be new ones - will remain the european citizen.

in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on structural reform of the european banking sector. this report calls on the european commission to legislate in this area. the new measures advocated in the report will now allow for a real separation of the activities of the financial sector from the day-to-day banking activities of european citizens. the oversized size of this sector and its impact on our real economies has shown its limits, and structural reform is therefore necessary to strengthen the security of european citizens and to regulate the risk-taking of financial institutions.
in writing. the banking sector has played a significant role in the emergence of the current economic and financial crisis. it was then necessary to take action to regulate and supervise banking activities. this is what the european union wants to do, since it has embarked on a major reform of the sector in order to achieve a real banking union. this text, which i voted in favour of, is the final piece of the puzzle, because it sets out the european parliament's priorities for banking reform. the text proposes, in particular, that the most risky activities be separated from the more prudent ones (e.g. loan operations), and that the members of the boards of directors be held personally liable in the event of errors. it also stresses the need to increase competition in the banking sector.

in writing. the complexity of the banking sector and excessive risk-taking lead to monstrous indebtedness, and are the cause of the financial crisis that has been affecting us for the last 5 years. europe had to be strong in this area to prevent such a crisis from happening again. the banking sector needs to restructure in order to offer more transparency. to this end, the eu proposes key principles for the overhaul of the sector, by strengthening competition and creating a responsible remuneration system that enables the bank to recover effectively. the repeated bailouts between 2008 and 2011 have increased the public debt of the member states, which are now struggling to cope. the resumption of growth in our continent depends on the overhaul of the european banking system. it is now imperative that eu states put in place shared arrangements to manage crisis situations together. we will only get through this with more europe and more solidarity.
in writing. − €1.6 trillion has been allocated to rescue the banking sector since 2007, equivalent to 12.8% of the european union's total gross domestic product. the aid to the banks has significantly increased the debt burden of already large member states. however, banks are still facing problems, especially those that have had to provide assistance. the commission notes that the bank has not provided any evidence that the bank has been able to achieve its objective of maintaining a viable banking sector. i believe that banks need to be more closely linked to the real economy and contribute to its stable and sustainable development. it is also important that banks have a higher level of quality capital as well as higher liquidity reserves. the problems that led to many banking crises could have been avoided by the timely introduction of stricter banking regulatory standards. this is true of excessive risk-taking, insufficient equity and liquidity, excessive use of derivatives, etc. the commission also found that the banks' business lines were not sufficiently diversified, with commercial and investment banks often pursuing similar business models and taking on similar levels of risk. the european parliament resolution on the restructuring of the banking sector sets out the principles on which reforms should be based in order to reduce excessive risk, increase competition and improve governance. the proposed reforms will promote fair and effective competition, which will help to revive the european banking sector, which is why i voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. european citizens have paid a heavy price since the economic and financial downturn began. by adopting today an own-initiative report on structural reform of the european union's banking sector, the european parliament has sent a strong signal that the strong financial integration of the european union and the logic of the common market cannot go hand in hand without the creation of a harmonised banking framework that protects consumers. while underlining the vital nature of the ongoing reforms in the european banking sector, this report clearly recognises the need to introduce further reforms in the structure of the sector: reducing excessive risk, ensuring competition, reducing complexity, and limiting porosity in european banks i therefore believe that the separation of the risky speculative activities of banks on the one hand and the activities linked to deposit and credit accounts (essential banking activities for households and businesses) on the other hand, which was voted on today, is not only necessary, it is indispensable. the report adopted recommends a separation in the form of a subsidiary: the separation would then be more operational than legal... the commission must now be persuaded to legislate in this area, so as not to endorse an ambiguity which could lead to inaction in the sector.
in writing. one of the tasks of the member states and the commission is to combat fraud or any other illegal activity affecting the financial interests of the union. in order to combat tax fraud effectively, it is important to look carefully at the monitoring and control systems put in place by states and to ensure that the data collected by these systems are relevant and reflect reality. it is important to recall that in 2011, 1230 irregularities were detected, with an impact of €404 million. considering that the irregularity rate in 2011 decreased by 37% compared to 2010, does this decrease correspond to an actual decrease in irregularities, or is it a reflection of a sluggish functioning of the control systems? in view of the points made in the report, i voted for the report.

in writing. before 16 march 2007, member states had to take measures to comply with the provisions of the council framework decision of 24 february 2005 on the main forms of criminal activity against information systems. while these were not specifically addressed when the framework decision was adopted, new attacks are now the focus of attention. the sale, purchase, import, distribution or making available of tools or devices for the purpose of committing offences will be criminalised, for example. aggravating circumstances will be considered based on the scale of the attacks and whether the attacks were committed by concealing the true identity of the attacker. in addition, it is provided that a mandatory response is provided following a request for assistance. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal which provides for stricter sanctions for cybercriminals, better prevention and enhanced police and judicial cooperation in the event of cyberattacks. cybercrime is on the rise in the european union, especially large-scale cyberattacks that cripple important it structures such as the one that hit the european commission in march 2011.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to update european legislation on the protection of information systems against criminal attacks. i welcome the compromise reached, which is very constructive. the introduction of minimum standards of protection and adequate liability will now be required, under penalty of sanction by the member states. cooperation between judicial authorities will also be strengthened in the member states, together with the private sector. i am glad that the attempts by the left to weaken the text were not compromised, because that would have meant a lower level of sanctions, to increase the responsibility of operators and producers, as if they were the only ones to bear the cost of better protection of information systems.
in writing. the financial cost of internet attacks is estimated at €750 billion a year in europe and, according to interpol, 80% of cybercrime cases are linked to organised gangs based in several countries. however, the legislation in the field of cybercrime differs greatly from one member state to another. technological advances also allow criminals to operate anonymously. this allows cybercriminals to make huge profits with little risk. the european union must therefore strengthen police and judicial cooperation in this area. penalties should be tightened for the most serious cyber-attacks, such as the use of "zombie networks" to remotely control computers by infecting them, and for attacks on critical infrastructure, such as nuclear power plants, transport networks and government sites. legal persons, in particular companies, must be held liable for offences committed on their behalf (for example, for hiring a hacker to gain access to a competitor's database).
in writing. i voted in favour of this text as it introduces measures to improve european cooperation in criminal justice, while consolidating the existing structure. the text allows for the strengthening of european information systems against cyber threats. the strengthening of the 24/7 contact points network allows the different member states to stay in touch, towards greater cooperation.
in writing. i fully supported the adoption of this directive, which aims to combat large-scale attacks on information systems. the text will, in particular, make it possible to better sanction the production, sale, import, distribution or making available of devices used to commit cyberattacks and also includes aggravating circumstances. it introduces the offence of illegal interception and measures to improve european judicial cooperation. the directive also addresses the need to provide statistical data on cybercrime by making it mandatory for member states and ensuring that an adequate system is in place for the recording, production and provision of statistical data. i support the fact that this directive is aimed primarily at combating those who act with the intention of causing harm, in particular piracy, since the author of the directive is seeking to profit from his action.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague monica hohlmeier. this report focused on the development of a legislative framework to combat attacks (including large-scale attacks) against information systems. it also sought to repeal council framework decision 2005/222/jha. cybercrime is a major problem in europe and worldwide. the european union had to act urgently. i am therefore pleased that this report has been adopted by a large majority.
in writing. cybercrime is a new form of crime that the european union is facing. the text, which i voted in favour of, adopts common sanctions against such cyberattacks. it calls for a minimum prison sentence of two years for crimes such as unlawful interception of communications or unlawful interference with data. heavier penalties are provided for attacks on critical infrastructure (nuclear power plants, government networks, for example). the text also facilitates prevention and strengthens police and judicial cooperation in this field.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text on attacks against information systems. indeed, cybercrime is growing alongside the booming digital economy. however, the risks posed by these attacks to economic, political and social stability are significant. with this in mind, we have decided to establish a european framework with common and stricter sanctions to punish cybercriminals severely. in addition, in the event of an attack within the eu, member states will have to respond to urgent requests for assistance from the actors concerned within eight hours. we want to increase cooperation between the police and judicial authorities of the eu countries in order to make the fight against cybercrime more effective.
in writing. the report gives priority to sanctions for attacks on information systems. however, punishments, however severe, do not solve the problem of crime. the greatest attention must therefore be paid to the prevention of crime through appropriate education, raising awareness from an early age of potential perpetrators of these offences. prevention, acting in the long term, is ultimately much more effective than repression. i therefore prefer prevention to these repressive logics and i voted against this report.
in writing. i voted against this revision of the cybercrime directive which aims to give us the means to fight against attacks on information systems. the agreement reached between the council and parliament did not even allow the few positive measures, notably on prevention, which had been agreed during the negotiations between meps, to be maintained. this revision is in line with the idea of a secure europe which, in the name of fighting crime, systematically and almost exclusively favours repression to the detriment of fundamental rights. the point is not to ignore the problems of cybercrime but to find the right balance. the council's position, which has prevailed, is based on repression and imposes a whole range of mandatory criminal sanctions. many imprecise definitions will extend the scope of the directive to ordinary users and will therefore lead to unacceptable criminalisation of many internet users. perhaps the worst thing is that this directive, which focuses on criminal law, makes only a marginal contribution to improving safety. it is always the same illusion: "strengthening repression is the most effective". all the studies show the opposite, but whatever, it's the display that counts.
mr president, i hear my colleagues, mr hannan, mr tannock and others, say that this is not very serious because all countries are, after all, spying on each other. yes, my dear colleagues, but the problem is that all the countries are resisting. when it happens on american soil or on russian soil, there is a serious reaction from the russians and the americans, not the kind of viscous cowardice that we see from the europeans today. the attitude of the governments of portugal, italy and france yesterday is truly disgraceful. this parliament, which is always talking about political asylum, should obviously give priority to julian assange and edward snowden, who have been our useful informants in this case. instead, one is virtually a recluse, a prisoner, under a ridiculous extradition threat in the ecuadorian embassy in london, the other is still in transit in moscow. the european governments, through their weakness and cowardice, and this parliament, have indeed disgraced themselves in this matter.
in writing. i abstained on the final vote on this resolution because i believe it should have included a request to postpone the opening of trade negotiations between the united states and the european union. i deplore the willingness of a majority of this parliament to negotiate with a partner who is simultaneously conducting totally unacceptable interception of communications between allies.
in writing. i voted unequivocally in favour of this resolution. the european states should have welcomed mr snowden in the best possible way and without delay. in this sense, each european country receiving an asylum application had to respond immediately in a favourable manner. unfortunately, that was not the case. mr. snowden is a champion of fundamental freedoms who deserves to be spared his own fate. europe had a responsibility to acknowledge the merits of this whistleblower who took risks to expose divergences that should never have existed between allies. europe is a political project based on values that can only be enchantments. i therefore regret very sadly and bitterly that my colleagues in the european parliament did not have the reflex to defend the fundamentals of our action.
in writing. i voted against the resolution on the us national security agency (nsa) surveillance programme. since the prism affair came to light, the eu must adopt a measured but consistent approach, and i considered that it might be more prudent to be more cautious, to ask the us for explanations before continuing negotiations on the eu-us free trade agreement. the establishment of free trade between two parties implies complete mutual trust, and it seems to me that the tension and uncertainty surrounding the us behaviour are currently preventing sound and calm negotiations.
in writing. relations between the eu and the us must be based on trust and respect for fundamental rights. these principles are now being undermined by the discovery of the prism surveillance programme, which allows the us authorities to access the personal data of european citizens, and the recent scandal of american spying on european institutions. europe must make its voice heard in the united states and say that what is happening is unacceptable and that we will not tolerate it. the commission's setting up of a committee of inquiry into us practices is a step in the right direction. but we must also demand from the us authorities full information on their surveillance programmes. in the meantime, we should postpone our negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment treaty.
in writing. the resolution on the prism case was voted on in plenary on 4 july. it was adopted by 483 votes to 98, with 65 abstentions. i'm sorry for what i did. i wanted to oppose it for several reasons. firstly, this text is full of good sentiments and is of a disconcerting naivety which totally discredits the action of the european institutions on security and intelligence matters. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a new regulation on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment in the event of a disaster. in agreeing with this text, we are not behaving like a great power. we appear weak. we are not credible. more seriously, we are showing the world that we have become mere objects of international relations. we're not in it anymore. - disconcerting naivety
in writing. the existence of prism was made public by edward snowden, a former employee of the us national security agency (nsa), in early june 2013. it denounces the nsa's direct access to data collected by the big web companies. the united states is also accused of having monitored several european union premises, including the headquarters of the european council. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this text which calls on the american authorities to provide all the information on these revelations as soon as possible and which also instructs parliament's committee on civil liberties to carry out a thorough study of the programmes in question. i also support this resolution when it calls for, among other things, increased protection for victims of such abuses and stricter provisions on privacy.
in writing. i supported the parliament's resolution on the us spy program prism by the nsa, surveillance agency. we have expressed both our surprise and our disapproval of our american partner in the face of the scale of this system of spying, which is affecting european citizens, the embassies of the member states and the european institutions. data protection and privacy and trusting relationships with our partners are key principles for europeans and we strongly condemn these developments. the commission's civil liberties committee has therefore been asked to carry out a thorough investigation into the interception of european communications in order to uncover the scandal. the commission will publish a report on the impact of this surveillance on the privacy and data protection of eu citizens by the end of the year. it will also make recommendations to prevent such events from happening again in the future.
in writing. the revelations of large-scale spying by the us authorities on millions of european citizens, institutions and businesses are very serious. this is a violation of the fundamental rights and privacy of european citizens. it is important that the european parliament should adopt a resolution condemning these practices. i regret, however, that parliament has not gone further in its resolution, in particular by also calling for the suspension of the negotiations on the free trade agreement between the european union and the united states and by demanding explanations from the north american authorities. i therefore abstained on that vote.
in writing. i abstained in the final vote on the european parliament's resolution on what should be called the prism-nsa affair. the european parliament has voted to reject the three amendments calling for the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) to be suspended until the european parliament is informed, depriving the eu of one of the few means of pressuring the us to finally respect the rights of european citizens in relation to their personal data. the eu has already abandoned too many of its principles in this area with the adoption of the swift (banking data) and pnr (air passenger data) agreements with the united states. in reality, the free trade agreement and cooperation with the united states in the fight against terrorism and crime, which is at the root of this widespread surveillance, are far more important to the majority of meps than the protection of the rights of european citizens. the creation of a committee of inquiry in the european parliament does not respond to the urgency of the situation. i also regret the rejection of our amendment to grant asylum to edward snowden. this resolution does not live up to the scandal of this mass surveillance and the threat to our public freedoms.
in writing. ensuring the transparency of elections is essential to enhance citizens' confidence in their institutions. this report sets out the practical arrangements for organising the 2014 european elections. thus, no results will be published before the end of the voting scheduled for sunday, may 25, 2014. the logo of the european political groups will have to appear on the ballot papers. the political groups will have to propose a candidate for the commission presidency within a time limit allowing a european-wide campaign to be carried out. in view of these facts, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of new modalities for the 2014 european elections. the candidates will now have to present their political programme in all member states and hold public debates. the aim of this reform is to oblige candidates to declare themselves early enough so that genuine electoral campaigns can be conducted at european level, on european issues, on the programme of european parties. the election of meps is the election with the highest abstention rate, we need to re-create a passion for european issues, to run real campaigns to raise awareness of meps and to curb abstention in european elections.
in writing. i voted in favour of the duff report on improving the 2014 european parliament elections. it contains a number of provisions which will enable parliament to derive full legitimacy from this vote and to make full use of the powers conferred on it by the treaty of lisbon. the introduction of the logo of the european political parties on the ballot paper, the provision of sufficient advance notice for the candidates for the presidency of the european commission, and the publication of the election results only after the polls have closed in the last member state are all measures which will increase the visibility of the european elections and the fight against abstention. if the new european parliament can thus be credibly strengthened, it will be in a stronger position vis-à-vis the council.
in writing. the 2014 european elections will be the first to be held since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which significantly increased the powers of the european parliament. and many of us want this election to be an opportunity for citizens to take back control of the european project. in this sense, european political parties are a platform and should be involved in the future of the european union, beyond national and local concerns, and in the sole general european interest.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it clarifies the arrangements for organising the european elections. by introducing greater visibility of votes, the publication of election results, among other things, the text is in line with greater political transparency. the adoption of this text will enable our citizens to be better informed about the various electoral procedures within our institution.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague andrew duff. the report was intended to set the framework for the forthcoming european elections. among many proposals, the report called on political parties to ensure that the names of candidates for the european parliament elections are made public at least six weeks before the elections. it also called on the member states and political parties to promote a greater presence of women on the lists of candidates. the report was adopted by 507 votes in favour, 120 against and 18 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the next european elections are crucial for the appointment of the union's leaders for the next five years. for the first time, the election of meps will strongly influence the future presidency of the european commission. however, practical arrangements are needed if this is to be a genuine democratic success. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which aims to bring europe closer to its citizens through a genuine european campaign. political parties will have to present their candidate to the commission, which will present its programme in all member states and participate in public debates. the text requires that ballot papers mention european and national parties and that citizens know the names of candidates for the european parliament at least six weeks before the elections.
in writing. i approved the report of the constitutional affairs committee, of which i am vice-chairman and in which i was involved, on the 2014 elections to the european parliament. the european elections in may 2014 will be the first to be held since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which has considerably increased the powers of our assembly. for example, in the election of the president of the european commission, the major european political parties will now nominate their candidate for the presidency of the commission, and the european parliament will have to vote for the future president of the european commission. we felt that these candidates should play a leading role in the future european election campaign, in particular by personally presenting their programme in all the member states of the union. we also made several recommendations on the need to carry out information and voting campaigns to curb abstention as much as possible, and we call on national political parties to respect parity, as far as possible, in all the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which proposes measures to make the next european campaign more visible and to bring coherence between the elections of members of the european parliament and the presidency of the european commission. each european party should specify which candidate it supports for the post of president of the european commission. the candidate whose party would win the most seats across the union should be considered first by the heads of state.
in writing. europe is experiencing an unprecedented crisis of euroscepticism. but in the face of the current economic crisis, i am convinced that europe will help us to overcome it. the next european elections are fast approaching and, in order to avoid a very high rate of abstention and a surge of pro-sovereignty parties, it is crucial to improve the procedures. in this respect, our main recommendations are as follows: national political parties shall inform citizens throughout the election campaign of their affiliation to a european political party and of their support for the candidate for president of the commission that they have nominated; european parties nominate their candidate for the presidency of the commission early enough to enable them to campaign for eu-wide elections on eu issues; candidates for the office of president of the commission present their political programme in all member states and organise a series of public debates; the voting ballots mention both national and european political parties. unfortunately, this is only a resolution of parliament, with no legislative effect. i hope, however, that we will be heard!
in writing. i voted against the resolution tabled by my socialist colleagues on european standards for arms exports. political sensitivities have been expressed on such a sensitive subject, and i could not approve this resolution signed by the s&ds and the gue, since it provides for an overly restrictive interpretation of the criteria of the common position of the member states. i have, however, welcomed the motion for a resolution signed by the epp which sets out an acceptable binding legal framework and encourages the implementation of the common position adopted by the member states.
in writing. i supported the joint motion for a resolution (epp, alde, ecr) on european standards for arms exports. the resolution signed by the epp, the ecr and alde was quite satisfactory, since it incorporated the amendments tabled by the epp. the resolution welcomed the adoption by the council in 2008 of a binding legal framework on arms exports. it also sought to encourage harmonisation in the interpretation and implementation of this common position by the member states. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the european union is the second largest arms exporter in the world, just behind the united states. council common position 2008/944/cfsp seeks to regulate this trade by setting out 8 criteria for authorisations for arms exports. while the first four must be respected in all cases, the last four remain at the discretion of member states which do not apply and interpret the 2008 common rules in a uniform manner. the consequence of this free movement is that the transparency of arms exports by each member state is undermined. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which calls on the union to strengthen its policy in this area in order to better control the arms exports of each member state. to this end, it proposed that each state should send the council all the information relating to its exports each year. it also called for the revision of the current criteria and for greater involvement of the european parliament and national parliaments in monitoring the application and implementation of the common rules.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the plurilateral agreement on services. since the deadlock in the wto negotiations and the importance of the services sector in european gdp, a new impetus was needed to bring new initiatives into the wto framework. with this vote we have authorized the commission, acting on behalf of the european union, to begin the multilateral negotiations. in addition, the exclusion of audiovisual and cultural services is kept outside the scope of the agreement, as is the case in the negotiations of the free trade agreement with the united states.
in writing. the service sector is a driving force in the european economy. the union is thus the world's largest exporter of services, accounting for 28% of global exports of services. the services sector accounts for three quarters of our gdp and employs 68% of the european workforce. the launch of negotiations on a plurilateral agreement on trade in services with 21 other wto member states is an opportunity for the union. while seeking to deepen cooperation in a wide range of services, it is nevertheless appropriate for the union, like the other parties to the agreement, to preserve a number of politically sensitive areas. therefore, in line with the approach taken in the wto general agreement on trade in services (gats), the negotiating mandate provides that the eu will not make commitments with regard to audiovisual services and that the negotiation will preserve public services.
in writing. "negotiations", but how many are there? yes, how many sectoral or general, plurilateral, multilateral or bilateral free trade agreements are there being negotiated between the european union and the united states? this acp agreement, on which we were not consulted before the negotiations were opened, aims to liberalize trade in services between some 20 countries, including the united states, in the same way as the wto general agreement on trade in services, but going further. it is important to remember that the latter opens the way to a kind of monstrous worldwide bolkenstein directive. what will be the link with the transatlantic agreement? what sector or industry, supposedly safeguarded in a highly publicised negotiation, has in fact been sacrificed in the other in a secret way? what are the negotiating bases, the red lines, of this acp? we don't know!
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution on the multilateral agreement on services. the motion for a resolution did not call into question the exclusion of audiovisual and cultural services from the scope of the agreement. so it was quite satisfactory. i'm glad you did.
in writing. for the eu trade in services is of paramount importance! they account for about three quarters of european gross domestic product and employment. the european states are therefore very interested in entering into negotiations with some 20 other wto members. the agreement should allow for further opening up of services markets but also introduce new rules on trade in services, in particular on public procurement, licensing procedures and access to communications networks. it is important that the eu negotiates in this area. in the long term, the agreement could be integrated into the joint wto agreements, and europe has certain requirements that it had to impose. it was out of the question that audiovisual and cultural services should be included in the negotiations, the fight for cultural exceptionalism has been won and we can welcome that. these negotiations, which are of great importance for european trade, will therefore have to be followed closely.
in writing. i voted in favour of increasing norwegian duties on agricultural products. norway is part of the european economic area and therefore has a mutually beneficial legal framework. but the recent protectionist measures taken by the norwegian government are in breach of the free trade agreement that binds the country to the eu. we have therefore called on the norwegian government to revise the free trade agreement on agricultural products in order to introduce fairer and more justified duties.
in writing. don't count on me to condemn norway's decision to protect its national interests by increasing its customs protections. quite the contrary! this is a healthy reflex which all our countries should emulate. you are shouting that this is a waste, but a more objective reflection would show how limited this measure is, certainly of rather little consequence for the interests of european agriculture and, moreover, compatible with norway's commitments to the wto. but norway has committed the ultimate crime: it has touched the taboo of free trade as conceived by the european union! well, long live the iconoclasts!
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution on the increase in norwegian duties on agricultural products. the motion for a resolution deplored in particular the measures recently imposed by the norwegian government. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. the resolution also asked the commission to specify the measures it envisaged to take if the norwegian authorities refused to back down. the proposal was adopted by a very large majority: 587 votes in favour, 48 against and 4 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. i supported the parliament's resolution on the increase in norwegian duties on agricultural products. we deplore the protectionist measures introduced by norway (which is not a member of the european union) which imposes excessive taxes on certain agricultural products from the union countries, including cheese, beef and lamb. we call on the authorities to lift these taxes, which are contrary to the trade agreements concluded between the two partners. the first countries to be affected by these acts of protectionism are france, denmark, spain, ireland, italy, the united kingdom and sweden.
in writing. in november 2012, when the eu-norway bilateral eea agreement had just entered into force, norway unilaterally decided to increase customs duties on certain cheeses and meat (from +277 to +429%) and, shortly before, on a variety of hydrangea (+72%). while these measures are in line with wto law, they are contrary to article 10 of the eu-norway bilateral agreement, which provides for reciprocal opening of markets between the partners. for several months now my group has rightly considered these measures to be protectionist and has asked the commission to open negotiations and take all the necessary measures. that is why i supported his request for a question to the european commission with a request for a reply in plenary, as well as this resolution which gives an update on the negotiations and the actions to be considered.
in writing. although outside the european union, norway is a member of the european economic area (eea) and enjoys privileged agreements with the member states. the country has just increased customs duties on imports of certain agricultural products from the european union. the resolution condemns the protectionist measures of norway and calls on the european commission to react firmly. in a frankly doctrinal tone, the eu 'presses the norwegian government and parliament to withdraw these measures' and even calls for further liberalisation of its market, particularly in agricultural matters. the european union is not content to put its member states under its tutelage, but is increasingly seeking to impose its neoliberal policies on all its economic partners and, in particular, on its immediate neighbours. what about the sovereign rights of states? this is unacceptable, especially as these measures are authorised by norway's list of concessions and commitments under the wto. and as one of our amendments points out, agricultural exports from the union to norway have increased by 150% since 2000. i therefore voted for our amendments and against this resolution which praises an ultra-liberal union that teaches lessons.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text to invite the member states and the commission to make the development of the digital single market a top priority and to adopt an ambitious strategy to make this beautiful project a reality on the ground. the idea of the digital single market is to invest in human capital to address skills shortages, by investing in the creation of future jobs with high growth potential, such as the green economy or health sectors. in my constituency, i am working on the establishment of a telemedicine system, which aims to address the shortage of doctors in medical deserts. i therefore strongly support the establishment of the digital single market, so that other local initiatives such as telemedicine can be implemented.
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution on completing the digital single market. this motion for a resolution contained many points. it stressed in particular that exploiting the single market through the services directive and the digital single market could, according to very serious studies, increase the output of the european economy by eur 800 billion. it also called on the commission to remove as a matter of urgency the remaining obstacles to the digital single market (the overly complex vat legal framework, the need for pan-european access to a secure online payment method, etc.). i'm glad you did.
in writing. i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on completing the digital single market. in the digital age, the potential of a single market in this area offers very positive prospects for economic growth and job creation. for example, a 10% increase in broadband in europe would be a gain of one growth point. the same is true for the development of ecommerce, whose 15% share in total trade (currently 5%) would bring an additional 1.7 growth points. we therefore emphasize the need to complete this project, which is being carried out by the french commissioner for the internal market, michel barnier. several draft reports are being prepared in parliament on the completion of the digital single market, in particular on the establishment of electronic invoicing, the reduction of costs for broadband deployment and data protection.
in writing. i hesitated to support this resolution on completing the digital single market: it is a good text overall, but i regret that its paragraph 39, which is enthusiastic about the proposal on the common european sales law, has been retained. in my view, the introduction of this instrument would pose many problems: optionally, this system would be introduced alongside national rights and would subject the same product to several regulations and guarantees. the regulatory framework would also be problematic in its articulation with the consumer rights directive, national rights, and the rome i regulation (to name but a few). i have finally decided to vote in favour of the text, so as not to jeopardise the fruit of a long work carried out on the subject of online commerce within our committee on the internal market and consumer protection. that said, i think it is inappropriate for our assembly to prejudge here, in an own-initiative resolution, the outcome of a controversial vote, of a legislative nature, which will culminate in the coming days in committee (and in a few weeks in plenary), precisely on the establishment or not of a common european sales law.
in writing. i have chosen to vote against the resolution on the commission's statement announcing a regulation on the completion of the digital single market. this resolution could have been an opportunity for the european parliament to put forward an ambitious digital project. at a time when this sector is becoming increasingly important in all areas of everyone's life, it would be essential, beyond words, to promote access for all, in particular through affordable prices. in many areas, especially rural or mountainous areas, access to such services is not always easy. it is therefore essential to ensure equal and universal access to wireless services. the establishment of a reliable infrastructure network is therefore an essential prerequisite. but this resolution does not provide for any of this and is mainly about further liberalising the digital 'market' in the name of completing the single market. we know what is going to happen, and the digital sector will also be subject to "free and undistorted" competition, the consequences of which are unfortunately well known.
in writing. austerity policies have particularly harmful consequences for the health of the most vulnerable among us. one third of greeks no longer have access to social security, and 'disappeared' diseases such as tuberculosis and malaria are returning to the union. 900,000 foreigners no longer have access to free healthcare in spain. it is time to sound the alarm and to confront our governments with the consequences of the very severe austerity measures which, in countries such as greece and spain, are causing intolerable health situations. in this report we call on the member states not to make drastic cuts in social and health spending, but to restore access to health care for all, including migrants. the dismantling of some health services is the least of the concerns. the social emergency in which we find ourselves calls for a social pact for europe which would include guaranteed universal access to certain health services essential for the coverage of basic needs and quality public services (in particular education and training). access to health care is a fundamental right, a guarantee of the future of our societies and our economies.
in writing. we cannot accept that children are no longer vaccinated, that unemployed people who are at the end of their working lives lose their health insurance. it is a whole model of society built on solidarity, through our social security systems, that is in danger of collapsing. if prevention of disease is no longer available to a section of the population, in the medium term it is people who will require more advanced care and who will be the more likely to seek personal assistance services. the latter are already in high demand, but lack of financial resources and professional recognition means that these personal assistance services cannot be developed in sufficient numbers. this is why, in terms of access to care, adequate and continuous training for health professionals must be ensured, structures for medical and social consultation must be developed, and investment in telemedicine must be increased to alleviate the medical deserts spreading throughout europe. i do not want this parliament to be accused of 'not helping europe in danger'.
in writing. the own-initiative report by my colleague jean lambert was adopted by a large majority: 537 votes in favour, 25 against and 65 abstentions. i have, for my part, chosen to abstain on the vote on the final resolution. it is our responsibility to stop the spiral of the crisis and to protect the most deprived. however, in my view, this report merely presents a catalogue of good intentions and denounces them. it offers no truly viable, effective and coherent solution. i'm sorry about that.
in writing. i supported the parliament's text on the impact of the crisis on access to care for vulnerable groups. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. almost a quarter of the european population is now at risk of poverty and exclusion. the health of these people is deteriorating and the disparities in access to care between the rich and the poor are growing. we therefore call on member states to promote investment in social services so that vulnerable groups in particular can receive adequate medical treatment. as such, it is essential that special attention be paid to the disabled, children and the longterm unemployed.
in writing. the issue of health, and in particular access to care, is a fundamental issue which, whatever the circumstances, should not be subject to any restrictions. however, as the report points out, the healthcare sector has not been spared by budgetary austerity measures, significantly affecting access to care for the most vulnerable. i find it appalling that the current political priorities are so contrary to the well-being of citizens. inadequate access to care, due to drastic cuts in health spending, has serious implications for the quality and dignity of human life, which must be avoided. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to congratulate mrs antonescu on her tenacity and her remarkable sense of consensus, since it took almost two years and several presidencies to arrive at this very balanced text. we have - as the rapporteur and the commissioner have pointed out - embarked on a major judicial reform since the beginning of this mandate: the right to information, the right to interpretation and translation. now we are preparing to vote tomorrow on access to a lawyer for all citizens of the european union. it is a great step forward towards a europe of justice which i am sure we will remember later. it is a balanced text which guarantees everyone the right to benefit from the expertise of a lawyer to advise and defend him, while taking into account the needs of the investigation so as not to impede all the efforts of the police forces in the service of truth and justice. the role of the lawyer is expanded to ensure a fair trial. the text also does not forget the imperative requirements which may require temporary and limited derogations from the right of access to a lawyer, such as the fight against terrorism and organised crime. this balanced text will thus strengthen justice by guaranteeing effective rights to suspects and accused persons, while allowing for the smooth conduct of investigations in order to ensure justice. however, i regret that this text was not tabled together with a proposal on legal aid. this would have made much more sense to the proposal, while allowing everyone - regardless of their resources - real and not just theoretical access to a lawyer.

the rapporteur. - mr president, madam commissioner, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this is a very technical text, but it has economic implications and, i would say, relatively important ethical implications. in the context of the 3x20 programme, we voted in 2008 for the obligation for member states to have 10% of their transport produced from renewable energy sources by 2020. the european parliament had already expressed the wish that the indirect effects of land use change (iluc/casi) could be taken into account, since this is a provision designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. the commission was therefore asked to draw up a report. it was based on the ifpri study, and the proposal before us today amends the fuel directive and the renewable energy directive. it has four objectives. firstly, to put an end to a policy which is not sustainable in the long term: that of having to choose, with regard to a food plant, whether to consume it or to make it into a fuel. secondly, to take into account the investments made by the industrialists - with a lot of community aid for the rest - since 2009, in order to develop the so-called first generation agrofuels. thirdly, to ensure that advanced agrofuels - those that can be made from algae, from power-to-gas, from carbon capture - can be widely encouraged in the years ahead. and finally, to make sure that our policy actually has an impact, that the reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are the ones we expect. it is in this context that the commission has put forward a proposal to us and that, following the debates we have had in parliament, we are now arriving at this text. the debate was very difficult because economic interests were extremely present. the report adopted by the committee on the environment was already a compromise report with all the groups, since all the groups had agreed on the basis of a reduction to 5.5 of first generation agrofuels and the inclusion of iluc/casi in the fuel quality directive from 2020 onwards. the report by the committee on the environment went a little further and, in the interests of compromise, i have therefore tried to find a solution for this vote in plenary that would have the support of the majority in parliament. we have reached this point in my group, with my colleague jens rohde, the representative of the itre committee, and i think that the proposal we have put forward is balanced. we are proposing 6% for first generation biofuels, including energy crops. we propose to apply iluc/casi only in the fuel quality directive and not in the sustainability criteria from 2020, with a clause for a methodology revision in 2016 or 2017. i would point out, however, that the ifpri report, which has been the subject of much criticism, much discussion and conflicting reports of studies - often, moreover, from those who have an interest in continuing to develop first generation agrofuels - has nevertheless been corroborated by a study published in july by the commission which shows that the actual data do indeed confirm the results that have been found. we also propose 2.5% for advanced agrofuels, i.e. to set a sub-target, as the itre committee wanted, and 1.5% for electricity. we propose to reduce the use of the multiplier proposed by the commission from two to four, keeping a factor of four only for the most advanced biofuels and a factor of two only for cooking oils and animal fats. finally, we propose to extend the fuel quality directive until 2025 with a target of 9%. it is perhaps less than a number of my colleagues would have wished. it is probably too much for a number of our colleagues in the epp, and i regret that they did not want to reach a compromise before coming to the plenary, but i hope that we can find a majority on the text i have just proposed.
mr president, madam commissioner, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this week we have the opportunity to correct a mistake we have made, a mistake which has seriously damaged the international order in recent years. i am, of course, referring to our desire to limit and contain biofuels. we cannot accept that one of our policies - for the simple reason that we want to achieve the quantified targets we have set ourselves - is starving the people of the poorest countries, is accelerating the dramatic deforestation of developing countries and is accelerating the rise in food prices. this is the result of our policy on biofuels. for all these reasons, i support a text that limits first generation biofuels and that makes a strict distinction between good and bad biofuels, a text that allows the incorporation of the iluc/casi factor into the renewable energy directive. i therefore strongly support the compromise tabled, which allows the limitation of first generation biofuels to 5.5%, while safeguarding the investments made by our companies, giving them time to adapt to the new standards in order to preserve jobs in our territories. international responsibility and securing jobs in our crisis economies must be the two pillars of this legislation, which we are about to vote on. answer is "blue cardboard". ladies and gentlemen, you are talking about indonesia. let us turn to indonesia. palm oil production is growing under pressure from the global demand for biofuels. palm oil plantations now cover 11 million hectares in indonesia and will cover 28 million hectares if no incentive is given by then. this palm oil cultivation has led to massive deforestation and the grabbing of indigenous lands for food crops, all in a climate of violence that is certain to be driven by local law enforcement. this is the difference between them and those who are for this order and this international justice, and who do not want to starve the people.
member of the commission. − mr president, i think that already from the start of this debate ms lepage was stressing how technical and complicated this file is, and that is indeed no exaggeration. i also think that we can hear that in the debate – that it invites too many rather different approaches. i must also say on behalf of mr oettinger and myself that, as we have been listening to this debate – an interesting debate with very different views presented – we have remained convinced that the commission’s proposal presents the most balanced compromise between environmental and economic interests. this is because it sends a clear signal to industry on the need to move to advanced biofuels that deliver substantial greenhouse-gas savings while respecting existing investments. in this context, we firmly believe in the need to maintain the limit that conventional biofuels make towards the renewable energy directive targets at current consumption levels. a sub-target for advanced biofuels may be complementary to this approach and improve the final biofuels mix in 2020. however, its application in isolation does not prevent further increase in the consumption of conventional biofuels. more importantly, a sub-target alone does not mitigate the negative environmental impact of conventional biofuels, which is the very reason why, in the existing directive, the commission was requested to come forward with this proposal. i think it was claude turmes and others who mentioned the question of whether we should invest in research into second-generation biofuels and advanced biofuels. of course we should, and that is also a priority in the new mff, as has been mentioned by the commission. but let me be clear. deleting the cap or increasing it to an unsustainable level, as proposed in some of the amendments, will mean that the iluc problem will continue to be largely unaddressed and further damage will take place. i would therefore, on behalf of the commission, ask you to support an ambitious cap in wednesday’s upcoming vote. furthermore, we need to improve transparency and raise awareness of the indirect land-use change impact associated with the biofuels we consume in the eu. this is why the commission maintains the inclusion of iluc factors in member states’ reports under the renewable energy and fuel quality directives. we believe that these values stem from the best available science. however, the commissioners have concerns that some alternative methodologies proposed in amendments submitted to the vote on wednesday and being used to justify the banning of imported biofuels are flawed. the commission is therefore not in a position to accept them. let me also stress that all the measures we introduce should of course be accompanied by suitable grandfathering provisions in order to allow for industry to adjust to the proposed changes. the 20% target for the overall renewable energy share, the 10% transport target and the 6% fuel quality directive target are pillars of our energy and climate package. the commission will therefore oppose any amendments lowering these levels of ambition. in this context, the commission has, for example, just as strong reservations about the need to increase multipliers for the use of renewable electricity by trains. actually, it is hard for us to see the added value in doing so. there is a pressing need to agree on an effective approach to tackle iluc in order to mitigate the environmental impact as well as to provide clear signals to investors. accordingly the commission remains fully available to the parliament and to the council to help achieve progress, with a view to finalising trialogue discussions before the end of the current term. just one final comment. yes, science is developing. of course it always is; it always will be. but we should not use that as an excuse for waiting, for inaction, and thereby continuing something that we already now know is unsustainable. may i just say that our scientific basis is robust and it is the best available science, as requested in the current directive, and recent studies have actually confirmed that the values used by the commission are (1) based on good science and (2) very much in line with the eu’s normal principle – the precautionary principle.

in writing. the lepage report highlights an important point: iluc factors must be included in the sustainability criteria. the potential problems associated with the large-scale exploitation of biofuels are numerous: monoculture, soil degradation, water pollution, deforestation. according to the 2007-2016 oecd/fao agricultural outlook, biofuels are radically changing agricultural markets and driving up global prices for many commodities. the cultivation of maize-based agrofuels not only competes with food production, but also consumes a lot of water: several hundred litres of water for one litre of ethanol. furthermore, according to a study published in the scientific journal critical reviews in plant science, the production of ethanol requires the consumption of six units of energy to produce one unit of ethanol. biofuels are not the miracle answer to the coming energy crisis. to replace all the oil currently used in transport with vegetable oil, the area cultivated in france would have to be tripled and devoted exclusively to oil. biofuels are therefore a political mistake and a major environmental hazard.
