in writing. the amendment to the regulation adopted is intended to adapt the legislation to the new rules of the treaty on the functioning of the european union introduced by the treaty of lisbon. these updates define the areas in which the european commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to amend or supplement non-essential elements of the regulation, and to adopt implementing acts to implement the regulation. these powers enable the european commission to implement measures quickly and lighten the legislative agenda of the parliament. meps nevertheless retain a power of control over the way the european commission uses its powers. i voted in favour of this text because it was necessary to adapt the regulation to the new rules laid down by the treaties.

in writing. the european parliament adopted on tuesday, 10 september, a report on the protection of certain fishery resources. this report will simplify the possibilities for action to avoid fishing for fry as regards the division of regions into geographical areas, the use of mesh combinations, the determination of the percentage of target species caught by several fishing vessels, the rules on technical descriptions and the method of use of authorised gear which may be attached to the fishing net. the commission should therefore avoid conflicts between member states which are harmful to fishermen by harmonizing legislation in this field. while i am generally reserved about the use of delegated acts by the european commission, which severely limits the scrutiny of the european parliament, the report states that the delegation of power should be limited in time to allow regular evaluations. this procedural loophole preserves the role of parliament in the institutional process without, however, hindering the effectiveness of delegated and implementing acts on issues as important and urgent as those of the conservation of fisheries resources.

in writing. there is an increasing number of unions between nationals of member states, whether marriages or partnerships registered with a public authority. today, one in seven marriages in the union involves citizens of more than one member state. the 2010 citizenship of the union report identifying obstacles to the exercise of union rights has established that uncertainty about the property rights of international couples, composed of nationals of two different member states, is a major challenge for europeans in their daily lives. it is therefore necessary to remove the obstacles faced by such international couples. the determination of the competent court and the law applicable in the event of separation or death of one of the spouses and better recognition of decisions between member states will thus contribute to establishing a clearer legal framework, while respecting the property rights of the different member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am in favour of clarifying the rules applying to the property effects of registered partnerships in the european union. i am particularly in favour of the possibility for registered partnerships to choose the law applicable to their property effects. however, i appreciate that this report does not oblige member states to recognise such a partnership.
in writing. this is a new development in everyday europe! we have adopted two texts this week to improve the rights of binational couples: more clarity, more simplification of the legal framework governing the relations of these binational couples in the european area. the main and not least advance of this text is that the rights of binational couples are guaranteed, whether they are married or in a civil partnership. another element of these two texts is that the persons concerned (a married couple or a civil partnership) will be able to choose the legislation applicable to their property rights when these two people separate and the marriage or civil partnership is terminated. finally, decisions will be mutually recognised throughout the european union, while respecting the different property rights applied in the member states.
in writing. i have given my full support to this text which will clarify the property rights of almost 16 million international couples living in europe, of whom 650 000 would, every year, face considerable difficulties in finding out which legislation applies to their case and which court has jurisdiction when their marriage or partnership comes to an end. it is essential to put an end to the current legal disparities between the 27 and to encourage the search for the most favourable court (forum shopping), often in favour of the wealthiest spouse. the aim is therefore to remove the legal uncertainty surrounding the property rights of these couples on the basis of clear rules to determine the applicable legislation, the competent court, and to provide rules for the recognition and enforcement of judicial decisions through a single procedure, which i welcome.
in writing. this directive will provide a clear legal framework for the 16 million international couples (of different nationalities and/or living abroad) in the european union. in the event of the death of one of the partners or separation, legal procedures will be simplified and their cost reduced by clarification of the law applicable to their property. the european union will therefore help these couples to avoid a legal "fighter's journey" in an already difficult period for them. the directive also clarifies the legislation governing the effects of registered partnerships on legal relationships between the couple or one of the partners and a third party, for example in the case of a mortgage. in the case of registered partnerships such as pacs, the assets will be subject to the country of registration of the partnership. i voted in favour of this text because international couples must be able to benefit from a clear legal framework and the same rights as other european couples.
in writing. i voted in favour of the reports on the regulations on matrimonial property regimes to clarify the legal situation of international couples, couples of different nationalities and/or couples living abroad. the latter face legal difficulties and high procedural costs due to uncertainties regarding the national laws applicable to their property. both texts address this problem by providing consistent rules for determining the court with jurisdiction and the applicable legislation.
in writing. - this regulation seeks to solve the legal difficulties encountered by couples living in 'registered partnerships', the european equivalent of the french pacs, when they are nationals of different member states. the definition of partnerships is neutral and open (including de facto partnerships between homosexual couples). of the 211 000 registered partnerships, 41 000 are in more than one member state. the text clarifies many procedural points such as the applicable law, the enforceability of contracts vis-à-vis third parties and the consequences for property in the event of separation. at present, in the event of a dispute, a better informed party can take advantage of the situation to bring his case before the court of the member state which is most favourable to him. the distinction between marriage and partnership emerged from a lengthy discussion. the commission did not want to have a single text for both, to take account of the specific features of the partnership, starting with the fact that it does not exist everywhere. parliament has reduced the distinction by bringing the law applicable to partnerships closer to that of marriage, in line with the principle of equality and the prohibition of discrimination in the union.

in writing. this directive is one of a series of proposals to ensure that the rights of european citizens arrested in another member state are respected, in particular those who have been the subject of a european arrest warrant. the right of access to a lawyer is a further step in the creation of a single area of justice in the european union. the directive provides, inter alia, for access to a lawyer to be guaranteed from the time of police questioning and throughout the criminal proceedings, for a person close to the suspect to be informed of his arrest and to be able to communicate with him, and for suspects in a state of which they are not nationals to be able to communicate with the consulate of their country and to receive visits. i voted in favour of this directive in order to strengthen and guarantee the right of european citizens to a fair trial in all member states.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings. this draft directive is part of the strategy launched by the council in 2009 to strengthen the procedural rights of persons suspected or prosecuted in criminal matters. the proposal essentially establishes the principle that any suspected or accused person should have the right to access a lawyer, as soon as possible and in a manner that allows him or her to effectively exercise his or her rights of defence. while this principle is recognised by the echr and by some member states, it continues to be flouted within the eu, as evidenced by some judgments of the european court of human rights (cyprus in 2008 or france in 2010). in addition, the rules of the directive will apply in the context of the european arrest warrant, i.e. the right of access to a lawyer will be guaranteed both in the issuing state and in the executing state, i.e. where one is arrested. this should make it possible to move towards the harmonisation of criminal proceedings in the union, to the benefit of the persons subject to the proceedings.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which guarantees every citizen access to a lawyer in all eu member states. any suspect or accused person may request the assistance of a lawyer before the start of any police questioning and throughout the criminal proceedings. in addition, prisoners will be allowed to communicate with a person of their choice. this right will be regulated so as not to impede the proper conduct of the investigation and not to obstruct the work of the police and the judiciary. procedures are also being revised to deal with emergencies such as terrorist threats.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which allows a person arrested in another eu member state to exercise his rights of defence in accordance with the standards of the echr. this should lead to the right to a lawyer at the time of arrest and before being questioned by the police, with the lawyer then being able to participate in the questioning. these provisions were not obtained without difficulty. the rapporteur had to fight hard against the council and the member states who wanted to introduce a number of exceptions which would have made access to a fair trial arbitrary. the council wanted in particular to derogate from the principle of confidentiality of communications between the accused and his lawyer (an extra layer) and to define minor offences broadly, which would have constituted as many exceptions to the rules of the directive. i welcome the adoption of this text, which is in line with the demands of the associations of lawyers and human rights defenders. the battle waged by the ep shows that the europe of rights is a fight worth fighting. french law will therefore have to evolve in this area. i regret, however, that the member states have been given a three-year deadline for implementation.
in writing. the subprime crisis that erupted in the us in 2007 exposed the weaknesses of the mortgage markets and the need for common rules. the new rules are designed to provide better information and better protection for european consumers. the borrower will thus have to be informed in a clear and precise manner of the risks involved in taking out a loan. the commission has already proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive. the sanchez presedo report, which i supported, sets out the solutions proposed to the borrower in the event of default. in the long term, these common rules will make it possible to achieve an integrated mortgage credit market.
in writing. i voted in favour of better information for consumers when they take out a loan to buy a residential property. at present, consumers are not well protected from market fluctuations and repayment difficulties. they will be better informed before the contract is signed about the conditions and risks of the loan and better advised during the contract. as member states try to revive their housing markets, consumer protection rules had to be strengthened and over-indebtedness fought.
in writing. borrowers will now be better protected, not only when signing their loan agreement, but also when repaying it. in the event of default, the text introduces measures to prevent them from falling into debt beyond the limits of what is reasonable, with a set of safeguards to protect them in case of difficulties. preventing families from becoming over-indebted, ending irresponsible behaviour that leads to excessive debt, is our objective and it is clear, because it was one of the main causes of the financial crisis.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i support the objective of better protecting consumers in the european union by taking into account the specific nature of loans relating to residential immovable property. i am particularly in favour of ensuring that consumers have a reasonable and sufficient period of time before they commit themselves to taking out a loan and of preventing practices which could lead them to take out a credit agreement which would not be in their best interests.
in writing. the economic crisis, which was first triggered by a mortgage crisis in the us in 2007, demonstrated that the mortgage market needed to be better regulated worldwide. the european commission had to act. the directive it put to the vote of the european parliament aims to create a single market for mortgage loans, which in 2009 accounted for more than half of the eu's gross domestic product (gdp) (€6 trillion), while protecting consumers. lenders or intermediaries will be able to operate throughout the european union after registering with the national authorities. lenders will be required to be more responsible, in particular through the prohibition of misleading advertising, the provision of a cooling-off period for consumers, the prohibition of granting a loan if borrowers are not considered solvent, and better information to consumers about contractual conditions and risks. i voted in favour of this text, because it will make it possible to regulate european consumers and the mortgage market better.
in writing. i voted with conviction for the directive on mortgage credit, which aims to protect the borrower from banks and credit institutions and to avoid over-indebtedness. this directive strengthens the liability of the lender for loans secured by a mortgage or any credit relating to the principal residence. the borrower's ability to repay will now be assessed and verified before the credit agreement is signed. this assessment shall take into account all factors that may affect the borrower's ability to repay, including all of its financial commitments and income. credit intermediaries, such as the large retailers, are developing credit with less and less supervision, creating dramatic situations of over-indebtedness for consumers. these intermediaries are the main targets of this directive. member states will need to improve their credit management and ensure in particular that assistance is available to the least experienced and most vulnerable borrowers such as first-time borrowers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to establish a common regulatory framework on market abuse. it ensures the integrity of financial markets in the european union by improving investor protection as well.
in writing. the financial crisis has undermined consumer confidence in the financial system. in the face of market abuse, insider trading and market manipulation, which have enriched some banks, the european union has decided to tighten its legislation. these new rules, which i supported, will act as a deterrent to companies being prosecuted for market abuse. financial penalties could reach up to 15% of their annual turnover.
in writing. i voted in favour of stricter rules on market abuse, in order to stabilise the financial system and better control the markets. some bankers have enriched themselves through insider trading and market manipulation, which has lowered the confidence of consumers and investors in banks. as europe tries to revive its markets, restoring confidence in banks and protecting consumers in the financial services sector is essential to clean up the system.
in writing. financial markets are now subject to simple and clear rules to prevent misuse and abuse: this helps to put an end to uncontrolled finance. i welcome the european union's reaction to this matter: after the scandals over the manipulation of the libor and euribor key rates, we have reached a balanced text to prevent such errors from being repeated. we also take account of technological developments in financial markets, such as high-frequency trading, and new trading practices: we must be realistic and adapt to market developments, and this text fulfils that objective.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i support, in particular, the introduction of stronger sanctions in cases of market abuse, which ensure a coherent approach in the different eu member states and enhance their deterrent effect. the future directive on criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation should strengthen these provisions.
in writing. the 2008 financial crisis showed that financial markets had taken advantage of deregulation to introduce practices that threaten the stability of our financial system and economy. while european citizens have had to support the bailout of banks, we must ensure that markets adopt healthier practices. the aim of this directive is to better regulate insider dealing, which allows investors with confidential information to profit from prices that do not reflect that information. the directive will also make it possible to better control market manipulation, which refers to operations aimed at artificially changing prices, for example by increasing trading volumes to raise prices or by spreading rumours to lower prices. the directive will now apply to all markets and new financial products and its application will be simplified. i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which provides for a tightening of the rules on market abuse. in particular, the report introduces a criminal regime for market abuse with minimum sanctions set at union level.
in writing. i abstained on this report on 'market abuse', i.e. insider dealing and market manipulation. the overall objective of preventing fraud and manipulation of financial markets is certainly a worthy one. five years after the unprecedented crisis caused by these same financial markets and with no harmonised regulation in place at present, it was high time that the european union addressed the issue. however, the motives displayed are chilling to the most enthusiastic: "to make the financial markets more attractive to those seeking to raise capital". that's all there is to it. how can we still say that we need to continue to make financial markets more attractive to anyone? when we know the divisions between the member states, we can only be sceptical. there are some minor adjustments, but we are still in the so-called moralization of financial capitalism. we still refuse to take this issue at face value. one example: on sanctions, the report proposes to establish 'minimum rules on administrative measures, penalties and fines' while leaving member states 'free to set higher standards'.

in writing. the eu member states have committed themselves to completing the internal energy market by 2014. such a market will benefit both consumers and businesses, who will both benefit from lower prices, thus promoting the competitiveness of businesses and their job creation. reducing the eu's energy dependence must be the first priority of a common energy policy. to do this, the eu must exploit the full potential of all renewable energy sources, while improving its energy efficiency in both the public transport sector and the building sector, where the potential for savings is greatest. europe must also guarantee energy security for each of its members and prevent the interruption of gas supplies to some eu countries that are heavily dependent on russia. a common gas market for the whole of europe, based on adequate infrastructure, storage capacity and strategic reserve requirements, together with solidarity between member states, is the only possible basis for a secure energy supply.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which proposes a wide range of concrete solutions to complete the internal energy market. it seems to me that in this proposal we have succeeded in reconciling in a coherent way the main objectives of the internal energy market: security of supply, the promotion of healthy competition in the european energy market for the benefit of consumers, and the reduction of energy dependence on third countries. we have no shortage of ideas, such as the creation of a european energy community, increased european funds for investment in renewable energy, and of course in infrastructure. the european energy network must be smart and forward-looking: european consumers will need more power and more knowledge to better control their energy bills. such a european energy policy would have a positive impact on consumers and on european growth, which is currently held back by europe's dependence on oil and gas imports.
in writing. as the price of energy falls in the us, particularly due to the exploration of shale gas, i am concerned about the rising energy bill for households and businesses in europe. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which proposes concrete ways of combating this perverse phenomenon of rising energy prices, which is a problem of both declining purchasing power and declining competitiveness. i particularly share the epp rapporteur's desire to find an alternative to the indexation of gas prices to those of oil, because it leads to an unjustified and disproportionate increase in gas prices. to bring down energy prices, competition in the energy sector should also be reinvigorated, so that consumers can choose between several quality suppliers. this requires a real separation of distribution and production activities. as long as an energy company has control of the infrastructure, it can block or alter access to its market and prevent the development of competition, to the detriment of the interests of companies, citizens and the european internal market!

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, since the 20th century, a number of factors have influenced the european eel population. this is the case, of course, with fishing, but also with the drying up of wetlands, drainage, poaching, migratory barriers, pollution, pumping, turbining and many other factors. as you can see, this list is long, probably too long. we must therefore pay attention to the preservation of this stock. however, we must be pragmatic and stop making fishing the scapegoat for the problems of the eel population. regulating fishing activities alone cannot be an adequate and appropriate response. the habitats of the species, which are endangered by various human activities, need to be restored but unfortunately this is not what is proposed in this report. the rapporteur forgets the contribution of the fishing sector to the recovery of the eel stock. in france, for example, the sector has made significant efforts and sacrifices to achieve the mortality reduction targets set by the 2020 management plan. the production of civilian consumption was reduced by 65% compared to the period 2004-2008. it's not a problem. the fishing fleet has been reduced by 50% since 2006. efforts have also been made to reduce prices. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. that would be putting the plow before the oxen. i would like parliament to adopt a report focusing solely on alignment with the lisbon treaty without amending regulation (ec) no 1100/2007.

in writing. like the vast majority of meps, i voted in favour of this report. this text follows the collective work, throughout the mandate, of the members of the intergroup on minority languages, of which i am an active member. i voted for this report because it advocates a heritage approach to the question of endangered european languages and linguistic diversity in europe. a language is a european heritage. when it disappears, european heritage is affected. article 3 (3) of the treaty on european union states that the eu 'shall respect the richness of its cultural and linguistic diversity and shall ensure the safeguarding and development of europe's cultural heritage'. it is therefore the eu's responsibility to preserve its languages. the report also calls on all member states to ratify the european charter for regional languages (only 16 have done so). the report also calls for the european commission to take concrete measures to protect endangered languages, including more financial support. this text is therefore a step forward and a clear message from the european parliament to the member states, and in particular to france, which must ratify the charter on languages!
in writing. i strongly support this report on 'endangered languages and linguistic diversity in europe' as there is an urgent need to relaunch support for regional languages and multilingualism. the report, adopted by a very large majority of meps, aims to support europe's linguistic heritage, which is now particularly threatened. we have in france, in europe, an exceptionally rich cultural heritage which must be promoted. regional languages are key elements of this wealth and these languages are now dying out, because the public authorities have neglected them for too long. this report is going in the right direction.
in writing. - i voted against this own-initiative report which calls for the ratification of the european charter for regional or minority languages. the consequences of ratification would be contrary to the laudable objectives of promoting the richness of france's heritage and the cultural diversity of its regions. once the charter has been ratified, any citizen who speaks a minority language recognised as such by the signatory country will be entitled to bring an action before the european court of human rights to have the texts of laws translated and to have administrative documents in his or her own language. that would create a real gas factory! france does not recognise the existence of minorities within its territory which as such have collective rights which can be challenged in its legal system. it considers that the application of human rights to all nationals of a state, in equality and non-discrimination, normally affords them, whatever their situation, the full protection to which they are entitled. finally, ratification of the charter is contrary to the french constitution, which states in article 2 that 'the language of the republic is french'.
in writing. language diversity contributes to the enrichment of cultures and i am of course a supporter of this principle. shakespeare, goethe, or voltaire could never have expressed their thought so well if they had to re-translate it into another language. i also believe that regional and minority languages are part of this linguistic heritage which we must protect and preserve. however, i am a legalist and therefore do not want a report on linguistic diversity to be used as an opportunity to circumvent the values and principles of our republic in order to obtain, through european pressure, what our constitutional council has declared incompatible. i have therefore chosen to reject the alfonsi report, which contains provisions requiring the member states to ratify the european charter for regional or minority languages, even though the constitutional council had given a negative opinion in 1999 on the grounds that the charter contained provisions which could call into question the principles of the indivisibility of the republic, equality before the law and the unity of the french people. article 2 of the french constitution states: "the language of the republic is french". no one but the french people has the authority to challenge it and to decree it.

in writing. this report calls for the ratification of the council of europe's european charter for regional or minority languages. this charter, clearly ethnically inspired, was declared by the constitutional council to be contrary to the fundamental principles of the french republic, and in particular to secularism. it provides for the granting of special rights to groups speaking a particular regional language in the public sphere, in particular in the operation of public services or the judiciary. it breaks citizens' equality and undermines the free exercise of citizenship. while this system may indeed suit national minorities in europe, it is a diversion from the attachment to regional languages and dialects in a single and indivisible republic like france. such a reference is unacceptable: to claim special rights for a category of the population in the name of differences is an attack on republican equality. that is why i am voting against.

in writing. we have just put the brakes on agrofuels to reduce their negative impact on deforestation, land grabbing and food security in developing countries. it was essential to vote for a cap on first generation agrofuels (the rate chosen is higher than hoped, 6% of the final energy consumed in transport), produced from food crops. we want to feed the men, not the cars. it was also essential to include casi (iluc) factors in greenhouse gas accounting, reflecting the climate impact of agrofuels due to the shift in food production from different raw materials. this was the minimum necessary to take concrete action to address the negative consequences (climate change, food insecurity and the social consequences of the shift of food production) of the current eu biofuels policy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. a first step has been taken, but the battle is far from won.

in writing. the aim of this directive is to promote the development of 'advanced' biofuels. these biofuels, which are produced from agricultural residues or algae, for example, have a lower impact on the environment because they do not lead to the destruction of natural areas or the conversion of agricultural land. increasing biofuel production poses two problems: agricultural land originally used for food crops is converted into land for biofuel production, and natural areas are converted into agricultural land, leading to a reduction in biodiversity and an increase in greenhouse gas emissions. we have therefore decided to increase the share of advanced biofuels to 2.5% of final fuel consumption. i supported this directive because we need to encourage innovation to make biofuels less polluting and to prevent their development from threatening food crops. the vote will also help the eu meet the target of using 10% renewable energy in transport by 2020.

in writing. in 2008, the eu set itself an ambitious target: by 2020, 10% of transport fuel should be produced from renewable energy sources. in this area, the eu relied heavily on biofuels. however, the shortcomings of so-called 'first generation' biofuels, i.e. those derived from cereals, sugars or oilseeds, have forced the eu to react. some say that the growing use of biofuels will lead to the deforestation of virgin forests in indonesia and brazil. deforestation would generate more greenhouse gases than fossil fuels. in addition, agrofuel cultivation is blamed for being at the expense of traditional agriculture. this would put pressure on food prices, raising the threat of further hunger riots. however, the amendments tabled by the committee on the environment go too far. they are not based on a sufficiently reliable methodology for calculating indirect land use change (casi) and place undue burdens on european farmers. i therefore opposed it, preferring the amendments tabled by the committee on industry.
in writing. after the initial euphoria about biofuels as the future of clean energy, the indirect problems of large-scale production are beginning to emerge. the cultivation of biofuels poses two main problems: intensive land use, and the substitution of food crops for energy crops. although biofuels can be a boon in the fight against greenhouse gas emissions, their expansion must be limited to preserve food crops. thus these constraints, the casi (criterion to limit the footprint on the soil) and the ghg (greenhouse gas emissions), must be cumulated to find a balance. i regret, as does the socialist group, that the right wing has timidly voted for a 6% ceiling for first generation biofuels. nevertheless, this directive is a step in the right direction and represents a step forward in terms of regulating energy production and a balanced distribution of land between energy and food needs.
in writing. biofuels have long been considered the most effective tool to achieve the eu's greenhouse gas emission reduction targets. first generation biofuels, produced from food crops, have many negative effects. they are leading to the reallocation of land for food crops to those used to produce them, are increasing deforestation, are contributing to food insecurity and to rising food prices. worse, developing countries are the first to be hit by the increase in biofuel production. the european union had to react and correct its policy to promote the development of biofuels. i therefore welcome the vote on the lepage report which sets a ceiling of 5.5% for the production of first generation biofuels, while promoting the development of second generation biofuels produced from non-food crops. finally, i would like to call for the strengthening of food stocks through the european plan of food aid for the most deprived (pead).
in writing. i voted in favour of this revision of two directives on the promotion and quality of biofuels. studies on agrofuels show that complementary factors need to be taken into account to improve their energy efficiency and energy savings in the fight against climate change. the increasing use of agricultural land for the production of agrofuels is causing ghg emissions, known as the casi (indirect land use change) phenomenon. the european parliament voted in favour of 6% integration of agrofuels of food origin into fossil fuels, but it only takes into account the casi factor from 2020 onwards. it supports advanced biofuels, produced from sources other than food. this half-baked result is the result of strong lobbying, but also of the timid proposal of the european commission, which, although acknowledging the casi phenomenon, only proposed to report the emissions of agrofuels related to casi! the vote on the amendments was significant, with the amendments from the industry and environment committees being returned back to back, almost all rejected by the liberal vote.

in writing. initially, biofuel policies were intended to reduce the eu's energy footprint and help combat global warming, but they have clearly had a negative indirect effect on the environment. indeed, land for agrofuels is often land that was previously used for food crops and untimely development of this sector can endanger the food security of producing countries. in addition, agrofuel cultivation can lead to deforestation in producing countries seeking to expand their crops. the european legislation should therefore be adapted accordingly to give priority to so-called 'second generation' agrofuels, based on more innovative and environmentally friendly techniques such as waste reprocessing. the approach taken by the european parliament, which sets a target of 6% of final energy consumed in transport by 2020, should allow a transition from one generation to the next while giving industry, which had invested in first-generation biofuels, time to adapt.
in writing. although it was adopted by the european parliament, i voted against this text, which i consider incomplete. while it is essential to protect our resources, it is also crucial to take into account the results of the latest scientific studies showing that the stock has recovered. that was not done and explains my lack of support for this text.
in writing. in 2007, the commission developed a european-wide eel management plan. in this report it is proposed that the commission should assess the current restocking measures to determine to what extent they are actually contributing to the recovery of the eel stock. i voted against these new restrictions, since the member states are still in the process of setting the 2007 targets and a significant effort is already required of them to achieve good ecological status of the waters. the 2007 recovery plan had already reduced fishing and catch opportunities, so i voted against the final report to support the fishermen.
in writing. i am deeply unfavourable to the lövin report, as it unjustifiably amends the 2007 eel regulation which developed a european eel management plan. the key point of this report is the request to the european commission to make a new proposal for an eel management plan by march 2014, even though there has been a 27% reduction in eel fishing enterprises. the revision of the eel plan every two years is also unnecessary, especially since all states are already implementing the 2007 objectives. i support strict alignment with the lisbon treaty without any substantive change to this regulation.
in writing. the european eel stock is under threat and there is an urgent need for a framework to better protect them. the commission will have to come forward with a proposal as soon as possible, and the states will have to be more vigilant, as it is a matter of preserving our biodiversity and our resources. but let us be careful not to go too far, to the detriment of our fishing and our jobs.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i agree in particular that the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts to take measures to deal with a significant decrease in the average market prices of eels for restocking compared to those of eels used for other purposes.
in writing. i voted in favour of this new legislative proposal. the european eel stock is in a critical state and we need to act as soon as possible to protect and conserve it. one of the main measures in the current recovery plan for european eel is not conservation, as it should be, but rather minimising damage to the fishing industry. the current practice of restocking, which involves moving eels from one place to another to repopulate the first, leads to overfishing and has become a real economic activity for the industry. we lack information on the means it uses to maximise the chances of survival of the eels that are restocked. so there are many gaps to be filled. the green group has therefore requested new requirements and new information on the state of the stock. the vote will lead the commission to present a new legislative proposal by march 2014.
in writing. − according to the iucn, the european eel was classified as endangered in 2010, and the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices) reported in 2011 that blinded stocking programmes are unlikely to contribute to the recovery of the stock. the eel stock is facing not only climate problems such as pollution or changing ocean currents, but also overexploitation and the inability to control it due to mismatched catch and export data. i therefore vote in favour of introducing a new regulation which will ensure the repopulation of eels, based on scientifically based guidelines which prevent, for example, the spread of diseases, and control the fisheries, ensuring that eels with a diameter of less than 20 cm in length reach the reproductive stage.
in writing. according to the scientific community, the stock of european eels has declined by 95% over the last 30 years. meps therefore adopted a resolution calling on the european commission to present a legislative proposal by march 2014. we want the member states to provide the information needed for stock assessments every two years instead of every six years. the member states which do not provide this information in time may be subject to sanctions. the european commission will also have to assess the effectiveness of the current restocking measures, which allow the recovery of the eel stock. i voted in favour of this resolution because it is essential to evaluate the current measures and to find new solutions to replenish the eel stock, as this is the future of european fisheries.
in writing. i voted against the report because the additional restrictions proposed for this fishery are unjustified. member states are already implementing an eu-wide eel management plan dating back to 2007. fishing is only one factor affecting the eel population, but other factors are also important: heavy metals, endocrine disruptors, water quality.
in writing. the eel stock is in a critical state. the efforts of french fishermen to repopulate water catchments are being thwarted by a gradual and steady deterioration of the environment. therefore, while the total abolition of levies by way of a ban would give the species a temporary and precarious reprieve, the root causes would not be addressed. the fight against poaching, the removal of obstacles to fish migration, the improvement of water quality, the continuation of restocking programmes and scientific evaluations will have to be the cornerstone of the next commission regulation establishing measures to restore the eel stock. this report foreshadows those leads. i vote for it.
in writing. in the context of the revision of the eel directive, i am opposed to a further restriction. this seems unjustified to me since the 2007 objectives are being implemented by all the states and the plan for the recovery of eel is working well. pcbs, heavy metals, endocrine disruptors, water quality, pests and turbines are all factors that have a huge impact on eel populations. fishing is no longer the major factor in these populations. so let us deal with the polluters before we bring the fishermen into the picture once again.
in writing. the eel is a fragile species that needs to be protected. this is the meaning of the community regulation adopted in 2007, which aims to ensure the recovery of stocks and the maintenance of the species. i do not see any urgent need to revise this regulation in depth: firstly, the publication of the report on the implementation of the management plans is still to come; on the other hand, since eels take ten years to reproduce, the effects of the current measures will not be clearly understood for several years. the report calls on the commission to submit a new proposal for a recovery plan by march 2014 and to review the national plans every two years. these measures seem to me to be disproportionate - let us not forget that eel fishermen are already facing significant restrictions. let us wait for the results of the current measures before we go any further! i therefore did not support the report. it is clear that the eel stock must be preserved, but this must also be done by looking at how to reduce the impact of other factors of eel mortality than fishing (traction in the turbines of hydroelectric power plants, loss of favourable habitats, deterioration of water quality).
in writing. i voted against this report because the measures it proposes are useless and counterproductive. the amendments tabled by mrs lövin distort the original proposal of the european commission and increase the constraints on river fishermen. however, the sector has been working hard to restore stocks since the implementation of the eel plan in 2007. the current state of resources does not justify a substantive amendment of the regulation as proposed in the text.
in writing. the single market and the customs union imply common rules for the european union in international trade and the law applicable to customs services. i voted in favour of this report, which updates these rules and brings them into line with the provisions of the lisbon treaty.
in writing. i voted in favour of modernising the customs code legislation which was 20 years old. this modernisation aims to increase efficiency while ensuring greater flexibility in the introduction of new customs clearance and control procedures. i found the final compromise satisfactory, since it is the result of interesting negotiations between economic operators and governments. it respects both the obligations of economic operators and the reality of the current public finances of the member states.
in writing. with this report, we will be able to achieve a modernised and simplified customs regulation, to make european customs faster and more efficient, to the benefit of european companies, their competitiveness and employment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because the customs union is one of the fundamental aspects of the establishment of a single market in europe, but it can only be fully achieved if its coherent application is ensured within the european union. i am in particular in favour of harmonised implementation in all 27 member states, preserving the fundamental spirit of computerised customs as described in the modernised customs code. therefore, derogations may be granted only exceptionally for a limited period of time.
in writing. i voted in favour of the customs code text which modernises legislation that is over 20 years old and introduces greater efficiency in the use of resources allocated to customs services.
in writing. the purpose of this text is to revise the union's customs code in line with the objective of absolute facilitation of international trade. in its commission version or in the version amended by parliament, this is a text intended to facilitate the movement of goods, justified by the objectives of competitiveness. i am voting against this text which is only intended to facilitate free trade, whereas the ecological and social emergency is more about the establishment of a european protectionism based on solidarity. i vote against it.
in writing. i am glad that we have finally voted on the revision of the customs code. after more than 20 years, the code needs a major modernisation to take account of the new challenges facing customs. it aims to achieve greater efficiency and pragmatism in the use of resources allocated to customs services, while giving greater flexibility in the establishment of new customs clearance and control procedures, in particular for authorised economic operators. this reform was necessary and i am convinced that it will make it possible to establish a system of operation more suited to the realities of the public finances of the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mrs constance le grip, which updates european customs legislation that is more than 20 years old. the aim is to harmonize the various customs practices which still exist between the member states in order to improve the efficiency of our customs policy. this improvement is achieved by reducing the data to be transmitted by economic operators, computerizing procedures and improving coordination between administrations. this reform will make it possible to control more closely the goods entering our territory, while at the same time streamlining trade and commerce.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the revised version of the eu customs code. customs is an essential component of consumer protection in our country. it is therefore vital that their rules are regularly updated to allow them the greatest possible freedom of action. however, this revised version did not address one of the most important legal problems: the vacuum created by the nokia/philips case-law concerning goods in transit. i hope that the work being done on this will be completed as soon as possible, in the interests of all european citizens.
in writing. i am not against a harmonised system of customs duties but it is necessary in particular that the manner and conditions under which the use of common electronic systems is applied in all member states are clear. in addition, the management of information by these systems is not clear. in the context of the nsa/prism case, distrust in this area is a matter of concern. there is also the question of who will be responsible for collecting and using the taxes. finally, finding a common rate in the context of harmonisation is particularly complex in view of the very different economic levels in the member states. i therefore voted against this report on the customs code, which raises too many doubts about the safety of citizens and the economic aspects of the code.

in writing. the agricultural accounting information network is an important tool for the development and evaluation of agricultural policies. it should therefore be up to date to enable the necessary data on the incomes, costs and turnover of union farms to be collected each year, in order to provide a basis for informed decision-making. the provisions governing it had to be brought into line with the new institutional framework resulting from the lisbon treaty. this text makes it possible to organise this, with a clear objective of simplification and efficiency.

in writing. the agricultural accountancy information network (aran) is the only harmonised database of microeconomic data for all member states. to date, some 80,000 farms are members of the network, which gives the commission all the data it needs to analyse the economic and structural situation and to analyse incomes, productivity and production costs. by voting in favour of the report, i express my wish to amend regulation (ec) no 1217/2009 in order to align the executive powers of the european commission with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) so that the whole machine can work better.
in writing. the adopted directive aims to change the european commission's powers vis-à-vis the agricultural accounting information network (aran), which makes it possible to assess farm incomes and the consequences of these developments for the common agricultural policy (cap). this tool enables the commission to gain a better understanding of farmers' incomes, productivity and production costs in order to develop the common agricultural policy. the directive defines the areas in which the european commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to amend or supplement non-essential elements of legislation in order to facilitate the management of the icao network. however, the european parliament retains a power of scrutiny, and the network's data and reports will be made publicly available on the internet. i voted in favour of this text because it was necessary to adapt this legislation to the new rules of the lisbon treaty.

in writing. this report proposes to set a stricter framework for the technical competences that the european parliament delegates to the european commission in the field of food safety. the report proposes several improvements to the commission's original proposal for better control by parliament. in particular, it requires that the power delegated to the commission be strictly limited to 'non-essential elements' of products, i.e. excluding product descriptions, definitions and names such as cocoa or sugars. the report also provides that the delegation of these powers is to be renewed every five years and that the commission is to present a report on its action before each renewal. i vote for it.

in writing. in the framework of relations between the eu and cape verde, a stable and democratic country, two agreements were concluded: one on the facilitation of the issuance of short-stay visas, the other on the readmission of persons in so-called irregular stay. these texts are a case study in the complete inconsistency of the union in the field of migration. the first text makes it easier to issue visas to citizens of both parties for stays of up to 90 days. the agreement also exempts from visa requirements members of official delegations and students and researchers attending seminars or sporting and cultural events. such an agreement will reduce the time and costs of preparing travel between the eu and cape verde and facilitate contacts between their peoples. i am glad that we have done so, and i voted for it. but at the same time, the union is signing a readmission agreement with cape verde, the content of which is well known and the consequences for the rights of migrants. i therefore voted against. between a fortress europe and increased trade between peoples, the eu must choose. at least i'm making it clear.

for our international commitments in the field of biodiversity. biodiversity is our life insurance, our natural capital. but the crisis, the loss of biodiversity, continues to worsen at an accelerating rate. a third of species are now threatened and more than 60% of ecosystems are degraded. we are facing a crisis of living conditions unprecedented in human history, the consequences of which for our societies have and will have a social, economic and environmental cost that, every day, makes the addition more and more salty. this report is of paramount political importance in our influence on how essential provisions of the nagoya protocol will be implemented. not being able to actively participate in these important decisions would be seriously detrimental to european union interests, including the interest of european union companies to access genetic resources abroad and thus produce bio-based innovations. many countries may even stop allowing access to genetic resources to eu researchers and industry. i should also stress that a failure to adopt eu measures on abs in a timely manner would not mean, as some seem to think, that there would be no abs legislation at all in the european union. in this scenario, member states, at least some of them, are likely to go ahead and establish their own national abs legislation in the interim, with the result that we would have an abs patchwork in the european union. this would certainly not be in the best interest of the common market and would not result in needed predictability and clarity for business operators and researchers. as you know, the nagoya protocol was a package deal: european users are confronted with problems in securing access to genetic resources in biodiversity-rich, mostly developing countries. in turn, for these countries to provide genetic resources under favourable conditions to european users, we have to fulfil our part of the deal. that means we have to ensure the compliance of users of those genetic resources in eu territory, so that the provider countries receive a share of the benefits. the aim of the proposed regulation we are discussing today is to create this legal framework for compliance in the eu. if we fail to establish compliance measures in the eu, third countries may start to see us as an unsafe or uncooperative jurisdiction, and become unwilling to give access to their genetic resources to european union users. therefore, delaying the process of ratification of the protocol would simply be against our own interests. moreover, not having ratified the protocol on time would have a very detrimental effect on our international commitments and on our image with our international partners in the framework of conserving biodiversity, including our credibility and influence at the upcoming conference of the parties of the convention as well as in other environment-related fora. having different views amongst the institutions prior to the start of trialogue discussions is not something uncommon. actually, that is what trialogues are for: to resolve the remaining problems and to find common ground for agreement. i am confident that through the trialogues we will be able to find acceptable compromises and arrive at a good outcome: one that is good for the european union, for its researchers, its businesses and also, of course, good for biodiversity. i still remember very well many of you enthusiastically helping me and also others in nagoya, with the common aim of reaching an agreement on the abs protocol and helping biodiversity, in the first place. all the eu institutions, civil society and also business representatives cooperated on this common and noble cause. the eu was instrumental in securing a deal on abs in nagoya in 2010. now is the time to remember those days again and to join forces again. reaching a timely agreement on abs regulation is, without any doubt, in the interest of the european union, in the interest of all of us and, not least, in the interest of european industry. we also need to deliver on our international commitment.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i am grateful for the interest shown by parliament in transnational collective bargaining, and i wish to thank the rapporteur for a constructive approach. it is clear that in a globalised economy, it is vital to step up the capacities of management and labour in transnational collective bargaining at company level. transnational company agreements are reciprocal commitments whose scope extends to the territories of several member states and which have been concluded between one or more representatives of a company or group of companies and one or more workers’ organisations. such agreements cover working and employment conditions and rules governing relations between employers and workers and their representatives. a commission public consultation last year showed the contribution that transnational company agreements have made to a wide range of important subjects in today’s changing economy, including matters such as anticipating and managing change, skills development, training, health, safety at work and equality, including gender equality. a recent fitness check on the worker information and consultation directive, published last july, underlined the role that transnational company agreements can play in making workers’ rights more effective by supplementing legal standards and adapting them to local conditions. the commission welcomes parliament’s timely report. we are convinced that it will usefully supplement the stakeholders’ views in their replies to the consultation, and they showed wide support for the development of transnational company agreements. the commission will continue to look into whether an optional european legal framework is needed for european transnational company agreements or not. information on existing agreements is available in a database on the commission’s website and we will continue developing this database, notably by including real-life examples from companies with a view to providing input for discussion at eu level.
