in writing. the visa system is an integral part of european migration policy. in view of the deviations in visa policy observed in recent years, the european union has decided to respond by introducing a policy of fair compensation and deterrence. i welcome that approach. by imposing stricter rules based on the principle of reciprocity on states which were previously exempt from the visa requirement, the european union is curbing abusive practices and holding states to account while promoting solidarity among member states for a more pragmatic management of our borders. from now on, any national who travels to an eu country on false grounds to stay there illegally or who files unfounded asylum applications will be held responsible by his or her home country. in the event of excessive migratory pressure from that state, it will be possible to suspend this exemption and re-establish the visa requirement until the state concerned takes the necessary measures.
in writing. i voted in favour of this reform of the european visa policy: it will now be possible to temporarily reintroduce the visa requirement in the event of a rapid and substantial increase in illegal entries into the european territory. in addition, a collective reaction will now be possible to denounce a third country which still imposes a visa requirement on the nationals of certain member states. the principle of reciprocity will make it possible to re-introduce the visa requirement for the third country concerned. this text provides important tools in case of excessive pressure on european asylum systems.
in writing. the present report proposes to tighten the conditions for movement within the eu by suspending the visa exemption for third country nationals, using mainly statistical criteria for countries for which there is an increase in the need to move within the eu. this security objective is complemented by the use of the police advisory services of frontex and europol. they are the ones who draw up the list of countries concerned by the visa waiver suspension procedure! these provisions in relation to third countries cannot be used to establish good diplomatic relations in the future, as their nationals are considered potential threats to the eu. i am voting against this text.
in writing. although the creation of the european banking authority (eba) in 2010 helped to improve cooperation between national supervisors, the crisis showed that this was not enough. the text i supported is limited to a practical adjustment of the arrangements allowing the eba to take account of the allocation of supervisory tasks to the ecb and to continue to protect the integrity, efficiency and proper functioning of the market.
in writing. the spanish banking crisis has confirmed the need for a strong crisis shield for the euro area. governments can no longer continue to bail out banks without addressing the root causes of the problem. the bailout of banks with european taxpayers' money must stop! it should be recalled that between 2008 and 2011, €4.5 trillion of public aid was injected, further increasing public deficits. the european parliament has therefore given its green light to the creation of a single supervisor of the euro area banks: the ecb. the giegold and thyssen reports, for which i voted, have ensured that the commission acts in a transparent manner by regularly reporting to parliament on its activities.
in writing. as part of the gradual establishment of a banking union, this report aims to adjust the responsibilities of the european banking authority vis-à-vis the european central bank. we had to ensure the integrity, efficiency and functioning of the internal market for financial services and the stability of the financial system as a whole. i therefore voted in favour of the details of the organisation of this european banking authority.
in writing. thanks to this text, the banking union will finally be able to come into being. i particularly support the idea that the european banking authority will have to develop a european supervisory manual in consultation with the national supervisory authorities to identify best supervisory practices.
in writing. the banks' difficulties are largely due to an absurd deregulation of the financial sector but also to the lack of serious european supervision. the granting of the ecb of the single supervisory capacity for european banks is therefore a major step forward. but this considerable change gives the bank much more responsibility. the increase in the ecb's powers must therefore be accompanied by greater transparency in its activities and by arrangements for democratic scrutiny by the european parliament. the single supervisory mechanism must also maintain a balance between the euro area and non-euro area countries and be fully compatible with the rules of the single market. the european union must therefore quickly adopt such a mechanism to restore confidence in the euro area, but in future it will be necessary to pay attention to its proper functioning.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text in order to strengthen the european central bank and contribute to the safety and soundness of credit institutions and the stability of the financial system within the eu and in each member state. i am in particular in favour of introducing early intervention powers for the competent national authorities and powers to adopt precautionary measures to ensure full and effective supervision in the union. the role of national parliaments is strengthened by this text, while ensuring effective cooperation with the union's institutions.
in writing. i supported the creation of a new banking supervision system to bring nearly 130 european banking groups under the direct supervision of the european central bank and to hold bankers more accountable for the effects of their actions in the real economy. this supervisory mechanism is essential to break the vicious circle between private and sovereign debt and to ensure the safety of our citizens' deposits. we must end financial fragmentation in order to ensure stable financing of the real economy for growth, which is why the establishment of the banking union must remain a priority.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which is an adjustment of the procedures under which the european banking authority operates in relation to the supervisory tasks conferred on the european central bank and to ensure that the eba will continue its functions of protecting the integrity, efficiency and the proper functioning of the internal market for financial services.
in writing. this report sets out the role, tasks and means of action of the european banking authority in the field of prudential supervision of banks. several provisions are aimed at greater control of financial activities. the text also provides that the authority may prohibit certain activities in an emergency in the event of excessive risks. the report also proposes that the european parliament appoint six people to the eba's board of directors, as opposed to none at present. but the main decisions will still be taken by the council of supervisory authorities, where the heads of the national authorities sit, so it is a false appearance. but this regulation is fully in line with the banking union decided by sarkozy and merkel, and validated by hollande. it therefore confirms the role of the european central bank and its independence. he even claims the independence of the latter. i cannot vote for such a text. i vote against this mock trial.
in writing. in addition to the sovereign debt crisis, some banks are fragile and exposed to the subprime crisis and the loss of some government bonds. in this context of a combination of heavy pressure on public accounts and private banks, everyone has been sucked in. indeed, any attempt by the public sector to save a private banking sector automatically meant an accumulation of debt beyond what was reasonable, reviving the unhealthy speculation of some vultures about the bankruptcy of countries such as spain or italy. this vicious circle gave rise to the idea of extending to private banks the european stability mechanism, originally designed to help the eurozone states in difficulty. the counterpart to this european aid to the banks is the establishment of supervision of their activities by the european central bank. our vote validates this new scaffolding and i welcome it. the ecb will now scrupulously monitor compliance by the 6000 largest european banks with the new sound financial health requirements, thereby preventing a further relapse that would affect the eu as a whole and undermine the economic recovery that is in sight.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which gives the ecb the ultimate responsibility and power to intervene in any credit institution in each member state participating in the single supervisory mechanism (including euro area countries and non-euro area countries participating in the mechanism).
in writing. the spanish banking crisis has confirmed the need for a strong crisis shield for the euro area. governments can no longer continue to bail out banks without addressing the root causes of the problem. the bailout of banks with european taxpayers' money must stop! it should be recalled that between 2008 and 2011, €4.5 trillion of public aid was injected, further increasing public deficits. the european parliament has therefore given its green light to the creation of a single supervisor of the euro area banks: the ecb. the giegold and thyssen reports, for which i voted, have ensured that the commission acts in a transparent manner by regularly reporting to parliament on its activities.
in writing. as part of the gradual establishment of a banking union, this report aims to define the powers and tasks of the european central bank. it will therefore be entrusted with the task of supervising the activities of financial institutions in the member states using the single currency. i therefore voted in favour of delegating such a task to the ecb in order to promote the security and soundness of our european financial system.
in writing. the banking union will finally take shape with this vote. the new supervisory tasks of the european central bank will give us an overview of the health of the banking sector and its stakeholders. it is a vital step towards the creation of a truly european euro. i particularly welcome the emphasis on strengthening the democratic accountability of the ecb.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text in order to strengthen the european central bank and to contribute to the safety and soundness of credit institutions and to the stability of the financial system within the eu and in each member state. i am in particular in favour of introducing early intervention powers for the competent national authorities and powers to adopt precautionary measures to ensure full and effective supervision in the union. the role of national parliaments is strengthened by this text, while ensuring effective cooperation with the union's institutions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is high time, after the banking crisis of recent years and the deep economic crisis which is still having its full effect, that we undertook a major reform to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past. i am particularly in favour of strengthening the democratic accountability of the ecb, which means in particular that the european parliament approves the appointment of those responsible for supervision and that there is better access to documents.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text which provides for specific tasks for the ecb in the field of the prudential supervision of credit institutions established in the member states. the ecb will be exclusively responsible for key supervisory tasks to identify risks to the viability of banks that require necessary action.
in writing. this report endorses the strengthening of the powers of the independent european central bank. the regulation endorsed by this report concentrates ultimate powers of bank accreditation, supervision and regulation of the major european banks with the ecb. the ecb also has specific supervisory tasks, which were previously assigned to the central banks and supervisory and control bodies of the eurosystem countries. it is not to be forgotten that the ecb has organised an act of war against cyprus by cutting off the circulation of euro money in that country on its own initiative. although the report provides for the ecb to be accountable for its new activities as a banking regulator, it reinforces its independence outside any democratic framework. i am voting against this new stage in the financial coup d'état in which the european union has become the instrument.
in writing. i voted in favour of ratifying the nagoya protocol as it is an essential instrument for the protection and good management of genetic resources. i nevertheless expressed my concern about the possible consequences for the activities of small seed producers and users. the answers to these questions will have to be found in the negotiations which are now about to begin with the council of ministers of the union.
in writing. the nagoya protocol, signed in 2010, aims to preserve biodiversity through regulations on access to and sharing of genetic resources. i welcome the ambitious report by sandrine bélier, which commits the eu to the transposition of this protocol. i fully share his concerns about the loss of biodiversity and the need for a fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge. i regret, however, that the rapporteur's proposal to create an eu fund for benefit-sharing was rejected by a majority of members.
in writing. as part of the eu's ratification of the nagoya protocol, the eu decided to have a new instrument for the conservation of biodiversity. the rapporteur has proposed ambitious objectives, going so far as to propose the retroactivity of commitments in terms of the protection of biodiversity. i voted against these measures because, although we must respect the commitments made in the nagoya protocol, we must avoid creating intolerable administrative conditions for operators and making access to genetic resources extremely complicated and legally risky. as things stand, i have voted against the rapporteur's report. but since the positions of the commission and the council are more reasonable, i voted in favour of the rapporteur's negotiating mandate, so that she can start the informal negotiations with the council.
in writing. i voted in favour of the bélier report which transposes into european law the nagoya protocol, an international treaty adopted in 2010 by the parties to the convention on biological diversity. this report guarantees that only legally acquired genetic resources will be used by researchers and businesses. i voted against amendment no 37 by the rapporteur. this amendment would have required operators to ensure retroactively that the resources used were acquired legally. this would have resulted in complicated and administratively untenable conditions for the use of these resources.
in writing. despite disagreements on some parts of the report, i voted in favour of the rapporteur's negotiating mandate. it is important that the eu ratifies the nagoya protocol on access to genetic resources under this parliament's mandate in order to retain its influence and influence in the decisions to be taken at the conference of the parties to the united nations convention on biological diversity in october 2014 in south korea. without ratification, the eu will simply have observer status. on amendment no 37, i voted against extending the scope to marketing and subsequent applications to avoid retroactivity and legal uncertainty. i voted against amendment no 60 to exclude the application for patents or rights relating to a new plant variety from the scope of the obligations.
in writing. i voted for the transposition of the nagoya protocol, which is today the only international tool to combat biopiracy. as in the vote on my report on bio-piracy last january, the ep has once again clearly said 'no!' to the concentration of the world's genetic resources and traditional knowledge in the hands of a few firms in the industrialised countries, with the dramatic consequences for indigenous peoples and small farmers. and 'no! to trafficking and use of illegally acquired genetic resources. after months of mobilisation in our various committees in the european parliament and a real obstacle course, it was essential to have a negotiating mandate with the council. the risk of the eu being absent from the negotiating table in 2014 has been avoided... but the price has been paid! we have lost out on key proposals, including the idea of the european fund for so-called 'historic' resources and the inclusion of the application to any new use of genetic resources, which is essential to make the application of the protocol effective. the future european regulation is reduced to a matter of "pain skin" since the resources already in circulation will not be affected...
in writing. i voted against the report because legal certainty is not ensured throughout the chain of use of genetic resources for users. i regret the mandate given to the rapporteur to conclude an agreement at first reading. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. the question of access to genetic resources is extremely important for the future of research and innovation in the agricultural or pharmaceutical sectors. the european union is the largest market for plant seed. it is also estimated that 26% of all new medicines approved in the last 30 years are natural products or derived from natural products. the report is a poor basis for negotiation and does not offer any new prospects for nature-based research. the concept of good conduct, which was crucial to facilitate compliance by european smes with the nagoya rules, has unfortunately been removed. finally, there is no recognition of the special nature of genetic resources when they are used for agriculture and food.
in writing. the european parliament, led by the coalition of the socialist, liberal and green groups, has chosen to give a negotiating mandate to ms sandrine bélier for the trilogue with the european commission and the council of the eu which will lead to the ratification of the nagoya protocol. i personally regret that the basis of the negotiating mandate which has just been approved is unrealistic and even dangerous for our industries and businesses. i am thinking in particular of the principle of reciprocity. that's why i've chosen to reject this warrant. however, i remain confident that the european commission and the council of the eu will take a more measured approach and will be able to reach a solution that is more reasonable and more in line with our interests. it is essential that the european union ratifies the nagoya protocol. the eu must not only be a spectator in future international negotiations, but must be able to influence and even bend the sometimes too radical positions of its international partners at the conference of the parties to the united nations convention on biological diversity (cop12) to be held in october 2014 in south korea.
in writing. - the loss of biodiversity, as far as the statistics we have are concerned, is an important issue for our attention and for our parliamentary political activity. the economic and social impact of biodiversity loss tells us significant numbers, such as losses of 7% of global gdp by 2050. therefore, preserving and allowing access to genetic resources, and access to them that is as fair as possible and equally guaranteed to the member states, is of paramount importance and is the aim of this report. investing in knowledge sharing, through the strengthening of infrastructure for the transmission of knowledge and the training of staff, is undoubtedly a good way to reverse the trend that is leading us to the loss of biodiversity.
in writing. i voted in favour of the amended resolution on the nagoya protocol on access to genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge which aims to combat illegal access by ensuring that only legally acquired genetic resources are used by researchers and businesses.
in writing. the eu's ratification of the nagoya protocol on biodiversity is good news in the fight against bio-piracy. the plundering of the genetic resources of the countries of the south by multinational corporations must stop. the commission's text was very inadequate. it essentially required declarations and moral obligations on the part of multinational companies to exercise 'due diligence'. the parliament's report goes much further. it prohibits the use of illegally acquired genetic resources. it requires prior consent from the suppliers before any use. it requires users of genetic resources to provide evidence of their compliance with the legislation at different stages of the manufacture of a product. it provides for the obligation to involve the indigenous and local communities of the supplier countries. it allows these suppliers the possibility of challenging the use of genetic resources in court. in order to make these advances possible, i am voting for this report.
in writing. micro generation can be defined as 1) the small-scale production by individuals and smes of energy to produce heat/cold and electricity to meet their own needs, and 2) the various forms of small-scale production, in a group or cooperative way at the community level, to meet local needs; other as this micro-generation is useful for the sustainable supply of energy in the union, i voted in favour of this resolution which sets out the means of developing it.
in writing. micro generation is the small-scale production of energy by individuals or smes to produce heat and electricity to meet their own needs. i voted in favour of this resolution in order to encourage such practices and to achieve the eu's long-term renewable energy objectives. these objectives can be achieved by investing in research and new technologies.
in writing. microgeneration is an interesting tool to enable energy consumers to become real players in the energy market. that is why i support this resolution which encourages reflection on the future of this tool. by calling for the removal of a number of obstacles, it calls for the completion of the european energy market. we must, however, remain vigilant so that the attraction of new technologies does not have an undue impact on the energy bills of europeans, and i welcome the emphasis on this in this text.
in writing. the resolution has the laudable intention of encouraging the development of microgeneration, i.e. small-scale energy production for local use. this would not only promote short circuits but also renewable energies, thanks to the technologies used. however, these gains will remain wishful thinking if the eu continues its wild liberalisation of its electricity market. unfortunately, this is what this perfectly hypocritical text is advocating by calling for the acceleration of the implementation of the third package of energy liberalisation directives. the report thus ignores the ecological and social impasses into which this liberalization is plunging the european union. i vote against, so as not to endorse this hypocrisy. and i affirm my support for the development of microgeneration, which will only be effective with ecological planning that will take energy out of the current wild competition.
in writing. it is totally unacceptable that in equal work there are still significant differences in pay between male and female workers. it is therefore with great conviction that i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the commission and the member states to strengthen the current measures in order to close the gap between the talk and the deeds and finally ensure real equality.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution which aims to establish equal pay for men and women workers. i also voted for binding measures on this matter, by imposing a reduction of 5% per year in the pay gap between men and women until 2020. in 2012, the average hourly earnings gap between men and women in the eu reached 16.2%. this means that women would have to work 59 days more than men to earn the same wage as men. the european union, the symbol of democracy and equality, cannot allow such differences to persist.
in writing. equal pay for men and women is still not a reality in the europe of 2013. the flexible incentives have not worked and it is high time to move up a gear. i support ambitious and binding targets in this area and i welcome the vote of the european parliament today: it is the mark of our ambition, and i support setting clear and strong targets to end discrimination.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the application of the principle of equal pay for men and women workers for equal work or work of equal value, because despite 40 years of efforts, actions and resources, it is clear that the pay gap between men and women in the european union is still significant. with this resolution, the european parliament hopes that these disparities will no longer exist by 2020. to achieve this, the european parliament proposes a multi-level approach such as the promotion of good practice between member states and the implementation of policies to reduce the gender pay gap.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which was adopted by a very large majority. this is a fight we have been waging in the femm committee since the beginning of the legislature and yet this year again, in europe, women would have had to work until 27 february 2013 to reach the salary men earn on 31 december 2012. the slow progress towards closing this pay gap reveals the ineffectiveness and inadequacy of the provisions of directive 2006/54/ec. we therefore call on the commission once again to revise it. reducing the gender pay gap is both a tool to address the demographic crisis, to increase employment opportunities for women, and to reduce the number of people at risk of poverty, as women are unfortunately the first victims of the current economic crisis. i regret, however, that my epp colleagues have called for a split vote on the target of reducing the gender pay gap by 5% per year, when we know that reducing the gender pay gap by one percentage point will increase economic growth by 0.1%.
in writing. this resolution reminds the commission of its duty by asking it to review directive 2006/54/ec on the pay gap between men and women. the text even sets ambitious targets to reduce this gap and achieve equal pay by 2020. i vote for it.

in writing. i voted in favour of a new strategy on cybersecurity, which represents a growing challenge to national security and the economic stability of the internal market. the protection and preservation of fundamental freedoms and rights online must be ensured by the implementation of training, education and awareness-raising programmes for citizens on the protection of personal data.

in writing. cybersecurity is a major issue of our time. we must ensure that the data that our citizens exchange on the internet is not misused, used without their knowledge, that they are not spied on. it is essential not only for the proper functioning of society and the economy but also for ensuring the physical integrity of citizens. it is important to ask each member state to put in place a real cybersecurity strategy, as it is our duty to ensure the protection and preservation of fundamental freedoms and rights online (in particular privacy and data protection). i am glad that i voted in favour of this resolution, which seems to me to be a first step in the right direction.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution in a context where cybersecurity has become a crucial issue for defence (internet as a support for terrorism, data protection in sensitive institutions) and more generally for citizens (protection of personal data and online transactions). europe must encourage the creation of cybersecurity strategies at member state level, which would include the participation of the private sector, and which would result in information sharing among all relevant actors. we also need to raise awareness among european citizens and businesses about online data protection and plan to train more engineers in cybersecurity. finally, let us highlight an innovative and practical proposal in this field: the creation of certs - computer emergency and response teams, whose objective would be to create synergies in this field, and which i welcome.

in writing. in the face of the terrible conflict in syria, the european parliament, through this resolution, condemns in the strongest possible terms the chemical weapons massacre of civilians on 21 august 2013, which according to western intelligence services killed at least 1 400 people, including 400 children, and notes that various sources seem to indicate that the syrian regime is responsible for this attack. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of enhanced cooperation on security issues, in order to find a solution to the syrian conflict as soon as possible, especially since the proven use of chemical weapons against the syrian population. the use of chemical weapons in syria is a war crime and a crime against humanity which calls for a strong, clear and common response. we strongly condemned the attack on 21 august and called on the united nations to take action to help the syrian people and refugees.
in writing. only a binding resolution of the un security council will bring an end to the use of chemical weapons in syria. that is the whole point of the resolution we have just adopted. i welcome the efforts of washington and moscow in negotiating such a resolution, but i regret that the european union is not also at the table in geneva. in syria, there is no military solution possible. the only solution is political, because it is a civil war that is now bloodying syria. it is therefore our responsibility to do everything we can to achieve a negotiated transitional solution so that in the end the syrians can have the regime of their choice. it is imperative that the opposition work to bring together all the moderates who want regime change by preventing the fundamentalist elements of the rebellion from gaining ground and that it appears to the communities and minorities as a guarantor of their security. on the humanitarian front, the eu must continue to take its share of responsibility and continue to help the countries in the region where the number of refugees is increasing. i am thinking in particular of lebanon.
in writing. the syrian conflict has brought its share of horror and terror. but last august, with the deadly chemical attack, we took another step into the unknowable. such a serious violation of human life cannot go unpunished. but in syria more than anywhere else, a response by force could have consequences of unimaginable scope. if firmness is required, so is caution. military intervention is a risky way of setting fire to a region that is only going to burn. if russia's proposal to put syria's chemical arsenal under international control is to be believed, it must not be seen as another diplomatic ploy to keep bashar al-assad in power. while the leaders are negotiating, the number of dead, but also and especially of refugees, keeps on increasing. we are now on the eve of winter and the eu, which is already doing a lot for refugees, still has to continue its solidarity effort.

in writing. the european union claims in this resolution to be relying on legitimate international institutions, since it states that chemical weapons have indeed been used against civilians and that they have been used by the government in power. an investigation by the un is still ongoing. i cannot support a text which claims not to await the un conclusions and thereby to deny international law. i vote against it.
in writing. the arab spring began in march 2011 and has resulted in 100,000 deaths, mostly civilians, 4.25 million displaced persons and 2 million refugees. but the horror of the chemical attack on august 21, 2013, which killed hundreds of people, was even more overwhelming. for two years now we have been faced with a paralysis of the international community which has not found a political solution, particularly because of the numerous chinese and russian vetoes. however, the syrian regime recently agreed to put its chemical arsenal under international surveillance. i hope that this first demonstration of goodwill by the syrian regime will be followed by real action that will allow the country to emerge from this deadly crisis. i support this resolution because the european union is working towards a diplomatic solution that will restore peace. i also welcome the union's daily efforts to provide much-needed humanitarian aid to refugees and displaced persons.

in writing. egypt is going through a very serious crisis that is undermining the democratic transition that began after the fall of the mubarak regime. first of all, the violence that has shaken the country in recent months must end as soon as possible. the government and the opposition forces must take responsibility and stop inciting hatred and fomenting aggression. secondly, the revival of the democratic process must include all the components of the egyptian political world and fully involve women and representatives of minorities. this is the prerequisite for egypt to move towards a genuine democracy, the only way out of the social and economic difficulties that are so hard hitting the country and its people. this progress in the political field must be accompanied by a stable economic situation. in this context, the continuation of assistance programmes to civil society and the most vulnerable is absolutely vital.
in writing. beyond the declarations of solidarity with the egyptian people and condemnation of the violence of the repression against the demonstrators mentioned in this resolution, it is recalled that the financial assistance to which egypt is entitled from the european union is conditional on compliance with the rules laid down by the imf. on the contrary, i think that the democratic transition is difficult to achieve under the yoke of financial institutions which impose austerity in an authoritarian manner wherever they operate. i'm not going to.
in writing. last july, the egyptian people decided to demonstrate against the ruling muslim brotherhood, highlighting president morsi's triple failure - political, economic and social. a president and an interim government were established with a roadmap to ensure a democratic transition. two months later, it is clear that the situation in egypt is very worrying. the polarization of society between pro-muslim brotherhood and pro-army groups has resulted in deadly clashes, terrorist attacks, violence against copts, harassment of human rights defenders and restrictions on press freedom. the european union supports egypt in its efforts to bring about a democratic transition and economic recovery, while condemning the violence and human rights violations committed by the army and the muslim brotherhood. i voted in favour of this resolution. two years after the arab spring, i still support the egyptian youth to make their aspirations for peace, democracy and freedom a reality.
in writing. i supported this resolution because it takes a full account of the events of the summer to better assess the consequences. at this stage of the country's democratic transition, we still lack the background to judge whether these events constitute a step forward or a step back. in our text we have taken the view that the analysis and the call for the egyptian people to rally behind the democratic values to which they are attached, as well as the respect for all human rights and fundamental freedoms, including that of worship, are necessary.
in writing. maritime space is the subject of increasingly intense geostrategic competition. i voted in favour of this text, which recalls that the european union has a strong interest in maintaining a safe, open and clean maritime environment, guaranteeing the free movement and safety of goods and people within maritime areas.
in writing. with a genuine maritime policy integrated into the common security and defence policy, the eu could create a safe, open and clean maritime environment to allow for free trade in the context of a peaceful, fair and sustainable use of our oceans. i therefore voted in favour of this report which calls on the high representative, the commission and the council to draw up this integrated maritime policy based on the coordination of european actors and member states concerned with maritime safety.
in writing. i voted in favour of the gomes report which, within the framework of the common security and defence policy (csdp), allows for the establishment of a secure maritime framework. the gomez report stresses the urgent need for cooperation between the eu member states by calling for control of european maritime flows, the identification of maritime security threats and the development of specific action capacities to deal with european issues. i therefore welcome the parliament's motion for a resolution which, in view of the european council in december 2013, makes it possible to express the views of the european parliamentarians.
in writing. the european maritime frontier has a strategic and economic importance that should not be overlooked, and yet current defence tools do not always take this into account sufficiently. our maritime borders must be protected in the same way as our physical borders: as we have seen, it is often by sea that certain threats come to us that we find difficult to control, such as piracy or illegal exploitation of resources. i welcome the call in this report for greater consideration of the maritime dimension in our security policies.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because a comprehensive approach combining political, diplomatic, economic and social tools seems to be the most appropriate way of addressing the challenges of the european maritime area, while ensuring the maintenance of a safe, open and clean area guaranteeing the free movement of goods and people within it.
in writing. this report is part of the smart defense project concocted by nato, taking for granted that the eu and nato would have the same interests. we demand a strict separation between the eu and nato. it is essential to make a clear and sharp distinction between civilian and military capabilities, contrary to what is advocated in this report. the report welcomes the success of the atalanta mission, which represents a denial of sovereignty, and proposes its model for the development of the csdp. military action must be conducted within the strict framework of the un charter and international law. france cannot go to war automatically without a vote by the national representation, as the report proposes in accordance with the eu treaty. this report does not propose anything against one of the real threats to the eu, namely us espionage, but on the contrary it proposes even greater cooperation with nato in terms of intelligence. piracy and migration are perceived as major risks for the eu without ever being addressed. the possibility of a non-military solution to these problems is not mentioned. i vote against it.
in writing. globalisation, international trade and new threats such as organised crime and piracy require the eu to put in place a maritime security policy to make our waters open but also safe. the union can be proud of its achievements in maritime security, as demonstrated by the strategy implemented in the horn of africa. we must continue our efforts and coordinate our common defence policy. i support this report because it highlights sensitive maritime areas and calls for our actions and initiatives to be pooled in order to provide an effective and lasting response to maritime instability and insecurity.
in writing. the european union is the world's leading maritime area, thanks in particular to its outermost regions, which allow it to assert its direct presence on the major international sea routes of major strategic importance. however, it is faced, on the one hand, with the arrival of new actors that upset the geostrategic maritime balance; on the other hand, with the emergence of new threats and the intensification of certain risks in the various areas where it is present. the european union must respond strongly to these new challenges, and this is what my colleague ana gomes' report highlights. its proposal to map the infrastructures of the eu member states and acp partners in strategic locations in order to organise specific operations makes it possible, in a crisis context, to make effective use of the tools already at the eu's disposal. i only regret that the outermost regions, because of their geostrategic location, are a major asset for the union and the future european policy on maritime security. however, their potential has not been sufficiently emphasised in this resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which presents a detailed assessment of the military capabilities which have been developed to date at european level. it also makes proposals on how to update the institutional framework of military structures, address major capacity gaps and enhance the operational effectiveness of eu military operations.
in writing. the member states have responded individually to the syrian crisis. it is important, in order to be credible and respected on the international scene, to react collectively and to work together in developing a genuine european security and defence policy. working together is our greatest strength in responding to the international crises that are exploding around the world. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which seeks to review the eu's military structures in the perspective of a genuine common security and defence policy.
in writing. i voted for the giannakou report on responding effectively and swiftly to international crises. the report calls on the member states to take the necessary measures to strengthen the eu's military structures and capabilities, if necessary in the framework of permanent structured cooperation. the reduction in military budgets, which is particularly denounced in this report, is ultimately extremely detrimental to the planning and conduct of military operations at european level. i support the establishment of a genuine common european security and defence policy through increased cooperation between member states.
in writing. the european union has shown its weakness twice in recent months: in mali and then in syria. this inability to act, to take strong decisions quickly, contributes to the image of a weak or non-existent europe on the international scene. what we are saying by voting for this report is that we must put an end to this weakness. it is time for europe to have rapid reaction capabilities, coordinated between the member states and able to act quickly where they are needed. we need more political will to do that. i hope that the next commission will be able to live up to this ambition.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to respond to the eu's military ambitions, which seeks to maintain and strengthen its indispensable role in international security and defence matters. i am particularly in favour of a comprehensive approach to crisis management that integrates diplomatic, economic, development and, as a last resort, military means.
in writing. the europe of defence has an appearance, the csdp, and a reality, nato. nato is destroying any possibility of european defence based on independence and collective security. it is plunging all european defence budgets into the hands of the us military-industrial complex. the defence budgets of the member states would be sufficient to ensure the security of each country if they were not used for nato missions and the oversized weapons programmes imposed by the united states. member states should replace galileo with gps. they must also invest in a european-only industry for military and civilian drones. the union must protect its communications and the communications of its citizens against the nsa's means of spying. nato's propensity for preventive warfare, for the use of tactical nuclear weapons and for the deployment of anti-missile systems in europe makes it a factor of insecurity and a danger to peace in the world. the union must withdraw from nato. such a political decision would produce a life-saving shock which would open the debate on the foundation of a european and mediterranean defence policy based on peace, collective security, cooperation and the independence of each people. that is why i am voting against this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which deplores the union's inadequate capacity to deal with international crises in a timely and effective manner. although the origins of the european union are rooted in the maintenance of peace, the protection of human rights and the prevention of conflict, the current situation is marked by the absence of a genuine common security and defence policy. the establishment of a functioning union staff within the european external action service (eeas) should be considered, as well as the pooling of costly equipment such as drones or special capabilities.
in writing. in summary, this report calls for support for the nato-concocted smart defense project, taking for granted that the eu and nato have the same interests. we demand a strict separation between the eu and nato. it is also essential to make a clear and sharp distinction between civilian and military capabilities, contrary to the current trend clearly advanced in this report of dangerously combining security and defence. military action must be conducted within the strict framework of the un charter and international law. france cannot go to war automatically without a vote by the national representation, as the report proposes in accordance with the eu treaty. this report does not propose anything against one of the real threats to the eu, namely us espionage, but on the contrary it proposes even greater cooperation with nato in terms of intelligence.
in writing. as belarus is the last dictatorship in europe, we have called in this resolution for the regime to release political prisoners and gradually turn towards democracy and the european union. i voted for this resolution which is firm on european values while reaching out to the belarusians.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendations on future eu-belarus relations on fundamental rights and democratic reforms, in view of the eastern partnership summit in vilnius in november. the eu has been trying to establish relations with belarus since 1995, but these were frozen in 1997 due to the political situation in the country, in particular the violations of electoral standards in the 2010 presidential elections and the repression of independent media. the eastern partnership will open a multilateral technical dialogue to consider the development of relations with the eu.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i support, in particular, the prospect of the resumption of political dialogue, as soon as the political prisoners have been released, which will promote democratic reforms such as free and fair elections with respect for the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report of recommendation to the council, the commission and the eeas on the union's policy towards belarus. the report calls on the belarusian authorities to guarantee respect for fundamental rights and to undertake democratic reforms.
in writing. the report aims at improving bilateral relations between the union and belarus through the gradual lifting of the restrictive measures imposed by the european union. the eu is also calling for the release of all political prisoners and the restoration of all their civil and political rights. i note that some of the points in this report go far beyond the human rights framework, such as the requirement to allow organisations to deposit their funds in offshore accounts, which is a strange request. this is all a farce. the belarusian regime is unbearable. the eu's imperialist and follow-on attitude. i'm not involved in the plague-cholera relationship. i'm not going to.
in writing. while the sovereignty of each country must be strictly respected on the international stage, russia seems to be putting pressure on its neighbours to abandon their friendly relationship with the european union. in view of this, i voted in favour of this resolution, which reaffirms the essential principles of international law.
in writing. in this resolution we called on russia to respect the right of the eu's eastern neighbours to negotiate association agreements with the union. recently, russia has been pressuring ukraine and moldova and threatening armenia to dissuade them from signing agreements with the eu. as part of its neighbourhood policy, the eu must assume its responsibility for defending the eastern partnership countries. the commission and the council will have to present concrete and effective measures to support these countries in their european aspirations and choices.
in writing. the joint resolution of the right, the greens and the social liberals is extremely aggressive against russia. it called on the eastern partnership countries (ukraine, armenia, georgia, moldova) to pursue political and economic reforms in line with european standards. in other words, free competition, the search for 'competitiveness'. she's also a hypocrite. these parties call for respect for the national sovereignty of the eastern partnership countries in protest against russian influence. but they call on the eu to step up its action in these countries to "promote the visibility of the eastern partnership and its benefits among the public opinion of the partner countries". and within the eu this sovereignty is systematically flouted by these same parties. it's an arrogant text with a neo-colonial touch. i vote against it. i am not going to go into the details of the matter. it called on the eu and russia to overcome their differences. it criticised the eu's choice to exclude russia from its eastern neighbourhood policy. and it called for referendums in the eastern countries so that the people could decide sovereignly on a possible alliance with the eu.
in writing. the eastern partnership summit will be held in vilnius at the end of november. this will be a unique opportunity to 'set things straight' with our eastern european neighbours, especially in trade. many of them are currently under intense pressure from russia to withdraw from the free trade area prepared by the union and its eastern neighbours. this resolution, which i supported in my vote in plenary, goes beyond mere trade disputes over the customs union, by highlighting the political and economic pressures facing our partners. it is the clear message of the european parliament ahead of the november summit.
in writing. i voted in favour of a new internal security strategy, implemented in accordance with the principles of the treaties such as freedom, security and justice within the european territory. eu action should focus on activities that are proven to reduce crime rates and prevent terrorist attacks.
in writing. this resolution on the internal security of eu citizens is surprisingly silent on the repeated violations of the fundamental rights of europeans by the united states of america and its espionage system. the big phrases about respect for fundamental rights and 'freedom' are completely hypocritical. this resolution also makes an unacceptable amalgamation between internal security and immigration by repeatedly and heavily emphasising the issue of border controls for migrants. we would have liked to have seen the same zeal in demanding controls on capital flows at the borders to combat organised crime and money laundering. but on this point, the resolution only 'regrets' that 'the fight against money laundering has not been included as a separate eu priority in the fight against organised crime' and merely 'invites' the commission to reconsider this decision. a damaging shyness where i feel the lobby's paw. i vote against it.
in writing. the europe 2020 strategy aims to achieve a 75% employment rate for the population aged 20-64 by 2020. i voted in favour of this text, which considers that the economic crisis should not be used as a pretext to undermine policies to prevent occupational risks. we again call on the commission to present its new european strategy for health and safety at work by 2020 and by the end of 2013.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which is intended to denounce the commission's failure to present its new european strategy for health and safety at work at the present time. it is nevertheless worrying that, while employment is a priority, the commission has still not presented its new action plan to ensure good health and safety at work.
in writing. we need to give europeans the assurance that their work will not endanger their health or safety and that, should this happen, they will be adequately protected. however, europe has not yet defined its ambitions for the coming years in this area, which is a cause for concern.
in writing. this resolution calls on the commission to take further initiatives in the field of occupational safety and health, which is a step in the right direction. nevertheless, it is surprising that a text promoting health at work should set the objective of keeping people at work until the age of 64, especially since the retirement age is fixed at 67 in many countries which have accepted the commission's current standards on this matter. it goes without saying that health at work also involves stopping work at a certain age. this is shown by the correlation between the decline in healthy life expectancy and the increase in the retirement age. i am voting against this text.
in writing. transnational enterprise agreements are new forms of social dialogue with multinational enterprises. they provide companies across europe with voluntary, innovative and socially acceptable solutions to tackle the problems of anticipation of change, restructuring, training, mobility, health and safety at work and equality. 224 transnational business agreements of this type have become increasingly important over the last ten years, since the first initiatives were undertaken in 2000. i voted in favour of this text which calls for greater transparency for these agreements and for greater legal certainty as to the effects of transnational business agreements.
in writing. while companies are increasingly operating on a global level, workers are more often organised at national level because the rules governing them differ from country to country. 'this asymmetry has a negative impact on the representation of workers' interests': this sentence was rejected in today's vote on the handel report. however, it does summarise the difficulties faced by workers in a globalised environment. the strengthening of international social dialogue must go hand in hand with the development of multinational enterprises. the aim of international agreements between companies - over 200 texts today - is to remedy the existing asymmetry. as these agreements evolve outside a legal framework, it seems appropriate to ask the commission to verify, with a view to legal certainty and transparency, whether an optional legal framework is useful. the need for the most favourable clause and the non-regression clause is recalled in the text which also stresses the autonomy of the social partners and the parties to a collective agreement.
in writing. europe is free movement, including free movement of workers. the consequence of this is the development of transnational agreements on industrial relations. to respond to this and to ensure the protection of workers, it is necessary to develop certain basic rules to govern such agreements. this is the aim of this text: efficient european enterprises, whose action is based on a high-quality social dialogue. i welcome the emphasis in this text on the need to strengthen women's participation in social dialogue and collective bargaining structures, and the encouragement to take into account the gender equality dimension.
in writing. i voted against this text because i am against the establishment of a european labour court and an optional european legal framework for transnational business agreements which might appear too restrictive for our companies.
in writing. the current framework for social dialogue is the national level, but companies are increasingly operating at european level, this asymmetry has a negative impact on the representation of workers' interests and puts workers at risk of being pitted against each other and being forced to accept lower wages, less favourable working conditions or other downward adjustments. the purpose of this report is to provide a framework for crossborder collective bargaining which adopts the principle of the most favourable clause and the non-regression clause. this is to prevent transnational company agreements at european level from undermining or damaging national collective agreements or national company agreements. this report is in favour of greater protection for workers, and i am voting in favour of it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which contains strategic guidelines and general recommendations to improve the situation and living conditions of unaccompanied minors in the european union. it aims to cover the main aspects of the living conditions of these minors as soon as they arrive on the territory of the union and to find sustainable solutions for their reception on that territory or for their return to their country of origin.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report to improve the situation of unaccompanied minors in the eu. the action plan put in place by the commission since 2010 is not satisfactory as it fails to overcome certain difficulties (such as the lack of statistics, the issue of return, etc.). we have a duty to protect unaccompanied young people at european level by setting minimum standards for fundamental rights and by establishing genuine coordination between european actors.
in writing. the arrival of unaccompanied minors on the territory of the union must receive an adequate response, which takes into account their specific needs and guarantees respect for the best interests of the child. i welcome the fact that this report recommends concrete adaptation of asylum procedures, for example by recommending that their cases be dealt with as a matter of priority or that national asylum systems be adapted to children.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is important to ensure that the interests of unaccompanied minors are protected as much as possible throughout the entire reception procedure. in particular, it is essential to combat the multiple violations of the fundamental rights of unaccompanied minors in certain member states. i would argue that there is a need for increased protection for children who are already disoriented by their isolation.
in writing. migration flows give rise to sometimes worrying phenomena such as cross-border criminal networks but also, in another context, to the increase in unaccompanied minors whose situation is perceived in different ways in different member states. the report by mrs griesbeck stresses that the best interests of the child must take precedence over all other considerations. of course, we cannot ignore the fact that a child is a vulnerable creature who cannot be treated in the same way as an adult and who deserves special attention. i therefore agree with the general guidelines of this report. but we cannot afford to be naive either. kindness does not preclude vigilance. there are situations where minors commit crimes and delinquency that cannot go unpunished. in situations where this is justified, detention may be allowed. the special situation of unaccompanied minors deserves to be raised and their interests, rights and conditions must be better taken into account in certain member states, but we cannot ignore certain situations when they represent a threat to public order.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which contains general guidelines and recommendations to improve the situation and living conditions of unaccompanied minors in the eu. member states should pay particular attention to the respect of the fundamental rights of minors arriving in the territory of the union.
in writing. this report provides an update on the situation of unaccompanied minors in the eu, taking a strong stand for the protection of children and the defence of their best interests. the eu's policy towards them must be guided by these principles and not by migration policies. it also urged member states to strictly respect the fundamental obligation never to detain a minor. i am voting for this text.
in writing. this report builds on the commission's communication which sets out a strategy to unlock the potential of the cultural and creative sectors for economic growth and social cohesion. i voted in favour of this text, which calls for the creation of the conditions necessary for the development of the cultural and creative sectors, the establishment of reliable statistics, the creation of networks and clusters, and the establishment of a common culture for the cultural and creative sectors.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr sanchez-schmid, on the cultural industry. the report defends intellectual and artistic production, a sector which has been able to withstand the crisis. each year, the cultural and creative sectors generate 4.5% of the eu's gdp and account for over 8 million jobs. it is therefore important to promote them and to continue to allocate funds to these sectors which are generators of jobs and growth.
in writing. this report adopts an ambitious vision: to go beyond the diversity of our cultural and creative systems to bring about a common identity through, for example, joint productions or common spaces for exchange and expression. it emphasises the importance of giving real recognition to professionals in the sector, as they are involved in an important economic activity that creates links. i welcome his realistic vision of enabling students to acquire a comprehensive training which takes account of the needs of the professional world through a closer relationship with the business world. it rightly recalls that these sectors are largely composed of smes, whose specificities must be taken into account, with a clear focus on their economic development and international influence.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it seems essential that the visibility of the creative and cultural sectors, which make europe the cultural exception, be supported and recognised at eu level and in the member states. i particularly welcome the fact that the creative and cultural sectors contribute to the influence of culture and the territories and i encourage the member states and, through them, the local authorities to promote these sectors, which have a diverse and effective impact on all the territories, and to use them as engines of economic and social development.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which responds to a communication from the european commission which sets out a strategy to unlock the potential of the cultural and creative sectors for economic growth and social cohesion. the report provides insights and improvements on several aspects of communication such as the prospects and challenges of digitalisation, globalisation and access to international markets.
in writing. this report deals with the cultural sector only from the economic point of view of market integration. so, despite some laudable intentions to help smes or to adapt social security systems to the reality of workers in the cultural and creative sectors, i cannot support this text. support for the creative sectors is envisaged only through loans. thus only for-profit enterprises will be able to access financing, while sectors that do not have a profit objective will be excluded, which is a testimony to the logic of the commodification of culture defended here. the cultural life that this mechanism prepares is indigence and stereotyping in the sauce of the majors. sanchez-schmid knows nothing about culture, so it's better to apply his recipes to the meat loaf. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which was supported by a large majority of our assembly. the eu has understood that it needs to promote the creative and cultural sectors (ccs), and i welcome this. firstly, because europe's cultural heritage must be preserved and enhanced. in this respect, i welcome the broad support for the idea of a common european identity, but also and above all the exclusion of cultural and audiovisual services from the negotiating mandate for the eu-us free trade agreement. parliament thus recalled that cultural and creative goods are not commodities like other commodities. i think it's obvious, but it seems that sometimes others doubt it. secondly, because these sectors, if effectively encouraged, create jobs and economic growth. i have supported in particular the support given to artists to encourage their mobility and to defend their profession, as well as measures to strengthen the intellectual property of authors.
in writing. i helped write this report which highlights the significant growth and job potential of the creative sectors. the challenge is to raise awareness of the potential for employment and growth in these sectors and their impact on the wider economy. the report also stresses the importance of artistic and cultural education from an early age. i tabled amendments to encourage the development of the arts and culture sectors. the role of the public authorities is also emphasised. it is indispensable in supporting associations and smes and in helping to organise the sectors and to promote and export works. public investment also plays a key role in the public artistic production that irrigates all these sectors. finally, i have been keen, together with my socialist and democratic colleagues, to include the social question in this report, in particular to ensure the sustainability of jobs, taking into account the specificities of these professions and their need to be fully covered by social protection.

mr president, the issues of greenhouse gas emissions and the energy transition are crucial for the future of our species. although this is a crucial issue, the union, true to its ultra-liberal dogma, continues to believe that only the market will solve the problem. the market guarantees speculation, the right of the richest to pollute and the relocation of industries to countries with little or no environmental legislation. the real solution is not through the market, competition, the pursuit of profit at any cost, but through public services and cooperation. this implies the construction of integrated public enterprises for energy, waste and rail freight production and service, enterprises to which specific objectives will be set. yes, we must act to protect the environment, but we cannot be the only ones who want to save the planet, and this means an environmental taxation at the union's borders, imports of manufactured products to finance investment and research and development by these public enterprises and european industry.
mr president, today we produce and fish less than 40% of the seafood we consume. we can be satisfied with real progress in these 40% of european products. even if not everything is resolved, our fisheries management and control efforts have resulted in, for example, 61% of stocks in the north-east atlantic reaching the mdg in 2012. but how can we spread this model of virtuous management so that our efforts are not drowned in the ocean? fisheries agreements, such as those with mauritania, are part of the response by providing a means of disseminating the european union's policies. a good fisheries agreement between the union and a third country must meet four conditions. firstly, the fishing rights granted to vessels must be limited to the renewal of the resource. secondly, third countries must agree to apply sustainability models. thirdly, the rights granted to union vessels must not be in competition with the coastal populations of the third country. fourthly, the counterparties must enable the economic and social development of the coastal states concerned. in a world context where some states are engaged in a veritable race for blue gold, where flags of convenience are displayed alongside other vessels dressed in the colours of the coastal states in the same logic of overexploitation of people and fisheries resources, depriving the poorest states of their food wealth, the european fisheries agreements can, more than ever, be a reference point but also require us to be vigilant in their application.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of mrs gomes' report, as it is a further step in the fight against organised crime, corruption and money laundering, both within and outside the eu's borders. it seeks to put an end to banking secrecy by asking member states to amend their criminal law and to promote the automatic exchange of information. each year, about 30% of official development assistance is diverted from public budgets in developing countries. the adoption of this report thus aims to encourage the participation of programme beneficiaries, by contributing to greater control, accountability and transparency of european aid beyond the borders of the european union. the union must be a major player in tax governance through these actions to combat fraud.
in writing. corruption, ranging from bribery and extortion to nepotism, can have a devastating effect on the economies of third countries. these practices drain the coffers of the state, undermine free trade and discourage investors. the cost of poor governance and corruption is between 3 and 5 percent of global gdp each year, and the volume of bribes is a trillion dollars, equivalent to the annual gdp of the entire african continent. corruption also has considerable social, political, and environmental costs. it undermines democracy and makes possible serious damage to the environment and human safety by bribing the authorities responsible for enforcing regulations. the eu, the world's largest contributor of development aid, must empower itself to become a credible actor in the fight against this scourge. it is essential that the recipients, as well as the donor countries, adopt a responsible attitude. in this sense, the integration of the concept of democratic ownership into development aid policies or the establishment of a monitoring system would be an important step forward.

in writing. this report is well-intentioned: to fight corruption. but it's a narrow view of corruption that's developed there. the most important part of corruption, tax evasion and fraud, is hardly mentioned. the eu's responsibility for the impoverishment and weakening of the state in the countries of the south has been ignored, while it is the liberalisation measures imposed by the eu in the economic partnership agreements that contribute to the development of corruption by depriving the states of their sovereignty. the report also suggests that corruption is the preserve of the public sector, as the private sector is largely spared from its considerations, while it is the main driver of corruption via international offshore finance. the means employed are not at all commensurate with the crime. the commission is also proposing to transfer the responsibility for assessing the risks of corruption to the imf, an undemocratic institution whose members are themselves accused of corruption. this is a bad joke. what good is it to denounce corruption without taking any action to actually tackle it? i vote against it because i do not want to encourage this hypocrisy.
in writing. this report analyses the impact of corruption on the functioning and development of states and the resulting human rights problems. however, while the stated objective of fighting corruption is laudable, nothing is said about the foundations of corruption that cause so many malfunctions at the state level. the report does not address the root causes that impede the action of states in their role of justice, control and redistribution of wealth, such as the increased influence of multinationals and lobbies on public decision-makers. worse still, the report points to a supposed direct link between corruption and the mentality of the societies in which it is prevalent. i therefore decided against this report which, while making a dangerous social observation, avoids addressing the real issues of the foundations of corruption in europe.
in writing. corruption is one of the reasons why states cannot develop and leads to the violation of human rights. when there is corruption, then a collusion is formed between the political, financial, corporate and organized crime communities, creating an elite that concentrates all power. the fight against corruption requires greater transparency and accountability on the part of all international actors. the resolution stresses the need to establish mechanisms for monitoring humanitarian aid or international aid provided by the european union in order to avoid corruption and ensure that the population benefits from it. i voted in favour of this resolution because the defence of the values of the european union requires the fight against corruption.
in writing. the poorest people in developing countries who are heavily dependent on public services are the main victims of corruption. these suffer disproportionately from the effects of petty corruption, including 'discreet corruption' where public officials do not provide the services or assistance for which they receive payment from the government (absent teachers in public schools or absent doctors in primary care facilities). i voted in favour of this report which analyses perfectly the shortcomings of corruption in developing countries. however, it is clear that the european union can only become a credible and influential actor in the fight against corruption if it responds appropriately to the problems of organised crime, corruption and money laundering within its own borders.
