in writing. i voted in favour of mrs regner's own-initiative report on private international law with a view to amending certain rules of labour law relating to jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. i fully support the adoption of this report which sets out the arrangements required for a substantial improvement in individual employment contracts and collective action. it provides better protection for employees.
in writing. the aim of this text is to encourage the emergence of rules enabling workers to enjoy the same protection before the courts throughout europe. the question of jurisdiction in matters of labour law remains an open question. we must protect workers, which is the obvious counterpart to the free movement of workers in the eu. i hope that this report will be a useful starting point for constructive reflection on the question of the protection of workers, particularly in crossborder disputes.
in writing. the increasing internationalisation of the activities of companies operating in several states and employing people of different nationalities requires an adequate update of the rules in force in the event of disputes between employers and employees. in this sense, the recast of the 'brussels i' regulation provides essential clarifications on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. the european union must ensure that the provisions protecting workers' rights are strengthened. this requires greater consistency between the member states: the applicable law and the courts with jurisdiction in the event of a dispute must be from the same state and the establishment taken into account must be the one which provides the worker with his daily instructions. a clearer european legal framework for workers will ensure more effective protection of the weaker party in the event of a dispute.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i agree, in particular, that the member states remain competent to legislate in the field of labour law and that it is therefore not for the european union to try to interfere with national legislation in this field. it seems to me therefore important to prevent the courts of other member states from infringing the rules of the labour law of each member state. similarly, it is necessary to ensure that a member state has jurisdiction over disputes to which its own labour law applies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague evelyn regner, which sets out the conditions for constructive dialogue between employers and employees, particularly in the event of a dispute. i welcome the broad approval of this report.
in writing. on 12 december 2012, the recast of the brussels i regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters was signed. the new rules will make it easier to enforce a judgment in another member state. the european parliament, however, regretted that certain questions concerning jurisdiction in the field of labour law remained unresolved and gave guidance on these issues in its resolution adopted on 8 october. i voted in favour of this text which proposes to simplify the rules of private international law in the field of labour, so that european citizens working in another member state know their rights and are protected in the event of a dispute. the resolution proposes, for example, that a worker who brings a claim against his employer should be able to consider the place from which he receives daily instructions rather than the place where he is employed.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report because the procedure for the recasting of the brussels i regulation, signed on 12 december 2012, on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, did not cover certain aspects of the rules of jurisdiction applicable to labour law, and it is necessary to make amendments to them.
in writing. this report is well-intentioned in order to protect the jurisdiction of national courts in matters of labour law and to prevent trade liberalisation from leading to legal situations which are unfavourable to workers. the aim is in particular to prevent the courts of other member states from infringing the rules of the labour law of each member state. however, this report has no legislative effect and will therefore not change the social dumping currently taking place in the union. the report is surprisingly silent on the services directive and the posting of workers directives, which are the main sources of circumvention of the laws and courts of the member states in the field of labour law. i am abstaining in order not to deny laudable improvements in crossborder judicial procedures, but i cannot endorse a report which ignores the root causes of the problem it denounces.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which calls for europe to clarify certain rules on jurisdiction in labour law, which are the eu's responsibility when dealing with crossborder disputes. in other words: which court will rule on a dispute involving more than one member state ? in the absence of effective rules, eu case law sometimes faces inconsistencies in this area (i am thinking in particular of the torline case in 2004, where the court of justice gave danish courts jurisdiction to rule on the legality of a collective action brought in sweden). this is potentially disadvantageous for workers and trade union representatives exercising their rights, but it also means that in some cases the courts have to apply foreign law, which is questionable to say the least. to remedy this, this owninitiative report introduces two rules of common sense. the first is in matters of collective action (choice of court depending on the place where the collective action was brought), the second is in the field of contracts governed by individual law (jurisdiction where the establishment which gives the worker his daily instructions is located rather than the place where he was employed).
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive because it aims to ensure that member states effectively verify that ships flying their flag comply with the maritime labour convention, which provides for extensive rights and protection at work for all seafarers.
in writing. the first maritime labour code, the ilo maritime labour convention, was adopted in 2006. this alignment, already transposed into eu law by directives in 2009, needed to be completed and improved as regards flag state liability. in 2009, the eu adopted rules on safety, quality management and pollution prevention. but the directive does not list the obligations of the flag state. with the berès report, these are clarified and seafarers' rights are strengthened. the state is obliged to ensure that its ships comply with the minimum international standards. the inspections, infringement procedures and complaint procedures on board are detailed in the text which member states must transpose in the coming months. the agreement reached between the council and parliament marks the end of the procedure and opens the way to a strengthening of the rules of maritime law.
in writing. i am pleased with the adoption of the report by mrs berès on ensuring decent working and living conditions on board eu ships in the exercise of their flag state powers. at community level, the implementation of the maritime labour convention (mlc), which provides for extensive rights and protection at work for all seafarers, is a determining factor in the european union's interest in maritime policy and its workers.
in writing. with this text, we guarantee equal protection for all maritime workers, bringing european provisions as close as possible to those of the international maritime labour convention. this would in particular help to limit the differences in interpretation which still too often lead to differences in treatment between workers and thus to unfair competition.
in writing. europe must have a social agenda for maritime transport to promote employment in this sector and ensure safe and decent working conditions for seafarers. the transposition into european law of certain standards of the maritime labour convention adopted by the ilo in 2006 will provide better protection for workers by establishing common minimum standards for all flags and seafarers. it is to be welcomed that the incorporation of the maritime labour convention into european legislation is the subject of a social dialogue involving shipowners and transport workers. the compromise reached on flag state responsibilities, which establishes mechanisms for inspecting compliance with european rules on board ships and sets out standards and procedures to be followed in the event of complaints from seafarers, provides a solid and precise framework for all maritime transport actors.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because the european union provisions on flag state control should take much better account of the rules established by the maritime labour convention. this would avoid differences of interpretation between member states, which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping. i agree in particular that there is no question of reducing the level of protection which workers currently enjoy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague pervenche berès which covers fundamental issues such as the minimum conditions required for work on board a ship and the conditions of employment. these arrangements will ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the maritime labour convention was adopted in 2006 by the international labour organisation. it protects the safety of international shipping personnel by regulating working and living conditions on board ships. these new rules have been the subject of a collective agreement to be applied at european level, but the european parliament has ensured that this agreement is properly applied. i voted in favour of this text which establishes a maritime labour certificate and a declaration of conformity for maritime labour, regulates inspection and enforcement of the maritime labour convention, complaint procedures on board, and the responsibilities of the labour supplier. we have also clarified the application of the convention by adopting the principle that each state shall assume its responsibilities in respect of ships flying its flag.
in writing. the international labour organisation (ilo) adopted the maritime labour convention (mlc) in 2006, which provides for extensive rights and protection at work for seafarers, regardless of their nationality and the flag state of their ship. i am voting in favour of this report which proposes that the provisions of the maritime labour convention 2006 on flag state control be incorporated into european union law in a more detailed and specific way. the level of protection of seafarers will be improved, including the addition of a system of inspection and certification of maritime working conditions ensuring that the working and living conditions of seafarers on board ships comply with international standards.
in writing. this text is one of the steps in the transposition into european law of the ilo maritime labour convention of 2006. this convention sets minimum rules for the protection of seafarers and provides for control procedures which make the flag state of the ship responsible for ensuring that these rules are applied. the directive as amended by the beres report concerns these control procedures, which it strengthens and harmonises in the eu. this should therefore help to reduce to a modest extent the disparities between states in the treatment of seafarers. the safeguards of the maritime labour convention are, however, too weak to stop the social dumping by certain shipping companies whose workers have far fewer rights. the report is silent on the fact that the eu is fuelling this dumping in the name of free competition and the free provision of services. on the contrary, foreign ships wishing to operate in the host country's ports should be required to comply with the host country's social legislation. i am not going to stop these meagre advances, but i have no illusions about the hypocrisy of the european social liberals who allow the development of savage competition between workers.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of this report which is a major step forward in the protection of maritime workers in the european union. the report not only calls on the member states to ensure that maritime labour law is properly respected on european ships, but also calls for a wider integration of the international maritime labour convention into the european union. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.
in writing. this directive lays down provisions to ensure that member states effectively fulfil their obligations to implement the maritime labour convention. the aim is to strengthen the rights of seafarers through control and certification. these provisions substantially improve working conditions at sea, fill the existing gaps in the application of the maritime labour convention, which has already been ratified by 51 states, and will re-engage member states to take the necessary measures. the pressure of international competition, which is reflected in the pressure of the sponsors on the crews, increases the working time of the seamen without the workforce following suit, thus creating the risk of fatigue and accidents. it is essential to take account of working conditions. the pressure of regulations increases the working hours of seamen without the workforce following suit. in addition, international competition between flags and those states which have not ratified the convention weakens the efforts of companies to improve safety. it is time for the european union to step up the implementation of the maritime labour convention 2006.

in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation which proposes to support a fisheries agreement which will establish fishing quotas for the european union, while proposing financial compensation for the development of the coastal fisheries sector in mauritania and making it conditional on respect for human rights. i'm very happy about the adoption.
in writing. - i voted against this report because i believe that the protocol setting out fishing opportunities and the financial contribution between the european union and mauritania cannot be concluded and that a new protocol must therefore be negotiated. mauritania has not developed a fishing tradition and the eu has already offered €156 million to help the country in its social and economic development in order to create the ideal conditions to encourage foreign investment. the current protocol, however, does not bring any benefits either for the european union, since the conditions for exploiting the fishing opportunities obtained prevent their profitability, or for mauritania, which without the eu fleet will lose a good part of the financial contribution.
in writing. two out of three fish consumed in europe are imported. to secure its supplies, the eu enters into agreements with producing countries, often developing countries, when these countries lack the know-how, technical and human resources or political will to exploit their fishery resources. these measures cause prices to fall and penalise local small-scale fishermen. today mauritania is in a position of strength. the terms of this agreement, which was negotiated at great length, are markedly different from those of the previous one. the conditions for access to the resource are tightening and obligations for the development of local populations are being introduced, while the financial counterparts are increasing. the rapporteur recommends that this agreement be rejected and its terms renegotiated. i also understand mauritania's motives for defending its fisheries resources in a sovereign manner. i vote against it.
in writing. the fisheries protocol between the european union and mauritania provides that european fishing vessels are allowed to catch various fish and shellfish species in mauritanian waters in return for an eu payment of €70 million per year, of which €3 million will be devoted to development aid for the local fisheries sector. this protocol, unlike the previous fisheries agreement, imposes strict requirements on european vessels, which are as much in favour of more sustainable fishing and the protection of marine resources as of the economic and social development of mauritania. for example, the crews of european vessels fishing in mauritanian waters must be 60% mauritanian fishermen and the european fleet will have to redistribute part of its fishery to the local populations. because it represents a balanced agreement and is designed to protect mauritanian resources as well as the commercial advantages of the european union, i have decided to vote in favour of this protocol.
in writing. i voted in favour of approving this protocol because the fisheries partnership agreement with mauritania, which has been in force since 1987, grants fishing opportunities to seven eu member states and its financial counterpart allows the development of small-scale fishing in mauritania. i therefore voted against the proposal by the rapporteur from the committee on fisheries, who called for the rejection of this protocol in the face of any legal certainty for companies in the sector. the rejection of this agreement would have resulted in the cessation of fishing activities for at least three years. i therefore welcome the outcome of the vote in plenary, which was overwhelmingly in favour of its approval.
in writing. i supported the adoption of the fisheries agreement between the european union and mauritania because it is beneficial for both parties: it proposes sufficient fishing quotas for hake, shrimp and tuna for european union fishing vessels, while offering a satisfactory financial counterpart to mauritania. this compensation will be used to develop the coastal fisheries sector in mauritania. in addition, the agreement includes a clause on respect for human rights in mauritania. i think it is important that the fisheries resources off the coast of african countries should first benefit the local populations, who do not have the same fishing resources as european seafarers. in this area, a coherent approach to development is needed. we cannot give development aid to the government of mauritania and at the same time prevent its people from enjoying the full benefits of their maritime resources.
in writing. this own-initiative report examines in particular the causes, current trends, consequences and ways of combating practices aimed at pre-birth sex selection, which can also take the form of negligent infanticide. it also calls for legislation against sex selection. i therefore chose to support this report by voting in favour.
in writing. in some parts of the world, gender inequality has taken a dramatic turn. selective abortion (matricide), abuse of women, the one-child policy and pressure for birth control have dramatic consequences for women and girls. globally, it is estimated that more than 200 million women are 'missing' because of genicide. the european union must mobilise all the means of its external policy to combat this ultimate crime, including gendercide in its dialogue with third states, recalling that equality between men and women remains one of the union's fundamental principles and encouraging the countries concerned to put in place binding legislation with criminal sanctions to end these practices. the eu must also work to eradicate the political, economic, social, cultural and religious causes that contribute to the privileging of men and the mistreatment of women.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because gendercide is a crime and a serious violation of human rights, which we, meps, must fight against. in particular, i am in favour of encouraging states to develop and promote empowerment legislation and policy frameworks to address the root causes of inequalities in sex selection.
in writing. "women are the future of humanity, they think of the community before they think of themselves", julienne lusenge said very rightly. violence against women is a challenge for the whole world. inequality, sexual slavery, female genital mutilation, gendercide, femicide, the list goes on and on of the violence that women suffer simply because they are women. these atrocious practices are endless and relentlessly violent! the result is a tragedy: more than 200 million women worldwide are "missing". the eu says it wants to make women's rights a priority in future sustainable development strategies. environmentalists are at the forefront of this, including by insisting that the issue of gender discrimination be included in human rights clauses in international agreements. as the fictional rapporteur on the opinion of the committee on development, i have followed this matter closely. the adoption of this report was fraught with significant challenges. its primary objective is to end the barbaric practice of female genicide, sometimes called prenatal sex selection. it is a complex, long-term task, with multiple socioeconomic and cultural factors.
in writing. i spoke in favour of a progressive report on women's health and respect for their rights. the report highlights the fundamental reasons why matricide persists in many societies: a preference for sons, gender inequality and a deeply rooted patriarchal culture. measures to end this exist, such as combating persistent discrimination against girls, guaranteeing inheritance rights for women, and preserving the economic, educational and political autonomy of women and girls. women's access to health care, including prenatal and maternal care, education and microcredit must also be developed to end this worrying phenomenon. finally, i voted against the amendments to restrict access to sexual and reproductive health services and to defend conscientious objection in hospitals and medical institutions, because they are certainly not adequate solutions to ending the practice of genicide.
in writing. i am pleased that this controversial report has been able to come to fruition by adopting a balanced approach to all forms of gendercide. it combines the need to combat gendercide while preserving women's right to access sexual and reproductive health services and builds on the work done by my colleague raul romeva in the previous legislature with his report on femicide adopted in 2007. this resolution explores both the causes, the different forms of current gendercide, the consequences and the means to combat such practices both outside and within the eu. i regret, however, that one of the amendments tabled by mrs zaborska and a minority of colleagues who in this parliament still advocate, in 2013, a restriction on access to sexual and reproductive health services, was adopted by a narrow margin. it is designed to prevent european funds from funding organisations that work on sexual and reproductive rights and provide essential health services to save the lives of thousands of women in developing countries.
in writing. this european parliament resolution condemns 'genericide', which consists of choosing the sex of a child before birth, and can also take the form of negligent infanticide. this paper examines the consequences and means of combating these practices, which are still unknown and whose impact both outside and inside the european union is still underestimated. i voted in favour of this resolution so that the european union and its member states can take concrete measures, including criminal sanctions for selective abortions. the european parliament, which is very active in the fight against discrimination against women, had to alert the european union to this sad reality.
in writing. i am voting for this report for the following reasons. it denounces the criminal act of genocide and fully supports women's rights to health and sexual and reproductive rights. it introduces the definition of gendercide as the systematic, deliberate and sexist murder of persons belonging to a particular sex. gender-based violence is an underestimated problem in many countries and also takes the form of infanticide and gender-selective violence. it stresses the importance of developing legislation against sex selection and better monitoring of the implementation of existing legislation, and places greater emphasis on the cultural and socioeconomic causes of the phenomenon. it called for greater cooperation between the commission and organisations such as the un, unicef, ohchr, unfpa, un women and who to combat gender selection practices and their root causes in all countries.
in writing. gendercide is a neutral term referring to the systematic, deliberate and selective mass killing of people of a particular gender. this is a growing problem: there are now 200,000 fewer women in the world. sex selection practices range from abortion to infanticide and are a reflection of patriarchal culture. this report focuses on the socioeconomic causes of this phenomenon and accordingly proposes the promotion of legislation in areas such as inheritance law, dowries and financial, social and other protection for the elderly. i vote for it.
in writing. the term "genocide" describes the practice of deliberately killing a person of the same sex solely because of that sex. recent estimates of the male-to-female ratio show an increase in the number of "absent" women in the world population, with the number approaching 200 million. i supported the adoption of this report, which has the immense merit of shedding light on this phenomenon, which unfortunately remains unknown. the report states that support measures for girls and women should be put in place by encouraging the creation of an educational and social environment in which women and men, as well as girls and boys, are treated equally. these programmes also involve the dissemination of non-stereotypical images of women and men and the strengthening of economic and social opportunities for women.
in writing. for years, some countries have had imbalanced male-to-female ratios, in that the proportion of the male population is higher than would be expected on the basis of the 'natural' ratio of men and women at birth and mortality rates. this imbalance is often the result of discrimination against boys, rooted in customs and economics, and exacerbated by declining fertility and pressures on smaller families. this has resulted in sex-selective practices, ranging from infanticide to more modern techniques of sex determination and choice, such as ultrasound scans and the sex-selective abortions that follow. the report 'genericide: missing women?' aims to combat this gender discrimination. i welcome the adoption of this resolution. i regret that many of the hard-line conservatives apparently did not understand the stakes of such a struggle. this was reflected in the vote on an amendment against forced abortion, which passed by 1 vote (316 to 315). abortion, of course, eugenics, not so much.
in writing. this report, commissioned and written by a colleague from my political group, highlights the impact of the economic crisis on the finances of regional and local authorities in the european union and the need to calibrate future regional policy as much as possible so that it can respond satisfactorily to these constraints. i therefore voted in favour of this own-initiative report.
in writing. i voted against the mazzoni report which is extremely critical of the economic governance that has been put in place in europe under this parliament. the report condemns in particular the stability and growth pact, which has helped to stabilise the euro area through the necessary budgetary discipline of the member states. it is also very critical of fundamental legislation such as the six-pack and the two-pack, which i supported. for these reasons i voted against the mazzoni report.
in writing. local authorities must be able to benefit from some flexibility in the management of their revenues to cope with the current trend of reducing their resources while increasing the expenditure required of them. however, i do not think that relaxing the conditions for the assessment of the stability and growth pact is the solution to their difficulties. we must remain consistent in our commitments and good governance efforts, and there is further flexibility to enable communities to cope with the current situation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i believe, in particular, that regional and local authorities have a role to play in achieving the europe 2020 strategy's objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. it is essential to make concrete proposals to introduce maximum flexibility in the national co-financing of the union's development expenditure in a context of strict implementation of the stability and growth pact.
in writing. my rejection of mrs mazzoni's report at the plenary session on 8 october naturally calls for clarification. it is important to assess how budgetary constraints are affecting our regions and to make recommendations where easing or improvements are needed. however, these proposals must be consistent with reality and respect the legal framework of the member states. mrs mazzoni denounces the 'austerity policies' pursued by the member states, without recognising that the policies of consolidation and rebalancing of public finances, although they are felt brutally in the daily lives of citizens, are the same ones that will ultimately guarantee the healthy recovery of their economies. the signs of recovery are already being felt in spain, italy... let us welcome them. the reduction in public spending must be targeted and not stifle promising projects. we must support the investments which will be the basis of growth. however, the stability and growth pact should not be manipulated in such a way as to impose on the european union and thus on all the member states what no single state can bear alone. let's not change the rules to accommodate weaknesses.
in writing. in this report, my colleague erminia mazzoni makes proposals to strengthen the role of regional and local authorities in the co-financing of the structural funds. the report was adopted by a large majority, with 433 votes in favour, 131 against and 50 abstentions. however, some points are too critical of the rules of economic governance, fiscal discipline policies and the stability and growth pact. in particular, it is important to support the introduction of macroeconomic conditionality in the 2014-2020 cohesion policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs erminia mazzoni's report because we have repeatedly stated, both as a member state and as the italian delegation of the epp, that we must take up the fight to ensure that investment expenditure relating to the european structural funds is dissociated from the calculation of the deficit/gdp ratio and, therefore, is free from budgetary constraints. the opening up of the eu to this kind of activity, announced by president barroso last july, must be strengthened and welcomed more. the strictness of the accounts and the observance of the financial discipline of the public treasuries do not directly imply a freezing of investments. we believe, however, that the structural funds can and must be spent effectively and efficiently, in accordance with the programming criteria, and that the national share of funding devoted to them cannot be considered as current expenditure, otherwise the dichotomy between european policies will not be resolved: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. this european parliament resolution aims to find solutions to manage the large number of refugees fleeing the conflict in syria. according to the united nations, 3.5 million refugees will have left syria by the end of the year, threatening to destabilize the entire region. i voted in favour of this resolution because i want the european union to be involved in the effort to protect these refugees. we have called for a humanitarian conference to help syria's neighbours (especially lebanon, jordan, turkey and iraq) to welcome syrian refugees in the best possible conditions. we have also asked the member states of the european union to step up their diplomatic efforts in syria and to provide humanitarian aid to these refugees. finally, we called on european states to take in syrian refugees themselves and to guarantee fair access to asylum procedures. in order to enable the resettlement of refugees in emergency situations, member states will be able to use european funds, in particular the migration and asylum fund.

in writing. the mazzoni report is paradoxical. on the one hand, it denounces the disastrous effects of austerity and highlights a chain of austerity that starts at the european and national levels and ends at the regional and local levels. on the other hand, it calls for the stability and growth pact (sgp) to be relaxed without calling into question the sgp and the tscg, whose famous 'golden rule' is in the same austerity vein. this is an inconsistent position: since the catastrophic effects of the drying up of public expenditure are being denounced, these two european texts must necessarily be attacked head-on. after we amended it, the right wing mobilized against this text. so i voted for it, not because i believed it, but because i wanted to defeat his manoeuvre.
in writing. with the crisis, local authorities are faced with the difficulty of securing productive investments in their territories. this own-initiative report presents concrete proposals to provide more flexibility for member states' public expenditure related to the implementation of programmes co-financed under cohesion and rural development policy. for example, the report proposes to exclude public expenditure related to the implementation of these programmes from the stability and growth pact. the report also very clearly rejects the principles of economic macro-conditionality, austerity policies and budgetary constraints. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which proposes concrete solutions to ensure the continuity of local public aid despite the crisis.
in writing. the global economic and financial crisis has undermined social, economic and territorial cohesion in the union with the consequences we are experiencing. the stability pact requires euro area countries to build budgets that are close to balance or in surplus. however, a contradiction soon appeared. if public investment expenditure is recorded as a liability in the public finances, these investments, which are conducive and even indispensable for future growth, will not be realised. no more stimulus policies. at a minimum, it was necessary to exclude from the deficit calculation public expenditure related to the implementation of programmes co-financed by the structural and investment funds under the csf (community stability pact). the left welcomes the fact that this resolution has received a majority of votes in the european parliament.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, the economic crisis has severely affected the financing capacity of the member states and of european regions, without the european union providing itself with the means for an ambitious recovery at community level. these budgetary constraints have a direct impact on the ability of our regions to implement projects that promote employment and the return of growth. the mazzoni report, whose vote i welcome, stresses the crucial role of cohesion policy and regional investment as a structuring element for our territories and a tool for promoting growth in europe. the strong proposal in this report, which calls for public expenditure linked to the implementation of programmes co-financed by the european structural and investment funds to be excluded from the definition of structural deficits, should also be underlined and applauded. the aim is to exclude community financing and its local, regional and national components from this definition.

in writing. i gave my full support to this report and congratulate my colleague bernadette vergnaud on her commitment to achieving a result that was unthinkable a few years ago, given the strong hostility of the member states to this project. this text shows how much europe can do for our citizens. the professional card will facilitate the procedures for professionals, improve exchanges between competent national authorities and reassure patients and customers. i particularly welcome the introduction of the recognition of paid and unpaid traineeships abroad as part of training in a regulated profession. this text will avoid too great differences in qualifications and ensure that the professional has a qualification to practise throughout europe. in particular, on the question of midwives, the changeover to a bachelor's degree level is maintained for access to the profession, and this despite strong opposition from germany, which is a great step forward.
in writing. good news for all professionals who want to work abroad: parliament has approved the modernisation of the legislation on the recognition of professional qualifications, which was an administrative headache of 15 directives, a real headache. the main innovation of this new legislation, which covers 800 professions, is the creation of a european professional card in the form of an electronic certificate which will promote the mobility of workers under facilitated conditions. but while bold, this legislation is not naive. healthcare professionals and those involved in the education of minors, for example, who have been convicted by a public authority or a court in their country and are prohibited from practising will be closely monitored. the competent authorities of the country of origin will be required to alert all other member states within three days. with this new text we are supporting the measures to promote employment and combat youth unemployment.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague bernadette vergnaud. this report concerns the modernisation of directive 2005/36/ec on the recognition of professional qualifications. the modernisation of the directive will allow the creation of a european professional card, the introduction of an alert mechanism for health professionals with automatic recognition, the establishment of common training frameworks and common training tests, and better access to information on the recognition of professional qualifications. the report was adopted by 596 votes in favour, 37 against and 30 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the recognition of professional qualifications within the internal market of the european union is an essential condition for promoting professional mobility between member states, which today affects only 4% of the working population. while almost a quarter of young people in the euro area are unemployed (24 per cent in july 2013), unemployment rates vary considerably between countries, for example 62.9 per cent in greece and 7.7 per cent in germany. the european parliament has therefore introduced new measures to facilitate the mobility of workers. for example, we have created a european professional card, an electronic certificate which will simplify the recognition of qualifications. we have also set up common training frameworks, which will make it possible to extend the automatic recognition mechanism to new professions. finally, we have improved citizens' access to information on the recognition of professional qualifications. i am convinced that these measures will contribute to economic recovery and to reducing unemployment in the european union, which is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, the provisions of which modernise the existing 2005 directive. the aim of this long-term work is to help to revive growth in europe through greater mobility of workers between member states. the introduction of a european professional card is one of the key measures which will enable professionals to present an electronic certificate in order to establish themselves in another member state. a tacit authorization is also introduced in the event of inaction by the host member state, which will speed up the recognition process. the member states will also be required to inform the competent authorities of all member states within three days if a health professional or a professional in the education of minors and young children is prohibited from practising. this is an important step forward for the protection of european patients and children and for cooperation between member states. there are about 800 regulated professions in the union, and seven of them are automatically recognised in all member states. finally, the minimum training requirements for doctors, dentists, pharmacists, nurses, midwives, veterinarians and architects have been updated.
in writing. the report validates the commission's core proposal. the aim is to create a european professional card. it will be issued by the home country and will certify that a worker has the qualifications required to practise a regulated profession (nursing, medicine, architecture, etc.) in another eu country. until now, the authorities of the host country have been responsible for this validation. they'll just record it. the report also makes positive changes to the commission's proposal (compulsory continuing training, mastery of the language of the host country). short-sighted motive and method. the common repository is essential. this project is unacceptable to me. facilitating the automatic recognition of qualifications between countries is not the best solution. on the contrary, common european standards must be developed. under the guise of professional mobility, this european professional card is intended to facilitate the plundering of the skilled labour force of the poorest countries by the richest, as germany has done. finally, facilitating labour mobility in the eu without ending the posting system can only exacerbate social dumping. i vote against it.
in writing. today, only 2% of european citizens live and work in a country other than their own, while surveys show that more than a third of europeans are considering working abroad. how do we explain this discrepancy? there are still many obstacles to mobility. one of them is the lack of recognition of professional qualifications. for some regulated professions, it takes months before the host state agrees to recognise a worker's qualifications. the procedures are complex, bureaucratic, the information is fragmented, the minimum requirements are outdated... the new directive is a big step forward and i want to welcome the work of michel barnier, elisabeth vergnaud and my colleague, constance le grip , which will simplify the rules, clarify the minimum requirements, include traineeships in professional experience and create a european recognition card. i also welcome the compromise for the nursing profession, which will preserve the quality of training and care. this text is a concrete response to the current unemployment of 5 million young people in europe. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the amendment of the 2005 directive had become necessary in view of the rapid and profound changes that the european labour market has undergone in recent years. thanks to the impetus given by commissioner barnier, who made it a priority of his mandate, citizens will now have a european professional card that will facilitate their procedures in all eu countries. we have taken particular account of specific sectors such as health, particularly nursing, and legal, such as notaries. moreover, despite the reluctance of the member states meeting in council, my group has been in the forefront of the fight to ensure that the inclusion of paid and unpaid traineeships in the scope of the directive is maintained. this is a realistic approach, as many students are now taking the opportunity of their compulsory postgraduate traineeship to do so in another eu country.
in writing. free movement is one of the pillars on which our european citizenship is based. it is a fundamental right enshrined in our treaties. however, this is de facto limited by the complexity of the rules governing the recognition of professional qualifications between member states. unfortunately, this reduces the opportunities for citizens to practise their profession in a member state other than their own. while the financial crisis has hit our people hard, making access to the labour market more difficult, professional mobility is a key element for competitiveness and employment in europe. it also represents a major challenge to the effectiveness of the single market since it requires, among other things, the approximation of the member states' legislation in the field of vocational training. this is underlined in the excellent report by my colleague bernadette vergnaud. it is taking an innovative approach by introducing a series of ambitious measures such as the european professional card, the principle of partial access and the recognition of traineeships completed abroad in the context of training in a regulated profession. this is a major step forward, which complements academic exchanges such as erasmus.
in writing. the european parliament adopted today by a very large majority (596 votes in favour, 37 against and 31 abstentions) my report on the mutual recognition of professional qualifications. this directive, identified as one of the 12 pillars of growth, must now be transposed in the member states. it brings a number of significant advances to facilitate the mobility of professionals in europe, while ensuring a high level of quality of services, with more confidence and protection for clients and patients, and increased cooperation between member states. this directive is a key text of the single market act. it aims to reorient the internal market to the benefit of citizens and contains many innovations: the introduction of a european professional card, a real tool for citizenship, which will facilitate administrative procedures by providing security for professionals and their clients, a major upgrade of common training bases, recognition and supervision of traineeships carried out abroad, etc. i am pleased to see this excellent result after more than four years of work. this directive will bring real european added value and demonstrate that europe can be dynamic, protective, at the service of citizens and is not only a free trade area but also the foundation of shared wealth and values.

in writing. on 25 september the environment committee voted a resolution objecting to the draft commission regulation on the visual inspection of pigmeat in slaughterhouses. this position is surprising to say the least. the commission's draft implementing text provides for the modernisation of inspection practices at the slaughterhouse by extending the use of visual inspection. it aims primarily to adapt the inspection procedures to the risks identified in the pig sector, taking into account the progress made in recent years in the health status of pig holdings. the committee on the environment opposes this positive development, which has been recognised by the european food safety authority and is supported by an overwhelming majority of member states within the standing committee on the food chain and animal health of the union. the draft does not call into question animal health safety or animal inspection procedures. it provides that inspections are always to be carried out by official veterinarians at the control posts along the slaughter chain. for all these reasons i voted against the resolution of the committee on the environment.

in writing. the motion for a resolution tabled opposes an amendment by the commission to the regulation on compulsory veterinary measures in pig slaughterhouses. the commission is seeking to speed up the health control procedures to allow for an increase in the slaughter rates (500 pigs are slaughtered per hour in large slaughterhouses). the veterinary control protocols are changed: visual inspection only without incision or palpation, which leads to a reduced probability of detecting abnormalities. the commission proposal seems to be the direct work of the pig lobbies whose slaughter rate is limited by the remaining health measures. i too am opposed to these amendments which put the health of citizens at risk for ever greater profits. and i vote for the resolution that seeks to prevent them.
in writing. the european parliament rejected this resolution rejecting the european commission's proposal on the control of foodstuffs and products of animal origin. this is to reduce the intensity of controls in certain slaughterhouses and cutting plants concerning hygiene, animal welfare and consumer health. such a proposal carries many risks, both to human health (meat unfit for human consumption may enter the food chain) and to animal welfare (greater difficulties in detecting breaches of regulations). veterinarians in several member states have expressed concern that the proposal could be adopted, as they fear that they would no longer be able to carry out their duties properly. even if the horse meat scandal is not over, such a proposal is incomprehensible. i therefore voted in favour of a rejection that favours health aspects in a sensitive area and i regret that the majority of the european parliament has chosen the opposite.

in writing. i opposed the commission's proposals on flight and rest times, because they are, in my view, threefoldly problematic. firstly, there is no real added value for the crew. i believe that if the european union is to take up this matter, it should have the ambition to improve working conditions. on the other hand, the working conditions envisaged may directly threaten the safety of passengers. finally, the increased role of the european aviation safety agency will allow it to take additional measures without the control of the european parliament.
in writing. the flight time added to the standby periods is still far too long; the job of a pilot is extremely difficult, and it requires constant attention. how can we ask them to stay awake for so many hours? this is not reasonable, because we are entrusting the lives of hundreds of europeans to our pilots every time: we must ensure that they are in the best possible physical and mental condition.
in writing. i regret the outcome of the vote in plenary. i felt it was essential to preserve the european parliament's legislative powers on these important matters, which must be subject to the co-decision procedure between the council and the european parliament, elected to represent the european citizens. i also regret that this vote was added in secret, depriving my colleagues of a serious look at the matter and our assembly of a thorough debate. parliament has today agreed to entrust the political decision-making on aviation safety and the labour law of aviation personnel to technicians.
in writing. i voted in favour of rejecting the commission's proposal for a harmonisation of the provisions on flight time for aircrew because i consider that this proposal is not satisfactory for several reasons. firstly, from the point of view of labour law, which is absolutely unsuitable for crews. the latter are themselves opposed to these proposals because of the risk of fatigue and therefore the risks to aviation safety, knowing that with the cumulation of flight time and waiting time, pilots could be forced to land an aircraft after 22 hours of wakefulness. secondly, as regards the form, the commission has proposed amendments which go far beyond mere administrative management and therefore require proper consultation of the european parliament, the co-legislator, rather than a simple yes or no.
in writing. i have chosen to reject the european commission's proposal and to support the motion adopted in the tran parliamentary committee. the proposal for revision sent to the european parliament on 25 july comprises two parts. however, the part concerning certification specifications is the sole responsibility of the executive director of the european aviation safety agency and thus deprives the european parliament of its right of access. in addition, the regulation currently in force allowed for the establishment of a common base of safety measures in the union; the revision of the regulation brings down the current safety measures. i regret the rejection of this motion for a resolution and would stress that the proposal for a revision of regulation no 1899/2006 does not respect the principle of non-regression or the right of the european parliament to have a say.
in writing. despite the alarm bells being sounded by the european parliament's transport committee and some trade unions, the european parliament rejected a resolution calling on the european commission to withdraw its implementing regulation on working time for airline pilots. this harmonization of european legislation is going in the right direction, reducing the maximum flight time to 11 hours instead of 11 hours and 45 minutes for example, and i can hear the fears of the pilots who wanted even stricter rules to be set. however, my decision to vote against this text is not linked to the proposed measures but to the undemocratic way in which they were adopted. i regret that the european parliament has not opposed the commission's regulation, which gives the european aviation safety agency (easa) extensive powers concerning pilot working conditions and passenger safety. the european parliament must not relinquish this essential competence, such measures must be able to be amended and voted on by the european members of parliament, who are the only representatives directly elected by citizens at european level.
in writing. this resolution opposes the amendments to the regulation made by the commission concerning technical requirements and administrative procedures applicable to air operations. these include extending the periods of wakefulness (up to 10 hours in a row), periods of actual work (15 hours of work in a row without a lunch break), reducing rest periods (up to 10 hours in the workplace or at the base). the amendments which the commission is introducing are contrary to common sense and do not meet the objective of passenger safety. moreover, the european parliament has not had access to the data on which the commission based its proposals. he was therefore not given the opportunity to exercise his right of observation with full knowledge of the issues involved. the commission has not provided sufficient scientific evidence to show that these measures do not pose a safety risk. i would add that the employment committee, which is responsible for the substance of the matter, has not even taken a position on the subject, since it is a question of working conditions. this text reflects the way the european institutions work: the commission acts with all its power while the parliamentarians are reduced to passing resolutions in an attempt to protect the security of their fellow citizens. i am voting for this text in order to frustrate the commission's manoeuvres.
in writing. improving the existing rules on flight time limitations for cabin crew and pilots in order to improve their working conditions and increase passenger safety is highly commendable. however, the way in which the european aviation safety authority has done this - the comitology procedure - is beyond democratic control and is not acceptable. further restrictions on the duration of night flights, new limits on flight times over a given period, additional rest periods to counteract the accumulated fatigue after long flights and in the event of disrupted schedules... these are essential changes to the existing regulation which have a direct impact on the working conditions of aviation personnel. we need harmonized rules in europe, but with the comitology procedure parliament can only reject or approve these new rules without changing them. i consider that democratic control must be exercised over such amendments and have therefore decided to reject the draft submitted to us. however, as it has been supported by a majority of my colleagues, these amendments will be effective - which i do not fundamentally criticise on the merits.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because i do not think that the procedure chosen by the european commission, that of the implementing regulation, is appropriate here. the regulation covers aspects that go far beyond simple technical and administrative requirements. the commission has also taken note of the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. which this proposal does not allow. we were not able to make this position prevail in the vote on wednesday, 9 october. i will therefore be vigilant in future as to the implementation of this text and its impact on the safety conditions of air operations.
in writing. the european parliament resolution on flight and rest times for pilots and cabin crew, which was voted in plenary, leaves a bitter taste of incomprehension. the excessively long working hours of flight staff do not guarantee the safety of crew and passengers and the european commission's proposal fails to address this problem. the question of the uniformity of the rules at european level has not been resolved, which creates great disparities between countries. in addition, the control of the adopted rules will escape the european parliament and will be entirely in the hands of the european aviation safety agency, which will be able, at its pleasure, to take liberties on possible future amendments, good or bad, which is quite questionable from a democratic point of view. i regret that the scientists have not been listened to, despite their serious warnings about the risks involved. will we have to wait for another catastrophe to change that? we cannot afford to ignore the question of working conditions. there should be no distinction between jobs on land, at sea or in the air.
in writing. − flight time regulations have a very significant impact on air transport safety and the social interests of workers, as for example in the field of car travel and leisure time. uniform eu rules in this area must ensure the well-being of workers in the sector, also because the safety of air passengers directly depends on it. the eu regulation on aircraft operations needs to build on the best examples of member states' legislation in this area in order to guarantee the safety of workers and passengers. however, the ec's initial proposal envisaged that in several member states the ratio of flight-to-holiday time for aviation staff would deteriorate rather than improve. it is essential that the new legislation prevents crew members from working long hours and becoming so fatigued that they endanger their own lives and the lives of others during and outside working hours. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all air carriers. i voted against the motion for a resolution by the committee on transport on the grounds that the ec is committed to making important changes to the proposal for a regulation which will take account of the welfare of workers in the aviation sector.
in writing. the european parliament has voted on a regulation on the working time and conditions of pilots, flight attendants and stewards. this regulation provides for standby times at the airport combined with flight times of up to 22 hours. the commission's proposal was rejected by the transport committee following a strong mobilisation of the employees' unions. however, on the basis of an agreement reached overnight, the etf partly agreed to negotiate with the european commission, with transport commissioner kallas having lobbied hard to defend its regulation. many trade unions and employee representatives have warned against this practice of negotiating in a corner of the table and without transparency. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the vote was unfortunately rejected by almost 30 votes to none. the vote was therefore taken and unfortunately it was the dogmatic liberal view of the european commission which took precedence over the safety of passengers and crew.
in writing. as a socialist, i believe that harmonisation at european level must necessarily bring added value: that is why i voted against the european commission's proposals on flight time and rest for airline pilots and cabin crew. the proposals on which we have just spoken today constitute a threat to the safety of passengers, a risk to the health and safety of seafarers and a risk of social regression. in addition, the european aviation safety agency (easa) will have full discretion to make further arrangements in this area without any political control. this is unacceptable because it is an attack on democracy: parliament will not play any role! i also regret that the last-minute negotiations have brought only minor improvements, without us having had time to consider the result calmly.
in writing. the flight time of pilots and flight crew has been decided on two levels. the eu first set a minimum safety standard (minimum rest periods, maximum night flight times, etc.) and then the member states decided on the application of the european text and could in particular impose higher (but never lower) safety standards. this double net was a guarantee of increased air safety for passengers and pilots. thus, when applying the european text, france could impose rest periods longer than the european minimum. the new commission proposal removes this possibility from the member states, since the european aviation safety agency (easa) would be responsible for defining the procedures for applying the european minimum, over which neither the european parliament nor the member states have any control. i opposed this proposal in the name of the principle of subsidiarity and i sincerely regret that a majority of my colleagues have succumbed to the commission's lobbying and have blindly adopted a transfer of power, which i do not wish to endorse!
in writing. in the face of the humanitarian catastrophe caused by the war in syria, which has made 2 102 582 people refugees, the vast majority of whom are women and children (source: unhcr) and whereas more than 50 000 asylum applications have been registered in europe since the beginning of the conflict, i was keen to support this european parliament resolution. the european union, its member states and the international community as a whole are urged to continue to show solidarity in order to help these displaced people and to guarantee asylum to syrian nationals who request it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution stressing the union's duty to do more to protect syrian refugees. i welcome the substantial humanitarian aid provided by the union and welcome the implementation of the common european asylum system (ceas). while the un regional plan for syrian refugees forecasts that syrian refugees will number 3.5 million by the end of 2013, mainly in neighbouring countries, the european union must continue to show solidarity to the best of its ability.
in writing. i supported this resolution. it was put on the agenda because of the urgency of the crisis in syria and in particular the situation of syrian refugees. it is important that the european union and its member states provide a humanitarian response to this crisis and call for a humanitarian conference on the situation of syrian refugees. this resolution was adopted by a large majority, and i welcome that.
in writing. this european parliament resolution aims to find solutions to manage the large number of refugees fleeing the conflict in syria. according to the united nations, 3.5 million refugees will have left syria by the end of the year, threatening to destabilize the entire region. i voted in favour of this resolution because i want the european union to be involved in the effort to protect these refugees. we have called for a humanitarian conference to help syria's neighbours (especially lebanon, jordan, turkey and iraq) to welcome syrian refugees in the best possible conditions. we have also asked the member states of the european union to step up their diplomatic efforts in syria and to provide humanitarian aid to these refugees. finally, we called on european states to take in syrian refugees themselves and to guarantee fair access to asylum procedures. in order to enable the resettlement of refugees in emergency situations, member states will be able to use european funds, in particular the migration and asylum fund.
in writing. the approach taken should be considered as positive. the measures advocated to allow syrian refugees to enter the eu are welcome. but they are still hypocritical: legal admission has so far been very low (around 50 000), with france showing a particularly low number. it would do well to take swift action to facilitate the admission of these refugees, instead of making a bellicose bid that increases their numbers. i am voting for this text, which is moving in the right direction, because of the exceptional seriousness of the dramatic issue of syrian refugees, which is finally being recognized.
in writing. according to figures from the united nations high commissioner for refugees (unhcr), there are currently nearly 2 million syrian refugees who have crossed the borders of syria to flee the fighting. of the refugees, 76% are women and children and of these children, 410,000 are of primary school age (i.e. between 5 and 11 years old). there are also more than 4 million internally displaced persons. in the face of such a situation, it is absolutely crucial that the european union, the world's leading humanitarian donor, continue its efforts to meet the needs of refugees and internally displaced persons. i therefore supported the text adopted by parliament which calls, among other things, for the european union to organise a humanitarian conference on the syrian refugee crisis and to give priority to measures for the countries in the region which are hosting these refugees (in particular lebanon, jordan, turkey and iraq).
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution, which was the result of difficult negotiations between the political groups. it is far from being up to the task of helping the refugees of the syrian war, because it is too much behind the action of the countries bordering syria. the european parliament, however, calls on the member states to take action and assume their responsibilities in favour of syrian refugees, a request that is all the more justified in the wake of the new tragedy in lampedusa. it is high time that the member states, and in particular france, "facilitate their resettlement beyond national quotas, by allowing them to enter the territory for humanitarian reasons", that they activate the temporary protection system and show more solidarity among themselves rather than leaving the southern states alone in the face of the flows of migrants. i welcome the adoption of my amendments on the obligation to provide rescue at sea, the refusal of refoulement and the strict application of the rules on the detention of migrants. the mediterranean must stop being the graveyard for hundreds of migrants every year and syrians must be able to find refuge in the eu.
in writing. we all feel for the syrian people, who are victims of the tyranny of a power that is beyond all limits of what is acceptable. the desperation of the syrians has forced hundreds of thousands of them to flee to lebanon, jordan and europe. this situation raises the question of how the union will respond to this massive influx of refugees fleeing terror. this is the subject of the resolution i have defended, which stresses the need for european support for syria's neighbours in responding to health emergencies. europe cannot accommodate all those who seek to escape from blood-thirsty diets. it does not have the means to do so and the issue of the management of the union's external borders is too sensitive to be taken lightly. but european countries, with a centuries-old humanist tradition, must help the countries bordering syria to ensure that refugees are received in decent conditions. this is an imperative of solidarity from which the union cannot escape, within the limits of its material and financial capacities. i therefore welcome this vote, which sends a positive and pragmatic message to its partners who are weakened by the syrian crisis.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, madam commissioner, honourable members, i am grateful for the opportunity to address this important issue. the situation of the roma people is a human crisis. millions of our fellow eu citizens lead desperate lives on the margins, in deep poverty and without any realistic opportunity of improving their situation. they are the poorest of the poor – frequently forgotten. the council very much shares the concern of this parliament over the situation of europe’s roma, our largest ethnic community. the promotion of roma integration is primarily a matter of social justice. it is not acceptable that any ethnic group should be so excluded in europe in the twenty-first century. our inability to protect and provide for a minority group risks calling into question our international credibility. it is difficult for the european union to criticise ethnic injustice on the world stage if we are unable to integrate and protect our own minorities. but improving the situation of europe’s roma is also an economic imperative. we cannot afford to waste the potential of so many of our citizens. they have the capacity to offer so much to society and to their own community. whilst everyone is born with the potential for self-fulfilment, a child raised in deep poverty has little chance of bringing that potential to fruition. many of the roma in europe today go without essentials such as decent housing, proper education and healthcare and have very little chance of securing employment. once entire communities fall into extreme deprivation, whatever their ethnic identity, they can only recover through long-term policies which provide for their social inclusion. that is why we must continue to put emphasis on developing an integrated approach which covers the full range of social issues. the council has already expressed its concern at the continuing social problems of the roma communities, focusing on the four key aspects of education, employment, healthcare and housing. in may 2011 the council adopted conclusions which established an eu framework for national roma integration strategies up to 2020. this work drew on parliament’s own report on the eu strategy on roma inclusion drawn up by mrs lívia járóka, which made a significant contribution to the european union’s work in this area. the council specifically called on the member states to pursue objectives in the four areas i have just mentioned, with the aim of closing the gap between marginalised roma communities and the general population. improving the situation of the roma is a vital long-term policy goal, one which needs to involve a wide range of actors. the eu institutions have a vital part to play. the commission has a particular role to play in monitoring and coordinating our overall approach. but the main responsibility, of course, lies with the member states. the policies for ensuring the social inclusion of the roma have to be addressed primarily at national level. it is also crucial that roma representatives, ngos and local authorities are all involved in the development of those policies. like parliament and the commission, the council has returned to the issue of roma integration regularly in recent years. the council is currently examining the commission’s proposal for a council recommendation. this instrument will support the implementation of the national strategies that have been developed within the eu framework that was put in place two years ago. the presidency hopes to see the recommendation adopted in december. i am convinced that this will provide additional impetus to our joint efforts in this important area.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, the situation of the roma people in our continent often leads to emotional and polarising debates. it calls our own definition of tolerance and our understanding of solidarity into question, and it involves us all: the european union, the member states, the local authorities, the roma themselves: each and every citizen. the vast majority of roma living in the european union are european citizens. the european commission makes sure that the eu legislation is respected when it comes to the roma, as it is for all other eu citizens too. to that effect we are following the situation in each member state, in particular with the directive securing the free movement of persons within the eu and the directive prohibiting any discrimination on the basis of ethnic origin. the european commission is also committed to stopping social and economic exclusion of the most vulnerable of our eu citizens, including the roma communities, of course, and in this respect, the european commission has proposed that every member state commit to do so with measures that are defined at national level, in relation to the dimension and challenge they face, and implemented at local level. the commission also insists on the need to empower local roma communities, because social inclusion brings better results when targeted communities are involved in the process. but the path towards roma integration is not straightforward, nor can we expect it to be short. there are no quick fixes here, and we know it. let me recall the commission’s role in stepping up roma inclusion. we have defined three major difficulties. first, the lack of coordination between actors promoting roma integration, in particular across the european union. that is why the creation of the network of roma national contact points, which was initiated by the commission with the strong support of parliament, has moved us forward in this respect. we finally see synergies among member states. similar synergies are taking place among international organisations, with the creation of a coalition of international organisations in which the commission participates. second, the lack of political will from national decision-makers. we have managed to put the roma issue on the agenda of the council in 2011 (by ‘we’, i mean the commission and the european parliament, by joining forces on this subject). following our call for action, all member states have adopted national roma integration strategies. our aim is to keep exercising political pressure and facilitating peer review, while at the same time providing guidance to member states in that domain. the third difficulty is the difficulty faced by stakeholders in mobilising the financial means to implement their plans and the commitments made at european and national levels. at national level we are seeing some progress, but we need now to reach out to the local authorities, making sure that they get what they need and that they develop meaningful plans to integrate roma communities. the commission is aware of the social and economic challenges that roma inclusion represents for all local authorities. that is why we have put a lot of effort into facilitating the use of the european structural and investment funds for projects dedicated to roma integration during the new programming period 2014-2020. in particular, the commission has set the convincing implementation of the national roma integration strategies as one of the conditionalities for the delivery of funds. in addition we are leading a dialogue with national and local authorities in order to facilitate exchanges of information on how better to use the funds for roma integration. last june the commission came with a set of recommendations in order to enhance the implementation of the national roma integration strategies by the national authorities. this proposal, which is currently being discussed in the council, gives concrete recommendations to support local and regional authorities, which are the key actors in roma integration and have been left alone for too long. the european commission also recommends facilitating transnational cooperation at regional and local level. finally, we recommend fighting prejudices by placing particular attention to the protection of children and women. next spring the commission will report to the european parliament and to the council on the impact of the national strategies for access to education, healthcare, employment and housing.
