president-in-office of the council. − madam president, vice-president of the commission, honourable members, i am grateful for this opportunity to respond to the various issues raised in the question which has been tabled jointly by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and the committee on foreign affairs. it is important to begin by recalling the legal framework within which both our institutions function. the treaties state clearly ‘national security remains the sole responsibility of each member state’. this means that the work of intelligence agencies of member states falls outside the remit of the european union and its institutions. the investigation of the allegation of involvement in the cia programme is therefore a matter for the member states. the activities of national security and intelligence services cannot be addressed at eu level. that is the treaty. and this is why the council has not been able to follow up on your resolution which was adopted in september 2012. it is simply not possible for the council to issue declarations concerning the activities of the security services of the member states, given that these fall outside its competence. for the same reason the council has not held hearings with the relevant eu security agencies. as far as the issue of mutual legal assistance in this area is concerned, this would be a purely bilateral matter between the member states involved. furthermore, it is not within the competence of the council to propose safeguards so as to guarantee respect for human rights in intelligence-sharing or to provide for any delimitation of roles between intelligence and law-enforcement activities. you will appreciate that a legal constraint on the council and indeed on all the eu institutions in relation to this issue means that the council has not been able to initiate any measures to provide for a follow-up to the recommendation in your report from last year. that does not mean that the council has been silent. it has stated clearly on several occasions that the fight against terrorism has to take place in full respect for international law, including human rights law, international humanitarian law and refugee law. it has been clear also that the existence of secret detention facilities where detained persons are kept in a legal vacuum is not in conformity with international law. we can only be successful in the fight against terrorism in the long term if we stay true to our core values. any violations of human rights and the rule of law by government agencies in the fight against terrorism give rise to grievances and could actually encourage individuals to resort to terrorism. of course such circumstances can never justify or excuse any act of terrorism under any circumstances. the eu holds a regular dialogue with the us involving legal advisers on international law aspects of the fight against terrorism. this dialogue is an opportunity to address questions such as the arrest, detention, interrogation and transfer of terrorist suspects. it also enables the eu to underline the importance of respect for international law and human rights. however, it should be clear that the specific activities of intelligence services are not covered in this dialogue. summaries of these meetings have been made available to parliament but full minutes have not been released, given the need to protect the confidential nature of the discussions. diplomatic exchanges such as these are only valuable if the participants can express themselves openly and freely. on such sensitive issues quiet diplomacy is more beneficial than more public pronouncements. the council does not therefore accept that it has breached the principle of loyal cooperation as far as access to documents is concerned. it handles all requests in accordance with the existing rules and practices. each of us operates within a legal framework which we have to respect. where we can make progress or take measures, we are ready to do so, as in the case of our dialogue with the us but, if we want to ensure that the principles which i have just outlined are respected, our best way of achieving that is through patient diplomacy and discreet pressure. that is the most effective way of achieving results.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, practices referred to as ‘renditions’ constitute a serious violation of several fundamental rights. they involve unlawful arrest, arbitrary detention and very often torture or other ill-treatment, and we have already underlined several times in this chamber that the fight against terrorism cannot justify such practices. this has also been confirmed now by the council presidency, which has also underlined another fact: questions of national security are outside the remit of the european union. the treaty does not give the commission any competence to lead investigations into such matters, which is why the commission has always stressed that it is up to the member states to conduct in-depth, independent and impartial investigation to establish the truth. this is a positive obligation which derives from the european convention on human rights in order to establish responsibilities and enable the victims to obtain compensation for damage. today the european parliament is again asking about the possible breach of eu provisions by those member states that, seemingly, collaborated with the cia programme. the questions refer mainly to judicial cooperation with the united states. let me now put the facts on the table. at the time of the execution of these cia programmes – between 2001 and 2003 – there was no eu provision applicable to judicial cooperation between the eu and the usa. only in october 2009 did the council adopt a decision approving the conclusion of two agreements with the united states: one on extradition and one on mutual legal assistance. both agreements entered into force on 1 january 2010, and both clarify and unify the legal framework of judicial cooperation in criminal matters with the united states from that moment on. i would like once again to make a clear distinction between two necessities. first, the obligation to uncover the truth. this falls exclusively within the responsibility of the member states. the commission cannot directly coordinate or even facilitate national investigations in this field, because it has no power to set up meetings of prosecutors, for example, or of other national authorities in charge of the investigations. the council is present at our discussions today, and it has already said very clearly what its responsibility in that matter is. the second element – to avoid reiteration – is that the eu’s and the member states’ actions against terrorism must always comply with fundamental rights standards. one of the key changes in the legal framework since the european parliament’s first resolution has been the entry into force of the eu-us agreement on extradition and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. this agreement represents the key channels for law enforcement cooperation, and the commission has to ensure that this instrument, as well as all other relevant eu legislation against terrorism, is implemented and applied in a manner fully compatible with the charter of fundamental rights. on this basis, commissioner malmström and myself sent a letter on 5 march 2013 to the ministers of the interior and the ministers of justice of all member states to stress the importance of using all relevant eu instruments in the fight against terrorism and to recall that these instruments must be implemented and applied in a manner fully compatible with the charter. only six member states have replied so far. the european commission services reminded the other member states about the letters in july, and the european commission will continue to urge member states to answer, as we have no intention of neglecting this important challenge for the future of judicial cooperation in criminal matters.

member of the commission. − madam president, let me start by congratulating the rapporteur on his birthday today and also thanking him and the libe committee and the team around them for the work they have done, enabling us to finish the trialogue on the eurosur regulation in less than six months. i hope that parliament and the council will adopt this regulation so that it can enter into force in december as provided for. this is something that has been under discussion since 2008, when the then commission presented its roadmap, and we have managed to develop, test, legislate for and implement the system in a relatively short time. the debate on eurosur is very timely, following directly on from the debate on lampedusa and underlining eurosur’s important role in protecting and saving the lives of migrants trying to reach european shores. we have no illusions that eurosur in itself will put an end to such horrific events – their causes are deep-rooted – but it can help to make a difference. on the commission’s side, we are currently putting a lot of effort into improving the capability of frontex and member states to detect migrants travelling in small and unseaworthy boats. as you know, the use of these types of vessel is the main reason why so many people die at sea. we have analysed the problem and have spoken with experts from member states and industry about how to detect the boats better. this has confirmed the approach chosen. the main challenges in detecting small boats are the lack of coordination between different national authorities and a lack of proper communication channels among them. so one of the key aims of eurosur is ‘inter-agency cooperation’. it will force member states internally to implement cooperation between different authorities and centres and to coordinate more effectively and make sure they are working together in the same room. thanks to the european parliament, the amendments to the eurosur regulation will require national coordination centres to ensure timely and exact information-sharing with search and rescue authorities and to report to frontex any incidents relating to a risk to the lives of migrants. also thanks to your amendments, the eurosur regulation will require that frontex cooperates not only with the european external action service but also with eu delegations abroad in order to collect information on migration routes. another very important characteristic of eurosur is ‘information exchange’. frontex is currently testing with the member states the eurosur communication network and the european situational picture. this will allow frontex to receive within minutes information from member states on incidents occurring at the external borders. eurosur will promote the exchange of information not only inside and between member states but also with neighbouring countries. this currently takes place outside the eu framework, but in future it will be regulated strictly under the eurosur regulation, with very clear provisions on non-refoulement and personal data protection. you also insisted in the negotiations that the commission be empowered to verify the compliance of any border surveillance agreement concluded between a member state and a third country, to ensure that the requirements of the eurosur regulation are accepted, and that we inform you accordingly. lastly, ‘solidarity’ is an important word in connection with eurosur. it will help to identify hotspots at our external borders and to provide support to the relevant authorities much faster. this will be done by dividing the external land and sea borders into border sections and by attributing an ‘impact level’ or ‘risk level’ to each section. depending on this level, member states and frontex will follow a step-by-step approach for providing support. it will be up to the national coordination centres to coordinate the support at national level. if that is not enough, member states can ask frontex for more support. this will allow limited resources to be deployed to the hotspots quickly and then redeployed to other hotspots when the situation changes or has improved. so thank you, mr mulder and the other people in the libe committee, for the work you have done.

author. - mr president, madam high representative, ladies and gentlemen, apartheid is the term which, beyond the regime it designates, evokes violence, discrimination and humiliation, and which the then indian prime minister, manmohan singh, chose to use in 2006 to speak of the condition of the untouchables in his country. despite these shocking statements, despite the abolition of untouchability by the indian constitution - written by the untouchable leader dr. ambedkar - despite the laws, 260 million broken men and women suffer daily atrocities with impunity. in india, between 2001 and 2005, three dalit women were raped every day. a crime or offense against a dalit occurred every 18 minutes. although india and pakistan have signed the universal declaration of human rights, millions of their citizens are denied the rights and freedoms it proclaims simply because of their birthplace. the committee on development, which i chair, has wanted to take up this matter again because these caste-based discriminations, besides being humanly unacceptable and contrary to international human rights law, are also a major structural factor in poverty and inequality. apartheid has terrible socioeconomic consequences: denied or withdrawn access to land, denied decent jobs, exclusion from education and health systems, denial of their basic rights by the police and justice services when these do not violate them outright. only 10% of dalit women receive education in this way. it is simply not possible to get out of extreme poverty under these conditions. and india's new emerging power status does not eradicate this phenomenon, quite the opposite. the gap between dalits and non-dalits has been widening since the early 1990s, highlighting the failure of development in writing. i voted in favour of the mulder report, which aims to create a european border surveillance system called eurosur. the establishment of such a mechanism will help to strengthen internal security by preventing the loss of human lives through the fight against illegal immigration. through increased cooperation and a permanent exchange of information between the member states of the union, the migratory flows of those entering the union will be regulated in a way that ensures respect for human rights principles, while contributing to the reduction of cross-border crime and drug trafficking.
in writing. freedom of movement is a chance for europeans. but we must ensure that it ensures the security of our territories and that it is implemented effectively. this is not a question of a single currency, but of a single currency. this text will enable us to strengthen our action at the borders, in particular by improving cooperation between agencies and with our partners in third countries.
in writing. the new european border surveillance system eurosur proposed by the european union should help to enhance the security of migrants while preventing cross-border crime. in practical terms, it will allow eu countries to share real-time images and data on refugee flows at the eu's external borders and thus to more quickly detect and assist refugee boats in distress. the tragedy of lampedusa is a painful reminder of the need for member states to work together to prevent further tragedies. this pan-european system can be a first response. it must be used to save the lives of migrants and its rules must respect human rights.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am in favour of strengthening control of the external borders of the schengen area, which would then guarantee full mutual trust between the member states and thus promote free movement within this area. i am in particular in favour of the creation of a common framework clearly defining the responsibilities and powers of the national coordination centres (ncs) responsible for border surveillance in the member states and of the frontex agency, which together form the backbone of eurosur.
in writing. the tragic tragedy of lampedusa is a stark reminder that we must act ruthlessly and firmly against illegal immigration networks, and this in cooperation with third countries. i voted in favour of this report because the creation of the new eurosur system will help to better protect the eu's external borders. if it is not enough on its own, it is at least a step in the right direction. specifically geared towards the surveillance of european borders, this mechanism aims to better combat illegal immigration and criminal networks, which exploit the misery of migrants with disregard for their lives. to send back the image of a 'screwdriver europe' would create an appeal of illusory air. the enhanced coordination between member states and the improved exchange of information provided for by the eurosur system are important progress. we also need to increase the budget for frontex. i call on the member states to deploy more border guards to reinforce the frontex european border guard team.
in writing. just a few days after the tragedy in lampedusa of a boat carrying eritrean and somali refugees, i supported the establishment of the eurosur system to prevent such tragedies, through a better exchange of information which will allow for a quicker determination of the steps to be taken and the responsible state in the event of detection of vessels in distress at sea. i particularly welcome the provisions added by the european parliament on saving the lives of migrants (especially at sea) and on respect for fundamental rights and the principle of non-refoulement as prerequisites for the proper functioning of the system. however, its implementation will need to be closely monitored to ensure that the right to non-refoulement and the right to access asylum procedures are fully respected.
in writing. the tragedy in lampedusa has highlighted a painful but real phenomenon which calls for national and european responses, because the fight against illegal immigration and smugglers cannot be won without european cooperation and cooperation with source and transit countries. the signals we send are fundamental in matters of both criminal policy and access to citizenship. on the national level, we must make our social policies less attractive. the more we show "light-heartedness", the more this phenomenon will increase. at european level, we must recognise that migration policies need to be better coordinated and our actions concerted. in the light of the facts, we must therefore respond with concrete action. that is why i am calling for the creation of a european border police under the aegis of frontex, whose financial resources have collapsed from a budget of 118 million in 2011 to 85 million in 2013, and for the rapid establishment of the eurosur border surveillance system.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague jan mulder. the creation of eurosur is intended to strengthen control of the external borders of the schengen area. it will establish a mechanism for member states' border surveillance authorities to exchange operational information and cooperate with each other and frontex in order to reduce the loss of life at sea and the number of migrants entering the european union illegally, and to strengthen internal security by preventing cross-border crime. eurosur shall start operations on 2 december 2013 in all member states with external borders and shall be operational on 1 december 2014 in the remaining member states. the legislative resolution was adopted by parliament with 479 votes in favour, 101 against and 20 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr mulder's report because, particularly after the recent tragic events in lampedusa, the introduction of a system of border control and a strengthening of security for those eu territories which represent the gateway to europe for migrants are all the more necessary. we have repeatedly stressed, including in the presence of commissioner malmström, the need to tackle this problem once and for all with a truly european and truly supportive approach. it is no longer possible to delegate the resolution of the immigration issue to italy or to the member states bordering the mediterranean alone. it is time for national governments, all those in the european union, to take responsibility and decide to invest in a european border surveillance system that can be effective and prevent further tragic incidents.
in writing. the eurosur border surveillance system is an integrated border management system in cooperation with the frontex agency, to combat migration and cross-border crime. this is an issue that has implications for the fundamental rights of migrants and asylum seekers. from 2 december 2013, southern and eastern member states will set up national coordination centres which will cooperate with frontex through the sharing of real-time information and data (satellite data and ship reports). the inclusion of some of the positive points achieved during the negotiations, such as respect for fundamental rights, the principle of 'non-refoulement' and the protection of personal data, cannot compensate for the vision of a 'fortress europe' criminalising migrants in this text. that is why i voted against the proposal for a regulation establishing the european border surveillance system. the confusion between the fight against cross-border crime and illegal immigration leads to the perception of migrants and asylum seekers as threats to internal security. the 'fortress europe' principle will be reinforced with the electronic system eurosur. and this is extremely costly surveillance and disproportionate to the numbers of so-called irregular migration.
in writing. i voted in favour of the creation of the agency called eurosur, which establishes a mechanism for exchange and cooperation between the authorities of the member states who monitor borders. the new agency complements the role of frontex, the cooperation body for the operational teams of the member states for border surveillance. eurosur shall establish a communication network allowing the exchange of sensitive information in a secure and real-time manner. monitoring tools such as satellites or ship reporting systems will thus be able to contribute to the fight against illegal immigration and the prevention of cross-border crime on a larger scale. eurosur will start operations on 2 december 2013 in the member states with external borders and on 1 december 2014 in the rest of the union.
in writing. the report before us amends the commission's text on the creation of a system for monitoring the eu's external borders: eurosur. the commission's original text was already borrowed from security ideology, and it is even more so in the mulder report. it emphasises the fight against illegal immigration, while remaining silent on the illicit movement of capital and goods. it proposes to create a specific entry illegal immigration in the national situation table. the military is also being asked to participate in the hunt for undocumented migrants. finally, to improve europe's operational efficiency in the pursuit of poverty, it proposes to monitor in particular migrants using 'small boats unsuitable for sea travel'. in the context of the 300 drowned on lampedusa, this report is abject. i vote against it. this monitoring system should instead be ecological and in the general interest rather than a system for hunting down the poor.
in writing. the sinking of the boat carrying african candidates in exile in lampedusa has left a deep impression on the minds and cast doubt on the eu's migration policy. how can we prevent thousands of immigrants, who are being ensnared by unscrupulous smugglers, from dying in their attempt to achieve the utopian european dream? in the first instance, only a pan-european border surveillance system with a rapid response capability will be able to help those who board these makeshift boats. i therefore voted in favour of the operating rules for 'eurosur', a system designed to improve the detection, prevention and fight against illegal immigration and crossborder crime, but also to help migrants in need.
in writing. the free movement of persons is one of the founding principles of the european construction. european citizens have repeatedly demonstrated their commitment to the abolition of border controls, which is one of the eu's greatest achievements. in order to improve the control of the external borders, it is necessary to facilitate the sharing of information and to improve cooperation between member states. i therefore supported the report on the european border surveillance system (eurosur) which aims to strengthen control of the external borders of the schengen area. it will establish a mechanism for member states' border surveillance authorities to exchange operational information and to cooperate better with each other.
in writing. i voted against this european legislation on the eurosur system, the european framework for the surveillance of the eu's external borders. the text agreed between the council and the european parliament strengthens the surveillance of the eu's external borders through the exchange of information and cooperation between member states and frontex. this system also allows cooperation and exchange of information with third countries under certain conditions. the eurosceptic efd mps and those on the far right, including marine le pen and her father, have come together to support this initiative against the rights of foreigners, not hesitating to ignore their primary anti-europeanism in favor of fortress europe and the hunt for immigrants. mrs le pen was thus shameless in contradicting her remarks during the debate on the tragedy of lampedusa on 9 october. despite the deaths of hundreds of migrants near lampedusa on 3 october, it was not possible to make rescue of migrants at sea compulsory. the amendment calling for this was rejected. reference to respect for fundamental rights and data protection is not enough to counterbalance new legislation that continues to strengthen the 'fortress europe'.
in writing. with this agreement in parliament, the union is taking a big step forward in managing its external borders and tackling threats to its security. i welcome today's vote, which gives europe an innovative system for detecting, preventing and combating illegal immigration and crime. the benefits of an internal market, with the disappearance of national borders, require that the security and safety of the union's borders, whether on land or at sea, be strengthened. thanks to the exchange of information in real time between the member states and the authorities responsible for border control with third countries, europe is making a considerable qualitative and operational leap in terms of protecting its territory against all kinds of trafficking. the implementation of eurosur will be effective in december 2013, and i urge that we move quickly to the next stage, namely the pooling of means of monitoring, monitoring and intervention, in order to put an end to the paradox that security is everyone's business, but the tools to ensure it are national.

in writing. − directive 2006/66/ec of the european parliament and of the council prohibits the placing on the market of portable batteries and accumulators containing more than 0.002% cadmium by weight. article 4 of that directive provides for a review of the exemption for cordless power tools. i voted in favour of amending the directive to limit the derogation to the use of cadmium in portable batteries and accumulators for wireless devices until 31 december 2016, thereby safeguarding the interests of both consumers and producers and ensuring the protection of the environment and human health.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report to ban the toxic substance cadmium in portable batteries for cordless power tools such as drills, screws, saws and keys from 31 december 2016. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the dangers of ionizing radiation. the text also ends the derogation for button batteries to reduce the risk of mercury leakage into the environment.
in writing. the text is designed to strengthen measures to protect the environment and public health. the effects of cadmium and mercury on human health and the environment are well established and well known. but this text does not propose a major breakthrough: cadmium batteries and accumulators are responsible for a small part of the cadmium emissions into the environment. moreover, these batteries are obsolete, replacement materials exist (lithium battery), and are already widely used as replacements. the measure comes after the battle. this is the ecology of the 25th hour. i vote in favour of encouraging these timid advances.
in writing. i voted in favour of this revision, which received the broad support of our assembly. the text ends the exception in the original directive for cordless portable tools in respect of cadmium, a carcinogenic metal which is toxic to the aquatic environment. the revised directive will ban the presence of metal in tools such as drills, screwdrivers or saws from 2017, giving manufacturers time to make a less costly transition. when the ban comes into force, nickel-cadmium batteries will only be allowed in emergency systems, such as alarms, and in medical equipment. in the other products, they will have been gradually replaced by the lithium-ion alternative. parliament also introduced a ban on mercury in button batteries (which are used in watches, toys and remote controls, among other things) from autumn 2015 to help reduce pollution, particularly related to the fact that these batteries easily escape recycling. these changes should enable the eu to innovate in the areas of batteries, materials and recycling, which i welcome.

in writing. caste discrimination is the exclusion of a section of the population on the grounds of their ethnic or religious origin. caste systems impose a hierarchy or even segregation in society, preventing a lower caste from accessing certain professions, condemning its members to poverty. members of the upper castes remain unpunished when they commit crimes or sexual violence against a member of a lower caste. i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls on the commission and the eeas to combat this discrimination as well as any other. the european union has also always been involved in the fight against discrimination and for respect for minorities.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text on caste discrimination. the caste system, which is very prevalent in south asia (especially india), also exists in several states in africa and the middle east. the report condemns the continuing violations of human rights against people facing the caste system and caste-based discrimination. such discrimination can take many forms, and includes the denial of equality between people, which prevents, for example, access to justice or employment for discriminated persons. in this report i also supported the proposal to the commission and the european external action service (eeas) to integrate the fight against caste discrimination into the union's legislation, policies and programming documents and to adopt guidelines for their implementation.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i am pleased to be able to present to you today this report on the monitoring of trade in drug precursors between the european union and third countries. we are indeed fortunate to have been able to reach agreement with the council and the commission quickly. the result of this trilogue agreement seems to me to be excellent. drug precursors are legal substances that can be used to synthesise drugs. for example, vinegar is used in the manufacture of heroin. in order to combat drug trafficking, it is important to be able to monitor the trade in precursors. the fewer precursors that are easy to divert from the legal market, the fewer synthetic drugs that are available. the challenge is therefore to find a balance in the monitoring of these substances without hindering the market. the current regulation is flawed and this is why the european commission has proposed a revision. we have found that drugs containing drug precursors are not subject to special controls and can therefore be easily misused. this is particularly the case with cold medicines, which contain ephedrine and pseudoephedrine. both substances are controlled drug precursors because they are essential for the manufacture of methamphetamines. drug dealers have been diverting drugs that they themselves have not been monitoring. rather than creating a separate system for cold medicines, we created a new category of controlled substances. they're called classified substances. in other words, it will take only a delegated act to add a new drug to the list if it is discovered that it is being misused to synthesise illicit substances. this allows for a rapid response to new drug trafficking trends without hampering the drug trade. only those whose precursor substance can be easily extracted from the medicinal product may be included among the classified substances. however, at present only medicinal products containing ephedrine and pseudoephedrine meet this criterion. to those who say that we should not impede the trade in medicines because it is vital for underdeveloped populations, i would like to say that at the moment the only medicines subject to controls are comfort medicines, since they treat exclusively colds. in addition, the substances to be included in this new category, including medicinal products containing ephedrine and pseudo-ephedrine, will be subject to a very light and very low-cost pre-export notification requirement. according to the impact study, this cost is about eur 15. in the long term, it is entirely possible to include other medicines in this very flexible category if the need arises. moreover, since the revision of this regulation is also an opportunity to adapt the comitology to the lisbon treaty, we felt that implementing acts, under the examination procedure, were the most appropriate, but i would like to remind you that this should not be a precedent in the negotiations between the council and the european parliament, particularly on other subjects. in conclusion, i would like to highlight the excellent cooperation between the various political groups and i would like to thank the fictitious rapporteurs for the confidence they have shown in me throughout this legislative process. i would also like to thank the council and the commission for the quality of our exchanges. i thank you, of course, for your attention and look forward to any comments you may have.

member of the commission. − mr president, the two proposals on medical devices and in vitro diagnostics that we are debating today are of the highest importance for patient safety. current legislation has shown shortcomings far beyond the pip breast implant scandal. this was a case of fraud which, even with the toughest pre-market controls, could not have been prevented. but we need better clarity for innovative and borderline products. we need stricter requirements for notified bodies and for their oversight of manufacturers. without changing the law, unannounced audits will not become obligatory. with such unannounced audits, even the pips scandals – though it was a case of fraud – would have been detected much earlier. these are just a few examples of why the revision is needed – and it is needed urgently in order to fully restore the trust of patients, consumers and healthcare professionals in the regulatory system. for this reason, let me thank the rapporteurs, ms roth-behrendt and mr liese, together with the shadow rapporteurs, for their determination, expertise and personal commitment towards advancing these two important files. i will not explain to you the details of the commission’s proposals again, as you are well aware of them. instead, let me address two key elements which have been subject to particularly intensive discussions over the last couple of months, including in parliament. as regards the system for the approval of devices, the commission’s proposal was to maintain a system of self-certification by the manufacturer in the case of low risk – and of verification by notified bodies in the case of medium-risk – medical devices. in high-risk cases, the commission has proposed allowing public authorities to have a second look at the assessment by the notified bodies in specific cases, for instance where the product is particularly innovative or where particular problems have occurred with the category of products. this was meant as an exceptional safeguard. in fact, our impact assessment assumed that something like 50 products would be scrutinised per year. different changes have been proposed in your committees. i have no problem accepting that the commission proposal can be improved. it may not have considered sufficiently, for example, how to ensure the necessary technical and scientific expertise for the scrutiny, but overall i believe that the scrutiny procedure, as a form of exceptional safeguard, is the best compromise to ensure a high level of patient safety while avoiding two burdensome processes. for the reprocessing of single-use medical devices, i strongly believe that we need european rules that fill the current regulatory gap. the commission has proposed strict rules on reprocessing based on the latest scientific evidence. it would allow the practice of reprocessing to develop further under clear and safe conditions, leading to potential savings for healthcare systems. i have followed attentively the different ideas that have been put forward in parliament on reprocessing, and i am, of course, open to carefully analysing the amendments you will be voting on after this debate in order to see whether they would further improve patient protection. apart from these issues, there are many other suggestions from parliament which i am happy to consider favourably. you propose, for example, strengthening the provisions on ethics committees or on minors and incapacitated patients. i am open to these changes, as long as they remain in line with the provisions that are currently being negotiated in the context of the proposed regulation on clinical trials on pharmaceuticals. similarly, there are a number of specific issues on the proposal concerning in vitro diagnostics which, in my view, are also valid and acceptable in principle. this concerns, for example, in-house exemption and counselling and informed consent in the field of genetic tests. i am very interested now in hearing your views on these, as well as on other issues on which you think the commission proposals need to be improved. i cannot give you a final position on all details, but i will commit myself to carefully analysing all the amendments you adopt on both of these proposals. my guiding principle will be the aim of ensuring the highest level of patient and consumer safety, whilst making sure that innovation continues to flourish. i count on you to give a strong mandate to the rapporteurs, ms roth-behrendt and mr liese, which will pave the way for successful negotiations, so that together we can deliver for citizens by concluding these important files within the current parliamentary term.

mr president, it is true that in recent years there have been a great many safety problems with medical devices involving risks, the most publicized of which was the pip. this scandal broke in 2010 and it was, it's true, a fraud by the industrialist. but contrary to what mr krahmer said, we found that there was a faulty chain of responsibility, too many links of which had allowed the fraud to go on far too long. the national authorities and notified bodies have shown intolerable negligence. in this context, we adopted a resolution in june 2012 and our group, the greens, introduced a system of prior marketing authorisation for class 2b and 3 medical devices that went further than the rapporteur's proposal. i regret that this system has not been included by the commission in its legislative proposal. there is a paradox, however, in that there are marketing authorizations for medicines, whereas there are no marketing authorizations for high-risk medical devices, for everything related to implants. it's still pretty aberrant that we haven't gotten to that system. today, a system of special notified bodies is proposed which are indicated for devices at risk, with increased control of their work by the authorities. this is a minimum, an acceptable minimum, and it must not be weakened any further. i am quite satisfied, however, that we have obtained a comparative clinical evaluation against existing treatments for the same indication, whether medical devices or drugs, as well as the evaluation of clinical data for high-risk medical devices. we think it's essential before it's on the market. finally, we were able to call for a ban on all carcinogens, mutagens and reproductive toxicants. at present, they are banned for cosmetics and toys, and we are now calling for them to be banned for medical devices as well.
mr president, pip breast implants and defective hip replacements are all scandals which have seriously damaged the confidence of patients and which make it our duty today to combine safety with innovation, because patients are in dire need of industrial progress. we've had some fraud, due to flaws in the medical device approval system. this is a simple ce marking, the same as that required for the approval of toasters. these frauds clearly show that this marking has serious shortcomings. so today, to restore the trust of users, we must first be extremely rigorous about the accreditation criteria of notified bodies, which we must strengthen. it is true that a marketing authorization should not have been imposed, because it is too long and too cumbersome a procedure which would have hindered innovation. restoring trust also involves random unannounced audits and sanctions, such as suspension or removal. and above all, the reprocessing of single-use devices must be avoided at all costs. i am absolutely convinced that the single-use medical device provides greater safety than sterilized and reconditioned equipment. there is far too much diversity in the member states in this respect. in conclusion, i would say that what we absolutely need is very strict material surveillance, just as we have pharmacovigilance for medicines.

in writing. i have today approved the two reports on the updating of the regulations on medical devices. at the end of 2011, the pip breast implant scandal revealed the lack of cooperation between member states and the malfunctioning of the medical device traceability system. more than 400 000 breast implants from the french company pip have been marketed worldwide despite non-compliance with quality criteria. today parliament has voted in favour of new requirements: to improve patient protection by strengthening traceability and controls to prevent a new scandal of this kind. this includes improving access to clinical data to improve product knowledge, the creation of an 'implant card' for implant recipients and greater information sharing between national authorities. i have a concern about the issue of accessibility of high-risk tests: the new legislation should not restrict the possibilities for member states to make tests (including hiv testing) more easily available to the public (including high-risk tests).
in writing. with this text, we can look forward to strong european ambitions to improve the health and safety of all european patients using in vitro testing. the text provides for the harmonization of the rules for these tests within the european union, for greater transparency, in the service of protecting the health of europeans.
in writing. the pip breast prosthesis scandal has highlighted the shortcomings of the european medical device control system. unlike medicines, these products do not require prior authorisation from a health authority, so it is essential to develop stricter certification rules that put patient safety first. with the revision of this system, the most risky medical devices - such as those intended to be implanted in the human body - will now be controlled by specialised bodies. access to clinical data on devices will allow for better market surveillance. when an incident occurs in one country, an early warning system will facilitate a rapid response in other european countries. the reprocessing of certain single-use medical devices may expose patients to health risks. this practice is now banned in france and other countries may do the same. the safety rules for in vitro diagnostic devices will also be strengthened by the establishment of an ethics committee. these new measures will restore consumer confidence in the sector, while preserving its capacity for innovation.
in writing. the vote on these texts on medical devices and on in vitro diagnostic medical devices is important as they will have direct repercussions on european public health and thus on the daily lives of eu citizens. in the wake of the series of health scandals, including the pip breast implant case, it seems to me essential that the new legislation address the current gaps, strengthen consumer protection and restore patient confidence in medicine. the texts i voted for support stricter measures in terms of monitoring, certification and traceability of medical devices. the controls will now be much more stringent for in vitro diagnostic medical devices and others. we have also decided to regulate the reprocessing of single-use devices in order to improve patient safety.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague peter liese which sets high safety and public health standards for in vitro medical devices and the notified bodies responsible for monitoring these medical devices. we voted against restrictions on self-testing which would have made it available only on prescription. the text also incorporates provisions adopted for the regulation on clinical trials in negotiation courts. i therefore welcome its very wide adoption by 525 votes to 21, with 132 abstentions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on in vitro diagnostic medical devices which introduces stricter rules on genetic testing, which must be supervised by doctors or by persons qualified under national law and be carried out after explicit information and consent. i voted against limiting self-diagnostic tests to prescription only. i believe that the hiv test, for example, should be available from a non-profit organization without a prescription.
in writing. in vitro medical devices are medical devices intended for diagnostic use outside the human body, i.e. in a laboratory or in the vicinity of the patient. they cover a very wide range of tests, such as self-diagnostics for blood sugar measurement, hiv tests and dna tests. the report proposes a number of improvements. a new risk classification system is proposed. the market surveillance and vigilance system will be strengthened. the unannounced inspections of enterprises will be mandatory. the report also allows the establishment of a network of european reference laboratories. the report ignores the crucial question of the social and ecological conditions under which these medical devices are produced. in the absence of such social harmonisation, the free movement of medical devices increases the risks of relocation of manufacturers. france is highly exposed to this since it already imports 55% of the medical devices consumed. however, its production capacity continues to decline, as shown by the closure of the sodimedical plant. i am voting in favour, to support the regulatory advances in product regulation. but i deplore a further step in the liberalisation of the goods market to the detriment of workers and the aim of relocating production as close as possible to their consumption.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report updating an earlier directive on in vitro diagnostic medical devices (ivds). these devices are intended to be used for diagnostic purposes outside the human body, i.e. in a laboratory or at the patient's bedside (self-diagnostics for measuring blood glucose, hiv tests, dna tests, etc.). the current directive does not guarantee that poor quality ivd medical devices are excluded from the market. however, since these products can circulate freely in the holy and sacred common market, it seemed important to remedy the current shortcomings. the market surveillance and vigilance system will now be strengthened, with mandatory unannounced inspections. the report also introduces the concept of 'informed consent' as a condition for tests, including prenatal or genetic tests: from now on, appropriate genetic counselling will have to be systematically offered to inform patients of the consequences before the test is carried out. as with the roth-behrendt report, i will remain vigilant with the eug in the forthcoming negotiations with the council on this directive.

in writing. i have today approved the agreement reached between the european parliament and the council on the ship recycling regulation. with almost all (90% in 2009) eu shipowners circumventing the general ban on the transfer of hazardous waste to non-oecd countries and dismantling their ships in countries such as india or bangladesh, there is an urgent need for stronger rules. the agreement reached will, i hope, make for cleaner dismantling, in particular through the creation of a global list of recycling facilities meeting minimum health and environmental criteria.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this text, which aims to put an end to a dangerous and environmentally irresponsible practice. it has two aspects which are of great importance to europe: it is not only intended to eliminate a threat to the environment, but it is also intended to ensure the protection of workers who are responsible for dismantling our ships under often unacceptable conditions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am in favour of reducing the harmful effects of recycling ships flying the flag of a member state of the european union, without imposing any unnecessary new financial burdens. more explicit requirements for ship recycling facilities should be introduced to ensure that recycling and waste treatment are environmentally sound. i support reducing the disparities between operators in the european union, oecd countries and third countries concerned in health and safety at work and environmental standards. the report also aims to facilitate the ratification of the hong kong convention. the convention will require these parties to dismantle their large merchant ships exclusively in countries which are parties to the convention. these may be asian countries whose decommissioning facilities will then have to meet internationally recognised standards. in doing so, the european union is advocating an environmentally sound management of ship dismantling.
in writing. i voted in favour of this agreement because it will allow for better treatment of end-of-life ship recycling in europe. as ships are made up of many dangerous and toxic substances, they should normally comply with strict recycling requirements, aimed at protecting both the environment and the health of workers. yet many end-of-life ships are sent to third countries for scrapping, where basic social and environmental standards are not respected. the agreement thus makes it possible to tighten up the legislation in force and to establish strict rules applying both to ships flying the european flag and to third-party ships entering and leaving union ports. it will thus allow for better compliance with environmental standards, while at the same time strengthening the competitiveness of the european ship recycling market, which creates many jobs in our ports.
in writing. the issue of ship dismantling and recycling is both an environmental and an industrial issue. more than ever, local zero-waste industrial cycles need to be promoted. europe must stop having its floating garbage cans in poor countries dismantled under the worst social and health conditions. the south must not be europe's garbage bin, allowing it to shine in ecological matters on the back of the health of slave workers in india, africa or bangladesh. the european union, if it had an industrial policy that served europeans and not ship owners and oil companies, would develop a ship recycling industry. this would lead to the development of new technologies and the creation of many skilled jobs. a port like cherbourg, which already specialises in the dismantling of nuclear submarines, could become a central european platform for this type of work. the regulation offers some small advances, but it fails to address the core of the problem: the regulatory loophole on depaving, which allows 90% of boats to be dismantled or stranded in asia in deplorable conditions. i therefore could not vote in favour of the report and abstained.
in writing. i supported this report. the text will improve and strengthen health and environmental standards for ship recycling and prevent end-of-life european vessels from being illegally sent to low-cost third countries to be dismantled under questionable conditions. this report will also help to support the competitiveness of our ship recycling industry. it was adopted by 591 votes to 47, with 32 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. many eu-flagged vessels are being dismantled at low cost in unacceptable environmental and sanitary conditions, particularly in south-east asia. the text adopted by the european parliament should improve and strengthen the health and environmental standards for ship recycling. i voted in favour of this text which improves environmental protection and contributes to the competitiveness of our ship recycling industry. the commission has also proposed that the eu should be able to provide for the dismantling of ships flying the european flag in facilities located in the european union (eu) or outside the eu that are approved at european level. in addition, every ship transiting through a european port will have to keep on board an inventory of the hazardous materials present in the ship's structure or equipment, specifying their location and approximate quantities. finally, controls will be strengthened and penalties for breaches of the rules will be more dissuasive. to help businesses adapt to the new rules, the european commission will have to submit a report within three years on the feasibility of a financial instrument to support environmentally and socially responsible ship recycling.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on ship recycling which improves the health and environmental standards for ship recycling. the text aims in particular to prevent european ships at the end of their life being transferred outside the european union, in particular to south-east asia, to be dismantled under dubious conditions, particularly in relation to the treatment of hazardous waste.
in writing. the developing countries cannot be the garbage of the world where ships die and are torn apart in social and ecological conditions that are unbearable. this report strengthens the obligations of shipowners for the treatment of end-of-life ships. it introduces the price of dismantling into the transport cost and promotes the development of recycling channels. these advances go beyond the convention currently in force. however, this regulation fails in one central point. it does not contain any binding clause to oblige a shipowner to have a ship dismantled in the european union. the text only provides for a tax on shipowners who refuse to undertake to have their ships dismantled in the union. the depavilling is therefore not prevented, this text only seeks to dissuade it by financial motives. shipowners will be able to continue to have their ships dismantled on the beaches of bangladesh and elsewhere. they will simply pay a tax and sell the ship once it has left the last european port. however, despite these serious shortcomings, this text opens a new period of treatment of this subject. i am voting in favour of the introduction of regulations.

in writing. in this report, the european parliament adopted an amendment to a regulation on the recycling of european ships. the vast majority of these vessels (90%) are now dismantled in non-oecd countries, mainly in asia. needless to say, the conditions for dismantling are deplorable both environmentally and socially. the european parliament has made some positive changes, including strengthening the obligations of shipowners on the treatment of end-of-life vessels and requiring that community-flagged vessels be dismantled in certified centres. however, these provisions are vague and do not provide sufficient guarantees. what is more, this regulation does not make it possible to combat complacency, which is the source of all the current deviations. i therefore abstained from voting.

in writing. i voted for the referral back of this ambiguous, ideological report, which clearly did not fall within the european union's remit. social issues as important as the opening up of ldcs to single women or lesbians, or sex education in schools, must be the subject of wide-ranging debates with our fellow citizens, and not be voted on in secret in the context of a simple own-initiative report. i am in favour of ldcs for heterosexual couples, but i am against ldcs for same-sex couples. there are other priorities for sex education in school, where many children leave without even knowing how to read properly. parental authority is involved, and it is up to the parents to decide what values they want to impart. i'm strongly opposed to gender theory. i am a daily advocate of a strong, practical and pragmatic europe, which responds to the concerns of our citizens. i regret that the european parliament is taking a position on such texts, which do not fall within its direct competence.
in writing. what could be more regrettable than to tackle such sensitive and controversial issues as sexual and reproductive health and rights. in both form and substance, it is one of those ethical and moral issues - when they appeal to the conscience of each individual - which cannot be reduced to a list of principles imposed by a political assembly which had not been asked for anything. the european parliament has always been very sensitive to the protection of rights, particularly those of consumers and users, and this is to its credit. but on this subject, which is not even a matter of the immediate concern of the citizens, parliament should have respected the principle of subsidiarity and the sovereignty of the states. i am therefore glad that the text has been referred back to committee and i will be vigilant in the next steps to ensure that it is never adopted.
in writing. i voted in favour of referring the estrela report on sexual and reproductive health and rights back to committee, given my opposition to this own-initiative report. first of all, it is a question of respecting the principle of subsidiarity, a fundamental principle of the european union following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. issues relating in particular to sex education are not within the competence of the european union and the member states remain the sole decision-makers in these matters. i would also like to emphasize my opposition to the teaching of gender theory in schools and to the vague notions of 'holistic' and 'interactive' sex education in the text of the report. the text is too ambiguous in its wording, which makes it dangerous. parliament voted to refer the text back to committee, on the basis of rule 175 (2) of parliament's rules of procedure. i'm glad you did.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the union's development aid policy. in its relations with developing countries, the report says the eu should step up its support for civil society organisations and local authorities at all levels. the aim is to ensure 'democratic ownership' of development policy, i.e. an increased role for civil society in the design, implementation and monitoring of projects. this principle of democratic ownership puts citizens at the heart of development and holds the governments of partner countries accountable for their policies. in practical terms, democratic ownership requires territorial development, decentralisation and a strengthening of local democratic structures. that is why i voted in favour of this report, but i cannot but be skeptical about its chances of implementation in the light of the evolution of european policies in this field.

in writing. the neved'alova report opens up avenues of reflection for the evolution of our education systems which convinced me to vote for it. it recalls the need to acquire and master at least one foreign language in a european and globalised context. it draws attention to vulnerable groups and stresses the importance of the role of the school in the integration process, whether in the case of minorities or disabled people. it recommends the implementation of tools and means to ensure lifelong learning. but the heart of this report is the situation of millions of young europeans who are unemployed and have left the training system and who are in urgent need of the youth guarantee, with the means to meet the challenges. i regret, however, that this text advocates the adaptation of training to the needs of enterprises or the labour market. this so-called miracle cure ignores the ever-faster changes in the economic world and the consequent urgent need to provide young people with an education which is sufficiently comprehensive to prepare them for many occupational changes.

in writing. i supported the adoption of the rossi report, which urged the member states of the european union to make efforts to reduce as much as possible the harm suffered by patients when they receive care. while care-associated infections (cas) affect about 5% of hospital patients, the report calls for support for research into the prevention of cas. it also provides extensive training for healthcare staff to prevent these collateral damage. the quality of healthcare and hospital care in europe is one of the highest in the world and must remain so. to this end, intensified cooperation between member states is crucial.
in writing. in this text, parliament calls for patient safety to be made a real priority for the european union: this requires first and foremost better information for patients and rigorous training for healthcare staff. prevention of the risks involved means avoiding considerable hospital costs and, above all, many deaths: it is considered that between 30 and 40% of adverse events in the hospital sector and in the hospital environment are caused by systemic factors, which are therefore preventable! these numbers are shocking, and we have a duty to put an end to them.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report in order to improve patient safety in the union, which still varies considerably from one member state to another. it is estimated that between 30 and 40 per cent of adverse events associated with care are preventable. these adverse events include care-associated infections (cas), which are estimated to affect an average of 5% of hospital patients, or 3.2 million people each year, and directly cause death in 37,000 of them. in addition to the obvious benefit to patients, any investment in patient safety is therefore a potential source of savings. the priority given to patient safety thus leads to a reduction in the costs of caring for patients suffering from adverse events associated with care and, as a result, to a better use of financial and human resources. improvements are needed in both inpatient and outpatient care in terms of training and education on patient safety, in terms of the detection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria and in terms of budgetary and staff resources for patient safety.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report which proposes measures to prevent adverse events in healthcare, such as misdiagnosis, prescribing two medicines that should not be combined or incorrect disinfection of equipment. several studies estimate that 30 to 40 percent of these adverse events could be prevented. we have emphasised the prevention of 'hospital-acquired diseases', which are contracted during care and affect 5% of patients each year in europe. hospital and non-hospital staff should be better trained on these issues. we also asked the member states to strengthen their financial, technological and human resources to prevent such incidents. these investments are all the more necessary as 13% to 16% of hospital costs (i.e. one euro in seven) are due to care-related incidents.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on patient safety, which calls for better training of hospital staff and carers on care-associated infections (cas). in order to improve patient safety, member states could put in place actions to empower citizens and prevent ibs. we need to invest in this area, which could become a more important issue in the future in the context of an ageing european population.
in writing. this report recommends measures to promote patient safety and control care-associated infections. but at the same time it recognises that the european union cannot interfere in the exercise of the member states' competences in the field of health. he tends to favor patient rights. it denounces the effects of the crisis and austerity which leads to a lack of human, financial and technological resources and which undermines the quality of care. but if we agree with all the measures proposed, how can we implement them when europe is imposing an austerity policy on the states with cuts in all budgets, including health? how can the recommendations of this report be implemented when regional health agencies impose reductions in beds, closures of services or hospitals, mergers of hospital centres and staff reductions? i vote in favour of supporting these good intentions.

in writing. i supported this report on the directive on misleading and comparative advertising in business-to-business relations (the provisions on comparative advertising also apply to business-to-consumer relations). it is a balanced report which has the merit of highlighting all the problems facing businesses in this field. the development of fraudulent practices such as 'directory companies' (offering directory-type services as 'free' and then charging companies excessively high rates for these services) is particularly damaging to businesses and must be combated.
in writing. the european parliament has revised a 2006 directive to improve the regulation of misleading and comparative advertising. i voted in favour of this text, which aims to protect professionals better against such practices, in particular those of companies which claim to include companies in directories for free but then charge for their services. companies will be better informed by means of a blacklist of deceptive commercial practices and companies that have been repeatedly convicted of using them. the directive will also strengthen cooperation between the competent national authorities and institutions such as banks, post offices and debt collection agencies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which calls on member states to better enforce the current rules on misleading advertising practices and for additional eu measures to better protect european businesses, especially smes, which are particularly vulnerable to them. the level of protection is not uniform between member states, which creates legal uncertainty in cross-border trade. the report calls for the creation of a national contact point where companies that have been the victims of deceptive practices could report them and obtain information on the remedies available.
in writing. the commission's communication and the jong report highlight a very important problem, which concerns many smes, but also many citizens of the european union. for smes, misleading advertising practices, especially those of directory companies, are a serious problem which member states must combat firmly and cooperate with each other, in particular to identify and define fraudulent practices, but also to list and sanction companies which engage in such practices. since the commission is obsessed with the 'cost-competitiveness' of enterprises, it will find a way to improve it without having to touch the salaries of employees. i am pleased to note that the jong report supports the commission's idea of drawing up a blacklist of deceptive practices and adding a blacklist of companies to it. i am in favour of this solution. more clarity for smes, more cooperation and coordination between member states, more firmness against deceptive practices and companies: i am voting for this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague from the gue/ngl group, cornelis de jong, on misleading advertising practices. misleading advertising practices can take different forms: misleading directory companies (companies filling out seemingly free forms that make them enter into paid contracts without their knowledge), misleading payment forms (companies receiving invoices for fictitious services), etc. the report asked the commission to draw up a blacklist of these unfair practices and a list of companies which had been repeatedly convicted of such acts and possibly even to prohibit them from receiving eu funding and from participating in public procurement procedures. the aim was therefore to encourage member states to cooperate more closely in combating this phenomenon. the report has been adopted and i am glad of that.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, after the vote on the basic regulation of the common fisheries policy a few months ago, we will vote tomorrow on the european maritime and fisheries fund. this fund shall constitute the financial component of the cfp for the period 2014-2020. the emff has a key role to play in ensuring a sustainable fishing model. our priority is the long-term preservation of fish stocks. my report therefore proposes concrete instruments for sustainable fishing, while at the same time allowing the sector to be competitive. some of these proposals are the subject of intense lobbying by ngos. there has been a lot of misinformation about amendment no 587, which concerns the renewal of the fleet and the reduction of capacity. in addition, the european commission has made unacceptable interference by telephone calls to members of parliament. the commission's role is to initiate legislation, but in no way to intervene directly in the parliamentary process and to try to influence the position of members. the commission does indeed propose, madam commissioner, but today, whether you like it or not, it is parliament and the council that decide. these are methods that are unacceptable to the elected representatives of the people that we are. i wanted to tell you. you are free, madam commissioner, not to support some of these proposals, but it is not appropriate to deploy a full battalion of dg mare staff to contact members one by one and urge them to vote against certain amendments. if i may make this remark, this time in a humorous tone: if the commission were to agree to spend on fleet renewal even the amount it has just spent on telephone bills to try to get the principle of renewal rejected, the safety and energy performance of our ships would already be somewhat improved. amendment no 587, which has been widely criticised, proposes to renew fishing vessels over 35 years old on condition that the capacity and fishing effort of the new vessel is 40% lower than that of the old one. i would point out that this only applies to vessels of less than 12 metres in length using the sleeper craft. this instrument will only address fleet segments with overcapacity. this is therefore the only capacity reduction measure in the whole reform of the common fisheries policy. amendment no 586 also proposes to cap aid for fleet renewal and engine replacement at 10% of the emff. this is a practical and reasonable measure to combat overcapacity and overfishing. while some people are content with incantations, i propose strong action for sustainable fishing and conservation of the resource. i would also remind you that 80% of the fishery and aquaculture products we consume in europe are imported products. do we want to be totally dependent on third countries, by eliminating our fishing activity in europe? not as far as i'm concerned. the renewal, as proposed, is a concrete measure for sustainable fishing and also for capacity reduction. what do those who oppose this measure propose? nothing, not at all. i would like to ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to draw the necessary conclusions from the noise of the lobbying against you. the reform of the common fisheries policy must be based on better controls and more robust data collection. the achievement of maximum sustainable yield requires a better knowledge of fish stocks. to achieve this, i therefore urge you to support the amendments which increase the resources allocated to controls and data collection. as you know, the new common fisheries policy provides for an obligation to land all catches. it is necessary to provide for intervention by the emff to significantly limit such discards. the emphasis will therefore have to be on the selectivity of fishing gear. it is also important to help fishermen and ports to make the necessary arrangements for the storage and treatment of any unwanted catches. it is the duty of the union to facilitate the implementation of zero emissions, including through public support. my report is in line with that. the reform of the common fisheries policy is also based on management plans and conservation measures. the emff has an important role to play in enabling these measures to be implemented effectively. i therefore ask you to support the amendments introducing biological rest periods and temporary stops. they are the key to sustainable fishing, which safeguards stocks and sustains the industry. ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow's vote will be an opportunity to promote a sustainable fishing model for the next ten years. for me, sustainable fishing is not just about wishful thinking and good feelings. sustainable fishing is above all about taking concrete measures to eliminate overfishing and to control the capacity of the fleet while allowing fishermen to make a living from their trade. i ask you to be pragmatic and responsible and to reject dogmatic considerations which will lead us nowhere. commissioner, in conclusion, i would like to express my disappointment at the fish love exhibition in brussels on monday. do you think that showing celebrities posing nude with fish will help us fight overfishing? my colleagues, the mass communication campaign of the so-called fish lovers is just a smokescreen to hide their lack of proposals. tomorrow, vote for sustainable fishing, vote against overfishing, vote for my report!
