president of the commission. − madam president, this week’s european council has a very broad agenda: the digital economy, innovation, services, youth unemployment, financing of the economy, regulatory fitness, emu and economic governance, emu and the social dimension, the banking union, eastern partnership and migration. my main message to the european council tomorrow is that, over the next weeks and months, the european union can – and must – achieve concrete results in all these areas. many of our initiatives can be brought to a successful conclusion even before this house rises ahead of next may’s elections. but i will make it clear that we can only deliver if there is the necessary political will among our member states. just yesterday, as you know, the commission approved a very substantial working programme for 2014. so there is a lot to do. the thematic focus of tomorrow’s european council will be on innovation and the digital agenda. digital services, telecommunications, e-government and skills are the drivers of tomorrow’s growth and productivity. even in the crisis, this is a sector that has continued to show growth potential, and we predict there will be nearly one million ict job vacancies unfilled in the coming years. this is unacceptable, given the level of youth unemployment that we face. this is why the commission has launched the grand coalition for digital jobs, a multi-stakeholder partnership to exploit the employment potential of ict. we need a thriving digital sector to drive all other parts of our economy, and the internal market for telecoms has to be at the heart of this programme. we must urgently address the underlying shortcomings and create the right environment for investment. there is now a major reform package for the telecoms sector on the table. let us all make maximum progress on this file by the end of this legislature. this package complements a number of important recent proposals on the completion of the digital single market, for example on reducing the cost of deploying high-speed broadband networks, on е-invoicing in public procurement, on cyber-security and on electronic identification and trust services for electronic transactions. these, too, are in your and the council’s hands, and i hope the european council will throw its weight behind the call to finalise them in the months to come. we need to build this digital single market in a manner that is consistent with our european values. that includes making sure that those who operate in the online world do not escape from fair taxation. the commission is actively working on a series of measures to fight against tax evasion in general, working with the g8, g20 and oecd. but there are some specific challenges which are posed by new digital business models which existing tax policies may not yet fully address. this is why the commission decided yesterday to set up an expert group on taxation in the digital economy, which will report by next summer. core european values, namely the respect of fundamental rights, including the right to privacy and security, also matter just as much on-line as off-line. recent disclosures concerning surveillance activities have cast a shadow on european union citizens’ trust. we need to combine the digital agenda with a better framework for the protection of data and privacy rights. trust in the data-driven economy has to be restored, not only in order to re-establish much-needed confidence but also for its potential impact on growth. i therefore strongly welcome this week’s vote in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs of this parliament, lending its strong support to the commission’s proposals. i want to thank parliament for the priority which it attaches to this file. we should do all we can to conclude this much-needed modernisation and strengthening of the eu data protection rules before the end of this legislature. the other thematic priority for this european council will be research and innovation. the evidence is there: member states that have continued to invest in innovation have fared better in the current crisis than those that have not. we will need to increase our efforts – public and private – to keep up with international competition. international investors are now finding their way to europe, but business research and development expenditure in the eu is far below that of our main competitors. the crisis has also taken its toll, with a decrease in public spending on r&d in 2011. europe is lagging behind, in particular in fast-growing markets and high tech. if no action is taken, the eu may miss out again on fast-growing markets linked to the technologies which tackle societal challenges. the commission has recently launched an indicator of innovation output to focus attention on the right r&d policies. but additional investment in r&d makes no sense without critical structural reforms of national research and innovation systems. the commission will continue to push for reforms to create a true european research area. we must enable the mobility of researchers and provide open access to publicly-funded research results and transnational access to research infrastructures. creating the right business environment is also key to stimulating growth. this is why the commission is removing unnecessary burdens on business across all policy areas. the commission has, since 2005, repealed 5 590 legal acts and reduced the administrative burden by eur 32.3 billion, and we are determined to go further. in our communication on regulatory fitness (refit), we have just launched a programme to further simplify legislation. we plan to withdraw some pending proposals and repeal existing laws which no longer serve their purpose. we act where action is needed at european level. we should not act where it can be done better at national or sub-national level. at the european council tomorrow i will be looking for a strong endorsement of the refit programme. but let me be clear: this is not about calling into question established policy goals, nor should it be a battle of competences between brussels and national capitals. this is about finding the right balance for using existing competences in full respect of subsidiarity and proportionality. i also expect member states to cut red tape at their level and avoid ‘gold plating’ eu legislation by adding new national burdens to european rules. this brings us, honourable members, to another issue i have repeatedly stressed in this house, as well as in the european council: financing the economy. this remains one of the biggest bottlenecks in the european economy. even with growth returning, confidence and pre-crisis lending patterns will not return quickly. we need to unblock the flow of credit and help businesses, especially smes. frankly, i am disappointed that the member states are not more ambitious here, and i will say this tomorrow to the european council. in some countries, the european union budget will be by far the most important source of public investment over the next few years. these funds will help kick-start private funding as well. this is key to future growth. the preparations for the next mff have come a very long way, but we are not yet there. we need a final push from all concerned in order to conclude. this is of the utmost importance and urgency for many of our member states and many of our regions. without the budget of the european union, they will simply not be able to invest, because they have no fiscal space to do so. i can assure you that the commission will continue to do its utmost to facilitate a fair and balanced outcome between the european parliament and the council – an outcome which is as close as possible to the commission’s level of ambition, something i know parliament shares. honourable members, you know that, together with the eib, we have also looked into other, alternative instruments for financing the economy, including forms of risk-sharing by pooling and leveraging parts of eu funds and eib loans. i will call upon member states to bring forward concrete pledges and to go beyond the status quo. we are not asking governments to renounce part of their funds, we are asking member states to increase the effect of the funds – including for the benefit of smes, which suffer the most from the fragmentation of europe’s credit markets. equally important in our comprehensive crisis response is that we move forward on the road to a deep and genuine economic and monetary union. in this sense, the european council is an intermediate step towards decisions in december, but every step is necessary. completing the banking union, in particular, is the single most significant and important advance we can make to end the unfair distortions of lending conditions in financial markets. so it must remain our absolute priority for the euro area. i congratulate the co-legislators on the final approval of the single supervisory mechanism. now we have to find a final agreement on the directive on bank recovery and resolution and a political agreement in council on the single resolution mechanism by the end of the year. our goal must be to conclude negotiations with this house in the spring. i want to thank the european parliament for its efforts and the hard work that has been done to prepare its position for these discussions. we also need to pay attention to the balance sheet assessment and forthcoming stress test exercise in the banking sector. the commission will support the european central bank and european banking authority in any way possible in that important work. we also expect member states to do their own work in terms of ensuring the availability of any necessary backstops in line with state aid rules if private solutions are not adequate, and in terms of the full cooperation of national supervisors, to bring this exercise to fruition. we have made significant progress as regards economic governance in the eu, in particular as regards the country-specific recommendations, which are the end-point of the european semester. but we must continue our efforts to strengthen economic policy coordination, in particular, within the euro area. we must make further progress on identifying the policy areas which require coordination, including ex-ante coordination. on the other hand, the implementation of the country-specific recommendations is not yet optimal. this is also due to insufficient ownership by each member state of the recommendations which are addressed to them. the widening of these to the social and employment dimensions will surely contribute to enhancing ownership. as you know, the commission has presented a communication on the social dimension of economic and monetary union. one of the core proposals is stronger surveillance of employment and social challenges and policy coordination. the role of the european parliament is crucial in this regard. the commission will cooperate with parliament to select the indicators for the alert mechanism report and will discuss with it the new scoreboard of key social and employment indicators. the commission intends to make use of those indicators in the forthcoming alert mechanism report. moreover, in the annual growth survey – to be adopted by the middle of next month – the commission will present a first overview of the implementation of the country-specific recommendations. we will spare no effort in making the european semester the real tool for economic coordination in the european union. we must also step up our efforts to fight against youth unemployment. as you know, in june the commission proposed the frontloading of the social funds so that the initial eur six billion is invested in the first two years. adopting the necessary regulations is a matter of urgency and of concern. we are approaching the programming period. the member states, with the support of the commission, are in the process of finalising the design of the the rapporteur. - madam president, i would like to inform my colleagues that the adoption of the commission's proposal as amended allows the committee on fisheries to start negotiations with the council immediately.
in writing. in the fight against drug trafficking, i voted in favour of this draft legislative resolution which will make it possible to deal more responsively and effectively with the trade in drug precursors between the eu and third countries. drug precursors are legal products that are used in the manufacture of drugs, through their trade and therefore subject to controls when exported to prevent diversion of these products by drug traffickers. the draft amends the european commission's proposal which organises this control and which determines in particular which substances are controlled.
in writing. drug precursors are legal substances, sometimes used in the manufacture of illicit drugs. they are subject to import and export controls, but medicines are currently exempt. yet, some drugs are misused to make drugs. the text aims to pay particular attention to the medicinal products concerned by establishing specific monitoring. this is an important step towards a stronger fight against illicit drugs in the eu.
in writing. drug precursors are legal substances used in the manufacture of drugs. two substances in particular, ephedrine and pseudo-ephedrine, which are found in medicines to treat colds, are very easily extracted and used by drug traffickers to make methamphetamine. the commission has therefore decided to extend the scope of the measures to include medicinal products containing ephedrine and pseudo-ephedrine. the fight against drug trafficking requires constant vigilance and responsiveness on the part of the european union and its member states. by cutting off drug traffickers' access to their key ingredients for drug manufacture, the union will help tackle this problem at its source more effectively.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am in favour of strengthening the fight against the illicit use of ephedrine for the manufacture of drugs. given the scale of this phenomenon, the union needs to put in place appropriate legislation. i therefore support the idea that any export of medicinal products containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine should be preceded by a pre-export notification sent by the competent authorities of the union to the competent authorities of the country of destination, as is already the case for other substances.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague, mr franck proust, which aims to establish surveillance and control of certain legal substances used in the manufacture of drugs when they are exported, imported or in transit with third countries. in order to limit the risk of circumvention of the legislation, rapid intervention and temporary surveillance clauses have also been introduced. i welcome the wide adoption of this report, with 583 votes in favour, 58 against and 39 abstentions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on trade in drug precursors between the community and third countries, which lays down rules for the surveillance of substances which are legal but used in the manufacture of drugs. the text provides for the extension of temporary surveillance to new substances and introduces some flexibility to adapt to new trends in the diversion of these substances. a rapid response mechanism would also allow authorities to seize consignments where there is sufficient suspicion of diversion.
in writing. this report proposes to fill a legal gap in the regulation laying down rules for the monitoring of trade in drug precursors between the european union and third countries. these precursors have a variety of lawful uses (medicinal, cosmetic, etc.) and are legally marketed. but some of these substances can also be diverted from the legal distribution channels and used for the manufacture of narcotics. the proposal therefore aims to impose stricter controls on these products and to improve border controls on them. the report's merit is that it targets traffickers before consumers. the commission is also proposing to establish a european database containing information on seizures and interceptions. i vote for it.
in writing. in order to encourage the fight against drug trafficking, in particular the diversion of drug precursors, i.e. those substances which, like acetic anhydride, are used in the manufacture of amphetamines, cocaine and heroin, i voted in favour of this draft legislative resolution. the commission is proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the legislative resolution also seeks to strengthen certain elements of the commission proposal, particularly with regard to data protection.
in writing. i supported the hedh report which aims to counter the diversion of chemicals from legal distribution channels. the union's drug policy is a priority. it considered that the monitoring and control of trade in chemicals which could be used for the manufacture of drugs should be strengthened. acetic anhydride is the main precursor to heroin. i therefore welcome the report's proposal to impose compulsory registration with the competent authorities on operators who market acetic anhydride, but also on users who hold it for their own use.
in writing. drug precursors are legal substances that are sometimes misused to produce illicit drugs. in adopting this text, we envisage the introduction of a stricter regulatory framework, paying particular attention to the collection of data and the registration of drug precursors. this is a breakthrough in the european fight against drugs.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am in favour of strengthening the fight against the illicit diversion of acetic anhydride for the manufacture of heroin. i believe that it is legitimate to impose registration requirements on the end users of this substance, as well as on the operators who market it. i think this is a coherent measure to prevent drug trafficking, and in particular the manufacture of heroin in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague anna hedh, which aims to prevent the diversion of intra-eu trade in products used for the manufacture of heroin. the text will lead to an obligation to register users of substances and to greater harmonisation of the provisions on such registration. i welcome the adoption of this report by a very large majority of 575 votes in favour, 34 against and 54 abstentions.
in writing. drug precursors are substances used by the chemical and pharmaceutical industries and also used in illicit drugs, such as ephedrine used to produce amphetamines or pmks used in ecstasy. drug traffickers are constantly inventing new ways to circumvent the very strict regulations governing the trade in these products, for example by setting up shell companies. the european parliament has therefore updated the legislation to take account of innovations by traffickers, without preventing legitimate economic operators from trading in these products. i voted in favour of this text because it strengthens the european union's capacity to combat drug trafficking. member states will be able to seize medicinal products if there is suspicion of illicit use. a european database on shipments and seizures of goods will be created. finally, a rapid response mechanism will enable the european commission and the member states to take account of the new diversionary tactics used by traffickers as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report to combat drug trafficking, in particular heroin. one chemical is acetic anhydride, which is used as a precursor in the manufacture of heroin and which 75% of seizures worldwide reveal to have been manufactured in europe. it is essential to remedy this situation. if precursors are manufactured for legal use, as in the case of pharmaceuticals, we must prevent their diversion to the drug trade and thus strengthen control of this trade. the registration of operators selling anhydride should be harmonised at european level, and the registration of users should be made compulsory in order to better control this market.
in writing. the diversion of chemicals from the legal trade chain to the illicit production of drugs is a phenomenon we must combat. the monitoring of transactions through clear registration authorisation requirements may be the means. however, the establishment of a european-wide database, the purpose of which is not clearly established, is highly questionable. this is all the more so as the types of personal data that may be processed and stored in the european database represent the traditional risk in this area. this is particularly so as the procedures for informing, accessing, correcting, deleting and blocking the data processed in that database are left to the discretion of the commission by means of delegated acts. i'm not going to.

in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the action plan on e-justice 2014-2020 presented by the european commission. we welcomed the role of the e-justice portal launched in 2010, which aims to make justice and the legal system more accessible to citizens, as well as to improve cooperation between practitioners and member states' administrations. e-justice systems reduce the cost of judicial and administrative procedures, in particular through the automation of the exchange of information, the distribution of official documents and the translation of certain procedural documents. we have highlighted the potential of e-justice to facilitate the use of certain european instruments, such as the european order for payment procedure or the european criminal records information system (ecris). the provision of multilingual standard forms could also facilitate administrative procedures. i voted in favour of this text, which sends a positive signal for the continuation of european work on the subject of e-justice.

action programme, and i look forward to that. this is a very great success for parliament, which fought to bring this programme into being. this programme sets out the broad guidelines for european environmental policy up to 2020, with nine priority objectives and a set of concrete commitments to improve the state of the environment in europe and worldwide. today, the challenges remain: pressure on natural resources, degradation of ecosystems, energy consumption, air and soil pollution, waste - especially marine waste - health risks and climate change. in my report and throughout the negotiations, i have been committed to advocating an environmental policy which is both ambitious and realistic in the face of the difficult economic environment and international challenges. first, i called for a high level of protection of natural capital and biodiversity, in line with my longstanding commitment to forests, seas and oceans, endangered species like bees, and protected species like wolves. in these times of economic crisis and austerity, emphasising environmental policy might seem secondary. but it's not. environmental action does have costs, but it also has benefits which public finances and private investors cannot ignore in the present period. this is why environmental concerns should no longer be the adjustment variable, but should be integrated very early on into the various sectoral policies. by proposing an overall scheme, this programme is presented as the founding act of a european green new deal, bringing greener growth and creating jobs. this new deal is ground. the communication of the union on its environmental policy will also have to be reviewed. more education is needed. i shall end with the international aspects. it was important to recognise in in writing. this report rejects the council's proposal for the 2014 union budget. the council's position is dictated by the austerity which applies throughout the union under the tscg treaty. the 2014 budget is being discussed even though the multiannual budgetary plan for 2014-2020, which is mandatory, has not been adopted by parliament. in concrete terms, the budget proposed by the council provides for a 6% reduction in appropriations compared to 2013. all programmes would be concerned: research funds, investment and regional aid, social funds, including those for the most deprived, etc. the new budgetary resources for young people announced by mr hollande and mrs merkel for 2014 are non-existent. the 2007-2013 payment delays are considerable: 52% of the 2014 budget appropriations would cover unpaid payments from the 2007-2013 period! austerity is thus synonymous with mismanagement. this resolution has the merit of rejecting the council's disastrous position. but the rapporteurs are in fact aligning themselves with the budget proposal originally proposed by the commission, which is insufficient. the european parliament should have a completely different general interest ambition for the revival of ecological activity and planning in europe. i'm not going to participate in that decision.
in writing. taking into account the new financial perspective for the years 2014-2020 and the public finance crisis, i voted in favour of this budget, which is 6% lower than in 2013. the budget will therefore amount to €142 billion for 500 million citizens (or about €280 per person), representing 1% of european gdp. of this 142 billion, 94% will be redistributed to the member states for regional development, agricultural policy, youth employment, erasmus, research and innovation, etc. despite a shrinking budget, the states are asking the eu for more and more - to control the borders, to invest for growth, to help the poorest - without giving it the means to do so, and then, finally, to criticize its inaction as was the case with the lampedusa tragedy. unfortunately, this inconsistency is creating confusion and disorder and fuelling a growing euroscepticism.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the "general draft of the european union for the financial year 2014 - all sections" i voted against subsidies for farmers who raise bulls for the sole purpose of making a spectacle of them. i think that giving public money to a bull farm that will be used only for bullfighting or bullfighting is not acceptable. these bloody spectacles, which only a small part of the population enjoys, should not be able to benefit from european subsidies. as vice-president of the intergroup on animal welfare, i am campaigning for a total ban on bullfighting and, in general, all acts of cruelty to animals. supporters of bullfighting consider it part of european culture and heritage! so why fund this heinous practice with money that's dedicated to agriculture? in addition, in this report i voted to restore the appropriations for the european fund for aid to the most deprived to eur 500 million, which the governments wanted to reduce to eur 365 million for the years 2014-2020.
in writing. the resolution seeks to justify the so-called arms race with the council on budgetary issues, in particular the 2014 budget. in this text, the european parliament attempts to bridge the gap between the defence of austerity measures and the defence of a budget which makes it possible to continue pursuing the various community policies. the european parliament says it 'cannot accept the council's decision to reduce the commitment appropriations and payment appropriations'. that is a positive statement that we can only endorse. however, there is a certain hypocrisy in this from a european parliament whose majority of members vote for the six pack, the two pack, the european semester, etc. - that is to say, all the elements of the european legal arsenal aimed at imposing budget cuts and 'structural reforms'. in this report, the european parliament is mired in its own contradictions. so i decided not to.
in writing. this report is the culmination of the european commission's green paper calling for a better understanding of the marine environment by 2020. the aim here is to make the most of the new technologies available in order to obtain the most comprehensive picture of the state of the natural resources and the marine environment as a whole. i voted in favour of the report, convinced that better information will help us to protect the marine environment.
in writing. i voted in favour of the patrão neves own-initiative report on the need to institutionalize a european marine observation and data transmission network (emodnet). at european level, achieving a digital mapping of the seabed would enable better management of fisheries resources. through close cooperation between the member states of the union and thus through the wide dissemination of knowledge on the marine environment, this report is in line with the objectives set by the new common fisheries policy and its financing component, the european maritime and fisheries fund.
in writing. to become involved in sustainable fisheries, data on the seabed must be better collected, transmitted and centralised as far as possible by 2020. currently owned by a large number of stakeholders, it is essential to have a comprehensive understanding of and easy access to the public. the aim is to reconcile two fundamental pillars of our action: raising awareness among europeans and protecting our marine environment, for the benefit of the economy, europeans, fishermen and the environment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which will help to stimulate the ambitious project proposed by the european commission, which is the development of an accessible and sustainable digital map of the european seabed. it is important to work with member states to identify the means and mechanisms available to develop our knowledge of the marine environment for the benefit of industry, public authorities, researchers and society. strengthening our knowledge of the marine environment is a step forward in the european union's project to foster the growth of a sustainable 'blue economy' that creates jobs in the marine and maritime sectors. this will enhance our competitiveness and the efficiency of our industry in these areas.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague mario do ceu patrao neves, which sets out how the fisheries sector could contribute to and benefit from the european digital underwater map project to be completed by 2020. the report focuses on the importance of sharing and disseminating information, while ensuring the validity of sources and the availability of data. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. − knowledge of the marine environment is of fundamental importance for promoting and developing the 'blue economy' and expanding oceanographic knowledge, and also contributing to the achievement of the 'europe 2020' objectives for the sea. improving oceanographic knowledge through the development of a continuous multi-resolution digital map of the european seabed will facilitate the use of resources for sustainable, targeted and inclusive growth for all actors such as public authorities and industry, education and research.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a report in response to the european commission's proposal to develop a digital map of the european seabed by 2020. the report stresses the importance of collecting and disseminating data on the seabed, which are currently held by a multitude of institutions, in a dispersed and fragmented manner. the european union must make this data accessible to a wide audience in order to encourage resource conservation, innovation and job creation in the marine and maritime sectors. this map will contain information on fishing activities, including areas subject to higher fishing intensity, species fished and catch volumes. i voted in favour of this text because i believe that more accurate information on the seabed will enable us to better manage fisheries resources and preserve fragile marine ecosystems.
in writing. i voted in favour of the marine knowledge report 2020 following the european commission's communication which stresses the need to unlock the economic potential of marine observations in order to foster sustainable economic growth and job creation. the issue of data processing and use is important in developing an effective tool, and data should be standardised and controlled for effective use.
in writing. this report proposes to create a map of the european seabed by bringing together data that has hitherto been fragmented and disciplines that do not or only little exchange. this will allow for better knowledge of marine environments and fisheries resources, which is necessary for better protection of the ecosystem in general and of vulnerable areas in particular. this map will be public. the considerable contribution of the internet to the dissemination and sharing of knowledge is beyond dispute. the collection, synthesis and networking of scientific and fisheries data that this report promotes is an approach that i support. however, as is often the case with the commission, there is a very wide gap between intentions and applications. the current urgent task is to establish a european register of fishing vessels and to improve the control of catch declarations by each member state. otherwise, fishermen in the states which comply with the declarations will be penalised to the benefit of fishermen and states which conceal their sampling. that reservation does not prevent me from voting for what will remain a breakthrough in knowledge.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation will enable the european union to enforce its rights when unfair or illegal trade measures are taken in a third country. with this text, the european union will be able to react much more quickly and strongly. given the importance of this text, i supported the rapporteur, including his request to launch negotiations with the union's council of ministers immediately so that an agreement can be reached as soon as possible and the union's trade policy can be strengthened quickly.
in writing. the european union needs a more responsive, more coherent and better representative trade policy for european businesses, especially smes. reciprocity should be the rule in business relations. as the wto notes a rise in trade restrictive measures by most of the union's trading partners, including emerging countries, it is imperative that europe also has the means to enforce its rights. the union has not always been able to take the rebalancing measures to which it had access under international trade agreements. this instrument will enable it to better enforce its rights, through more systematic recourse to the wto dispute settlement mechanism and the possibility of countering unfair trade practices. if used properly, it should help to make the union's trade relations with these partners more balanced.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is essential to ensure that the european union's rights under international trade agreements are respected. an effective legislative instrument seems legitimate in order to meet the requirements of the lisbon treaty, which calls for the establishment of a european framework for the implementation of the common commercial policy. reciprocity must be a non-negotiable precondition for any agreement between the european union and a third country. it is unacceptable that our european companies should be penalized in any way by the conclusion of international trade agreements.
in writing. i supported this report. the commission has put forward a proposal for a regulation laying down rules on how the european union would enforce and defend its rights in the event of unfair or illegal trade measures taken in a third country. to enforce its rights, the eu takes a case-by-case approach, with regulations adopted by the council on the basis of a commission proposal. in order to comply with the lisbon treaty, these regulations follow the ordinary legislative procedure and union action could lose in effectiveness and credibility. the initiative therefore aims to provide the union with a single legislative instrument enabling it to defend its interests in a rapid, efficient and flexible manner in order to encourage offending countries to put an end to illegal behaviour. the report was adopted by 573 votes to 25, with 79 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. i would like to stress in particular the novelty which the european parliament has proposed in the area of the application and observance of international trade rules, namely the possibility for the commission to target goods coming from a member state which does not comply with its obligations arising from a decision of the specialised bodies of the organisation and to also target the services of the country which commits the infringement.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the application and enforcement of international trade rules, which establishes rules enabling the european union to defend itself against unfair or illegal trade measures taken in a third country. it is important that the union should have such a legal instrument in order to discourage infringing countries from continuing their practices.
in writing. this draft regulation illustrates the hypocrisy of the 'europe that protects'. officially, this is to facilitate the procedure for the european union to take trade retaliatory measures. it would be urgent to put an end to the guilty laissez-faire of the european liberals. but the spirit of the text is only to counter the states which do not respect free trade agreements by strengthening the commission's autonomy to decide retaliation. the commission's ultraliberal approach makes it possible to doubt the meaning of this initiative. it can be seen as a way of preventing states from protecting themselves in their own interests. as for co2 emissions from vehicles, or the solar panel industry, the commission will be following the most influential country: germany. the rapporteur's arguments betray the thinking of the eurocrats: 'the mere existence of this regulation already constitutes a credible threat and it is to be hoped that it will dissuade our trading partners from breaking the rules of the game', so as not to have 'the slightest protectionist purpose'! we want to build a solidarity protectionism so that free trade is replaced by cooperation and relocation. this text is part of a project that is totally opposite. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff). with a budget of eur 6.5 billion, the fund is the financial component of the reform of the common fisheries policy for 2014-2020. given the depletion of marine resources, it was important that european financial means did not support unsustainable fishing methods. i have therefore opposed funding for fleet renewal and supported initiatives to improve data collection. this legislative package will help to steer the european union towards a sustainable fisheries policy that is resource-based, while at the same time offering fishermen the necessary opportunities to adapt their activities.
in writing. by adopting my report, parliament is giving our fishing model a future. the emff will not be an instrument for the conversion of fishermen out of fishing as proposed by the european commission. on the contrary, it will promote access for young people to the fishing industry by providing assistance for the establishment of such a sector. it will also allow, under certain conditions, the replacement of engines for lower consumption and co2 emissions. the emff as adopted by parliament gives fishermen the means to implement the reform of the common fisheries policy in the context of sustainable fisheries. my report provides for financial resources to strengthen the selectivity of fishing gear. it is used to finance periods of biological rest, to support temporary stops in the event of conservation measures and to increase the resources allocated to monitoring and data collection. the adoption of my report is an undeniable success for the conservation of fisheries resources and for the competitiveness of the sector. i will defend these principles in the negotiations with the council.
in writing. this fund is intended to enable european fishermen to face global competition, which is unfair in economic and social terms and which today leads to the import of more than 60% of the seafood we consume. yet, despite these advances, there is still a regret. we cannot demand changes in the fishing industry without renewing the working tool, that is to say the vessel. and we can renew the fleet without increasing fishing capacity. to improve economic efficiency, safety, selectivity to avoid discharges, to equip ships with less polluting propulsion systems, public aid is needed. until proven otherwise, the free global market is not a tool for implementing european policies, let alone a food policy. market forces will not help old ships to become models of selectivity. i am in favour of public aid when it contributes to europe's prosperity and not to its decline. i would continue to fight for the european union to help this activity to be renewed and preserved.
in writing. the european maritime and fisheries fund is a key instrument for financing the common fisheries policy, and the rapporteur's proposals were in the right direction, towards sustainable fisheries and support for european fishermen, especially those working in small structures. i welcome the fact that measures have been taken to improve data collection, which will enable us to know more about the state of the resource and to adapt our actions as much as possible.
in writing. today, over 88% of fish stocks in europe are overfished. the european maritime and fisheries fund must help to put an end to this problem and enable the sector to move towards sustainable fishing that respects the resources that the oceans offer. it is crucial for the balance of the seas and for the balance of fisheries itself (especially small-scale, artisanal and coastal fishing) to allow the renewal of resources. these are common goods which everyone must preserve. the money of european taxpayers must not be used to finance the renewal of vessels, which would lead to overfishing and depletion of stocks. this strategy also requires that we give ourselves the means to control its implementation. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to provide the necessary financial support to the fisheries sector. fishermen in the outermost regions, who face geographical realities radically different from those of continental europe, have not been forgotten by this reform. the new emff will double their allocation for fisheries and will help fishermen in their local development strategies.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is important to provide the european union with a european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) which would give rise to a realistic fisheries policy. this means reducing fishing capacity, while guaranteeing the activity of our fishermen. i particularly welcome the european desire to support young fishermen.
in writing. we voted in favour of the european fisheries funding programme for the period 2014-2020. this fund (emff) constitutes the financial component of the cfp. this instrument is essential if sustainable european fisheries are to be effectively established. i did not support mr cadec's proposal because it jeopardises the possibility of a truly sustainable fishery! some of our proposals, such as increasing the funds allocated to research and control and not reintroducing subsidies for fleet renewal, have been accepted. but the ambitious reform of the cfp recently adopted by the ep risks being jeopardised. instead of ending overfishing, the majority of meps preferred to allocate these funds to practices that are in conflict with the sustainability of the cfp. in particular, they have reintroduced direct funds to encourage new fishing capacity, in other words: we increase the capacity of catches (e.g. more efficient engines), which should be reduced without creating jobs. this fund was supposed to ensure responsible european fisheries, the protection of marine biodiversity and the future of fishermen, but this may not be the case.
in writing. as we know, fish stocks in our seas are dwindling, threatening the livelihoods of certain species and the activity of our fishermen. the european fund we have just approved aims to move our fisheries towards a more sustainable model which respects the resources of the sea, and i welcome this. we have recently adopted the principle of small-scale coastal fishing. this fund validates this vision by making it possible to combat illegal fishing more effectively, by promoting the renewal of a more sustainable fleet and by enabling fishermen to better comply with the ban on discards. the fund will also help young fishermen to settle in the community, provided they purchase a small-scale or coastal fishing vessel. this is a measure to build the future that i welcome.
in writing. concerned about the protection of small-scale fisheries, i voted in favour of this report, which makes it possible to preserve fish stocks while ensuring the future of our fishermen. the european fund will provide eur 6.3 billion for a new common fisheries policy. it should help finance more modern engines for the fishing fleet, safer and less polluting boats. by making aid conditional on vessels' capacity being limited, it will help to ensure that fish stocks are renewed. the emff also provides for increased support for data collection, assistance for the settlement of young fishermen engaged in sustainable fishing, and an ambitious social component to improve the living and working conditions of fishermen.
in writing. although it is not entirely satisfactory, i spoke in favour of the emff, considering that this fund must first enable european fishermen to face unfair global competition, economically and socially, which today leads us to import more than 60% of the seafood we consume. i have therefore supported public aid for the renewal of vessels, because it is essential to promote changes in fishing which are required at european level. the aid must therefore improve economic efficiency, safety, selectivity in avoiding discharges and equip vessels with less polluting propulsion systems. finally, i supported an approach which, unlike the commission's proposals, which were more about encouraging the profession to change, encouraged fishermen to look to the future with confidence.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the report by my colleague, mr alain cadec, on the european maritime and fisheries fund. after 18 months of difficult negotiations, this report reflects a good balance between the desire to ensure the survival of an entire sector weakened by the crisis and the need to guarantee sustainable fisheries with respect for ecosystems. to help fishermen stay in this highly competitive sector, europe will allocate €6.5 billion for the period 2014-2020. this will enable fishermen who work in very difficult conditions and whose courage is to be commended to pass on their knowledge to the new generations through the aid for installation. the conservation of fisheries resources is another priority which, beyond the environmental imperative, will enable fishermen to continue their activity in the coming decades with the financing of biological rest periods and the increase in the resources allocated to monitoring and data collection.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague alain cadec on the european maritime and fisheries fund, which is the financial component of the common fisheries policy. the report aims to ensure sustainable, competitive and social fisheries by introducing conservation measures, diversifying fishermen's income and enforcing compliance with social legislation. i regret, however, the rejection of the only instrument for reducing fishing capacity, which made aid for the renewal of small-scale fishing vessels in fleets with overcapacity conditional on reducing their fishing capacity and energy consumption.
in writing. the european parliament has approved a budget of €6.5 billion for the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) 2014-2020, which is the financial component of the reform of the common fisheries policy. i voted in favour of this text which will allow the development of a sustainable and competitive fishery. the new european fund will support small-scale fishing, innovation and diversification of fishermen's activities. aid for the replacement of vessels over 35 years old will be granted for small-scale fishing vessels (less than 12 metres in length and not using trawls). this replacement should result in a 40% reduction in the vessel's capacity, fishing effort and energy consumption. we have also improved social standards and provided assistance for the establishment of young fishermen. finally, we have taken measures to preserve stocks, with priority given to the elimination of discards at sea and to strengthening data collection and controls. finally, the rules of the emff have been aligned with those of the other european funds, which will simplify the management of the fund and increase the coherence of the european union's action.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the rules of the european maritime and fisheries fund. the €6.5 billion fund will help fishermen implement the fisheries reform adopted at european level for sustainable fisheries. european aid will be used to modernise the engines of vessels which will have to be less powerful, to install young fishermen, and to collect and manage fisheries data, among other things.
in writing. the launch of a european market in fishing rights was the black spot of the reform of the common fisheries policy. this parliament report revises this and removes the possibility of selling and buying fishing quotas (transferable fishing concessions). that is a decisive positive point. the commission has also proposed that the emff should provide financial support to fishermen during the periods of biological rest necessary for the reproduction of species and support for young fishermen to help them establish themselves. that's good. the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity. it proposes to reintroduce the possibility of financing renewal. this will help small fishermen to reduce fuel consumption and improve working conditions. but this was only acceptable if it was accompanied by a safeguard against the race to productivism. the text does this by making funding conditional on a reduction in fishing effort. aid to small-scale fishing should have been better described. however, the key points that are favourable to the fishery resource and to the fishermen are included. i vote for it.
in writing. this €6.5 billion european fisheries fund closes the financial part of the reform of our common fisheries policy (cfp). with our vote, this fund will make concrete the ambitious reforms achieved in the regulatory area of maximum fishing yield, which reflect our desire to ensure a transition to sustainable fishing. our first victory is that we have contributed to a greater fight against overfishing. we have prevented a massive renewal of the fishing fleet from becoming a real disaster for jobs and fish stocks, by drastically reducing the number of crew on board and increasing fishing capacity in coastal areas already heavily overfished. i am also proud that we voted for an increase in the funds allocated to data collection and monitoring of cfp compliance, which were largely inadequate. these funds will make it possible to calculate efficiently the maximum yield required by the new cfp, in order to maintain the size of the fish stock at its maximum productivity, as well as to ensure compliance with the cfp, which is far from the case today.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague alain cadec on the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff). with a budget of €6.5 billion, the fund will be the financial arm of the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) for the period 2014-2020. the appropriations will enable fishermen to comply with the ban on the discharge of unwanted fish into the sea, to improve safety and working conditions, to collect better data on stocks and to adapt port infrastructures. the text also allows the removal, replacement and modernisation of boat engines, provided that the new engine is at least 40% less powerful than the engine being replaced. the report also proposes that the eu should help young fishermen under the age of 35 by granting them a subsidy of eur 100 000 when they buy a small-scale fishing vessel. this fund will help to limit overfishing while maintaining sustainable jobs in the maritime sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff), which provides the common fisheries policy with more than eur 6 billion for the years 2014-2020. in europe, fish stocks are becoming scarcer. it is clear that our fleet is overcapacitated: there are too many fishing vessels taking too much fish from the ocean to replenish stocks. i therefore voted against the provisions for public aid for the renewal of the fleet which were proposed in this report. on the contrary, i believe that the funds provided should be used to strengthen controls against illegal fishing, to finance scientific research programmes to improve knowledge of the marine world and to finance effective data collection to enable us to know the evolution of fish stocks. as a general rule, i voted in favour of the european maritime fund so that it can enable the european union to achieve its transition to sustainable fishing and to achieve its objective of restoring fish stocks.
in writing. the vote on the emff represents a major step forward, giving fishermen confidence in the future of their profession. it shows that it is possible to reconcile sustainable fishing without condemning the fishermen. the community must be able to take action to combat this scourge. by voting for the cadec report, we are sending a strong signal to a sector in crisis. i particularly welcome the adoption of the provisions for the outermost regions. the emff recognises the obvious, our fishermen face different geographical realities than their continental european colleagues. i welcome the increase of over 150% in the budget for the overseas departments and the measures to allocate part of the funds to supporting fishermen in their local development strategies. finally, i welcome the introduction of funding for the fish concentration scheme. this measure will provide a sustainable option for west indian fishermen in the face of the chlordedecone crisis.
in writing. − the vote on the fisheries fund was crucial to reaching a political agreement by the end of the year to allow the fund to start work in january 2014. support sustainable management of fisheries resources, which will in turn ensure stability in the development of the fisheries sector and ensure the long-term well-being of the population. i therefore voted against aid for shipbuilding and in favour of precise limits on the amount of public funding that member states can grant to fleets. i believe that funds should be allocated to projects that contribute to the future sustainability of the fisheries sector and coastal communities, the restoration of fish stocks, the reduction of the impact of fishing on the marine environment and the progressive elimination of discarding practices. i supported the fact that the fisheries fund should increase investment in small-scale fisheries, which will be particularly important for latvia in order to preserve traditional fishing, long-standing traditions and the quality of catches, such as carnikava's necks, which will probably soon be included in the list of traditional products of the eu.
in writing. this report covers the budgetary framework and the guidelines for the financing of the common fisheries policy and the integrated maritime policy by 2020 through the european maritime and fisheries fund. provisions for improving the working conditions of fishermen, particularly in the areas of health, safety at work and respect for collective agreements, are included in this report. it also stresses the need to promote sustainable, environmentally friendly fishing. the gue/ngl group tabled amendments to increase eu co-financing for the collection and management of biological data and to finance the temporary cessation of fishing activities during biological rest periods. we also stressed the importance of eu co-financing linked to small-scale fishing, which is essential for the economic, social and ecological development of coastal communities. i voted in favour of the report, and the abolition of the possibility of buying or selling fishing rights is one of the key points. i voted for the postponement of the final vote pending agreement on the regulation laying down common provisions governing the five european funds for 2014-2020.
in writing. the decline in fish stocks is a cause for concern for both citizens who are consumers and fishermen who have been living off this activity for generations. to meet this challenge, member states have set strict fishing quota rules, which will come into force in 2015. if these rules are necessary, i also know that they are a significant economic constraint on our fishermen. that is why i voted in favour of the report by my ump colleague, alain cadec, which makes the european fisheries and maritime fund an ambitious instrument to support our fishermen in the transition and modernisation needed to meet the challenges ahead. the fund will help fishermen invest in energy-efficient boats and more selective fishing gear, thereby reducing unwanted catches and their discards. in addition to the support measures for sustainable fishing, i welcome the adoption of support measures, particularly for the establishment of young fishermen and the protection of small-scale fishing, which is threatened by industrial and intensive fishing, as is the case in my region.
in writing. at the recent conferences (durban and doha), the international community committed itself to a global, binding regime for the effective reduction of co2 emissions by 2015 and to applying it by 2020. the latest ipcc report shows how urgent it is to move forward. i voted in favour of this resolution because it gives a clear and ambitious roadmap to the delegation of 10 meps who will be travelling to the warsaw 'conference of the parties' (cop19). i am glad that this resolution rejects the principle that developed countries should make every effort. in reality, climate change is everyone's business. our international partners are aware of the consequences and are beginning to take action. if it fails, i believe the european union will have to take responsibility and introduce a carbon tax at the eu's borders to rebalance international competition with those who would not make the effort. i regret that the european parliament, by a narrow margin, rejected the amendment i had tabled to this effect, which had been adopted by the parliament's committee on the environment. i am continuing my crusade on this essential point.
in writing. climate change is now widely accepted by the scientific community. in this respect, the latest report of the intergovernmental panel on climate change (ipcc) is encouraging. let us be clear: the environment is a decisive key to overcoming the endless crisis of our economic "model". with this resolution, the european parliament is sending a welcome warning signal, even though we could have gone further in our proposals. i have voted in favour of a number of ambitious and unambiguous amendments against oil and shale gas, which are an environmental and economic deadlock. finally, i believe that the european union should move decisively towards a carbon contribution at the external borders of its space in order not to penalise our companies which are directly subject to ecological dumping by our trading partners.
in writing. i voted for this resolution. in view of the warsaw conference on climate change in november 2013, this motion for a resolution has the merit of calling for a global regime that abolishes all distinctions between industrialized and developing countries. i welcome the rejection of the amendment calling for a 30% reduction in co2 emissions by 2020 and a 50% reduction by 2050. in the absence of an international agreement, the european union cannot impose such a constraint on itself. i regret, however, the rejection of the carbon tax at the union's borders. the introduction of this tax would have avoided the commercial dumping by some of our trading partners exporting to the union.
in writing. the fight against climate change is a major ambition on the european agenda: the european parliament is the voice of europeans on this issue, and that is why it was necessary for us to define a clear position so that it can be relayed during the international negotiations that will soon take place in warsaw. i welcome the fact that this position is realistic: we must align climate objectives and industrial, research and innovation policy, to protect jobs and growth without jeopardising the environment. i regret, however, that the proposal to integrate a carbon mechanism at the border has been rejected: it is a common sense measure, for the benefit of all europeans and their environment, and i will remain committed to this issue.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it will enable parliament to send a clear and pragmatic message to the warsaw conference. the unrealistic targets of 30 to 50% reduction in emissions by 2020 and 2030 have been removed from the text, and i welcome this. while tackling climate change must clearly be a priority, it cannot be done at the expense of the competitiveness of our industrial fabric. at a time when our industry is facing an unprecedented crisis, it would be irresponsible to burden it even more by setting unattainable targets, which would weigh heavily on investment and, ultimately, on employment. this text is a strong signal in favour of a climate policy negotiated at global level and which is not a burden for our companies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution for the climate change conference in warsaw. it reiterated the european union's support for an ambitious but realistic policy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. i welcome the fact that our commitments for 2020 are conditional on the adoption of similar commitments by the main issuing countries. i welcome the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a common position ahead of the un climate change conference in warsaw in november. although the fight against climate change must remain a priority for the european union (eu), i voted against this resolution in which we make unilateral commitments. i believe that the european union should not be left to reduce greenhouse gases on its own, when it accounts for only 11% of global emissions. as such, the commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 30% by 2020 provided that other major emitters make similar commitments is a step in the right direction. i regret, however, that the resolution adopted does not call for the introduction of a carbon tax at the eu's borders. such a tax would protect european industry, which is subject to the eu's emissions quota system, while non-eu companies are excluded. this situation leads to a distortion of competition and a loss of competitiveness for our companies. it seems to me that it is essential that such systems be extended globally to have a real impact on climate change.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the climate change conference in preparation for the un conference in warsaw in november, which will bring together the 192 countries party to the kyoto protocol. the 20% target for reducing co2 emissions by 2020 must be maintained, and the eu could support a 30% reduction target if other emitting countries commit to this target.
in writing. this resolution is a reminder of the environmental emergency we are facing. climate change is an imminent and potentially irreversible threat to human societies, biodiversity and the planet, and therefore requires an international action plan involving all parties. the warsaw conference will be crucial in achieving a legally binding global agreement by 2015 to meet the '2°c target'. unfortunately, the necessary paradigm shift is not on the agenda. this text is part of the logic of green capitalism. it persists in measures that we know are ineffective, such as the greenhouse gas emissions trading system. he even claims that "a global carbon market would provide a sound basis for substantial emissions reductions". i vote against it because i do not want to encourage these things.
in writing. according to the world bank, current levels of co2 emissions suggest a global warming of 2°c above pre-industrial levels by 2050 and 4°c by 2100. a 4°c increase in temperature could have catastrophic consequences: floods, increased malnutrition, worsening drought, heat waves, water shortages, irreversible loss of biodiversity, climate migrations... i therefore voted in favour of this ambitious text which will serve as a negotiating mandate for members attending the next un climate conference in warsaw in november. however, if no binding global agreement on emissions reductions is reached in 2015, i believe the eu will need to put in place a carbon tax at the border so that imported products that do not comply with any environmental measures do not compete with european products subject to strict co2 emission requirements.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which reaffirms the need to take the climate change issue into our own hands. a new conference of the parties on these issues will be held in warsaw in november 2013. the last durban conference, of the same nature, made little progress. these interim conferences are intended to prepare for the paris conference in 2015, which will be of particular importance after the failures of copenhagen and doha. i supported this report which stresses the catastrophic effects of climate change and supports the responsibility of all states to cooperate in order to take urgent action. as the findings of the ipcc fifth assessment report indicate, human activity is indeed responsible for climate change. the temperature increase could exceed 2 degrees, the level allowed to avoid falling into the climate disorder with unsuspected consequences. western countries must take responsibility. the eu played a positive role in the development of the kyoto protocol. since then, under pressure from its member states, it has moved away from multilateralism and thus from taking account of the general interest. but in terms of climate, it is the only way forward.
in writing. in 2012, parliament set up a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering to develop an action plan to tackle these activities at eu level. i voted in favour of this report, which concludes the work of this committee and sets out the european union's future in this area.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the iacolino report giving the european union the instruments to fight against criminal groups within the borders of the european union. on money laundering, the report advocates the abolition of banking secrecy. in the case of corruption, the right of citizens to access information relating to public administration is protected. the report recommends that penalties be imposed for crimes against the security of persons, such as imprisonment and financial penalties of a high amount, commensurate with the damage suffered. the emphasis is on the essential cooperation between the member states of the union. crime of all kinds must be eradicated from the union; the report is a means by which the european union can do this.
in writing. this evaluation report on the state of organised crime, corruption and money laundering in europe paints an alarming picture of the situation in the union. this may partly explain the current feeling of distrust among citizens towards the institutions and leaders of the european union and its member states. this is why the states and the union must quickly take up the task of moralizing public life. part of the answer lies at the european level; the commission should also be able to provide the necessary information to the member states in order to ensure that the criminal organisations concerned are able to take advantage of the lack of coordination between member states. the european agencies such as frontex, europol and eurojust must be equipped with sufficient means to combat these networks. i also wish for the rapid establishment of a european public prosecutor's office to combat offences affecting the union's financial interests, as provided for in the community treaties.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i want to encourage the european union's efforts to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering. these global phenomena require a concerted response from the european union. i am therefore in favour of strengthening the fight against money laundering by promoting a more transparent banking system and business world, and by anti-money laundering measures to prevent crime from becoming a lucrative activity. it is up to us, the members of the european parliament, to ensure that we fight tax evasion effectively, particularly in times of crisis. it is not right that the european union still suffers from such evils as corruption and tax evasion. i would therefore like to stress that the european union must continue to pay particular attention to these issues in order to deal with phenomena which are aggravating the already difficult economic situations in our member states.
in writing. organised crime, corruption and money laundering in the european union are plagues that are eating away at europe, along with violence, insecurity, etc. in order to put a stop to these phenomena, our parliament has therefore taken a position on these matters by adopting the final report of the crim parliamentary committee, which recommends the development of a european union strategy and the adoption of binding legal instruments at european level and in the member states, and i welcome the adoption of this report. i would also like to stress that i voted in favour of the paragraphs in favour of greater tax harmonization and the harmonization of corporate taxation in europe. moreover, there is an urgent need to act in this area, because in addition to economic considerations, organised crime is a danger that threatens the freedom and security of all european citizens.
in writing. i gave my full support to this report in order to launch action lines to fight organised crime, corruption and money laundering more effectively. i am particularly in favour of the prosecution of the financial assets and sources of income of organised crime, the exclusion from public procurement tenders in the eu of any person convicted of organised crime, corruption or money laundering, and a ban on the exercise of public office. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. to protect the eu's financial interests, in a context of persistent economic crisis, the removal of banking secrecy and the elimination of tax havens in the eu are also necessary. i also believe that the property of criminals seized should be reused for social purposes. finally, i believe that legal entities such as companies and their subsidiaries should be required to reimburse any public funding they have received if they have committed a financial crime.
in writing. i supported this report. this report marks the completion of the work carried out so far by the crim committee, which was set up 18 months ago. the rapporteur strongly recommends the establishment of a european action plan to eradicate organised crime, corruption and money laundering and to define a list of priority positive actions. it also proposes the organisation of a 'european day of remembrance for the victims of organised crime'. the report was adopted by 526 votes to 25, with 87 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the european parliament adopted on wednesday measures to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering. according to europol, nearly 3600 international criminal organisations were active in the european union in 2013, and 70% of them had members in more than one country. i voted in favour of this text because it is essential to coordinate the actions of the member states in order to make the fight against organised crime more effective. we have in particular called on the european union and the member states to exclude from public procurement tenders and public contracts persons convicted of organised crime, corruption or money laundering. we also stressed the importance of creating a european public prosecutor's office to coordinate national investigations. finally, we have called for the abolition of banking secrecy and tax havens to facilitate the freezing of assets of criminal networks. according to the united nations office on drugs and crime (unodc), illegal activities account for about 3.6 percent of the world's gdp. once seized, criminal assets could be reused for social purposes.
in writing. i voted for this text, which concludes 18 months of work by the parliamentary committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the fight against organized crime must be our priority! it is time to react and develop ways to better fight criminals who do not wait for us to cooperate with each other. after hearing from many experts, we have drawn up a european action plan to combat this phenomenon at different levels. at the criminal level, member states should harmonise their definition of criminal offences, such as money laundering, and the applicable sanctions. the strengthening of judicial and police cooperation at european and international level is a key element in tracking mafia networks that go beyond our borders. at the level of public administrations, progress is possible in making all information related to administrative organisation and activity accessible in order to fight corruption. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. the iacolino report has the advantage of addressing organised crime in multiple dimensions, ranging from money laundering to trafficking in human beings, arms and drugs trafficking, environmental crime and cybercrime. i agree with some of his proposals, including the importance to be attached to the fight against white collar crime and tax evasion, the fight against companies with branches in tax havens, the fight against forced labour, support for investigative journalism, the fight against shoe-throwing, increased controls on financial products and online gambling. however, this report does not propose radical measures against tax havens, such as a total ban on the activities of european banks in these territories, as proposed in the joly report on this subject. some points are problematic, such as the importance attached to the banking union, which gives all power to a ecb that is not accountable to the people, but also the reference to nato as a framework for collective security when it is a factor of disorder and danger for europe. i am voting against this text.
in writing. i supported this resolution, which sets out an action plan to tackle organised crime, both at european and international level. in addition to the resulting corruption, which the commission estimates at just over 1% of eu gdp, several hundred thousand forced labourers worldwide are caught in the grip of this phenomenon. about a quarter are victims of sexual exploitation. the plan includes the creation of a european public prosecutor's office to coordinate national investigations into organised crime. this is often the result of transnational transactions, activities or networks. the other key measure advocated in the report is the freezing and confiscation of ill-gotten gains of organised crime networks. we have also proposed that once seized, these criminal assets can be reused for social purposes, in particular to combat human trafficking and forced labour. finally, we stressed the urgent need to achieve a single legal definition of organised crime and to harmonise offences such as match-fixing, vote buying and participation in a mafia organisation.
in writing. i abstained on this report on organised crime. while it gives high priority to white collar crime and economic crime (which do inflict the most serious social damage) and to the issues of corruption and money laundering, it does not provide a convincing response to the challenges posed by these problems. the report advocates a uniform approach based on repression and surveillance for all countries of the european union. it also links immigration and organised crime, welcoming 'the beneficial action of frontex for europe and its citizens'; this is a bad time to say the least. finally, the rapid access of european administrations to national data banks, in particular those of the tax authorities, the vehicle registration register, the land register and the banking register, makes me fear for the protection of our personal data.
in writing. i supported this motion for a resolution. in the context of the european neighbourhood policy (enp) and in recent months, the commission and the european external action service (eeas) have been insisting that the principle of 'more for more' be better implemented and strongly linked to progress in building democracy and respecting the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms. as regards the eastern partnership, the union should be ready to support states facing pressure from third states in the run-up to the vilnius summit. with regard to the southern part of the enp, it is essential that a dialogue between the different political actors in egypt is initiated; the european union is also calling for the immediate release of all political prisoners and for the simultaneous condemnation of the use of chemical weapons against the civilian population in syria and for political and humanitarian support to be provided. i welcome the fact that this resolution was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the european neighbourhood policy stating that respect for the fundamental principles of democracy must be at the heart of eu policy, which should focus its assistance on the development of democratic institutions and political parties.
