in writing. the european union's neighbourhood policy is mainly about exporting the liberal model. there are a few sentences on respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, including the rights of women and minorities, and freedom of expression, but under conditions whose non-respect is a hindrance to the opening up of markets. if there is arbitration between the two, we should remember the arbitrations that the union had in libya and tunisia a few weeks before the revolutions. the deep and comprehensive free trade agreements (dcftas) are presented here as "a model of reforms that benefit everyone". the resolution also regrets the delays in the negotiations for the signing and ratification of free trade agreements with many neighbouring countries. i don't share that regret. i vote against it.
in writing. the european parliament adopted today the report by elisa ferreira on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies. we european socialists have won two major victories. for the first time, the european parliament recognises that countries with budgetary or trade surpluses need to stimulate demand. this clear message to germany is an important step forward. another socialist success, the european parliament is calling for democratic control of the troika (ecb, imf, european commission). on the other hand, we regret that the right wing has opposed the establishment of a budget specific to the euro area, which we fundamentally need to finance growth in a period of recession and to reduce economic and social disparities between countries. finally, the european socialists had made a strong proposal for the gradual introduction of a european unemployment insurance system. the right has once again shown its anti-social face by rejecting this proposal based on the principle of solidarity.
in writing. i supported mrs ferreira's own-initiative report on the key measures for economic convergence at european level. the european union's economic and budgetary policies will be better coordinated upstream, and this will only strengthen the stability, growth and competitiveness of the euro area. in a social and dynamic europe, it sets thoughtful and concrete priorities, particularly in the fight against unemployment. this report provides a framework for analysis which can be of full benefit to the various european economies. it called on the commission to provide more detail in its recommendations to the member states of the european union.
in writing. the european semester, which provides a framework for the economic and budgetary policies of the member states, is an indispensable tool of economic governance. it is a further step towards a genuine monetary union. this coordination at european level must be done in a smart way and give priority to growth and employment in the member states, cohesion, investment and a macroeconomic rebalancing of the euro area. it is also essential that the european parliament, as the democratic body of the european union, should be more closely involved in the work of the european semester.
in writing. unsurprisingly, the report endorses the european semester, the exercise in which member states dictate their budgets and the policies they must implement. it welcomed the country-specific recommendations, which call, for france and others, for the precariousness of employment, for structural reform of pensions, for the total liberalisation of the energy market and for the freedom to set up large-scale businesses. it cannot, however, ignore the catastrophic social consequences of the austerity policies pursued by the states, under the ironclad constraint, for some, of the commission-ecb-imf troika. the most distressing thing is that the main changes proposed to mitigate these consequences are the introduction of a purely european system under the supervision of parliament, as if that changes anything! the report also calls for the troika's communication strategy to be improved. the impoverished people of greece, spain and portugal, the fraudulent savers of cyprus and the millions of unemployed in these countries subject to the troika will be delighted to learn that they are the victims of a miscommunication! as for the rest, it is the usual discourse calling for an increase in a clientelistic and largely useless european budget, and the acceleration of the construction of the european superstate. this is unacceptable !
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague elisa ferreira on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies because we, the socialist members of parliament, are here to defend increased parliamentary control of economic governance, in particular of the 'troika' (ecb, imf, european commission), in contrast to the intergovernmental logic which currently prevails. we want europe to have a genuine mechanism of community solidarity. the banking sector needs to be subject to increased controls to better combat tax evasion and tax fraud. i also supported the creation of a euro-area budget, which is the budget we need to finance growth in times of recession and to reduce economic and social inequalities between member states.
in writing. i supported this report on the country-specific recommendations to each member state that the european commission has published. these recommendations are based on a thorough analysis of the public finance consolidation plans of each member state and the measures implemented to stimulate growth and employment (national reform programmes). it is essential to pursue the objective of growth and employment in the context of the european semester for economic policy coordination. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies. we have called for better implementation of the economic recommendations that the european commission addresses to each member state, whereas only 15% of the reforms recommended by the european union were implemented by member states in 2012. we have called for greater convergence of economic policies, which is essential for the stability of the euro area, in particular through the creation of an instrument for convergence and competitiveness. this instrument would provide eu countries with the funds needed to mitigate the short-term negative effects of economic reforms. we also called on the european commission to give priority to the fight against unemployment, in particular through investment in education and better financing for small businesses. the social policies of the member states should also be better coordinated, which is why we propose to create a minimum unemployment benefit in the euro area. i voted in favour of this resolution, which proposes some interesting work for the european commission's work in the first half of 2014.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies. this coordination at european level is not sufficient to significantly encourage growth, employment and investment. stricter criteria could improve economic convergence and provide more incentives for member states to implement the reforms recommended by the european union.
in writing. this report does not shy away from some positive proposals. but this is to drown them in an unacceptable mix of congratulations to the european commission and calls for further 'structural reforms' and austerity. moreover, this report is fully in line with the logic of the european semester. the european semester, like other austerity measures, cannot be improved. it must be fought. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted against this report on the european semester. the european semester is the direct implementation of the sixth pack, to use european jargon. its aim is to 'coordinate at european level economic and budgetary policies in relation to the stability and growth pact' and to monitor the implementation of structural reforms. we all know what that means. it is the implementation and, in this case, the control by the european parliament of austerity policies with the same leitmotif: reduction of excessive deficits. the house also expressed its deep concern at the continuing insecurity of private investors, their lack of confidence and their reluctance to invest, particularly because of productivity standards. calls on states to 'modernize their health care and pension systems and open up their service sectors'; 'calls for the full and proper implementation of the european services directive'. the gue/ngl will continue to reject all these austerity policies in general and to promote alternative policies based on a different distribution of wealth.
in writing. the series of tragedies which have struck the italian and maltese coasts is yet another consequence of the ongoing wars and must be a turning point for the union. this unacceptable situation is a sign of the failure of an immigration policy designed at the national level alone. the european union has a tool to deal with this emergency: temporary refugee status. but this is now the burden of the coastal countries, which are obliged to examine the files as the first host country. official and secure arrival points throughout the eu are therefore essential if we are to avoid such dramatic voyages off our coasts. beyond asylum, there is the issue of illegal immigration, which can lead to the worst. this issue must be dealt with at the source. we must fight firmly against the smuggling and trafficking networks. the control of this scourge must be a long-term plan and be part of a concerted policy on asylum and immigration which is fair and respects human rights.
in writing. many of the proposals made in this resolution are totally irresponsible: to consider de facto that every immigrant is a potential asylum seeker and not just an economic immigrant, to want to organize the forced distribution of these pseudo-refugees throughout europe and to give a list of places suitable for the disembarkation of immigration candidates rescued at sea... why not reorganise frontex ships into shipping companies and distribute brochures to future passengers so that they can choose their country of destination? emotion is not a good counselor. already, the blaming of europeans for their alleged indifference to rescue at sea has allowed smugglers to organize. to know that a frontex patrol is nearby is to be able to cram hundreds of people onto makeshift boats, with the near certainty that they will be picked up before the worst happens and taken to europe! risking the lives of children is a voluntary strategy to avoid the return of adults. you want to welcome the misery of the world, but you are only adding to the misery that the crisis and your policies have produced right here in europe, and which should be your top priority.
in writing. history stutters and repeats itself. our parliament has just adopted a new resolution on the tragic and recent events in lampedusa: a new drama that reminds us that every day men and women fleeing the horrors of war are dying in the mediterranean trying to find refuge in europe. i welcome the adoption of this strong resolution, which i immediately co-signed; i regret that every year new shipwrecks take place when we could have avoided them. the european union has a host of instruments, a set of tools, a panoply of means, but nothing is happening. so, despite the months that have passed, we are still asking the same thing: we are asking the states to take the urgency of the situation into account; we are asking the states to respect their obligations in the matter of rescue at sea and then to act, to take real action, on the one hand, to prevent such disasters and, on the other hand, to have a common migration policy. for all these reasons, i voted resolutely in favour of this resolution.
in writing. the tragedy of lampedusa should be a wake-up call for the whole of the european union. in supporting this resolution, i wanted to call on the european commission, as well as the council, to make a radical change in the approach to migration. i have advocated, in particular, the abolition of any provision punishing persons who rescue migrants in distress at sea, the strengthening of member states' international obligations in the field of search and rescue at sea and the development of legal pathways for migrants and asylum seekers to reach europe. until the eu and member states adopt a comprehensive approach that includes the multiple facets of migration issues, migrants will continue to rely on traffickers or criminal networks and risk their lives on increasingly dangerous routes. it is time for everyone to take responsibility and seek to implement an integrated european migration policy, addressing both the symptoms and the root causes of the phenomenon, in order to avoid the recurrence of tragedies such as those we have witnessed in recent weeks.
in writing. the european parliament reacted to the news on wednesday 23 october by adopting a resolution on migration flows in the light of the migrant shipwreck off lampedusa. i have already had the opportunity to speak on this subject. the deaths of these migrants are a tragedy that cannot be ignored, and i do not forget that these migrants often flee conflict zones to seek, in europe, even if only illusory, security. however, europe today is no longer able to accommodate these thousands of illegal immigrants because the member states themselves are going through a very difficult period economically and socially which reveals how inadequate our immigration and integration systems of the 20th century are. that is why i think it is essential that we rethink our overly attractive social model which allows free health care for illegal immigrants while citizens have to pay a deductible of up to 50 euros. i also note that the instability in the sub-saharan african region and the mediterranean area should encourage us to intensify our dialogue with the source and transit countries. finally, i believe that it is absolutely essential to strengthen the capacity and financial resources of frontex by creating a border police force.
in writing. i supported this motion for a resolution. in recent months, the migration flows have increased sharply in the mediterranean and human tragedies have occurred, notably that of lampedusa. the ppe group therefore asked at the last plenary session for a discussion with the commission. the resolution also discusses the issues of border defence, the various traffics in the area and possible agreements with north african countries, among others. this resolution was adopted by a large majority, and i welcome that.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution with a number of recommendations to the member states for the european council on 23 and 24 october, which focused in particular on european immigration policy. we have demanded the reinstatement of the appropriations cut in the 2014 draft budget to strengthen the capacity of frontex, the agency responsible for managing cooperation at the eu's external borders, and the european asylum support office. we also wanted new rules on interception at sea. the laws of member states which provide for sanctions against persons rescuing migrants at sea should be revised, as local populations are often present before rescue and can save lives. finally, we called for greater solidarity from the european union towards the countries of southern europe, which are facing large flows of illegal immigration to europe. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union must adopt a genuine immigration policy, improve cooperation between member states and allocate more resources to existing instruments.
in writing. following the recent tragic events in lampedusa, member states should take additional measures to prevent people from dying at sea. a european strategy based on solidarity and responsibility is needed. member states should deepen their cooperation and facilitate exchanges between their coastguards. additional funds should be allocated to european agencies such as frontex and the european asylum support office to help member states at the eu's external borders, which are most in need of assistance. in the criminal field, member states should adopt strong sanctions against smugglers in order to combat the phenomenon of trafficking in human beings and to deter traffickers. finally, the union must continue its humanitarian action in the crisis areas of north africa and the middle east in order to tackle the root causes of these migratory pressures.
in writing. according to the international organisation for migration, at least 20,000 people have died at sea since 1993. the resolution, which follows the recurring tragedies in lampedusa, stresses once again the need to make every effort to save the lives of people in danger and that member states must fulfil their international obligations in the field of rescue at sea. migrants are referred to as victims of human traffickers and smugglers, never as victims of europe's aggressive trade policies. but the resolution also calls for increased funding for the frontex agency, whose role is to combat illegal immigration. this purely police approach to migration will not in any way help to solve the human tragedies that are taking place on the eu's coasts. as long as europe does not turn its back on the wild trade liberalization that is destroying the economies of the countries of the south, forced migration will continue, even if the union is transformed into a fortress. i vote against it.
in writing. i supported the epp group's proposal to postpone the vote on the resolution on the swift agreement. we cannot seriously contemplate suspending the swift agreement at the moment, as proposed by the other political groups, even though we have not been given any evidence of a breakdown in the agreement. both the european commission and europol certify that they cannot consider that the united states has breached the terrorist financing surveillance programme. we must also await the final results of the nsa investigation group within the libe committee. it is irresponsible to call into question such an agreement, which enables us to fight terrorism better. we cannot play with the safety of european citizens.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution despite the hesitations of the european right, which asked for a postponement of the vote without obtaining it. we believe there are clear indications that the nsa could retrieve information about our businesses and our citizens from the swift server and hijack it. we ask that this agreement be temporarily suspended, as provided for in the tftp, until a number of facts have been clarified. we also ask europol to open an inquiry into unauthorised access to financial payment data under this agreement. the moment your partner starts spying on you, that's when trust is broken. since april i have been calling for the suspension of the pnr and swift agreements with the usa. europe should go further by freezing the negotiations on the free trade agreement with the united states! respect for the fundamental rights of european citizens must be a precondition for any agreement!
in writing. the alleged spying by the nsa on the banking data of eu citizens, via the swift system, constitutes a serious breach of the fundamental rights and freedoms of european citizens. these two principles form the basis of what unites europeans today and as such deserve to be treated very seriously. it is essential that europe should speak out and say that this violation of the contract with the united states is unacceptable. the suspension of the terrorist financing tracking programme (tftp) until the us has answered the many questions from the eu is a strong signal to this effect. we need a relationship of trust in our diplomatic and trade relations. that trust has now been broken and that is why, beyond this agreement, i reiterate my call in july last year to postpone our negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment treaty.
in writing. according to media reports, the nsa directly exploits swift systems. if these allegations are proven, this would constitute a very serious breach of the swift agreement - on the processing and transfer of financial messaging data from the european union to the united states for the purposes of the terrorist finance monitoring program. in these circumstances, the commission should have taken immediate measures to suspend the agreement pending clarification. that is what our group has been defending since the very first allegations, and that is what the european parliament is asking for in a resolution adopted last week. i welcome the adoption of this resolution and expect the commission to take up its responsibilities, because we cannot continue our cooperation in data exchange with the us authorities in good faith under these conditions, just as we cannot compromise on issues relating to the protection of the privacy and personal data of european citizens.
in writing. following revelations of unauthorised access to swift data by the nsa, i voted in favour of the joint resolution by the socialists, liberals and greens calling for the suspension of the tftp agreement governing the transfer of data. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft agreement on the free movement of goods and services. it is unacceptable that european companies should be subject to surveillance which may have other purposes than the fight against terrorism and serious transnational crime. these are serious matters to which clear answers must be given. without this clarification, the good faith of our american partner is likely to be seriously questioned. by supporting this proposal, member states will be able to show that they are listening to the concerns of european citizens. it is also in this spirit that we invite them to ask europol to open an investigation into the unauthorised access to financial payment data managed by this agreement.
in writing. i voted against the resolution calling for the suspension of the swift agreement because of the nsa surveillance, as this agreement is irrelevant to the issues of wiretapping and would undermine the fight against terrorism which threatens both the european union and the united states. i therefore regret the adoption of this disproportionate resolution.
in writing. i voted in favour of my political group's resolution because i believe that the eu-us data transfer agreement is important for the fight against terrorism. we must not react hastily and suspend an agreement that is essential for the security of european citizens while the allegations of non-compliance with the tftp agreement by the united states are not proven.
in writing. the resolution has the merit of capturing the full extent of the facts. it denounces the activities of the nsa in relation to direct access to financial messaging data and related data. it called for a full technical investigation into the unauthorised access by the us government to data held on swift servers on the ground, and regretted that no state had requested it. unfortunately, this resolution merely calls for the 'suspension' of the swift agreement until a full and complete explanation of the facts of which the united states is accused is obtained. it's not right for us. we demand the complete abolition of the swift system. we are calling for a halt to the negotiations on the transatlantic trade treaty. despite this reservation in substance, i am voting for this text so that there is at least one document from parliament against the activities of the united states against the freedom of peoples.
in writing. according to reports widely circulated in recent days, the us national security agency (nsa) has spied on the personal financial data of european citizens. the us authorities' access to this financial data is strictly limited by the agreement on the processing and transfer of financial messaging data to monitor the financial flows of terrorism, which entered into force in 2010. if proven, these activities constitute a clear and unacceptable violation of the eu-us agreement. it is essential that an investigation be carried out as soon as possible in order to clarify the situation. i regret that this was not done sooner. in addition, pending the clarification of these allegations, the eu-us agreement on banking data should be suspended. that is what the text of this resolution calls for, and i fully support it. of course, i am aware that parliament has no formal powers to suspend - or denounce - an international agreement, but i hope the commission will hear us!

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it will improve the protection of our citizens against exposure to ionising radiation. ionizing radiation is the radiation emitted by radioactive materials, which is present in many industrial sectors, in particular the medical sector (radiotherapy, etc.) and, of course, the nuclear industry. the text voted by parliament aims to clarify and supplement existing legislation, to take better account of the latest scientific data on radiation protection and to cover possible exposure situations more widely. medical devices emitting ionising radiation, which were previously covered by two different directives, will be dealt with in a single framework, which already provides for numerous control and monitoring tools. this will also avoid duplication and red tape for manufacturers and operators of these devices. the clarified legislative framework resulting from the amendments will therefore provide for enhanced protection against ionising radiation.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the dangers of exposure to ionising radiation which updates the existing text, in particular in the light of the most recent scientific data and operational experience. the directive should set a uniform minimum level of protection in the member states for workers, the general public, patients and other persons exposed to medical exposure to ionising radiation. the text clarifies that hazard information should be mandatory and extends the application to different exposure situations, whether planned, existing, accidental or emergency.

member of the commission. − mr president, let me first pay tribute to the work of the rapporteur, doris pack, and to the shadow rapporteurs. i think we would all agree that this is one of the european union’s most important and respected programmes. europe’s economic and social crisis has only given new urgency to our support for education, training and youth policy. i am happy to say that the text we are debating today does justice to our collective efforts. in 2011, the commission put forward a proposal for a new eu programme for education, training, youth and sport. in the light of slow economic growth, unacceptably high youth unemployment, and the huge challenges brought about by new technology and the digital shift, the commission was convinced that business as usual was not an option. our spending priorities have to match our political aspirations. to tackle some of the most urgent challenges facing europe today, we must invest more in education, training and youth participation. that is why the commission had originally proposed a 70% increase on current spending. nevertheless – and i am pleased that this is due in no small part to the support of the european parliament – despite the overall decrease in the eu budget, the eu budget for these policies will amount to eur 14.7 billion over the next seven years, which represents a 40% increase on current spending. the recent survey on the skills of europe’s adult population shows that 20% of working-age people have low literacy and low numeracy skills, and that 25% of adults lack the skills to exploit new information technologies. today, almost six million young people are unemployed, varying from less than 10% in some countries to more than 50% in other countries. at the same time, paradoxically we see more than two million vacancies in europe, while one in three enterprises has difficulty finding people with the right skills. this is why we need an eu programme that strives to improve levels of competences and skills, and to modernise our learning institutions, both formal and informal. we have to help them deliver the skills we need today and for the foreseeable future. erasmus plus offers a number of innovations. first, in higher education, it brings together all internal and international capacity-building and mobility instruments under one roof. this will increase the efficiency, coherence and visibility of eu action, and trigger synergies. second, we will integrate our main youth activities under the new programme building bridges between non-formal learning and formal education, fostering much needed cooperation across sectors. third, and in line with our policy goals, we are strengthening the links between education and the world of work by stimulating new partnerships and putting stronger focus on the employability of young people. and fourth, for the very first time, we are offering eu funding to the world of sport so as to improve its governance and address threats such as racism, doping and match-fixing and to support grassroots sports organisations in serving eu citizens better. this means that the new programme will expand the opportunities for both citizens and education, training, youth and sports bodies. it will offer more possibilities to students of higher education and vocational education to spend part of their studies abroad or to gain valuable work experience in another country. more funding will be set aside for youth exchanges and youth volunteering. staff from all educational sectors, as well as the youth sector, will have more opportunities to update their skills abroad. the programme will also offer opportunities for institutions and youth organisations to work together with partners in other countries, exchange experience, learn from each other and build common projects, and it will offer support to member states for innovation and new policy development. all of this will help to raise the quality of education, training and youth systems across europe. honourable members, today you have the chance to give your full backing to a new and ambitious programme that can help change the lives of millions of europeans and change them for the better.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i would first like to thank my co-rapporteurs, mrs ayala sender and mrs vălean, for the very good cooperation we had in the discussions on the interconnection mechanism in europe. i would also like to thank the ten-t rapporteurs, mr koumoutsakos and mr ertug, with whom we worked closely throughout these negotiations, which made it possible to bring our two texts into perfect harmony. finally, i would also like to thank - once again - the presidency for its excellent cooperation, with a special thought for michael harper. i would like to express my regret at the weakness of the budget for this mechanism for interconnection in europe as it resulted from the discussions on the multiannual financial framework. the budget of €33 billion is far from the €50 billion originally proposed by the commission. this is all the more damaging as the use of the innovative financial instruments, which mrs vălean mentioned and which would have made it possible to compensate in part for these limited resources, has been restricted at the council's request. and yet, financial markets are very demanding of these long-term investments supported by stable assets, such as large infrastructure projects. nevertheless, this fund will improve the free movement of persons, goods and services. it has always been at the heart of the european integration project. because, sixty years after the start of our adventure, it is clear that much progress still needs to be made: delays at the borders, missing sections on some networks, difficulties in planning a long-distance journey, difficulties in interconnecting energy networks, and weak telecommunications networks. with the forthcoming entry into force of the connecting europe facility, we will continue our efforts to tackle bottlenecks, remove missing links, connect cross-border crossing points, and optimise the management of rail, air, river, sea and road traffic. but we will also increase both the energy security of europe as a whole and its capacity in the new digital world. the new fund therefore holds the promise that citizens will find their private and business travels facilitated, and that companies will be able to offer their products and services more easily outside europe. concerns about climate change were also taken into account, with a focus on sustainable transport modes, including rail and inland waterway transport. i am convinced that by speeding up the development of the transeuropean transport, energy and telecommunications networks, this new fund will help us to overcome the crisis that the european union has been experiencing for the last few years. investment in infrastructure projects has an impact on growth, employment and competitiveness on three levels: first, by stimulating hiring at the time of construction; second, by creating opportunities to exploit this new infrastructure; and third, by enhancing the attractiveness of the regions concerned and their competitiveness. i would like to emphasize that this new legislative framework we are about to adopt represents a real improvement on the current system, thanks to the dual approach, which should make it possible to better identify projects to be financed as a matter of priority, and through the promotion of projects with synergies between the three sectors covered by the framework, budget that will provide the appropriations needed in 2014 to finance the new programmes and actions commonly agreed in the multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020. the fully-fledged start of programmes and actions under the current multiannual financial framework and to pay the related invoices that will be received in the course of 2014. it is also important that, in these times of in writing. the european parliament today voted on the eu's multiannual financial framework, i.e. the financing of eu policies from 2014 to 2020. for the first time in the history of the eu, a budget in regression was voted by a large majority in the european parliament thanks to an alliance between the right and the socialist group. it is an austerity budget, cut by no less than €50 billion compared with the previous financial framework. with over 120 million people at risk of poverty or social exclusion in the european union, or 23% of the eu population, and unemployment exploding, the eu is cutting back on its solidarity programmes. moreover, the conditions under which this budget was adopted are unacceptable. the president of the european parliament, the german socialist martin schulz, who is pursuing personal aims (he wants to become president of the commission) has used a blocked vote procedure, preventing any possibility of voting on the key points of the text by prohibiting any possibility of amendments... while some amendments may concern several million or even several billion of public funds, meps were not able to speak in plenary...
in writing. following months of debate between the european institutions, the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 was finally adopted by a large majority in the european parliament on tuesday 19 november. the community budget is maintained at eur 960 billion for the next seven years, as decided by the european council on 8 february, a real decrease of 3.5% compared with the previous period. however, the european parliament has made important concessions, and i welcome this, because we are speaking in the direct interest of the european citizens. we have thus achieved a mid-term review of the budget which will take account of the changing economic situation in europe, the setting up of a high-level group to consider the establishment of own funds to relieve the burden on net contributing member states, the closure of the 2013 budget, more flexibility in the transfer of funding between community policies and the securing of an additional €1 billion for aid to the poorest.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleagues jean-luc dehaene and ivailo kalfin. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' in the definition of the term 'commercial vehicle'. it is important to emphasize that as a result of the negotiations between parliament, the commission and the council, parliament first of all obtained full flexibility in the cfp, thus allowing the transfer of unused funds from one year to the next and from one sector to another. this flexibility will be used in particular to combat youth unemployment in europe. parliament also obtained a revision of the mff by 2016, allowing the future parliament to readjust the budget. finally, the principles of unity and maximum transparency will be applied. i would like to stress that the epp group has succeeded in securing more funds for the erasmus, cosme and horizon 2020 programmes; the european union is also committed to the development of the social dimension of the internal market. the report was adopted by 537 votes in favour, 126 against and 19 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. − the negotiations leading up to the final vote on the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework were intense and difficult. for the first time we have a budget cut compared to the previous programming, and this is mainly due to the serious economic crisis affecting the eu member states. given the starting points, the final agreement satisfies us, albeit moderately. however, i feel i must reiterate, in line with what my colleagues have done, the need for a strong mid-term review (in 2016), a change in the approval procedure and an effective reform of the own resources system, so as to give the european budget real autonomy.
in writing. as regards the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, we endorsed in plenary on tuesday the agreement reached between parliament's budgetary negotiating team, led by our colleague alain lamassoure, president of the budget committee, and the member states. after almost two years of intensive and laborious negotiations, we have finally 'arrived' at the best possible agreement, indeed the only one, given the budgetary context and the constraints on the national budgets of the 28 member states. for the period 2014-2020, it is a multiannual finance law with a budget of €960 million. the conditions set by the european parliament in the negotiations were accepted by the other stakeholders, in particular the flexibility , i.e. the ability to transfer appropriations from one budget line to another, and the revision clause , which implies a mid-term review in 2016 of this multiannual financial framework, with a view to adjusting and revising it, as appropriate, in the light of the evolution of the european economic and budgetary situation.
in writing. i vote against the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, which was negotiated without taking into account the proposals set out by parliament and the commission. to ensure its adoption, the council used the possibility of a new refusal and thus of a suspension of funds, since the vote on the other programmes (cap, cohesion, horizon 2020, erasmus +...) was conditional on its adoption. the cfp will condemn europe and its citizens to even more austerity, since it has €960 billion of commitments, €40 billion less than the previous framework. this is the first time in the history of european integration that a financial framework has been less financially endowed than its predecessor. the cfp is therefore unable to compensate for the european austerity measures which have been imposed by governments. the few victories of parliament on a working party on new resources, or a review clause, could not counteract this austerity trend, so i voted against this budget.
in writing. i voted in favour of the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, which contains several improvements to the functioning of the mff, as requested by the european people's party. these include greater flexibility in the transfer of unused funds from one year to the next and between categories, a revision of the mff, by 2016 at the latest, in line with the evolution of the economic situation, the establishment of a high-level group working on the possibilities of feeding the european budget with own resources. we have also been able to secure an additional eur 1 billion for the european fund for the most deprived, compared with the council's proposal.
in writing. this draft european budget for 2014-2020 applies increased austerity. it removes 50 billion from the previous 2007-13 budget, while the union's population has increased by 10 million. the union would thus have a budget at a historically low level, less than 1% of its wealth, whereas the treaties allow it to rise to 1.27%. this budget will worsen the contraction in activity without providing the means for future investments, which the heads of state have been touting. no budgetary demands made by parliament have been met: the amounts in the budget have not moved a cent from those adopted by the council last june. martin schulz announced the capitulation of parliament to merkel before parliament had even debated and voted. how can what was considered "insufficient" in july now be considered acceptable by the epp and pse rapporteurs? the agreement submitted to parliament is all the more damaging because it extends to all european funds the 'macro-economic conditionality', allowing the european commission to suspend payments to the states in case of non-compliance with its liberal recommendations. i vote against this new austerity coup.
in writing. the multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020 is the union's budget for the next seven years, until 2020. and this new budget is down, not for one year, not for three years, but for seven years! we even had to fight until the last minute to get the heads of state to stop cutting more than 30% of the budget allocated to food aid for the poorest of our citizens. this is particularly true in times of crisis, when inequality and poverty are at their highest. this budgetary austerity is detrimental to the whole of the union and i have therefore voted against the seven years of austerity proposed for the whole of the european union.
in writing. i am pleased to have finally voted on the draft multiannual budget for the period 2014-2020. it's about time! this agreement is certainly not up to the ambitions advocated by parliament, but it is a reasonable compromise which should allow a significant level of funding to be maintained for programmes such as erasmus or for programmes such as the cap or regional funds. above all, parliament has stood firm on what i consider to be the essential point: resources. instead of asking the member states for a cheque every year, we would rather have our own resources. the new mff is a real step forward in this respect.
in writing. for the first time in its history, the union has a declining multiannual budget. with 960 billion in commitment appropriations and 908 billion in payment appropriations for the period 2014-2020, the member states have just imposed seven years of austerity on us! the various arrangements obtained by the negotiating team may make it possible to relax this framework in the future, but they do little to hide the humiliation suffered by the representatives of the peoples of europe. moreover, the structure of this framework, although slightly reoriented in favour of competitiveness expenditure, remains locked in a logic inherited from the 1980s where two headings (agriculture and cohesion) have the lion's share. in these circumstances, i have decided to abstain from voting on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 as it emerged from the discussions with the council. we cannot always demand more from europe without giving it the means to do so. with the adoption of this framework, i am very concerned about the future of european construction and i fully support the calls for reform of this budgetary procedure, in particular its resources component, in order to reduce the control of the states which continue to provide a large part of it.
in writing. although it was very difficult to negotiate this financial framework for the next programming period, i am satisfied with the compromises reached. above all, we have been able to achieve our objectives in the three key areas of this new framework, namely the settlement of the current mff invoices, the completion of the negotiations on the legal basis for the next programming periods and the setting up of a reflection group on the own resources of the european budget. these three conditions being met, i have supported this report by my vote in plenary.
in writing. i voted in favour of the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 because we have shown responsibility. anyone who falsely accuses the european union of increasing its spending should look at the figures: despite ever-increasing powers, its budget is falling. the long and intense negotiations have shown the limits of the current revenue system: our institutions are strapped down by the treatment of net contributors whose only concerns are to reduce their contributions and maximize their returns on investment. these negotiations without democratic control have had their day: the council has committed itself to setting up its own resources to calm the budgetary debate and make real political choices. in the meantime, parliament has managed to preserve the investments for the future: an increase in erasmus, continued aid to the poorest, regional funds targeted at growth and increased research and innovation programmes. now we must move forward, and maximise the impact on growth and employment of every euro from the european budget.
in writing. despite months of tense negotiations, the council has not been able to propose to the european parliament an acceptable multiannual financial framework for the european union for the period 2014-2020. the overall amount of this budget is not only unsatisfactory but, moreover, down on the previous period. at a time when europe needs more than ever the mobilisation of all to boost growth and employment, the reduction of all amounts, and more particularly those for the european social fund, is not acceptable. parliament had set five sine qua non conditions for its support last july. however, despite some slight progress, it is clear that the commitment to revise the budget mid-term and the level of payments are not reflected in the own resources. that is why the european parliament's members of the democratic movement did not support this agreement.
in writing. i abstained in the final vote on this text. the european parliament has certainly succeeded in getting some improvements on this text, such as the possibility of revising this agreement in 2016 or increasing budget flexibility by moving unused funds from one year to the next and from one financial programme to another. however, parliament's negotiators were unable to secure more funds from the council. the adopted multiannual financial framework is indeed an austerity budget which clearly illustrates the lack of ambition of the member states for the european union. i did not vote for this budget because i believe that the european union must not be a prisoner of the selfishness and cowardice of the member states. at a time when everyone is recognising that efforts to promote growth, jobs and competitiveness must be stepped up and that the european budget is one of the best ways of achieving this, the budget is shrinking! i also believe that the future of europe depends on own resources, which could be financed, for example, by taxes on financial transactions.
in writing. after a long debate, i voted in favour of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 proposed by the council and the european commission, which sets out the envelopes for the five future budgets of the european union in different policy areas. i regret, however, that he has not been ambitious enough on many points. the multiannual financial contribution thus voted is 9% lower than the previous one. it does not meet the ambitions of investment for growth and employment. i voted against the compromise on the provisions for macro-conditionality, that is to say the requirements imposed on states in difficulty to receive european subsidies, which are deplorable. but the budgetary commitment to the youth guarantee, the food aid fund and the increase in appropriations for job creation convinced me to vote.

in writing. this report endorses the 8th amending budget of the union for 2013. it allows for an increase of eur 3.9 billion in the available payment appropriations to be used to pay the oldest arrears to the various european funds. far from covering all outstanding arrears, this extension will only cover those arrears which expose member states to financial penalties from the suppliers or service providers concerned. the extension had been requested in vain as early as march 2013, but it was not until the first financial penalties were imposed that the council reacted. this new bricolage reflects the chronic under-budgeting of the union budget for several years. the report rightly deplores the resulting "abnormally high number of unpaid invoices". parliament has been denouncing it in its budgetary resolutions, but to no avail. however, the situation is getting worse and the 2013 budget will still leave almost 20 billion in commitments unpaid. i am voting for this report in order not to prevent the release of funds without which the member states would be exposed to financial penalties. but i deplore the totally chaotic management of the european budget under austerity auspices.
in writing. spain has experienced a sudden collapse in the construction sector following the economic and financial crisis, with unemployment rising to 29% in the valencia region. i therefore supported the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, which specifically provides additional support for workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade.
in writing. i voted in favour of mobilising the egf because spain faces 630 redundancies in 140 enterprises due to a large loss of market shares in the production of other non-metallic mineral products. the commission established the profitability of the union industry by expressing the pre-tax net profit of the sales of the like product to unrelated customers in the union as a percentage of the turnover of those sales. the redundancies in spain are linked to major changes in the structure of international trade, which have led to an increase in imports into the union of other non-metallic mineral products and a reduction in the union's share of the world market in the manufacture of these products.
in writing. the comunidad valenciana is currently facing a number of economic difficulties, mainly due to the rapid developments in world trade. to enable it to cope with this, and to support the workers concerned in these difficult times, i support the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. it is a concrete manifestation of european solidarity.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it seems to me appropriate, in this situation, to call on the european globalisation adjustment fund which was set up to provide additional support to workers suffering the consequences of major changes in the structure of world trade. spain and the valencian community meet the criteria for assistance from the egf because the construction sector has been severely affected by the consequences of the economic crisis and is also subject to strong external competition. such repercussions in this particularly important sector in spain have now greatly aggravated the already fragile situation of the region's labour market. this is why aid seems legitimate to deal with redundancies and to revive employment in this region.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague andrej plenkovic which aims to provide €840 000 to the region of valencia, which has been hit hard by the crisis. the report calls for the mobilisation of these funds to be accelerated, which will benefit 140 enterprises in the region. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of mobilising the european globalisation adjustment fund to the tune of eur 840 000 for spain, which is facing redundancies in the manufacturing of construction materials. the purpose of this legislative instrument is to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in world trade and to assist their reintegration into the labour market.
in writing. the globalisation fund is doing its job well. instead of helping workers, it encourages companies and governments to submit to the dictates of liberal thinking. the example of the comunidad valenciana is a case in point: the construction sector is experiencing a sharp decline due to the massive increase in imports of products directly competing with those manufactured in spain. 630 redundancies occurred in 140 construction companies (non-metallic minerals). it is not a question of blaming the 'crisis' as the spanish government is doing, but of putting in place a solidarity protectionism which will allow the maintenance of an ecologically and socially acceptable industrial activity in europe. i abstain in order not to deprive spanish workers of this fund.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund for the region of valencia, which is currently experiencing significant financial difficulties. the aid will help to co-finance active labour market measures in the region aimed at the reintegration of dismissed workers and the creation of sustainable jobs for the population of the region.
in writing. the agreement on government procurement (gpa) is a multilateral treaty concluded with some members of the world trade organisation (wto) which deals with the conditions for the award of public contracts. i voted in favour of the conclusion of a protocol amending the gpa in order to increase clarity and transparency and to improve its operation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the agreement on public procurement because its main aim is to guarantee its signatories (ec + 14) equal treatment between tenderers for a public contract (regardless of their nationality). its main contribution is to provide legal certainty for eu companies wishing to access foreign markets. it is a major concern that creates a disproportionate feeling. on the one hand we open up our public procurement to foreign competition, but on the other hand there is no principle of reciprocity and national preference applies in third countries. the two improvements made relate to the rules governing invitations to tender (transparency, equal treatment, possibility of using electronic tendering, obligation for the parties to create a central database containing notices of public contracts free of charge, possibility of taking account of the environmental dimension, etc.) and then to the scope of the agreement, including the abolition of sectoral exemptions enjoyed by certain parties (korea, japan, israel, etc.).
in writing. the public procurement agreement is a tool of choice for eu companies to expand into foreign markets. by extending this agreement, we are further reducing the barriers that could prevent them from accessing it, and we are making the rules on public procurement more transparent and effective. this is a real step forward for the competitiveness of all european enterprises, and especially smes.
in writing. multilateral agreements negotiated within the wto must ensure balanced trade relations between states. today, competition with certain third countries in the field of public procurement is neither fair nor equitable. while european markets are open to foreign products and investments, the reverse is not always automatic. the wto agreement on government procurement should therefore allow european companies better access to public procurement in third countries. this agreement should not exempt the union from having its own rules to defend its commercial interests. this will be the subject of the forthcoming reform of trade defence instruments.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i support the conclusion of a protocol amending the previous agreement on public procurement of the world trade organisation. the binding agreement has been renegotiated to adapt to developments in information technology, to broaden its scope and to remove the remaining discriminatory measures. in the course of renegotiating this agreement, the european union has managed to obtain several benefits which i support, including the acquisition of some eur 30 billion in new market access opportunities for our european companies.
in writing. you have described this amendment to the wto agreement on government procurement, which concerns only 15 signatories, as a remarkable step forward. i hope that is not the measure of what you are able to do in the transatlantic negotiations. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. more than 90% of public contracts in the union are now, in fact or in law, unilaterally opened to competition from operators in third countries, compared with only 32% in the united states, 28% in japan and 16% in canada. and the protocol only changes those proportions marginally. a regulation to impose reciprocity in these areas is apparently under consideration. commissioner de gucht even claims that it is necessary, so that we can negotiate on an equal footing with our main partners. but then why did we approve this protocol or sign the agreement with canada, since this means, on the contrary, that in at least these two cases we have been abused, because we are not on the same footing as the others?
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague helmut scholz approving the signing by the european commission of the 1996 public procurement agreement as amended. the main aim of the agreement is to guarantee its signatories (eu+14) equal treatment of tenderers for public contracts, irrespective of their nationality. it thus provides legal certainty for eu companies wishing to access foreign markets. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the amendments to the government procurement agreement, which is the only legally binding agreement of the world trade organisation (wto) dealing with public procurement. this report marks the conclusion of negotiations with stakeholders, including the eu and the us, which started in 1999. this amended version of the agreement is clearer and more transparent, it is closer to the european directives on public procurement and it guarantees european suppliers new market access opportunities.
in writing. this report proposes to ratify the trade agreement negotiated by the commission to further open up national and local public procurement to international competition. in the context of the wto, this agreement extends the number of signatory countries, particularly among the countries of the south. it is therefore welcome that the scholz report offers new trade opportunities for the european union. the committee on development and cooperation also regrets that the trade protection of the southern countries is weakened by this agreement, which fears the "economic and social costs resulting from the loss of public contracts by national companies". more generally, the agreement opens up new sectors of public procurement to international competition, particularly in services and construction. it will repeal some of the localisation clauses applied by certain countries, notably the usa (the 'buy american' rule). the possibility of introducing environmental conditions in tendering procedures is a very small step forward in the face of the risks of this new trade liberalization. it contradicts the efforts to relocate the activity and to promote short purchasing cycles. i am voting against this agreement, which seriously undermines the sovereignty of states in the award of public contracts.
in writing. the 'erasmus for all' or 'erasmus+' programme brings together all existing programmes and actions in the fields of education, training and youth. this programme is essential and i voted in favour of this report because it made it possible, among other things, to provide a new source of funding for sport of eur 240 million, or 1.8% of the total budget for this programme.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of the pack report, which guarantees the european union's commitment to education and youth. young people are the future of europe. this new 'erasmus plus' scheme promotes quality training by extending the previous mobility programmes. this european academic and professional exchange mechanism will now concern not only students but also apprentices, professionals in training, youth association leaders, volunteers and young sportsmen. this programme is the symbol of european unity in its cultural and linguistic diversity. i have chosen to pass on and honour this european heritage. this is a major step forward for european identity, training and employment of young people.
in writing. i strongly supported the adoption of the erasmus+ programme. the guarantee mechanism for loans for master's students is a worrying deviation, but the french socialists have ensured that it is limited in terms of the budget allocated and strictly controlled. two key victories are worth noting. the 40% increase in the budget will enable some 5 million young people to benefit from an experience of mobility abroad, thus improving their skills, especially linguistic ones. the new programme also extends the mobility opportunities for young people in apprenticeship or vocational training, contributing to equal opportunities in europe. with the introduction of the youth guarantee, this new erasmus+ programme is tangible proof that europe has understood the importance of giving all its chances to the young generation.
in writing. with the new erasmus+ programme, europe is moving towards a more dynamic vision of education, and more importantly, one that is better adapted to constantly changing knowledge, techniques and needs. erasmus+ is more coherent: the programme now brings together all youth programmes, whether they concern initial, continuing education or sport, while retaining the strong identity of each programme, including the best known of all, the erasmus for students programme, whose success has marked generations of students. the programme will also focus on reducing administrative burden and simplifying procedures, so a more efficient and accessible programme should emerge. i welcome the fact that some of my proposals have been incorporated into the final text, particularly with regard to the establishment of concrete monitoring and evaluation actions to ensure the full effectiveness of the programme.
in writing. the erasmus and erasmus mundus programmes are two of the european union's outstanding achievements in the field of education and vocational training, which have also helped to forge a sense of belonging and attachment to the european project among the younger generations. the second generation of erasmus for all has made progress in terms of both its structure and its budget. it will no longer be for the benefit of a few hundred thousand privileged people but for students of all ages, apprentices and young workers. the programme also recovers an increase of more than 40% in the allocation for the period 2014-2020, i.e. an overall budget of around €14.7 billion. 4 million young europeans aged 13-30 are expected to benefit from the exchange programme. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this is a welcome step but it is not enough. in the long term, erasmus for all should be offered to a majority of young europeans. this will require the mobilisation of all in the coming years to enable this programme to be a true european federator.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am in favour of this new programme for education, training, youth and sport, which is supposed to be more effective and has a clearer structure to meet the european union's ambitions in this area. i believe it is particularly important to support good education and training conditions for our young people by encouraging learning mobility abroad and encouraging cooperation on good practice and innovation. this is why we must give our young people the means to move around our territory and to live a european experience, thus spreading the feeling of belonging to european citizenship through the discovery of our continent.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which will encourage mobility in the fields of education, training, youth and sport. erasmus for all (or erasmus+) will bring together all the former programmes relating to international mobility in education and training (erasmus, comenius, leonardo da vinci, etc.). this emblematic programme is one of those that really show the added value that europe can bring to its citizens! the simpler and more readable 'erasmus for all' will help to bring the great opportunities of mobility to more young people, notably through a budget increase from previous years, which will reach over €14 billion. in the face of the crisis and the ever-worsening unemployment of young people, it was urgent to implement a youth policy that would strengthen skills and make europe more attractive internationally.
in writing. i have given my full support to the new erasmus+ programme, which will have a stronger budget, with a doubling of mobility grants, and which will ultimately benefit 5 million europeans. i also welcome the adoption of a programme for vocational education and training which also includes this part of education which has long been excluded from european exchanges. i will, however, remain vigilant about the introduction of a loan mechanism for master students: while these loans are accompanied by certain guarantees (such as a reduced interest rate, non-discrimination, etc.), they must nevertheless remain at a low level of the programme (3.5% of the budget) and not encourage young people to take on debt in the future. similarly, the individual mobility of people in the labour market and of adults which was provided by the leonardo and grundtvig programmes is now being transferred to the structural funds, which will require special attention to ensure that the funds can actually be used to finance these mobility actions.
in writing. the erasmus student exchange programme, which has benefited many students, is one of the very few successes of the european union today. it is one of the only european programmes to see its budget increase, while appropriations are being massively cut. in its cruel lack of recognition, the european union has not dared to attack this symbol head-on. the attack is more insidious. it is the very structure of scholarships that is threatened by the programme voted on today by the european parliament. until now, the erasmus programme has only included a grant scheme. from now on, students will be encouraged to take out loans. as unemployment explodes in europe, can we ask our young people to enter the labour market with debt up to their necks? how can you ask a young person to pay off a loan when your first job is an internship paying $470 a month? for this reason i voted against the new version of the erasmus programme submitted to the european parliament, which dangerously paves the way for an american-style university system.

in writing. this new programme for education and training, youth and sport 2014-2020 does have some positive aspects (simplification, combating early school leaving, mass sport). but he is introducing an "erasmus master" through a "student loan guarantee mechanism" the details of which are left to the technocrats. it is a time bomb, institutionalizing student debt at european level, as in the united states, where more than 40% of people under 30 are already in debt after taking out a loan for their studies. it is also a way for the european commission to compete with national scholarships and to give itself a new area of competence, accelerating the bologna process which organises competition and the commercialisation of higher education. i am voting against this sword of damocles over future generations, whose over-indebtedness is already under way, particularly in the countries which are subject to the intervention of the troika.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which establishes a connecting europe facility (cef) because i am convinced that such an instrument will be effective in accelerating investment and mobilising the necessary funding for the development of transport, energy and telecommunications infrastructure. the eic will not only contribute to the europe 2020 strategy by developing trans-european networks that take into account future transport flows and create a more favourable environment for private, public or public-private partnership investments; the commission will also be able to support projects with real european added value. i was particularly attentive to the objective of this mechanism in the transport sector, which is to remove bottlenecks and to establish missing links, particularly for cross-border sections, for all modes of transport. these measures will thus really help to facilitate traffic in our territory and particularly in crossborder regions such as mine. it is through this mechanism that the lgv bordeaux-toulouse line will finally be able to benefit from priority european funds to be completed as soon as possible.
in writing. in the negotiations with the council on the priority transeuropean transport networks (ten-t), the greens succeeded in integrating new criteria: sustainability, social (creating jobs), the need for european added value (the projects financed could not be without europe). that's very positive. i voted against this agreement, however, because there is a total mismatch between these sustainability criteria and the fact that it focuses only on nine corridors, which are strategic, but which have a good chance of being funded anyway. with the €26 billion provided, hundreds of small cross-border projects/infrastructures could be financed. projects that would never be funded without europe's input. this is a real european added value. rather than focusing on megaprojects, the eu's role could be different.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it will make it possible to develop the trans-european transport, energy and telecommunications networks, and thus improve the economic and social cohesion of our territories. the agreement reached between the institutions will provide the connecting europe facility (cef) with an overall budget of €33 billion. i regret, however, that this budget has been reduced by 17 billion compared with the original proposal. these are strategic infrastructures for our economy! infrastructure financed as a priority should have a high added value at union level, be smart, sustainable and benefit all member states and their regions. i am therefore pleased that the lyon-turin railway project has been selected as one of the priority projects in the mediterranean corridor, which will allow for substantial european co-financing. the lyon-turin line for freight and passengers is an essential infrastructure for the attractiveness of the alpine region and a driving force for growth, employment and competitiveness for our companies.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report establishing the connecting europe facility, which aims to accelerate investment in the trans-european transport, energy and telecommunications networks. the €23 billion investment over the period 2014-2020 will make a significant contribution to european economic growth and job creation through investment in transport, energy and telecommunications networks. these are crucial for the internal market and will improve cross-border mobility, interconnection of energy networks to diversify gas supply and explore the possibility of transporting renewable energy.
in writing. this report deals with the 'connecting europe facility' (cef) and sets out the common rules and procedures for the granting of eu financial assistance to trans-european networks in three main areas: transport, energy and telecommunications. these sectors are of primary concern to the general european interest. the commission's aim is not the social and ecological utility of the projects financed, but the completion of the internal market and competitiveness. the objectives are not the right ones. nor are the means used to achieve them, since it is planned to rely for a large part on public-private partnerships. the rapporteur does not question this logic, but rather encourages it. they point to the lack of public funds and call not for more funds but for projects to be sorted out and therefore not to be implemented in part. we must reverse this logic and implement a genuine ecological planning in the service of the general human interest. i am voting against this text.

in writing. with the connecting europe facility, europe is getting a new tool for growth, jobs and competitiveness. investment in transport, energy and telecommunications infrastructure should stimulate hiring at the time of construction, create operating opportunities at commissioning, and increase the attractiveness of the regions concerned. by promoting the interoperability of electricity and gas networks, the text should help to reduce the energy insecurity of the member states. by stimulating the use of intelligent transport systems, it will contribute to the harmonious development of traffic in europe. i therefore voted in favour of the connecting europe facility, especially as it is a powerful instrument for european integration and the creation of sustainable infrastructure. my only regret will be the small budget allocated to this facility (eur 33 billion instead of the 50 requested), which will be only slightly offset by the use of innovative financial instruments, restricted by the will of the member states, despite their ability to raise private funds for projects that meet our political priorities.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on a transeuropean transport network, which will improve the functioning of the current system, which we see is lagging behind and has problems with project financing. the new regulation introduces two distinct objectives: the establishment of a central network by 2030 to link the eu's main urban nodes, its main ports and its border crossing points. the second objective is longer-term: by 2050, it aims to create new roads, which will extend from the central level to the regional and national levels.
in writing. the commission conceives the transeuropean transport network as a means of linking together large areas which are generally very attractive and often already well connected. the aim is to enable the people of the union, but also and above all goods, to move quickly from one end of europe to the other within the framework of the european single market. although targets for reducing greenhouse gases are mentioned, they are not binding. the rapporteur for parliament improves the text in the margins, in particular by taking into account areas with a low population density and by adding the notion of 'contribution [of transport] to well-being'. unfortunately, it is useless to improve a text with bad background, bad aims and bad methods. we must have a real ecological planning system, with short-distance transport being the priority, and where short-distance transport is not possible, infrastructure must be created to enable goods to be transported over long distances in an environmentally friendly way. the text of parliament is not up to the social and ecological challenges of our time. i vote against it.

in writing. the purpose of this report is to extend the eu's support for three decommissioning projects in bulgaria, lithuania and slovakia. the european union is once again faced with a situation which illustrates the dangers of nuclear power and, above all, the large amount of unknowns surrounding it. even if decommissioning is only one aspect of the major problem facing nuclear power, this report is necessary to fill the initial gaps in these decommissioning projects. it draws some conclusions from these failures, particularly in the follow-up of the steps taken to decommission and distribute the funds. it is not, however, concerned with the dangers and the impossibility of managing the nuclear risk under acceptable conditions of safety and environmental protection. furthermore, since decommissioning of nuclear power stations is largely an unknown activity and the funds provided cover only one fifth of the estimated additional costs, additional aid is likely to be needed. i am voting for this report in order to contribute to the denuclearisation of these countries.
