i'm the reporter. - mr president, commissioner responsible for the internal market and services, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow the european parliament will express its position on the proposal for a regulation on the key information document on investment products. in its communication of april 2009 on retail packaged investment products prips , the commission identified two areas for further development: rules on sales and rules on product information. the current proposal is the result of work on the latter and is part of a wider package of legislative measures aimed at restoring consumer confidence in financial markets, building on a thorough review of the insurance intermediation directive and strengthening the depositary function for ucits. the product information measures contained in this draft regulation complement, in particular, those on investor protection concerning investment advice and sales services within the meaning of the mfi directives and regulations. i have argued from the beginning of the parliamentary debate that the key information document should not be intended primarily to help product initiators sell products, but to inform retail investors to make an appropriate investment decision. this led me to believe that the commission's original proposal could not be limited to packaged products alone. that is why i have proposed that its scope be extended to equities, interest rate based savings products, including sovereign and corporate bonds, term bank accounts and life insurance. as the commission proposal stands, even though the title of the draft regulation covers all investment products, there is a risk that the key information document will encourage smaller investors to buy more complex financial products whose contribution to the financing of the real economy is questionable. in order to secure a large majority in the european parliament, i proposed, just a month ago, at the time of the vote in the committee on economic and monetary affairs, a compromise which would finally exclude shares and sovereign bonds from the scope of application, while maintaining corporate bonds and financial instruments issued by securitisation institutions. the amendment tabled by some members of the epp group to exclude life insurance contracts has been rejected. beyond the scope issue, the european parliament's negotiating team made a useful contribution to improving the commission's draft regulation by stressing that indicative scenarios for future performance should be based on a multifactor analysis rather than relying solely on a risk indicator based on past performance data. the european parliament's different sensibilities also reflected on the information to be provided on the impact of the investment product in terms of environmental, social and governance criteria, which are now essential elements that the retail investor should take into account when making his investment decision. three other issues have been raised and remain sensitive for certain groups, but they seem to me to be essential to the objective pursued, namely that of effective consumer information and protection in the context of their investment decision. firstly, it is a question of the possibility for national and european supervisory authorities to harmonize their powers so as to give them the possibility of temporarily suspending or prohibiting the marketing of investment products which would prove to be dangerous. the second proposal is for a complexity label to be established for products with highly complex characteristics. the third proposal is to verify the compatibility of the characteristics of these products with the target investors. finally, i considered it necessary to supplement the information provided by the product initiator with that provided by the distributor as regards the costs of the investment, which may vary from one distributor to another. i hope that on this basis parliament will give us a broad negotiating mandate tomorrow so that we can complete this legislation during the current term.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, minister, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by expressing my thanks to a number of people for the words of the previous speaker. the work we are reporting today is of course a collective work, a long, rich, extremely interesting work which undoubtedly marks a new page in the history of the cap, since this is the first time that parliament, the representative of the peoples, has been fully involved in the preparation of this political act. i would also like to say a word to my coordinator, mr albert deß, since i was a new member of parliament during this term and he trusted me with a report which was not anecdotal. the new cap is marked first of all - and this is regrettable, it is a decision of the heads of state and government - by a reduction in the available appropriations, the budget of the states and the budget of the cap. nevertheless, we had an obligation to do better and better. we have, through the report on the common organization of the market, preserved the market orientation of european agriculture, while giving more resources and room for manoeuvre to the actors, producers and sectors. the safety net will take account not only of changes in production costs but also, for the first time, of changes in profit margins. the safeguard clause, which is introduced for all sectors, will make it possible to react quickly when there are serious disturbances on the market. finally, the creation of a crisis reserve, which unfortunately is fed by a levy on the first pillar, will enable us to act. we've been bringing new solutions to a number of productions. we have introduced the milk package even though, in the view of parliament, the decisions taken do not go far enough, and we have not yet taken the necessary decisions. we are counting on you, commissioner, to make new proposals because we do not think that the current tools are sufficient - despite what some players in the sector say - to really follow up on the end of the quota system. the sugar sector will be subject to new provisions from 2017. we wanted to preserve a negotiating framework that works between the players in the sector. agreements between sugar undertakings and producers will continue to be developed within a community framework. finally, the wine sector, which should not have been dealt with, is a sector for which parliament has fought at the request of many members, irrespective of the wine-growing regions of our countries. the authorisation system in place until 2030 will allow for better demand management but will also allow for a balance between supply and demand. finally, as the public authorities put less money on the table, it was i think extremely important to allow the actors to talk to each other and act together. this will be possible through agreements signed by producer organisations and interbranch organisations which will be in line with competition law. finally, the last point i would like to mention is the issue of export refunds, a subject which is being debated, on which there are sometimes different positions when we are here in the house or when we are on the ground. we've secured an agreement to back up this tool in case of a crisis. i thank all those who have contributed to this balance, this new balance between the north and the south of europe, because i believe that the introduction of parliament into the debate has also made it possible to rebalance policies by taking better account of the aspirations of the different peoples who make up our union.
the committee on regional development has tabled a number of amendments to the proposal. - madam president, commissioner, we regret the agreement reached in the trilogues, which marks the end of sugar quotas for 2017. it is a revolution that is operated when you know that for decades the whole system was based on guaranteed prices and quotas. from now on, in my region, on the island of reunion, sugarcane growers will be subject to fluctuations in international prices and it is the stock exchanges that will hold in their hands the fate of thousands of sugarcane growers and the development of our islands, organized around this traditional sector. however, commissioner, as you saw during your visit to réunion, the cane sector has achieved a high level of performance and has the resources to cope with this shock. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
for the gue/ngl group madam president, commissioner, is this reform of the common agricultural policy meeting the challenges of the moment? the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. no, because the law of the jungle of the world market will continue to dictate agricultural prices to producers, since this cap still refuses to fix basic prices for small farms. it just consents to create a meager safety net. for example, the protection of our products and the environment? no, because the free trade law, which allows the import of gm soybeans or north american beef under intensive conditions, will not compensate for the greening "measures" proposed here. and this will be aggravated tomorrow with the free trade agreement with canada, or even the transatlantic single market or the agreement with mercosur. the ones for greater social justice? nor is it because the proposal we have defended for modulation of aid and a ceiling on public aid has been defeated, particularly by the council. fortunately, this can be somewhat tempered by the possibility of granting a premium for the first hectares, at the request of the french government, as well as by increasing aid to young farmers and by defining the concept of 'active agriculture'. on the other hand, milk quotas will be abolished, against family farms, which will encourage the industrialisation of milk production in europe. the challenges posed by the necessity of embarking on a process of environmental transition, which is necessarily long, taking account of climate change, concerned with the sustainable management of agricultural and water resources, which requires new instruments, new incentive tools at the service of the working peasants in the interests of society as a whole, are also not being addressed despite the initial proposals you made, commissioner. instead of contributing to solidarity, the council has pressed for budget cuts and our parliament unfortunately accepted this yesterday. in the end, this is a serious missed opportunity to establish a new peasant agriculture, rich in jobs, revitalizing the territories, guaranteeing the quality, security and food sovereignty that we lack.
madam president, commissioner, i would first of all like to denounce the lack of respect for democracy in this final vote on the cap. president schulz's attitude of voting the texts directly, in blocks, so that the last amendments tabled are not discussed is unacceptable and says a lot about his vision of democracy. the cap voted today maintains injustices between farmers by refusing to cap aid. a handful of big farmers will continue to receive millions as europe goes through an unprecedented social and economic crisis. but this cap maintains the injustices between farmers in the different member states. it misses the ecological conversion by rejecting the introduction of a crop rotation including a pulse crop. it sabotages rural development by allowing member states to recover up to 25% of this envelope for payments under the first pillar. it endorses the re-nationalisation of the cap and exacerbates competition between farmers in different regions. it undermines the only common policy we have managed to put in place by allowing member states to nationalise it. unfortunately, it does not strengthen the power of farmers in negotiations with large retailers and large companies. finally, i hope that the work on delegated acts will allow for real transparency and real dialogue before they are put in place. perhaps we can, through these delegated acts on agriculture, initiate new work at european level. i would also like to say that, despite the attitude of the agri-food lobbies, despite the selfishness of the countries, we have made it possible to start a new agricultural policy, at least in its spirit. i would like to commend the role of commissioner cioloş, who has put forward a number of ideas. i am now giving you an appointment to start the long-awaited reform: the cap by 2020. answer is "blue cardboard". it is clear that the way in which president schulz refused to take account of the few amendments tabled which did not call into question the duration of the debate, is an unacceptable attitude. the fact that we want to vote as a group, without taking amendments into account beforehand, is something that cannot be described and is contrary to the spirit of this parliament.
madam president, while aid to farmers is essential for the maintenance and development of agriculture and rural areas, it cannot in itself constitute a genuine agricultural policy. by limiting itself to the distribution of aid, by liquidating the last quotas for milk in 2015 and for sugar beet in 2017, and by refusing to put in place a policy of price and volume regulation, the cap 2014-2020 definitively abdicates its role as agricultural policy by completing the deregulation process started 20 years ago. this cap gives free rein to social dumping, which is currently ravaging french agriculture and seriously destabilizing european agriculture. because today, some of the most brutal attacks are coming from certain member countries. i would like to mention just one example: germany, which has a policy of mass supply in the pig sector, based on an hourly labour cost of less than 4 euros, both in the farms and in the slaughterhouses. this regular offensive to take over the markets of other member states is totally unacceptable. yet, for years, nothing has been done to stop it. and what will the new cap weigh tomorrow in relation to the free trade agreements negotiated with canada and the united states? i didn't say anything. we know that the production costs of farmers across the atlantic are up to 25% lower than ours and that they also benefit from the advantages of a currency that is weaker than the euro on export markets. finally, nothing is said about the unbearable pressure that large-scale distribution is putting on the margins of our farmers.
mr president, commissioner, i would like to congratulate parliament on the work it has done in its new role as co-legislator. we have not achieved the perfect reform that i, as a socialist, could have imagined, but we have made real progress. progress for equity, for greening, for regulation. in a crisis, we need to be more vigilant than ever about the legitimacy of public support. we must start from the assumption that 80% of the aid went to 20% of the farmers. we must get rid of the policy of supporting the agricultural pension. at the moment of this debate, in my country, france, the farmers who are demonstrating today are those who have the highest incomes, which seems to me totally inappropriate. this reform, although it does not go far enough, initiates a process towards employment, added value and income, by abandoning historical references, a significant internal convergence and a surplus of the first hectares, as well as the ceiling, which, for the first time, has become mandatory beyond 150 000 euros. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. we shall therefore have to see what choice is made by the member states, although i would have preferred that this ceiling or choice be made at union level. we must now prepare for the future reform, as has already been said, in order to go further on the initiative taken by the text we are presenting today. i would like to conclude by calling for vigilance, as has also been said by previous speakers, on the question of delegated acts. we cannot, commissioner, when drafting delegated acts, fundamentally go beyond the content of the reform which was adopted at the end of the trilogues between the council, parliament and the commission.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, with a budget of over eur 400 billion for the next programming period, the cap remains the first european policy. only five years ago - i will remind you - it was almost accepted that this support for our agriculture should be abolished. this is a very important policy: today we are affirming our commitment to a sustainable and competitive agricultural model. we support our farmers' commitment to environmental protection while strengthening the competitiveness of their businesses. we are also focusing on young farmers by setting up a youth entry support for farmers under 40. the reform also provides safety nets to reduce the volatility of commodity prices. the market for our agricultural products must be regulated. in this connection, it is important to remember that, in the context of trade agreements, we will not accept the entry of agricultural products which do not comply with our health, social and environmental standards on the european market. you see who i'm talking about. it is now up to the french authorities to make good decisions on the allocation of aid at national level. the capping of aid to the largest farmers is a first step. i would nevertheless suggest that certain sectors of agriculture which are better off than others should show solidarity and allow the creation of a specific livestock aid by giving up part of the funds which could be theirs under the direct aid per hectare. this aid will support our farmers in the economic and structural crisis they are going through.
the rapporteur. - mr president, 'unity in diversity' is the motto of europe. this is probably the motto we are really putting into practice in this reform of the cap. the fact is that in a europe of 28 countries, the reality of the environment, the sociological perception of the agricultural question, the relationship with food in our different countries are different, and yet we are together in building the future. i think we have built a project-based cap rather than a shop-shop cap. the question now is to build a cap that enables farmers to act and professional organisations to act. the budget to be implemented is 100 euros per capita per year. we all need to remember that. this is a choice made by the european taxpayer, since the consumer does not want to pay for his products at the real price. we can see the excitement caused by the increase of a few cents in the price of bread. at the end of this very long work, i would like to thank the commissioner once again for his attention and for his personal contribution to this reform. i'd also like to thank the team that surrounded me. parliament's work is not finished: we must now be the guarantors of the political agreement. we will be watching the delegated acts, commissioner, but we will also be watching, mr president-in-office, how the states will react to this agreement. we must ensure, in particular, that competition law is applied uniformly in our various countries. we must ensure that the barriers we have sought to re-establish to prevent europe from being a sieve for certain products coming from outside, with production ratios that have nothing to do with those we impose on our producers, are respected.

in writing. i abstain on this report on european satellite radio navigation systems, which refers to the galileo programme and its financing from the european budget. galileo, a european initiative to give the eu its own global satellite navigation system, provides highly accurate data under civilian control. galileo could be used for military and surveillance purposes; that's why i don't support this satellite navigation system. although it is a priori independent of us control, i am cautious about the possible dual use of this system.
in writing. to ensure the independence and sovereignty of the european union vis-à-vis the united states, it is important that the eu has its own satellite radio navigation system, and the galileo and egnos programmes are moving in the right direction by ensuring better continuity of service. unfortunately, this report does not define democratic control of this programme in a satisfactory way and it even limits its scope. for the project to be fully cohesive, it should not be reduced to a mere technical independence but should be part of a more comprehensive political strategy and a european defence programme detached from nato, a dimension excluded from the report which is limited to a specifically civilian definition of the solution. i therefore abstain in order to denounce this lack of ambition.
in writing. this report supports the proposal for a regulation to establish a governance framework to ensure the success of the european galileo and egnos programmes. the first is a satellite radio navigation system project, while the second will improve galileo's accuracy. the aim is to ensure european independence from the us gps and the russian glonass, while at the same time offering important research prospects. these two factors justified my support for this report.
in writing. i think it cannot be said enough: the success of the european construction is measured by the public recognition it receives. in the industrial field, aeronautics and space are by far the best examples. our constituency is also at the forefront of this, since it is the seat of very large companies. it is therefore essential that europe should take on major industrial projects. space still offers us enormous prospects. it is therefore logical that galileo and egnos should be supported for the next financial period. however, the funding and governance framework for european programmes needed to be revised in order to bring them up to date and make them more operational. but it's done now.
in writing. today, we no longer need to look at a map at every street corner to make sure we are driving in the right direction. driving in unfamiliar terrain is thus made smoother and safer, all thanks to an american invention - gps. however, access to this valuable and indispensable tool is not guaranteed. it is the property of the us department of defense, which can alter its signal at any time for strategic reasons. this strong dependence on the us tool has led the eu to develop its own satellite navigation system, galileo. while espionage practices have reignited tensions between the eu and the us, this policy of independence is taking on a special significance. in total, galileo will have 30 satellites, which, combined with the european ground stations (egnos), will provide much better geolocation than the american gps. the first tests of the european system reveal a quality of satellite radio navigation beyond expectations, so it is with great conviction, and not without a sense of pride, that i voted for the galileo commissioning budget.
in writing. the eu-jordan relations are part of the european neighbourhood policy and the eu-jordan euro-mediterranean association agreement. the arab spring and the influx of syrian refugees into jordanian territory have had a serious impact on the jordanian economy, and i believe that solidarity should be shown and i support this decision to grant macrofinancial assistance to jordan.
in writing. i voted in favour of macro-financial assistance to jordan. eu macro-financial assistance is an exceptional crisis response instrument that the eu makes available to neighbourhood countries, and is conditional on compliance with an economic programme supported by the imf. the decision provides for macro-financial assistance to jordan in the form of loans for a maximum total amount of eur 180 million over a maximum period of 15 years. the eu will therefore only lend the amount that will be repaid.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague vital moreira. this report concerns the commission's proposal to grant macro-financial assistance of eur 180 million to jordan. in view of the situation in jordan, the macro-financial assistance should be disbursed swiftly. this assistance will demonstrate the european union's political and financial support for the transitions taking place in the arab spring countries. it should also be recalled that jordan has been facing massive arrivals of refugees from the syrian conflict for the past two years. more than 550,000 refugees have been registered so far. the country is facing a critical budgetary situation. the union's macro-financial assistance shall be implemented in accordance with the union's macro-financial assistance programmes. the report was adopted by 626 votes in favour, 50 against and 13 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the european union is considering providing jordan with macro-financial assistance (mfa) of eur 180 million in the form of a medium-term loan. this aid is intended to contribute to the economic stabilisation and reforms of the country. however, the granting of this mfa is always complementary to the imf programme programme, with a conditionality. in 2012, the jordanian government decided to introduce a 6% fuel tax and remove octane subsidies, as requested by the imf. many protests have taken place, as these subsidies are vital for the workers and the poor. in 2013 new measures are planned, such as the increase in the price of diesel and kerosene, which will again affect the workers and the popular strata. i therefore vote against this conditional aid.
in writing. i voted in favour of eu aid to jordan of €180 million to support the transition of one of the arab spring countries. jordan is facing particular difficulties in the context of the syrian conflict, as it is hosting a massive influx of refugees. this assistance is part of the broader context of the eu's engagement in the context of the syrian conflict.
in writing. the resolution proposes macrofinancial assistance to jordan in the form of a loan of up to eur 180 million (at 9%, repayable over 15 years). this loan is obviously conditional. the text thus evokes the respect for democratic mechanisms or the importance of the fight against women's unemployment, but without asserting itself in the face of the authoritarian monarchy in place. on the other hand, respect for the liberal doxa is widely recalled. the aim of the macrofinancial assistance (mfa) is to force the country to comply with the adjustment and reform programmes agreed with the imf. under the control of the commission and the imf, which ensure that 'structural reforms' are respected. this european loan will increase the country's debt, at a time when it would be necessary to mobilize to cancel it at least in part. since 2007, when the amf was set up, the eu has acted as the imf's watchdog in its neighbourhood. the union for the mediterranean project is no longer limited to the creation of a large free trade area with free and undistorted competition. i vote against it.
in writing. macro-financial assistance is an exceptional crisis response instrument that the eu makes available to neighbouring countries. it is subject to compliance with an economic programme receiving financial support from the imf. the regulation will allow the eu to grant temporary financial assistance to jordan to cope with the influx of syrian refugees on its territory. as the fictitious rapporteur for this text for my group, i was able to attend the final negotiations with the european commission and the council. the consensus was reached very quickly, both between the political groups present and between the institutions: jordan has sufficient guarantees and, above all, this one-off aid meets a real need.
in writing. as part of my commitment to combating drugs in all their forms, i supported this draft decision which aims to conclude an agreement between the eu and the russian federation to improve the monitoring of the trade in drug precursors, which are free but regulated products and are used in the manufacture of many drugs.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the eu-russia agreement on drug precursors. the eu is also considering the possibility of extending the scope of the eu's cooperation with russia to include the eu's neighbours in the region. russia and its vast territory are fairly easily crossed by drugs from certain middle eastern countries. the most famous trafficking is opium from afghanistan, which later feeds all other trafficking in europe, whether it is the mafia, organized crime, trafficking in women, arms trade, etc.
in writing. i voted for the proust report ratifying the agreement signed on 4 june 2013 between the european union and russia on the monitoring of trade in drug precursors. the control of trade in chemicals which can be used for the manufacture of narcotic drugs must be strengthened. the report thus lays a solid foundation for mutual assistance between russia and the union so that drug precursors are not diverted from the legal trade. the emphasis is therefore on the need for scientific and technical cooperation and the exchange of data between the two parties.
in writing. i welcome this agreement, which aims to strengthen the surveillance of drug precursors in the framework of trade cooperation between the eu and russia. these legal substances, which are sometimes converted into synthetic drugs, must be subject to increased surveillance in the framework of our partnership with russia. this is an important step towards closer relations with russia and should be welcomed.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am in favour of closer cooperation with russia on the monitoring of the trade in drug precursors. these legal substances can be dangerous because they can be used in the chemical process of manufacturing synthetic drugs, including heroin. in order to protect our citizens from drug trafficking, i therefore support increased surveillance, including pre-export notification by the exporting country, followed by a three-week period during which the importing country may oppose the entry of this product into its territory for security reasons.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation by my colleague, mr franck proust, to ratify an agreement between the eu and russia signed on 4 june to monitor products used in the manufacture of drugs. the agreement, which has already been concluded with 10 other countries, will make it possible to combat drug trafficking more effectively. i am therefore pleased that this recommendation has been adopted by a very large majority.
in writing. i voted in favour of the eu-russia agreement to combat the diversion of chemicals that can be used as precursors in the manufacture of drugs. the agreement with russia provides for increased monitoring of trade in these products and an exchange of information between the parties.
in writing. this proposal for an agreement between the european union and the russian federation aims to improve cooperation in the surveillance of trade in drug precursors. these precursors are legal substances that can be used in the chemical process of manufacturing synthetic drugs. for example, acetic acid is used in the manufacture of heroin. the russian federation is one of the main producers of precursors used in the production of drugs. it is therefore important to strengthen cooperation between the european union and the russian federation. however, the report stresses the need to avoid any 'protectionism' and not to impede the free movement of these products. the mutual assistance mechanism envisaged takes the form of an exchange of data, some of which are confidential, which leads to a reservation on this agreement. the commission notes that the russian authorities have not provided any evidence that the measures in question are imputable to the state. i'm not going to.
in writing. the report focuses on the eu-russia agreement to improve cooperation between the two countries in the surveillance of drug precursor trade. precursors are legal chemicals that are highly sought after by traffickers who divert them from the market to make synthetic drugs (amphetamines, heroin, etc.). i therefore decided to vote in favour of this eu-russia agreement because it would make it possible to monitor the trade in drug precursors more closely and thus reduce the possibilities for the manufacture of synthetic drugs.
in writing. it is for the council to determine which third states and organisations europol shall conclude agreements with. however, given that the commission has recently made a proposal for a new regulation on europol, i voted in favour of parliament's legislative resolution asking the council not to adopt this decision and the europol management board not to enter into negotiations with the states covered by this decision until stricter security guarantees, contained in the new commission proposal, are adopted.
in writing. i voted in favour of the legislative resolution to reject the draft council decision on the list of third states and organisations with which europol has agreements. we believe that this decision should be adopted under the ordinary legislative procedure (and therefore the european parliament should not only be consulted). moreover, the text as it stands does not sufficiently protect fundamental rights.
in writing. i voted against this text: yes, europol's mission is crucial and the list of states and organisations with which europol concludes agreements should be adapted. but europol is currently undergoing a reform, the text of which is being studied. there is no point in promoting doubt and instability by voting on a text that could be changed in a few months. this would only increase the lack of understanding and mistrust of the european institutions. i also support the emphasis in this text on the need to strengthen data protection.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it may be beneficial for europol services to extend the list of countries with which it can conclude agreements to brazil, the united arab emirates, georgia and mexico. nevertheless, i support the rapporteur's concerns about the level of data protection in these states, which should lead us to be vigilant in concluding potential agreements.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague philip claeys. europol's management board decided to recommend to the council that brazil, georgia, mexico and the united arab emirates be added to the list of third states and organisations with which europol has agreements. the report proposes to reject the council's proposal as parliament is currently discussing a new europol regulation which could change the provisions governing the conclusion of agreements with third states and organisations, as well as the procedure for doing so. the report was adopted by 679 votes in favour, 11 against and 4 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. i voted in favour of the decision proposing that the council reject a cooperation agreement between europol and four third countries. the legal basis for europol is currently being examined by the european institutions. the commission will amend the conditions attached to international agreements. it is more appropriate to wait for the adoption of the new legal basis of europol to take this decision.
in writing. this report opposes the draft council decision on additions to the list of states and third countries with which europol has agreements. the countries are brazil, georgia, mexico and the united arab emirates. in the case of eu police cooperation with third countries via europol, it is necessary to ensure that the countries with which the eu concludes agreements offer all the guarantees of respect for freedoms. this is not the case in georgia or the united arab emirates. the recent scandal of the giant nsa spying on european governments and institutions should lead to a strengthening of the precautionary principle in the protection of personal data, both within the eu itself and in relations between the eu and third parties. that is why i am voting for it.
in writing. in december 2012, the council made a legislative proposal to add four third states (brazil, mexico, georgia and the united arab emirates) to the list of countries with which europol may negotiate and conclude cooperation agreements. the council has competence under the european decision on the establishment and operation of europol, but the treaty of lisbon has entered into force and requires the european parliament to give its consent to any international agreement of the eu. i therefore voted in favour of rejecting the council's request. i do not support this council proposal because the least that can be said is that these four states do not provide all the guarantees in the field of human rights. moreover, it seems to me surprising to put the negotiation of agreements in such a sensitive area in the hands of an agency. international police cooperation is necessary but too important to be left to the european police cooperation agency alone, and this in a political context of increasing security and repression.
in writing. the community legal framework for a consortium for a european research infrastructure needs to be amended, so i have voted in favour of this parliament's legislative resolution which approves the commission's proposal on this subject.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it will make it possible to establish at eu level a new legal instrument allowing the creation of european research infrastructures with legal personality and recognised in all member states.
in writing. this text will open the consortium for a european research infrastructure to new partners: it will therefore be a crucial instrument towards a dynamic and innovative research europe, and i therefore welcome its adoption.
in writing. i voted in favour of this draft to encourage the opening up of this regulation to europe's neighbours. it is worth noting that countries such as norway, which is a member of efta, already participate in many agreements and programmes with the eu. it therefore seemed to me logical to open the eric regulation to our european partners in order to increase the sharing of competences.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague amalia sartori. this report concerns the proposal for a council regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 723/2009 on a community legal framework for a european research infrastructure consortium (eric). the report was adopted by 658 votes in favour, 17 against and 10 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the community legal framework for a consortium for a european research infrastructure. the technical amendments proposed by the european commission should allow for better account to be taken, through their voting rights, of the involvement of third countries or associated countries in erics.
in writing. currently, half of total research expenditure is in 30 of 254 regions and a majority of the projects listed by the eu under this framework are concentrated in only 10 member states. this amendment to the regulation may therefore allow other countries in europe, outside the european union, to join these european research infrastructure consortia (erics) and vote on an equal footing with the member states. in terms of scientific output, europe remains the world's largest centre for r & d after the united states; the european union has a strong interest in working towards greater sharing of grey matter across the continent. however, erics are linked to horizon 2020, which focuses on a short-term vision of research and aims to bring new economic products to the market. for that reason, i abstain.
in writing. this regulation lays down the rules applicable to 5 european funds which are of great importance to europeans: the european regional development fund, the european social fund, the cohesion fund, the european agricultural fund for rural development and the european maritime and fisheries fund. having contributed to the preparation of this report myself, as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on the environment, i welcome the modernisation, the slight greening of the rules applicable to these funds and the creation of the category of regions in transition (financial benefit to 10 french regions, including auvergne and limousin). i therefore voted in favour of this report. however, i would have liked the simplification of the rules to go much further, for example through genuine trust contracts to reduce controls. in addition, it would have been desirable to provide for the money for the european social fund (esf) to represent at least 25% of eu cohesion policy. in france, this share is traditionally much higher and this is a good thing because it is important to invest in training and developing the skills of workers.
in writing. cohesion policy is an essential element of social and territorial cohesion. the structural funds are a genuine redistributive instrument, and it is through them that citizens benefit from the eu in a concrete way. however, i voted against the outcome of the negotiations on the 2014-2020 cohesion package for one main reason: because the 25% originally provided for the european social fund is not in the final text. in these times of crisis, the european social fund, which has a vital role to play, should be strengthened. the social emergency in europe would require greater commitment to strengthening social inclusion, vocational integration and the fight against poverty. i therefore deeply regret this bad signal to the european citizens.
in writing. i voted against the compromise which takes up the whole of the agreement reached in the trilogue (amendment 488) so that i can then vote in favour of the amendments which raise the minimum share of the european social fund to 25% (amendments 468 and 469). unfortunately, the compromise has been approved. the esf has already had to provide the funding not originally planned for: - the youth employment initiative (yei) with eur 3 billion and - the eafrd with eur 3.5 billion, a total of eur 6.5 billion from the initial esf budget. the battle for the minimum 25% share of cohesion policy funds was therefore more topical than ever to fill the budget gap needed to support employment policies within the european union. the european social fund has been an effective policy for re-employment since the treaties of rome. since 2008, the crisis has reinforced its need. the esf is jobs for all!
in writing. i voted in favour of the agreement reached by parliament and the council on the common regulation on cohesion policy. the adoption of the new cohesion policy is a strong signal for growth in europe. the structural funds will represent 325 billion euros of investment in our territories over the period 2014-2020. the creation of the category of 'regions in transition' is in line with the principle of greater fairness in the distribution of aid. this category offers appropriate support to regions that are neither too rich nor too poor. the new cohesion policy will also be better targeted through thematic concentration and conditionality. we must move from a shop-shop approach to a project approach, with a focus on investments that create jobs and growth. as regards the european social fund, however, i would have preferred that its budget should be at least 25% because employment must be the union's priority.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of these common provisions governing cohesion policy instruments. they are key tools in supporting the cohesion and competitiveness of our territories, in their diversity. upgrading them will increase their efficiency and ensure that they have the best possible impact.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i believe it is important to adopt an effective framework for the european union's cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020. the various european funds contain common provisions which need to be highlighted in order to achieve a coherent and clear policy. simplification is the key. i am therefore in favour of a common strategic framework (csf) defining the means of addressing the main territorial challenges, as well as the means of ensuring coordination with other relevant cooperation policies and activities of the union. in this way, european funds can then be used appropriately to benefit our fellow citizens more effectively. moreover, by concentrating these funds on a limited number of common objectives, while leaving some room for manoeuvre, the regions will be better able to meet their specific needs.
in writing. i did not vote for any of the reports on european funds to finance the european union's regional policy. the new regional policy is supposed to be more efficient and rational than the previous one. sometimes there are even good things. but it is still basically a policy of profiteering and patronage, aimed at creating political and financial links of dependence between the brussels bureaucracy and subnational entities, while concealing the states. it has another defect: it aims to implement the eu 2020 strategy which consists, among other things, and not only, in 'flexibilising' the labour market, thus making workers more precarious, and finally handing over to competition what remains of public services. finally, it has a perverse effect: its compulsory co-financing is an incentive to public spending, as the reports on the countries in difficulty - greece, spain, etc. - half-heartedly admit. the choice of programmes financed is more often based on their ability to benefit from european funding than on their actual economic and social utility. in short, it is a costly mechanism for european propaganda.
in writing. i abstained on this report. the advances are notorious and the greens have had many victories. the regional funds for 2014-2020 will make it possible to invest massively in the energy transition, against exclusion and poverty. however, these gains are being undermined by a drastic 8% cut in the budget for regional policy, which is a way out of the crisis and an investment in the future. another shadow in the picture is the rule of macro-conditionality, which will make this policy a sanctioning tool to enforce the sacred and holy fiscal stability pact. by making public deficits a condition for the disbursement of funds, this macroeconomic clause holds the regions hostage, even though they are not responsible for the economic governance of their state.
in writing. i supported this report, but voted against the amendment which provides for allocating to the european social fund (esf) only a minimum of 21.3% of the cohesion policy funds, whereas i had voted for a minimum of 25%. i very much regret the lack of ambition in the text adopted in the face of the scale of the challenges to be faced, and i deplore the fact that the french government has not been able to defend the 25% objective during the interinstitutional negotiations. the european social fund is one of the european union's main instruments for citizens. it is intended to combat unemployment and precariousness and is aimed in particular at young people, whose unemployment rate in some eu countries is over 50%! it also contributes to the european food aid fund, which helps millions of europeans who are food insecure. in the midst of the economic crisis, strong and effective support must be provided to the most vulnerable of our fellow citizens. to combat the unemployment problem, europe could have done better than a discount agreement!
in writing. after more than two years of negotiations, the european parliament has finally adopted the cohesion policy regulations with a budget of €325 billion for the next seven years. france will receive €14.3 billion, a figure that remains stable compared with the previous period. i am glad that the creation of transition regions, a proposal which i supported in the committee on regional development, has been approved because it will enable ten of our french regions, including auvergne, to benefit from more european aid. of course, they would have every interest in being among the best performing regions in europe, but this depends above all on the strategic and public policy choices of our regional councils. however, the late adoption of these regulations raises concerns that the implementation of the operational programmes will take place in the middle of 2014, which will cause regrettable delays. i therefore expect the regional councils to be responsible for managing european aid for transparency in the management of funds and especially in the selection of projects.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleagues lambert van nistelrooij and constanze angela krehl, which sets out the framework for a new regional policy, based on objectives and priorities, while allowing for some flexibility in the use of funds. one of the main new features is the introduction of macroeconomic conditionality, which can lead, as a last resort, to a partial suspension of payments in the event of persistent non-compliance with the principles of sound public expenditure management. i welcome the adoption of this report by a large majority of 479 votes in favour, 126 against and 85 abstentions.
in writing. the italian delegation voted against the legislative package which refused to put to the vote some important amendments related to macroeconomic conditionality. we cannot accept a block on the spending of the structural funds for all those economies, many of the italian regions, which have to submit to the rigidity of the stability pact. the introduction of the amendments we requested was in the direction of greater flexibility which could allow the exclusion of investment-related expenditure from the calculation of the deficit/gdp ratio. it would have been significant and consistent with the announcements made in the past about less short-sighted austerity to ensure that this did not happen, among other things, by a forcing by the presidency at the time of the indication of the voting procedure.
in writing. i voted against the report by van nistelrooij (epp, netherlands) and krehl (s&d, germany) on the provisioning of the european funds. this report was presented with the cohesion policy package. it is in particular within this envelope that the eu's social actions are financed. this is one of the areas which has suffered the most cuts in the new budgetary framework. the transfer of solidarity funds to competitiveness programmes was a priority of the european right with the idea of using these funds as incentives to the commission's economic objectives. the report on the provisions for the european funds incorporates several new tools into cohesion policy: macroeconomic conditionality, including a coercive component that may lead to the suspension of commitments and payments; the 'performance reserve' which conditions 6% of funds to results and performance. the minimum threshold for the european social fund is set at 23.1%, whereas even the commission wanted it to be close to 25%. i therefore spoke out against this coercive aspect of conditionality and this instrumentalisation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the common provisions for the european funds, which provide for better synergy between the funds, but also with other funds such as horizon 2020, life, etc. implementation rules have also been simplified and management, control and evaluation systems have been strengthened.
in writing. my comrades in the gue fought hard to get the references to the european stability mechanism (esm) removed from the text. they got it and i consider that a great thing. however, in my view, this is not enough to turn a bad text into a good text. the regulation extends macroeconomic and financial conditionality to all european funds: in other words, it will allow the commission to suspend payments to a state in the event of non-compliance with the enhanced austerity standards of the stability pact. i also disapprove of the use of gdp/capita as an indicator of development, the multiple references to public-private partnerships, the use of financial instruments which will serve as new income for the private sector and the veto power of the commission at every stage of the implementation of the funds, the willingness to push for the movement of workers without having first worked for the harmonization of wages from above ... all of this is a lot. it's too much. i am voting against this text.
in writing. like most meps, i share the concerns raised by the maintenance of macroeconomic conditionality which, although weakened by the european parliament in interinstitutional negotiations, will unfairly weigh on the regions. however, we were able to make many improvements during the negotiations, in particular by taking account of the specific features of the ors, whose cofinancing rate is maintained at 85%. all the regions expect to be able to commit these funds for their projects as from 1 january 2014, and in this context, the spirit of responsibility must prevail. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report, while remaining aware of the work ahead of us to consolidate regional policy beyond 2020.
in writing. the structural funds are at the heart of european integration. it is through these achievements that citizens are able to take stock of the european reality, which is sometimes perceived as too distant. it is therefore essential to maintain ambition and a substantial budget. i am pleased to have supported the creation of this new category of regions, called 'intermediate' or 'in transition', since the beginning of my mandate, which is an unprecedented step forward. it will benefit my region of languedoc-roussillon in particular, with a focus on a few major structural themes. i would like to reiterate, however, that the structural funds must not be used for political purposes, but for the benefit of the territories and the initiatives that are beneficial to them.
in writing. i supported the conditions of this new programming period for the european funds because they are favourable to the french regions. thanks to our efforts, picardy and nord-pas-de-calais will be able to continue to benefit from it. as they now belong to the category of regions in transition, they will be able to receive up to 60% of the co-financing of their projects from european funds. the new provisions make it possible to better control the final use of these funds, based on concrete results.
in writing. despite serious shortcomings, i voted in favour of the new regulation on cohesion policy. two points in particular are in dispute. firstly, macro-conditionality, which imposes a double penalty on member states in difficulty by suspending financing to a member state in a state of public deficit, in relation to the european commission's criteria. the regions would therefore no longer receive aid. the second concern is for the european social fund, which now offers a wide range of financing to promote the integration of young people and low-skilled workers, as well as support for enterprises in the face of change. this need for employment, particularly for young people, was shared but is growing. the threshold chosen is 23.1% of the cohesion policy budget, whereas the socialists asked for 25%. so we have to deal with a shrinking budget while the demand is rising. despite these shortcomings, the regions need these funds to be released as soon as possible, and a rejection would have delayed adoption beyond 2014, which would have put them in difficulty.
in writing. this vote brings a major innovation for cohesion policy, with a regulation establishing a common strategic framework for cohesion policy funds, the eu's second budgetary envelope and a vehicle for growth and economic, social and territorial cohesion. the concentration of these funds on eleven thematic objectives put an end to the drift of cofinancing, which jeopardized their effectiveness and the impact on the territories. i also welcome the creation of a youth employment initiative, which is being promoted by my political family. i do have two regrets, though. the first concerns the refusal by a majority of my colleagues to allocate 25% of the €313 billion allocated to the european social fund, which is intended for employment and social inclusion. lowering this share to 23.1% would cut this major crisis-time leverage of almost €3 billion. the second concerns the delegation of the management of the funds by the regional councils, which raises the concern that the socialist regions will use them as variables for adjusting their budgets. i call on the commission to monitor these funds closely to ensure that they are not diverted from their intended purpose.
in writing. the various european cohesion funds set themselves very ambitious objectives; the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them. the desire to control expenditure more effectively will remain unfulfilled. according to the european court of auditors, regional development is the european policy with the most "errors". worse still, the principle of macroeconomic conditionality conceals an unacceptable principle: that of subjecting european aid to the good will of the european commission and to the application by the member state of economic policies dictated by brussels. how could the states, including france, accept such a principle?
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which sets out the investment priorities for the thematic objectives and lays down the specific provisions for operational programmes co-financed by the european social fund, as well as the eligible expenditure. strong support should be given to the overall minimum share of the esf of 25% of the structural and cohesion funds budget to help anticipate new skills needs and thus significantly reduce unemployment.

in writing. the european grouping of territorial cooperation (egtc) is a legal instrument created in 2006 to develop political cooperation across borders. it has its own legal personality and facilitates cross-border, transnational and interregional cooperation between actors at different levels (member states, regional and local authorities, etc.) who wish to tackle common problems together. egtcs enable these partners to implement joint projects, exchange experience and improve coordination in spatial planning. some 40 egtcs have already been set up within the european union, of which about 10 are in france, such as the lille-kortrijk-tournai eurometropolis, which facilitates cooperation between the french and the belgians, both from the french-speaking region of wallonia and the dutch-speaking region of flanders. the new rules described in this report for the period 2014-2020 strengthen egtcs, in particular by facilitating their creation and the amendment of their statutes. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report which seeks to improve the gender balance among non-executive directors of listed companies by setting a target of a minimum of 40% of members of each sex on company boards. these targets are to be achieved by 2020 for non-executive directors and by 2018 for publicly listed companies. the gender balance among executive directors is a flexible objective. the proposal covers public and private companies listed on the stock exchange. listed small and medium-sized enterprises within the meaning of eu recommendation 2003/361/ec (< 250 employees and ≤ € 50 million turnover) are excluded from the scope of the directive, as are sectors where women represent less than 10% of the workforce. member states are free to choose the appropriate sanctions; provided that they are effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
in writing. whether in terms of wages, careers, pensions, parttime work (which is overwhelmingly done by women, and often suffered by them), inequalities remain glaring in europe. progress on gender equality is slow and often constrained. in most eu member states, laws and sanctions are necessary to advance equality. the directive we voted today aims to introduce a procedural quota to strengthen the place of women on boards. by 2020, the target is to reach 40% of women in these bodies - in non-executive positions - which would be a breakthrough. france, like a dozen other european countries, has already adopted legislation in this direction. but other countries, as a blocking minority, block the adoption of such legislation in the council. we are voting in favour of this instrument and we are calling on the council to do the same quickly.

in writing. i vote in favour of this report which proposes to ensure gender balance on the boards of listed companies and to promote gender equality in economic decision-making. my group voted in favour of this directive, unlike the far-right groups who voted massively against the advancement of women's rights. the report calls on companies to ensure that at least 40% of their directors are women. publicly traded companies will have until 2020 to achieve this target, while public institutions will have to do so by 2018. however, this increase is limited, since only non-decisive items are concerned. in addition, it is a procedural quota and not a quantitative quota, which means that the companies concerned will not be required to meet this quota a priori, but to have in place adequate selection procedures ensuring that qualified women are taken into account in order to achieve this objective. the report also calls for a transparent, open and merit-based recruitment process in which gender balance is the main point. the council will have to reach a common position, and it already seems that it will be difficult to achieve this.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text encouraging greater representation of women on boards of directors. companies, especially those listed on stock exchanges, should change their procedure for appointing members of their boards of directors to make them more open and transparent. it is not normal that in 2013 women represent only 17.6% of the members in these positions.
in writing. this report promotes a relative parity in the decision-making bodies of listed companies. this is a good thing if we consider that capitalist activity is useful. in any case, the text has many limitations. the penalties provided for do not concern non-compliance with the directive but only non-compliance with the requirements of an open and transparent procedure. it does not concern smes, which further limits its action. finally, it is based on differentialist arguments (women have a more collective mindset) which is opposed to my universalist view of the human race. i'm not going to.
in writing. this report deals with the proposal for a directive to introduce a 40% quota for women on boards of directors, whereas women currently make up on average only 13.7% of the members of these bodies. if france is one of the good students, having already enacted binding quotas with penalties, many european countries have not legislated on the subject and this directive is thus an opportunity to harmonise the member states' legislation in this area. so i decided to support her.
in writing. in france, the proportion of women on the boards of the french cac 40 companies increased by 10 percentage points to 22.3% between october 2010 and january 2012. in italy, where a law was passed in 2011, the number of women on the boards of listed companies increased by 4.9 points between january 2012 and october 2012. this example shows that in this particular area, self-regulation is not the right solution. that is why i voted in favour of this report and will be attentive to the transposition of this directive into national law.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive which will allow for greater representation of women in large companies. in 2013, only 17.6% of non-executive board members of the largest european companies were women. the text proposes that listed companies apply transparent selection procedures so that by 2020 at least 40% of their non-executive directors are women. it is crucial to combat the stereotypes and glass ceilings that hold back the careers of those belonging to the 'weaker sex'. however, this is by no means a question of preferring gender over merit. the principle of this measure is to propose that, with equal qualifications and competence, a company should be enriched by the diversity of its personnel and open up to candidates of the underrepresented sex. failure to comply with the appointment procedures may result in sanctions for these large companies. smes are exempt from these rules.
in writing. across europe, the proportion of women in publicly traded companies appears to be increasing. in france, the proportion of women on the boards of cac40 companies jumped by 10 percentage points between october 2010 and january 2012 to 22.3%. it is not by means of a european directive that this process, which necessarily requires time, must be changed or accelerated. quotas are never a substitute for merit. this text is also inconsistent and inapplicable as demonstrated by the following proposed amendment: 'where the pre-selection of candidates is based on an election or a vote, for example by employees or their representatives, the procedure should be adapted throughout the process in order to contribute to the objective of better gender parity within the board of directors as a whole, while ensuring that the sex of the director elected by this procedure has in no way been decided in advance.' good luck to the lawyer who's gonna have to create the procedure...
in writing. the package of legislative reports on the common agricultural policy (cap) for the period 2014-2020 being in line with my objectives of a strong agricultural policy, remunerative for farmers (in particular in the auvergne, centre and limousin regions) allowing the development of quality products, safe for the health of european citizens and finally an agricultural policy compatible with environmental and climate issues, i voted for each of these reports. the principles of cross compliance set out in the la via report should promote environmental protection without hampering the work of farmers. i welcome the fact that financial controls are now proportionate to the errors found. the commission will also be able to reduce controls in regions where management errors are not so widespread.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report 'the way forward for the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap) for the period 2014-20'. with a budget of over €400 billion, the cap remains the leading european policy. it helps to support our farmers' commitment to environmental protection and at the same time strengthens the competitiveness of their businesses. i particularly welcome the adoption of the support for the entry into the agricultural sector of young people under 40 and the establishment of safety nets to counter the volatility of raw material prices. the market for our agricultural products must be regulated. we will not accept the entry onto the european market of agricultural products which do not meet our health, social and environmental standards.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which deals with the financing, management and monitoring of the common agricultural policy for the period 2014-2020, because in view of the challenges posed by the european objectives of food security, environmental protection and territorial development, it is essential to ensure the effectiveness of this policy with appropriate budgetary resources. the european union's strategy for the common agricultural policy has major implications for our citizens, who are subject to the vagaries of the agricultural market. i am in particular in favour of making the financing system more transparent by strengthening the role of the coordinating body for the paying agencies, which will also reduce the administrative burden on national administrations.
in writing. the compromise reached by parliament and the council on all the texts which will now regulate agricultural policy is not a good compromise. it continues and completes the deregulation of a sector whose specificities and strategic importance are obvious and fully justify a general derogation from your competitive and ultra-bargaining obsessions. it maintains unfair competition within the european union; it may even lead to harmful interregional competition within the member states; it is, of course, in the context of a world market which is in the process of being totally liberalised. in france, one farmer commits suicide every day. this is a shocking figure which reflects the despair of an entire profession, and for which european policy and its national variations are largely responsible. farmers don't ask to be assisted. they demand that their products be paid at a price that reflects the costs they bear and allows a decent remuneration for their work. it is not necessary to recall that a large part of these costs is due to the constraints imposed by brussels. i repeat: only market regulation and rigorous application of national and european preference can make this possible.

in writing. the common agricultural policy (cap) represents the largest share of the eu budget: €373 billion for the next 7 years. the budget voted, however, has been severely cut compared to the previous budget of 426 billion. this is at a time when the agricultural sector is facing a serious crisis. farmers face fluctuating market prices, skyrocketing costs and struggle to balance their farms. the cap money does not help to stop the problem, because it goes massively to the large farms. we had proposed that a single farm should not receive more than eur 100 000 from the cap. but no ceiling system was accepted. what we are advocating is: the stabilization of markets, decent remuneration for farmers' work by ensuring stable prices for a given volume of production, the supply of quality food at reasonable prices, and respect for food sovereignty. this text, which was advertised as a reform, changes little. what is worse is that the budget is falling, while we need ambitious policies. we have therefore voted against this reform of the cap.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague giovanni la via, which reforms the common agricultural policy for the period 2014-2020, in particular as regards its management and monitoring. variable geometry controls will be introduced, increasing controls in the most problematic regions and reducing those in the regions most compliant with the cap rules. in addition, the commission will have to present an evaluation of the cap's performance every four years to measure its effectiveness. farmers will have specific and verifiable obligations in respect of the environment, which will be conditional on the payment of certain aid, in order to ensure green and sustainable agriculture in the european union. member states will be required to provide advice to farmers to help them comply with the principles laid down by the cap. in addition, full transparency will be required of the member states as to who receives aid, with the exception of aid for the smallest farmers. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. following the adoption of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament worked for the first time in its history on an equal footing with the member states to define a new structure for the cap. in particular, the rules on penalties were revised and the principle of proportionality introduced, with an alert system, which makes it possible to warn the farmer in the event of irregularity and to apply the penalty the following year, retroactively, if the situation has not been corrected.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the financing, management and monitoring of the common agricultural policy is essentially technical in nature and concerns the rules governing: the financing of cap expenditure, including rural development expenditure; the agricultural advisory system; the management and control systems to be set up by the member states; the conditionality system; and the settlement. but all these provisions apply to a system of aid which encourages the concentration of agricultural production and the destruction of jobs. i vote against it.
in writing. two points in particular motivated my support for this regulation, which sets the general conditions for the reform of the cap. on the one hand, the list of subjects on which member states will be required to advise farmers has been extended to include, in particular, conditionality, direct green payments, or the conditions for maintaining land eligible for direct payments. on the other hand, a crisis reserve will be created each year for an amount of eur 400 million, and if this crisis amount is not used, it will be reimbursed to farmers in the form of direct payments the following year.
in writing. agriculture is today at the crossroads of major challenges: climate, energy, food. the need for a transformation of production is now becoming unavoidable. through the new european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd, the cap's financing instrument) and in line with the desire to revive the european economy, the new cap will have to promote the integration of young farmers and provide a strong incentive for investment. i welcome the phasing out of direct aid, the convergence of aid per hectare (the principle of which is to reduce the gap between the aid received by the member states and the community average), the introduction of a ceiling which will prevent the owners of the largest number of hectares from receiving the largest number of aid, and the premium for the first 52 hectares. the creation of the young farmer payment per hectare, which will be in addition to the existing support based on the young farmer allowance and subsidised loans, is also welcome. it also reinforces the necessary move towards agri-environmental measures and sets out measures to revitalise rural areas and develop more sustainable agriculture.
