in writing. - i am voting in favour of the report by mr luis manuel capoulas santos on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation laying down rules on direct payments to farmers under support schemes under the common agricultural policy, as the new direct payments provide for a resource allocation criterion which will not allow any member state to receive less than 65% of the eu average. as regards the distribution of aid within individual member states, more attention will be paid to those areas and sectors where a too sudden reduction in aid could have a negative impact on the incomes of agricultural producers.
in writing. this report is part of the package on the cap, which was adopted after the vote on the european budget (a general reduction of 10%). with the cap budget being sharply reduced (from €426 billion to €373 billion for 2014-2020, a 13% decrease), it was important to change the current direction of the large farms and to take stock of the plight of small farms in a system of fierce competition. the commission's proposals were a sign of awareness and an embryo response so that the funds would benefit more environmentally friendly production and limit the amounts going to large farms. i have tabled amendments to push these proposals towards a more humane agriculture: protecting the incomes of small farmers; limiting the funds paid to farms to eur 100 000; maintaining a strong ecological conditionality. these were rejected and the most interesting proposals of the commission were stripped of their substance by the council. the cap 2014-2020 was a missed opportunity, so i voted against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text on direct payments, which shows a positive evolution in the role of the farmer who is no longer paid only for production but also for the environmental public goods he delivers, i.e. the maintenance of permanent grasslands, the diversification of crops, the maintenance of hedges, trees, hedgerows, biotopes, useful for the preservation of biodiversity.
in writing. this report focuses on a central aspect of the new cap. of course, it does show some progress compared to the current cap: a certain redistribution of aid between countries and within each country (convergence of aid) and the possibility for countries to provide additional support to the smallest farms (in france, the first 52 hectares). but this reform is not intended to ensure a real redistribution of aid between european countries and between farmers. it is very much below what would be necessary. it does not put an end to a system which increases income inequality rather than alleviating it and thus encourages the concentration of agricultural production and the destruction of jobs. there is still no ceiling on aid for the largest farms. moreover, 'greening' (environmental conditions for granting direct aid) is far from sufficient to encourage a genuine ecological transition in agriculture. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which will better frame the direct financial support that the european union provides to farmers. the new common agricultural policy aims to combine several key priorities: food security, the competitiveness and quality of european agriculture, environmental protection and the fair distribution of european funds. the cap will only support active farmers, not golf clubs or airports as it has been able to do in the past. in addition, it will give priority to young people settling in the countryside to maintain their livelihood, offering an additional payment of 25% for their first hectares. the new cap will also be fairer: it will require convergence of payments both between european countries and within each member state, so that some farms do not receive all the appropriations. for example, farmers in my region, languedoc-roussillon, will thus be better assisted by the european union. finally, the cap will be greener: 30% of direct payments will be conditional on compulsory greening measures, such as crop diversification, the maintenance of permanent grasslands or the creation of 'areas of ecological interest'.
in writing. agriculture is today at the crossroads of major challenges: climate, energy, food. the need for a transformation of production is now becoming unavoidable. through the new european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd, the cap's financing instrument) and in line with the desire to revive the european economy, the new cap will have to promote the integration of young farmers and provide a strong incentive for investment. i welcome the phasing out of direct aid, the convergence of aid per hectare (the principle of which is to reduce the gap between the aid received by the member states and the community average), the introduction of a ceiling which will prevent the owners of the largest number of hectares from receiving the largest amount of aid, and the premium for the first 52 hectares. the creation of the young farmer payment per hectare, which will be in addition to the existing support based on the young farmer allowance and subsidised loans, is also welcome. it also reinforces the necessary move towards agri-environmental measures and sets out measures to revitalise rural areas and develop more sustainable agriculture.
in writing. the common agricultural policy is essential to ensure food security for europeans. however, over the years, this policy has been increasingly contested and criticized. some rightly point to the fact that non-agricultural enterprises are the majority beneficiaries of such aid, while others are indignant that the larger farms receive the most subsidies. by limiting the granting of aid to active farmers, by capping aid to large farms and by introducing a favourable regime for small farmers, the european agreement on the cap 2014-2020 responds precisely to the demand for a fairer and more efficient distribution of aid. the agreement also responds to the demand for a more environmentally friendly cap, while ensuring the economic viability of the agricultural sector: 30% of direct aids will be conditional on compliance with certain ecological practices. i believe we have reached a balanced agreement which reflects the idea of a greener, fairer and more efficient cap, for the benefit of farmers and consumers alike.
in writing. the package of legislative reports on the common agricultural policy (cap) for the period 2014-2020 being in line with my objectives of a strong agricultural policy, remunerative for farmers (in particular in the auvergne, centre and limousin regions) allowing the development of quality products, safe for the health of european citizens and finally an agricultural policy compatible with environmental and climate issues, i voted for each of these reports. as the agreement on the future cap was reached too late in 2013 to be directly applicable on 1 january 2014, this report provides for a gradual transition from the old to the new rules.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the text adopted allows us to reaffirm our commitment to a sustainable and competitive agricultural model
in writing. the objective of this text is to ensure the continuity of the cap for 2014 while providing for adaptation to the new conditions defined in the next programming period. it will in particular reduce the administrative burden on farmers and local authorities, in order to ensure more effective implementation of the measures of the common agricultural policy. there is still work to be done to support our farmers in the face of the difficulties they face, but these measures are moving in the right direction.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which allows for a better staggering of payments to the agricultural sector. the agricultural sector is a major activity in france, and i therefore support any action by the european union to strengthen support for this sector. the reformed common agricultural policy is expected to be implemented at the beginning of 2014. however, in order to facilitate a smooth transition, it is necessary to put in place transitional arrangements to allow the agricultural world to adapt smoothly to these new measures. i am in favour of giving member states more flexibility to meet the needs of their sector in terms of transferring funds so that each state can adopt an appropriate strategy according to its specific circumstances.
in writing. farmers should not pay the price for the power and influence play between the european institutions. these are not figures, subsidies or standards, but men and women who work, often hard, to feed france and europe. today farmers, especially the most vulnerable, are entitled to expect protection from europe rather than being forced to accept new rules and a forthcoming opening to global competition. the greening ideology, which casts a priori suspicion on agriculture, has fortunately been somewhat relaxed, but it is still very much alive. in addition, the commission inherits a great deal of interpretative power from the delegated acts and the poorly thought-out transition creates a new administrative burden that the profession does not need.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague albert dess which provides for transitional arrangements for 2014 pending the entry into force of the new agricultural policy. this report will allow for a smooth transition to the new system by allowing applications for transitional year funding for a number of rural development measures. in addition, the administrative burden on farmers and local authorities will be reduced, while member states will be able to start redistributing payments to smaller farmers as from 2014. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the report by mr albert deß on the proposal for a regulation laying down transitional provisions in relation to the application of the new cap, because although it will enter into force on 1 january 2014, it is certainly unlikely that all the aspects covered by this new programming will be activated by that date. transitional arrangements are therefore necessary to allow for a harmonious adjustment of the conditions of the new cap, both as regards direct payments and as regards rural development. the transitional provisions will be a useful way of establishing the rules for the transition between the two programming periods, which will certainly have to be linked.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on transitional provisions for rural development support. the rapid vote on this report is necessary because it covers the transitional period before the new cap rules, which will not apply from 1 january 2014, are put in place. this will allow applications for support to continue to be submitted during the transitional year.
in writing. this report provides for transitional arrangements for the disbursement of european funds between the end of the cap and the new cap. as i am opposed to the new cap, i cannot vote for these transitional arrangements. but the parliament's report avoids the worst by providing for the possibility for the states to pay the surcharge to small farms as from 2014. i'm not going to do anything to stop this little advance.
in writing. the economic crisis affecting europe has reduced the financial resources of the member states and thus their ability to contribute to the co-financing of projects partly financed by european funds. this means that the implementation of thousands of projects has been paralysed by lack of financial resources, particularly in slovakia and romania. to deal with this situation, i voted in favour of this report, which slightly loosens the rules to facilitate the use of these funds and thus the economic recovery of these countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because, in response to the prolonged economic and financial crisis, it aims to ensure the proper implementation of cohesion policy programmes and concerns the member states most affected by the crisis. the inability of some member states to achieve growth and employment targets because of the crisis requires us to adopt exceptional measures, limited in time, which allow for maximum and optimal use of the structural and cohesion fund appropriations available at the end of the programming period.
in writing. i am pleased that this text reflects a general ambition that we are now largely implementing to deal with the consequences of the crisis: that of increased flexibility to direct european funds and instruments towards the regions and populations that need them most. the text will make it possible to implement cohesion policy in the most effective way, in support of growth and employment in the regions most affected by the crisis.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague oldrich vlasák. some member states are currently experiencing serious difficulties in maintaining and ensuring their financial stability. we are approaching the end of the programming period and the priority must be to absorb funds efficiently. the report was adopted by 440 votes to 238 with 10 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. this proposal, adopted in response to the prolonged economic and financial crisis, aims to ensure the proper implementation of cohesion policy programmes and concerns the member states most affected by the crisis. the aim is to reduce the pressure on their public finances and to facilitate the implementation of projects by avoiding the loss of funds remaining available at the end of the current programming period. but to act effectively, we should rather question the absurd chain of budgetary gold rules that leads to recession. i am voting in favour of this so as not to prevent the release of this fund.
in writing. to address high levels of unemployment, including youth unemployment, and the increase in the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion, a decision to increase certain national envelopes of the european social fund (esf) was taken at the european council in june 2013. we must therefore take note of this political decision and amend the regulation on the financial allocation of the esf to certain european countries.
in writing. the increase in the esf allocation to france, spain and italy underlines the importance of the fund for promoting employment and social inclusion and for strengthening the social dimension of the european union in the current economic situation. this also supports the allocation of a minimum of 25% of cohesion policy resources to the esf during the 2014-2020 programming period.
in writing. this additional €150 million for the european social fund will provide france, italy and spain with additional resources to help them to deal with the consequences of the crisis, in particular unemployment and social exclusion. i welcome the support of the european union for the recovery in these states.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague jan olbrycht, which aims to provide an additional €126 million to france, italy and spain from the european social fund for 2013. this is intended to help combat unemployment, especially among young people, poverty and social exclusion. in the context of the economic crisis, i can only welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. this proposal for a regulation amends the financial allocation granted to france, italy and spain under the esf. the objective is to address certain issues affecting these countries arising from the final outcome of the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. it is also a question of remedying the inequalities generated by the british rebate, which penalises these three countries in the first place. as these appropriations relate to the year 2013 and the financial allocation currently granted to france, italy and spain under the esf has been fully committed to the union budget, the entry into force of this regulation is of an urgent nature. i vote for it.
in writing. this report supports a proposal for a regulation to amend the esf financial allocation to france, spain and italy to provide them with an additional envelope to compensate for the inequalities generated by the uk rebate in the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. this additional appropriation for 2013 will be used to support the fight against unemployment (especially youth unemployment), poverty and social exclusion in these countries. the commission has already decided to grant a loan of ecu 83 million to france alone. i support this proposal and will be particularly vigilant to ensure that these additional appropriations are specifically allocated to the most deprived areas.
in writing. i have approved this new protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement (fpa) with kiribati. it provides for fishing opportunities in kiribati's territorial waters for spanish, french and portuguese vessels. as kiribati has virtually no resources other than fishing activities, it is appropriate to provide guidance for the action of european vessels and, in particular, to grant a financial contribution to the republic of kiribati in return.
in writing. i voted in favour of this new protocol allowing access to the fishing zones of kiribati for several tuna fleets of the european union, including spanish, french and portuguese fleets until 15 september 2015. the last joint commission meeting, involving the european commission, the government of kiribati and the european parliament as observers, concluded that the agreement was mutually beneficial.
in writing. i voted in favour of the lövin report authorising the european fleet to fish in the exclusive economic zone of kiribati. by ensuring the sustainable exploitation of tuna resources, this agreement respects international conventions and satisfies both parties - the european union and kiribati. the fisheries sector in kiribati is supported. a financial envelope of eur 350 000 is allocated for the sectoral development of small-scale fisheries in kiribati.
in writing. i support the conclusion of a fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and kiribati: the first beneficiaries of such an agreement are european fishermen, and i welcome the fact that it respects our ambitions for sustainable fisheries. the concerns about tuna fishing will need to be given special attention, but i am hopeful that the european union and kiribati will manage to have a partnership that is both sustainable and mutually beneficial.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague isabella lövin, which sets out a new protocol for access to the fishing areas of kiribati for european fleets until 2015. the protocol is supported by the government of kiribati, which considers it to be mutually beneficial. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the partnership agreement with kiribati, the protocol to which complies with the conditions laid down in the framework of the wcpfc regional fisheries organisation.
in writing. fishing has become global. fish is not eaten where it is caught, and two out of three fish eaten in europe are imported. i do not like this model, i advocate relocating production and developing short circuits. participatory ecological planning work will have to be carried out. for the time being, the agreements between the european union and the producing countries must at least be of a high environmental and social standard. which is clearly not the case here. the democratic republic of kiribati has virtually no resources other than the fishing activities deployed in its vast exclusive economic zone (eez). by signing this agreement, kiribati would be in breach of the nauru agreement which coordinates the management of fisheries in the eezs and would deprive itself of its fishery resources. i vote against, not to participate in this pillage.
in writing. the report concerns the signing of a partnership agreement between the eu and the kiribati islands. the agreement will grant 10 european vessels exclusive fishing rights for three years in the exclusive economic zone of the kiribati islands. while economically beneficial for the european union, this agreement is very damaging for the sustainable management of fisheries resources in the pacific ocean and for the fishing capacity of the territories in the area. it is in fact contrary to the efforts made by the small pacific island states to manage the exploitation of resources and therefore risks altering the fishing capacity of certain octs, notably new caledonia, french polynesia and wallis and futuna. i have therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new fisheries protocol between the european union and kiribati and i am very pleased that the european parliament has authorised the ratification of this agreement. it is important that the european union is present in the pacific region and, through this protocol, promotes the establishment of responsible and sustainable fisheries. under the new protocol, the european union will allocate €1.325 million per year to kiribati, for a total of €4.428 million over the three-year period. these substantial resources are expected to contribute to the economic development of kiribati, which is heavily dependent on official development assistance.
in writing. this report on the location of the seats of the institutions of the european union, which in reality deals only with the question of the seat of the european parliament, and which is based on an anti-strasbourg a priori and extremely questionable figures, i voted against it. this does not mean, however, that all debate on this subject should be opposed. there is a need for a real, honest, impartial debate on the question of the advantages and disadvantages of the localisation of all the european institutions. finally, it should be remembered that this issue is enshrined in the european treaties and that any amendment would have to be accepted by all the member states in order to be validated and applied.
in writing. i voted against the report on the location of the seats of the european institutions because it is, in my view, a symbol of sloppy, ideological and ill-considered work. under the guise of saving money, british eurosceptic meps have managed to gather enough support to ask for the location of the parliament to be decided by them, something that is hardly done anywhere else in the world! the member states decide. false figures are circulating about the cost of strasbourg: the parliament costs between 51 and 55 million euros a year, or 0.04% of the budget, or 10 cents a year per head of population! it is true that we must save money, but to want to destroy a symbol, and this is in france, for 10 cents a year is to forget what a parliament is. this report, full of errors and, above all, useless, will give the british conservatives the opportunity to boast that they have destroyed a european symbol. i am not hiding my surprise at the fact that french meps who are both environmentalists and centrists voted against the siege of strasbourg in order to reduce its environmental impact. the strasbourg council is the weakest of all the european institutions. in short, it's a bad report.
in writing. i voted against the häfner and fox report on the seat of the european institutions. this report proposes a single place of work for the european parliament. he thus called into question the single seat of strasbourg. under european law, the seat of the european institutions cannot be changed without the consent of the member states of the union.
in writing. i voted against this report, which caricatures this parliament and sends a very bad signal to the citizens: at a time when europeans are facing the consequences of the crisis, does not parliament have better things to do than to clash over institutional issues? moreover, this text has no legal significance: what a waste of time and energy for all the members of this assembly! the text is also full of falsehoods and dubious interpretations of european texts.
in writing. the treaties of the european union made strasbourg the seat of the european parliament for historical and symbolic reasons. strasbourg is the rule and brussels the exception. a change of the seat of the european parliament could therefore only be made by a unanimous decision of the council. in any event, as the court once again stated in december 2012, the european parliament has no legitimacy, no possibility to decide for itself where its seat is. the vote in plenary is therefore completely useless. moreover, in these times of crisis, our parliament would be well advised to focus on the real issues that affect the lives of europeans.
in writing. i voted against this text in order to defend the interests of strasbourg as the seat of the european parliament. the alsatian capital is a city where the european dimension is very prominent. the council of europe has had its seat in the city since 1949, and the european court of human rights since 1998. if the european parliament were to be abolished from strasbourg, what would remain for france, the eu's founding member? moreover, the veracity of these figures can be questioned insofar as the ngo which published them was financed by a political party clearly opposed to the strasbourg siege. it is the lifeblood of an entire economy and generates considerable benefits for hoteliers, restaurateurs and other businesses. in one region, the bas-rhin, where the unemployment rate is constantly rising and is now at 9% (insee, 2nd quarter of 2013), the withdrawal of the seat of the european parliament would be a blow to the local economy. i cannot therefore support such a text.
in writing. the anti-strasbourg lobby won a victory today by getting this report adopted. the same lobby has removed the mention of brussels as the only seat it calls for. as if that would fool anyone! the lobby is happy to call the strasbourg sessions and the travelling associated with them a 'circus'. if there is a circus, it is the debate and the vote on this report. he claims to be interested only in his own seat, but is not interested in the existence of many administrative departments of the parliament in luxembourg, which are also responsible for managing staff mostly based in brussels. as anxious as he is to save the european taxpayer money, he should also, comically, call the commission to account, which scatters its useless agencies across europe like so many little gifts to certain cities or countries. yes, there is only one seat of the european parliament: it is in strasbourg. if we have to group together its activities, we should do so in strasbourg! and it is the increasingly localized nature of certain activities in brussels, with the complicity or lack of reaction for 25 years of the french governments of the right and the left, that is to be condemned.
in writing. it is for parliament, composed of representatives elected by direct universal suffrage, to decide sovereignly on the place where it will meet. on this point, the fox report voted on today is going in the right direction. i abstained, however, because it is essential to reconcile two different imperatives: on the one hand, to facilitate the work of parliament, whose interlocutors (council, commission and civil society) are in brussels, and to put an end to the extra costs generated by this monthly travel. on the other hand, we must preserve the symbolic dimension of strasbourg. the travel of members could be stopped, but for ten years the money saved would be sufficient, for example, to finance an independent european foundation responsible for organising in strasbourg, in the european parliament, a european forum for debates and the confrontation of ideas for all civil society: young people, elected representatives, trade unionists, ngos... its purpose would be to advance work and reflection on the history of europe, the rapprochement of the peoples of europe and europe's role in the world.
in writing. i rejected this report, which is a legitimate attack on the strasbourg seat, when its mandate should have covered the seats of all the european institutions. this own-initiative report is based on erroneous reasoning, arguing that parliaments should be able to decide on their seats, a situation which is unknown in comparative law and which could lead to a change of seat, at the discretion of the political majorities. it also draws a line through the history of european construction, at a time when memory is more than necessary in the face of europe's worrying evolution towards nationalism and other forms of extremism. finally, the argument that this type of report could help to combat the prevailing euroscepticism seems to me to be more than fallacious, because this euroscepticism has its roots in much deeper causes than the mere question of the seat of the parliament in strasbourg. at a time when poverty and misery are increasing all over europe, our role as parliamentarians is much more to be concerned with finding solutions to get back on the path to growth rather than wasting our time in this kind of fruitless polemics.
in writing. i must express my dismay after the vote on the report on the seat of the eu institutions, which was hijacked by the supporters of the single seat of the european parliament, opposed to strasbourg. i am surprised that members of parliament spend so much time on this subject when citizens are asking them to mobilize their forces to fight unemployment, save businesses and restore the economy. these mps do not advocate for the institutions and contribute to increasingly disconnecting them from their citizens. i do not forget that this campaign of slander, lies and the like is being carried out mainly by british members of parliament whose critical views of the european project are well known and not in keeping with the original ambitions of the founding fathers. i am afraid that by attacking the symbol of europe, the european project is gradually being deconstructed and that in the end we are playing into the hands of those who do not really like europe.
in writing. i strongly opposed the report by my colleagues ashley fox and gerald häfner. the text contains serious legal errors which clearly call into question the drafting of this own-initiative report. paragraph 4 requiring that parliament may decide on its seat and internal organisation is unfounded. the seats of the institutions are fixed by the treaties and the geographical definition of the seat of the parliament is contained in protocol no 6 to the treaty of lisbon. this text is a danger to the legitimacy of the european parliament and the european union, given its violent attack on the only institution directly elected by and accountable to the european citizens. politically, this report is a manoeuvre to try to make the siege of strasbourg disappear. i totally regret the adoption of this text.
in writing. - in a context of economic crisis and of the tarnishing of the image of the european union, the issue of the european parliament's dual institutional seat must be resolved immediately. the waste of politics is no longer acceptable, all the more so in the face of public opinion which is demanding from its representative class an attitude conscious of the reality of the crisis in which it lives. we therefore strongly urge once again that the waste of the european parliament's two seats be stopped and that the only place of work be the belgian capital.
in writing. as rapporteur for the epp group on the question of the seat of the institutions, i regretted the outcome of the vote in plenary. a large majority of members adopted the report, which was actually rejected in strasbourg. the usual opponents of the parliament's seat in strasbourg have shown intellectual dishonesty by using incorrect, outdated and controversial figures on costs and carbon balance to denigrate strasbourg. the use of the principle that meps should choose their own seat has been the screen behind which the opponents of the strasbourg seat have hidden themselves in order to attack the institutional seat. but this principle does not exist anywhere, and only in agreement with the european council could a revision of the treaties be considered, which is necessary for any change in the seat of the parliament, as well as for any change in the seats of other european institutions. the text is therefore merely an own-initiative report which does not have the force of law, but it has become a political object which must encourage us, as french people, to redouble our efforts to preserve the seat of our european institution on our national territory.
in writing. the report explains that parliament should have only one seat, and that it should have the right to decide on its working arrangements, including when and where it meets. the report also calls for the european parliament to be consulted on any changes to the seat or workplace which require amendment of the treaty and the consent of the member states. the question of the seat of the institutions is an old one, and that of the european parliament is a subject of constant debate. the seat of the parliament has been the subject of judgments of the court of justice of the european communities, guaranteeing the right of member states to set sessions in strasbourg, but highlighting the disadvantages of the plurality of workplaces. the location of the european institutions is the result of negotiations between the member states, which have thus defined strasbourg as the seat of the parliament, just as the seat of the ecb has been fixed in frankfurt, or the european agencies in different capitals. to return to the seat in strasbourg is to return to that allocation which is the result of compromise between states at the expense of strasbourg. that is why i voted against it, as did a large majority of french meps.
in writing. with this report, a british conservative and a german green party join forces to propose abolishing the strasbourg seat of the european parliament by amending the european treaties. under the guise of good management, their report is a crude anti-french operation, and therefore anti-european. they also fail to take account of the symbolic dimension of the city of strasbourg in europe. nor is it legitimate for france to host at least one of the eu institutions when belgium has four, luxembourg three, and germany and the netherlands each one... in this connection, the report 'decides not to make any recommendations as to the seats of the other institutions of the union'. only strasbourg is concerned. this is yet another demonstration of the hostility of liberals of all stripes against the republican identity of france in europe, conceived on a regional and feudal model. i vote against it.
in writing. i have of course voted against such a report which contains many wrong figures and legal and political inaccuracies. this report, which was to cover the seats of all the institutions of the european union, focuses solely on the seat of the european parliament. while the european parliament's sole seat is strasbourg, as is very clearly stated in the treaties, the authors of this report want - without however mentioning it explicitly - the entire european parliament to move permanently to brussels. this report ignores the symbol of strasbourg for the construction of europe and proposes that the european parliament should be able to decide where its seat is, whereas in the member states no parliament has this power. changing the seats of the institutions requires a change in the treaties which requires the unanimity of the member states. finally, this report flouts the recent decision of the court of justice of the european union which clearly states that the seat of the parliament is in strasbourg. for all these reasons, i have opposed the adoption of this report by the european parliament.
in writing. i deplore the spectacle offered by a majority of this parliament, which is discrediting itself by adopting a biased report on the fixing of the seats of the european institutions. this text has been diverted from its purpose and has served as a platform for those opposed to the european parliament's official seat in strasbourg. it is disappointing that such an attack on the symbol of franco-german peace should raise doubts in the minds of european citizens about its usefulness. do we really want a europe that is turned towards itself in its ivory tower in brussels? and what has happened to respect for our founding treaties, which establish the legitimacy of strasbourg to host the 12 annual plenary sessions? i do not accept the intellectual dishonesty and the manipulation of figures which have underpinned a deplorable attempt to wipe the strasbourg parliament off the map. for these reasons i voted against this report, which should never have been published. in the eyes of the french and the europeans, strasbourg remains the capital of europe, the manifestation of franco-german reconciliation and the guarantee of a european union that is not in the midst of brussels.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i am pleased to have the opportunity to participate in this important debate on horizon 2020. research and innovation are at the heart of our policies to bring europe back to a path of growth and sustainable development. economic recovery depends very much on our developing an effective, knowledge-based society. the first pillar of the new programme ‘excellent science’ will support frontier or basic research, which constitutes the foundation for economic growth and future prosperity. in the context of a knowledge-based society, researchers will be able to work together and exchange and develop ideas that will offer solutions which can act as a catalyst for economic growth. there will, in particular, be a significant increase in support for the extremely successful european research council and marie curie actions. this will encourage high-level research and mobility for the benefit of european citizens. there will also be guaranteed support for future and emerging technologies and research infrastructures. the economic crisis has affected europe’s competitiveness. industry and smes in particular have struggled to maintain europe’s leadership in a globalised market where competition is fierce. horizon 2020 will also help to boost competitiveness. the new programme includes a second pillar, ‘industrial leadership’, to help companies and support business research and innovation, including key enabling technologies – such as ict, nanotechnology and biotechnology – and support for innovation in smes. smes are the backbone of the european economy, and horizon 2020 includes a dedicated instrument to provide support to smes in the area of research and innovation. this new instrument will help fill existing funding gaps, and encourage innovation. although we are beginning to emerge from the worst of the economic crisis, significant challenges in a wide range of areas such as health, transport and energy lie ahead. these challenges are reflected in horizon 2020, under ‘societal challenges’. these challenges are about addressing the well-being of europeans citizens. research in these areas aims to create innovative solutions which will enhance the quality of life in europe, as well as the sustainability of our economic model and of the entire planet. we have also committed ourselves to widening participation in the implementation of the programme. we particularly appreciate the efforts of this parliament to spread excellence and help unlock the potential for innovation, as well as to ensure that science becomes an integral part of our society. the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) will also continue to strengthen the innovation capacity of the european union and its member states by integrating the elements of the ‘knowledge triangle’ of higher education, research and innovation. with a substantial budget increase, five new knowledge and innovation communities (kics) will be launched over the programming period in three waves. finally, i would like to underline the importance of simplification. we have consistently offered our support to those in the parliament who have sought to simplify the programme. we welcome the emphasis on providing simpler rules – thereby cutting red tape and allowing those involved to focus on actual research. our encompass two initiatives under my responsibility: the european institute of innovation and technology – the eit – and the marie skłodowska-curie actions. at a time when europe is severely challenged the marie skłodowska-curie actions will have a budget of eur 6.1 billion. that represents an increase of 30 % on current funding. these actions will strengthen our support for researchers in europe by combining mobility across countries and sectors with excellence in research and top-quality training. in other words, the marie skłodowska-curie actions will build on the excellent progress we have already made. we have already supported more than 75 000 researchers of 130 nationalities since the creation of the programme and we expect to support another 65 000 over the next seven years. the new marie skłodowska-curie actions will fund industrial doctorates – programmes which require researchers to spend half of their time in industry – as well as joint doctorates and other innovative forms of research training that provide experience outside academia. it is not by chance that some 30 marie curie researchers took part in the research which led to the discovery of the higgs boson at cern, and the nobel prize in physics awarded to peter higgs and françois englert. marie curie supports excellence and it will continue to do so. the second initiative i want to mention is the european institute of innovation and technology. over the last three years, we have successfully tested the concept of the eit and produced promising results. by putting universities at the centre of the innovation chain, and by gathering all the actors of innovation – businesses, research centres, universities and local authorities – within structured and well governed public-private partnerships – the so-called kics – the eit is bringing about a step change in the way we address innovation in europe. with more than 352 partners directly involved across europe, the eit has already created more than 100 start-ups, around 90 new services or products and more than 400 business ideas which are still being incubated. by the end of the year, more than 1 000 students will have been trained in masters courses bearing the eit label. with the eit we are investing in the entrepreneurs of tomorrow, and in the capacity of europe to innovate and to remain competitive. with a budget of more than eur 2.7 billion, we will be able to ensure that the eit grows in strength by giving enhanced support to existing kics and gradually launching five new kics over the next seven years. we will make sure that the benefits of the eit’s work are shared across europe. in particular, the regional innovation scheme, spearheaded by the european parliament, will only strengthen the tools that the kics use to share their experience and best practices as widely as possible. finally, i would like to once again thank the rapporteurs of horizon 2020, and in particular ms matias, mr lamberts, mrs riera madurell and mr ehler, but also the shadow rapporteurs, for their outstanding work on these files. special thanks also go to mrs carvalho who, together with other members of the eit frameworks, have tried all along to strengthen the eit.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to thank the fictitious rapporteurs and the chairman of the committee, mrs sharon bowles, with whom we have really worked hand in hand. this report concerns the revision of the regulation governing the european statistical system. its main objective is to strengthen the reliability of statistics through the independence of statisticians and the transparency of the processes. as a reminder, in this context - where the european union is still shaken by the scandal of the manipulation of greek statistics - we have, in this parliament, under joint decisionmaking, initiated a number of reforms of european economic governance in respect of which the reliability of the figures is necessary for a proper assessment of economic policies in the context of the six-pack. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. secondly, to give the commission extensive powers of investigation and coordination. thirdly, to strengthen the independence of eurostat by consulting parliament on the appointment of its director-general. on all these points we have reached agreement with the previous presidency of the council. that is the text which is being put to the vote tomorrow. unfortunately, the commission is opposed to this agreement, and it is using the powers conferred on it by the treaties to block the agreement by imposing a unanimous vote in the council. it has also helped to form an unlikely alliance in the council against the agreement, composed of delegations that want to strengthen the agreement and others that want to empty it of its substance. the council is now so deadlocked that the presidency has not been able to obtain a new negotiating mandate to continue the trilogue discussions. the commission considers in particular that the provisions at national level are too weak. however, we are going further than the commission proposal on many points, particularly with regard to the directors of the national institutes. the agreement for example provides for heads of institutes to produce national guidelines to ensure the quality of all statistics produced by all actors at national level, a step which is not included in the commission's proposal. the article also provides for gender equality in the appointment of heads of national institutes, which is again a step forward compared to the commission's text. there is no majority today to go further in the council on the other points, as some of the member states consider that we are already going too far. this compromise at national level is therefore the best possible one. the commission also opposes the presence of two members of parliament in relation to the strengthening of eurostat's independence. we believe that this requires, in particular, consultation of parliament before the appointment of the director-general and transparent dismissal and disciplinary procedures. these provisions, which the council is in a position to accept, are progress and the commission should not oppose them. eurostat is not a commission directorate-general like any other, it is the european statistical office, which requires greater transparency and independence. i would have liked to present a final trilogue agreement but unfortunately this is not possible for the reasons i have outlined. i therefore propose that you adopt tomorrow the text of the first agreement with the presidency and ask the council to take a position. we need progress in parliament to break the impasse in which the negotiations are now, and i stand ready to resume the negotiations immediately after the vote. the european statistical system is based on cooperation and not coercion: it is up to the commission to convince the member states to move gradually towards an ever more transparent and independent system. if the negotiations were to fail because of the commission's blockage, it would be a major political failure for the commission, which would lose its leadership role in the european statistical system. i have no doubt that the commission will be constructive and i hope that i can count on it as a partner in defending the general european interest.

artificial development of natural environments is increasing, the situation is all the more worrying because half of the wildlife is now threatened. in this context, the financing of environmental policies and local actions is of course crucial. this is all the more so as, in this period of budgetary austerity and the european union's loss of dynamism, the preservation of biodiversity requires investments that will have immediate, but also long-term, positive effects for all european citizens. the report by pavan sukhdev states that one euro invested today will be worth 100 euros in 2050. mr president, commissioner, i should like to begin by welcoming the members of the court and its president, mr caldeira. i would like to make a few comments, first on the timetable. it is november 2013, we will vote in april 2014: it is unacceptable that an institution of the quality of ours is so late, no matter how complex our organizations are. in highly complex private global entities, audit opinions are issued on 30 january following the year audited. we are objecting to the problems of translation, but 80% of the documents we receive are in english. so i hope we can remedy this situation. as regards the accounts certified by the court, i would like to reiterate my concern about the accounting of staff pensions. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i do not think that this is the right situation, because it means that the union's accounts are now 40 billion in debt on own funds. i will conclude on the opinion of the court, which i cannot understand. the treaty requires a statement of assurance on the accounts and the underlying transactions. in fact, we have a statement of assurance on the accounts, but on the underlying transactions we have a favourable opinion on the revenue and a favourable opinion on the commitments. the problem is even more complex when it comes to payments: evidence to support the negative opinion and, finally, a negative opinion. it's incomprehensible to me! the commissioner says he disagrees with the error rates, when it's a contradictory debate. i would like an audit report to be drawn up in accordance with the international auditing standards for the control of public funds.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report which proposes a regulation establishing a framework programme for research and innovation. this is the main proposal in the h2020 package. this report defines the three pillars that are the foundation of horizon 2020: pillar i 'scientific excellence', pillar ii 'industrial leadership', and pillar iii 'society challenges'. in addition, special attention has been paid to smes in order to facilitate their access to the programme, but also to guarantee them at least 20% of the combined budget of the 'leadership in generic and industrial technologies'. europe is thus participating in investment and in the industrial and scientific recovery.

in writing. i voted in favour of the new framework programme for research and innovation 'horizon 2020' (2014-2020). the programme brings together all the union's research and development funding actions, with a total budget of €70.2 billion. it is one of the largest research and innovation funds in the world. this is an increase of 15% compared to the previous period 2007-2013. i am pleased to see that european funding is focused on smes, whose potential for innovation and development is crucial to ensuring sustainable growth in the european union. the aim is to facilitate their access to the programme's funds through simplification mechanisms and to guarantee them at least 20% of the pillars 'industrial leadership' (pillar ii) and 'societal challenges' (pillar iii). in order to ensure that innovative enterprises can fully benefit from this programme, a special instrument to support smes has been set up. this instrument will be financed by the allocation of 7% of the budget over the entire duration of the programme. in addition, a single contact point for smes has been set up to facilitate their administrative procedures.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this programme because, despite a limited budget, it will ensure a balance between innovation and basic research, or strengthen the mobility of researchers through the increase of marie curie actions. other highlights: the new mechanism, the 'innovation expressway', will speed up the marketing and distribution of products by reducing the time between design and market launch; smes will benefit from facilitated access through shorter and simplified procedures and the establishment of a single point of contact and a support process throughout the innovation cycle. in short, these are all assets for improving european competitiveness, more than indispensable to support the recovery of the european economy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague teresa riera madurell, which amends the main proposal of the horizon 2020 package, which is based on three pillars: scientific excellence, industrial leadership and societal challenges. particular attention has been paid to smes to facilitate their access to the programme and to guarantee them a share of the budget. the report also supports open access to research publications that have received eu funding, while the results and data of research projects should be disseminated efficiently but with respect for the protection of commercially sensitive data. finally, in the field of ethics, research will have to respect national, european and international regulations, such as the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. i welcome the adoption of this report.

in writing. the european parliament has adopted a framework programme for research and innovation called horizon 2020, which will have a budget of €70.2 billion from 2014 to 2020. several european programmes that funded research and innovation have been merged in order to simplify the rules and to increase the coherence and effectiveness of this policy. horizon 2020 focuses on excellence in research and innovation, as well as addressing societal challenges and enhancing industrial competitiveness. we have identified three pillars for this policy: scientific excellence, industrial leadership in key technologies such as nanotechnology or biotechnology, and societal challenges in key areas such as food security, sustainable agriculture and energy. we have made it easier for smes to access eu funds by simplifying and reducing the time needed for procedures. smes will benefit from at least 11% of the horizon 2020 budget. i voted in favour of this programme, which will help to coordinate european research and promote innovation, particularly in smes, in order to stimulate our economy.
in writing. this framework programme for european research aims to strengthen the links between research and innovation. the model proposed is that of a forced convergence between research and the economy, of a system with the autonomy of universities (which must increase their external revenues in particular) and the contracting of researchers, etc. the programme thus aims to concentrate resources for the purpose of bringing new products to the market. research, particularly fundamental research, cannot and must not be subject to such a commercial and short-term view. i vote against it.

in writing. in the framework of the 2014-2020 research and innovation policy, horizon 2020 , the european parliament has defined new rules for participation and dissemination of results for the beneficiaries of funds. the new research policy should be more accessible to small research centres, thanks to simplified participation procedures. from now on, a single funding rate will be applied to each type of action funded by horizon 2020 . the rate of financing may be up to 100% for research and development activities and up to 70% for activities close to the market. the eligible costs have been better defined to provide participants with better information. we managed to reduce the deadline for grant awarding to eight months, which was a deterrent for potential applicants for european funds. we have also defined a new procedure to support innovative projects, based on calls for proposals without a mandated theme with shorter grant procedures. i voted in favour of this text because i believe it clarifies the rules applicable to participants and facilitates access to european funding for small structures.

in writing. smes account for more than 95% of european enterprises and are a particularly important source of employment in our territories. unfortunately, they are also the ones who suffer the most in times of economic downturn such as the one we are currently experiencing. it is particularly difficult for them to obtain bank loans to finance their establishment or expansion. and when they cannot obtain bank credit and investors are reluctant to take risks, a great deal of potential for employment and innovation is often lost! to remedy this situation, we have just adopted the sme support programme (cosme). now, businesses struggling to finance themselves with banks will be able to ask for the eu guarantee to get the credit they need. and the youngest and most promising of them will be able to benefit from direct eu funding. in total, almost €1.4 billion will be mobilised to support 400 000 smes in the eu from 2014 to 2020. proof that the eu is putting finance at the service of the real economy!

in writing. i voted for the report on european statistics because an increasing number of citizens do not trust european statistics. yet, reliable and accurate european statistics fulfil two key functions as a public good: they are the basis on which policy-makers make their decisions, and they serve as a barometer of the state of our economy and society and provide assurances to other governments and financial markets. the european statistical system therefore deserves special attention in order to make the targeting of our policies more effective.
in writing. the independence of statistical data is the key to judging the effectiveness of public policies, and an essential tool in the development of new measures. this is why this text is important: it aims to strengthen the confidence we can place in statistics by making them clearer, by making the process of producing them more transparent, and by putting in place the necessary measures to guarantee the independence of the bodies in charge of them. it is therefore a set of measures which are essential to the confidence which we europeans have in ourselves, and that is why i support this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i am in favour of guaranteeing the independence of the statistical authorities from political pressure that could be exerted at national and european level and of ensuring high quality of statistical data. especially in times of economic difficulties, it is essential that users of these statistics can be sure of their reliability. that is why i am particularly in favour of producing easily accessible statistics which are regularly updated to take account of european realities.
in writing. i enthusiastically supported the report by my colleague liem hoang ngoc to strengthen the independence of the national statistical institutes, of eurostat and to introduce strong sanctions in case of attempted manipulation of statistics. member states need to have a new instrument, the 'statistics confidence commitments', to implement the 'statistics code of conduct' and to put an end to certain practices which have seriously undermined the confidence of all in the real health of some european partners. it is in this sense that the council and the commission, which do not seem to share these objectives, should nevertheless return to the negotiating table and join the european parliament's efforts to achieve ambitious reform.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague liem hoang ngoc. this report concerns the revision of the regulation governing the european statistical system. in terms of european statistics, the objective remains to strengthen the reliability of data, the independence of statisticians and the transparency of the studies carried out. one of the important points of this report is the consultation of the european parliament during the process of appointing the director-general of eurostat. the report was adopted by 517 votes to 20, with 65 abstentions. i'm glad you did.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution on european statistics, which make it possible to assess the economic and social situation in europe. some errors or political pressures in the past have led to inaccurate statistics, so we have reiterated the need to guarantee the independence of the statistical authorities and asked eurostat and the national statistical institutes to respect a code of good practice. national statistical institutes and member state authorities will need to coordinate better with eurostat to ensure the transmission of accurate data. we have also asked the director-general of eurostat to report to the european parliament, in order to strengthen the democratic control of statistics. i voted in favour of this text which will make statistics more reliable and increase public confidence in these statistics.
in writing. the hoang ngoc report provides positive elements on the evaluation of european statistics to meet policy needs and the challenges created by recent economic developments. it advocated safeguarding the independence of the national statistical institutes, coordination between the national statistical offices and eurostat, and cooperation with the courts of auditors. however, i shall abstain because, while i support the principle of the independence of the national statistical offices, statistics need a complete revision to reflect current socioeconomic problems, which unfortunately are not covered in this report.
in writing. this report amends a european regulation which strengthens the independence of the european (mainly eurostat) and national statistical services to address the fraud and manipulation of statistics recently observed. the report recommends that european statistics be produced in the economic and social fields as a whole and not just for the data needed for budgetary surveillance under the stability pact. for example, he advocates the excellent idea that statistics on private debt should be published in the same way as those on public debt. the increased powers given to the commission to investigate possible statistical manipulation by member states are much more questionable, as are the proposed european fines. national administrative and judicial sanctions exist and could be strengthened rather than inventing a new european enforcement apparatus in the hands of the commission. applied in the context of the troika's austerity plans, these new powers of investigation and sanction could seriously undermine the sovereignty of states. i am afraid that the commission will not be able to accept this amendment.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the report on the revision of the regulation governing the european statistical system. to make good decisions, parliamentarians need reliable data, produced in a transparent manner and by independent statisticians. this text makes three improvements. it reinforces the code of conduct by commitments between the commission and the member states. it gives the commission extensive investigative and coordination powers. it improves the independence of eurostat by consulting parliament on the appointment of its director-general. i regret the commission's resistance, however. eurostat is the european statistical office and requires greater transparency and independence. unfortunately, the commission is opposed to parliament's demands and is trampling on its prerogatives. yet the memory of the emergence of the sovereign debt crisis persists and reminds us of the long way to go. a number of reforms to european economic governance are needed for a proper assessment of economic policies under the six-pack.
in writing. progress, eures and the microfinance facility: these three tools are now grouped together in a single programme for the period 2014-2020. the programme for employment and social innovation is part of the context of the crises we are experiencing. the idea is to support actions to increase social innovation, notably through experimentation with social policies, but also to develop the eures network to become a real european employment service and to encourage social entrepreneurship through easier access to finance. the grouping of three social instruments under one programme should allow for better coordination and thus greater efficiency in supporting those on the ground and those seeking employment or setting up a business.

in writing. the european parliament adopted the social change and social innovation programme, which merges three existing programmes. we have strengthened the cross-border dimension of the eures programme, which promotes worker mobility by allowing public employment services in different member states to exchange information on jobseekers and vacancies. we have also strengthened the progress programme to better coordinate member states' policies in the fields of employment, social inclusion, working conditions and the fight against discrimination. finally, we have maintained the european progress microfinance instrument, which offers micro-credits of less than eur 25 000 for the creation or development of small businesses, especially social enterprises. i am also pleased that parliament has obtained simplification of the management of this programme and that we have been able to reserve a percentage of the budget for youth employment. although the harmonisation of the social policies of the member states is still too limited, i voted in favour of this programme, which sets the stage for improved european cooperation in the field of social and employment policies.
in writing. this is the eu programme for social change and innovation. it combines three existing programmes - progress, eures and the microfinance facility. during the trilogue, the european parliament's negotiating team gave in to the commission and the council on the more progressive positions of the steinrück report. the text is therefore devoid of any measure that would actually promote social change. the eu's ridiculously small budget (€131 million per year) is a good indication of the eu's commitment to social innovation. i abstain, not to support but not to sanction what remains of the social ideal.

in writing. i am voting against this report which sets budgetary restrictions for the life programme for a period of 7 years. life has been one of the most successful eu programmes in addressing environmental and climate-related challenges. life has been running for 20 years and has been highly appreciated by local, regional and national public administrations, ngos, research institutes and smes. the budget allocated to life will be 0.318% of the eu budget, i.e. €3,456,655,000. this part is particularly weak in relation to the challenges and opportunities of the transition to a biodiversity-rich, resource-efficient and low-carbon society.
in writing. this text proposes a development on the margins of european environmental policy, whereas a real revolution in the field is needed. it does not abandon the liberal illusion, but persists in this course by not proposing any major policy of ecological bifurcation of our ways of life and production. it does identify some negative points such as geographical inequalities but does not offer anything convincing to solve them. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it is also satisfied with the budgetary surpluses which the european commission is willing to allocate to environmental matters. finally, it simply bypasses the member states in order to promote a europe of the regions. i vote against it.

in writing. i voted in favour of the new european environment programme 'life' with a budget of €3.46 billion for the next 7 years. the priorities of the new life programme are many and include nature and biodiversity, energy efficiency and climate change mitigation and adaptation. one of the major advances in this new programme is that our overseas territories, in particular new caledonia, french polynesia and wallis and futuna, will now be able to participate and receive european funding. this new opportunity is part of the continuity of my parliamentary action which led to the creation in 2011 and for 3 years of a preparatory action entitled best, to finance actions to protect biodiversity and enhance ecosystem services in overseas regions and communities. overseas holds more than 80% of europe's biodiversity, so it was necessary for europe to protect and enhance this wealth under the new life programme. so i am very pleased that this extension is extended to all our overseas communities.
in writing. since 1992, the european funding programme life has supported many good environmental protection initiatives. i am thinking, for example, of the eco-camps project in aquitaine, which is concerned with the eco-design of buildings in campsites, the aware project to reduce water pollution in languedoc-roussillon, or the reclionbat project, which is concerned with the construction of an innovative heavy metal recycling plant in the midi-pyrénées region, to mention only my constituency. at the time of the renewal of the european funding programmes for 2014-2020, i gave my full support to this new life+ programme, which shows the persistence of european ambition in the field of the environment. this ambition is first manifested at the quantitative level, since a significant increase in the budget is proposed, in favour of the opening of a sub-programme "climate action". the programme also creates new measures such as the creation of 'integrated projects', which aim to implement environmental strategies on a wider territorial scale and to mobilise other european, national or private funds. the success of these small initiatives should not make us forget the need to set up a large environmental project at european level.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new european programme for financing environmental projects, the famous life programme. this agreement, which was supported by a very large majority in the european parliament, is the result of several months of negotiations with the governments. life was set up in 1992 to finance environmental projects and to combat climate change. i welcome its renewal for seven years and the increase of its budget by 50%, from the current eur 2.2 billion to eur 3.4 billion. but the most notable advance is in the philosophy of the programme. the projects will be financed by the european union on the basis of their qualities and not according to a breakdown by country. the explicit recognition of the overseas territories is also to be welcomed. they alone represent 85% of biodiversity in europe and will benefit from these funds. i am glad that the commitments made continue to give the environment the importance it deserves. the development of europe's environmental wealth cannot be achieved without adequate funding.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european life programme, a budgetary programme for projects in the environmental and climate fields. while the overall budget for the life programme is less than 1% of the eu budget, as requested by the european parliament, it has been increased from €2.2 billion for the period 2007-2013 to €3.1 billion for the period 2014-2020, an increase of almost 50%. the european parliament's battle against the council will allow more projects to be launched with eu support to safeguard biodiversity and protect nature. the selection will be based on their quality and thus their potential to achieve environmental and climate objectives. that's a good thing. the programme also introduces a provision on integrated projects aimed at improving and strengthening the integration of environmental and climate objectives into other eu policies. they will be able to receive other european funding in the context of the application of european environmental legislation. despite this paltry funding in the face of climate issues and the urgency of taking action against certain pollutants (water, air), this is a step in the right direction, which is not so common today.

in writing. the fiscalis programme aims to combat tax fraud and evasion. these represent more than €1 000 billion in losses per year for the member states of the european union. i am therefore surprised that it is not proposed to increase the fiscalis budget more strongly and to introduce the possibility of financing human resources. i denounce the silence in this report on the european factors that contribute to the development of tax evasion: liberalization of capital movements, european transfer pricing regulation that allows large groups to avoid taxation, the eu's complacency towards tax havens and banking secrecy. the union cannot afford to ignore the austerity policies it decides on, which have a serious impact on the tax services of the member states and thus undermine the fight against fraud. i therefore vote against this text, which ignores the real means of combating tax evasion.

in writing. this draft legislative resolution establishes an action programme for customs in the european union for the period 2014-2020 (customs 2020). this could be an opportunity to affirm an objective of combating fiscal, social and environmental dumping and a serious public programme for the management of goods entering the union by sea. it's not. the policy priorities in customs policy described relate to facilitating global trade and enhancing competitiveness. the only concrete measure mentioned is that of replacing the general shortage of resources (human and material) caused by the crises in the public finances of the member states by a strengthening of electronic management, which cannot replace the human competence of knowledge of flows, the capacity for physical control which must remain the pivot of customs work. the text therefore again promotes a liberal framework for international trade, which is opposed to an effective customs policy geared to the solidarity-based protectionism we need. i vote against it.

the result of long negotiations to strike a balance between the conservation of the resource and the preservation of employment in the fisheries and aquaculture sectors. we have put in place important conservation mechanisms. one of the main objectives of this policy is to achieve biomass levels beyond those that can produce maximum sustainable yield by 2015. we have also approved the obligation to land all catches. i would like to say that this will be difficult for the fishermen, whose vessels are not always equipped to land everything. the de minimis threshold of 5% will still allow fishermen more selective gear. parliament also calls for funding for data collection and controls. we want measures for fisheries that are environmentally, economically and socially sustainable. the generalisation of multiannual management plans will also provide a long-term view of the resource. i would also like to point out that the member states are free to manage quotas collectively if they so wish. it is a long battle that parliament has fought to give this freedom of choice over the management of fishing rights. we have managed to avoid the obligation of transferable fishing concessions, i.e. the commodification and liberalisation of a market in fishing rights. the common market organisation has given producer organisations a greater role. they manage the marketing of mr president, we had three challenges, three major issues to be dealt with in the report on the large funds. firstly, to protect vulnerable stocks; secondly, to ensure that all species in the deep sea can regenerate themselves in a sustainable way; thirdly, to preserve jobs in the fishing sector. the adoption of the compromise reached in the committee on fisheries will enable all three objectives to be achieved. i, for one, will not betray my word. the partial ban on trawling and the sanctioning of an ecological footprint in 90% of the international waters of the north-east atlantic, the setting of quotas for all species, which are therefore more stringent than the cfp, and the mapping of vulnerable areas within two years have given us the means to achieve the environmental objectives we have set ourselves. but it is equally important to say that, through compromise, we are meeting our third challenge, which is to maintain a vulnerable activity in the 10% of areas retained for deep-sea fishing. that is at least 758 vessels, according to the commission's own impact study, and therefore thousands of fishing seamen who could continue to operate. in these unemployment times, the loss of these jobs would drive some of our regions in scotland, ireland, france, spain and portugal over the edge.
