madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the fisheries agreement between the european union and morocco, which both parties have been waiting for for so long, is finally put to the vote in the european parliament. the new protocol to the agreement, initialled on 24 july, allows 126 eu vessels to fish for surplus in moroccan waters thanks to the financial contribution of the agreement, which amounts to €30 million. half of this financial contribution is for access to water and the other half is for the development of the moroccan fisheries sector. the kingdom of morocco shall be required to submit regular detailed reports on the use of the financial contribution for the development of the fisheries sector. i would like to remind you that this agreement is excellent because it is mutually beneficial. all recommendations of the european parliament's resolution of 14 december 2011 have been taken into account. this agreement is sustainable, the fishing zones have been modified to meet morocco's requirements and the opinions of the scientists of the moroccan research institute have been taken into account. the quotas for pelagic fisheries have not been increased. the agreement also contains an exclusivity clause, which avoids private licences over which the european union has no visibility. it also contains a genuine clause on respect for human rights. the obligations for moroccan seamen to be on board are higher than under the previous protocol. the financial compensation shall be spread over the whole territory; so the whole local population will benefit. i therefore look to the wisdom of this institution tomorrow to give a favourable opinion on the conclusion of this agreement.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, two years of negotiations, which you, madam commissioner, have been conducting, two years which have finally resulted in a proposal for an agreement which will actually enable european fishermen, especially spanish fishermen, and all moroccan and sahrawi fishermen to work and earn a decent living from their fishing activity. what should we say today? i appeal to my colleagues in parliament and my group. that all the complaints of the meps have been answered positively. secondly, that sustainability is ensured since only surplus fish will be fished. thirdly, that the fairness of the agreement is ensured. morocco will provide an annual report detailing the economic impact of the agreement, in particular for the sahrawis. fourthly, and finally, that international law be respected. the legal opinion of the european parliament concluded that the measure was legal, with a human rights clause. i therefore call for a vote in favour and i am very pleased that my socialist and democratic group, through the voice of our colleague capoulas santos, is calling, by a large majority, for a vote tomorrow in favour of this fisheries agreement between the european union and the kingdom of morocco.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, if i tell you that the automobile industry is going through an unprecedented crisis, it will probably sound familiar. yet, it is a very serious reality. the sector recorded barely 12 million units sold in 2012 compared to around 17 million in 2007, just before the crisis, a decline from the 1990s. the car is a pillar of our economy in many ways: a pillar of our growth, because it represents almost 4% of gdp; a pillar of the regional economy, as it is the main economic activity in dozens of regions in europe; the second pillar is the social pillar, with 12 million direct and indirect jobs. but above all, it is a technological pillar, because 80% of private investment in research is made by the automobile. all of this allows us to say one thing: the automobile industry, by its position at the heart of industry, is an undeniable indicator of the state of our economy. today, the peoples of europe are wondering about the future of this production. it was therefore inconceivable that the members of the european parliament, the only direct representatives of the people, should not take part in the debate. we have addressed this issue and we have done well. with this report, we have examined the cars 2020 action plan, which the commission launched in november 2012. this action plan, i must say, was an excellent starting point, and i would like to thank vice-president tajani for all the work that has gone into it. i would like to welcome the cars 21 process, which has been a long but fruitful process of consultation with industry. however, the action plan sometimes fails to be as succinct as it should be. so we had to add real value to it to be heard. the report i am presenting to you today has only one ambition: to propose innovative solutions to get back to growth in the automotive sector, innovative solutions because we have two challenges to face. in the very short term, the urgency must prevail, the urgency of getting this sector out of the vicious circle of crisis, and in the medium term we must have the ambition to bring our policies in the motor industry closer together so that we can act as one rather than as divided. in the end, we must fight for a europe that acts, but above all, a europe that protects. this report emphasizes a number of points. firstly, to improve the commission's approach considerably by identifying more precisely overcapacity and restructuring as the main points of the crisis in the sector, which are too little present in the action plan. the report will then call for the gradual introduction of clearer and more predictable regulation for industry. it will encourage investment. we must first let the industry get its head out of the water before we impose new standards on it which will only make it a little more vulnerable. the report also points out that technological advancement and know-how are europe's only competitive advantages over the rest of the world. we must therefore concentrate on what we do best to ensure that we are competitive in the long term. we welcome and encourage flexibility of work based on social dialogue and reorientation and the improvement of employee know-how in the light of market developments. finally, we call for a strengthening of our legal arsenal and our practices to combat unfair competition within europe and in external markets. ladies and gentlemen, here are the main lines of the report. it reflects a good compromise, which was supported by a very large majority of the votes in the industry committee. so tomorrow, by voting in favour of this report, you will be demonstrating that just because a fight is difficult it does not mean that it cannot be won.

member of the commission. − mr president, at the outset i would like to thank ms gardini and all the members of the european parliament who have worked tirelessly over the years to shape the legislation presented to you today. the decision you will be taking is about providing better protection for our citizens and for our economies against a clear trend of more frequent and more devastating disasters. it is also about our ability to offer better assistance to disaster victims worldwide. you are aware that in the last decades we have witnessed a very clear increase in the frequency and intensity of disasters here in europe. we have lost in 10 years 100 000 of our citizens to summer heat, to floods, to summer and winter storms, and this has also affected significantly our economy with a cumulative cost of over eur 150 billion. this is a trend that we are experiencing worldwide. in just the last three years, for the first time in human history, we have damage costs that exceed usd 100 billion a year and we know that this is only a fraction of the costs because what it reflects is the insured damage, and not the damage overall. here in europe this summer the floods in the central part of our continent have cost us over eur 12 billion, and for germany this has been the highest damage cost on record. so there is not a day to be lost in acting against this trend and with the new legislation we are taking a leap forward in creating a robust disaster management system for europe: one that focuses on preparedness and prevention, and one that delivers a pre-planned predictable coordinated response. for the first time in european history, our member states will accept a legal obligation in the field of preparedness and prevention, and we will set up a voluntary pool of eu assets and experts on standby for immediate deployment should a disaster overwhelm one of our countries or a country overseas. this legislation responds to a call by parliament that i have personally heard many times: that we need europe to be as one in the face of disasters. the european emergency response capacity that you have asked for many times will become a reality with this legislation. we have followed a bottom-up approach, one that is based on voluntary contributions by member states to the pool and that respects the principle of subsidiarity. i would like to finish by saying that just weeks ago in the philippines i saw with my own eyes what it means to have europe acting as one and i am very proud of this achievement. in the future, implementing the legislation would again require your support and i very much count on it.

in writing. the fisheries protocol between the european union and its moroccan partner expired in february 2011 and the protocol that should have succeeded it was rejected by the european parliament on 14 december 2011. the new proposal has considerable advantages for both partners and appears more balanced, as the cost to the european taxpayer is reduced by 30% and fishing opportunities are increased by 33%. the european fleet is facing a serious economic and social crisis, and the income from fishing under the agreement could be €2.5 for every euro invested. such a benefit cannot be overlooked, especially since environmental criteria are also required. finally, many concerns have been raised about the distribution of the economic and social benefits of the protocol to the general population. i heard them. and that is why i would like to point out that a provision on respect for human rights has been included. the two sides have reached a very acceptable agreement and i therefore wish to commend the efforts and conciliatory spirit of the moroccan authorities.
in writing. i supported the recommendation of my colleague carmen fraga estévez to renew the protocol to the eu-morocco fisheries agreement. the previous protocol had been the subject of a number of criticisms which prevented its extension. the new partnership, on the other hand, has made significant progress in environmental, economic and financial terms. the text was adopted by 310 votes to 204, with 49 abstentions. i am very pleased with this result.
in writing. on 10 december, the european parliament adopted a fisheries agreement between the european union and france, which affects 11 countries, including france, and more than 1500 fishermen. european vessels will be able to fish in moroccan waters in exchange for an annual payment from the european union of €30 million, including €14 million to support the development of the moroccan fishing sector. the previous agreement was criticised for its cost, but the terms of the agreement we have approved are very satisfactory, its cost has been reduced and fishing opportunities have been increased by one third. the agreement also stipulates that the local population must benefit from the money paid by the european union. i therefore voted in favour of this agreement, which offers new fishing opportunities to european vessels while respecting and supporting local fishermen.
in writing. as a member of the eu/morocco friendship group, i have been interested in the renewal of fisheries agreements with morocco. renewing these agreements was essential if the european union was to remain the leading partner in the region more generally. i am therefore pleased that the agreement was voted for.
in writing. under this fisheries agreement, 126 vessels will be able to fish in moroccan waters in return for a four-year allocation of €30 million to morocco. compared with the old protocol, this allocation is down by 17%, while fishing opportunities are up by 33%. but the fisheries agreement with morocco does not respect international law, since it does not exclude the coastal waters of western sahara, and the sahrawi population has not been consulted. the kingdom of morocco is therefore not entitled to issue fishing authorisations in those maritime areas. in addition, the protocol raises concerns about the sustainability of fisheries. it is stated that: the eu will have to ensure that morocco respects the economic and social consequences for the people of western sahara, and a suspension mechanism is also provided for in the event of violations of human rights and democratic principles. but these clauses remain subject to the commission's discretion. i voted against this fisheries protocol, as the openings cannot compensate for the violation of international law.
in writing. i voted in favour of the eu-morocco fisheries partnership agreement which brings improvements over the agreement rejected by the european parliament in december 2012. the agreement allows 126 eu vessels to fish in moroccan waters in return for €30 million to develop the moroccan fishing industry. the agreement respects the parliament's demands on human rights, the protection of resources and the obligation to take moroccan seamen on board european vessels.
in writing. the aim of this agreement is to establish a partnership between the eu and morocco on fisheries. although it is very economically beneficial for the union, i cannot accept that it should also apply to the fishery resources of western sahara. the population of this territory, whose moroccan occupation is not recognised by the un and the international court of justice, was not involved in the negotiations and was therefore unable to assert its claims. a vote in favour of this agreement is therefore de facto to approve the illegal occupation of this territory and to turn a blind eye to the repression suffered by the sahrawis, which i cannot accept. i therefore voted against this agreement.
in writing. on this international human rights day, parliament approved by 310 votes to 204 the fisheries agreement between the eu and morocco, whose extension had been rejected by the same parliament a year ago by 296 votes to 326. however, morocco has no sovereignty over western sahara and therefore no competence to sign international agreements, as the hague court pointed out in 1975 and as has been reiterated in numerous un resolutions. during the debate, the european fisheries commissioner justified this agreement by referring to the respect of human rights in western sahara. that was amazing. the repression of peaceful demonstrations is still as violent in the occupied territories and the condemnations of sahrawi activists are still as heavy. nothing's changed since last year. but the economic concerns of an agreement that would be beneficial to the eu won out this time. the european parliament, under pressure from the member states, has renounced its prerogatives and a key means of pressure to secure respect for the rights of the saharawi people. i have not changed my mind: i voted against.
in writing. after several years of negotiations and despite many lies and delaying manoeuvres, i welcome the conclusion of the fisheries agreement between the european union and the kingdom of morocco. our moroccan friends are privileged partners of europe and it was incomprehensible that some would try to block this agreement, which is mutually beneficial and meets all the conditions we had set: the sustainability of fishing activities and real economic and social benefits for the local populations. the renewal of this old fisheries agreement will allow european vessels to sail and fish in moroccan territorial waters, including those off western sahara, which i consider to be an integral part of the kingdom of morocco, despite what some ill-informed and ill-intentioned members of parliament would have us believe. this is therefore a further step towards deepening the euro-moroccan partnership and strengthening our economic relations on both sides of the mediterranean. as a strong advocate of further integration of eu-morocco relations, i see this as a source of great satisfaction and a very promising step forward for the future.

in writing. the international labour organisation (ilo) convention on the safety of chemicals at work (convention no 170) is an important instrument for strengthening the protection of workers, the environment and, more broadly, society as a whole. i have therefore decided to support this report which gives its approval to the council's decision to allow the member states to ratify it.
in writing. the aim of this recommendation, which was adopted by parliament and which i supported, is to enable the council to conclude, on behalf of the european union, the protocol against the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition. this additional protocol to the united nations international convention against transnational organized crime provides for measures to confiscate arms which have been illicitly manufactured or trafficked, and for measures to prevent the illicit reactivation of deactivated firearms. the adoption of this protocol is part of the wider fight against terrorist organisations. the gun trade is a source of income and material for terrorist groups.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mrs véronique mathieu houillon, on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition. it also benefits criminal groups and terrorists by providing them with an additional source of income and by increasing their destructive potential. the protocol improves the prevention and fight against illicit trafficking in firearms by enhancing controls on weapons through their marking, import and export authorisations, and by strengthening cooperation and the exchange of information between states parties. information and exchanges are the key to better coordination in the fight against criminal networks by our customs, police and military forces.
in writing. the fight against illicit trafficking in firearms knows no borders and requires international action. with this text, we are giving a new impetus to the fight against transnational crime and the illicit trafficking of firearms in europe and thus to the protection of our fellow citizens. the aim of this text is to improve cooperation between the member states in this field by sharing information.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it is essential to strengthen the fight against organised crime in the european union through the united nations convention specific to this matter. the figures for firearms in the european union are alarming to say the least. almost half a million of them are lost or stolen in the eu and are still unaccounted for. in france, the authorities reported a 40% increase in seizures of stolen civilian and military weapons between 2010 and 2011. moreover, in view of the arrival of large quantities of powerful weapons for military use in the union, in particular from the western balkans and the former soviet bloc, it is time to have a legislative arsenal that addresses this issue.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague véronique mathieu houillon which supports the ratification of an additional protocol to the united nations convention against transnational organized crime. the agreement will allow for more effective control of weapons through their marking and will strengthen cooperation and the exchange of information between member states. this text was adopted by a very large majority, with 578 votes in favour, 5 against and 18 abstentions, which i welcome.
in writing. when a member of the world trade organisation (wto) has negotiating rights in a state which joins the european customs union by acceding to the eu, the eu is obliged to enter into negotiations with those wto members to counterbalance the effects of accession which bring previously concluded wto agreements into disarray. the eu-china agreement, for which i voted, is a direct consequence of the accession of bulgaria and romania and provides for mutually satisfactory compensation vis-à-vis china.

in writing. i supported the report by my colleague helmut scholz which adapts the compensation agreements with china following the entry into the customs union of bulgaria and romania. the accession had indeed caused a trade loss for china, necessitating this adaptation of the agreements. i welcome the adoption of this text.

in writing. i voted for the report on beef imports because the memorandum of understanding signed between the european union and the united states has allowed for the gradual lifting and suspension of sanctions imposed by the united states on agricultural products from the union in return for the opening of an autonomous tariff quota with zero duty for high-quality beef from non-hormone treated bovine animals. parliament approved an amendment to increase the annual amount of the autonomous tariff quota for high-quality beef to 45 000 tonnes on the basis of the most favoured nation principle.
in writing. i supported the recommendation of my colleague, mr vital moreira, that an agreement be concluded with the united states on beef from animals not treated with growth hormones. the signing of this agreement has allowed the gradual lifting of us sanctions on european agricultural products. i welcome the adoption of this text.
in writing. − the european union and the united states signed a memorandum of understanding in 2009 on imports of us beef not treated with growth hormones and on increased us duties on certain eu products. by voting in favour, i express my willingness to extend this protocol until 2015. with this extension we intend to further increase the climate of mutual trust, which will lead to greater economic integration between the united states and the european union, also promoting the definition of the ongoing negotiations for the transatlantic trade and development partnership (ttip).
in writing. in 1988, the european union imposed an embargo on american beef, much of which was treated with growth hormones. the united states retaliated by imposing very high customs duties, which led to the closure of the american market to many european products. after 20 years of unsuccessful proceedings before the world trade organisation (wto), the european union has reached an interim compromise with the united states, which has allowed us to maintain the ban on the import of hormone-treated cattle in exchange for increased import quotas for high-quality beef from the united states and canada and the lifting of us sanctions. unfortunately, no final solution has been found with the united states and the agreement is coming to an end. as of february 2014, the united states could have imposed sanctions on the european union of up to $116 million per year. this solution was not acceptable to european producers, so i voted in favour of extending the deadline to put an end once and for all to a trade conflict that has lasted for more than twenty years and which has had serious effects on a large number of european agricultural products.
in writing. the agreement in the moreira report is a follow-up to what was put in place in 2009 to resolve the long-running trade dispute between the us and the eu over beef. the dispute led to the imposition of customs duties by the united states, following the european blockade on the use of growth hormones and the conditions of farming. the text adopted aims to allow the import of 45 tonnes of beef free of customs duties, as 'high quality beef' (without hormones in particular), until august 2015. this extension of the agreement does not contain any amendment to the current legislation, but given the prospect of a transatlantic trade agreement with the united states, which is implicit in the proposal, i refused to support the proposal.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which sets out, through a revised memorandum of understanding, the modalities for the opening of a phase 3 in the framework of the measures on meat and meat products (hormones) which is the subject of a dispute between the eu and the us before the wto.
in writing. while waiting for the eu-us free trade agreement to enter into force, despite my wishes, and thus for the arrival on the european market of us food products treated with hormones or chlorine, i decided to support the parliamentary report which wants to limit the import of us beef to beef not treated with growth hormones. i am voting to confirm my commitment to offering quality food products to european consumers.
in writing. i voted in favour of the application of this decision, which is the second step in the implementation of the agreement signed between the us and the eu to settle the trade dispute over hormone-treated beef. while the agreement is working well in our trade relations with the united states, i regret that it has been much slower to implement with canada, which had concluded the same type of memorandum in a similar dispute. for reasons of consistency, and at a time when our trade agreement with canada is undergoing legal revision, i hope that the two agreements, the american and the canadian, will be able to apply together quickly.

in writing. i supported the report by my colleague elisabeth jeggle which stresses the complementarity of the agreements being negotiated with canada and recalls that such agreements must include conditionality and political clauses on human rights and democracy. the report was adopted by 509 votes to 111, with 39 abstentions, which i welcome.
in writing. on 10 december, the european parliament adopted a resolution to encourage the european union and canada to sign a strategic partnership agreement to strengthen their economic, political and cultural relations. the agreement will complement the comprehensive economic and trade agreement, for which negotiations were concluded on 18 october. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that cooperation between the european union and canada should be strengthened. we must nevertheless remain vigilant about the terms of this agreement, which is why we have insisted on the need to respect reciprocal conditionality and to consult civil society.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. the motion by mrs jeggle was adopted. some of the proposals in this report were in the right direction, such as the inclusion of a human rights clause allowing any agreement with canada to be suspended, or the involvement of civil society, but it is still a vote that steers the union towards a free trade without safeguards. the recommendation calls on the other institutions to sign the trade and economic agreement as soon as possible. however, the latter has been negotiated in total opacity so far, including for parliamentarians, and the main point that has emerged is the strengthening of the right of investors, who will now be able to attack the member states on their legislation. this is very dangerous for the community acquis and for the precautionary policy, particularly as regards shale gas or gmos. i voted against this agreement, which, despite its positive aspects, is the seal of an economic and trade agreement of which we know very little.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the negotiations for a strategic partnership agreement between the eu and canada, historic trading partners. the eu and canada have negotiated a strategic partnership agreement to strengthen their economic, political and cultural relations. it is important for this agreement, as for others, that there are reciprocal conditionality clauses on human rights and democracy.
in writing. canada and the european union have started negotiations towards a strategic partnership agreement. an agreement in principle was reached between the two sides but canada rejects certain passages which refer to human rights and efforts to prevent the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. these two elements appear to be essential and are the most important points of this agreement. i therefore decided to vote against the report because it supports the conclusion of the agreement. indeed, apart from being opposed to free trade agreements of this type, the fact that canada does not wish to recognise human rights and does not participate in the non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction led me to vote against the report.
in writing. i voted against this report on the negotiations on the eu-canada strategic partnership agreement. the agreement is part of the extension of the "comprehensive economic and trade agreement" concluded on 18 october 2013 between the eu and canada, the content of which is still unknown but which, according to the commission, represents a full-scale test for the great transatlantic market. moreover, if the status of strategic partner is an empty shell (it confers no special rights or duties if such a country is only supposed to "help the european union to enforce its external policies"), it seems in the present case that even filling out such an unambitious specification would be too much to ask. the negotiations between the eu and canada are aimed at including elements in the text of the agreement which would refer to the importance of affirming human rights and efforts to prevent the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. free trade at the heart of the partnership, the absence of safeguards which should be taken for granted: the union could do without this kind of agreement.
in writing. as part of the global effort to make the financial system more resilient, there is a need for all market participants to have a clearer understanding of the impacts that financial markets can have on their functioning and business model. the report acknowledges that there are many other non-bank entities that must nevertheless be considered as financial institutions, including insurance companies, asset managers and payment systems. however, as international work on these areas is not yet completed or is under negotiation, this report i supported focuses on the next steps to be taken to ensure that the european banking system becomes one of the safest in the world.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the recovery and resolution framework for non-bank institutions. the financial crisis has revealed the extent to which the global financial system is integrated and how contagious a failure in a risk management procedure in a major market player can be. as part of the global effort to strengthen the resilience of the system, all market players need to understand better how to operate or orderly shut down their business in a stressed situation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the swinburne report, which aims to make the european economic market work more efficiently by strengthening controls on the activities of non-banking actors, including insurance agencies. the report calls on the financial authorities to monitor closely the financial health of these institutions and, if necessary, to take appropriate measures to avoid exposing the european economy to collateral risks.
in writing. in view of the current economic difficulties, it is essential to ensure an effective recovery and resolution framework for non-bank institutions. such european harmonisation of responses to financial difficulties makes it possible to overcome the economic weaknesses of certain non-bank institutions. the measures proposed in this text therefore strengthen these institutions and in particular restrict the potential contagion effects between financial institutions which are damaging to our european economies.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to clarify the situation concerning non-banking institutions. i support any action by the european union which stresses the importance of drawing up european legislation based on the principles adopted at the level of the world bank and the international monetary fund. however, i believe that non-bank financial institutions themselves should develop comprehensive recovery plans, which identify the core activities and services in order to clarify this situation as much as possible. there is no room for such ambiguities in the economic and financial context in which the european union and our citizens find themselves.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague kay swinburne which stresses the need for operators of market-critical infrastructure to demonstrate good governance and strong risk management to avoid contagion effects in the event of a global financial crisis. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the recovery and resolution framework for non-banks which recommends the establishment of comprehensive arrangements for the recovery of non-banks, including protection against all foreseeable circumstances.
in writing. currently, only banks need to develop recovery and resolution plans in order to have the capacity to react in the event of a financial market crash and thus avoid systemic impacts. this owninitiative report aims to establish a similar framework for non-bank financial institutions, as their failures can, like banks, have disastrous consequences for society. the report covers, for example, the shares of insurance companies and asset managers. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it is essential to frame and increase the stability of non-bank financial institutions in order to avoid new financial crises and the disastrous consequences this can have on society.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european union's space industrial policy which aims to improve the competitiveness of the eu's space industry. it must be able to exploit its full potential as china revives the idea of a race to the moon. better coordination and efficiency in industry are at the heart of this report.

in writing. i support the development of a strong space industrial policy in the european union. article 189 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union gives the european union the competence to develop this potential. an ambitious space industrial policy can generate jobs and growth. i support in particular the priority given to the copernicus programme in the establishment of this industrial space policy. to ensure its full effectiveness, this programme needs a clear framework.
in writing. space technology, one of the cornerstones of the european economy, is of particular importance for the competitiveness of the european union. today, the total revenue of the space industry is in the order of 5.5 billion euros a year. at the same time, the space sector in europe represents 30 000 direct jobs in some 2 000 companies. the growth potential of this sector must therefore be unlocked by putting it at the service of the telecommunications, transport, environment and agriculture sectors. in other words, it is a question of giving it a genuine european orientation. this approach is part of a wider logic of reindustrialisation of the european continent. europe must support sectors in which it is at the forefront, such as space technologies, while working towards the emergence of new industrial production sectors, especially in innovation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because a european review of space policy is now indispensable. as a member of parliament from a constituency where aerospace is a major economic driver, with major players such as airbus, thales and the national centre for space studies, i am trying to defend this sector of the future in the european parliament. i therefore consider that supporting research and innovation in the space sector is essential for this sector, which represents a high added value for the union and the region i represent. what was once the driving force behind the construction of europe must now be continued. that is why i fully support these initiatives to modernise the european space industry.
in writing. the european parliament has just adopted a report on the european space industry. the industry employs 35,000 highly skilled workers. a multitude of services depend directly or indirectly on space technologies, making this industry a driver for growth and innovation (satellite communication services, for example). the european parliament has always advocated an ambitious european space policy, as does this report, which calls for better cooperation between the european space agency and the national agencies. with eads just announcing the elimination of 5 800 jobs in europe, including a thousand in france, we need ambitious policies more than ever. we must build a european public hub for scientific, industrial and military space and make the european space agency sustainable, while guaranteeing its missions of public and scientific utility. let us continue to defend european cooperation, without falling into the trap of an internal market in the space industry. it would be a death threat to this industry.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague angelika niebler, which aims to improve the competitiveness of the european space industry, a sector that is a driver of growth and innovation. this requires better coordination of space activities of the eu, the european space agency and the member states and an acceleration of the development of the galileo and copernicus programmes. i welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which aims to create a genuine internal market for the space industry, a vehicle for growth and innovation. it is important for the eu to remain competitive and to continue to lead in this strategic area.
in writing. the success of the european project is measured by the public recognition it receives. in the industrial field, aeronautics and space are by far the best examples. our constituency is also at the forefront of this, since it is the seat of very large companies. it is therefore essential that europe should have an industrial policy and major industrial projects for space. space still offers us enormous prospects.
in writing. the space sector is crucial for europe in many ways. the industry generates an annual turnover of almost eur 6.5 billion and employs 34,500 highly qualified people. citizens use a multitude of services in their daily lives that depend directly or indirectly on the space sector (television, high-speed internet, navigation systems and the european automatic emergency call system). finally, the space industry, which creates high value-added jobs, has great potential for growth and innovation. we all know that the space industry requires heavy investment and particularly long development cycles, and in the face of increasing competition from new space nations such as china and india, the efforts of the individual member states of the union are no longer sufficient to meet the challenges of the future in this sector. a strong european space policy is therefore needed, strengthening coordination between member states and allowing synergy effects with efforts developed by each in this field. that is the spirit of this resolution, which i supported.
in writing. the european parliament has just voted on a report on the space industry. a multitude of services depend on space technology. many sectors outside space benefit from the technical discoveries made in this industry, which plays a leading role in many areas of the european economy (satellite communication services for example). the european parliament also called for a european space policy to be ambitious, while the united states remains the world's leading space nation and other nations such as china and india are also making progress in this field. i voted for this report.

in writing. the common fisheries policy (cfp) has been thoroughly reformed in recent months. parliament and the council reached consensus on maximum sustainable yield (msy), quota management and the principle of no-discharge. i voted in favour of this new version of the cfp, which should therefore enter into force on 1 january 2014, as it will make the eu one of the world's leading models for sustainable fisheries.
in writing. i voted against the amendment in order to support the recommendations for second reading because the report makes it possible to: ensure environmentally, socially and economically sustainable fisheries and aquaculture; apply the precautionary approach to fisheries to achieve biomass levels above those achieving maximum sustainable yield; eliminate discharges into the sea by means of the landing obligation; adapt fishing capacity to fishing opportunities; continue to guarantee a fair standard of living for those who depend on fishing; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the aquaculture sector is not left behind.
in writing. i voted in favour of the basic regulation of the new common fisheries policy for the period 2014-2020. this regulation aims to strike a balance between the protection of the resource and the preservation of employment in the fisheries and aquaculture sectors. a realistic timetable will allow the progressive reduction of discards at sea. i think, however, that the obligation to land all catches will be difficult to implement. the vessels are not equipped to land all their catch. with this regulation, i support the construction of more selective instruments and the generalization of multiannual management plans which allow a long-term view of the resource. finally, i welcome the abolition of the obligation to grant transferable fishing concessions, which would have resulted in the commercialisation of fishing rights. the new common fisheries policy provides a structural framework for environmentally, economically and socially sustainable fisheries.
in writing. with this text, we are taking an important step towards avoiding overfishing by encouraging controlled and sustainable fisheries. in other words, it gives us the means to ensure responsible management of fisheries resources. finally, this text will allow for the regionalisation of decision-making, which will give member states greater latitude and stimulate local development.
in writing. today, europe's fish stocks, particularly in the atlantic and the mediterranean, are threatened by overfishing. with over 350 000 europeans dependent on fisheries and the processing industry, a lasting reform of the common policy was needed to preserve this important sector of the european union's economy in the medium and long term. under the new common fisheries policy, the annual renewal criteria will help maintain fish stocks. traditional fishing techniques will also be recognised and preserved. conservation of fish stocks and an end to discards - more than a quarter of catches are wasted each year - are also key elements in the continuation of small-scale, artisanal and coastal fishing. this new common fisheries policy is a major step forward for france, which is europe's leading maritime interface.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal because the conservation of the seabed and fisheries resources are major issues for the coming decades. as a member of parliament representing a constituency stretching from the mediterranean sea to the atlantic ocean, i am a strong advocate of the need to implement future programmes to preserve marine diversity. in this respect, i support the general objective of the proposal to ensure that fishing and aquaculture activities create long-term sustainable environmental conditions that contribute to food security. this sector is one of the main strengths of our regions and requires special attention.
in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation by my colleague ulrike rodust, which amends the common fisheries policy by introducing measures to make it more sustainable. this is achieved by requiring vessels to retain all quota fish caught instead of discarding the least profitable species, by establishing protected areas because of their sensitive ecosystem and by establishing maximum sustainable ceilings to ensure the recovery of fish stocks. i therefore welcome the adoption of this recommendation.
in writing. on 10 december, the european parliament adopted the new common fisheries policy for the period 2014-2020. some of the measures in this policy are moving in the right direction, notably efforts in the area of labelling and consumer information, which will help to favour quality products and local artisanal fishing. nevertheless, i regret the adoption of this text, whose very restrictive measures will put even more pressure on an industry which is already experiencing great difficulties. i particularly opposed the radical nature of the measures to prohibit discards, which will oblige fishermen to land at least 95% of the fish caught, even if they cannot be sold for human consumption. while fishermen have already made a lot of efforts to limit overfishing, i believe that these rules are not flexible enough and that we need to give the sector more time to adapt to environmental requirements.
in writing. the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) addresses the problem of the constant overexploitation of the seas and proposes to put an end to overfishing. the proposal covered two important parts of the reform: the basic regulation reforming the cfp and the regulation on the common organisation of the market (com). the reform adopted provides for a ban on discards at sea by 2019 (despite exemptions) and for a european fisheries sustainability policy. the union will have to create protected areas for their biological sensitivity, and fishing levels must not threaten the reproduction of stocks (maximum sustainable yield). the new cfp also provides for a strong decentralisation of decision-making, but the general framework and other standards, principles and objectives will still be defined by the european legislator. the two main changes for the cmo are that producer organisations will receive financial support for storage and that information to consumers will now be mandatory: production method, gear category used, catch or farming area, etc., pending the possibility proposed by the commission to create an eco-label award system. in view of these developments, i supported these reports.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the common fisheries policy which amends many cfp rules such as provisions to combat overfishing and the fact that the sustainability principle will apply to european vessels fishing outside eu waters.
in writing. this vote is a good compromise, the result of long negotiations. the fisheries policy is still subject to heated debate, and the arguments are sometimes not rational. we had to preserve the resources, of course, but we also had to ensure that our fishermen, particularly in france, had a certain visibility so that they could maintain and develop their activities and jobs.
in writing. i supported this report on the basic regulation on the common fisheries policy (cfp). after long and difficult negotiations, the objectives of the cfp are now clearly defined and reflect the values of the european union: the establishment of sustainable management and a stronger framework for fisheries practice in eu waters for the 28 member states. this reform will increase the traceability of fishery products and ensure the sustainable use of marine resources by significantly reducing waste. in parallel, i welcome the introduction of a human rights clause in fisheries partnership agreements, which is already present in many eu trade agreements and which may lead to the suspension of the agreement. by introducing this clause, the european union continues to ensure that its values are disseminated and respected internationally.

in writing. the various food scandals that have made headlines in recent years have strongly aroused the distrust of our citizens who demand more transparency and information about the products they consume. fishery and aquaculture products are no exception. after two years of long, long debates illustrating the importance and sensitivity of the subject, we have managed to vote on the regulation on the common organization of the market (com). the latter is based on two pillars. on the one hand, it is a question of strengthening the competitiveness of producers who have to face global competition. it also encourages greater transparency. the commission has also proposed that the european ecolabel be established, and that additional information be provided in the form of labelling standards. finally, it imposes additional requirements on the products we import into europe. this was essential when we know that over 65% of the seafood we consume is imported. i therefore welcome the vote on the report by my colleague, mr stevenson.
in writing. the european parliament recently rejected a total ban on deep-sea trawling beyond 600 metres. i have personally supported and worked to bring an end to it, but in vain. although the ban was not voted on, i supported the report in the end because it still provides more scope for this disastrous practice than before by incorporating a clause for a review in four years' time to perhaps finally ban it for good.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. it is a compromise, so by definition it cannot bring total satisfaction. nevertheless, we have succeeded in oblige ing the commission to carry out impact studies on deep-sea species and vulnerable marine ecosystems. moreover, through a number of binding measures, it has the merit of preserving ecosystems and maintaining economic activity, if consumer demand persists. i voted in favour of this compromise because it guarantees that no new fishing areas will be allowed and that trawls can only pass through the areas they have already passed through. this will help to preserve cold-water corals and sponges, which are indicative of a living ecosystem that we need to preserve. the obligation for all vessels fishing exclusively for deep-sea species to take on board observers from the european union is a guarantee of precise and unquestionable scientific monitoring. these observers will be able to identify violations which will be severely punished. they will also collect data which will enable an assessment of the fisheries to be made in four years' time and a decision to be taken whether or not to stop fishing. i hope that in these four years the fishermen will be held to account in an exemplary manner.
in writing. this report, which i supported, is the result of a compromise adopted by a large majority in the committee on fisheries. through a number of binding measures, this compromise has the merit of preserving ecosystems and maintaining economic activity. the principle of freezing the trawl, which means only using trawls where they have been used and keeping the rest of the fishing areas as sanctuaries, is a fundamental principle. it will preserve cold-water corals and sponges. the obligation for all vessels fishing exclusively for deep-sea species to take on board observers from the european union is a guarantee of precise and unquestionable scientific monitoring. these observers will collect data which will enable us to take stock of this fishery in four years' time and decide whether it can be continued or stopped. this fishery involves some 350 vessels off the french coast, whose deep-sea species catch represents less than 10% of the fishery, but it often balances the exploitation account. it would have been irresponsible to ban this fishery altogether, because it would have led to the destruction of many jobs.
in writing. i voted against this text because i regret that a more ambitious policy on deep-sea trawling has not been adopted. the compromise reached by the committee on fisheries does not seem satisfactory to me, given the vulnerability of this ecosystem. deep-sea fishing is a real danger to some marine species. i regret that it will take four years for the commission to carry out an assessment of the environmental impact of this activity. i therefore supported the amendments proposing a complete ban on deep-sea trawling at depths of over 600 metres within two years. the amendments were intended to replace the compromise proposed by the committee on fisheries. since it was adopted, we were unable to vote on the amendments. for that reason i voted against the report as a whole.
in writing. deep-sea trawling is a fishing method that destroys deep-sea fisheries. between 30 and 60 percent. species picked up by industrial trawlers are thrown back into the sea, often already dead, including endangered species, but above all this practice damages ecosystems that take several thousand years to build. it is crucial for the balance of the seas and for the balance of fisheries itself - especially small-scale, artisanal and coastal fishing - to allow these resources to be renewed. these are common goods and must be protected.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which facilitates strict controls, the preservation of vulnerable marine ecosystems and the in-depth study of the seabed. it should be borne in mind that since 2008, measures have been put in place at european level for the conservation of deep-water species that have allowed the achievement of the maximum sustainable yield for three of the main commercial deep-water species. finally, the compromise reached is balanced and allows deep-sea fishermen to prepare for a possible cessation of fishing in four years' time, leaving them the opportunity to shift their activities to another type of fishing.
in writing. deep-sea fishing is a practice whose consequences on a poorly known and fragile ecosystem are very damaging for many vulnerable species. the fisheries sector survives only with the help of substantial subsidies and aid, in clear contradiction to the eu's other environmental protection policies. moreover, the practice generates relatively few jobs compared to other less harmful techniques. meanwhile, the artisanal fishermen and local fishing businesses are dying. french and european efforts must be directed towards more conventional and respectful fishing.
in writing. dark day for the seabed... we have just lost a crucial vote on fisheries. the european parliament has just rejected a historic measure: the ban on deep-sea trawling, despite the considerable destruction of the marine environment caused by this fishing technique. the amendment tabled by the green/efa group to reinstate this ban on deep-sea trawling was rejected by 342 votes to 326. the socialists and the ump have taken up indefensible positions which run counter to the common will of the european citizens (more than 750 000 citizens called for this measure) and have thus made possible the 'victory' of industrial fishing which is destructive for the environment and for employment. two very different worldviews. even in the face of the increasing scarcity of sea resources, it is still the productivist logic of always more, farther, deeper that has prevailed. what a shame! the european parliament, however, opted for a common fisheries policy based on sustainability criteria last february. the citizens' mobilization continues and as environmentalists, we actively support it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this compromise because it proposes a balanced approach between the need to protect deep-sea species and vulnerable seabeds and the equally necessary need to preserve the thousands of jobs involved. it provides for a no-fishing zone, protecting vulnerable seabeds, and a partial geographical authorisation. the commission has already proposed a ban on fishing for deep-sea species in 90% of the international waters of the north-east atlantic. the text also allows deep-sea fish to be caught only to the extent that the fishing quotas allowed for their reproduction. i would stress that several thousand jobs are at stake here and that if we deprive our european fishermen of these opportunities, we would have to import even more to meet our food needs, which would seriously jeopardise our food independence and lead us to import products from countries whose environmental and social standards are not as respectful of people and ecosystems as those defined by this compromise. finally, these measures will have four years to prove their worth, after which we will assess their effectiveness for possible revision.
in writing. fishermen have been worried for some months about a possible ban on deep-sea fishing. that threat has just been lifted. the european parliament has adopted a less forceful position and calls on the member states to rely on better scientific and technical information to identify vulnerable marine ecosystems and to consider specific measures for these areas. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. this is a good thing, since arbitrary decisions for certain coastal areas are too often taken at european level for lack of information. small-scale fishing, although the most environmentally friendly, is the first to be endangered in favour of industrial fishing by unrelenting and inadequate european policies. the legislative procedure is not yet complete. the council (representing the governments of the member states) has yet to decide. next year parliament will be dealing with the regulation again, so we are keeping a close watch.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague mr kriton arsenis, which, without prohibiting deep-sea fishing, introduces concrete protection measures for the areas affected and calls on the commission to carry out an impact study on deep-sea fishing which could lead to a ban on deep-sea fishing and trawling. this will give european fishermen, who use trawls for the most part, including for shallow-water fishing, four years to prepare for a possible ban. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report by 567 votes to 91, with 32 abstentions.
in writing. i voted in favour of a report on deep-sea fishing which was adopted by the european parliament on 10 december. this will allow the implementation of measures to protect deep-sea species and vulnerable marine ecosystems by clearly demarcating fishing areas where trawling is allowed, limiting fishing to areas currently fished to preserve protected ecosystems, and ensuring that a scientific observer is on board all deep-sea fishing vessels. the latter measure will allow accurate data to be collected to assess the impact of this fishery on the environment and to decide on the future of deep-sea fishing in four years' time based on these results. however, it would have been irresponsible to ban deep-sea fishing and i have spoken out against an immediate and definitive halt to this type of fishing. such a decision would have had dramatic effects on our economy, with more than 350 ships and 1600 jobs affected, including 400 jobs in lorient.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on deep-sea fishing. like my colleagues in the ump, i have more specifically approved the compromise which seems to me to be a good balance between preserving our ecosystems and maintaining this economic activity. so while we have banned deep-sea trawling in vulnerable areas, we have refused to simply ban deep-sea fishing.
in writing. i voted against amendment no 62 in order to open up the existing compromise on deep-sea fishing and amend it on the use of deep-sea trawls. the amendment i supported, co-signed by my group and supported by many environmental organisations, proposed a ban on 'bottom trawls or bottom trawls at a depth of more than 600 metres' within two years. it was not a question of banning ships with this type of equipment, but of banning the use of this heavy equipment in fragile areas - the deep sea - which are still very little known to us. the arsenis report as adopted also takes a cautious position on this practice. a list of vulnerable areas will be drawn up by the commission and bottom trawling will be prohibited. four years after the entry into force of the regulation, the commission will assess its impact and may decide to allow deep-sea fishing authorisations to expire. if our cautious approach to deep-sea fishing has not been adopted, the fact remains that this report intends to reopen the question while setting out the practices. that's why i supported his adoption.

in writing. we had to meet the challenge of deep-sea fishing, reconciling what seemed irreconcilable: ecological, social and economic requirements. i think we've got it. i particularly welcome the agreement reached on the issue of trawl fishing, which will now be allowed in an area representing about 10% of international waters. a zoning that can be reduced if it turns out that there are vulnerable marine ecosystems that are therefore protected. the compromise we voted for protects vulnerable marine habitats, preserves deep-sea species by imposing scientific monitoring and quotas on all species, and maintains fishing activity on our atlantic coasts. it is worth noting that this concerns at least 758 vessels, or thousands of jobs. it is therefore a balanced agreement.

in writing. the european parliament adopted a draft regulation on deep-sea fishing which is a compromise between ecological, social and economic requirements. to protect vulnerable seabeds, the text provides that deep-sea trawling will only be allowed in an area representing about 10% of the international waters of the north-east atlantic. this area could be further reduced if the mapping to be carried out by the member states within two years revealed vulnerable marine ecosystems. the compromise then provides for the reinforcement and extension of the requirements of the common fisheries policy on the conservation of deep-sea species by imposing scientific monitoring and quotas on all species. finally, it helps to preserve the fishing activity on our atlantic coasts. it is with this desire to strike a balance between the need to protect species of great value and the equally necessary need to preserve the jobs involved that i have supported the compromise text. but i abstained on the key amendment authorising deep-sea trawling because i think that preserving the resource is also essential to safeguarding jobs in the future, and that this amendment revealed a very short-term misconception.

in writing. the proposal by elisabetta gardini is linked to the increase in the number and severity of natural and man-made disasters in recent years and aims to establish a civil protection mechanism for the union. the financial envelope for the implementation of this mechanism is €368.3 million, divided as follows: 20% for prevention, 50% for preparation and 30% for response. the framework of the new mechanism therefore covers these three periods of civil protection, and will cover not only the population but also the environment and cultural heritage. the types of disasters for which this programme can be mobilised are also broadened in the proposal, since it will deal with acts of terrorism, technological, radioactive and environmental disasters, water pollution and health emergencies, whether within the union or outside. i therefore voted in favour of the mechanism.

in writing. since 2001, the eu civil protection mechanism has facilitated cooperation in disaster prevention and response (earthquake, tsunami, forest fire) between 32 countries - the eu28, macedonia, iceland, liechtenstein and norway. conscious that this is an area where citizens unquestionably want more europe, i supported this text to strengthen the current system. disaster prevention will be enhanced: member states will regularly share their risk assessments, exchange best practice examples, and jointly identify areas where additional efforts are needed. the disaster response will be improved, including: - the establishment of a european emergency response capacity (replacing current provisions with a more predictable and reliable system); - better training of civil protection staff operating outside their country of origin; - additional exercises to test the response capabilities of civil protection (search and rescue teams, field hospitals, etc.). finally, the budget for civil protection has been increased and will now amount to more than eur 368 million for the period 2014-2020.

in writing. the european union's emissions trading system (eu ets) sets a number of greenhouse gas emission allowances per member state, which are then distributed to a number of industrial enterprises. thus, if a company is short of allowances, it has the option of buying from an excess company on the basis of auctions. the initial objective of this instrument was therefore to raise the price of carbon on the basis that the demand for polluting rights would be greater than the supply. the price was eventually to reach a certain level that would encourage business investment in low-carbon technologies. however, industrial enterprises in the eu are in a situation of surplus quotas. in fact, 995 million allowances have accumulated due to the slowdown in activity following the economic and financial crisis, which does not favour investments in low-emission technologies. i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to introduce provisions enabling the european commission to withdraw up to 900 million allowances from the market. this is a key measure to combat climate change, in that it will raise the price of carbon and thus encourage companies to invest in technologies that emit less greenhouse gases.

in writing. the automotive industry in the union directly or indirectly employs 12 million people in europe and is thus a sector of strategic importance for the european economy. the commission must therefore implement a sustainable strategy for this industry, so that it can remain efficient, competitive and able to access new markets. this also implies that the union effectively defends its enterprises against unfair trade practices by third countries. this strategy for the automotive sector must be part of the wider framework of a genuine industrial policy, which the european union needs now more than ever to support the competitiveness of its manufacturers and to encourage innovation in key sectors.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it is important to support the automotive sector in europe, at a time when many factories in france are closing and manufacturers are deciding to move to countries where the labour force is more advantageous. the text promotes various initiatives which are part of the logic of green growth. to this end, this communication promotes the european green vehicle initiative and aims to reduce co2 and pollutant emissions and noise pollution, which i welcome. and this is an opportunity that our automotive stars must seize. in addition, efforts in bilateral cooperation with third countries must also be stepped up with a view to eliminating non-tariff barriers in the automotive sector which are still detrimental to the european economy. we must help our companies to export products produced in our own countries and thus revitalise the industrial network in europe. in the face of indian or chinese competitors who have already developed many technologies in this field, europe must react and apply its know-how. that is why i welcome all these initiatives.
in writing. i am afraid that the commission's action plan for the automotive industry is symptomatic of its weak commitment to a genuine industrial policy. the vision remains general, global, focused on competitiveness and competition but also lacking: subcontracting, maintenance, secondary market are forgotten. it remains ambiguous as to what it is necessary to support: the so-called 'european' manufacturers, regardless of the place of production, i.e. the shareholders, or on the contrary the jobs in the existing production areas, i.e. the citizens. i must say that supporting romanian employment at dacia by watching the renault factories in france close is not in my interest at all. this is the crux of the problem: in the current state of the european union, an industrial policy at european level, based on the commission's long-standing and outdated principles of action (no support, no protection, intra-european competition, even exacerbated and unfair) may be costly for some countries, notably france. i am not sure that it is at european level, the same one that imposes austerity and therefore contributes to the lack of demand, that solutions should be sought.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it proposes a specific action plan to support the competitiveness and sustainability of our automotive industry. this historic industry is facing an unprecedented crisis, despite the fact that it creates more than 12 million direct and indirect jobs in europe and accounts for almost 6.9% of the union's gross domestic product. it is urgent to put the automotive industry back at the heart of european growth! the report is a step in the right direction, encouraging member states to implement structural reforms to boost the competitiveness of the sector and advocating 'smart' and less bureaucratic regulation. it also stresses the importance of technological innovation in promoting the advance of european industry in future markets such as clean vehicles. finally, it does not forget the importance of human capital by emphasising the training and "know-how" of employees in the sector.
in writing. the european parliament voted on the strategy for the automotive industry up to 2020. statistics show that the number of vehicles sold has decreased significantly in recent years: minus 6.85% for personal vehicles and minus 10.87% for commercial vehicles. this is a direct consequence of austerity policies which reduce the purchasing power of households and the investment opportunities of firms. to deal with this crisis and to build a european industry that creates jobs and enables innovative and environmentally friendly solutions, we need european public cooperation in research and development. the 'cars 2020' strategy proposed to the european parliament goes in the opposite direction. all the amendments i tabled on this report in the committee on industry were rejected. the report calls for 'restructuring' and defends unbridled competitiveness, including towards third countries. i voted against this report which can only benefit the shareholders of the large companies.
in writing. the automotive sector has been particularly affected by the crisis. france has a painful memory of factory closures in this sector, as in many others. today, the automotive sector accounts for 12 million direct and indirect jobs, 4% of european gdp and generates €90 billion in gross trade surpluses per year. that is why i am convinced that we need an innovative industrial policy that is aggressive on international markets. however, it seems to me that a european industrial policy requires genuine economic cooperation within the eu and that unfair competition and social dumping must stop. i also believe that this action plan lays the foundations for the sector to regain global markets: - to focus on innovation and to concentrate research and development on cutting-edge sectors such as eco-innovation and green cars; - to encourage member states to restructure their economies in order to promote the competitiveness of the sector in the domestic and international markets; - to promote smart regulation so as not to further weaken the sector. finally, i fully share my colleague franck proust's proposal to introduce a conditionality clause in european aid to companies that relocate.

in writing. the european parliament voted today on the eu strategy for the automotive industry. the automobile industry in europe is suffering. statistics show that the number of vehicles sold has decreased significantly in recent years: down 6.85% for personal vehicles and down 10.87% for commercial vehicles. to deal with this crisis and to build a european industry that creates jobs and enables innovative and green solutions, we need european public cooperation in research and development. the 'cars 2020' strategy proposed to the european parliament goes in the opposite direction. this strategy advocates the exclusive path of competitiveness and competition. the measures proposed range from aid to the 'restructuring' of the sector, and we know what this means for employees, to the promotion of the single market. moreover, the distortions of competition which are problematic according to this strategy concern only the 'distortions' linked to national technical regulations, but no criticism of the social dumping which may be practised in the automobile sector. so nothing new under the sun... the only interests defended here are those of the big corporations. i therefore voted against.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report which provides a fair diagnosis of the european strategy to support the automotive sector. while the sector has been hit hard by the crisis, i believe that this fall in the european car market is not only due to the economic situation, but also to structural weaknesses. the crisis has revealed in particular that production sites are overcapacity and mainly focused on the european market. in this context, the eu must be a responsible and ambitious actor. it must do its utmost to assist our manufacturers in their painful but necessary restructuring. this requires the appropriate mobilisation of european funds to support regions that are highly exposed to the change in the automotive sector. the eu must also put our manufacturers in a favourable position to better capture the international growth drivers that will maintain a high level of activity in europe. to do this, it must overcome all the barriers which currently prevent european manufacturers from gaining free access to emerging markets. these are the two levers we have identified that the eu must activate if it is to boost a car sector that has been the pride of all for decades.
