in writing. this is the second time in a few months that the estrela report on sexual and reproductive rights has been submitted to the european parliament. for several weeks it had been the subject of a campaign of lies by lobbyists, particularly those of the catholic fundamentalists, including those who oppose marriage for all in france. the report was, however, only a snapshot of the situation regarding sexual and reproductive rights in the eu, recalling the right to respect for the freedom to control contraception and the need for health services accessible to all. the right wing of this house has used the argument of subsidiarity to refuse to vote on this report which merely reaffirms the traditional positions of the european parliament and has instead voted on a meaningless alternative resolution with the support of the far right. the european parliament spends a great deal of its time voting recommendations to the member states. and there is no mention of any challenge to the sovereignty of the member states. this refusal is therefore purely electoral, under pressure from the most reactionary lobbies. i therefore voted against the alternative resolution tabled by the epp without hesitation.
in writing. i have decided to support the alternative resolution of my epp political group calling for the rejection of this report on the sexual education of children. beyond the approximate and even dangerous content of this report, i am opposed to the very principle that the eu can decide on this kind of issue, which is obviously a matter of subsidiarity and should be dealt with only at the level of the member states. it is high time that our assembly did a more selective job of sorting out the reports and topics it wishes to deal with. the eu's desire to be all-inclusive goes beyond its mandate, its capacity to be useful and its credibility in the eyes of its citizens. it is the responsibility of each of us not to go beyond our area of competence, because this contributes to the growth of europhobia, which we are also trying to combat.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on voluntary activities in europe. volunteering is an expression of commitment, support and active participation in social life. the creation of a european skills passport, presenting a comprehensive overview of volunteers' skills through official recognition, for professional purposes as well as for learning purposes, is a clear example of this. the current economic crisis has certainly put a strain on activities which by their nature have no immediate economic interest. however, the success of the activities carried out has shown that, even in difficult times, solidarity prevails over retreat.
in writing. i voted for the scurria report calling on the member states of the union to set up a framework which is conducive to the various forms of volunteering that exist within the european union. the report calls for the creation of a single european service responsible for coordinating the various institutions responsible for voluntary activities. as an active involvement of civil society, volunteering needs to be strengthened. i therefore support the establishment of training courses for this type of commitment. i also support facilitating access to european funding for non-governmental organisations.
in writing. the vote on this text underlines the importance of volunteering, especially for sports and leisure activities. it called for the rights of volunteers to be strengthened, in particular by asking the member states to make insurance coverage for these workers compulsory. volunteering is not only a professional added value but also a sign of solidarity between generations. the aim of the text is to promote european voluntary service in universities and other higher education institutions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report presented by the commission on the broad lines of the 2011 european year of volunteering, as i believe it is important to develop this type of action at european level. in many member states, this action has helped to establish a genuine legislative framework for volunteering, as was the case in bulgaria, lithuania and slovenia. the 2011 year of volunteering was also the founding element of the 2013 european year of citizens. moreover, these projects continue to spread european citizenship and membership, which i can only welcome.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this own-initiative report on volunteering and voluntary activities in europe. as millions of young people across europe volunteer every day in europe, it was essential that parliament conveyed its recommendations on the future of european volunteering policy in a precise and clear manner. we have thus highlighted the benefits of volunteering, whether in encouraging intercultural learning, creating a sense of european identity or developing solidarity between generations. the report also sheds light on some of the current dysfunctions and shortcomings of volunteering. we stress the need to guarantee safe and quality work for all. the house particularly wants an environment conducive to volunteering to be created, in particular by the introduction of a legislative framework which is still lacking today. among our main recommendations is the adoption of a european statute for voluntary associations to promote their legal and institutional recognition.
in writing. on tuesday 10 december, the european parliament adopted a resolution to take stock of the european year of volunteering 2011 and to outline prospects for the future. we found that this european year has enabled several member states to implement measures to develop the voluntary sector and to obtain more accurate data on voluntary activities in europe. we called on member states to step up their efforts to recognise and promote volunteering as a great school for acquiring skills that are very useful in the labour market. we have also encouraged better coordination between the european services responsible for this issue. i voted in favour of this text because i consider it very important to recognise the essential role of volunteers in european societies and to facilitate and highlight their commitment.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on volunteering and volunteering activities in europe, which, following the european year of volunteering 2011, calls on member states to define a legal framework for the recognition of volunteering in the member states and to have comparable data to know the valuable contribution of volunteering to society.
in writing. solidarity is one of the pillars of the european project. i am proud to have supported this text. this is further proof that europe is a place of solidarity. it was important, after the european year of volunteering in 2011, to drastically improve the framework offered. both for the volunteers and the volunteers themselves, and for the organizations that host them. i am talking about working conditions, tasks, relations with public institutions and the promotion of volunteering among the public.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on volunteering in the european union. we are right to want to support these activities, which are beneficial in all respects: solidarity, social inclusion and innovation, local and even cross-border development, economic and humanitarian potential in particular. among the many proposals in the report, two in particular win my support. firstly, the idea of a european skills passport, which would make it possible to officially recognise the skills acquired through volunteering, both at the professional and educational level. secondly, the establishment of a european statute for associations and a training and qualification framework for volunteer trainers, integrated into the european framework of certifications, in order to develop the framework for volunteering at a multinational level. i would also like to point out the interesting idea of creating a simplified visa system for third country nationals who wish to go to the union to volunteer there.
in writing. volunteering activities experienced a significant upsurge in 2011, the european year of volunteering. but the development of volunteering activities has been far beyond the year 2011 alone. like my colleagues, i believe that a common european approach to volunteering will create more opportunities for the mobility and employability of young people, in particular by enabling them to acquire useful skills. i therefore believe that we could go further by adopting the solutions proposed by the international labour organisation in the field of volunteering, in order to make our action international, in addition to our european actions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report although i regret the choice of the english term 'voluntary' instead of the appropriate term 'volunteer'. i welcome the fact that many of my amendments have been incorporated, in particular the one reiterating the request for a european statute for associations, after the long silence of the commission on this matter and the request for clarification of the concept of subsidies to associations, with the aim of providing financial support to associations, often the first victims of budgetary restrictions. this report is a step in the right direction, as it is important to give greater value to voluntary activities. volunteering is an essential factor for individual and collective emancipation, solidarity and social cohesion. parliament also called on the member states to ensure better protection for volunteers. the proposal to abolish visas for volunteers was rejected by a large majority of members. the same anti-immigrant obsession, even though the european parliament did not want to impose any obligations in this area. a possibility to relax these visas was nevertheless maintained. this is a good thing, even if it is not binding on the states.

in writing. after the 2007 crisis, the emergency mobilisation of public funds to bail out european banks was very unpopular with citizens, who rightly asked us to better regulate these financial institutions. today, i think i can say that we are meeting those demands. after adopting new capital and debt requirements for banks and giving the ecb the role of bank policeman, we are on the verge of creating a private bail-out mechanism for distressed banks. in future, rather than asking the taxpayers, it will be the bank's managers, shareholders and creditors who will be mobilized. if that is not enough, a bank resolution fund fuelled by bank taxes of around €50 billion or €60 billion will come in to help with the restructuring. the european stability mechanism (esm), originally designed to help states that are having difficulty financing themselves, may eventually be able to intervene to complete the bailout. the taxpayer can therefore only be approached as a last resort.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which extends the pericles programme until 2020. it contributes to raising awareness among eu citizens of the need to strengthen the protection of the euro. because of its importance as a global currency, the euro requires international protection, which can be ensured by providing the funds needed to purchase equipment for use, for example, by agencies in european and third countries for their investigations into counterfeiting of euro coins.

in writing. pericles 2020 is an exchange, assistance and training programme to combat counterfeiting of the euro. it will in particular help to protect coins and banknotes from counterfeiting by supporting the member states and the competent european and national authorities in their efforts to cooperate with the commission. third countries and competent international organisations are also concerned. the programme should therefore be able to provide active support for the fight against this particular form of organised crime, and i have given my support to it accordingly.

in writing. a few cases of domestic workers becoming "domestic slaves" made headlines because their employers were famous people. but how many cases are never in the news? our vote today is to authorize the member states of the union and therefore also to ask them to ratify ilo convention no 189 on decent work for domestic workers. the aim is to ensure that these workers, who are particularly vulnerable, have decent working conditions with social rights and to combat violence and all forms of abuse, including child labour. the convention entered into force on 5 september last; the european union is not a party to the treaty of rome.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because ilo convention no 189 requires the protection of domestic workers, who are often women and migrants, and are often exposed to discrimination and various types of abuse which constitute serious violations of human rights. in several countries of the union, domestic work is characterized by precariousness, the absence of a contract of employment, late payment of wages, the requirement of overtime without compensation, non-respect of the right to rest and leave periods, non-payment of holidays or vacations, non-payment of social security amounts, among others. it should be noted that the convention does provide that ratification of the convention must not affect the more favourable provisions applicable to the rights of domestic workers (article 19).
in writing. i supported the adoption of the zuber report calling on the member states of the european union to ratify the international labour organisation (ilo) convention on decent work for domestic workers. in order to combat domestic slavery, the adoption of this report introduces guarantees relating to the fundamental rights of such workers, in particular respect for human rights and their legal rights, as well as the right to free movement.
in writing. i welcome the vote on this text which aims to protect the rights of domestic workers. it encourages the framing of a status which is still too approximate by offering a series of guarantees to these workers. this includes the social rights attached to domestic workers' working conditions and the prevention of abuse, violence and child labour in domestic work.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which seeks to ratify the international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers. this proposal is part of the european union's strategy to eradicate trafficking in human beings. this text will oblige the signatory states to take measures to prevent acts of violence is the assurance of a consideration of this problem, which i can only encourage.
in writing. domestic workers are an important but largely invisible labour force in europe. domestic workers, who are predominantly women, many of whom are of migrant origin, are extremely vulnerable to mass exploitation. by giving its green light for the member states to ratify the 2011 international labour organisation convention on domestic work, parliament is thus contributing to the eu's drive for decent work for all, of which the protection and improvement of workers' working conditions are important aspects. it is essential that the european union should have the existing instruments to help combat the exploitation and abuse of domestic workers effectively. the ratification of ilo conventions by member states in general and of the domestic workers convention in particular will enable the eu to improve the effectiveness, coordination and coherence of the fight against trafficking in human beings.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report to ensure that member states ratify, in the interest of the european union, the 2011 international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers. the convention entered into force in september 2013 and provides guarantees on the fundamental principles concerning the rights of domestic workers, and respect for their human and legal rights.
in writing. the resolution before us supports the establishment of a convention for domestic workers. this text provides legal tools and definitions for states and refers to the major standards on rights at international level. it lays down, in particular, obligations on the establishment of judicial and control mechanisms. even if the abolition of austerity policies is necessary to ensure consistent respect for the principles of defending workers' rights as laid down in this convention, i support these advances and i vote in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by ines zuber, portuguese member of parliament for my group, the gue/ngl. this report calls on member states to ratify a 2011 international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers. this convention underlines the urgent need to grant such persons the same rights, protections and social security cover as any other employee. it is intolerable that even today employees are left without recourse to abuse by their employers. i am glad that this report has been adopted because it is high time that the member states took up this issue which concerns the most vulnerable groups of the population. the main victims are women, particularly migrant women, often without papers, who work in isolation, making collective action virtually impossible. it is to be hoped that this appeal will be heard by the member states. unfortunately, nothing is less certain because such a text has no binding force on the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the conclusion of the protocol will lay the foundations for the gradual opening up of certain eu programmes to armenia or for the country's increased participation in them, which will not only strengthen ties in the fields of culture, education, the environment, technology and science, intensify people-to-people contacts and sectoral cooperation, but also consolidate political relations in favour of the eastern partnership and the association agreement.
in writing. i voted in favour of the eu-armenia framework agreement to allow armenia to participate in the work of community agencies and in specific community programmes open to the participation of third states, in order to promote reform, modernisation and transition in armenia. the agreement will allow the eu to strengthen its links with armenia in the fields of culture, education, environment, technology and science.
in writing. this partnership will allow armenia to participate in eu programmes in the fields of cultural, environmental and other cooperation. these proposals are not bad in themselves, but this protocol is part of the european neighbourhood policy, whose primary objective is to prepare the economies of neighbouring states for the establishment of deep and comprehensive free trade areas (dcftas), to the detriment of the latter. the republic of armenia refused to sign the free trade agreement at the vilnius summit last november. the european union is the watchdog of the imf and of neoliberal economic conditions. this protocol cannot be taken out of its political context, and i am voting against it.
in writing. relations between the eu and armenia have been continuously deepening since 2007. the european parliament's plenary session last october was an example of this. the same time, a readmission agreement was voted on, which is still unacceptable from a migration point of view, and a visa liberalisation agreement, which is in the right direction but is rather hypothetical. the report adopted on 11 december 2013 concerns armenia's participation in the neighbourhood policy (nep) and has consequently benefited from certain eu programmes. negotiations with armenia have been ongoing since april 2012. i voted in favour of this agreement because it will allow armenia to benefit from eu assistance in particular in the cultural, educational, environmental and scientific fields, unfortunately, the establishment of this cooperation is being carried out in parallel with negotiations for the establishment of a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta) between the eu and armenia.
in writing. as saint-barthélemy ceased to be an outermost region of the union on 1 january 2012 when it acquired the status of an overseas country and territory, france had undertaken to conclude the necessary agreements to ensure that the interests of the union were safeguarded. the aim of this agreement is therefore to ensure that the union's taxation and savings legislation continues to apply to saint barthélemy despite its change of status, which i supported.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because since 29 october 2010 the territorial community of the island of saint barthélemy has ceased to be an outermost region of the union and has acquired the status of an overseas country and territory, with effect from 1 january 2012. decision 2010/718/eu specifies that france has undertaken to conclude the necessary agreements to ensure that the interests of the union are protected in the light of these developments. in order to move forward in this direction, the european commission in 2011 authorised france to negotiate the terms of the agreement. more specifically, the authorisation concerns an agreement between the french republic, acting on behalf of saint-barthélemy, and the european union providing for the application, with regard to that territory, of union legislation on the taxation of savings and administrative cooperation in the field of taxation.
in writing. in view of the change in the status of the municipality of saint-barthélemy, it seems legitimate that the rules should be imposed in a uniform manner on the territory in the metropolitan area as well as overseas. it is important to pay particular attention to taxation issues during this period. the text allows saint-barthélemy to apply the same rules of administrative cooperation in tax matters and taxation of savings as metropolitan france.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which promotes transparency in financial cooperation between saint barthélemy and the european union. saint barthélemy has enjoyed a relatively favourable tax situation, but at a time when the european union is trying to promote tax transparency, the particularity of this island is becoming a source of conflict. the european union now has a precise arsenal of legislation. as a result, various tax mechanisms have been created, such as dispute settlement, and the aim is that the tax systems applicable to saint-barthélemy should be equivalent to those applicable in metropolitan france. i therefore welcome the efforts made in the field of tax transparency to clarify this situation.
in writing. saint barthélemy is a french territory with a very special status. since 1 january 2012, it is no longer considered an outermost region of the eu but an overseas country and territory. as such, although the island is still a french territorial collectivity, it is no longer part of the european union. however, the purpose of the agreement between the union and france is to apply european legislation on taxation of savings and cooperation between tax administrations on the island. that is a laudable goal. this meagre european harmonisation of taxation of savings will, however, remain a dead letter in the absence of any action by the french government to challenge the status of saint-barthélemy as a tax haven. the eu is also ill-placed to teach lessons in the fight against tax evasion, since it accepts well-known tax havens such as luxembourg. i am voting against this agreement which enshrines the common hypocrisy of the netherlands and the eu in relation to tax havens.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report to allow spain to exempt the canary islands from a tax on certain locally produced products. the purpose of this extension is to support economic activity in this outermost region.
in writing. council decision no 2 of 20 june 2002 authorises spain to provide, until 31 december 2011, for exemptions or reductions from the tax on arbitrary imports and deliveries of goods in the canary islands (aiem) applicable to certain products manufactured locally in the canary islands. the council has already extended its period of application until 31 december 2013. the report proposed to extend its application until 1 july 2014, when it will enter into force. this decision will support the diversification of the canary islands' economy and reduce its dependence on tourism. i vote for it.

in writing. disasters cause considerable economic losses and very heavy human losses. according to the united nations, disasters have affected 64 percent of the world's population in the last 20 years, caused 1.3 million deaths and $2 trillion in damage. more than 95% of humanitarian funding is allocated to responding to disasters and their consequences, and less than 5% to reducing their likelihood. we need to change these paradigms. this report calls for this, in particular through better risk analysis and management to reduce vulnerability to disasters, and also through better involvement of society as a whole (local authorities, civil society organisations and citizens). it also recognised that food and nutritional insecurity was one of the most important causes of vulnerability and therefore called for the elimination of practices such as dumping of agricultural products and unfair trade regulations. all of this is full of good intentions. i have no illusions about the will to implement them, but i voted in favour.

in writing. the development cooperation financing instrument (dci) is divided into three categories of programme: geographical, thematic and the pan-african programme, which enables the implementation of the eu-africa strategy. i could only support this instrument which contributes to the reduction and fight against poverty in developing countries. with an amount of eur 19.6 billion for the period 2014-2020, it is characterised by the introduction of the principle of aid differentiation, namely the concentration of european funds on the countries that need them most.
in writing. the report we voted on concludes the work of two long years which have not been too long to wrest from the council measures to democratize our development aid. this is one of the few european policies that can boast the support of 85% of our citizens! the desire for greater democracy in the functioning of our union also applies to international cooperation. unfortunately, this desire for transparency has only been partially met with the development cooperation financing instrument (dci), which would have been more open to co-decision. we can nevertheless be pleased that we have made substantial progress on many points, such as the allocation of 20% of the future icd to support basic social actions, with a particular focus on education and health. the strengthening of the dialogue with national parliaments, local authorities and civil society on all programming documents is also welcome. i therefore welcome the vote on the berman report, which establishes an instrument that contributes both to the fight against poverty and to the promotion of the values on which the eu is founded.
in writing. i have said this several times in plenary in recent years: the globalisation adjustment fund (gfa) is, in my view, one of the only tools that, in times of crisis, allows the eu to provide concrete assistance to workers who have been made redundant. since its creation in 2007 until today, the fund has clearly demonstrated its usefulness. in 2012, €73.5 million was mobilised in 11 countries to support more than 15 000 workers. however, allowing it to continue to exist until 2020 has not been easy. i therefore welcome the agreement we are voting on today and the action taken by marian harkin, rapporteur for the empl committee, to preserve the egf. even if its budget for 2014-2020 is reduced, the egf will be able to continue to support workers made redundant as a result of the current crisis and will be extended to workers on fixed-term contracts as well as young people (in regions with high unemployment) and self-employed people.
in writing. i voted for the continuation of the egf for the next 7 years, because with its €1.05 billion it will help workers made redundant, even young jobseekers if they come from the region affected by the redundancies, as well as self-employed or temporary workers linked to a company for which they were subcontractors and which would lay off more than 500 employees due to the crisis and/or globalisation.
in writing. i supported the adoption of the harkin report guaranteeing a significant financial amount for the european globalisation adjustment fund for the period 2014-2020. in order to combat unemployment due to relocations, this report provides financial assistance to workers who are victims of globalisation-related unemployment. in addition to one-off aid, this report establishes a european mechanism to help people return to work, in particular through training and the acquisition of new skills.

in writing. the european parliament has managed to maintain the european globalisation adjustment fund, which helps people who have been made redundant. the new fund for the period 2014-2020 will be extended to new categories of workers, such as the self-employed, temporary workers and employees on fixed-term contracts. aid may also be granted to young people who are "neither students, nor employed, nor in training" in regions with high unemployment. thanks to the action of the european parliament, the european union's share in funding measures to help people find jobs, train and set up businesses has been increased. i voted in favour of these measures which are essential to support the many people who are unemployed or at risk of losing their jobs today. however, i am very disappointed by the lack of resources available to us and the incomprehensible opposition of governments to these measures. the budget has been reduced from 500 million to 150 million euro per year, even though european aid is very effective. the reintegration rate for people who have received support from the globalisation adjustment fund is 48%.
in writing. i voted in favour of maintaining european aid for redundant workers for the period 2014-2020. the european globalisation adjustment fund provides assistance to workers who have been made redundant as a result of the closure of their company or the relocation of the production site. it is important to plan an eu response to changes in world trade which force companies to make large redundancies. the fund finances measures relating to job search assistance and vocational guidance for a fixed period of time.
in writing. the european globalisation adjustment fund is the symbol of the hypocrisy of the current european union. on the one hand, free and undistorted competition and relocations are encouraged, on the other hand, a palliative is created to the 'potential negative consequences' of this policy. the report contains some positive points. it proposes to extend the scope of the fund to workers with fixed-term contracts, temporary workers and selfemployed persons (including farmers). it also opens up access to the fund to smes. but at the same time it is endorsing the reduction of its budget from 500 million to 425 million. the aim is to increase the number of applicants for this fund while reducing the resources. above all, this fund will be included in the regulation on common provisions, i.e. macro-conditionality. i vote against it.

in writing. this report proposes to extend the automatic exchange of information (aei) between european tax administrations, as part of the enhanced fight against tax fraud. dividends, capital gains, and all other forms of financial income will be affected by these automatic exchanges. i regret, however, that these exchanges concern only natural persons and not international companies, especially banks. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to provide a more effective response to the crisis. once again, the commission does not take the fight against tax evasion seriously and proposes only small measures, even excluding whole sections of the goods and income that are the source of this organized theft. this automatic exchange of information is also useless if it is not accompanied by the establishment of a real european financial register to enable the identification of who owns what, a form of european capital tax to oblige those who do not do so to hide it and firm and precise sanctions. i'm not going to do it because i don't want to seem like i'm satisfied with these half-measures that won't solve anything.

in writing. the question of the evolution and improvement of european regulations on the transport of radioactive materials has been raised for some time. the mountain of promises has given birth to a mouse: the kovács report, which offers no other vision than that of liberalizing the transport of radioactive materials, thus leaving aside all the necessary measures to strengthen safety requirements. the proposal to set up a system of registration of carriers is very small compared to the real challenges that accompany this regulation: lowering the limits of radiation intensities, separation of the transport of radioactive and explosive materials, inclusion of depleted uranium or raising the requirements for signalling convoys. worse still, this system of registration risks gradually shifting responsibility from manufacturers to transporters and making the transport of these materials trivial. there is nothing in the text to prevent this risk. no, the transport of radioactive materials is not an ordinary transport, and the industrial producers of these materials do not have to be exempted from their responsibilities in the event of an incident. i vote against it.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the lisbon treaty has been in force for four years. it gave the european council the status of a community institution without changing its role. the european council gives the union the necessary impetus, defines its general political guidelines and priorities. it does not exercise legislative functions. that's the theory. in practice, under the pressure of the crisis, the european council has considerably expanded its role. he has multiplied the extraordinary meetings - the 20 summits of the last chance - and has raised, at his level, issues normally dealt with at ministerial level, thereby overstepping his role and encroaching on legislative functions. the result is confusion, lack of transparency and weakening of parliamentary control. for example, on economic governance, the european council decided overnight to renegotiate provisions identical to those already made applicable by an earlier regulation. the adoption of the multiannual financial framework was a real legislative deadlock, since, in order to obtain the necessary unanimity within the council, it pre-decided the content of many policies financed by the european budget. on all these matters, which are by definition the most important, the absence of a formal dialogue between our parliament and the council has prevented us from playing our full role as co-legislators as laid down in the treaties. president van rompuy - and i would like to pay tribute to him - was sensitive to these inconveniences. it has tried to take account as much as possible of the requirements of information and transparency and it seemed to us that the time had come, at the end of this parliamentary term, to take note of the progress that has been made in the relationship between our two institutions and to go further in preparing for the future. in the light of these four years of experience, the aim is to improve and formalise the working relations between the european council on the one hand and the european parliament on the other. this can take the form of an exchange of letters, joint statements or interinstitutional agreements, whatever. we have five major proposals. firstly, we propose that every meeting of the european council be preceded by a debate in this parliament, in this house, allowing for the adoption of a resolution before the meeting, with the presentation by the president of the european council himself of the guidelines he proposes. secondly, to ensure that the european council meetings are held after parliament's weekly sessions and not before or during them. thirdly, we propose that every year a major debate on the state of the european union be held in the presence of the president of the european council, the high representative for foreign affairs and security policy and the president of the commission, without prejudice of course to the debate which is currently taking place every year on the commission's legislative programme. fourthly, we ask that whenever the european council undertakes an action plan or a procedure which may involve a legislative dimension, the european parliament be involved in good time and be able to cooperate in the preparation of these texts in the form appropriate to each individual. finally, and this is very important, the treaty of lisbon introduces a major innovation for the democratization of the union. the president of the commission will no longer be appointed as a senior international official, but will be elected by universal suffrage through the european parliament. but this essential progress requires that the european council play the game, that it applies the spirit of the treaty rather than the letter and that it makes clear, before the start of the next european elections campaign, how it intends to apply the treaty in this area. it is on this condition that the citizens will finally take power in europe.

answer is "blue cardboard". i will answer briefly. madam president, the problem raised by mr lamassoure's report, which is also mentioned in passing, is that there are three interlocutors, who have three different levels of legitimacy: the permanent president of the european council, mr van rompuy, the rotating presidency every six months by a minister from a member state of the council of ministers, and the president of the commission, whose democratic legitimacy will increase. under these circumstances, as henry kissinger once said, i do not know who to call when i want to speak to europe. it's a contradiction in terms. from the europeanist point of view, which is not mine but mr lamassoure's, we have a three-headed europe. it's a normative monster, in a way.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, in the absence of commissioner de gucht, i very much welcome the opportunity presented by professor moreira’s oral question to discuss the implementation of the eu's flagship trade and human rights initiative: the gsp+. beneficiaries will receive their first individual scorecards upon notification of their gsp+ entry, or immediately thereafter. these initial scorecards will constitute the starting point for each country in monitoring the effective implementation of the 27 international conventions linked to gsp+ tariff preferences. the commission will then engage with the authorities in beneficiary countries, drawing their attention to the areas identified in the scorecards and, with the support of the european external action service, will make contact at regular intervals to review the efforts made by beneficiaries to tackle the issues described in the scorecards. this monitoring can involve, for example, ad hoc or existing dialogues, using eu delegations to engage with authorities locally, and interaction with the monitoring bodies of the relevant conventions. the process aims to help gsp+ countries meet their existing commitments under international conventions and thus progressively improve their implementation record. it is not meant to create new or additional commitments or targets. the commission will keep monitoring the reports from the relevant monitoring bodies of each convention. it will also assess information received from other sources, including the european parliament. scorecards will be updated and drafted, shared with both member states and the european parliament before they are communicated to the beneficiary countries. such scrutiny ensures transparency and further strengthens the integrity of gsp+ monitoring. as foreseen in the gsp regulation, reports from relevant monitoring bodies are core documents for the purposes of monitoring the continued gsp+ eligibility. however, other sources of information may now also be considered, provided that they are accurate and reliable. without prejudice to other sources, this could include information from civil society, social partners, the european parliament and the council. this is one of the novelties of the scheme brought about by the new gsp regulation. we are already consulting, briefing and sharing documents extensively with the european parliament with respect to gsp+ scorecards. as the scheme is implemented, we would expect more opportunities for further work together. the european commission looks forward to good cooperation on this file.

president of the european central bank. − president, honourable members of the european parliament, i am very pleased to take part in this debate on the ecb annual report for 2012. today is the last time in this legislature that i will participate in the plenary. this represents a good opportunity to take stock of the progress made over the past few years in strengthening the resilience and stability of the euro area. to introduce the debate, i would first like to review the more recent ecb monetary policy decisions. i will then address institutional matters of particular interest to your house, as well as the progress made so far in reinforcing european monetary union governance. i will hence address most of the issues which the committee on economic and monetary affairs highlighted in its draft resolution on the ecb annual report. let me begin by describing the economic environment of the past years. the economic recovery that followed the post-lehman global recession of 2008–2009 was aborted in the euro area as the sovereign debt crisis took hold. financial stability was threatened; the viability of banks that had survived the first phase of the crisis was called into question. credit was curtailed and the recession that ensued lasted until the first quarter of this year. since then, we have been experiencing a weak recovery. weak economic activity and high unemployment have resulted in subdued inflation. against this backdrop, and in respect of the price stability mandate that was assigned to us by the treaty, we have lowered our key interest rates to historically low levels. to clarify the orientation of our monetary policy going forward in an exceptionally uncertain environment, we introduced forward guidance in july 2013. we stated that we expected key interest rates to remain at present or lower levels for an extended period of time. that statement was conditional and based on an overall subdued outlook for inflation extending into the medium term, given the broad-based weakness of the real economy and subdued monetary dynamics. in november we acted upon that conditional pledge by reducing two of our key interest rates, as price pressures have diminished further and we anticipate inflation weakness to be protracted. in keeping with these anticipations, we also reconfirmed our forward guidance in its original formulation. over the past two years our interest rate cuts were transmitted only unevenly across euro area countries, due to the fragmentation of financial markets along national borders. to address this problem, we adopted a series of non-standard measures. the purpose of these was – and remains – a more effective transmission of the ecb’s interest rate cuts, so that our monetary policy can reach euro area companies and households. our measures addressed those distortions in sovereign debt markets that were due to the redenomination risk and alleviated funding pressures on euro area banks. at our november meeting we also decided to extend the time horizon for the application of the fixed rate full allotment procedures in our liquidity operations until at least july 2015. this decision reassures our counterparties that the liquidity necessary to refinance their core activities will be forthcoming at our main refinancing rate. as a direct consequence, bank lending rates for households and non-financial corporations have decreased at the euro area level. in this way, our measures have also helped small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the backbone of the euro area economy. we have, in addition, taken direct measures to alleviate the funding situation for smes through our collateral framework, and we have worked with the european commission to further improve sme financing conditions. let me now turn to institutional developments and focus in particular on measures related to accountability and transparency. since our creation, we have always gone beyond the treaty requirements in making our work transparent and accessible. the monthly press conferences, which were without precedent at the time among major central banks, are a telling example. this year has also shown that the ecb stands ready to adapt its communication policy, where deemed necessary. for example, we have published the procedures governing the provision of emergency liquidity assistance, the so-called ela. we have started internal reflections on how to increase the transparency of the deliberations in the governing council without undermining independent decision-making by its members. our commitment to accountability and transparency has also become apparent in the agreement concluded between our two institutions on the single supervision mechanism, the so-called ssm. supervision necessitates a differentiated form of accountability from monetary policy, while preserving the independence of the ecb as a whole. the interinstitutional agreement strikes the right balance between ensuring high standards of accountability, transparency and safeguarding confidential information. i am confident that the implementation of the interinstitutional agreement will open a new chapter of successful cooperation between our two institutions. in this context, let me also welcome your positive vote on ms nouy’s nomination. following her final appointment by the council, she will become your main interlocutor on all matters related to the ssm as of 1 january. i would also like to address an issue which i know is as much a concern to you as it is to me: the gender balance at the ecb. today, 17% of our management positions are filled by female staff. it is clearly not enough. this is why the executive board decided this summer to introduce gender targets aiming at 35% women in management positions by 2019 and this is not an empty promise. the ecb has started to implement a diversity action plan that will help us to attain those targets. let me now share my thoughts on the process of completing european monetary union. as this legislature comes to the end of its term, it is an opportune time to reflect on what we have achieved in such a short space of time. not so long ago, the euro area was facing an uncertain future. in the meantime, doubts about the integrity of the single currency have dissipated. notably, a road map for a genuine emu has been outlined that encompasses four pillars: banking union, fiscal union, economic union and, ultimately, political union. through a concerted legislative effort the euro area, and the eu as a whole, has been put on a more stable footing. your institution has made a decisive contribution to this effort. the establishment of the single supervisory mechanism represents probably the most significant change to the european union since the establishment of the single currency, and i am happy to report the internal preparations are well underway. i strongly welcome the political agreement on the bank recovery and resolution directive you reached with the council last night. swift agreement on the other key component of banking union – the single resolution mechanism – is of paramount importance. i trust you will succeed in adopting the relevant legislation before your term comes to an end. these institutions are essential to implement the single rulebook in the years to come. looking ahead we will have a stronger set of rules for capital and liquidity. we will also have a new toolbox for the resolution of financial institutions and we will have stronger national deposit guarantee schemes. banking union, however, is not a panacea for eliminating financial market fragmentation and fully stabilising the european monetary union. it is a necessary, but not sufficient, condition to break the bank-sovereign nexus and restore sustainable economic growth. equal borrowing conditions can only be ensured through the joint implementation of other measures. this not only includes continued fiscal consolidation and implementation of structural reforms but also progress on the other unions; only then can we say we have created a genuine european monetary union. let us seize the opportunity of the next european parliament elections to have an open public debate on the further steps needed to strengthen the architecture of the european monetary union.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would first like to thank the rapporteur, mr gianni pittella, and the committee on economic and monetary affairs for their very valuable work on this important report. this ex-post assessment of the ecb’s activities by parliament is an essential element of the democratic accountability of the ecb and a necessary complement to the ecb’s independence. the commission shares parliament’s view that the ecb has reacted decisively in a challenging environment and played an active role in stabilising financial and bond markets through the ltros and the omt decision. the commission has confidence in the conduct of monetary policy by the ecb and fully respects its independence. this implies that the commission does not comment on the ecb’s monetary policy decisions. let me comment instead on some issues touched on in your report which fall under the remit of the commission’s mandate. first, regarding the banking union, the setting up of the single supervisory and resolution mechanisms is a major step towards completing economic and monetary union and of course building confidence now in the short and medium term. maintaining the reform momentum is key to further progress. the srm will have to ensure that bank resolution will be orderly and that the european taxpayers will be protected. we need to finalise the work in time – the political agreement next week and the legislative work before the end of the current parliamentary term. another issue which is essential – even crucial – for opening up the bottlenecks to growth in europe is access to finance by smes. mr pittella’s remarks on this matter were certainly to the point. we have worked very hard to put together a truly bold initiative to counter the fragmentation of the financial markets and reduce the borrowing costs of european smes because there is no economic growth without credit growth. as always, let me be frank with you about this. the prospective decisions of the european council next week do not seem to go far enough, nor to be concrete and bold enough in this regard. we as the european union – that is both the eu institutions and the eu member states – must do better and step up a gear to boost affordable lending to smes for the sake of sustainable growth and job creation in europe. what does this mean in practice? first the eu member states should be bolder when allocating structural and investment funding for the purpose of leveraging sme lending. the commission is fully committed to this as regards the eu budget. secondly, the european investment bank and the european investment fund should consider increasing their budgets for lending to smes, which calls for the support of eu member states as owners or shareholders of the eib and the eif. thirdly, the ecb could benchmark the funding for lending scheme of the bank of england which has substantially supported sme lending in the uk. as we know, the uk now has a higher rate of growth than the euro area. i trust that mr draghi will do his utmost to convince his fellow members of the governing council and succeed in this. it is only a matter of repairing the monetary policy transmission mechanism. you can be sure that the commission will support you on this and so will the smes in europe as they need affordable lending to create jobs and make the european economy grow. indeed we need to boost sustainable growth and job creation in europe by all possible means. let me conclude by stressing that i see much common ground between your views and those of the commission. it is reassuring indeed to know that i can count on your support in building the sustained recovery we need, the foundations for sustainable growth and job creation. i agree with mr draghi that the next european elections should be used to discuss and design the way forward in regard to how we complete the reconstruction of the economic and monetary union by building on emu 2.0, which will look very different from the emu 1.0 of 15 years ago with all its systemic shortcomings. we need to complete the work on the reconstruction of the economic and monetary union. i look forward to having a constructive and productive debate with you here today.

in writing. as from 1 january 2014, mayotte will change from the status of an overseas country and territory (oct) to that of an outermost region within the meaning of article 349 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). the outermost regions have in many cases a derogation from the rest of the union, so a number of directives, particularly on vat, need to be amended to explicitly exclude mayotte from their scope, which parliament has approved.
in writing. the european council decided to amend the status of mayotte with regard to the european union with effect from 1 january 2014. therefore, as from that date, mayotte will cease to be an overseas territory and will become an outermost region of the union within the meaning of articles 349 and 155 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. following this change in the legal status of mayotte, union law will apply to mayotte as from 1 january 2014. however, taking into account the specific structural economic and social situation of mayotte as a new outermost region, it is appropriate to lay down certain specific measures relating to the special conditions of application of union law. it is planned to grant mayotte additional time to transpose several directives.
in writing. the mayotte region has changed its status to become an outermost region, and our european legislation needs to be adapted to this new situation. the text then makes it possible to amend the legislation on the common system of value added tax and the general excise duty system. the exclusion of mayotte from the scope of these directives, as is the case with the other outermost regions, is thus a matter of consistency in the application of european legislation.

in writing. in 2011, mayotte's status was changed in the french constitutional context from overseas territory to overseas department. following this change and at the request of france, the european council amended the status of the new overseas department with regard to the european union, which became that of an outermost region. from 1 january 2014 mayotte will have the status of an outermost region (orr) instead of an overseas country and territory (oct). the commission proposal is purely technical and aims to ensure that it is treated in the same way as the other french outermost regions, namely guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique and réunion. the amendments concern two directives, one of which excludes mayotte from the scope of the common system of value added tax under the secondary legislation of the european union. i vote for it.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which i believe is one of the european projects that make the eu a reality for citizens. in this case, bank accounts are the target here, with the ambitious aim of improving their accessibility, conditions of use and customer information. the overall approach to accessibility is successful: we have agreed to the principle that all payment service providers will have to provide any legal resident of an eu country who so wishes with a payment account with basic services (payments, withdrawals, transactions, but no obligation to authorise overdrafts). we have ensured this. i am particularly pleased with this measure, which goes far beyond what the european commission proposed. the balance is also positive for the rest. the transparency of bank charges and offers has been further improved, with banks being required to report them and the comparison being made via an independent website set up in each member state. in addition, consumers will be able to change their accounts much more easily and quickly in a context where banks tended to curb these procedures.
in writing. the european union has the largest maritime area in the world. i voted in favour of this report which seeks to establish a procedural framework for the establishment and implementation of maritime spatial planning programmes and integrated coastal zone management strategies by the member states.
in writing. i voted for maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal zone management because the sea represents many sectoral activities (fisheries, aquaculture, oil, transport, etc.) but all of this takes place in a fragile environment that we do not yet know enough about and whose beauty and richness we must preserve for future generations. the high population density and the high level of human activities in coastal and maritime areas put pressure on these ecosystems. therefore, a reasonable balance between economic, social and environmental factors is crucial in order to successfully promote the growth of the maritime economy while ensuring sustainable development. as the interplay between marine and coastal areas is very complex, it is crucial that this governance and management process ensures land-sea connectivity and includes oceans, seas and coasts.
in writing. i voted in favour of the meissner report for integrated coastal zone management. this report calls for more crossborder cooperation in the implementation of integrated maritime spatial management. i do believe that a successful framework for maritime spatial planning requires local, national and transnational approaches. in order to achieve this objective, i supported the rapporteur's proposal to postpone the final vote on adoption of the report by parliament so that negotiations with the council can begin.
in writing. coastal areas are the main population centres and dynamic employment areas. the aim of this text is not only to develop the maritime economy in a sustainable way but also to guarantee legal certainty for smes in this sector. to achieve this, the union needs coherent, but above all common, planning. that is what this text encourages. it is essential to ensure that this framework directive is in line with the principle of subsidiarity and leaves member states a margin of manoeuvre to integrate their particular interests and specificities at national level.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text in order to take full account of the issue of maritime spaces. one of the challenges of this proposal for a directive is to provide a legal framework for maritime space, particularly as very few member states have maritime planning programmes. the current framework has demonstrated its investment limitations. large companies need legal certainty to be able to guarantee their investments in future technologies or in costly projects, which the future directive will be able to guarantee. moreover, from an environmental point of view, maritime and coastal activities and uses often take place in ecologically sensitive areas. therefore, the ecosystem-based approach to managing and planning these activities fully meets this expectation, which i can only welcome.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal zone management which will allow for a coordinated approach to the development of maritime activities taking into account the protection of ecosystems.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this directive which proposes a framework for the development of coastal areas. i have been particularly interested in this issue because maritime and coastal planning is of strategic importance and i have in particular succeeded in finding a balance between the development of economic activities and the protection of the environment. only a healthy ecosystem can be productive and provide the levers for growth, competitiveness and employment. the requirement to ensure that integrated coastal zone management takes account of the needs and specificities of the territory explains why the eu proposes guidelines, which the states, in conjunction with local authorities, are responsible for implementing, to ensure the coexistence of sometimes competing activities in the same area. the development of tourism, the promotion of renewable marine energy and sustainable fisheries are all issues that will find their place in our strategy. with this vote, our assembly is urging the eu to finally turn to the sea, thus breaking with a habit that has shown its limits by looking only inland. we now have an effective land-use planning tool to support blue growth.
