in writing. this report is a continuation of the austerity policies implemented within the eu and in particular of what they call in european jargon the euro plus pact, the six-pack, the two-pack, which are nothing but the translation into european law of the budgetary pact. the european parliament proposes a multi-speed approach. some will be offered different timetables but of course without changing the objectives. this is what france in particular has agreed to. in the medium term, some will be able to 'maximize' the possibilities offered by the existing treaty, i.e. to use the flexibility clause (article 352 tfeu) and enhanced cooperation (article 20 teu). we pinch each other... in other words, we are going straight to the point and, despite the opinion of a growing number of experts, we are pursuing the same policies that are leading us straight into the wall with the social consequences we know. this is in line with the logic of an increasingly aggressive economic federalism in which the states renounce any possibility of going backwards. it is anti-democratic and a denial of national and popular sovereignty. i voted against this report without hesitation.
in writing. i voted for the report by my colleague alain lamassoure on the relations between the european parliament and the institutions representing national governments, as it aims to draw lessons from the first years of application of the lisbon treaty and proposes to formalise the relations between the parliament and the european council.
in writing. in the four years since the treaty of lisbon entered into force, the institutional framework has been constantly evolving in the face of economic upheavals, with the european council taking on the heavy task of giving europe a clear direction, even though it has been criticised on many occasions for taking short-sighted decisions. however, while the crisis has made it the real decision-making body, the democratic legitimacy of the treaty has also been weakened. the heads of state and government are elected by their nations, but the democratic representation embodied in the european parliament has lost all credibility. how can we weigh decisions when bets are being made? the practice of recent years has shown that the european council has become the nerve centre of community life and, while parliament, the commission and the council of ministers continue to be the daily animators, it now appears essential to formalise its role. that is why, as my colleague alain lamassoure suggests, i hope that the european council will clearly define the procedures for the election of the president of the european commission in 2014.
in writing. as the european elections approach, we feel it is essential to clarify our expectations of the council. we ask that in future the president of the european council should systematically come to the plenary session of parliament in strasbourg to present the topics on the agenda of the european summits. we also believe that the future president of parliament should be able to take part in all the meetings of these summits, alongside the heads of state and government. finally, we wanted to remind member states that when they present their candidate for the post of president of the european commission, they will have to take account of the results of the european elections and respect the choice of the electors. since the future president of the european commission will have to be sworn in by the european parliament, the heads of state or government will have every interest in nominating the person who is likely to command the largest majority of the votes of the parliamentarians. the major european political parties have all committed themselves to nominating their candidates before the elections, and we hope that this new political issue will be of a nature to encourage voter participation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report which proposes to formalise the council's relations with the european parliament. among the parliament's proposals, any council meeting should be preceded by a debate before the european parliament where the president of the council would present the items on the agenda.
in writing. this report, which calls for democracy and the strengthening of parliament's powers, is a monument to hypocrisy and cynicism. indeed, its main political position is to boast forcefully of the work of the eurocrat van rompuy who presides over the european council without any people having deliberated on it and without anyone knowing who he represents. but it is the same van rompuy who just helped merkel trample on the rights of the european parliament to adopt the eu budget 2014-2020. so much so that parliament's resolution on the subject went so far as to point out in november the characteristic violations of the treaties by the european council. the rapporteur, who voted for this resolution, does not seem to remember it. while he talks about the council's lack of collective responsibility and criticises the states, he is also totally unaware of the european commission's lack of concrete responsibility. yet this is the heart of the daily denial of democracy in europe. the pointlessness of this report is finally confirmed by its empty proposals: to make a joint statement of the council and parliament or to exchange letters ! i vote against it.
in writing. in the current economic and financial crisis, the european council has considerably increased its role to the detriment of the co-legislators, the eu council and the european parliament. this is unacceptable and the formalisation of working relations between parliament and the european council must become a priority. i therefore support the proposal by my colleague, alain lamassoure, the rapporteur, to have a debate in parliament and to adopt a resolution before each european council. moreover, in view of the forthcoming european elections, it is essential that declaration no 11 annexed to the treaty of lisbon on the election of the future president of the commission be respected and that the european council make clear how it intends to apply the treaty when electing the next president of the commission so that the place and role of european citizens are fully respected.
in writing. i abstained on this report on the european parliament's relations with the institutions representing national governments, namely the council of the european union (the ministers) but especially the european council (the heads of state or government). the report rightly pointed out that the european council has consistently exceeded the role conferred on it by the treaty of lisbon, namely to promote general political priorities, with a ban on exercising legislative functions. the opposite has happened (on the question of patents, the banking supervisory authority or the european budget for the next seven years, for example) and the european parliament's role in the drafting of legislation has been reduced. but instead of shouting and proposing measures, parliament should have taken up its responsibilities, engaged in a show of force with the european council, enforced its prerogatives and refused to endorse major political choices made without it.
in writing. the essential role of green spaces is not sufficiently taken into account in public policies and actions undertaken on the ground. these areas are essential for, among other things, flood control, biodiversity protection and the survival of insects, especially bees, on which pollination depends. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on green infrastructure policy. this is a huge potential in terms of investment, jobs but also in terms of fighting climate change which we must support for the future of our planet.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this resolution which recognises the major importance of green infrastructure for the effective protection of europe's natural capital, the conservation of natural habitats and species and the good ecological status of water bodies. it is up to the member states to integrate green infrastructure issues into their spatial planning plans, consulting and educating stakeholders and the local population, and responding to ecological, economic and societal needs in both urban and rural areas. the example of green and blue networks launched in france under the presidency of nicolas sarkozy is a model at european level.
in writing. the resolution aims to encourage the development of what the european parliament calls in its technocratic jargon green infrastructure , to be understood as the greening of urban spaces. this development is considered, in due course, necessary for a whole range of reasons such as public health, biodiversity, water quality and even social. but as always, the european parliament's environmental policy is a private matter. the first leverage mentioned is to increase private sector investment. no truly coercive proposals are ever considered for the establishment of ecological planning at european level. planning is left to the private sector, for the betterment of their profits. this resolution is therefore not fully in line with the fight against climate change. the global ecological crisis is that of the capitalist mode of production, encouraged by the public policies currently in place, particularly those of the european union. i vote against. environmental planning, stop the anti-environmental policies of the european union.
in writing. the european commission, following an oral question from the environment, public health and food safety committee of the european parliament, has given some clarifications on the guidelines of european policies in favour of so-called green infrastructure, and these guidelines are what the european parliament has examined in this report. these infrastructures are defined as 'a network of natural and semi-natural areas and other environmental elements' and are intended to protect nature as part of land use planning and development. - what's the deed? the implementation of the recommended measures is particularly important in the context of the fight against climate change, the prevention of natural disasters such as floods and the restoration of biodiversity, including forests. i am not deluding myself, particularly in view of the resources needed to implement such policies, which are unimaginable in the context of the current budget cuts, but i voted for this report in the hope that at least some of the measures proposed will be implemented and will make it possible to turn words into action.
in writing. i voted in favour of a report which takes stock of the ecb's performance in 2012. this is particularly the case for the ecb's monetary policy and other related decisions. the consequences of the financial crisis, as well as the current sovereign debt crisis, are the backdrop to most of these decisions.
in writing. with this text, we support the activities of the ecb, which played a key role in stabilising our economies in the face of the crisis in europe. it encourages a more integrated monetary policy, in particular through the establishment of a single supervisory mechanism (ssm) separate from the member states. finally, particular attention is paid to supporting smes, which may appear to be more vulnerable in the face of the crisis. the text is intended to facilitate their access to credit.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the activities of the european central bank, encouraging it to support more the real economy and smes. action to improve access to credit for smes and the industrial sector in europe is needed to support employment and growth.
in writing. this report welcomes the disastrous action of the european central bank (ecb). the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question were necessary to restore the viability of the financial system. the report welcomes the fact that the ecb has "relieved the financial markets". the funds mobilised were considerable: over 1 000 billion in liquidity provided to banks at a rate of only 1% between the end of 2011 and the end of 2012. easy money that has not returned to the real economy: over the same period credit growth in the eu has been cut in half, with bank lending growing less rapidly than activity itself. while it could have ended the sovereign debt crises by lending to the states, the ecb has only bought back 200 billion sovereign bonds by making money off the backs of the states. and she let the banks keep strangling them. the new historic decrease in the ecb's key rate to 0.5% in 2013 shows that this absurd policy in the service of banks continues. i am voting against this report, which does not propose any reorientation of the ecb's role.
in writing. the scale of tax fraud and evasion undermines citizens' confidence in the fairness and legitimacy of public administrations and their tax systems. moreover, unilateral national measures have proved ineffective and insufficient, underlining the need for a coordinated and multi-pronged approach based on concrete strategies and objectives defined at national, european and international levels. i supported this text calling for a series of concrete objectives to reduce the fiscal gap at european and national level. the main objective is to reduce the tax gap by 2020.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution in favour of a measurable and binding commitment against tax fraud and tax evasion in the european union. fighting tax fraud and tax evasion more effectively would bring hundreds of billions of euros back into national budgets and the eu, thus helping to close many of our deficits and boosting investment.
in writing. i supported the resolution for a measurable and binding commitment against tax fraud and evasion in the european union. tax evasion is a major shortfall in europe. this phenomenon knows no borders and needs to be dealt with at international level. the european union therefore appears to be a key player in dealing with this problem. i am in favour of introducing a series of concrete targets to be achieved by 2020 to combat tax fraud and evasion.
in writing. the scale of crossborder tax evasion is immense, and unilateral national measures are not enough to stop it. i voted for a new common system which is both binding on the member states and allows them to exchange the information needed to combat tax evasion. it is absolutely essential to close the 'tax gap', i.e. the revenue lost due to illegal tax fraud and evasion practices that exploit gaps and asymmetries between different tax regimes. we need european cooperation and commitment in this area to prevent this shortfall from having too great an impact on the growth of our economies. the obligation on member states to improve the capacity to collect taxes and to fight fraud should thus be strengthened.
in writing. this joint resolution by the right and the social democrats aims to propose concrete solutions to combat tax fraud and evasion. unfortunately, it is content with the measures proposed by the commission, such as the automatic system for the exchange of tax information, which is a strainer. behind the general phrases calling for better coordination and common will this report is silent on the eu's responsibilities in the development of fraud. there is no mention of the wild liberalization of capital flows, the transfer prices which allow large groups to avoid paying taxes, or the austerity which is decimating tax controls. there are simple solutions to eradicate fraud: banning european banking activities in tax havens or publishing the lists of tax evaders held by several governments. i am voting against this report, which only marginally tackles fraud.
author. - mr president, the least we can say is that the situation in the central african republic has changed somewhat since this emergency resolution was put on our agenda. this is the third time we have discussed this since the beginning of the year. but in the years before that, the european parliament was not particularly concerned about the human rights violations in this country, which has gone from one dictatorship to another since its independence. dictatorships always supported, or even installed with the more or less active complicity of the french governments, because the central african republic is one of the hubs of what some - yes, madame de keyser - call françafrique, one of its rear military bases, from which many of the fifty or so french military interventions that have taken place on the african continent since the end of the colonies have originated. for several weeks, french military forces had been preparing to intervene, and it was, no doubt, the imminence of this intervention that precipitated things in bangui. the anti-balaka have intervened in a coordinated way, claiming to fight against the abuses of the selaka. and it is clear that at least some of them are fighting for bozizé, the ousted former president. they spread death in their path, setting off a spiral of unprecedented violence - several hundred deaths in a matter of hours. once again, the religious question was exploited. these acts of violence have served to justify the intervention of the french army, with or without a un resolution. yes, the population has a right to security, yes we can pay tribute to the two french soldiers who paid with their lives for international negligence. we would have liked the resolution to explicitly recall respect for the un mandate, and above all to speak about the future, the future of the central africans, who should finally have the right to speak. (the speaker agrees to answer a question on the 'blue card' (rule 149 (8) of the rules of procedure))
answer is "blue cardboard". mr. preda, you're used to listening to me carefully. i do not think that i have ever spoken out against military intervention, but i regret that we are being led to such interventions. indeed, in the face of international indifference, it is easy to say: "france must intervene". for a year, indeed, a un resolution has been requested, and it is not satisfactory. the un force on the ground, formerly african forces, which are still not actually in place, are not in a position to move forward. it is international negligence, it is collective responsibility that is at issue. i didn't say anything about military intervention. i've regretted the death of two french soldiers.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, since the seleka rebels seized power on 24 march 2013, the atrocities against civilians, the looting and rape have plunged the central african republic into a terrible outbreak of violence and sectarian clashes. hundreds of thousands of central africans have fled their homes, others have fled the country, the humanitarian situation has become dramatic. so action was urgent. this is the decision taken unanimously by the security council. and it is on the basis of the united nations mandate that france has been intervening, since 5 december, alongside african forces, with the support of the european union, which supports and finances misca, to protect the populations, disarm the militias and prepare for the democratic transition. i welcome the european parliament's support for the french intervention and i want to pay tribute to the two french soldiers who were killed in the course of this mission to help the civilian population. i would add that this crisis called for urgent action, but we also need to build a comprehensive and lasting response, starting today, which must include not only security but also humanitarian action, development, political transition and the organisation of free elections. we need the full involvement of the european union in all these areas to respond to the crisis in the central african republic. that is the message of the european parliament. i hope he's heard.
